CHAPTER 5

![](images/00149.jpg)

*Nightmares Walking*

Leaping from his bed, 페린 snatched his axe and ran outside, barefoot and wearing nothing but thin linen, heedless of the cold. The moon bathed the clouds with pale white. More than enough light for his eyes, more than enough to see the shapes slipping through the trees from all sides, shapes almost as big as 로이알, but with faces distorted by muzzles and beaks, half-human heads wearing horns and feathered crests, stealthy forms stalking on hooves or paws as often as booted feet.

He opened his mouth to shout warning, and suddenly the door of 모이라인’s hut burst open and 란 dashed out, sword in hand and shouting, “트롤록s! Wake, for your lives! 트롤록s!” Shouts answered him as men began to tumble from their huts, garbed for sleep, which for most meant not at all, but with swords ready. With a bestial roar, the 트롤록s rushed forward to be met with steel and cries of “시엔나르!” and “The 용의 환생!”

란 was fully clothed—페린 would have bet the 감시자 had not slept—and he flung himself among the 트롤록s as if his wool were armor. He seemed to dance from one to another, man and sword flowing like water or wind, and where the 감시자 danced, 트롤록s screamed and died.

모이라인 was out in the night as well, dancing her own dance among the 트롤록s. Her only apparent weapon was a switch, but where she slashed a 트롤록, a line of flame grew on its flesh. Her free hand threw fiery balls summoned from thin air, and 트롤록s howled as flames consumed them, thrashing on the ground.

An entire tree burst into flame from root to crown, then another, and another. 트롤록s shrieked at the sudden light, but they did not stop swinging their spiked axes and swords curved like scythes.

Abruptly 페린 saw Leya step hesitantly out of 모이라인’s cabin, halfway around the bowl from him, and all thought of anything else left him. The Tuatha’an woman pressed her back against the log wall, a hand to her throat. The light from the burning trees showed him the pain and horror, the loathing on her face as she watched the carnage.

“Hide!” 페린 shouted at her. “Get back inside and hide!” The swelling roar of fighting and dying swallowed his words. He ran toward her. “Hide, Leya! For the love of the Light, hide!”

A 트롤록 loomed up over him, a cruelly hooked beak where its mouth and nose should have been. Black mail and spikes covered it from shoulders to knees, and it moved on a hawk’s talons as it swung one of those strangely curved swords. It smelled of sweat and dirt and blood.

페린 crouched under the slash, shouting wordlessly as he struck out with his axe. He knew he should have been afraid, but urgency suppressed fear. All that mattered was that he had to reach Leya, had to get her to safety, and the 트롤록 was in the way.

The 트롤록 fell, roaring and kicking; 페린 did not know where he had hit it, or if it were dying or merely hurt. He leaped over it, where it lay thrashing, and ran scrambling up the slope.

Burning trees cast lurid shadows across the small valley. A flickering shadow beside 모이라인’s hut suddenly resolved into a 트롤록, goat-snouted and horned. Gripping a wildly spiked axe with both hands, it seemed on the point of rushing down into the fray when its eyes fell on Leya.

“No!” 페린 shouted. “Light, no!” Rocks skittered away under his bare feet; he did not feel the bruises. The 트롤록’s axe rose. “Leyaaaaaaaa!”

At the last instant the 트롤록 spun, axe flashing toward 페린. He threw himself down, yelling as steel scored his back. Desperately he flung out a hand, caught a goat hoof, and pulled with all his strength. The 트롤록’s feet came out from under it, and it fell with a crash, but as it slid down the slope, it seized 페린 in hands big enough to make two of his, pulling him along to roll over and over. The stink of it filled his nostrils, goat-stench and sour man-sweat. Massive arms snaked around his chest, squeezing the air out; his ribs creaked on the point of breaking. The 트롤록’s axe was gone in the fall, but blunt goat-teeth sank into 페린’s shoulder, powerful jaws chewing. He groaned as pain jolted down his left arm. His lungs labored for breath, and blackness crept in on the edges of his vision, but dimly he was aware that his other arm was free, that somehow he had held on to his own axe. He held it short on the handle, like a hammer, with the spike foremost. With a roar that took the last of his air, he drove the spike into the 트롤록’s temple. Soundlessly it convulsed, limbs flinging wide, hurling him away. By instinct alone his hand tightened on the axe, ripping it loose as the 트롤록 slid further down the slope, still twitching.

For a moment 페린 lay there, fighting for breath. The gash across his back burned, and he felt the wetness of blood. His shoulder protested as he pushed himself up. “Leya?”

She was still there, huddled in front of the hut, not more than ten paces upslope. And watching him with such a look on her face that he could barely meet her eyes.

“Don’t pity me!” he growled at her. “Don’t you—!”

The 미르드랄’s leap from the roof of the hut seemed to take too long, and its dead black cloak hung during the slow fall as if the 반쪽 인간 were standing on the ground already. Its eyeless gaze was fixed on 페린. It smelled like death.

Cold seeped through 페린’s arms and legs as the 미르드랄 stared at him. His chest felt like a lump of ice. “Leya,” he whispered. It was all he could do not to run. “Leya, please hide. Please.”

The 반쪽 인간 started toward him, slowly, confident that fear held him in a snare. It moved like a snake, unlimbering a sword so black only the burning trees made it visible. “Cut one leg of the tripod,” it said softly, “and all fall down.” Its voice sounded like dry-rotted leather crumbling.

Suddenly Leya moved, throwing herself forward, attempting to wrap her arms around the 미르드랄’s legs. It gave an almost casual backwards swing of its dark sword, never even looking around, and she crumpled.

티어s started in the corners of 페린’s eyes. *I should have helped her . . . saved her. I should have done . . . something!* But so long as the 미르드랄 stared at him with its eyeless gaze, it was an effort even to think.

*We come, brother. We come, 어린 황소.*

The words inside his mind made his head ring like a struck bell; the reverberations shivered through him. With the words came the wolves, scores of them, flooding into his mind as he was aware of them flooding into the bowl-shaped valley. Mountain wolves almost as tall as a man’s waist, all white and gray, coming out of the night at the run, aware of the two-legs’ surprise as they darted in to take on the Twisted Ones. Wolves filled him till he could barely remember being a man. His eyes gathered the light, shining golden yellow. And the 반쪽 인간 stopped its advance as if suddenly uncertain.

“페이드,” 페린 said roughly, but then a different name came to him, from the wolves. 트롤록s, the Twisted Ones, made during the 그림자 전쟁 from melding men and animals, were bad enough, but the 미르드랄—. “Neverborn!” 어린 황소 spat. Lip curling back in a snarl, he threw himself at the 미르드랄.

It moved like a viper, sinuous and deadly, black sword quick as lightning, but he was 어린 황소. That was what the wolves called him. 어린 황소, with horns of steel that he wielded with his hands. He was one with the wolves. He was a wolf, and any wolf would die a hundred times over to see one of the Neverborn go down. The 페이드 fell back before him, its darting blade now trying to deflect his slashes.

햄string and throat, that was how wolves killed. 어린 황소 suddenly threw himself to one side and dropped to a knee, axe slicing across the back of the 반쪽 인간’s knee. It screamed—a bone-burrowing sound to raise his hair at any other time—and fell, catching itself with one hand. The 반쪽 인간—the Neverborn—still held its sword firmly, but before it could set itself, 어린 황소’s axe struck again. Half severed, the 미르드랄’s head flopped over to hang down its back; yet still leaning there on one hand, the Neverborn slashed wildly with its sword. Neverborn were always long in dying.

From the wolves as much as his own eyes 어린 황소 received impressions of 트롤록s thrashing on the ground, shrieking, untouched by wolf or man. Those would have been linked to this 미르드랄, and would die when it did—if no one killed them first.

The urge to rush down the slope and join his brothers, join in killing the Twisted Ones, in hunting the remaining Neverborn, was strong, but a buried fragment that was still man remembered. *Leya.*

He dropped his axe and turned her over gently. Blood covered her face, and her eyes stared up at him, glazed with death. An accusing stare, it seemed to him. “I tried,” he told her. “I tried to save you.” Her stare did not change. “What else could I have done? It would have killed you if I hadn’t killed it!”

*Come, 어린 황소. Come kill the Twisted Ones.*

Wolf rolled over him, enveloped him. Letting Leya back down, 페린 took up his axe, blade gleaming wetly. His eyes shone as he raced down the rocky slope. He was 어린 황소.

Trees scattered around the bowl-shaped valley burned like torches; a tall pine flared into flame as 어린 황소 joined the battle. The night air flashed actinic blue, like sheet lightning, as 란 engaged another 미르드랄, ancient 에스 세다이–made steel meeting black steel wrought in Thakan’dar, in the shadow of 세이올 굴. 로이알 wielded a quarterstaff the size of a fence rail, the whirling timber marking a space no 트롤록 entered without falling. Men fought desperately in the dancing shadows, but 어린 황소—페린—noted in a distant way that too many of the 시엔나르an two-legs were down.

The brothers and sisters fought in small packs of three or four, dodging scythe-like swords and spiked axes, darting in with slashing teeth to sever hamstrings, lunging to bite out throats as their prey fell. There was no honor in the way they fought, no glory, no mercy. They had not come for battle, but to kill. 어린 황소 joined one of the small packs, the blade of his axe serving for teeth.

He no longer thought of the greater battle. There was only the 트롤록 he and the wolves—the brothers—cut off from the rest and brought down. Then there would be another, and another, and another, until none were left. None here, none anywhere. He felt the urge to hurl the axe aside and use his teeth, to run on all fours as his brothers did. Run through the high mountain passes. Run belly-deep in powdery snow pursuing deer. Run, with the cold wind ruffling his fur. He snarled with his brothers, and 트롤록s howled with fear at his yellow-eyed gaze even more than they did at the other wolves.

Abruptly he realized there were no more 트롤록s standing anywhere in the bowl, though he could feel his brothers pursuing others as they fled. A pack of seven had a different prey, somewhere out there in the darkness. One of the Neverborn ran for its hard-footed four-legs—its horse, a distant part of him said—and his brothers followed, noses filled with its scent, its essence of death. Inside his head, he was with them, seeing with their eyes. As they closed in, the Neverborn turned, cursing, black blade and black-clad Neverborn like part of the night. But night was where his brothers and sisters hunted.
어린 황소 snarled as the first brother died, its death pain lancing him, yet the others closed in and more brothers and sisters died, but snapping jaws dragged the Neverborn down. It fought back with its own teeth now, ripping out throats, slashing with fingernails that sliced skin and flesh like the hard claws the two-legs carried, but brothers savaged it even as they died. Finally a lone sister heaved herself out of the still-twitching pile and staggered to one side. Morning Mist, she was called, but as with all their names, it was more than that: a frosty morning with the bite of snows yet to come already in the air, and the mist curling thick across the valley, swirling with the sharp breeze that carried the promise of good hunting. Raising her head, Morning Mist howled to the cloud-hidden moon, mourning her dead.

어린 황소 threw back his head and howled with her, mourned with her.

When he lowered his head, 민 was staring at him. “Are you all right, 페린?” she asked hesitantly. There was a bruise on her cheek, and a sleeve half torn from her coat. She had a cudgel in one hand and a dagger in the other, and there was blood and hair on both.

They were all staring at him, he saw, all those who were still on their feet. 로이알, leaning wearily on his tall staff. 시엔나르ans, who had been carrying their fallen down to where 모이라인 crouched over one of their number with 란 standing at her side. Even the 에스 세다이 was looking his way. The burning trees, like huge torches, cast a wavering light. Dead 트롤록s lay everywhere. There were more 시엔나르ans down than standing, and the bodies of his brothers were scattered among them. So many. . . .

페린 realized he wanted to howl again. Frantically he walled himself off from contact with the wolves. Images seeped through, emotions, as he tried to stop them. Finally, though, he could no longer feel them, feel their pain, or their anger, or the desire to hunt the Twisted Ones, or to run. . . . He gave himself a shake. The wound on his back burned like fire, and his torn shoulder felt as if it had been hammered on an anvil. His bare feet, scraped and bruised, throbbed with his pain. The smell of blood was everywhere. The smell of 트롤록s, and death.

“I. . . . I’m all right, 민.”

“You fought well, blacksmith,” 란 said. The 감시자 raised his still-bloody sword above his head. *“Tai’shar Manetheren! Tai’shar 안도르!”* True Blood of Manetheren. True Blood of 안도르.

The 시엔나르ans still standing—so few—lifted their blades and joined him. *“Tai’shar Manetheren! Tai’shar 안도르!”*

로이알 nodded. *“Ta’veren,”* he added.

페린 lowered his eyes in embarrassment. 란 had saved him from the questions he did not want to answer, but had given him an honor he did not deserve. The others did not understand. He wondered what they would say if they knew the truth. 민 moved closer, and he muttered, “Leya’s dead. I couldn’t. . . . I almost reached her in time.”

“It wouldn’t have made any difference,” she said softly. “You know that.” She leaned to look at his back, and winced. “모이라인 will take care of that for you. She’s 치유 those she can.”

페린 nodded. His back felt sticky with drying blood all the way to his waist, but despite the pain he hardly noticed it. *Light, I almost didn’t come back that time. I can’t let that happen again. I won’t. Never again!*

But when he was with the wolves, it was all so different. He did not have to worry about strangers being afraid of him just because he was big, then. There was no one thinking he was slow-witted just because he tried to be careful. Wolves knew each other even if they had never met before, and with them he was just another wolf.

*No!* His hands tightened on the haft of his axe. *No!* He gave a start as Masema suddenly spoke up.

“It was a sign,” the 시엔나르an said, turning in a circle to address everyone. There was blood on his arms and his chest—he had fought in nothing but his breeches—and he moved with a limp, but the light in his eyes was as fervent as it had ever been. More fervent. “A sign to confirm our faith. Even wolves came to fight for the 용의 환생. In the Last Battle, the Lord Dragon will summon even the beasts of the forest to fight at our sides. It is a sign for us to go forth. Only 어둠의 친구들 will fail to join us.” Two of the 시엔나르ans nodded.

“You shut your bloody mouth, Masema!” Uno snapped. He seemed untouched, but then Uno had been fighting 트롤록s since before 페린 was born. Yet he sagged with weariness; only the painted eye on his eyepatch seemed fresh. “We’ll flaming go forth when the Lord Dragon bloody well tells us, and not before! You sheep-headed farmers flaming remember that!” The one-eyed man looked at the growing row of men being tended by 모이라인—few were able to as much as sit up, even after she was done with them—and shook his head. “At least we’ll have plenty of flaming wolf hides to keep the wounded warm.”

*“No!”* The 시엔나르ans seemed surprised at the vehemence in 페린’s voice. “They fought for us, and we’ll bury them with our dead.”

Uno frowned, and opened his mouth as if to argue, but 페린 fixed him with a steady, yellow-eyed stare. It was the 시엔나르an who dropped his gaze first, and nodded.

페린 cleared his throat, embarrassed all over again as Uno gave orders for the 시엔나르ans who were fit to gather the dead wolves. 민 was squinting at him the way she did when she saw things. “Where’s 랜드?” he asked her.

“Out there in the dark,” she said, nodding upslope without taking her eyes off him. “He will not talk to anyone. He just sits there, snapping at anyone who comes near him.”

“He will talk to me,” 페린 said. She followed him, protesting all the while that he ought to wait until 모이라인 had seen to his injuries. *Light, what does she see when she looks at me? I don’t want to know.*

랜드 was seated on the ground just beyond the light of the burning trees, with his back against the trunk of a stunted oak. Staring at nothing, he had his arms wrapped around himself, hands under his red coat, as if feeling the cold. He did not appear to notice their approach. 민 sat down beside him, but he did not move even when she laid a hand on his arm. Even here 페린 smelled blood, and not only his own.

“랜드,” 페린 began, but 랜드 cut him off.

“Do you know what I did during the fight?” Still staring into the distance, 랜드 addressed the night. “Nothing! Nothing useful. At first, when I reached out for the True Source, I couldn’t touch it, couldn’t grasp it. It kept sliding away. Then, when I finally had hold of it, I was going to burn them all, burn all the 트롤록s and 페이드s. And all I could do was set fire to some trees.” He shook with silent laughter, then stopped with a pained grimace. “*Saidin* filled me till I thought I’d explode like 불꽃놀이. I had to channel it somewhere, get rid of it before it burned me up, and I found myself thinking about pulling the mountain down and burying the 트롤록s. I almost tried. That was my fight. Not against the 트롤록s. Against myself. To keep from burying us all under the mountain.”

민 gave 페린 a pained look, as if asking for help.

“We . . . dealt with them, 랜드,” 페린 said. He shivered, thinking of all the wounded men down below. And the dead. *Better that than the mountain down on top of us.* “We didn’t need you.”

랜드’s head fell back against the tree and his eyes closed. “I felt them coming,” he said, nearly whispering. “I didn’t know what it was, though. They feel like the taint on *세이딘.* And *세이딘* is always there, calling to me, singing to me. By the time I knew the difference, 란 was already shouting his warning. If I could only control it, I could have given warning before they were even close. But half the time when I actually manage to touch *세이딘*, I don’t know what I am doing at all. The flow of it just sweeps me along. I could have given warning, though.”

페린 shifted his bruised feet uncomfortably. “We had warning enough.” He knew he sounded as if he were trying to convince himself. *I could have given warning, too, if I’d talked with the wolves. They knew there were 트롤록s and 페이드s in the mountains. They were trying to tell me.* But he wondered: If he did not keep the wolves out of his mind, might he not be running with them now? There had been a man, 엘리아스 Machera, who also could talk to wolves. 엘리아스 ran with the wolves all the time, yet seemed able to remember he was a man. But he had never told 페린 how he did it, and 페린 had not seen him in a long time.

The crunch of boots on rock announced two people coming, and a swirl of air carried their scents to 페린. He was careful not to speak names, though, until 란 and 모이라인 were close enough for even ordinary eyes to make them out.

The 감시자 had a hand under the 에스 세다이’s arm, as if trying to support her without letting her know it. 모이라인’s eyes were haggard, and she carried a small, age-dark ivory carving of a woman in one hand. 페린 knew it for an *angreal*, a remnant from the 전설의 시대 that allowed an 에스 세다이 to safely channel more of the Power than she could alone. It was a measure of her tiredness that she was using it for 치유.

민 got to her feet to help 모이라인, but the 에스 세다이 motioned her away. “Everyone else is seen to,” she told 민. “When I am done here, I can rest.” She shook off 란 as well, and a look of concentration appeared on her face as she traced a cool hand across 페린’s bleeding shoulder, then along the wound on his back. Her touch made his skin tingle. “This is not too bad,” she said. “The bruising of your shoulder goes deep, but the gashes are shallow. Brace yourself. This will not hurt, but. . . .”

He had never found it easy being near someone he knew was channeling the 하나의 힘, and still less if it actually involved him. Yet there had been one or two of those times, and he thought he had some idea what the channeling entailed, but those 치유s had been minor, simply washing away tiredness when 모이라인 could not afford to have him weary. They had been nothing like this.

The 에스 세다이’s eyes suddenly seemed to be seeing inside him, seeing through him. He gasped and almost dropped his axe. He could feel the skin on his back crawling, muscles writhing as they knit back together. His shoulder quivered uncontrollably, and everything blurred. Cold seared him to the bone, then deeper still. He had the impression of moving, falling, flying; he could not tell which, but he felt as if he were rushing—somewhere, somehow—at great speed, forever. After an eternity the world came into focus again. 모이라인 was stepping back, half staggering until 란 caught her arm.

Gaping, 페린 looked down at his shoulder. The gashes and bruises were gone; not so much as a twinge remained. He twisted carefully, but the pain in his back had vanished as well. And his feet no longer hurt; he did not need to look to know all the bruises and scrapes were gone. His stomach rumbled loudly.

“You should eat as soon as you can,” 모이라인 told him. “A good bit of the strength for that came from you. You need to replace it.”

Hunger—and images of food—were already filling 페린’s head. Blood rare beef, and venison, and mutton, and. . . . With an effort he made himself stop thinking of meat. He would find some of those roots that smelled like turnips when they were roasted. His stomach growled in protest.

“There’s barely even a scar, blacksmith,” 란 said behind him.

“Most of the wolves who were hurt made their own way to the forest,” 모이라인 said, knuckling her back and stretching, “but I Healed those I could find.” 페린 gave her a sharp look, yet she seemed to be just making conversation. “Perhaps they came for their own reasons, yet we would likely all be dead without them.” 페린 shifted uneasily and dropped his eyes.

The 에스 세다이 reached toward the bruise on 민’s cheek, but 민 stepped back, saying, “I’m not really hurt, and you’re tired. I’ve had worse falling over my own feet.”

모이라인 smiled and let her hand fall. 란 took her arm; she swayed in his grip. “Very well. And what of you, 랜드? Did you take any hurt? Even a nick from a 미르드랄’s blade can be deadly, and some 트롤록 blades are almost as bad.”

페린 noticed something for the first time. “랜드, your coat is wet.”

랜드 pulled his right hand from under his coat, a hand covered in blood. “Not a 미르드랄,” he said absently, peering at his hand. “Not even a 트롤록. The wound I took at Falme broke open.”

모이라인 hissed and jerked her arm free from 란, half fell to her knees beside 랜드. Pulling back the side of his coat, she studied his wound. 페린 could not see it, for her head was in the way, but the smell of blood was stronger, now. 모이라인’s hands moved, and 랜드 grimaced in pain. “ ‘The blood of the 용의 환생 on the rocks of 세이올 굴 will free mankind from the Shadow.’ Isn’t that what the Prophecies of the Dragon say?”

“Who told you that?” 모이라인 said sharply.

“If you could get me to 세이올 굴 now,” 랜드 said drowsily, “by Waygate or Portal Stone, there could be an end to it. No more dying. No more dreams. No more.”

“If it were as simple as that,” 모이라인 said grimly, “I would, one way or another, but not all in *The 카라에손 순환* can be taken at its face. For every thing it says straight out, there are ten that could mean a hundred different things. Do not think you know anything at all of what *must* be, even if someone has told you the whole of the Prophecies.” She paused, as if gathering strength. Her grip tightened on the *angreal*, and her free hand slid along 랜드’s side as if it were not covered in blood. “Brace yourself.”

Suddenly 랜드’s eyes opened wide, and he sat straight up, gasping and staring and shivering. 페린 had thought, when she Healed him, that it went on forever, but in moments she was easing 랜드 back against the oak.

“I have . . . done as much as I can,” she said faintly. “As much as I can. You must be careful. It could break open again if. . . .” As her voice trailed off, she fell.

랜드 caught her, but 란 was there in an instant to scoop her up. As the 감시자 did so, a look passed across his face, a look as close to tenderness as 페린 ever expected to see from 란.

“Exhausted,” the 감시자 said. “She has cared for everyone else, but there’s no one to take her fatigue. I will put her to bed.”

“There’s 랜드,” 민 said slowly, but the 감시자 shook his head.

“It isn’t that I do not think you would try, sheepherder,” he said, “but you know so little you might as soon kill her as help her.”

“That’s right,” 랜드 said bitterly. “I’m not to be trusted. 르웨어스 테린 동족 살해자 killed everyone close to him. Maybe I’ll do the same before I am done.”

“Pull yourself together, sheepherder,” 란 said harshly. “The whole world rides on your shoulders. Remember you’re a man, and do what needs to be done.”

랜드 looked up at the 감시자, and surprisingly, all of his bitterness seemed to be gone. “I will fight the best I can,” he said. “Because there’s no one else, and it has to be done, and the duty is mine. I’ll fight, but I do not have to like what I’ve become.” He closed his eyes as if going to sleep. “I will fight. Dreams. . . .”

란 stared down at him a moment, then nodded. He raised his head to look across 모이라인 at 페린 and 민. “Get him to his bed, then see to some sleep yourselves. We have plans to make, and the Light alone knows what happens next.”

CHAPTER 6

![](images/00147.jpg)

*The Hunt Begins*

페린 did not expect to sleep, but a stomach stuffed with cold stew—his resolve about the roots had lasted until the smells of supper’s leftovers hit his nose—and bone weariness pulled him down on his bed. If he dreamed, he did not remember. He awoke to 란 shaking his shoulders, dawn through the open door turning the 감시자 to a shadow haloed with light.

“랜드 is gone,” was all 란 said before he left at a run, but it was more than enough.

페린 dragged himself up yawning and dressed quickly in the early chill. Outside, only a handful of 시엔나르ans were in sight, using their horses to drag 트롤록 bodies into the woods, and most of those moved as if they should be in a sickbed. A body took time to build back the strength that being Healed took.

페린’s stomach muttered at him, and his nose tested the breeze in the hope that someone had already started cooking. He was ready to eat those turnip-like roots, raw if need be. There were only the lingering stench of slain 미르드랄, the smells of dead 트롤록s and men, alive and dead, of horses and the trees. And dead wolves.

모이라인’s hut, high on the other side of the bowl, seemed a center of activity. 민 hurried inside, and moments later Masema came out, then Uno. At a trot the one-eyed man vanished into the trees, toward the sheer rock wall beyond the hut, while the other 시엔나르an limped down the slope.

페린 started toward the hut. As he splashed across the shallow stream, he met Masema. The 시엔나르an’s face was haggard, the scar on his cheek prominent, and his eyes even more sunken than usual. In the middle of the stream, he raised his head suddenly and caught 페린’s coat sleeve.

“You’re from his village,” Masema said hoarsely. “You must know. Why did the Lord Dragon abandon us? What sin did we commit?”

“Sin? What are you talking about? Whyever 랜드 went, it was nothing you did or didn’t do.” Masema did not appear satisfied; he kept his grip on 페린’s sleeve, peering into his face as if there were answers there. Icy water began to seep into 페린’s left boot. “Masema,” he said carefully, “whatever the Lord Dragon did, it was according to his plan. The Lord Dragon would not abandon us.” *Or would he? If I were in his place, would I?*

Masema nodded slowly. “Yes. Yes, I see that, now. He has gone out alone to spread the word of his coming. We must spread the word, too. Yes.” He limped on across the stream, muttering to himself.

Squelching at every other step, 페린 climbed to 모이라인’s hut and knocked. There was no answer. He hesitated a moment, then went in.

The outer room, where 란 slept, was as stark and simple as 페린’s own hut, with a rough bed built against one wall, a few pegs for hanging possessions, and a single shelf. Not much light entered through the open door, and the only other illumination came from crude lamps on the shelf, slivers of oily fat-wood wedged into cracks in pieces of rock. They gave off thin streamers of smoke that made a layer of haze under the roof. 페린’s nose wrinkled at the smell.

The low roof was only a little higher than his head. 로이알’s head actually brushed it, even seated as he was on one end of 란’s bed, with his knees drawn up to make himself small. The 오지어’s tufted ears twitched uneasily. 민 sat cross-legged on the dirt floor beside the door that led to 모이라인’s room, while the 에스 세다이 paced back and forth in thought. Dark thoughts, they must have been. Three paces each way was all she had, but she made vigorous use of the space, the calm on her face belied by the quickness of her step.

“I think Masema is going crazy,” 페린 said.

민 sniffed. “With him, how can you tell?”

모이라인 rounded on him, a tightness to her mouth. Her voice was soft. Too soft. “Is Masema the most important thing in your mind this morning, 페린 Aybara?”

“No. I’d like to know when 랜드 left, and why. Did anyone see him go? Does anyone know where he went?” He made himself meet her look with one just as level and firm. It was not easy. He loomed over her, but she was 에스 세다이. “Is this of your making, 모이라인? Did you rein him in until he was so impatient he’d go anywhere, do anything, just to stop sitting still?” 로이알’s ears went stiff, and he motioned a surreptitious warning with one thick-fingered hand.

모이라인 studied 페린 with her head tilted to one side, and it was all he could do not to drop his eyes. “This is none of my doing,” she said. “He left sometime during the night. When and how and why, I yet hope to learn.”

로이알’s shoulders heaved in a quiet sigh of relief. Quiet for an 오지어, it sounded like steam rushing out from quenching red-hot iron. “Never anger an 에스 세다이,” he said in a whisper obviously meant just for himself, but audible to everyone. “ ‘Better to embrace the sun than to anger an 에스 세다이.’ ”

민 reached up enough to hand 페린 a folded piece of paper. “로이알 went to see him after we got him to bed last night, and 랜드 asked to borrow pen and paper and ink.”

The 오지어’s ears jerked, and he frowned worriedly until his long eyebrows hung down on his cheeks. “I did not know what he was planning. I didn’t.”

“We know that,” 민 said. “No one is accusing you of anything, 로이알.”

모이라인 frowned at the paper, but she did not try to stop 페린 from reading. It was in 랜드’s hand.

> *What I do, I do because there is no other way. He is hunting me again, and this time one of us has to die, I think. There is no need for those around me to die, also. Too many have died for me already. I do not want to die either, and will not, if I can manage it. There are lies in dreams, and death, but dreams hold truth, too.*

That was all, with no signature. There was no need for 페린 to wonder who 랜드 meant by “he.” For 랜드, for all of them, there could be only one. Ba’alzamon.

“He left that tucked under the door there,” 민 said in a tight voice. “He took some old clothes the 시엔나르ans had hanging out to dry, and his flute, and a horse. Nothing else but a little food, as far as we can tell. None of the guards saw him go, and last night they would have seen a mouse creeping.”

“And would it have done any good if they had?” 모이라인 said calmly. “Would any of them have stopped the *Lord Dragon*, or even challenged him? Some of them—Masema for one—would slit their own throats if the *Lord Dragon* told them to.”

It was 페린’s turn to study her. “Did you expect anything else? They swore to follow him. Light, 모이라인, he’d never have named himself Dragon if not for you. What did you expect of them?” She did not speak, and he went on more quietly. “Do you believe, 모이라인? That he’s really the 용의 환생? Or do you just think he’s someone you can use before the 하나의 힘 kills him or drives him mad?”

“Go easy, 페린,” 로이알 said. “Not so angry.”

“I’ll go easy when she answers me. Well, 모이라인?”

“He is what he is,” she said sharply.

“You said the Pattern would force him to the right path eventually. Is that what this is, or is he just trying to get away from you?” For a moment he thought he had gone too far—her dark eyes sparkled with anger—but he refused to back down. “Well?”

모이라인 took a deep breath. “This may well be what the Pattern has chosen, yet I did not mean for him to go off alone. For all his power, he is as defenseless as a babe in many ways, and as ignorant of the world. He channels, but he has no control over whether or not the 하나의 힘 comes when he reaches for it and almost as little over what he does with it if it does come. The power itself will kill him before he has a chance to go mad if he does not learn that control. There is so much he must learn, yet. He wants to run before he has learned to walk.”

“You split hairs and lay false trails, 모이라인.” 페린 snorted. “If he is what you say he is, did it never occur to you that he might know what he has to do better than you?”

“He is what he is,” she repeated firmly, “but I must keep him alive if he is to do anything. He will fulfill no prophecies dead, and even if he manages to avoid 어둠의 친구들 and 그림자태생, there are a thousand other hands ready to slay him. All it will take is a hint of the hundredth part of what he is. Yet if that were all he might face, I would not worry half so much as I do. There are the 버림받은 자들 to be accounted for.”

페린 gave a start; from the corner, 로이알 moaned. “ ‘어둠의 존재 and all the 버림받은 자들 are bound in 세이올 굴,’ ” 페린 began by rote, but she gave him no time to finish.

“The seals are weakening, 페린. Some are broken, though the world does not know that. Must not know that. The 거짓의 아비 is not free. Yet. But as the seals weaken, more and more, which of the 버림받은 자들 may be loosed already? 란피어? 사마엘? 아스모데안, or Be’lal, or Ravhin? 이샤마엘 himself, the Betrayer of Hope? They were thirteen altogether, 페린, and bound in the sealing, not in the prison that holds the 어둠의 존재. Thirteen of the most powerful 에스 세다이 of the 전설의 시대, the weakest of them stronger than the ten strongest 에스 세다이 living today, the most ignorant with all the knowledge of the 전설의 시대. And every man and woman of them gave up the Light and dedicated their souls to the Shadow. What if they are free, and out there waiting for him? I will not let them have him.”

페린 shivered, partly from the icy iron in her last words, and partly from thought of the 버림받은 자들. He did not want to think of even one of the 버림받은 자들 loose in the world. His mother had frightened him with those names when he was little. *이샤마엘 comes for boys who do not tell their mothers the truth. 란피어 waits in the night for boys who do not go to bed when they are supposed to.* Being older did not help, not when he knew now they were all real. Not when 모이라인 said they might be free.

“Bound in 세이올 굴,” he whispered, and wished he still believed it. Troubled, he studied 랜드’s letter again. “Dreams. He was talking about dreams yesterday, too.”

모이라인 stepped closer, and peered up into his face. “Dreams?” 란 and Uno came in, but she waved them to silence. The small room was more than crowded now, with five people in it besides the 오지어. “What dreams have *you* had the last few days, 페린?” She ignored his protest that there was nothing wrong with his dreams. “Tell me,” she insisted. “What dream have you had that was not ordinary? Tell me.” Her gaze seized him like smithy tongs, willing him to speak.

He looked at the others—they were all watching him fixedly, even 민—then hesitantly told of the one dream that seemed unusual to him, the dream that came every night. The dream of the sword he could not touch. He did not mention the wolf that had appeared in the last.

*“칼란도르,”* 란 breathed when he was done. Rock-hard face or no, he looked stunned.
“Yes,” 모이라인 said, “but we must be absolutely certain. Speak to the others.” As 란 hurried out, she turned to Uno. “And what of your dreams? Did you dream of a sword, too?”

The 시엔나르an shifted his feet. The red eye painted on his patch stared straight at 모이라인, but his real eye blinked and wavered. “I dream about flam—uh, about swords all the time, 모이라인 Sedai,” he said stiffly. “I suppose I’ve dreamed about a sword the last few nights. I don’t remember my dreams the way Lord 페린 here does.”

모이라인 said, “로이알?”

“My dreams are always the same, 모이라인 Sedai. The groves, and the Great Trees, and the *stedding.* We 오지어 always dream of the *stedding* when we are away from them.”

The 에스 세다이 turned back to 페린.

“It was just a dream,” he said. “Nothing but a dream.”

“I doubt it,” she said. “You describe the hall called the Heart of the Stone, in the fortress called the Stone of 티어, as if you had stood in it. And the shining sword is *칼란도르*, the Sword That Is Not a Sword, the Sword That Cannot Be Touched.”

로이알 sat up straight, bumping his head on the roof. He did not seem to notice. “The Prophecies of the Dragon say the Stone of 티어 will never fall till *칼란도르* is wielded by the Dragon’s hand. The fall of the Stone of 티어 will be one of the greatest signs of the Dragon’s Rebirth. If 랜드 holds *칼란도르*, the whole world must acknowledge him as the Dragon.”

“Perhaps.” The word floated from the 에스 세다이’s lips like a shard of ice on still water.

“Perhaps?” 페린 said. “Perhaps? I thought that was the final sign, the last thing to fulfill your Prophecies.”

“Neither the first nor the last,” 모이라인 said. “*칼란도르* will be but one fulfillment of *The 카라에손 순환*, as his birth on the slopes of 용산 was the first. He has yet to break the nations, or shatter the world. Even scholars who have studied the Prophecies for their entire lives do not know how to interpret them all. What does it mean that he ‘shall slay his people with the sword of peace, and destroy them with the leaf’? What does it meant that he ‘shall bind the nine moons to serve him’? Yet these are given equal weight with *칼란도르* in the *Cycle.* There are others. What ‘wounds of madness and cutting of hope’ has he healed? What chains has he broken, and who put into chains? And some are so obscure that he may already have fulfilled them, although I am not aware of it. But, no. *칼란도르* is far from the end of it.”

페린 shrugged uneasily. He knew only bits and pieces of the Prophecies; he had liked hearing them even less since 랜드 had let 모이라인 put that banner in his hands. No, it had been before that, even. Since a journey by Portal Stone had convinced him his life was bound to 랜드’s.

모이라인 was continuing. “If you think he has simply to put out his hand, 로이알 son of 아렌트 son of 할란, you are a fool, as is he if he thinks it. Even if he lives to reach 티어, he may never attain the Stone.

“타이런s have no love for the 하나의 힘, and less for any man claiming to be the Dragon. Channeling is outlawed, and 에스 세다이 are tolerated at best, so long as they do not channel. Telling the Prophecies of the Dragon, or even possessing a copy of them, is enough to put you in prison, in 티어. And no one enters the Stone of 티어 without permission of the High Lords; none but the High Lords themselves enter the Heart of the Stone. He is not ready for this. Not ready.”

페린 grunted softly. The Stone would never fall till the 용의 환생 held *칼란도르. How in the Light is he supposed to reach it—inside a bloody fortress!—before the fortress falls? It is madness!*

“Why are we just sitting here?” 민 burst out. “If 랜드 is going to 티어, why aren’t we following him? He could be killed, or . . . or. . . . Why are we sitting here?”

모이라인 put a hand on 민’s head. “Because I must be sure,” she said gently. “It is not comfortable being chosen by the Wheel, to be great or to be near greatness. The chosen of the Wheel can only take what comes.”

“I am tired of taking what comes.” 민 scrubbed a hand across her eyes. 페린 thought he saw tears. “랜드 could be dying while we wait.” 모이라인 smoothed 민’s hair; there was a look almost of pity on the 에스 세다이’s face.

페린 sat down on the end of 란’s bed opposite 로이알. The smell of people was thick in the room—people and worry and fear; 로이알 smelled of books and trees as well as worry. It felt like a trap, with the walls around them, and all so close. The burning slivers stank. “How can my dream tell where 랜드 is going?” he asked. “It was my dream.”

“Those who can channel the 하나의 힘,” 모이라인 said quietly, “those who are particularly strong in Spirit, can sometimes force their dreams on others.” She did not stop her soothing of 민. “Especially on those who are—susceptible. I do not believe 랜드 did it on purpose, but the dreams of those touching the True Source can be powerful. For one as strong as he, they could possibly seize an entire village, or perhaps even a city. He knows little of what he does, and even less of how to control it.”

“Then why didn’t you have it, too?” he demanded. “Or 란.” Uno stared straight ahead, looking as if he would rather be anywhere else, and 로이알’s ears wilted. 페린 was too tired and too hungry to care whether he showed proper respect for an 에스 세다이. And too angry, as well, he realized. “Why?”

모이라인 answered calmly. “에스 세다이 learn to shield their dreams. I do it without thinking, when I sleep. 감시자s are given something much the same in the bonding. The Gaidin could not do what they must if the Shadow could steal into their dreams. We are all vulnerable when we sleep, and the Shadow is strong in the night.”

“There’s always something new from you,” 페린 growled. “Can’t you tell us what to expect once in a while, instead of explaining after it happens?” Uno looked as though he was trying to think of a reason to leave.

모이라인 gave 페린 a flat look. “You want me to share a lifetime of knowledge with you in a single afternoon? Or even a single year? I will tell you this. Be wary of dreams, 페린 Aybara. Be very wary of dreams.”

He pulled his eyes away from hers. “I am,” he murmured. “I am.”

After that, silence, and no one seemed to want to break it. 민 sat staring at her crossed ankles, but apparently taking some comfort from 모이라인’s presence. Uno stood against the wall, not looking at anyone. 로이알 forgot himself enough to pull a book from his coat pocket and try to read in the dim light. The wait was long, and far from easy for 페린. *It’s not the Shadow in my dreams I’m afraid of. It’s wolves. I will not let them in. I won’t!*

란 returned, and 모이라인 straightened eagerly. The 감시자 answered the question in her eyes. “Half of them remember dreaming of swords the last four nights running. Some remember a place with great columns, and five say the sword was crystal, or glass. Masema says he saw 랜드 holding it last night.”

“That one would,” 모이라인 said. She rubbed her hands together briskly; she seemed suddenly full of energy. “Now I *am* certain. Though I still wish I knew how he left here unseen. If he has rediscovered some Talent from the 전설의 시대. . . .”

란 looked at Uno, and the one-eyed man shrugged in dismay. “I bloody forgot, with all this flaming talk about bloo—” He cleared his throat, shooting a glance at 모이라인. She looked back expectantly, and he went on. “I mean . . . uh . . . that is, I followed the Lord Dragon’s tracks. There’s another way into that closed valley, now. The . . . the earthquake brought down the far wall. It’s a hard climb, but you can get a horse up it. I found more tracks at the top, and there’s an easy way from there around the mountain.” He let out a long breath when he was done.

“Good,” 모이라인 said. “At least he has not rediscovered how to fly, or make himself invisible, or something else out of legend. We must follow him without delay. Uno, I will give you enough gold to take you and the others as far as Jehannah, and the name of someone there who will see that you get more. The 게알단in are wary of strangers, but if you keep to yourselves, they should not trouble you. Wait there until I send word.”

“But we will go with you,” he protested. “We have all sworn to follow the 용의 환생. I do not see how the few of us can take a fortress that has never fallen, but with the Lord Dragon’s aid, we will do what must be done.”

“So we are ‘the People of the Dragon,’ now.” 페린 laughed mirthlessly. “ ‘The Stone of 티어 will never fall till the People of the Dragon come.’ Have you given us a new name, 모이라인?”

“Watch your tongue, blacksmith,” 란 growled, all ice and stone.

모이라인 gave them both sharp looks, and they fell silent. “Forgive me, Uno,” she said, “but we must travel quickly if we are to have a hope of overtaking him. You are the only 시엔나르an fit enough for a hard ride, and we cannot afford the days the others will need to regain full strength. I will send for you when I can.”

Uno grimaced, but he bowed in acquiescence. At her dismissal, he squared his shoulders and left to tell the others.

“Well, I am going along, whatever you say,” 민 put in firmly.

“You are going to 타르 발론,” 모이라인 told her.

“I am no such thing!”

The 에스 세다이 went on smoothly as if the other woman had not spoken. “The 아미를린 석좌 must be told what has happened, and I cannot count on finding one I can trust who has messenger pigeons. Or that the Amyrlin will see any message I send by pigeon. It is a long journey, and hard. I would not send you alone if there were anyone to send with you, but I will see you have money, and letters to those who might help you on your way. You must ride quickly, though. When your horse tires, buy another—or steal one, if you must—but ride quickly.”

“Let Uno take your message. He’s fit; you said so. I am going after 랜드.”

“Uno has his duties, 민. And do you think a man could simply walk up to the gates of the 백색 탑 and demand an audience with the 아미를린 석좌? Even a king would be made to wait days if he arrived unannounced, and I fear any of the 시엔나르ans would be left kicking their heels for weeks, if not forever. Not to mention that something so unusual would be known to everyone in 타르 발론 before the first sunset. Few women seek audiences with the Amyrlin herself, but it does happen, and it should occasion no great comment. No one must learn even as much as that the 아미를린 석좌 has received a message from me. Her life—and ours—could depend on it. You are the one who must go.”

민 sat there opening and closing her mouth, obviously searching for another argument, but 모이라인 had already gone on. “란, I very much fear we will find more evidence of his passing than I would like, but I will rely on your tracking.” The 감시자 nodded. “페린? 로이알? Will you come with me after 랜드?” From her place against the wall, 민 gave an indignant squawk, but the 에스 세다이 ignored it.

“I will come,” 로이알 said quickly. “랜드 is my friend. And I will admit it; I would not miss anything. For my book, you see.”

페린 was slower to answer. 랜드 was his friend, whatever he had become in the forging. And there was that near certainty of their futures being linked, though he would have avoided that part of it if he could. “It has to be done, doesn’t it?” he said finally. “I will come.”

“Good.” 모이라인 rubbed her hands together again, with the air of someone settling to work. “You must all ready yourselves at once. 랜드 has hours on us. I mean to be well along his trail before midday.”

Slender as she was, the force of her presence herded all of them but 란 toward the door, 로이알 walking stooped over until he was through the doorway. 페린 thought of a goodwife herding geese.

Once outside, 민 hung back for a moment to address 란 with a too-sweet smile. “And is there any message you want carried? To 니나브, perhaps?”

The 감시자 blinked as if caught off guard, like a horse on three legs. “Does everyone know—?” He regained his balance almost immediately. “If there is anything else she needs to hear from me, I will tell her myself.” He closed the door nearly in her face.

“Men!” 민 muttered at the door. “Too blind to see what a stone could see, and too stubborn to be trusted to think for themselves.”

페린 inhaled deeply. Faint smells of death still hung in the valley air, but it was better than the closeness inside. Some better.

“Clean air,” 로이알 sighed. “The smoke was beginning to bother me a little.”

They started down the slope together. Beside the stream below, the 시엔나르ans who could stand were gathered around Uno. From his gestures the one-eyed man was making up for lost time with his cursing.

“How did you two become privileged?” 민 demanded abruptly. “She *asked* you. She didn’t do me the courtesy of asking.”

로이알 shook his head. “I think she asked because she knew what we would answer, 민. 모이라인 seems able to read 페린 and me; she knows what we’ll do. But you are a closed book to her.”

민 appeared only a little mollified. She looked up at them, 페린 head and shoulders taller on one side and 로이알 towering even higher on the other. “Much good it does me. I am still going where she wants as easily as you two little lambs. You were doing well for a while, 페린. Standing up to her like she’d sold you a coat and the seams were popping open.”

“I did stand up to her, didn’t I,” 페린 said wonderingly. He had not really realized he had done that. “It was not so bad as I’d have thought it would be.”

“You were lucky,” 로이알 rumbled. “ ‘To anger an 에스 세다이 is to put your head in a hornet’s nest.’ ”

“로이알,” 민 said, “I need to speak to 페린. Alone. Would you mind?”

“Oh. Of course not.” He lengthened his stride to its normal span and quickly moved ahead of them, pulling his pipe and tabac pouch from a coat pocket.

페린 eyed her warily. She was biting her lip, as if considering what to say. “Do you ever see things about him?” he asked, nodding after the 오지어.

She shook her head. “I think it only works with humans. But I’ve seen things around you that you ought to know about.”

“I’ve told you—”

“Don’t be more thickheaded than you have to be, 페린. Back there, right after you said you’d go. They were not there before. They must have to do with this journey. Or at least with you deciding to go.”

After a moment he said reluctantly, “What did you see?”

“An 아일man in a cage,” she said promptly. “A Tuatha’an with a sword. A falcon and a hawk, perching on your shoulders. Both female, I think. And all the rest, of course. What is always there. Darkness swirling ’round you, and—”

“None of that!” he said quickly. When he was sure she had stopped, he scratched his head, thinking. None of it made any sense to him. “Do you have any idea what it all means? The new things, I mean.”

“No, but they’re important. The things I see always are. Turning points in people’s lives, or what’s fated. It’s always important.” She hesitated for a moment, glancing at him. “One more thing,” she said slowly. “If you meet a woman—the most beautiful woman you’ve ever seen—run!”

페린 blinked. “You saw a beautiful woman? Why should I run from a beautiful woman?”

“Can’t you just take advice?” she said irritably. She kicked at a stone and watched it roll down the slope.

페린 did not like jumping to conclusions—it was one of the reasons some people thought him slow-witted—but he totaled up a number of things 민 had said in the last few days and came to a startling conclusion. He stopped dead, hunting for words. “Uh . . . 민, you know I like you. I like you, but. . . . Uh . . . you sort of remind me of my sisters. I mean, you. . . .” The flow stumbled to a halt as she raised her head to look at him, eyebrows arched. She wore a small smile.

“Why, 페린, you must know that I love you.” She stood there, watching his mouth work, then spoke slowly and carefully. “Like a brother, you great wooden-headed lummox! The arrogance of men never ceases to amaze me. You all think everything has to do with you, and every woman has to desire you.”

페린 felt his face growing hot. “I never. . . . I didn’t. . . .” He cleared his throat. “What did you see about a woman?”

“Just take my advice,” she said, and started down toward the stream again, walking fast. “If you forget all the rest,” she called over her shoulder, “heed that!”

He frowned after her—for once his thoughts seemed to arrange themselves quickly—then caught up in two strides. “It’s 랜드, isn’t it?”

She made a sound in her throat and gave him a sidelong look. She did not slow down, though. “Maybe you aren’t so boneheaded after all,” she muttered. After a moment she added, as if to herself, “I’m bound to him as surely as a stave is bound to the barrel. But I can’t see if he’ll ever love me in return. And I am not the only one.”

“Does 에그웨인 know?” he asked. 랜드 and 에그웨인 had been all but promised since childhood. Everything but kneeling in front of the Women’s Circle of the village to speak the betrothal. He was not sure how far they had drifted from that, if at all.

“She knows,” 민 said curtly. “Much good it does either of us.”

“What about 랜드? Does he know?”

“Oh, of course,” she said bitterly. “I told him, didn’t I? ‘랜드, I did a viewing of you, and it seems I have to fall in love with you. I have to share you, too, and I don’t much like that, but there it is.’ You’re a wooden-headed wonder after all, 페린 Aybara.” She dashed a hand across her eyes angrily. “If I could be with him, I know I could help. Somehow. Light, if he dies, I don’t know if I can stand it.”

페린 shrugged uncomfortably. “Listen, 민. I’ll do what I can to help him.” *However much that is.* “I promise you that. It really is best for you to go to 타르 발론. You’ll be safe there.”

“Safe?” She tasted the word as if wondering what it meant. “You think 타르 발론 is safe?”

“If there’s no safety in 타르 발론, there’s no safety anywhere.”

She sniffed loudly, and in silence they went to join those preparing to leave.
