*Punishments*

Lying on her narrow bed, 에그웨인 frowned up at the flickering shadows cast on the ceiling by her single lamp. She wished she could form some plan of action, or reason out what to expect next. Nothing came. The shadows had more pattern than her thoughts. She could hardly even make herself worry about 맷, yet the shame she felt at that was small, crushed by the walls around her.

It was a stark, windowless room, like all those in the 수련생s’ quarters, small and square and painted white, with pegs on one wall for hanging her belongings, the bed built against a second, and a tiny shelf on a third, where in other days she had kept a few books borrowed from the Tower library. A washstand and a three-legged stool completed the furnishings. The floorboards were almost white from scrubbing. She had done that task, on hands and knees, every day she had lived there, in addition to her other chores and lessons. Novices lived simply, whether they were innkeepers’ daughters or the Daughter-Heir of 안도르.

She wore the plain white dress of a 수련생 again—even her belt and pouch were white—but she felt no joy at having rid herself of the hated gray. Her room had become too much of a prison cell. *What if they mean to keep me here. In this room. Like a cell. Like a collar and. . . .*

She glanced at the door—the dark 허락받은 자 would still be standing guard on the other side, she knew—and rolled close to the white plastered wall. Just above the mattress was a small hole, almost invisible unless you knew where to look, drilled through into the next room by 수련생s long ago. 에그웨인 kept her voice to a whisper.

“엘레인?” There was no answer. “엘레인? Are you asleep?”

“How could I sleep?” came 엘레인’s reply, a reedy whisper through the hole. “I thought we might be in some trouble, but I did not expect this. 에그웨인, what are they going to do to us?”

에그웨인 had no answer, and her guesses were not of the sort she wanted to voice aloud. She did not even want to think of them. “I actually thought we might be heroes, 엘레인. We brought back the 발레르의 뿔 safely. We discovered Liandrin is 흑색 아자.” Her voice skipped on that. 에스 세다이 had always denied the existence of a 흑색 아자, an 아자 that served the 어둠의 존재, and were known to become angry with anyone who even suggested it was real. *But we know it’s real.* “We should be heroes, 엘레인.”

“ ‘Should and would build no bridges,’ ” 엘레인 said. “Light, I used to hate it when Mother said that to me, but it’s true. Verin said we mustn’t speak of the Horn, or Liandrin, to anyone but her or the 아미를린 석좌. I do not think any of this will work out the way we thought. It is not fair. We’ve been through so much; you’ve been through so much. It just is not fair.”

“Verin says. 모이라인 says. I know why people think 에스 세다이 are puppetmasters. I can almost feel the strings on my arms and legs. Whatever they do, it will be what they decide is good for the 백색 탑, not what is good or fair for us.”

“But you still want to be 에스 세다이. Don’t you?”

에그웨인 hesitated, but there was never any real question as to her answer. “Yes,” she said. “I still do. It is the only way we will ever be safe. But I will tell you this. I’ll not let myself be stilled.” That was a new thought, voiced as soon as it came to her, but she realized she did not want to take it back. *Give up touching the True Source?* She could sense it there, even now, the glow just over her shoulder, the shining just out of sight. She resisted the desire to reach out to it. *Give up being filled with the 하나의 힘, feeling more alive than I ever have before? I won’t!* “Not without a fight.”

There was a long silence from the other side of the wall. “How could you stop it? You may be as strong as any of them, now, but neither one of us knows enough yet to stop even one 에스 세다이 from shielding us from the Source, and there are dozens of them here.”

에그웨인 considered. Finally she said, “I could run away. Really run away, this time.”

“They would come after us, 에그웨인. I’m sure they would. Once you show any ability at all, they don’t let you go until you’ve learned enough not to kill yourself. Or just die from it.”

“I am not a simple village girl anymore. I have seen something of the world. I can keep out of 에스 세다이 hands if I want to.” She was trying to convince herself as much as 엘레인. *And what if I don’t know enough, yet? Enough about the world, enough about the Power? What if just channeling can still kill me?* She refused to think of that. *So much I have to learn yet. I won’t let them stop me.*

“My mother might protect us,” 엘레인 said, “if what that Whitecloak said is true. I never thought I would hope something like that was the truth. But if it isn’t, Mother is just as likely to send us both back in chains. Will you teach me how to live in a village?”

에그웨인 blinked at the wall. “You will come with me? If it comes to that, I mean?”

There was another long silence, then a faint whisper. “I do not want to be stilled, 에그웨인. I will not be. I will not be!”

The door swung open, crashing against the wall, and 에그웨인 sat up with a start. She heard the bang of a door from the other side of the wall. Faolain stepped into 에그웨인’s room, smiling as her eyes went to the tiny hole. Similar holes joined most of the 수련생 rooms; any woman who had been a 수련생 knew of them.

“Whispering with your friend, eh?” the curly-haired 허락받은 자 said with surprising warmth. “Well, it grows lonely, waiting by yourself. Did you have a nice chat?”

에그웨인 opened her mouth, then closed it again hastily. She could answer 에스 세다이, 셰리암 had said. No one else. She regarded the 허락받은 자 with a level expression and waited.

The false sympathy slid off Faolain’s face like water running off a roof. “On your feet. The Amyrlin’s not to be kept waiting by the likes of you. You are lucky I did not come in in time to hear you. Move!”

Novices were supposed to obey the 허락받은 자 almost as quickly as they obeyed 에스 세다이, but 에그웨인 got to her feet slowly, and took as much time as she dared in smoothing her dress. She gave Faolain a small curtsy and a tiny smile. The scowl that rolled across the 허락받은 자’s face made 에그웨인’s smile grow before she remembered to rein it in; there was no point in pushing Faolain too far. Holding herself straight, pretending her knees were not shaking, she preceded the 허락받은 자 out of the room.

엘레인 was already waiting outside with the apple-cheeked 허락받은 자, looking fiercely determined to be brave. Somehow, she managed to give the impression that the 허락받은 자 was a handmaid carrying her gloves. 에그웨인 hoped that she herself was doing half so well.

The railed galleries of the 수련생s’ quarters rose tier on tier above, in a hollow column, and fell as many below, to the Novices’ Court. There were no other women in sight. Even if every 수련생 in the Tower had been there, though, less than a quarter of the rooms would have been filled. The four of them walked ’round the empty galleries and down the spiraling ramps in silence; none could bear to have the sounds of voices emphasize the emptiness.

에그웨인 had never before been into the part of the Tower where the Amyrlin had her rooms. The corridors there were wide enough for a wagon to pass down easily, and taller than they were wide. Colorful tapestries hung on the walls, tapestries in a dozen styles, of floral designs and forest scenes, of heroic deeds and intricate patterns, some so old they looked as if they might break if handled. Their shoes made loud clicks on diamond-shaped floor tiles that repeated the colors of the seven 아자s.

There were few other women in evidence—an 에스 세다이 now and then, sweeping majestically along with no time to notice 허락받은 자 or 수련생s; five or six 허락받은 자 hurrying self-importantly about their tasks or studies; a sprinkling of serving women with trays, or mops, or armfuls of sheets or towels; a few 수련생s moving on errands even more quickly than the servants.

니나브 and her slim-necked escort, Theodrin, joined them. Neither spoke. 니나브 wore an 허락받은 자’s dress, now, white with the seven colored bands at the hem, but her belt and pouch were her own. She gave 에그웨인 and 엘레인 each a reassuring smile and a hug—에그웨인 was so relieved to see another friendly face that she returned the hug with barely a thought that 니나브 was behaving as if she were comforting children—but as they walked on, 니나브 gave her thick braid a sharp tug from time to time, too.

Very few men came into that part of the Tower, and 에그웨인 saw only two: 감시자s walking side by side in conversation, one with his sword on his hip, the other with his on his back. One was short and slender, even slight, the other almost as wide as he was tall, yet both moved with a dangerous grace. The color-shifting 감시자 cloaks made them queasy-making to watch for long, parts of them sometimes seeming to fade into the walls beyond. She saw 니나브 looking at them, and shook her head. *She has to do something about 란. If any of us can do anything about anyone after today.*

The antechamber of the 아미를린 석좌’s study was grand enough for any palace, though the chairs scattered about for those who might wait were plain, but 에그웨인 had eyes only for 리안 Sedai. The Keeper wore her narrow stole of office, blue to show she had been raised from the 청색 아자, and her face could have been carved from smooth, brownish stone. There was no one else there.

“Did they give any trouble?” The Keeper’s clipped way of talking gave no hint now of either anger or sympathy.

“No, 에스 세다이,” Theodrin and the apple-cheeked 허락받은 자 said together.

“This one had to be pulled by the scruff of her neck, 에스 세다이,” Faolain said, indicating 에그웨인. The 허락받은 자 sounded indignant. “She balks as if she has forgotten what the discipline of the 백색 탑 is.”

“To lead,” 리안 said, “is neither to push nor to pull. Go to Marris Sedai, Faolain, and ask her to allow you to contemplate on this while raking the paths in the Spring Garden.” She dismissed Faolain and the other two 허락받은 자, and they dropped deep curtsies. From the depth of hers, Faolain shot a furious look at 에그웨인.

The Keeper paid no attention to the 허락받은 자’s leaving. Instead, she studied the remaining women, tapping a forefinger against her lips, till 에그웨인 had the feeling they had all been measured to the inch and weighed to the ounce. 니나브’s eyes took on a dangerous sparkle, and she had a tight grip on her braid.

Finally 리안 raised a hand toward the doors to the Amyrlin’s study. 거대한 뱀 bit its own tail, a pace across, on the dark wood of each. “Enter,” she said.

니나브 stepped forward promptly and opened one of the doors. That was enough to get 에그웨인 moving. 엘레인 held her hand tightly, and she gripped 엘레인’s just as hard. 리안 followed them in and took a place to one side, halfway between the three of them and the table in the center of the room.

The 아미를린 석좌 sat behind the table, examining papers. She did not look up. Once 니나브 opened her mouth, but closed it again, at a sharp look from the Keeper. The three of them stood in a line in front of the Amyrlin’s table and waited. 에그웨인 tried not to fidget. Long minutes went by—it seemed like hours—before the Amyrlin raised her head, but when those blue eyes fixed them each in turn, 에그웨인 decided she could have waited longer. The Amyrlin’s gaze was like two icicles boring into her heart. The room was cool, but a trickle of sweat began to run down her back.

“So!” the Amyrlin said finally. “Our runaways return.”

“We did not run away, Mother.” 니나브 was obviously straining for calm, but her voice shook with emotion. Anger, 에그웨인 knew. That strong will was all too often accompanied by anger. “Liandrin told us we were to go with her, and—” The loud crack of the Amyrlin’s hand slapping the table cut her off.

“Do not invoke Liandrin’s name here, child!” the Amyrlin snapped. 리안 watched them with a stern serenity.

“Mother, Liandrin is 흑색 아자,” 엘레인 burst out.

“That is known, child. Suspected, at least, and as good as known. Liandrin left the Tower some months ago, and twelve other—*women*—went with her. None has been seen since. Before they left, they tried to break into the storeroom where the *angreal* and *sa’angreal* are kept, and did manage to enter that where the smaller *ter’angreal* are stored. They stole a number of those, including several we do not know the use of.”

니나브 stared at the Amyrlin in horror, and 엘레인 suddenly rubbed her arms as if she were cold. 에그웨인 knew she was shivering, too. Many times she had imagined returning to confront Liandrin and accuse her, to see her condemned to some punishment—except that she had never managed to imagine any punishment strong enough to suit that doll-faced 에스 세다이’s crimes. She had even pictured returning to find Liandrin already fled—in terror of her return, it was usually. But she had never imagined anything like this. If Liandrin and the others—she had not really wanted to believe there were others—had stolen those remnants of the 전설의 시대, there was no telling what they could do with them. *Thank the Light they did not get any sa’angreal*, she thought. The other was bad enough.

*Sa’angreal* were like *angreal*, allowing an 에스 세다이 to channel more of the Power than she safely could unaided, but far more powerful than *angreal*, and rare. *Ter’angreal* were something different. Existing in greater numbers than either *angreal* or *sa’angreal*, though still not common, they used the 하나의 힘 rather than helping to channel it, and no one truly understood them. Many would work only for someone who could channel, needing the actual channeling of the Power, while others did what they did for anyone. Where all the *angreal* and *sa’angreal* 에그웨인 had ever heard of were small, *ter’angreal* could seemingly be any size. Each had apparently been made for a specific purpose by those 에스 세다이 of three thousand years ago, to do a certain thing, and 에스 세다이 since had died trying to learn what; died, or had the ability to channel burned out of them. There were sisters of the 갈색 아자 who had made *ter’angreal* their life’s study.

Some were in use, if likely not for the purposes they had been made. The stout white rod that the 허락받은 자 held while taking the 세 가지 맹세 on being raised to 에스 세다이 was a *ter’angreal*, binding them to the oaths as surely as if they had been bred in the bone. Another *ter’angreal* was the site of the final test before a 수련생 was raised to the 허락받은 자. There were others, including many no one could make work at all, and many others that seemed to have no practical use.

*Why did they take things no one knows how to use?* 에그웨인 wondered. *Or maybe the 흑색 아자* does *know.* That possibility made her stomach churn. That might be as bad as *sa’angreal* in Darkfriend hands.

“Theft,” the Amyrlin went on in tones as cold as her eyes, “was the least of what they did. Three sisters died that night, as well as two 감시자s, seven guards, and nine of the servants. When there are fish heads and blood in the water, you don’t need to see the silverpike to know they are there.”

The Amyrlin barked a mirthless laugh. “You think so, do you, child? It may be your salvation that no one in the Tower but Verin, 리안, and I even suspects you had anything to do with Liandrin. If that were known, much less the little demonstration you put on for the 백의단—no need to look so surprised; Verin told me everything—if it were known you had gone off with Liandrin, the Hall might very well vote for stilling the three of you before you could take a breath.”

“That is not fair!” 니나브 said. 리안 stirred, but 니나브 went on. “It is not right! It—!”

The Amyrlin stood up. That was all, but it cut 니나브 short.

에그웨인 thought she was wise to keep quiet. She had always believed 니나브 was as strong, as strong-willed, as anyone could be. Until she met the woman wearing the striped stole. *Please keep your temper, 니나브. We might as well be children—babes—facing our mother, and this Mother can do far worse than beat us.*

It seemed to her a way out was being offered in what the Amyrlin had said, but she was not sure what way. “Mother, forgive me for speaking, but what do you intend to do to us?”

“Do to you, child? I intend to punish you and 엘레인 for leaving the Tower without permission, and 니나브 for leaving the city without permission. First, you will each be called to 셰리암 Sedai’s study, where I’ve told her to switch you till you wish you had a cushion to sit on for the next week. I have already had this announced to the 수련생s and the 허락받은 자.”

에그웨인 blinked in surprise. 엘레인 gave an audible grunt, stiffened her back, and muttered something under her breath. 니나브 was the only one who seemed to take it without shock. Punishment, whether extra labors or something else, was always between the 수련생 감독관 and whoever was called to her. Those were usually 수련생s, but included the 허락받은 자 who stepped far enough beyond the bounds. *셰리암* always *keeps it between you and her*, 에그웨인 thought bleakly. *She* can’t *have told everyone. “The announcement is part of the punishment, of course,” the Amyrlin went on, as if she had read 에그웨인’s mind. “I have also had it announced that you are all three assigned to the kitchens, to work with the scullions, until further notice. “And you, 엘레인?” the Amyrlin said. “The Daughter-Heir of 안도르 is used to gentler treatment.”

“I want to be 에스 세다이, Mother,” 엘레인 said in a firm voice.

The Amyrlin fingered a paper in front of her on the table and seemed to study it for a moment. When she raised her head, her smile was not at all pleasant. “If any of you had been silly enough to answer otherwise, I had something to add to your tally that would have had you cursing your mother for ever letting your father steal that first kiss. 에그웨인 found herself offering silent thanks. A prickle ran over her skin as the Amyrlin continued.

니나브 surprised 에그웨인 by saying, “I know we have done . . . things . . . we should not have, Mother. I assure you, we will do our best to live as if we had taken the 세 가지 맹세.”

The Amyrlin grunted. “See that you do,” she said dryly. “If I could, I’d put the 맹세 막대 in your hands tonight, but as that is reserved for being raised to 에스 세다이, I must trust to your good sense—if you have any—to keep you whole. As it is, you, 에그웨인, and you, 엘레인, are to be raised to the 허락받은 자.”

엘레인 gasped, and 에그웨인 stammered a shocked, “Thank you, Mother.” 리안 shifted where she stood. 에그웨인 did not think the Keeper looked best pleased. Not surprised—she had obviously known it was coming—but not pleased, either.

“Do not thank me. Your abilities have gone too far for you to remain 수련생s. The Amyrlin’s smile was even grimmer than her last. “As well that you do, child, because I have no intention of letting 모르가세 have you. 엘레인 grimaced at the mention of the 수련생 감독관’s study, but she drew herself up as 리안 came to her side. “As you command, Mother,” she said formally, lowering herself in a perfect curtsy, skirts sweeping wide, “so shall I obey.” She followed 리안 out with her head held high.

*The 회색 인간*

Outside the 아미를린 석좌’s study, 에그웨인 and 니나브 found the corridors empty except for an occasional serving woman, hurrying about her duties on soft-slippered feet. 에그웨인 was grateful for their presence. The halls suddenly seemed like caverns, for all the tapestries and stonework. Dangerous caverns.

니나브 accompanied her all the way back to the 수련생s’ quarters, not turning aside to the 허락받은 자’s quarters. The galleries were still empty, and they met no one as they climbed the spiraling ramps.

Haste, and images that kept intruding on the emptiness, images of her head being ripped apart like a rotten melon by a heavy quarrel that went on to bury itself in 니나브. She took a deep breath and tried again, and finally the rose floated in nothingness, opened to the True Source, and the Power filled her.

I’ll put a lightning bolt through him!” She could feel it building, pressing on her to loose it. “It *is* a man, isn’t it?” She could not imagine a man coming into the 수련생s’ quarters, but it was impossible to picture a woman carrying a crossbow through the Tower.

“I don’t know.” Quiet anger filled 니나브’s voice; her anger was always at its worst when she grew quiet with it. “I thought I saw—Yes! There!” 에그웨인 felt the Power pulse in the other woman, and then 니나브 was unhurriedly getting to her feet, brushing at her dress as if there were nothing more to worry about.

에그웨인 stared at her. “What? What did you do? 니나브?”

“ ‘Of the Five Powers,’ ” 니나브 said in a lecturing tone, faintly mocking, “ ‘Air, sometimes called Wind, is thought by many to be of the least use. This is far from true.’ ” She finished with a tight laugh. “I told you there were other ways to defend ourselves. I used Air, to hold him with air. If it is a he; I could not see him clearly. A trick the Amyrlin showed me once, though I doubt she expected me to see how it was done. Well, are you going to lie there all day?”

에그웨인 scrambled up to hurry after her around the gallery. Before long a man did come into sight around the curve, dressed in plain brown breeches and coat. He stood facing the other way, balanced on the ball of one foot, with the other hanging in midair as if he had been caught in the middle of running. The man would feel as if he were buried in thick jelly, yet it was nothing but air stiffened around him. 에그웨인 remembered the Amyrlin’s trick, too, but she did not think she could duplicate it. 니나브 only had to see a thing done once to know how to do it herself. When she could manage to channel at all, of course.

They came closer, and 에그웨인’s melding with the Power vanished in shock. The hilt of a dagger stood out from the man’s chest. His face sagged, and death had already filmed his half-closed eyes. He crumpled to the gallery floor as 니나브 loosed the trap that had held him.

He was an average-appearing man, of average height and average build, with features so ordinary 에그웨인 did not think she would have noticed him in a group of three. She only studied him a moment, though, before realizing that something was missing. A crossbow.

She gave a start and looked about wildly. “There had to be another one, 니나브. Somebody took the crossbow. And somebody stabbed him. He could be out there ready to shoot at us again.”
“Calm yourself,” 니나브 said, but she peered both ways along the gallery, jerking at her braid. “Just be calm, and we will figure out what to—” Her words cut off at the sound of steps on the ramp leading up to their level.

에그웨인’s heart pounded, seemingly in her throat. Eyes fastened on the head of the ramp, she desperately strove to touch *세다르* again, but for her that required calm, and her heartbeats shattered calm.

셰리암 Sedai stopped at the top of the ramp, frowning at what she saw. “What in the name of the Light has happened here?” She hurried forward, her serenity gone for once.

“We found him,” 니나브 said as the 수련생 감독관 knelt beside the corpse.

셰리암 put a hand to the man’s chest, and jerked it back twice as fast, hissing. Steeling herself visibly, she touched him again, and maintained the Touch longer. “Dead,” she muttered. “As dead as it is possible to be, and more.” When she straightened, she pulled a handkerchief from her sleeve and wiped her fingers. “You found him? Here? Like this?”

에그웨인 nodded, sure that if she spoke, 셰리암 would hear the lie in her voice.

“We did,” 니나브 said firmly.

셰리암 shook her head. “A man—a dead man, at that!—in the 수련생s’ quarters would be scandal enough, but this . . . !”

“What makes him different?” 니나브 asked. “And how could he be *more* than dead?”

셰리암 took a deep breath, and gave them each a searching look. “He is one of the 영혼 없는 자. A 회색 인간.” Absently, she wiped her fingers again, her eyes going back to the body. Worried eyes.

“The 영혼 없는 자?” 에그웨인 said, a tremor in her voice, at the same time that 니나브 said, “A 회색 인간?”

셰리암 glanced at them, a look as penetrating as it was brief. “Not a part of your studies, yet, but you seem to have gone beyond the rules in a great many ways. And considering you found this. . . .” She gestured to the corpse. “The 영혼 없는 자, the Gray Men, give up their souls to serve the 어둠의 존재 as assassins. They are not really alive, after that. Not quite dead, but not truly alive. And despite the name, some Gray Men are women. A very few. Even among 어둠의 친구들, only a handful of women are stupid enough to make that sacrifice. You can look right at them and hardly notice them, until it is too late. He was as much as dead while he walked. Now, only my eyes tell me that what is lying there ever lived at all.” She gave them another long look. “No 회색 인간 has dared enter 타르 발론 since the 트롤록 전쟁.”

“What will you do?” 에그웨인 asked. 셰리암’s brows rose, and she quickly added, “If I may ask, 셰리암 Sedai.”

The 에스 세다이 hesitated. “I suppose you may, since you had the bad luck to find him. It will be up to the 아미를린 석좌, but with everything that has happened, I believe she will want to keep this as quiet as is possible. We do not need more rumors. You will speak of this to none but me, or to the Amyrlin, should she mention it first.”

“Yes, 에스 세다이,” 에그웨인 said fervently. 니나브’s voice was cooler.

셰리암 appeared to take their obedience for granted. She gave no sign of having heard them. Her attention was all on the dead man. The 회색 인간. The 영혼 없는 자. “There will be no hiding the fact that a man was killed here.” The glow of the 하나의 힘 suddenly surrounded her, and just as abruptly, a long, low dome covered the body on the floor, grayish and so opaque that it was hard to see there was a body under it. “But this will keep anyone else from touching him who can discover his nature. I must have this removed before the 수련생s come back.”

Her tilted green eyes regarded them as if she had just remembered their presence. “You two go, now. To your room, I think, 니나브. Considering what you are already facing, if it became known you were involved in this, even on the edge of it. . . . Go.”

에그웨인 curtsied, and tugged at 니나브’s sleeve, but 니나브 said, “Why did you come up here, 셰리암 Sedai?”

For a moment 셰리암 looked startled, but on the instant she frowned. Fists on her hips, she regarded 니나브 with all the firmness of her office. “Does the 수련생 감독관 now need an excuse for coming to the 수련생s’ quarters, 허락받은 자?” she said softly. “Do 허락받은 자 now question 에스 세다이? The Amyrlin means to make something of you two, but whether she does or not, I will teach you manners, at least. Now, the pair of you, go, before I haul you both down to my study, and not for the appointment the 아미를린 석좌 has already set for you.”

A sudden thought came to 에그웨인. “Forgive me, 셰리암 Sedai,” she said quickly, “but I must fetch my cloak. I feel cold.” She rushed away, around the gallery before the 에스 세다이 could speak.

If 셰리암 found that crossbow bolt in front of her door, there would be too many questions. No pretending they had only found the man, that he had no connection to her, then. But when she reached the door to her room, the heavy bolt was gone. Only the jagged chip in the stone beside the door said it had ever been there.

에그웨인’s skin crawled. *How could anyone take it without one of us seeing. . . . Another 회색 인간!* She had embraced *세다르* before she knew it, only the sweet flow of the Power inside her telling her what she had done. Even so, it was one of the hardest things she had ever done, opening that door and going into her room. There was no one there. She snatched the white cloak off its peg and ran out, anyway, and she did not release *세다르* until she was halfway back to the others.

Something more had passed between the women while she was gone. 니나브 was attempting to appear meek, and succeeding only in looking as if she had a sour stomach. 셰리암 had her fists on her hips and was tapping her foot irritably, and the stare she was giving 니나브, like green millstones ready to start grinding barley flour, took in 에그웨인 equally.

“Forgive me, 셰리암 Sedai,” she said hastily, dropping a curtsy and settling her cloak on her shoulders at the same time. “This . . . finding a dead man—a . . . a 회색 인간!—it made me cold. If we may go now?”

At 셰리암’s tight nod of dismissal, 니나브 made a bare curtsy. 에그웨인 seized her arm and hustled her away.

“Are you trying to *make* more trouble for us?” she demanded when they were two levels down. And safely out of earshot of 셰리암, she hoped. “What else did you say to her, to make her glare like that? More questions, I suppose? I hope you learned something worth making her mad at us.”

“She would not say anything,” 니나브 muttered. “We must ask questions if we are to do any good, 에그웨인. We will have to take a few chances, or we’ll never learn anything.”

에그웨인 sighed. “Well, be a little more circumspect.” From the set of 니나브’s face, the other woman had no intention of going easy or avoiding risks. 에그웨인 sighed again. “The crossbow bolt was gone, 니나브. It must have been another 회색 인간 who took it.”

“So that is why you. . . . Light!” 니나브 frowned and gave a sharp tug to her braid.

After a time 에그웨인 said, “What was that she did to cover the . . . the body?” She did not want to think of it as a 회색 인간; that reminded her there was another one out there. She did not want to think of anything at all, right then.

“Air,” 니나브 replied. “She used Air. A neat trick, and I think I see how to make something useful with it.”

The use of the 하나의 힘 was divided into the Five Powers: Earth, Air, Fire, Water, and Spirit. Different Talents required different combinations of the Five Powers. “I don’t understand some of the ways the Five Powers are combined. Take 치유. I can see why it requires Spirit, and maybe Air, but why Water?”

니나브 rounded on her. “What are you babbling about? Have you forgotten what we’re doing?” She looked around. They had reached the 허락받은 자’s quarters, a stack of galleries lower than the 수련생s’ quarters, surrounding a garden rather than a court. There was no one in sight except for another 허락받은 자, hurrying along on another level, but she lowered her voice. “Have you forgotten the 흑색 아자?”

“I am trying to forget it,” 에그웨인 said fiercely. “For a little while, anyway. I am trying to forget that we just left a dead man. I’m trying to forget that he almost killed me, and that he has a companion who might try it again.” She touched her ear; the drop of blood had dried, but the nick still hurt. “We are lucky we aren’t both dead right now.”

니나브’s face softened, but when she spoke her voice held something of the time when she had been the Wisdom of Emond’s Field, saying words that had to be said for someone’s own good. “Remember that body, 에그웨인. Remember that he tried to kill you. Kill us. Remember the 흑색 아자. Remember them all the time. Because if you forget, just once, the next time, it may be you lying dead.”

“I know,” 에그웨인 sighed. “But I do not have to like it.”

“Did you notice what 셰리암 did not mention?”

“No. What?”

“She never wondered who stabbed him. Now, come on. My room is just down here, and you can put your feet up while we talk.”

CHAPTER 16

![](images/00635.jpg)

*Hunters Three*

니나브’s room was considerably larger than the 수련생 rooms. She had a real bed, not one built into the wall, two ladder-back armchairs instead of a stool, and a wardrobe for her clothes. The furnishings were all plain, suitable for a middling successful farmer’s house, but compared to the 수련생s, the 허락받은 자 lived in luxury. There was even a small rug, woven with scrolls of yellow and red on blue. The room was not empty when 에그웨인 and 니나브 entered.

엘레인 stood in front of the fireplace, arms crossed beneath her breasts and eyes red at least partly from anger. Two tall young men sprawled in the chairs, all arms and legs. One, with his dark green coat undone to show a snowy shirt, shared 엘레인’s blue eyes and red-gold hair, and his grinning face marked him plainly as her brother. The other, 니나브’s age and with his gray coat neatly buttoned, was slender and dark of hair and eye. He rose, all sure confidence and lithely muscled grace, when 에그웨인 and 니나브 came in. He was, 에그웨인 thought not for the first time, the most handsome man she had ever seen. His name was 갈라드.

“It is good to see you again,” he said, taking her hand. “I have worried much over you. We have worried much.”

Her pulse quickened, and she took back her hand before he should feel it. “Thank you, 갈라드,” she murmured. *Light, but he’s beautiful.* She told herself to stop thinking that way. It was not easy. She found herself smoothing her dress, wishing he were seeing her in silk instead of this plain white wool, perhaps even one of those 도마니 dresses 민 had told her of, the ones that clung and seemed so thin you thought they must be transparent even though they were not. She flushed furiously and banished the image from her mind, willed him to look away from her face. It did not help that half the women in the Tower, from scullery maids to 에스 세다이 themselves, looked at him as if they had the same thoughts. It did not help that his smile seemed for her alone. In fact, his smile made it worse. *Light, if he even suspected what I was thinking, I’d die!*

The golden-haired young man leaned forward in his chair. “The question is, where have you been? 엘레인 dodges my questions as if she has a pocket full of figs and doesn’t want me to have any.”

“I have told you, 가윈,” 엘레인 said in a tight voice, “it is none of your affair. I came here,” she added to 니나브, “because I did not want to be alone. They saw me, and followed. They would not take no for an answer.”

“Wouldn’t they,” 니나브 said flatly.

“But it is our affair, sister,” 갈라드 said. “Your safety is very much our affair.” He looked at 에그웨인, and she felt her heart jump. “The safety of all of you is very important to me. To us.”

“I am not your sister,” 엘레인 snapped.

“If you want company,” 가윈 told 엘레인 with a smile, “we can do as well as any. And after what we went through just to be here, we deserve some explanation of where you’ve been. I would rather let 갈라드 thump me all over the practice yard all day than face Mother again for a single minute. I’d rather have Coulin mad at me.” Coulin was Master of Arms, and kept a tight discipline among the young men who came to train at the 백색 탑 whether they aspired to become 감시자s or just to learn from them.

“Deny the connection if you will,” 갈라드 told 엘레인 gravely, “but it is still there. And Mother put your safety in our hands.”

가윈 grimaced. “She’ll have our hides, 엘레인, if anything happens to you. We had to talk fast, or she’d have hauled us back home with her. I have never heard of a queen sending her own sons to the headsman, but Mother sounded ready to make an exception if we don’t bring you home safely.”

“I am sure,” 엘레인 said, “that your fast talk was all for me. None of it was meant to let you stay here studying with the 감시자s.” 가윈’s face reddened.

“Your safety was our first concern.” 갈라드 sounded as if he meant it, and 에그웨인 was sure he did. “We managed to convince Mother that if you did return here, you would need someone to look after you.”

“Look after me!” 엘레인 exclaimed, but 갈라드 went on smoothly.

“The 백색 탑 has become a dangerous place. There have been deaths—murders—with no real explanations. Even some 에스 세다이 have been killed, though they have tried to keep that quiet. And I have heard rumors of the 흑색 아자, spoken in the Tower itself. By Mother’s command, when it is safe for you to leave your training, we are to return you to Caemlyn.”

For answer, 엘레인 lifted her chin and half turned away from him.

가윈 ran a hand through his hair in frustration. “Light, 니나브, 갈라드 and I are not villains. All we want to do is help. We would do it anyway, but Mother commanded it, so there’s no chance of you talking us out of it.”

“모르가세’s commands carry no weight in 타르 발론,” 니나브 said in a level voice. “As for your offer of help, I will remember it. Should we need help, you will be among the first to hear of it. For now, I wish you to leave.” She gestured pointedly to the door, but he ignored her.

“That is all very well, but Mother will want to know 엘레인 has come back. And why she ran off without a word, and what she was doing these months. Light, 엘레인! The whole Tower was in a turmoil. Mother was half-crazed with fear. I thought she’d tear the Tower down with her bare hands.” 엘레인’s face took on a measure of guilt, and 가윈 pressed his advantage. “You owe her that much, 엘레인. You owe me that much. Burn me, you’re being as stubborn as stone. You’ve been gone for months, and all I know about it is that you’ve run afoul of 셰리암. And the only reasons I know that much are because you’ve been crying and you won’t sit down.” 엘레인’s indignant stare said he had squandered whatever momentary advantage he might have had.

“Enough,” 니나브 said. 갈라드 and 가윈 opened their mouths. She raised her voice. “I said enough!” She glared at them until it was clear their silence would hold, then went on. “엘레인 *owes* the two of you nothing. Since she chooses to tell you nothing, that is that. Now, this is my room, not the common room of an inn, and I want you out of it.”

“But, 엘레인—” 가윈 began at the same time that 갈라드 said, “We only want—”

니나브 spoke loudly enough to drown them out. “I doubt you asked permission to enter the 허락받은 자’s quarters.” They stared at her, looking surprised. “I thought not. You will be out of my room, out of my sight, before I count three, or I will write a note to the Master of Arms about this. Coulin Gaidin has a much stronger arm than 셰리암 Sedai, and you may be assured that I will be there to see he makes a proper job of it.”

“니나브, you wouldn’t—” 가윈 began worriedly, but 갈라드 motioned him to silence and stepped closer to 니나브.

Her face kept its stern expression, but she unconsciously smoothed the front of her dress as he smiled down at her. 에그웨인 was not surprised. She did not think she had met a woman outside the 적색 아자 who would not be affected by 갈라드’s smile.

“I apologize, 니나브, for our forcing ourselves on you unwanted,” he said smoothly. “We will go, of course. But remember that we are here if you need us. And whatever caused you to run away, we can help with that, as well.”

니나브 returned his smile. “One,” she said.

갈라드 blinked, his smile fading. Calmly, he turned to 에그웨인. 가윈 got up and started for the door. “에그웨인,” 갈라드 said, “you know that you, especially, can call on me at any time, for anything. I hope you know that.”

“Two,” 니나브 said.

갈라드 gave her an irritated look. “We will talk again,” he told 에그웨인, bowing over her hand. With a last smile, he took an unhurried step toward the door.

“Thrrrrrrrrr”—가윈 darted through the door, and even 갈라드’s graceful stride quickened markedly—“ree,” 니나브 finished as the door banged shut behind them.

엘레인 clapped her hands delightedly. “Oh, well done,” she said. “Very well done. I did not even know men were forbidden the 허락받은 자’s quarters, too.”

“They aren’t,” 니나브 said dryly, “but those louts did not know it, either.” 엘레인 clapped her hands again and laughed. “I’d have let them just leave,” 니나브 added, “if 갈라드 had not made such a show of taking his time about it. That young man has too fair a face for his own good.” 에그웨인 almost laughed at that; 갈라드 was no more than a year younger that 니나브, if that, and 니나브 was straightening her dress again.

“갈라드!” 엘레인 sniffed. “He’ll bother us again, and I do not know whether your trick will work more than once. He does what he sees as right no matter who it hurts, even himself.”

“Then I will think of something else,” 니나브 said. “We can’t afford to have them looking over our shoulders all the time. 엘레인, if you wish, I can make a salve that will soothe you.”

엘레인 shook her head, then lay down across the bed with her chin in her hands. “If 셰리암 found out, we would no doubt both have yet another visit to her study to look forward to. You have not said very much, 에그웨인. Cat caught your tongue?” Her expression became grimmer. “Or perhaps 갈라드 has?”

에그웨인 blushed in spite of herself. “I simply did not choose to argue with them,” she said in as dignified a tone as she could manage.

“Of course,” 엘레인 said grudgingly. “I will admit that 갈라드 is good-looking. But he is horrid, too. He *always* does right, as he sees it I know that does not sound horrid, but it is. He has never disobeyed Mother, not in the smallest thing that I know of. He will not tell a lie, even a small one, or break a rule. If he turns you in for breaking one, there isn’t the slightest spite in it—he seems sad you could not live up to his standards, if anything—but that doesn’t change the fact that he *will* turn you in.”

“That sounds—uncomfortable,” 에그웨인 said carefully, “but not horrid. I cannot imagine 갈라드 doing anything horrid.”

엘레인 shook her head, as if in disbelief that 에그웨인 found it so hard to see what was clear to her. “If you want to pay attention to someone, try 가윈. He is nice enough—most of the time—and he’s besotted with you.”

“가윈! He has never looked at me twice.”

“Of course not, you fool, the way you stare at 갈라드 until your eyes look ready to fall out of your face.” 에그웨인’s cheeks felt hot, but she was afraid it might well be true. “갈라드 saved his life when 가윈 was a child,” 엘레인 went on. “가윈 will never admit he is interested in a woman if 갈라드 is interested in her, but I have heard him talk about you, and I know. He never could hide things from me.”

“That is nice to know,” 에그웨인 said, then laughed at 엘레인’s grin. “Perhaps I can get him to say some of those things to me instead of you.”

“You could choose 녹색 아자, you know. Green sisters sometimes marry. 가윈 truly is besotted, and you would be good for him. Besides, I would like to have you for a sister.”

“If you two are finished with girlish chatter,” 니나브 cut in, “there are important matters to talk about.”

“Yes,” 엘레인 said, “such as what the 아미를린 석좌 had to say to you after I left.”

“I would rather not talk about that,” 에그웨인 said awkwardly. She did not like lying to 엘레인. “She did not say anything that was pleasant.”

엘레인 gave a sniff of disbelief. “Most people think I get off easier than the others because I am Daughter-Heir of 안도르. The truth is that if anything, I catch it harder than the rest because I’m Daughter-Heir. Neither of you did anything I did not, and if the Amyrlin had harsh words for you, she would have twice as harsh for me. Now, what did she say?”

“You must keep this just between us three,” 니나브 said. “The 흑색 아자—”

“니나브!” 에그웨인 exclaimed. “The Amyrlin said 엘레인 was to be left out of it!”

“The 흑색 아자!” 엘레인 almost shouted, scrambling up to kneel in the middle of the bed. “You cannot leave me out after telling me this much. I won’t be left out.”

“I never meant for you to be,” 니나브 assured her. 에그웨인 could only stare at her in amazement. “에그웨인, it was you and I who Liandrin saw as a threat. It was you and I who were just nearly killed—”

“Nearly killed?” 엘레인 whispered.

“—perhaps because we are still a threat, and perhaps because they already know that we were closeted alone with the Amyrlin, and even what she told us. We need someone with us who they do not know about, and if she isn’t known to the Amyrlin, either, so much the better. I am not sure we can trust the Amyrlin much further than the 흑색 아자. She means to use us for her own ends. I mean to see she doesn’t use us up. Can you understand that?”

에그웨인 nodded reluctantly. Just the same, she said, “It will be dangerous, 엘레인, as dangerous as anything we faced in Falme. Maybe more so. You do not have to be part of it, this time.”

“I know that,” 엘레인 said quietly. She paused, then went on. “When 안도르 goes to war, the First Prince of the Sword commands the army, but the Queen rides with them, too. Seven hundred years ago, at the Battle of Cuallin Dhen, the 안도르men were being routed when Queen Modrellein rode, alone and unarmed, carrying the Lion banner into the midst of the 타이런 army. The 안도르men rallied and attacked once more, to save her, and won the battle. That is the kind of courage expected of the Queen of 안도르. If I have not learned to control my fear yet, I must before I take my mother’s place on the Lion Throne.” Suddenly her somber mood vanished in a giggle. “Besides, do you think I would pass up an adventure so I could scrub pots?”

“You will do that anyway,” 니나브 told her, “and hope that everyone thinks that is all you are doing. Now listen carefully.”

*치유*

Going was beginning to be a better idea by the minute. He slid awkwardly off the bed and made his way unsteadily to the wardrobe, still clutching his blanket around him. “Good. He took a deep breath. “So long as I live,” he said in a dull voice, and the Amyrlin nodded. “You could have let me die.” She nodded again. “Then you could have had anyone you want blow it, and it would have worked for them.” Another nod. “Blood and ashes! But 세이올 굴 knows it has been found, and that means at least some 어둠의 친구들 know.

맷 wished he had another blanket, and maybe a goose-down comforter. The room suddenly felt very cold. “Are you telling me 어둠의 친구들 could come after me here? The pie grew cold on the table.

*A World of Dreams*

에그웨인 scrubbed her hands with a hand towel as she hurried down the dimly lit corridor. She had washed them twice, but they still felt greasy. She had not thought there could be so many pots in the world. And today had been bake day, so buckets of ashes had had to be hauled from the ovens. And the hearths cleaned. And the tables rubbed bone-white with fine sand, and the floors scrubbed on hands and knees. Ash and grease stained her white dress. Her back ached, and she wanted to be in her bed, but Verin had come to the kitchens, supposedly for a meal to eat in her rooms, and whispered a summons to her in passing.

Verin had her quarters above the library, in corridors used only by a few other Brown sisters. There was a dusty air to the halls there, as if the women who lived along them were too busy with other things to bother having the servants clean very often, and the passages took odd turns and twists, sometimes dipping or rising unexpectedly. The tapestries were few, their colorful weavings dulled, apparently cleaned as seldom as everything else here. Many of the lamps were unlit, plunging much of the hall into gloom. 에그웨인 thought she had it to herself, except for a flash of white ahead, perhaps a 수련생 or a servant scurrying about some task. Her shoes, clicking on bare black and white floor tiles, made echoes. It was not a comforting place for one thinking of the 흑색 아자.

She found what Verin had told her to look for. A dark paneled door at the top of a rise, beside a dusty tapestry of a king on horse back receiving the surrender of another king. Verin had named the pair of them—men dead hundreds of years before 아투르 호크윙 was born; Verin always seemed to know such things—but 에그웨인 could not remember their names, or the long-vanished countries they had ruled. It was the only wall hanging she had seen that matched Verin’s description, though.

민us the sound of her own footsteps, the hallway seemed even emptier than before, and more threatening. She rapped on the door, and entered hurriedly on the heels of an absentminded “Who is it? Come in.”

One step into the room, she stopped and stared. Shelves lined the walls, except for one door that must lead to inner rooms and except for where maps hung, often in layers, and what seemed to be charts of the night sky. She recognized the names of some constellations—the Plowman and the Haywain, the Archer and the Five Sisters—but others were unfamiliar. Books and papers and scrolls covered nearly every flat surface, with all sorts of odd things interspersed among the piles, and sometimes on top of them. Strange shapes of glass or metal, spheres and tubes interlinked, and circles held inside circles, stood among bones and skulls of every shape and description. What appeared to be a stuffed brown owl, not much bigger than 에그웨인’s hand, stood on what seemed to be a bleached white lizard’s skull, but could not be, for the skull was longer than her arm and had crooked teeth as big as her fingers. Candlesticks had been stuck about in a haphazard fashion, giving good light here and shadows there, although seeming in danger of setting fire to papers in some places. The owl blinked at her, and she jumped.

“Ah, yes,” Verin said. She was seated behind a table as cluttered as everything else in the room, a torn page held carefully in her hands. “It is you. Yes.” She noticed 에그웨인’s sideways glance at the owl, and said absently, “He keeps down mice. They chew paper.” Her gesture took in the entire room, and reminded her of the page she held. “Fascinating, this. Rosel of Essam claimed more than a hundred pages survived the Breaking, and she should have known, since she wrote barely two hundred years afterwards, but only this one piece still exists, so far as I know. Perhaps only this very copy. Rosel wrote that it held secrets the world could not face, and she would not speak of them plainly. I have read this page a thousand times, trying to decipher what she meant.”

The tiny owl blinked at 에그웨인 again. She tried not to look at it. “What does it say, Verin Sedai?”

Verin blinked, very much as the owl had. “What does it say? It is a direct translation, mind, and reads almost like a bard reciting in High Chant. Listen. ‘Heart of the Dark. Ba’alzamon. Name hidden within name shrouded by name. Secret buried within secret cloaked by secret. Betrayer of Hope. 이샤마엘 betrays all hope. Truth burns and sears. Hope fails before truth. A lie is our shield. Who can stand against the Heart of the Dark? Who can face the Betrayer of Hope? Soul of shadow, Soul of the Shadow, he is—’ ” She stopped with a sigh. “It ends there. What do you make of it?”

“I don’t know,” 에그웨인 said. “I do not like it.”

“Well, why should you, child? Like it, or understand it? I have studied it nearly forty years, and I do neither.” Verin carefully placed the page inside a silk-lined folder of stiff leather, then casually stuffed the folder into a stack of papers. “But you did not come for that.” She rummaged across the table, muttering to herself, several times barely catching a pile of books or manuscripts before it toppled. Finally she came up with a handful of pages covered in a thin, spidery hand and tied with nubby string. “Here, child. Everything that is known about Liandrin and the women who went with her. Names, ages, 아자s, where they were born. Everything I could find in the records. Even how they performed in their studies. What we know of the *ter’angreal* they took, too, which isn’t much. Only descriptions, for the most part. I do not know whether any of this will help. I saw nothing of any use in this.”

“Perhaps one of us will see something.” A sudden wave of suspicion took 에그웨인 by surprise. *If she didn’t leave something out.* The Amyrlin seemed to trust Verin only because she had to. What if Verin was 흑색 아자 herself? She gave herself a shake. She had traveled all the way from Toman Head to 타르 발론 with Verin, and she refused to believe this plump scholar could be a Darkfriend. “I trust you, Verin Sedai.” *Can I, really?*

The 에스 세다이 blinked at her again, then dismissed whatever thought had come to her with a shake of her head. “That list I gave you may be important, or it may be so much waste of paper, but it isn’t the only reason I summoned you.” She started moving things on the table, making some shaky stacks taller to clear a space. “I understand from Anaiya that you might become a Dreamer. The last was Corianin Nedeal, four hundred and seventy-three years ago, and from what I can make of the records, she barely deserved the name. It would be quite interesting, if you do.”

“She tested me, Verin Sedai, but she couldn’t be sure that any of my dreams foretold the future.”

“That is only part of what a Dreamer does, child. Perhaps the least part. Anaiya believes in bringing girls along too slowly, in my opinion. Look here.” With one finger, Verin drew a number of parallel lines across the area she had cleared, lines clear in dust atop the old beeswax. “Let these represent worlds that might exist if different choices had been made, if major turning points in the Pattern had gone another way.”

“The worlds reached by the Portal Stones,” 에그웨인 said, to show she had listened to Verin’s lectures on the journey from Toman Head. What could this possibly have to do with whether or not she was a Dreamer?

“Very good. But the Pattern may be even more complex than that, child. 수레바퀴 weaves our lives to make the Pattern of an Age, but the Ages themselves are woven into the Age Lace, the Great Pattern. Who can know if this is even the tenth part of the weaving, though? Some in the 전설의 시대 apparently believe that there were still other worlds—even harder to reach than the worlds of the Portal Stones, if that can be believed—lying like this.” She drew more lines, cross-hatching the first set. For a moment she stared at them. “The warp and the woof of the weave. Perhaps the Wheel of Time weaves a still greater Pattern from worlds.” Straightening, she dusted her hands. “Well, that is neither here nor there. In all of these worlds, whatever their other variations, a few things are constant. One is that the 어둠의 존재 is imprisoned in all of them.”

In spite of herself, 에그웨인 stepped closer to peer at the lines Verin had drawn. “In all of them? How can that be? Are you saying there is a 거짓의 아비 for each world?” The thought of so many 어둠의 존재s made her shiver.

“No, child. There is one Creator, who exists everywhere at once for all of these worlds. In the same way, there is only one 어둠의 존재, who also exists in all of these worlds at once. If he is freed from the prison the Creator made in one world, he is freed on all. So long as he is kept prisoner in one, he remains imprisoned on all.”

“That does not seem to make sense,” 에그웨인 protested.

“Paradox, child. 어둠의 존재 is the embodiment of paradox and chaos, the destroyer of reason and logic, the breaker of balance, the un-maker of order.”

The owl suddenly took flight on silent wings, landing atop a large white skull on a shelf behind the 에스 세다이. It peered down at the two women, blinking. 에그웨인 had noticed the skull when she came in, with its curled horns and snout, and vaguely wondered what sort of ram had so big a head. Now she took in the roundness of it, the high forehead. Not a ram’s skull. A 트롤록.

She drew a shuddering breath. “Verin Sedai, what does this have to do with being a Dreamer? 어둠의 존재 is bound in 세이올 굴, and I do not want to even think of him escaping.” *But the seals on his prison are weakening. Even 수련생s know that, now.*

“Do with being a Dreamer? Why, nothing, child. Except that we must all confront the 어둠의 존재 in one way or another. He is prisoned now, but the Pattern did not bring 랜드 al’Thor into the world for no purpose. The 용의 환생 will face the 무덤의 군주; that much is sure. If 랜드 survives that long, of course. 어둠의 존재 will try to distort the Pattern, if he can. Well, we have gone rather far afield, haven’t we?”

“Forgive me, Verin Sedai, but if this”—에그웨인 indicated the lines drawn in the dust—“has nothing to do with being a Dreamer, why are you telling me about it?”

Verin stared at her as if she were deliberately being dense. “Nothing? Of course it has something to do with it, child. The point is that there is a third constant besides the Creator and the 어둠의 존재. There is a world that lies *within* each of these others, inside all of them at the same time. Or perhaps surrounding them. Writers in the 전설의 시대 called it *Tel’aran’rhiod*, “the Unseen World.” Perhaps “the World of Dreams” is a better translation. Many people—ordinary folk who could not think of channeling—sometimes glimpse *Tel’aran’rhiod* in their dreams, and even catch glimmers of these other worlds through it. I won’t know what they are doing till it is too late. If there is even a spark of life left when they find me, they can still do it. Please, 에그웨인. For the love of the Light. Kill me.”

“I—I can’t, 랜드. Light help me, I cannot!”

*The way back will come but once. Be steadfast.*

She looked over her shoulder, and a silver arch filled with white light took up most of the open space among the rubble.

“에그웨인, help me.”

*Be steadfast.*

She stood and took a step toward the arch. It was right there in front of her. One more step, and. . . .

“Please, 에그웨인. Help me. I can’t reach it. For the love of the Light, 에그웨인, help me!”

“I cannot kill you,” she whispered.

“I can’t. Forgive me.” She stepped forward.

“HELP ME, EGWENE!”

Light burned her to ash.

Staggering, she stepped out of the arch, neither noticing her nakedness nor caring. A shudder ran through her, and she covered her mouth with both hands. “I couldn’t, 랜드,” she whispered. “I couldn’t. Please forgive me.” *Light help him. Please, Light help 랜드.*

Cold water poured over her head.

“You are washed clean of false pride,” 엘라이더 intoned. “You are washed clean of false ambition. You come to us washed clean, in heart and soul.”

As the Red sister turned away, 셰리암 gently took 에그웨인’s shoulders and guided her toward the last arch. “One more, child. One more, and it is done.”

“He said they could turn him to the Shadow,” 에그웨인 mumbled. “He said the 미르드랄 and the Dreadlords could force him.”

셰리암 missed a step, and looked around quickly. 엘라이더 was almost back to the table. The 에스 세다이 surrounding the *ter’angreal* stared at it, seeming lost to anything else. “An unpleasant thing to talk of, child,” 셰리암 said finally, and softly. “Come. One more.”

“Can they?” 에그웨인 insisted.

“Custom,” 셰리암 said, “is not to speak of what happens within the *ter’angreal.* A woman’s fears are her own.”

“Can they?”

셰리암 sighed, glanced at the other 에스 세다이 again, then dropped her voice to a whisper and spoke swiftly. “This is something known only to a few, child, even in the Tower. You should not learn it now, if ever, but I will tell you. There is—a weakness in being able to channel. That we learn to open ourselves to the True Source means that we can be—opened to other things.” 에그웨인 shuddered. “Calm yourself, child. It is not so easily done. It is a thing not done, so far as I know—Light send it has not been done!—since the 트롤록 전쟁. It took thirteen Dreadlords—어둠의 친구들 who could channel—weaving the flows through thirteen 미르드랄. You see? Not easily done. There are no Dreadlords today. This is a secret of the Tower, child. If others knew, we could never convince them they were safe. Only one who can channel can be turned in this way. The weakness of our strength. Everyone else is as safe as a fortress; only their own deeds and will can turn them to the Shadow.”
“Thirteen,” 에그웨인 said in a tiny voice. “The same number who left the Tower. Liandrin, and twelve more.”

셰리암’s face hardened. “That is nothing for you to dwell on. You will forget it.” Her voice climbed to a normal volume. “The third time is for what will be. The way back will come but once. Be steadfast.”

에그웨인 stared at the glowing arch, stared at some far distance beyond it. *Liandrin and twelve others. Thirteen 어둠의 친구들 who can channel. Light help us all.* She stepped into the light. It filled her. It shone through her. It burned her to the bone, seared her to the soul. She flashed incandescent in the light. *Light help me!* There was nothing but the light. And the pain.

에그웨인 stared into the standing mirror, and was not sure whether she was more surprised by the ageless smoothness of her face or the striped stole that hung around her neck. The stole of the 아미를린 석좌.

*The way back will come but once. Be steadfast.*

*Thirteen.*

She swayed, caught at the mirror and almost toppled it and herself to the blue-tiled floor of her dressing chamber. *Something is wrong,* she thought. The wrongness had nothing to do with her sudden dizziness, or at least that was not what felt wrong. It was something else. But she had no idea what.

There was an 에스 세다이 at her elbow, a woman with 셰리암’s high cheekbones but dark hair and concerned brown eyes, and the hand-wide stole of the Keeper on her shoulders. Not 셰리암, though. 에그웨인 had never seen her before; she was sure she knew her as well as she knew herself. Haltingly, she put a name to the woman. Beldeine.

“Are you ill, Mother?”

*Her stole is green. That means she was raised from the 녹색 아자. The Keeper always comes from the same 아자 as the Amyrlin she serves. Which means if I’m the Amyrlin—if?—then I was 녹색 아자, too.* That thought shook her. Not that she had been 녹색 아자, but that she had to reason it out. *Light, something is wrong with me.*

*The way back will come bu. . . .* The voice in her head trailed away to finish in a buzz.

*Thirteen 어둠의 친구들.*

“I am well, Beldeine,” 에그웨인 said. The name felt strange on her tongue; it felt as if she had been saying it for years. “We mustn’t keep them waiting.” *Keep who waiting?* She did not know, except that she felt infinitely sad about ending that wait, endlessly reluctant.

“They will be growing impatient, Mother.” There was a hesitation in Beldeine’s voice, as if she felt the same reluctance as 에그웨인, but for a different reason. Unless 에그웨인 missed her guess, behind that outer calm, Beldeine was terrified.

“In that case, we had best be about it.”

Beldeine nodded, then took a deep breath before crossing the carpet to where her staff of office, topped with the snowdrop White Flame of 타르 발론, stood propped beside the door. “I suppose we must, Mother.” She took up the staff and opened the door for 에그웨인, then hurried ahead so that they made a procession of two, 연대기 수호자 leading the 아미를린 석좌.

에그웨인 noticed little of the corridors they took. All her attention was directed inward. *What is the matter with me? Why can’t I remember? Why is so much of what I . . . almost remember wrong?* She touched the seven-striped stole on her shoulders. *Why am I half sure I’m still a 수련생?*

*The way back will come but on*—This time it ended abruptly.

*Thirteen of the 흑색 아자.*

She stumbled at that. It was a frightening thought, but it chilled her to the marrow beyond fear. It felt—personal. She wanted to scream, to run and hide. She felt as if they were after her. *Nonsense. The 흑색 아자 has been destroyed.* That seemed an odd thought, too. Part of her remembered something called the Great Purge. Part of her was sure no such thing had happened.

Eyes fixed ahead, Beldeine had not noticed her stumble. 에그웨인 had to lengthen her stride to catch up. *This woman is scared to her toenails. What in the Light is she taking me to?*

Beldeine stopped before tall, paired doors, their dark wood each inlaid with a large silver Flame of 타르 발론. She wiped her hands on her dress, as if they were suddenly sweaty, before opening one door and leading 에그웨인 up a straight ramp of the same silver-streaked white stone that made 타르 발론’s walls. Even here it seemed to shine.

The ramp let into a large, circular room under a domed ceiling at least thirty paces high. A raised platform ran around the outer edge of the room, fronted by steps except where this ramp and two others came out, spaced equally around the circle. The Flame of 타르 발론 lay centered in the floor, surrounded by widening spirals of color, the colors of the seven 아자s. At the opposite side of the room from where the ramp entered, a high-backed chair stood, heavy and ornately carved in vines and leaves, painted in the colors of all the 아자s.

Beldeine rapped her staff sharply on the floor. There was a tremor in her voice. “She comes. The Watcher of the 봉인. The Flame of 타르 발론. The 아미를린 석좌. She comes.”

With a rustle of skirts, shawled women on the platform got up from their chairs. Twenty-one chairs in groupings of three, each triad painted and cushioned in the same color as the fringe on the shawls of the women who stood before them.

*The 탑의 회의실*, 에그웨인 thought as she crossed the floor to her chair. The 아미를린 석좌’s chair. *That’s all it is. The 탑의 회의실, and the 의석자들 for the 아자s. I’ve been here thousands of times.* But she could not remember one of them. *What am I doing in the 탑의 회의실? Light, they’ll skin me alive when they see. . . .* She was not sure what it was they would see, only that she prayed they did not.

*The way back will come but—*

*The way back will—*

*The way—*

*The 흑색 아자 waits.* That, at least, was whole. It came from everywhere. Why did no one else seem to hear it?

Settling in the chair of the 아미를린 석좌—the chair that was also the 아미를린 석좌—she realized she had no idea what to do next. The other 에스 세다이 had seated themselves when she did, all but Beldeine, who stood beside her with the staff, swallowing nervously. They all seemed to be waiting on her.

“Begin,” she said finally.

It seemed to be enough. One of the Red 의석자들 stood. 에그웨인 was shocked to recognize 엘라이더. At the same time she knew that 엘라이더 was foremost of the 의석자들 for the Red, and her own bitterest enemy. The look on 엘라이더’s face as she stared across the chamber made 에그웨인 shiver inside. It was stern and cold—and triumphant. It promised things best not thought of.

“Bring him in,” 엘라이더 said loudly.

From one of the ramps—not the one 에그웨인 had entered by—came the crunch of boots on stone. People appeared. A dozen 에스 세다이 surrounding three men, two of them burly guards with the white teardrops of the Flame of 타르 발론 on their chests, tugging the chains in which the third stumbled as if dazed.

에그웨인 jerked forward in her chair. The chained man was 랜드. Eyes half-closed, head sagging, he seemed nearly asleep, moving only as the chains directed.

“This man,” 엘라이더 proclaimed, “has named himself the 용의 환생.” There was a buzz of distaste, not as if the listeners were surprised, but as though it were not something they wanted to hear. “This man has channeled the 하나의 힘.” The buzz was louder now, disgusted and tinged with fear. “There is only one penalty for this, known and recognized in every nation, but pronounced only here, in 타르 발론, in the 탑의 회의실. I call on the 아미를린 석좌 to pronounce the sentence of gentling on this man.”

엘라이더’s eyes glittered at 에그웨인. *랜드. What do I do? Light, what do I do?*

“Why do you hesitate?” 엘라이더 demanded. “The sentence has been set down for three thousand years. Why do you hesitate, 에그웨인 al’Vere?”

One of the Green 의석자들 was on her feet, anger bright through her calm. “Shame, 엘라이더! Show respect for the 아미를린 석좌! Show respect for the Mother!”

“Respect,” 엘라이더 answered coldly, “can be lost as well as won. Well, 에그웨인? Can it be you show your weakness, your unfitness for your office, at last? Can it be you will not pronounce sentence on this man?”

랜드 tried to lift his head and failed.

에그웨인 struggled to her feet, head spinning, trying to remember she was the 아미를린 석좌 with the power to command all these women, screaming that she was a 수련생, that she did not belong here, that something was dreadfully wrong. “No,” she said shakily. “No, I cannot! I will not—”

“She betrays herself!” 엘라이더’s shout drowned out 에그웨인’s attempt to speak. “She condemns herself out of her own mouth! Take her!”

As 에그웨인 opened her mouth, Beldeine moved beside her. Then the Keeper’s staff struck her head.

Blackness.

First there was pain in her head. There was something hard under her back, and cold. Next came the voices. Murmurs.

“Is she still unconscious?” It was a rasp, a file on bone.

“Do not worry,” a woman said from far, far away. She sounded uneasy, afraid, and trying not to show either. “She will be dealt with before she knows what is happening to her. Then she is ours, to do with as we will. Perhaps we will give her to you for sport.”

“After you make your own use of her.”

“Of course.”

The distant voices moved further away.

Her hand brushed against her leg, touched bare, pebbly flesh. She opened her eyes a crack. She was naked, bruised, lying on a rough wooden table, in what seemed to be a disused storeroom. Splinters stuck her back. There was a metallic taste of blood in her mouth.

A cluster of 에스 세다이 stood to one side of the room, talking among themselves, voices low yet urgent. The pain in her head made thinking difficult, but it seemed important to count them. Thirteen.

Another group, black-cloaked and hooded men, joined the 에스 세다이, who seemed caught between cowering and trying to dominate with their presence. One of the men turned his head to look toward the table. The dead white face within the hood had no eyes.

에그웨인 had no need to count the 미르드랄. She knew. Thirteen 미르드랄, and thirteen 에스 세다이. Without another thought, she screamed in pure terror. Yet even in the midst of fear that tried to split her bones, she reached out for the True Source, clawed desperately for *세다르.*

“She’s awake!”

“She cannot be! Not yet!”

“Shield her! Quickly! Quickly! Cut her off from the Source!”

“It’s too late! She is too strong!”

“Seize her! Hurry!”

Hands reached for her arms and legs. Pasty pale hands like slugs under rocks, ordered by minds behind pale, eyeless faces. If those hands touched her flesh, she knew she would go mad. The Power filled her.

Flames burst from 미르드랄 skin, ripping through black cloth as if they were solid daggers of fire. Shrieking Halfmen crisped and burned like oiled paper. Fist-sized chunks of stone tore themselves free of the walls and whizzed across the room, producing shrieks and grunts as they thudded into flesh. The air stirred, shifted, howled into a whirlwind.

Slowly, painfully, 에그웨인 pushed herself off the table. The wind whipped her hair and made her stagger, but she continued to drive it as she stumbled toward the door. An 에스 세다이 loomed in front of her, a woman bruised and bleeding, surrounded by the glow of the Power. A woman with death in her dark eyes.

에그웨인’s mind put a name to the face. Gyldan. 엘라이더’s closest confidante, always whispering together in corners, closeting themselves in the night. 에그웨인’s mouth tightened. Disdaining stones and wind, she balled up her fist and punched Gyldan between the eyes as hard as she could. The Red sister—the *Black* sister—crumpled as if her bones had melted.

Rubbing her knuckles, 에그웨인 staggered out into the hall. *Thank you, 페린*, she thought, *for showing me how to do that. But you didn’t tell me how much it hurts when you do.*

Shoving the door shut against the wind, she channeled. Stones around the doorway shivered, cracked, settled against the wood. It would not hold them for long, but anything that slowed pursuit for even a minute was worth doing. 민utes might mean life. Gathering her strength, she forced herself to break into a run. It wobbled, but at least it was a run.

She must find some clothes, she decided. A woman clothed had more authority than the same woman naked, and she was going to need every bit of authority. They would look for her first in her rooms, but she had a spare dress and shoes in her study—and another stole—and that lay not far off.

It was unnerving, trotting through empty hallways. The 백색 탑 no longer held the numbers it once had, but there was usually someone about. The loudest sound was the slap of her bare soles on the tiles.

She hurried through the antechamber of her study to the inner room, and at last she found someone. Beldeine was sitting on the floor, head in her hands, weeping.

에그웨인 stopped warily, as Beldeine raised reddened eyes to meet hers. No glow of *세다르* surrounded the Keeper, but 에그웨인 was still cautious. And confident. She could not see her own glow, of course, but the power—the Power—surging through her was enough. Especially when added to her secret.

Beldeine scrubbed a hand across tearstained cheeks. “I had to. You must understand. I had to. They. . . . They. . . .” She took a deep, shuddering breath; it all came out in a rush. “Three nights ago they took me while I slept and stilled me.” Her voice rose to a near shriek. “They *stilled* me! I cannot channel any longer!”

“Light,” 에그웨인 breathed. The rush of *세다르* cushioned her against the shock. “빛 help and comfort you, my daughter. Why didn’t you tell me? I would have. . . .” She let it trail away, knowing there was nothing she could do.

“What would you have done? What? Nothing! There’s nothing you can do. But they said they could give it back to me, with the power of . . . the power of the 어둠의 존재.” Her eyes squeezed shut, leaking tears. “They hurt me, Mother, and they made me. . . . Oh, Light, they hurt me! 엘라이더 told me they would make me whole again, make me able to channel again, if I obeyed. That’s why I. . . . I had to!”

“So 엘라이더 *is* 흑색 아자,” 에그웨인 said grimly. A narrow wardrobe stood against the wall, and in it hung a green silk dress, kept for when she had no time to return to her rooms. A striped stole hung beside the dress. She began to dress herself, quickly. “What have they done with 랜드? Where have they taken him? Answer me, Beldeine! Where is 랜드 al’Thor?”

Beldeine huddled, lips trembling, eyes turned bleakly inward, but finally she roused herself enough to say, “The Traitor’s Court, Mother. They took him to the Traitor’s Court.”

Shivers assaulted 에그웨인. Shivers of fear. Shivers of rage. 엘라이더 had not waited, not even an hour. The Traitor’s Court was used for only three purposes: executions, the stilling of an 에스 세다이, or the gentling of a man who could channel. But all of the three took an order from the 아미를린 석좌. *So who wears the stole out there?* 엘라이더, she was sure. *But how could she make them accept her so quickly, with me not tried, not sentenced? There cannot be another Amyrlin until I’ve been stripped of stole and staff. And they’ll not find that easy to do. Light! 랜드!* She started for the door.

“What can you do, Mother?” Beldeine cried. “What can you do?” It was not clear whether she meant for 랜드 or for herself.

“More than anyone suspects,” 에그웨인 said. “I never held the 맹세 막대, Beldeine.” Beldeine’s gasp followed her from the room.

에그웨인’s memory still played hide-and-seek with her. She knew no woman could achieve the shawl and the ring without pledging the 세 가지 맹세 with the 맹세 막대 firmly in hand, the *ter’angreal* sealing her to keep those oaths as if they had been engraved on her bones at birth. No woman became 에스 세다이 without being bound to them. Yet she knew that somehow, in some fashion she could not begin to dredge up, she had done just that.

Her shoes clicked swiftly as she ran. At least she knew now why the halls were empty. Every 에스 세다이, except perhaps those she had left in the storeroom, every 허락받은 자, every 수련생, even all the servants, would be gathered in the Traitor’s Court, according to custom, to watch the will of 타르 발론 made fact.

And the 감시자s would be ringing the courtyard against the possibility that someone might try to free the man to be gentled. The remnants of Guaire Amalasan’s armies had attempted it, at the end of what some called the War of the Second Dragon, just before 아투르 호크윙’s rise had given 타르 발론 other things to worry it, and so had Raolin Darksbane’s followers, long years earlier. Whether 랜드 had any followers or not, she could not remember, but 감시자s remembered such things, and guarded against them.

If 엘라이더, or another, truly did wear the stole of the Amyrlin, the 감시자s might well not admit her to the Traitor’s Court. She knew she could force a way in. It would need to be done quickly; there was no point if 랜드 was gentled while she was still wrapping 감시자s in Air. Even 감시자s would break if she loosed the lightnings on them, and balefire, and broke the ground under their feet. *마화?* she wondered. But it would also do no good if she broke 타르 발론’s power to save 랜드. She had to save both.

Well short of the ways that led to the Traitor’s Court, she turned aside and climbed, up stairs and ramps that grew narrower and tighter the higher she went, until she thrust open a trapdoor and climbed out onto a sloping tower top, a roof of nearly white tiles. From there, she could see across other roofs, past other towers, into the broad open well of the Traitor’s Court.

The court was crowded except for a cleared space in the middle. People filled the windows overlooking it, crowded the balconies and even the rooftops, but she could make out the lone man, small at that distance, swaying in his chains in the center of the cleared space. 랜드. Twelve 에스 세다이 surrounded him, and another—who 에그웨인 knew had to be wearing a seven-striped stole, even though she could not distinguish it—stood before 랜드. *엘라이더.* The words she must be saying crept into 에그웨인’s head.

*This man, abandoned of the Light, has touched* 세이딘, *the male half of the True Source. Thus do we hold him. Most abominably has this man channeled the 하나의 힘, knowing that* 세이딘 *is tainted by the 어둠의 존재, tainted for men’s pride, tainted for men’s sin. Thus do we chain him.*

Forcefully, 에그웨인 pushed the rest of it out of her thoughts. *Thirteen 에스 세다이. Twelve sisters and the Amyrlin, the traditional number for gentling. The same number as for. . . .* She rid herself of that, too. She had no time for anything but what she was there to do. If she could only manage to reason out how.

At that distance, she thought she could manage to lift him with Air. Pick him right out of the circle of 에스 세다이 and float him straight to her. Maybe. Even if she could find the strength, even if she did not drop him to his death halfway, it would be a slow process, with him a helpless target for archers, and the glow of *세다르* pointing out her own position for any 에스 세다이 who looked. Any 미르드랄, for that matter.

“Light,” she muttered, “there’s no other way short of starting a war inside the 백색 탑. And I may do that anyway.” She gathered the Power, separated skeins, directed flows.

*The way back will come but once. Be steadfast.*

It had been so long since she last heard those words that she gave a start, slipped on the smooth tiles, barely caught herself short of the edge. The ground lay a hundred paces down. She looked over her shoulder.

There on the tower top, tilted to sit flat against the sloping tiles, was a silver arch filled with a glowing light. The arch flickered and wavered; streaks of angry red and yellow darted through the white light.

*The way back will come but once. Be steadfast.*

The archway thinned to transparency, grew solid again.

Frantic, 에그웨인 gazed toward the Traitor’s Court. There had to be time. There had to be. All she needed was a few minutes, perhaps ten, and luck.

목소리s bored into her head, not the disembodied, unknowable voice that warned her to be steadfast, but women’s voices she almost believed she knew.

*—can’t hold much longer. If she does not come out now—*

*Hold! Hold, burn you, or I’ll gut you all like sturgeons!*

—*going wild, Mother! We can’t—*

The voices faded to a drone, the drone to silence, but the unknowable spoke again.

*The way back will come but once. Be steadfast.*

*There is a price to be 에스 세다이.*

*The 흑색 아자 waits.*

With a scream of rage, of loss, 에그웨인 threw herself at the arch as it shimmered like a heat haze. She almost wished she would miss and plunge to her death.

Light plucked her apart fiber by fiber, sliced the fibers to hairs, split the hairs to wisps of nothing. All drifted apart on the light. Forever.
