CHAPTER 23

![](images/00147.jpg)

*Sealed*

Light pulled her apart fiber by fiber, sliced the fibers to hairs that drifted apart, burning. Drifting and burning, forever. Forever.

에그웨인 stepped out of the silver arch cold and stiff with anger. She wanted the iciness of anger to counter the searing of memory. Her body remembered burning, but other memories scored and scorched more deeply. Anger cold as death.

“Is that all there is for me?” she demanded. “To abandon him again and again. To betray him, fail him, again and again? Is that what there is for me?”

Suddenly she realized that all was not as it should be. The Amyrlin was there now, as 에그웨인 had been taught she would be, and a shawled sister from each 아자, but they all stared at her worriedly. Two 에스 세다이 now sat at each place around the *ter’angreal*, sweat running down their faces. The *ter’angreal* hummed, almost vibrated, and violent streaks of color tore the white light inside the arches.

The glow of *세다르* briefly enveloped 셰리암 as she put a hand on 에그웨인’s head, sending a new chill through her. “She is well.” The 수련생 감독관 sounded relieved. “She is unharmed.” As if she had not expected it.

Tension seemed to go out of the other 에스 세다이 facing 에그웨인. 엘라이더 let out a long breath, then hurried away for the last chalice. Only the 에스 세다이 around the *ter’angreal* did not relax. The hum had lessened, and the light began the flickering that signaled the *ter’angreal* was settling toward quiescence, but those 에스 세다이 looked as if they were fighting it every inch of the way.

“What . . . ? What happened?” 에그웨인 asked.

“Be silent,” 셰리암 said, but gently. “For now, be silent. You are well—that is the main thing—and we must complete the ceremony.” 엘라이더 came, close to running, and handed the final silver chalice to the Amyrlin.

에그웨인 hesitated only a moment before kneeling. *What happened?*

The Amyrlin emptied the chalice slowly over 에그웨인’s head. “You are washed clean of 에그웨인 al’Vere from Emond’s Field. You are washed clean of all ties that bind you to the world. You come to us washed clean, in heart and soul. You are 에그웨인 al’Vere, 허락받은 자 of the 백색 탑.” The last drop splashed onto 에그웨인’s hair. “You are sealed to us, now.”

The last words seemed to have a special meaning, just between 에그웨인 and the Amyrlin. The Amyrlin thrust the chalice at one of the other 에스 세다이 and produced a gold ring in the shape of a serpent biting its own tail. Despite herself, 에그웨인 trembled as she raised her left hand, trembled again as the Amyrlin slipped the Great Serpent ring onto the third finger. When she became 에스 세다이, she could wear the ring on the finger she chose, or not at all if it was necessary to hide who she was, but the 허락받은 자 wore it there.

Unsmiling, the Amyrlin pulled her to her feet. “Welcome, Daughter,” she said, kissing her cheek. 에그웨인 was surprised to feel a thrill. Not child, but daughter. Always before she had been child. The Amyrlin kissed her other cheek. “Welcome.”

Stepping back, the Amyrlin regarded her critically, but spoke to 셰리암. “Get her dry and into some clothes, then be certain she is well. Certain, you understand.”

“I am certain, Mother.” 셰리암 sounded surprised. “You saw me delve her.”

The Amyrlin grunted, and her eyes shifted to the *ter’angreal*. “I mean to know what went wrong tonight.” She strode away in the direction of her glare, skirts swaying purposefully. Most of the other 에스 세다이 joined her around the *ter’angreal*, now only a silver structure of arches on a ring.

“The Mother is worried about you,” 셰리암 said as she drew 에그웨인 to one side, to where there was a thick towel for her hair, and another for the rest of her.

“How much reason did she have?” 에그웨인 asked. *The Amyrlin wants nothing to happen to her hound till the deer is pulled down.*

셰리암 did not answer. She merely frowned slightly, then waited until 에그웨인 was dry before handing her a white dress banded at the bottom with seven rings.

She slipped into that dress with a flash of disappointment. She was one of the 허락받은 자, with the ring on her finger and the bands on her dress. *Why don’t I feel any different?*

엘라이더 came over, her arms filled with 에그웨인’s 수련생 dress and shoes, her belt and pouch. And the papers Verin had given her. In 엘라이더’s hands.

에그웨인 made herself wait for the 에스 세다이 to hand the bundle to her rather than snatch them away. “Thank you, 에스 세다이.” She tried to eye the papers surreptitiously; she could not tell if they had been disturbed. The string was still tied. *How would I know if she’s read all of them*? Squeezing her pouch under cover of the 수련생 dress, she felt the peculiar ring, the *ter’angreal,* inside. *At least that’s still here. Light, she could have taken that, and I don’t know that I would have minded. Yes, I would. I think I would.*

엘라이더’s face was as cold as her voice. “I did not want you to be brought forward tonight. Not because I feared what happened; no one could foresee that. But because of what you are. A wilder.” 에그웨인 tried to protest, but 엘라이더 kept on, as implacable as a mountain glacier. “Oh, I know you learned to channel under 에스 세다이 teaching, but you are still a wilder. A wilder in spirit, a wilder in ways. You have vast potential, else you would never have survived in there tonight, but potential changes nothing. I do not believe you will ever be part of the 백색 탑, not in the way the rest of us are, no matter on which finger you wear your ring. It would have been better for you had you settled for learning enough to stay alive, and gone back to your sleepy village. Far better.” Turning on her heel, she stalked away, out of the chamber.

*If she isn’t 흑색 아자*, 에그웨인 thought sourly, *she’s the next thing to it.* Aloud, she muttered to 셰리암, “You could have said something. You could have helped me.”

“I would have helped a 수련생, child,” 셰리암 replied calmly, and 에그웨인 winced. She was back to “child” again. “I try to protect 수련생s where they need it, since they cannot protect themselves. You are 허락받은 자, now. It is time for you to learn to protect yourself.”
에그웨인 studied 셰리암’s eyes, wondering if she had imagined an emphasis on that last sentence. 셰리암 had had as much opportunity as 엘라이더 to read the list of names, to decide that 에그웨인 was mixed in with the 흑색 아자. *Light, you’re becoming suspicious of everybody. Better that than dead, or captured by thirteen of them and. . . .* Hastily, she stopped that line of thought; she did not want it in her head. “셰리암, what did happen tonight?” she asked. “And don’t put me off.” 셰리암’s eyebrows rose almost to her scalp, it seemed, and she hastily amended her question. “셰리암 Sedai, I mean. Forgive me, 셰리암 Sedai.”

“Remember you aren’t 에스 세다이 yet, child.” Despite the steel in her voice, a smile touched 셰리암’s lips, yet it vanished as she went on. “I do not know what happened. Except that I very much fear you almost died.”

“Who knows what happens to those who do not come out of a *ter’angreal*?” Alanna said as she joined them. The Green sister was known for her temper and her sense of humor, and some said she could flash from one to the other and back again before you could blink, but the look she gave 에그웨인 was almost diffident. “Child, I should have stopped this when I had the chance, when I first noticed that—reverberation. It came back. That is what happened. It came back a thousandfold. Ten thousand. The *ter’angreal* almost seemed to be trying to shut off the flow from *세다르*—or melt itself through the floor. You have my apologies, though words are not enough. Not for what almost happened to you. I say this, and by the First Oath you know it is true. To show my feelings, I will ask the Mother to let me share your time in the kitchens. And, yes, your visit to 셰리암, too. Had I done as I should, you would not have been in danger of your life, and I will atone for it.”

셰리암’s laugh was scandalized. “She will never allow that, Alanna. A sister in the kitchens, much less. . . . It is unheard of. It’s impossible! You did what you believed right. There is no fault to you.”

“It was not your fault, Alanna Sedai,” 에그웨인 said. *Why is Alanna doing this? Unless maybe to convince me she* didn’t *have anything to do with whatever went wrong. And maybe so she can keep an eye on me all the time.* It was that image, a proud 에스 세다이 up to her elbows in greasy pots three times a day just to watch someone, that convinced her she was letting her imagination run away with her. But it was also unthinkable that Alanna should do as she said she would. In any case, the Green sister certainly had had no chance to see the list of names while tending the *ter’angreal. But if 니나브 is right, she wouldn’t need to see those names to want to kill me if she is 흑색 아자. Stop that!* “Really, it wasn’t.”

“Had I done as I should,” Alanna maintained, “it would never have happened. The only time I have ever seen anything like it was once years ago when we tried to use a *ter’angreal* in the same room with another that may have been in some way related to it. It is extremely rare to find two such as that. The pair of them melted, and every sister within a hundred paces had such a headache for a week that she couldn’t channel a spark. What’s the matter, child?”

에그웨인’s hand had tightened around her pouch till the twisted stone ring impressed itself on her palm through the thick cloth. Was it warm? *Light, I did it myself.* “Nothing, Alanna Sedai. 에스 세다이, you did nothing wrong. You have no reason to share my punishments. None at all. None!”

“A bit vehement,” 셰리암 observed, “but true.” Alanna only shook her head.

“에스 세다이,” 에그웨인 said slowly, “what does it mean to be 녹색 아자?” 셰리암’s eyes opened wider with amusement, and Alanna grinned openly.

“Just with the ring on your finger,” the Green sister said, “and already trying to decide which 아자 to choose? First, you must love men. I don’t mean be in love with them, but love them. Not like a Blue, who merely likes men, so long as they share her causes and do not get in her way. And certainly not like a Red, who despises them as if every one of them were responsible for the Breaking.” Alviarin, the White sister who had come with the Amyrlin, gave them a cool look and moved on. “And not like a White,” Alanna said with a laugh, “who has no room in her life for any passions at all.”

“That was not what I meant, Alanna Sedai. I want to know what it *means* to be a Green sister.” She was not sure Alanna would understand, because she was not certain she herself understood what she wanted to know, but Alanna nodded slowly as if she did.

“Browns seek knowledge, Blues meddle in causes, and Whites consider the questions of truth with implacable logic. We all do some of it all, of course. But to be a Green means to stand ready.” A note of pride entered Alanna’s voice. “In the 트롤록 전쟁, we were often called the Battle 아자. All 에스 세다이 helped where and when they could, but the 녹색 아자 alone was always with the armies, in almost every battle. We were the counter to the Dreadlords. The Battle 아자. And now we stand ready, for the 트롤록s to come south again, for Tarmon Gai’don, the Last Battle. We will be there. That is what it means to be a Green.”

“Thank you, 에스 세다이,” 에그웨인 said. *That is what I was? Or what I* *will be? Light, I wish I knew if it was real, if it had anything at all to do with here and now.*

The Amyrlin joined them, and they swept deep curtsies to her. “Are you well, Daughter?” she asked 에그웨인. Her eyes flicked to the corner of the papers sticking out from under the 수련생 dress in 에그웨인’s hands, then back to 에그웨인’s face immediately. “I will know the why of what occurred tonight before I am done.”

에그웨인’s cheeks reddened. “I am well, Mother.”

Alanna surprised her by asking the Amyrlin just what she had said she would.

“I never heard of such a thing,” the Amyrlin barked. “The owner doesn’t muck out with the bilge boys even if he has run the boat on a mud-flat.” She glanced at 에그웨인, and worry tightened her eyes. And anger. “I share your concern, Alanna. Whatever this child has done, it did not deserve that. Very well. If it will assuage your feelings, you may visit 셰리암. But it is to be strictly between you two. I’ll not have 에스 세다이 held up to ridicule, even inside the Tower.”

에그웨인 opened her mouth to confess all and let them take the ring—*I don’t want the bloody thing, really*—but Alanna forestalled her.

“And the other, Mother?”

“Do not be ridiculous, Daughter.” The Amyrlin was angry, and sounded more so by the word. “You’d be a laughingstock inside the day, except for those who decided you were mad. And don’t think it would not follow you. Tales like that have a way of traveling. You would find stories told of the *scullion 에스 세다이* from 티어 to 마라도나. And that would reflect on every sister. No. If you need to rid yourself of some feeling of guilt and cannot handle it as a grown woman would, very well. I have told you that you may visit 셰리암. Accompany her tonight when you leave here. That will give you the rest of the night to decide if it was of any help. And tomorrow you can start finding out what went wrong here tonight!”

“Yes, Mother.” Alanna’s voice was perfectly neutral.

The desire to confess had died in 에그웨인. Alanna had shown only one brief flash of disappointment, when she realized the Amyrlin would not allow her to join 에그웨인 in the kitchens. *She doesn’t want to be punished any more than any sensible person does. She did want an excuse to be in my company. Light, she couldn’t have deliberately caused the* ter’angreal *to go wild; I did that. Can she be 흑색 아자?*

Wrapped in thought, 에그웨인 heard a throat cleared, then again, more roughly. Her eyes focused. The Amyrlin was staring right into her, and when she spoke, she bit off each word.

“Since you seem to be asleep standing up, child, I suggest you go to bed.” For one instant her glance flashed to the nearly concealed papers in 에그웨인’s hands. “You have much work to do tomorrow, and for many days thereafter.” Her eyes held 에그웨인’s a moment longer, and then she was striding away before any of them could curtsy.

셰리암 rounded on Alanna as soon as the Amyrlin was out of earshot. The Green 에스 세다이 glowered and took it in silence. “You *are* mad, Alanna! A fool, and doubly a fool if you think I will go lightly on you just because we were 수련생s together. Are you taken by the Dragon, to—?” Suddenly 셰리암 became aware of 에그웨인, and the target of her anger shifted. “Did I not hear the 아미를린 석좌 order you to your bed, 허락받은 자? If you breathe a word of this, you will wish I had buried you in a field to manure the ground. And I will see you in my study in the morning, when the bell rings First and not one breath later. Now, go!”

에그웨인 went, her head spinning. *Is there anybody I can trust? The Amyrlin? She sent us off chasing thirteen of the 흑색 아자 and forgot to mention that thirteen is just the number needed to turn a woman who can channel to the Shadow against her will. Who can I trust?*

She did not want to be alone, could not stand the thought of it, and so she hurried to the 허락받은 자’s quarters, thinking that tomorrow she would be moving there herself, and immediately after knocking pushed open 니나브’s door. She could trust her with anything. Her and 엘레인.

But 니나브 was seated in one of the two chairs, with 엘레인’s head buried in her lap. 엘레인’s shoulders shook to the sound of weeping, the softer weeping that comes after no energy is left for deeper sobs but the emotion still burns. Dampness shone on 니나브’s cheeks, too. 거대한 뱀 gleaming on her hand, smoothing 엘레인’s hair, matched the ring on the hand 엘레인 used to clutch at 니나브’s skirt.

엘레인 lifted a face red and swollen from long crying, sniffing through her sobs when she saw 에그웨인. “I could not be that awful, 에그웨인. I just couldn’t!”

The accident with the *ter’angreal*, 에그웨인’s fear that someone might have read the papers Verin had given her, her suspicions of everyone in that chamber, all these had been terrible, but they had buffered her in a rough, ungentle way from what had happened inside the *ter’angreal.* They had come from outside; the other was inside. 엘레인’s words stripped the buffer away, and what was inside hit 에그웨인 as if the ceiling had collapsed. 랜드 her husband, and Joiya her baby. 랜드 pinned and begging her to kill him. 랜드 chained to be gentled.

Before she was aware of moving, she was on her knees beside 엘레인, all the tears that should have fallen earlier coming out in a flood. “I couldn’t help him, 니나브,” she sobbed. “I just left him there.”

니나브 flinched as if struck, but the next moment her arms were around both 에그웨인 and 엘레인, hugging them, rocking them. “Hush,” she crooned softly. “It eases with time. It eases, a little. One day we will make them pay our price. Hush. Hush.”

CHAPTER 24

![](images/00144.jpg)

*Scouting and Discoveries*

Sunlight through the carved shutters, creeping across the bed, woke 맷. For a moment, he only lay there, frowning. He had not reasoned out any plan for escaping from 타르 발론 before sleep had overtaken him, but neither had he given up. Too much memory still lay covered with fog, but he would not give up.

Two serving women came bustling with hot water and a tray heavy with food, laughing and telling him how much better he looked already, and how soon he would be back on his feet if he did what the 에스 세다이 told him. He answered them curtly, trying not to sound bitter. *Let them think I mean to go along.* His stomach rumbled at the smells from the tray.

When they left, he tossed aside his blanket and hopped out of bed, pausing only to stuff half a slice of ham into his mouth before pouring out water to wash and shave. Staring into the mirror above the washstand, he paused in lathering his face. He did look better.

His cheeks were still hollow, but not quite as hollow as they had been. The dark circles had vanished from under his eyes, which no longer seemed set so deep in his head. It was as if every bite he had eaten the night before had gone into putting meat on his bones. He even felt stronger.

“At this rate,” he muttered, “I will be gone before they know it.” But he was still surprised when, after shaving, he sat down and consumed every scrap of ham, turnip, and pear on the tray.

He was sure they expected him to climb back into bed once he had eaten, but instead, he dressed. Stamping his feet to settle them in his boots, he eyed his spare clothes and decided to leave them, for now. *I have to know what I’m doing, first. And if I have to leave them*. . . . He tucked the dice cups into his pouch. With those, he could get all the clothes he needed.

Opening the door, he peeked out. More doors paneled in pale, golden wood lined the hall, with colorful tapestries between, and a runner of blue carpet ran down the white-tiled floor. But there was no one out there. No guard. He tossed his cloak over one shoulder and hurried out. Now to find a way outside.

It took some little wandering, down stairs and along corridors and across open courts, before he found what he wanted, a doorway to the outside, and he saw people before then: serving women and white-clad 수련생s hurrying about their chores, the 수련생s running even harder than the servants; a handful of roughly dressed male servants carrying large chests and other heavy loads; 허락받은 자 in their banded dresses. Even a few 에스 세다이.

The 에스 세다이 did not seem to notice him as they strode along, intent on whatever purpose, or else they gave him no more than a passing glance. His were country clothes, but well made; he did not look a vagabond, and the serving men showed that men were allowed in this part of the Tower. He suspected they might take him for another servant, and that was just as well with him, so long as no one asked him to lift anything.

He did feel some regret that none of the women he saw was 에그웨인 or 니나브, or even 엘레인. *She’s a pretty one, even if she does have her nose in the air half the time. And she could tell me how to find 에그웨인 and the Wisdom. I cannot go without saying goodbye. Light, I don’t suppose one of them would turn me in, just because they are becoming 에스 세다이 themselves? Burn me, for a fool! They’d never do that. Anyway, I will risk it.*

But once out-of-doors, under a bright morning sky with only a few drifting white clouds, he put the women from his mind for the time. He was looking across a wide, flagstoned yard with a plain stone fountain in the middle and a barracks on the other side that was made of gray stone. It looked almost like a huge boulder among the few trees growing out of rimmed holes in the flagstones close by. Guardsmen in their shirtsleeves sat in front of the long, low building, tending weapons and armor and harness. Guardsmen were what he wanted, now.

He sauntered across the yard and watched the soldiers as if he had nothing better to do. As they worked they talked and laughed among themselves like men after the harvest. Now and again one of them looked curiously at 맷 as he strolled among them, but none challenged his right to be there. From time to time he asked a casual question. And finally he got the answer he sought.

“Bridge guard?” said a stocky, dark-haired man no more than five years older than 맷. His words had a heavy 일리안er accent. Young he might have been, but a thin white scar crossed his left cheek, and the hands oiling his sword moved with familiarity and competence. He squinted up at 맷 before returning to his task. “I do be on the bridge guard, and back there again this even. Why do you ask?”

“I was just wondering what conditions were like on the other side of the river.” *I might as well find that out, too.* “Good for traveling? It can’t be muddy, unless you have had more rain than I know about.”

“Which side of the river?” the guardsman asked placidly. His eyes did not lift from the oiled rag he was running along his blade.

“Uh . . . east. The east side.”

“No mud. 백의단.” The man leaned to one side to spit, but his voice did not change. “백의단 do be poking their noses into every village for ten miles. They have no hurt anyone yet, but them just being there do upset the folk. Fortune prick me if I do no think they wish to provoke us, for they do look as if they would attack if they could. No good for anyone who do want to travel.”

“What about west, then?”

“The same.” The guardsman raised his eyes to 맷’s. “But you will no be crossing, lad, east or west. Your name do be 매트림 카우톤, or Fortune abandon me. Last night a sister, herself in person, did come to the bridge where I did stand guard. She did drill your features at us till each could speak them back to her. A guest, she did say, and no to be harmed. But no to be allowed out of the city, either, if you must be tied hand and foot to keep you from it.” His eyes narrowed. “Is it that you did steal something from them?” he asked doubtfully. “You do no have the look of those the sisters do guest.”

“I didn’t steal anything!” 맷 said indignantly. *Burn me, I didn’t even get a chance to work around to it easy. They must* all *know me.* “I’m no thief!”

“No, it is no that I do see in your face. No thievery. But you do have the look of the fellow who did try to sell me the 발레르의 뿔 three days gone. So he did claim it did be, all bent and battered as it did be. Do you have a 발레르의 뿔 to sell? Or mayhap it do be the Dragon’s sword?”

맷 gave a jump at the mention of the Horn, but he managed to keep his voice level. “I was sick.” Others of the guardsmen were looking at him now. *Light, they’ll all know I am not supposed to leave, now.* He forced a laugh. “The sisters Healed me.” Some of the guardsmen frowned at him. Perhaps they thought other men should show more respect than to call the 에스 세다이 sisters. “I guess the 에스 세다이 don’t want me to go before I have all my strength back.” He tried willing the men, all of those watching him now, to accept that. *Just a man who was Healed. Nothing more. No reason to trouble yourself about him any further.*

The 일리안er nodded. “You do have the look of sickness in your face, too. Perhaps that do be the reason. But never did I hear of so much effort to keep one sick man in the city.”

“That’s the reason,” 맷 said firmly. They were all still looking at him. “Well, I need to be going. They said I have to take walks. Lots of long walks. To build up strength, you know.”

He felt their eyes following him as he left, and he scowled. He had simply meant to find out how well his description had been passed around. If only the officers among the bridge guards had had it, he might have been able to slip by. He had always been good at slipping into places unseen. And out. It was a talent you developed when your mother always suspected you were up to some mischief and you had two sisters to tell on you. *And now I’ve made sure half a barracks full of guardsmen will know me. Blood and bloody ashes!*

Much of the Tower grounds were gardens full of trees, leatherleaf and paperbark and elms, and he soon found himself walking along a wide, twisting graveled path. It could have led through countryside, if not for the towers visible over the treetops. And the white bulk of the Tower itself, behind him but pressing on him as if he carried it on his shoulders. If there were ways out of the Tower grounds that were not watched, this seemed the place to find them. If they existed.

A girl in 수련생 white appeared ahead on the path, striding purposefully toward him. Wrapped in her own thoughts, she did not see him at first. When she came close enough for him to make out her big, dark eyes and the way her hair was braided, he grinned suddenly. He knew this girl—memory drifting up from shrouded depths—though he would never have expected to find her here. He had never expected to see her again at all. He grinned to himself. *Good luck to balance bad.* As he remembered, she had quite an eye for the boys.

“Else,” he called to her. “Else Grinwell. You remember me, don’t you? 맷 카우톤. A friend and I visited your father’s farm. Remember? Have you decided to become 에스 세다이, then?”

She stopped short, staring at him. “What are you doing up and out?” she said coldly.

“You know about that, do you?” He moved closer to her, but she stepped back, keeping her distance. He stopped. “It’s not catching. I was Healed, Else.” Those large, dark eyes seemed more knowing than he remembered, and not nearly so warm, but he supposed studying to be an 에스 세다이 could do that. “What is the matter, Else? You look like you don’t know me.”

“I know you,” she said. Her manner was not as he remembered, either; he thought she could give 엘레인 lessons now. “I have . . . work to be about. Let me by.”

He grimaced. The path was broad enough for six to walk abreast without crowding. “I told you it isn’t catching.”

“Let me by!”

Muttering to himself, he stepped to one edge of the gravel. She went past him along the other side, watching to make sure he did not come closer. Once by, she quickened her steps, glancing over her shoulder at him until she was out of sight around a bend.

*Wanted to make sure I didn’t follow her*, he thought sourly. *First the guardsmen, and now Else. My luck is not in, today.*

He started off again, and soon heard a ferocious clatter from one side ahead, like dozens of sticks being beat together. Curious, he turned off toward it, into the trees.

A little way brought him to a large expanse of bare ground, the earth beaten hard, at least fifty paces across and nearly twice as long. At intervals around it under the trees stood wooden stands holding quarterstaffs, and practice swords made of strips of wood bound loosely together, and a few real swords and axes and spears.

Spaced across the open ground, pairs of men, most stripped to the waist, flailed at each other with more practice swords. Some moved so smoothly it almost seemed they danced with one another, flowing from stance to stance, stroke to counterstroke in continuous motion. There was nothing quickly apparent aside from skill to mark them from the others, but 맷 was sure he was watching 감시자s.

Those who did not move so smoothly were all younger, each pair under the watchful eyes of an older man who seemed to radiate a dangerous grace even standing still. *감시자s and students*, 맷 decided.

He was not the only audience. Not ten paces from him, half a dozen women with ageless 에스 세다이 faces and as many more in the banded white dresses of the 허락받은 자 stood watching one pair of students, bare to the waist and slick with sweat, under the guidance of a 감시자 shaped much like a block of stone. The 감시자 used a short-stemmed pipe in one hand, trailing tabac smoke, to direct his pupils.

Sitting down cross-legged under a leatherleaf, 맷 rooted three large pebbles out of the ground and began to juggle them idly. He did not feel weak, exactly, but it was good to sit. If there was a way out of the Tower grounds, it would not go away while he took a short rest.

Before he had been there five minutes he knew who it was the 에스 세다이 and 허락받은 자 were watching. One of the blocky 감시자’s pupils was a tall, lithe young man who moved like a cat. *And almost as pretty as a girl*, 맷 thought wryly. Every woman was staring at the tall fellow with sparkling eyes, even the 에스 세다이.

The tall man handled his practice sword almost as deftly as the 감시자s, now and then earning an approving gravelly comment from his teacher. It was not that his opponent, a youth more 맷’s age, with red-gold hair, was unskilled. Far from it, as much as 맷 could see, though he had never claimed to know anything about swords. The golden-haired man met every lightning attack, turning it away before the bound strips could strike him, and even launched an occasional attack of his own. But the handsome fellow countered those attacks and flowed back into his own in the space of a heartbeat.

맷 shifted the pebbles to one hand, but kept them spinning in the air. He did not think he would care to face either of them. Certainly not with a sword.

“Break!” The 감시자’s voice sounded like rocks emptying out of a bucket. Chests heaving, the two men let their practice swords fall to their sides. Sweat matted their hair. “You can rest till I finish my pipe. But rest fast; I am almost in the dottle.”

Now that they had stopped dancing about, 맷 got a good look at the youth with the red-gold hair and let the pebbles drop. *Burn me, I’ll bet my whole purse that’s 엘레인’s brother. And the other one’s 갈라드, or I’ll eat my boots.* On the journey from Toman Head it had seemed half of 엘레인’s conversation had been of 가윈’s virtues and 갈라드’s vices. Oh, 가윈 had some vices according to 엘레인, but they were small; to 맷 they sounded like the sort of things no one but a sister would consider vices at all. As for 갈라드, once 엘레인 was pinned down, he sounded like what every mother said she wanted her son to be. 맷 did not think he wanted to spend much time in 갈라드’s company. 에그웨인 blushed whenever 갈라드 was mentioned, though she seemed to think no one noticed.

A ripple seemed to pass through the watching women when 가윈 and 갈라드 stopped, and they appeared on the point of stepping forward almost as one. But 가윈 caught sight of 맷, said something quietly to 갈라드, and the two of them walked by the women. The 에스 세다이 and 허락받은 자 turned to follow with their eyes. 맷 scrambled to his feet as the pair approached.

“You are 맷 카우톤, are you not?” 가윈 said with a grin. “I was sure I recognized you from 에그웨인’s description. And 엘레인’s. I understand you were sick. Are you better now?”

“I’m fine,” 맷 said. He wondered if he was supposed to call 가윈 “my Lord” or something of the sort. He had refused to call 엘레인 “my Lady”—not that she had demanded it, actually—and he decided he would not do her brother better.

“Did you come to the practice yard to learn the sword?” 갈라드 asked.

맷 shook his head. “I was only out walking. I don’t know much about swords. I think I’ll put my trust in a good bow, or a good quarterstaff. I know how to use those.”
“If you spend much time around 니나브,” 갈라드 said, “you’ll need bow, quarterstaff, *and* sword to protect yourself. And I don’t know whether that would be enough.”

가윈 looked at him wonderingly. “갈라드, you just very nearly made a joke.”

“I do have a sense of humor, 가윈,” 갈라드 said with a frown. “You only think I do not because I do not care to mock people.”

With a shake of his head, 가윈 turned back to 맷. “You should learn something of the sword. Everyone can do with that sort of knowledge these days. Your friend—랜드 al’Thor—carried a most unusual sword. What do you hear of him?”

“I haven’t seen 랜드 in a long time,” 맷 said quickly. Just for a moment, when he had mentioned 랜드, 가윈’s look had gained intensity. *Light, does* he *know about 랜드? He couldn’t. If he did, he’d be denouncing me for a Darkfriend just for being 랜드’s friend. But he knows something.* “Swords aren’t the be-all and end-all, you know. I could do fairly well against either of you, I think, if you had a sword and I had my quarterstaff.”

가윈’s cough was obviously meant to swallow a laugh. Much too politely, he said, “You must be very good.” 갈라드’s face was frankly disbelieving.

Perhaps it was that they both clearly thought he was making a wild boast. Perhaps it was because he had mishandled questioning the guardsman. Perhaps it was because Else, who had such an eye for the boys, wanted nothing to do with him, and all those women were staring at 갈라드 like cats watching a jug of cream. 에스 세다이 and 허락받은 자 or not, they were still women. All these explanations ran through 맷’s head, but he rejected them angrily, especially the last. He was going to do it because it would be fun. And it might earn some coin. His luck would not even have to be back.

“I will wager,” he said, “two silver marks to two from each of you that I can beat both of you at once, just the way I said. You can’t have fairer odds than that. There are two of you, and one of me, so two to one are fair odds.” He almost laughed aloud at the consternation on their faces.

“맷,” 가윈 said, “there’s no need to make wagers. You have been sick. Perhaps we will try this some time when you are stronger.”

“It would be far from a fair wager,” 갈라드 said. “I’ll not take your wager, now or later. You are from the same village as 에그웨인, are you not? I . . . I would not have her angry with me.”

“What does she have to do with it? Thump me once with one of your swords, and I will hand over a silver mark to each of you. If I thump you till you quit, you give me two each. Don’t you think you can do it?”

“This is ridiculous,” 갈라드 said. “You would have no chance against one trained swordsman, let alone two. I’ll not take such advantage.”

“Do you think that?” asked a gravel voice. The blocky 감시자 joined them, thick black eyebrows pulled down in a scowl. “You think you two are good enough with your swords to take a boy with a stick?”

“It would not be fair, 햄mar Gaidin,” 갈라드 said.

“He has been sick,” 가윈 added. “There is no need for this.”

“To the yard,” 햄mar grated with a jerk of his head back over his shoulder. 갈라드 and 가윈 gave 맷 regretful looks, then obeyed. The 감시자 eyed 맷 up and down doubtfully. “Are you sure you’re up to this, lad? Now I take a close look at you, you ought to be in a sickbed.”

“I am already out of one,” 맷 said, “and I’m up to it. I have to be. I don’t want to lose my two marks.”

햄mar’s heavy brows rose in surprise. “You mean to hold to that wager, lad?”

“I need the money.” 맷 laughed.

His laughter cut off abruptly as he turned toward the nearest stand that held quarterstaffs and his knees almost buckled. He stiffened them so quickly he thought anyone who noticed would think he had just stumbled. At the stand he took his time choosing out a staff, nearly two inches thick and almost a foot taller than he was. *I have to win this. I opened my fool mouth, and now I have to win. I can’t afford to lose those two marks. Without those to build on, it will take forever to win the money I need.*

When he turned back, the quarterstaff in both hands before him, 가윈 and 갈라드 were already waiting out where they had been practicing. *I have to win.* “Luck,” he muttered. “Time to toss the dice.”

햄mar gave him an odd look. “You speak the 고대어, lad?”

맷 stared back at him for a moment, not speaking. He felt cold to the bone. With an effort, he made his feet start out onto the practice yard. “Remember the wager,” he said loudly. “Two silver marks from each of you against two from me.”

A buzz rose from the 허락받은 자 as they realized what was happening. The 에스 세다이 watched in silence. Disapproving silence.

가윈 and 갈라드 split apart, one to either side of him, keeping their distance, neither with his sword more than half-raised.

“No wager,” 가윈 said. “There’s no wager.”

At the same time, 갈라드 said, “I’ll not take your money like this.”

“I mean to take yours,” 맷 said.

“Done!” 햄mar roared. “If they have not the nerve to cover your wager, lad, I’ll pay the score myself.”

“Very well,” 가윈 said. “If you insist on it—done!”

갈라드 hesitated a moment more before growling, “Done, then. Let us put an end to this farce.”

The moment’s warning was all 맷 needed. As 갈라드 rushed at him, he slid his hands along the quarterstaff and pivoted. The end of the staff thudded into the tall man’s ribs, bringing a grunt and a stumble. 맷 let the staff bounce off 갈라드 and spun, carrying it on around just as 가윈 came within range. The staff dipped, darted under 가윈’s practice sword, and clipped his ankle out from under him. As 가윈 fell, 맷 completed the spin in time to catch 갈라드 across his upraised wrist, sending his practice sword flying. As if his wrist did not pain him at all, 갈라드 threw himself into a smooth, rolling dive and came up with his sword in both hands.

Ignoring him for the moment, 맷 half turned, twisting his wrists to whip the length of the staff back beside him. 가윈, just starting to rise, took the blow on the side of his head with a loud thump only partly softened by the padding of hair. He went down in a heap.

맷 was only vaguely aware of an 에스 세다이 rushing out to tend 엘레인’s fallen brother. *I hope he’s all right. He should be. I’ve hit myself harder than that falling off a fence.* He still had 갈라드 to deal with, and from the way 갈라드 was poised on the balls of his feet, sword raised precisely, he had begun to take 맷 seriously.

맷’s legs chose that moment to tremble. *Light, I can’t weaken now.* But he could feel it creeping back in, the wobbly feeling, the hunger as if he had not eaten for days. *If I wait for him to come to me, I’ll fall on my face.* It was hard to keep his knees straight as he started forward. *Luck, stay with me.*

From the first blow, he knew that luck, or skill, or whatever had brought him this far, was still there. 갈라드 managed to turn that one with a sharp clack, and the next, and the next, and the next, but strain stiffened his face. That smooth swordsman, almost as good as the 감시자s, fought with every ounce of his skill to keep 맷’s staff from him. He did not attack; it was all he could do to defend. He moved continually to the side, trying not to be forced back, and 맷 pressed him, staff a blur. And 갈라드 stepped back, stepped back again, wooden blade a thin shield against the quarterstaff.

Hunger gnawed at 맷 as if he had swallowed weasels. Sweat rolled down into his eyes, and his strength began to fade as if it leached out with the sweat. *Not yet. I can’t fall yet. I have to win. Now.* With a roar, he threw all his reserves into one last surge.

The quarterstaff flickered past 갈라드’s sword and in quick succession struck knee, wrist, and ribs and finally thrust into 갈라드’s stomach like a spear. With a groan, 갈라드 folded over, fighting not to fall. The staff quivered in 맷’s hands, on the point of a final crushing thrust to the throat. 갈라드 sank to the ground.

맷 almost dropped the quarterstaff when he realized what he had been about to do. *Win, not kill. Light, what was I thinking?* Reflexively he grounded the butt of the staff, and as soon he did, he had to clutch at it to hold himself erect. Hunger hollowed him like a knife reaming marrow from a bone. Suddenly he realized that not only the 에스 세다이 and 허락받은 자 were watching. All practice, all learning, had stopped. 감시자s and students alike stood watching him.

햄mar moved to stand beside 갈라드, still groaning on the ground and trying to push himself up. The 감시자 raised his voice to shout, “Who was the greatest blademaster of all time?”

From the throats of dozens of students came a massed bellow. “Jearom, Gaidin!”

“Yes!” 햄mar shouted, turning to make sure all heard. “During his lifetime, Jearom fought over ten thousand times, in battle and single combat. He was defeated once. By a farmer with a quarterstaff! Remember that. Remember what you just saw.” He lowered his eyes to 갈라드, and lowered his voice as well. “If you cannot get up by now, lad, it is finished.” He raised a hand, and the 에스 세다이 and 허락받은 자 rushed to surround 갈라드.

맷 slid down the staff to his knees. None of the 에스 세다이 even glanced his way. One of the 허락받은 자 did, a plump girl he might have liked to ask for a dance if she were not going to be an 에스 세다이. She frowned at him, sniffed, and turned back to peering at what the 에스 세다이 were doing around 갈라드.

가윈 was on his feet, 맷 noted with relief. He pulled himself up as 가윈 came over. *Mustn’t let them know. I’ll never get out of here if they decide to nurse me from sunup to sunup.* Blood darkened the red-gold hair on the side of 가윈’s head, but there was neither cut nor bruise apparent.

He pushed two silver marks into 맷’s hand with a dry “I think I will listen next time.” He noticed 맷’s glance, touched his head. “They Healed it, but it was not bad. 엘레인 has given me worse more than once. You are good with that.”

“Not as good as my da. He’s won the quarterstaff at Bel Tine every year as long as I can remember, except once or twice when 랜드’s da did.” That interested look came back into 가윈’s eyes, and 맷 wished he had never mentioned Tam al’Thor. The 에스 세다이 and the 허락받은 자 were all still clustered around 갈라드. “I . . . I must have hurt him badly. I did not mean to do that.”

가윈 glanced that way—there was nothing to be seen but two rings of women’s backs, 허락받은 자’s white dresses making the outer ring as they peered over the shoulders of crouching 에스 세다이—and laughed. “You did not kill him—I heard him groaning—so he should be on his feet by now, but they are not going to let this chance pass, now they have their hands on him. Light, four of them are 녹색 아자!” 맷 gave him a confused look—*녹색 아자? What does that have to do with anything?*—and 가윈 shook his head. “It doesn’t matter. Just rest assured that the worst 갈라드 has to worry about is finding himself 감시자 to a Green 에스 세다이 before his head clears.” He laughed. “No, they would not do that. But I will wager you those two marks of mine in your hand that some of them wish they could.”

“Not your marks,” 맷 said, shoving them in his coat pocket, “mine.” The explanation had made little sense to him. Except that 갈라드 was well. All he knew of what passed between 감시자s and 에스 세다이 were the pieces he remembered of 란 and 모이라인, and there was nothing there like what 가윈 seemed to be suggesting. “Do you think they’d mind if I collected my wager from him?”

“They very likely would,” 햄mar said dryly as he joined them. “You are not very popular with those particular 에스 세다이 right now.” He snorted. “You’d think even Green 에스 세다이 would be better than girls just loose from their mother’s apron strings. He isn’t *that* good-looking.”

“He is not,” 맷 agreed.

가윈 grinned at both of them, until 햄mar glared at him. “Here,” the 감시자 said, pushing two more silver coins into 맷’s hand. “I will collect from 갈라드 later. Where are you from, lad?”

“Manetheren.” 맷 froze when he heard the name come out of his mouth. “I mean, I’m from the 두 강. I have heard too many old stories.” They just looked at him without saying anything. “I. . . . I think I will go back and see if I can find something to eat.” Not even the Midmorning bell had rung yet, but they nodded as if it made sense.

He kept the quarterstaff—no one had told him to put it back—and walked slowly until the trees hid him from the practice yard. When they did, he leaned on the staff as though it were the only thing holding him up. He was not sure it was not.

He thought that if he parted his coat, he would see a hole where his stomach should have been, a hole growing larger as it pulled the rest of him in. But he hardly thought of hunger. He kept hearing voices in his head. *You speak the 고대어, lad? Manetheren.* It made him shiver. *Light help me, I keep digging myself deeper. I have to get out of here. But how?* He hobbled back toward the Tower proper like an old, old man. *How?*

CHAPTER 25

![](images/00093.jpg)

*Questions*

에그웨인 lay across 니나브’s bed, chin in her hands, watching 니나브 pace back and forth. 엘레인 sprawled in front of the fireplace, which was still full of the ashes of last night’s fire. Yet again 엘레인 was studying the list of names Verin had produced, patiently reading every word one more time. The other pages, the list of *ter’angreal*, sat on the table; after one shocked reading they had not discussed that one further, though they had talked of everything else. And argued, too.

에그웨인 stifled a yawn. It was only the middle of the morning, but none of them had gotten much sleep. They had had to be up early. For the kitchens, and breakfast. For other things that she refused to think about. The little sleep she herself had managed had been filled with unpleasant dreams. *Maybe Anaiya could help me understand them, those that need understanding, but. . . . But what if she is 흑색 아자?* After staring at every woman in that chamber last night, wondering which was 흑색 아자, she was finding trust for anyone but her two companions hard to come by. But she did wish she had some way of interpreting those dreams.

The nightmares about what had happened inside the *ter’angreal* last night were easy enough to understand, though they had made her wake up weeping. She had dreamed of the 쇼엔찬, too, of women in dresses with lightning bolts woven on their breasts, collaring a long line of women who wore Great Serpent rings, forcing them to call lightning against the 백색 탑. That had started her awake in a cold sweat, but that had to be just a nightmare, too. And the dream about 백의단 binding her father’s hands. A nightmare brought on by homesickness, she supposed. But the others. . . .

She glanced at the other two women again. 엘레인 was still reading. 니나브 still paced with that steady tread.

There had been a dream of 랜드, reaching for a sword that seemed to be made of crystal, never seeing the fine net dropping over him. And one of him kneeling in a chamber where a parched wind blew dust across the floor, and creatures like the one on the Dragon banner, but much smaller, floated on that wind, and settled into his skin. There had been a dream of him walking down into a great hole in a black mountain, a hole filled with a reddish glare as from vast fires below, and even a dream of him confronting 쇼엔찬.

About that last, she was uncertain, but she knew the others had to mean something. Back when she had been sure she could trust Anaiya, back before she had left the Tower, before she learned the reality of the 흑색 아자, a little cautious questioning of the 에스 세다이—done, oh, so carefully, so Anaiya would think it no more than the curiosity she showed about other things—had revealed that a Dreamer’s dreams about *ta’veren* were almost always significant, and the more strongly *ta’veren*, the more “almost always” became “certainly.”

But 맷 and 페린 were *ta’veren*, too, and she had also dreamed of them. Odd dreams, even more difficult to understand than the dreams of 랜드. 페린 with a falcon on his shoulder, and 페린 with a hawk. Only the hawk held a leash in her talons—에그웨인 was somehow convinced both hawk and falcon were female—and the hawk was trying to fasten it around 페린’s neck. That made her shiver even now; she did not like dreams about leashes. And that dream of 페린—with a beard!—leading a huge pack of wolves that stretched as far as the eye could see. Those about 맷 had been even nastier. 맷, placing his own left eye on a balance scale. 맷, hanging by his neck from a tree limb. There had been a dream of 맷 and 쇼엔찬, too, but she was willing to dismiss that as a nightmare. It had to have been just a nightmare. Just like the one about 맷 speaking the 고대어. That had to come from what she had heard during his 치유.

She sighed, and the sigh turned into another yawn. She and the others had gone to his room after breakfast to see how he was, but he had not been there.

*He is probably well enough to go dancing. Light, now I will probably dream about him dancing with 쇼엔찬! No more dreams*, she told herself firmly. *Not now. I will think about them when I am not so tired.* She thought of the kitchens, of the midday meal soon to come, and then supper, and breakfast again tomorrow, and pots and cleaning and scrubbing going on forever. *If I am ever not tired again.* Shifting her position on the bed, she looked at her friends again. 엘레인 still had her eyes on the list of names. 니나브’s steps had slowed. *Any moment now, 니나브 will say it again. Any moment.*

니나브 came to a halt, staring down at 엘레인. “Put those away. We have been over them twenty times, and there isn’t a word that helps. Verin gave us rubbish. The question is, was it all she had, or did she give us rubbish on purpose?”

*As expected. Maybe half an hour till she says it again.* 에그웨인 frowned down at her hands, glad she could not see them clearly. 거대한 뱀 ring looked—out of place—on hands all wrinkled from long immersion in hot, soapy water.

“Knowing their names helps,” 엘레인 said, still reading. “Knowing what they look like helps.”

“You know very well what I mean,” 니나브 snapped.

에그웨인 sighed and folded her arms in front of her, rested her chin on them. When she had come out of 셰리암’s study that morning, with the sun still not even a glint on the horizon, 니나브 had been waiting with a candle in the cold, dark hall. She had not been seeing very clearly, but she was sure 니나브 had looked ready to chew stone. And knowing chewing stones would not change anything in the next few minutes. That was why she was so irritable. *She’s as touchy about her pride as any man I ever met. But she should not take it out on 엘레인 and me. Light, if 엘레인 can stand it, she should be able to. She isn’t the Wisdom anymore.*

엘레인 hardly appeared to notice whether 니나브 was irritable or not. She frowned into the distance thoughtfully. “Liandrin was the only Red. All the other 아자s lost two each.”

“Oh, do be quiet, child,” 니나브 said.

엘레인 wiggled her left hand to display her Great Serpent ring, gave 니나브 a meaningful look, and went right on. “No two were born in the same city, and no more than two in any one country. Amico Nagoyin was the youngest, some fifteen years older than 에그웨인 and I. Joiya Byir could be our great-grandmother’s great-grandmother.”

에그웨인 did not like it that one of the 흑색 아자 shared her daughter’s name. *Fool girl! People sometimes have the same name, and you never had a daughter. It wasn’t real!*

“And what does that tell us?” 니나브’s voice was too calm; she was ready to explode like a wagon full of 불꽃놀이. “What secrets have you found in it that I missed? I am getting old and blind, after all!”

“It tells us it is all too neat,” 엘레인 said calmly. “What chance that thirteen women chosen solely because they were 어둠의 친구들 would be so neatly arrayed across age, across nations, across 아자s? Shouldn’t there be perhaps three Reds, or four born in 케렌, or just two the same age, if it was all chance? They had women to choose from or they could not have chosen so random a pattern. There are still 흑색 아자 in the Tower, or elsewhere we don’t know about. It must mean that.”

니나브 gave her braid one ferocious tug. “Light! I think you may be right. You did find secrets I couldn’t. Light, I was hoping they all went with Liandrin.”

“We do not even know that she is their leader,” 엘레인 said. “She could have been ordered to . . . to *dispose* of us.” Her mouth twisted. “I am afraid I can only think of one reason for them to go to such lengths to spread everything out so, to avoid any pattern except a lack of pattern. I think it means there *is* a pattern of some kind to the 흑색 아자.”

“If there’s a pattern,” 니나브 said firmly, “we will find it. 엘레인, if watching your mother run her court taught you to think like this, I’m glad you watched closely.” 엘레인’s answering smile made a dimple in her cheek.

에그웨인 eyed the older woman carefully. It seemed 니나브 was finally ready to stop being a bear with a sore tooth. She raised her head. “Unless they want us to think they’re hiding a pattern, so we will waste our time hunting for it when there isn’t one. I am not saying there isn’t; I am only saying we do not know yet. Let’s look for it, but I think we ought to look at other things, too, don’t you?”

“So you finally decided to rouse,” 니나브 said. “I thought you had gone to sleep.” But she was still smiling.

“She is right,” 엘레인 said disgustedly. “I have built a bridge out of straw. Worse than straw. Wishes. Maybe you are right, too, 니나브. What use is this—this rubbish?” She snatched one paper out of the stack in front of her. “Rianna has black hair with a white streak above her left ear. If I am close enough to see that, it’s closer than I want to be.” She grabbed another page. “Chesmal Emry is one of the most talented Healers anyone has seen in years. Light, could you imagine being Healed by one of the 흑색 아자?” A third sheet. “Marillin Gemalphin is fond of cats and goes out of her way to help injured animals. Cats! Paah!” She scrabbled all the pages together, crumpling them in her fists. “It *is* useless rubbish.”

니나브 knelt beside her and gently pried her hands from around the papers. “Perhaps, and perhaps not.” She smoothed the pages carefully on her breast. “You found in them something for us to look for. Perhaps we will find more, if we are persistent. And there is the other list.” Both her eyes and 엘레인’s darted to 에그웨인, brown and blue alike frowning worriedly.

에그웨인 avoided looking at the table where the other sheets lay. She did not want to think about them, but she could not avoid it. The list of *ter’angreal* had etched itself into her mind.

Item. A rod of clear crystal, smooth and perfectly clear, one foot long and one inch in diameter. Use unknown. Last study made by Corianin Nedeal. Item. A figurine of an unclothed woman in alabaster, one hand tall. Use unknown. Last study made by Corianin Nedeal. Item. A disc, apparently of simple iron yet untouched by rust, three inches in diameter, finely engraved on both sides with a tight spiral. Use unknown. Last study made by Corianin Nedeal. Item. Too many items, and more than half the “use unknowns” last studied by Corianin Nedeal. Thirteen of them, to be exact.

에그웨인 shivered. *It’s getting so I do not even like to think of that number.*

The knowns on the list were fewer, not all of any apparent real use, but hardly more comforting, as she saw it. A wooden carving of a hedgehog, no bigger than the last joint of a man’s thumb. Such a simple thing, and surely harmless. Any woman who tried to channel through it went to sleep. Half a day of peaceful, dreamless sleep, but it was too close not to make her skin crawl. Three more had to do with sleep in some way. It was almost a relief to read of a fluted rod of black stone, a full pace in length, that produced balefire, with the notation DANGEROUS AND ALMOST IMPOSSIBLE TO CONTROL writ so strong in Verin’s hand that it tore the paper in two places. 에그웨인 still had no idea what balefire was, but though it surely sounded dangerous if anything ever did, it just as surely had nothing to do Corianin Nedeal or dreams.

니나브 carried the smoothed-out pages to the table and set them down. She hesitated before spreading the others out and running her finger down one page, then the next. “Here’s one 맷 would enjoy,” she said in a voice much too light and airy. “Item. A carved cluster of six spotted dice, joined at the corners, less than two inches across. Use unknown, save that channeling through it seems to suspend chance in some way, or twist it.” She began to read aloud. “ ‘Tossed coins presented the same face every time, and in one test landed balanced on edge one hundred times in a row. One thousand tosses of the dice produced five crowns one thousand times.’ ” She gave a forced laugh. “맷 would love that.”

에그웨인 sighed and got to her feet, walked stiffly to the fireplace. 엘레인 scrambled up, watching as silently as 니나브. Pushing her sleeve as far up her arm as it would go, 에그웨인 reached carefully up the chimney. Her fingers touched wool on the smoke shelf, and she pulled out a wadded, singed stocking with a hard lump in the toe. She brushed a smear of soot from her arm, then took the stocking to the table and shook it out. The twisted ring of striped, flecked stone spun across the tabletop and fell flat atop a page of the *ter’angreal* list. For a few moments they just stared at it.

“Perhaps,” 니나브 said finally, “Verin simply missed the fact that so many of them were last studied by Corianin.” She did not sound as if she really believed it.

엘레인 nodded, but doubtfully. “I saw her walking in the rain once, soaking wet, and took a cloak to her. She was so wrapped up in whatever she was thinking, I do not believe she knew it was raining until I put the cloak around her shoulders. She could have missed it.”

“Maybe,” 에그웨인 said. “If she did not, she had to know I’d notice as soon as I read the list. I do not know. Sometimes I think Verin notices more than she lets on. I just do not know.”
“So there’s Verin to suspect,” 엘레인 sighed. “If she is 흑색 아자, then they know exactly what we are doing. And Alanna.” She gave 에그웨인 an uncertain, sidelong look.

에그웨인 had told them everything. Except what happened inside the *ter’angreal* during her testing; she could not bring herself to talk about that, any more than 니나브 or 엘레인 could tell of their testings. Everything that happened in the testing chamber, what 셰리암 had said about the terrible weakness conferred by the ability to channel, every word Verin had said, whether it seemed important or not. The one part they had had trouble accepting was Alanna; 에스 세다이 just did not do things like that. No one in her right mind did anything like that, but 에스 세다이 least of all.

에그웨인 glowered at them, almost hearing them say it. “에스 세다이 are not supposed to lie, either, but Verin and the Mother seem awfully close with what they tell us. There are not *supposed* to be 흑색 아자.”

“I like Alanna.” 니나브 tugged her braid, then shrugged. “Oh, very well. Perha—That is, she did behave oddly.”

“Thank you,” 에그웨인 said, and 니나브 gave her an acknowledging nod as if she had heard no sarcasm.

“In any case, the Amyrlin knows of it, and she can keep an eye on Alanna far more easily than we can.”

“What about 엘라이더 and 셰리암?” 에그웨인 asked.

“I have never been able to like 엘라이더,” 엘레인 said, “but I cannot truly believe she is 흑색 아자. And 셰리암? It’s impossible.”

니나브 snorted. “It should be impossible for any of them. When we do find them, there is nothing says they’ll all be women we do not like. But I don’t mean to put suspicion—not this kind of suspicion!—on any woman. We need more to go on than that they might have seen something they shouldn’t.” 에그웨인 nodded agreement as quickly as 엘레인, and 니나브 went on: “We will tell the Amyrlin that much, and put no more weight to it than it deserves. If she ever looks in on us as she said she would. If you are with us when she comes, 엘레인, remember she does not know about you.”

“I am not likely to forget it,” 엘레인 said fervently. “But we should have some other way to get word to her. My mother would have planned it better.”

“Not if she could not trust her messengers,” 니나브 said. “We will wait. Unless you two think one of us should have a talk with Verin? No one would think that remarkable.”

엘레인 hesitated, then gave her head a small shake. 에그웨인 was quicker and more vigorous with hers; slip of the mind or not, Verin had left out too much to be trusted.

“Good.” 니나브 sounded more than satisfied. “I am just as pleased we cannot talk to the Amyrlin when we choose. This way we make our own decisions, act when and as we decide, without her directing our every step.” Her hand ran down the pages listing stolen *ter’angreal* as if she were reading it again, then closed on the striped stone ring. “And the first decision concerns this. It’s the first thing we have seen that has any real connection to Liandrin and the others.” She frowned at the ring, then took a deep breath. “I am going to sleep with it tonight.”

에그웨인 did not hesitate before taking the ring out of 니나브’s hand. She wanted to hesitate—she wanted to keep her hands by her sides—but she did not, and she was pleased. “I am the one they say might be a Dreamer. I do not know whether that gives me any advantage, but Verin said it’s dangerous using this. Whichever of us uses it, she needs any advantage she can find.”

니나브 gripped her braid and opened her mouth as if to protest. When she finally spoke, though, it was to say, “Are you sure, 에그웨인? We do not even know if you *are* a Dreamer, and I can channel more strongly than you. I still think I—” 에그웨인 cut her off.

“You can channel more strongly if you are angry. Can you be sure you’ll be angry in a dream? Will you have time to become angry before you need to channel? Light, we don’t even know that anyone can channel in a dream. If one of us has to do it—and you are right; it is the only connection we have—it should be me. Maybe I really am a Dreamer. Besides, Verin did give it to me.”

니나브 looked as if she wanted to argue, but at last she gave a grudging nod. “Very well. But 엘레인 and I will be there. I do not know what we can do, but if anything goes wrong, perhaps we can wake you up, or. . . . We will be there.” 엘레인 nodded, too.

Now that she had their agreement, 에그웨인 felt a queasiness in the pit of her stomach. *I talked them into it. I wish I did not want them to talk me out of it.* She became aware of a woman standing in the doorway, a woman in 수련생 white, with her hair in long braids.

“Did no one ever teach you to knock, Else?” 니나브 said.

에그웨인 hid the stone ring inside her fist. She had the strangest feeling that Else had been staring at it.

“I have a message for you,” Else said calmly. Her eyes studied the table, with all the papers scattered on it, then the three women around it. “From the Amyrlin.”

에그웨인 exchanged wondering looks with 니나브 and 엘레인.

“Well, what is it?” 니나브 demanded.

Else arched an eyebrow in amusement. “The belongings left behind by Liandrin and the others were put in the third storeroom on the right from the main stairs in the second basement under the library.” She glanced at the papers on the table again and left, neither hurrying nor moving slowly.

에그웨인 felt as if she could not breathe. *We’re afraid to trust anybody, and the Amyrlin decides to trust Else Grinwell of all women?*

“That fool girl cannot be trusted not to blab to anyone who’ll listen!” 니나브 started for the door.

에그웨인 grabbed up her skirts and darted past her at a run. Her shoes skidded on the tiles of the gallery, but she caught a glimpse of white vanishing down the nearest ramp and dashed after it. *She must be running, too, to be so far ahead already. Why is she running?* The flash of white was already disappearing down another ramp. 에그웨인 followed.

A woman turned to face her at the foot of the ramp, and 에그웨인 stopped in confusion. Whoever she was, this was certainly not Else. All in silver and white silk, she sparked feelings 에그웨인 had never had before. She was taller, more beautiful by far, and the look in her black eyes made 에그웨인 feel small, scrawny, and none too clean. *She can probably channel more of the Power than I can, too. Light, she is probably smarter than all three of us put together on top of it. It isn’t fair for one woman to*—Abruptly she realized the way her thoughts were going. Her cheeks reddened, and she gave herself a shake. She had never felt—less—than any other woman before, and she was not about to start now.

“Bold,” the woman said. “You are bold to go running about so, alone, where so many murders have been done.” She sounded almost pleased.

에그웨인 drew herself up and straightened her dress hurriedly, hoping the other woman would not notice, knowing she did, wishing the woman had not seen her running like a child. *Stop that!* “Pardon, but I am looking for a 수련생 who came this way, I think. She has large, dark eyes and dark hair in braids. She’s plump, and pretty in a way. Did you see which way she went?”

The tall woman looked her up and down in an amused way. 에그웨인 could not be sure, but she thought the woman might have glanced a moment at the clenched fist by her side, where she still held the stone ring. “I do not think you will catch up to her. I saw her, and she was running quite fast. I suspect she is far away from here by now.”

“에스 세다이,” 에그웨인 began, but she was given no chance to ask which way Else had gone. Something that might have been anger, or annoyance, flashed through those black eyes.

“I have taken up enough time with you for now. I have more important matters to see to. Leave me.” She gestured back the way 에그웨인 had come.

So strong was the command in her voice that 에그웨인 turned and was three steps up the ramp before she realized what she was doing. Bristling, she spun back. *에스 세다이 or no, I—*

The gallery was empty.

Frowning, she dismissed the nearest doors—no one lived in those rooms, except possibly mice—and ran down the ramp, peered both ways, followed the curve of the gallery with her eyes all the way around. She even peered over the rail, down into the small Garden of the 허락받은 자, and studied the other galleries, higher as well as lower. She saw two 허락받은 자 in their banded dresses, one Faolain and the other a woman she knew by sight if not name. But there was no woman in silver and white anywhere.
