CHAPTER 6

![](images/00583.jpg)

*Doorways*

“랜드 al’Thor,” 모이라인 told the air in a low, tight voice, “is a mule-headed, stone-willed fool of a . . . a . . . a man!”

엘레인 lifted her chin angrily. Her childhood nurse, Lini, used to say you could weave silk from pig bristles before you could make a man anything but a man. But that was no excuse for 랜드.

“We breed them that way in the 두 강.” 니나브 was suddenly all half-suppressed smiles and satisfaction. She seldom hid her dislike of the 에스 세다이 half as well as she thought she did. “두 강 women never have any trouble with them.” From the startled look 에그웨인 gave her, that was a lie big enough to warrant having her mouth washed out.

모이라인’s brows drew down as if she were about to reply to 니나브 in harder kind. 엘레인 stirred, but she could not find anything to say that would head off argument. 랜드 kept dancing through her head. He had no right! But what right did she have?

에그웨인 spoke instead. “What did he do, 모이라인?”

The 에스 세다이’s eyes swung to 에그웨인, a stare so hard that the younger woman stepped back and snapped her fan open, nervously fluttering it at her face. But 모이라인’s gaze settled on Joiya and Amico, the one watching her warily, the other bound and unaware of anything but the far wall.

엘레인 gave a small start at realizing Joiya was not bound. Hastily she checked the shield blocking the woman from the True Source. She hoped none of the others had noticed her jump; Joiya frightened her nearly to death, but 에그웨인 and 니나브 were no more scared of the woman than 모이라인 was. Sometimes it was difficult being as brave as the Daughter-Heir of 안도르 should be; she often found herself wishing she could manage as well as those two.

“The guards,” 모이라인 muttered as if to herself. “I saw them in the corridor still, and never thought.” She smoothed her dress, composing herself with an obvious effort. 엘레인 did not believe she had ever seen 모이라인 so out of herself as tonight. But then, the 에스 세다이 had cause. *No more than I do. Or do I?* She found herself trying not to meet 에그웨인’s eyes.

Had it been 에그웨인 or 니나브 or 엘레인 who was off balance, Joiya would surely have said something, subtle and of two meanings, calculated to upset them a little more. If they had been alone, at least. With 모이라인, she only watched uneasily, silently.

모이라인 walked the length of the table, her calm restored. Joiya was nearly a head the taller, but had she also been dressed in silks, there would have been no doubt which was in command of the situation. Joiya did not quite draw back, but her hands tightened on her skirts for a moment before she could master them.

“I have made arrangements,” 모이라인 said quietly. “In four days you will be taken upriver by ship, to 타르 발론 and the Tower. There they are not so gentle as we have been. If you have not found the truth so far, find it before you reach Southharbor, or you will assuredly go to the gallows in the Traitors’ Court. I will not speak to you again unless you send word that you have something new to tell. And I do not want to hear a word from you—not one word—unless it *is* new. Believe me, it will save you pain in 타르 발론. 아비엔다, will you tell the captain to bring in two of his men?” 엘레인 blinked as the 아일 woman unfolded herself and vanished through the doorway; sometimes 아비엔다 could be so still she seemed not to be there.

Joiya’s face worked as if she wanted to speak, but 모이라인 stared up at her, and finally the Darkfriend turned her eyes away. They glittered like a raven’s, full of black murder, but she held her tongue.

To 엘레인’s eyes a golden-white glow suddenly surrounded 모이라인, the glow of a woman embracing *세다르*. Only another woman trained to channel could have seen it. The flows holding Amico unraveled more quickly than 엘레인 could have managed. She was stronger than 모이라인, potentially, at least. In the Tower, the women teaching her had been almost unbelieving at her potential, and at 에그웨인’s and 니나브’s. 니나브 was the strongest of them all—when she could manage to channel. But 모이라인 had the experience. What they were still learning to do, 모이라인 could do half asleep. Yet there were some things 엘레인 could do, and the other two, that the 에스 세다이 could not. It was a small satisfaction in the face of how easily 모이라인 cowed Joiya.

Freed, able to hear, Amico turned and became aware of 모이라인 for the first time. With a squeak, she dropped a curtsy as deep as any new 수련생. Joiya was glaring at the door, avoiding anyone’s gaze. 니나브, arms crossed and knuckles white from gripping her braid, was giving 모이라인 a stare almost as murderous as Joiya’s. 에그웨인 fingered her skirt and glowered at Joiya; 엘레인 frowned, wishing she were as brave as 에그웨인, wishing she did not feel she was betraying her friend. Into that walked the captain with two more Defenders in black and gold on his heels. 아비엔다 was not with them; it seemed she had taken her opportunity to escape 에스 세다이.

The grizzled officer, two short white plumes on his rimmed helmet, shied as his eyes met Joiya’s, though she did not even seem to see him. His gaze skittered from woman to woman uncertainly. The mood of the room was trouble, and a wise man did not want any part of trouble among this sort of women. The two soldiers clutched their tall spears to their sides almost as if they feared they might have to defend themselves. Perhaps they did fear it.

“You will take these two back to their cells,” 모이라인 told the officer curtly. “Repeat your instructions. I want no mistakes.”

“Yes, Ae—” The captain’s throat seemed to seize. He gulped a breath. “Yes, my Lady,” he said, watching her anxiously to see if that would do. When she only continued to look at him, waiting, he gave an audible sigh of relief. “The prisoners are to talk to no one except myself, not even each other. Twenty men in the guardroom and two outside each cell at all times, four if a cell door has to be opened for any reason. I myself will watch their food prepared and take it to them. All as you have commanded, my Lady.” A hint of question tinged his voice. A hundred rumors floated through the Stone concerning the prisoners, and why two women needed to be guarded so heavily. And there were whispered stories about the 에스 세다이, each darker than the last.

“Very good,” 모이라인 said. “Take them.”

It was not clear who was more eager to leave the room, the prisoners or the guards. Even Joiya stepped quickly, as if she could not bear keeping silent near 모이라인 for another moment.

엘레인 was certain she had kept her face calm since entering the room, but 에그웨인 came to her, put an arm around her. “What is the matter, 엘레인? You look about to cry.”

The concern in her voice made 엘레인 feel like bursting into tears. *Light*! she thought. *I will not be that silly. I will not! “A weeping woman is a bucket with no bottom.”* Lini had been full of sayings like that.

“Three times—” 니나브 burst out at 모이라인, “only three!—you have consented to help us question them. This time you vanish before we begin, and now you calmly announce you are sending them off to 타르 발론! If you will not help, at least do not interfere!”

“Do not presume on the Amyrlin’s authority too far,” 모이라인 said coolly. “She may have set you to chase Liandrin, but you are still only 허락받은 자, and woefully ignorant, whatever letters you carry. Or did you mean to keep questioning them forever before reaching a decision? You 두 강 people seem to work at avoiding decisions that must be made.” 니나브 opened and closed her mouth, eyes bulging, as if wondering which accusation to answer first, but 모이라인 turned to 에그웨인 and 엘레인. “Pull yourself together, 엘레인. How you can carry out the Amyrlin’s orders if you think every land has the customs you were born to, I do not know. And I do not know why you are so upset. Do not let your feelings hurt others.”

“What do you mean?” 에그웨인 said. “What customs? What are you talking about?”

“Berelain was in 랜드’s chambers,” 엘레인 said in a small voice before she could stop herself. Her eyes flickered guiltily toward 에그웨인. Surely she had kept her own feelings hidden.

모이라인 gave her a reproachful look and sighed. “I would have spared you this if I could, 에그웨인. If 엘레인 had not let her disgust with Berelain overcome her sense. The customs of Mayene are not those either of you were born to. 에그웨인, I know what you feel for 랜드, but you must realize by now that nothing can come of it. He belongs to the Pattern, and to history.”

Seemingly ignoring the 에스 세다이, 에그웨인 peered into 엘레인’s eyes. 엘레인 wanted to look away, and could not. Suddenly 에그웨인 leaned closer, whispering behind a cupped hand. “I love him. Like a brother. And you like a sister. I wish you well of him.”

엘레인’s eyes widened, a smile spreading slowly across her face. She answered 에그웨인’s hug with a fierce hug of her own. “Thank you,” she murmured softly. “I love you too, sister. Oh, thank you.”

“She got it wrong,” 에그웨인 said half to herself, a delighted grin blooming on her face. “Have you ever been in love, 모이라인?”

What a startling question. 엘레인 could not imagine the 에스 세다이 in love. 모이라인 was 청색 아자, and it was said Blue sisters gave all their passions to causes.

The slender woman was not at all taken aback. For a long moment she looked levelly at the pair of them, each with an arm around the other. Finally she said, “I could wager I know the face of the man I will marry better than either of you knows that of your future husband.”

에그웨인 gaped in surprise.

“Who?” 엘레인 gasped.

The 에스 세다이 appeared regretful of having spoken. “Perhaps I only meant we share an ignorance. Do not read too much into a few words.” She looked at 니나브 consideringly. “Should I ever choose a man—should, I say—it will not be 란. That much I will say.”

That was a sop to 니나브, but 니나브 did not seem to like hearing it. 니나브 had what Lini would have called “a hard patch to hoe,” loving not just a 감시자 but a man who tried to deny returning her love. Fool man that he was, he talked of the war against the Shadow he could not stop fighting and could never win, of refusing to dress 니나브 in widow’s clothes for her wedding feast. Silly things of that sort. 엘레인 did not see how 니나브 put up with it. She was not a very patient woman.

“If you are finished chatting about men,” 니나브 said acidly, as though to prove just that, “perhaps we can go back to what is important?” Gripping her braid hard, she picked up speed and force as she went along, like a waterwheel with the gears disengaged. “How are we to decide whether Joiya is lying, or Amico, if you send them away? Or whether they both are? Or neither? I don’t relish dithering here, 모이라인, no matter what you think, but I have walked into too many traps to want to walk into another. And I don’t want to run after Jak-o’-the-Wisps, either. I . . . we . . . are the ones the Amyrlin sent after Liandrin and her cronies. Since you don’t seem to think they are important enough to spare more than a moment to help us, the least you can do is not crack our ankles with a broom!”

She seemed about to rip that braid free and try to strangle the 에스 세다이 with it, and 모이라인 wore a dangerously cool crystalline calm that suggested she might be ready to teach again the lesson on holding her tongue that she had taught Joiya. It was, 엘레인 decided, time for her to stop moping. She did not know how she had fallen into the role of peacemaker among these women—sometimes she wanted to take them all by the scruff of the neck and shake them—but her mother always said no good decision was ever made in anger. “You might add to your list of what you want to know,” she said, “why were we summoned to 랜드? That is where Careen took us. He is all right, now, of course. 모이라인 Healed him.” She could not repress a shudder, thinking of her brief glimpse inside his chamber, but the diversion worked a charm.

“Healed!” 니나브 gasped. “What happened to him?”

“He almost died,” the 에스 세다이 said, as calmly as if she were saying he had a pot of tea.

엘레인 felt 에그웨인 tremble as they listened to 모이라인’s dispassionate report, but perhaps some of the trembling was her own. Bubbles of evil drifting through the Pattern. Reflections leaping out of mirrors. 랜드 a mass of blood and wounds. Almost as an afterthought, 모이라인 added that she was sure 페린 and 맷 had experienced something of the same, but escaped unharmed. The woman must have ice instead of blood. *No, she was heated enough about 랜드’s stubbornness. And she wasn’t cold when she spoke of marrying, however much she pretended to be*. But now she could have been discussing whether a bolt of silk was the right color for a dress.

“And these . . . these *things* will keep on?” 에그웨인 said when 모이라인 finished. “Is there nothing you can do to stop it? Or that 랜드 can do?”

The small blue stone dangling from 모이라인’s hair swung as she shook her head. “Not until he learns to control his abilities. Perhaps not then. I do not know if even he will be strong enough to push the miasma away from himself. At the least, though, he will be better able to defend himself.”

“Can’t you do something to help him?” 니나브 demanded. “You are the one of us who is supposed to know everything, or pretends to. Can’t you teach him? Some part of it, anyway? And don’t quote proverbs about birds teaching fish to fly.”

“You would know better,” 모이라인 replied, “if you had taken the advantage of your studies that you should have. You should know better. You want to know how to use the Power, 니나브, but you do not care to learn *about* the Power. *Saidin* is not *세다르*. The flows are different, the ways of weaving are different. The bird has a better chance.”

This time 에그웨인 took a turn at diffusing tension. “What is 랜드 being stubborn about, now?” 니나브 opened her mouth, and she added, “He can be stubborn as a stone, sometimes.” 니나브 shut her mouth with a snap; they all knew how true that was.

모이라인 eyed them, considering. At times, 엘레인 was not sure how much the 에스 세다이 trusted them. Or anyone. “He must move,” the 에스 세다이 said at last. “Instead, he sits here, and the 타이런s already begin to lose their fear of him. He sits here, and the longer he sits, doing nothing, the more the 버림받은 자들 will see his inaction as a sign of weakness. 패턴 moves and flows; only the dead are still. He must act, or he will die. From a crossbow bolt in his back, or poison in his food, or the 버림받은 자들 banding together to rip his soul from his body. He must act or die.” 엘레인 winced at each danger on her list; that they were real only made it worse.

“And you know what he must do, don’t you?” 니나브 said tightly. “You have this action planned.”

모이라인 nodded. “Would you rather he go haring off alone once more? I dare not risk it. This time he might be dead, or worse, before I find him.”

That was true enough. 랜드 hardly knew what he was doing. And 엘레인 was sure 모이라인 had no wish to lose the little guidance she still gave him. The little he allowed her to give.

“Will you share your plan for him with us?” 에그웨인 demanded. She was certainly not helping soothe the air now.

“Yes, do,” 엘레인 said, surprising herself with a cool echo of 에그웨인’s tone. Confrontation was not her way when it could be avoided; her mother always said it was better to guide people than try to hammer them into line.

If their manner irritated 모이라인, she gave no sign of it. “As long as you understand that you must keep it to yourselves. A plan revealed is a plan doomed to fail. Yes, I see you do understand.”

엘레인 certainly did; the plan was dangerous, and 모이라인 was not sure it would work.

“사마엘 is in 일리안,” the 에스 세다이 went on. “The 타이런s are always as ripe for war with 일리안 as the other way around. They have been killing each other off and on for a thousand years, and they speak of their chance for it as other men speak of the next feastday. I doubt even knowing of 사마엘’s presence would change that, not with the 용의 환생 to lead them. 티어 will follow 랜드 eagerly enough in that enterprise, and if he brings 사마엘 down, he—”

“Light!” 니나브 exclaimed. “You not only want him to start a war, you want him to seek out one of the 버림받은 자들! No wonder he is being stubborn. He is not a fool, for a man.”

“He must face the 어둠의 존재 in the end,” 모이라인 said calmly. “Do you truly think he can avoid the 버림받은 자들 now? As for war, there are wars enough without him, and every one worse than useless.”

“Any war is useless,” 엘레인 began, then faltered as comprehension suddenly filled her. Sadness and regret had to show on her face, too, but certainly comprehension. Her mother had lectured her often on how a nation was led as well as how it was governed, two very different things, but both necessary. And sometimes things had to be done for both that were worse than unpleasant, although the price of not doing them was worse still.

모이라인 gave her sympathetic look. “It is not always pleasant, is it? Your mother began when you were just old enough to understand, I suppose, teaching you what you will need to rule after her.” 모이라인 had grown up in the Royal Palace in 케렌, not destined to reign, but related to the ruling family and no doubt overhearing the same lectures. “Yet sometimes it seems ignorance would be better, to be a farm woman knowing nothing beyond the boundaries of her fields.”

“More riddles?” 니나브 said contemptuously. “War used to be something I heard about from peddlers, something far away that I didn’t really understand. I know what it is, now. Men killing men. Men behaving like animals, reduced to animals. Villages burned, farms and fields burned. Hunger, disease and death, for the innocent as the guilty. What makes this war of yours better, 모이라인? What makes it cleaner?”

“엘레인?” 모이라인 said quietly.
She shook her head—she did not want to be the one to explain this—but she was not sure even her mother sitting on the Lion Throne could have kept silent under 모이라인’s compelling, dark-eyed stare. “War will come whether 랜드 begins it or not,” she said reluctantly. 에그웨인 stepped back a pace, staring at her in disbelief no sharper than that on 니나브’s face; the incredulity faded from both women as she continued. “The 버림받은 자들 will not stand idly and wait. 사마엘 cannot be the only one to have seized a nation’s reins, just the lone one we know. They will come after 랜드 eventually, in their own persons perhaps, but certainly with whatever armies they command. And the nations that are free of the 버림받은 자들? How many will cry glory to the Dragon banner and follow him to Tarmon Gai’don, and how many will convince themselves the fall of the Stone is a lie and 랜드 only another false Dragon who must be put down, a false Dragon perhaps strong enough to threaten them if they do not move against him first? One way or another, war *will* come.” She cut off sharply. There was more to it, but she could not, would not, tell them that part.

모이라인 was not so reticent. “Very good,” she said, nodding, “yet incomplete.” The look she gave 엘레인 said she knew 엘레인 had left out what she had on purpose. Hands folded calmly at her waist, she addressed 니나브 and 에그웨인. “Nothing makes this war better, or cleaner. Except that it will cement the 타이런s to him, and the 일리안ers will end up following him just as the 타이런s do now. How could they not, once the Dragon banner flies over 일리안? Just the news of his victory might decide the wars in 타라본 and 아라드 도만 in his favor; there are wars *ended* for you.

“In one stroke he will make himself so strong in terms of men and swords that only a coalition of every remaining nation from here to the 황무지 can defeat him, and with the same blow he shows the 버림받은 자들 that he is not a plump partridge on a limb for the netting. That will make them wary, and buy him time to learn to use his strength. He must move first, be the hammer, not the nail.” The 에스 세다이 grimaced slightly, a hint of her earlier anger marring her calm. “He *must* move first. And what does he do? He reads. Reads himself into deeper trouble.”

니나브 looked shaken, as if she could see all the battles and death; 에그웨인’s dark eyes were large with horrified understanding. Their faces made 엘레인 shiver. One had watched 랜드 grow up, the other had grown up with him. And now they saw him starting wars. Not the 용의 환생, but 랜드 al’Thor.

에그웨인 struggled visibly, latching onto the smallest part, the most inconsequential, of what 모이라인 had said. “How can reading put him in trouble?”

“He has decided to find out for himself what the Prophecies of the Dragon say.” 모이라인’s face remained cool and smooth, but suddenly she sounded almost as tired as 엘레인 felt. “They may have been proscribed in 티어, but the Chief Librarian had nine different translations in a locked chest. 랜드 has them all, now. I pointed out the verse that applies here, and he quoted it to me, from an old 캔도리 translation.

> *“ ‘Power of the Shadow made human flesh,*

> *wakened to turmoil, strife and ruin.*

> *The Reborn One, marked and bleeding,*

> *dances the sword in dreams and mist,*

> *chains the Shadowsworn to his will,*

> *from the city, lost and forsaken,*

> *leads the spears to war once more,*

> *breaks the spears and makes them see,*

> *truth long hidden in the ancient dream.’ ”*

She grimaced. “It applies to this as well as it does to anything. 일리안 under 사마엘 is surely a forsaken city. Lead the 타이런 spears to war, chain 사마엘, and he has fulfilled the verse. The ancient dream of the 용의 환생. But he will not see it. He even has a copy in the 고대어, as if he understood two words. He runs after shadows, and 사마엘, or 라빈, or 란피어 may have him by the throat before I can convince him of his mistake.”

“He is desperate.” 니나브’s gentle tone was not for 모이라인, 엘레인 was sure, but for 랜드. “Desperate and trying to find his way.”

“So am I desperate,” 모이라인 said firmly. “I have dedicated my life to finding him, and I will not let him fail if I can prevent it. I am almost desperate enough to—” She broke off, pursing her lips. “Let it be enough that I will do what I must.”

“But it isn’t enough,” 에그웨인 said sharply. “What is it you’ll do?”

“You have other matters to concern you,” the 에스 세다이 said. “The 흑색 아자—”

“No!’ 엘레인’s voice was knife-edged and commanding, her knuckles a hard white where she gripped her soft blue skirts. “You keep many secrets, 모이라인, but tell us this. What do you mean to do to him?” An image flashed in her mind of seizing 모이라인 and shaking the truth out of her if need be.

“Do to him? Nothing. Oh, very well. There is no reason you should not know. You have seen what the 타이런s call the Great Holding?”

Oddly for a people that feared the Power so, the 타이런s held in the Stone a collection of objects connected to the Power second only to that in the 백색 탑. 엘레인, for one, thought it was because they had been forced to guard *칼란도르* so long, whether they wanted or not. Even the Sword That Is Not a Sword might seem less than what it was when it was one among many. But the 타이런s had never been able to make themselves display their prizes. The Great Holding was kept in a filthy series of crowded rooms buried even deeper than the dungeons. When 엘레인 had first seen them the locks on the doors had long since rusted shut, where the doors had not simply collapsed from dry rot.

“We spent an entire day down there,” 니나브 said. “To see if Liandrin and her *friends* took anything. I don’t think they did. Everything was buried in dust and mold. It will take ten riverboats to transport all of it to the Tower. Perhaps they can make some sense of it there; I surely could not.” The temptation to prod 모이라인 was apparently too great to avoid, for she added, “You would know all this if you had given us a little more of your time.”

모이라인 took no notice. She seemed to be looking inward, examining her own thoughts, and she spoke almost to herself. “There is one particular *ter’angreal* in the Holding, a thing like a redstone doorframe, subtly twisted to the eye. If I cannot make him reach *some* decision, I may have to step through.” The small blue stone on her forehead trembled, sparkling. Apparently she was not eager to take that step.

At the mention of *ter’angreal*, 에그웨인 instinctively touched the bodice of her dress. She had sewn a small pocket there herself, to hide the stone ring it now held. That ring was a *ter’angreal*, powerful in its way if small, and 엘레인 was one of only three women who knew she had it. 모이라인 was not one of the three.

They were strange things, *ter’angreal*, fragments of the 전설의 시대 like *angreal* and *sa’angreal*, if more numerous. *Ter’angreal* used the 하나의 힘 instead of magnifying it. Each had apparently been made to do one thing and one thing alone, but though some were used now, no one was sure if those uses were anything like what they had been made for. The 맹세 막대, on which a woman took the 세 가지 맹세 on being raised 에스 세다이, was a *ter’angreal* that made those oaths a part of her flesh and bone. The last test a 수련생 took on being raised to 허락받은 자 was inside another *ter’angreal* that ferreted out her most heartfelt fears and made them seem real—or perhaps took her to a place where they *were* real. Odd things could happen with *ter’angreal*. 에스 세다이 had been burned out or killed, or had simply vanished, in studying them. And in using them.

“I saw that doorway,” 엘레인 said. “In the last room at the end of the hall. My lamp went out, and I fell three times before I made it to the door.” A slight flush of embarrassment reddened her cheeks. “I was afraid to channel in there, even to relight the lamp. Much of it looks rubbish, to me—I think the 타이런s simply grabbed anything that anyone hinted might be connected to the Power—but I thought if I channeled, I might accidentally empower something that wasn’t rubbish, and who knows what it might do.”

“And if you had stumbled in the dark and fallen through the twisted doorway?” 모이라인 said wryly. “That needs no channeling, only to step through.”

“To what purpose?” 니나브 asked.

“To gain answers. Three answers, each true, about past, present or future.”

엘레인’s first thought was for the children’s tale, *Bili Under the Hill*, but only because of the three answers. A second thought came on its heels, and not to her alone. She spoke while 니나브 and 에그웨인 were still opening their mouths. “모이라인, this solves our problem. We can ask whether Joiya or Amico is telling the truth. We can ask where Liandrin and the others are. The names of the 흑색 아자 still in the Tower—”

“We can ask what this thing is that is dangerous to 랜드,” 에그웨인 put in, and 니나브 added, “Why haven’t you told us of this before? Why have you let us go on listening to the same tales day after day when we could have settled it all by now?”

The 에스 세다이 winced and threw up her hands. “You three rush in blindly where 란 and a hundred 감시자s would tread warily. Why do you think I have not stepped through? Days ago I could have asked what 랜드 must do to survive and triumph, how he can defeat the 버림받은 자들 and the 어둠의 존재, how he can learn to control the Power and hold off madness long enough to do what he must.” She waited, hands on hips, while it sank in. None of them spoke. “There are rules,” she went on, “and dangers. No one may step through more than once. Only once. You may ask three questions, but you must ask all three and hear the answers before you may leave. Frivolous questions are punished, it seems, but it also seems what may be serious for one can be frivolous coming from another. Most importantly, questions touching the Shadow have dire consequences.

“If you asked about the 흑색 아자, you might be returned dead, or come out a gibbering madwoman, if you came out at all. As for 랜드. . . . I am not certain it is possible to ask a question about the 용의 환생 that does not touch the Shadow in some way. You see? Sometimes there are reasons for caution.”

“How do you know all this?” 니나브 demanded. Planting fists on hips she confronted the 에스 세다이. “The High Lords surely never let 에스 세다이 study anything in the Holding. From the filth down there, none of it has seen sunlight in a hundred years or more.”

“More, I should think,” 모이라인 told her calmly. “They ceased their collecting nearly three hundred years gone. It was just before they stopped completely that they acquired this *ter’angreal*. Up until then it was the possession of the Firsts of Mayene, who used its answers to help keep Mayene out of 티어’s grasp. And they allowed 에스 세다이 to study it. In secret, of course; Mayene has never dared anger 티어 too openly.”

“If it was so important to Mayene,” 니나브 said suspiciously, “why is it here, in the Stone?”

“Because Firsts have made bad decisions as well as good in trying to keep Mayene free of 티어. Three hundred years ago the High Lords were planning to build a fleet to follow Mayener ships and find the oilfish shoals. Halvar, the then First, raised the price of Mayener lamp oil well above that of oil from 티어’s olives, and to further convince the High Lords that Mayene would always put its own interests behind those of 티어, made them a gift of the *ter’angreal*. He had already used it, so it was no further good to him, and he was almost as young as Berelain is now, apparently with a long reign ahead of him and many years of needing 타이런 goodwill.”

“He was a fool,” 엘레인 muttered. “My mother would never make such a mistake.”

“Perhaps not,” 모이라인 said. “But then, 안도르 is not a small nation cornered by a much larger and stronger. Halvar *was* a fool as it turned out—the High Lords had him assassinated the very next year—but his foolishness does present me with an opportunity, if I need it. A dangerous one, yet better than none.”

니나브 muttered to herself, perhaps disappointed that the 에스 세다이 had not tripped herself up.

“It leaves the rest of us right where we were.” 에그웨인 sighed. “Not knowing who is lying, or whether they both are.”

“Question them again, if you wish,” 모이라인 said. “You have until they are put on the ship, though I very much doubt either will change her tale now. My advice is to concentrate on Tanchico. If Joiya speaks truly, it will take 에스 세다이 and 감시자s to guard 마즈림 타임, not just the three of you. I sent a warning to the Amyrlin by pigeon when I first heard Joiya’s story. In fact, I sent three pigeons, to make sure one reaches the Tower.”

“So kind of you to keep us informed,” 엘레인 murmured coolly. The woman did go her own way. Just because they were only pretending to be full 에스 세다이 was no reason for 모이라인 to keep them in the dark. The Amyrlin had sent *them* out to hunt the 흑색 아자.

모이라인 inclined her head briefly, as if accepting the thanks for real. “You are welcome. Remember that you are the hounds the Amyrlin set after the 흑색 아자.” Her slight smile at 엘레인’s start said she knew exactly what 엘레인 had been thinking. “The decision on where to course must be yours. You have pointed that out to me, as well,” she added drily. “I trust it will prove an easier decision than mine. And I trust you will sleep well, what sleep is left before daybreak. A good night to you.”

“That woman . . .” 엘레인 muttered when the door had closed behind the 에스 세다이. “Sometimes I could almost strangle her.” She dropped into one of the chairs at the table and sat frowning at her hands in her lap.

니나브 gave a grunt that might have been agreement as she went to a narrow table against the wall where silver goblets and spice jars stood next to two pitchers. One pitcher, full of wine, rested in a gleaming bowl of now mostly melted ice, brought all the way from the 세계의 척추 packed in chests of sawdust. Ice in the summer to chill a High Lord’s drink; 엘레인 could barely imagine such a thing.

“A cool drink before bed will do us all good,” 니나브 said, busying herself with wine and water and spices.

엘레인 lifted her head as 에그웨인 took a seat next to her. “Did you mean what you said, 에그웨인? About 랜드?” 에그웨인 nodded, and 엘레인 sighed. “Do you remember what 민 used to say, all her jokes about sharing him? I sometimes wondered if that was a viewing she did not tell us about. I thought she meant we both loved him, and she knew it. But you had the right to him, and I didn’t know what to do. I still don’t. 에그웨인, he loves you.”

“He will just have to be put straight,” 에그웨인 said firmly. “When I marry, it will be because I want to, not just because a man expects me to love him. I will be gentle with him, 엘레인, but before I am done, he will know he is free. Whether he wants to be or not. My mother says men are different from us. She says we want to be in love, but only with the one we want; a man needs to be in love, but he will love the first woman to tie a string to his heart.”

“That is all very well,” 엘레인 said in a tight voice, “but Berelain was in his chambers.”

에그웨인 sniffed. “Whatever she intends, Berelain won’t keep her mind on one man long enough to make him love her. Two days ago she was casting eyes at Rhuarc. In two more, she’ll be smiling at someone else. She is like Else Grinwell. You remember her? The 수련생 who spent all her time out at the practice yards fluttering her eyelashes at the 감시자s?”

“She was not just fluttering her eyelashes, in his bedchamber at this hour. She was wearing even less than usual, if that is possible!”

“Do you mean to let her have him, then?”

“No!” 엘레인 said it very fiercely, and she meant it, but in the next breath she was full of despair. “Oh, 에그웨인, I do not know what to do. I love him. I want to marry him. Light! What will mother say? I would rather spend a night in Joiya’s cell than listen to the lectures mother will give me.” 안도르an nobles, even in royal families, married commoners often enough that it hardly occasioned comment—in 안도르, at least—but 랜드 was not exactly the usual run of commoner. Her mother was quite capable of actually sending Lini to drag her home by her ear.

“모르가세 can hardly say much if 맷 is to be believed,” 에그웨인 said comfortingly. “Or even half believed. This Lord Gaebril your mother is mooning after hardly sounds the choice of a woman thinking with her head.”

“I am sure 맷 exaggerated,” 엘레인 replied primly. Her mother was too shrewd to make herself a fool over any man. If Lord Gaebril—she had never even heard of him before 맷 spoke his name—if this fellow dreamed he could gain power through 모르가세, she would give him a rude awakening.

니나브 brought three goblets of spiced wine to the table, beads of condensation running down their shining sides, and small green-and-gold woven straw mats to put them on so the damp would not mar the table’s polish. “So,” she said, taking a chair, “you’ve discovered you are in love with 랜드, 엘레인, and 에그웨인 has discovered she isn’t.”

The two younger women gaped at her, one dark, the other fair, yet a near mirror image of astonishment.

“I have eyes,” 니나브 said complacently. “And ears, when you don’t take the trouble to whisper.” She sipped at her wine, and her voice grew cold when she continued. “What do you mean to do about it? If that chit Berelain has her claws into him, it will not be easy to pry them loose. Are you sure you want to go to the effort? You know what he is. You know what lies ahead of him, even setting the Prophecies aside. 광기. Death. How long does he have? A year? Two? Or will it begin before summer’s end? He is a man who can channel.” She bit off each word in tones of iron. “Remember what you were taught. Remember what he is.”

엘레인 held her head high and met 니나브 stare for stare. “It does not matter. Perhaps it should, but it doesn’t. Perhaps I am being foolish. I do not care. I cannot change my heart to order, 니나브.”

Suddenly 니나브 smiled. “I had to be sure,” she said warmly. “You must be sure. It isn’t easy loving any man, but loving this man will be harder yet.” Her smile faded as she went on. “My first question still has to be answered. What do you mean to do about it? Berelain may look soft—she certainly makes men see her so!—but I do not think she is. She will fight for what she wants. And she’s the kind to hold hard to something she doesn’t particularly want, just because someone else does want it.”

“I would like to stuff her in a barrel,” 에그웨인 said, gripping her goblet as if it were the First’s throat, “and ship her back to Mayene. In the bottom of the hold.”

니나브’s braid swung as she shook her head. “All very well, but try to offer advice that helps. If you cannot, keep silent and let her decide what she must do.” 에그웨인 stared at her, and she added, “랜드 is 엘레인’s to deal with, now, not yours. You have stepped aside, remember.”

The remark should have made 엘레인 smile, but it did not. “This was all supposed to be different.” She sighed. “I thought I would meet a man, learn to know him over months or years, and slowly I would come to realize I loved him. That is the way I always thought it would be. I hardly know 랜드. I’ve talked with him no more than half a dozen times in the space of a year. But I knew I loved him five minutes after I first set eyes on him.” Now that *was* foolish. Only, it was true, and she did not care if it was foolish. She would tell her mother the same to her face, and Lini. Well, perhaps not Lini. Lini had drastic ways of dealing with foolishness, and she seemed to think 엘레인 had not aged beyond ten. “As matters stand, though, I don’t even have the right to be angry with him. Or Berelain.” But she was. *I would like to slap his face till his ears ring for a year! I’d like to switch her all the way to the ship that takes her back to Mayene!* Only, she did *not* have the right, and that made it all the worse. Infuriatingly, a plaintive tone touched her voice. “What can I do? He has never looked at me twice.”

“In the 두 강,” 에그웨인 said slowly, “if a woman wants a man to know she is interested in him, she puts flowers in his hair at Bel Time or Sunday. Or she might embroider a feastday shirt for him any time. Or make a point of asking him to dance and no one else.” 엘레인 gave her an incredulous look, and she hastened to add, “I am not suggesting you embroider a shirt, but there are ways to let him know how you feel.”

“Mayeners believe in speaking out.” 엘레인’s voice held a brittle edge. “Perhaps that is the best way. Just tell him right out. At least he’ll know how I feel, then. At least I’ll have some right to—”

She snatched her spiced wine and tilted her head back, drinking. Speak out? Like some *Mayener* hussy! Setting the empty goblet back on the small mat, she drew a deep breath and murmured, “What *will* Mother say?”

“What’s more important,” 니나브 said gently, “is what you will do when we have to leave here. Whether it’s Tanchico, or the Tower, or somewhere else, we will have to go. What will you do when you’ve just told him you love him, and you must leave him behind? If he asks you to stay with him? If you want to?”

“I will go.” There was no hesitation in 엘레인’s reply, but a touch of asperity. The other woman should not have had to ask. “If I must accept him being the 용의 환생, he must accept that I am what I am, that I have duties. I want to be 에스 세다이, 니나브. It isn’t some idle amusement. Neither is the work we three have to do. Could you really think I would abandon you and 에그웨인?”

에그웨인 hurried to assure her that the thought had never crossed her mind; 니나브 did the same, but slowly enough to give herself the lie.

엘레인 looked from one to the other of them. “In truth, I feared you might tell me I was foolish, fretting over a thing like this when we have the 흑색 아자 to worry about.”

A slight flicker of 에그웨인’s eyes said the thought had occurred to her, but 니나브 said, “랜드 is not the only one who might die next year, or next month, We might, too. Times are not what they were, and we cannot be, either. If you sit and wish for what you want, you may not see it this side of the grave.”

It was a chilling sort of reassurance, but 엘레인 nodded. She was *not* being silly. If only the 흑색 아자 could be settled so easily. She pressed her empty silver goblet to her forehead for the coolness. What were they to do?

CHAPTER 7

![](images/00577.jpg)

*Playing with Fire*

With the sun barely above the horizon the next morning, 에그웨인 presented herself at the doors to 랜드’s chambers, followed by a foot-dragging 엘레인. The Daughter-Heir wore a long-sleeved dress of pale blue silk, cut in the 타이런 fashion, and pulled low after some little discussion. A necklace of sapphires like a deep morning sky, and another strand woven into her red-gold curls, showed up the blue of her eyes. Despite the damp warmth, 에그웨인 wore a plain, deep red scarf, as large as a shawl, around her shoulders. 아비엔다 had supplied the scarf, and the sapphires too. Surprisingly, the 아일 woman had a tidy store of such things somehow.

For all she had known they were there, 에그웨인 gave a start when the 아일 guards glided to their feet with startling suddenness. 엘레인 let out a small gasp, but quickly eyed them with that regal bearing she managed so well. It seemed to have no effect on these sun-dark men. The six were *Shae’en M’taal*, Stone Dogs, and appeared relaxed for 아일, meaning they seemed to be looking everywhere, seemed ready to move in any direction.

에그웨인 drew herself up in imitation of 엘레인—she did wish she could do that as well as the Daughter-Heir—and announced, “I . . . we . . . want to see how the Lord Dragon’s wounds are.”

Her remark was plainly foolish, if they knew much about 치유, but that likelihood was small; few people did, and 아일 probably less than most. She had not intended to give any reason for being there—it was enough that they thought her 에스 세다이—but when the 아일 appeared almost to spring out of the black marble floor, it suddenly seemed a good idea. Not that they were making any move to stop 엘레인 and her, of course. But these men were all so tall, so stone-faced, and they carried those short spears and horn bows as if using them would be as natural as breathing, and as easy. With those light-colored eyes regarding her so intently, it was all too easy to remember stories of black-veiled 아일, without mercy or pity, of the 아일 War and the men like these who had destroyed every army sent against them until the last, who had only turned back to the 황무지 after fighting the allied nations to a standstill during three blood-soaked days and nights before 타르 발론 itself. She very nearly embraced *세다르*.

Gaul, the Stone Dogs’ leader, nodded, looking down at 엘레인 and her with a touch of respect. He was a handsome man, in a rugged way, a little older than 니나브, with eyes as green and clear as polished gems and long eyelashes so dark they seemed to outline his eyes in black. “They may be troubling him. He is in a foul mood this morning.” Gaul grinned, just a quick flash of white teeth, in understanding of a temper when wounded. “He has chased off a group of these High Lords already, and threw one of them out himself. What was his name?”

“Torean,” another, even taller man replied. He had an arrow nocked, the short, curved bow held almost casually. His gray eyes rested on the two women for an instant, then went back to searching among the anteroom’s columns.

“Torean,” Gaul agreed. “I thought he would slide as far as those pretty carvings . . .” He pointed a spear to the ring of stiff-standing Defenders. “. . . but he came short by three paces. I lost a good 타이런 hanging, all hawks in gold thread, to Mangin.” The taller man gave a brief, contented smile.

에그웨인 blinked at the image of 랜드 physically pitching a High Lord across the floor. He had never been violent; far from it. How much had he changed? She had been too busy with Joiya and Amico, and he too busy with 모이라인 or 란 or the High Lords, to do more than speak in passing, a few words about home here and there, about how the Bel Tine festival might have gone this year and what Sunday would be like. It had all been so brief. How much had he changed?
“We have to see him,” 엘레인 said, a slight tremor in her voice.

Gaul made a bow, grounding the point of one spear on the black marble. “Of course, 에스 세다이.”

It was with some trepidation that 에그웨인 entered 랜드’s chambers, and 엘레인’s face spoke volumes of the effort those few steps took.

No evidence of last night’s horror remained, unless it was the absence of mirrors; lighter patches marked the wall panels where those hanging there had been taken away. Not that the room came anywhere near neatness; books lay everywhere, on everything, some lying open as if abandoned in the middle of a page, and the bed was still unmade. The crimson draperies were pulled open on all the windows, facing westward toward the river that was 티어’s heartvein, and *칼란도르* sparkled like polished crystal on a huge gilded stand of surpassing gaudiness. 에그웨인 thought the stand the ugliest thing she had ever seen decorating a room—until she glimpsed the silver wolves savaging a golden stag on the mantel above the fireplace. Scant breezes off the river kept the room surprisingly cool compared to the rest of the Stone.

랜드 sat in his shirtsleeves, sprawled in a chair with one leg over the arm and a leather-bound book propped against his knee. At the sound of their footsteps, he snapped the book shut and dropped it among the others on the scroll-worked carpet, bounding to his feet ready to fight. The scowl on his face faded as he took in who they were.

For the first time in the Stone, 에그웨인 looked for changes in him and found them. How many months before then since she had seen him last? Enough for his face to have grown harder, for the openness that had once been there to fade. He moved differently, too, a little like 란, a little like the 아일. With his height and his reddish hair, and eyes that seemed now blue, now gray, as the light took them, he looked all too much like an 아일man, too much for comfort. But had he changed inside?

“I thought you were . . . someone else,” he mumbled, sharing out embarrassed glances between them. That was the 랜드 she knew, even to the flush that rose in his cheeks every time he looked at her or 엘레인, either one. “Some . . . people want things I can’t give. Things I *will* not give.” Suspicion grew on his face with shocking suddenness, and his tone hardened. “What do *you* want? Did 모이라인 send you? Are you supposed to convince me to do what she wants?”

“Don’t be a goose,” 에그웨인 said sharply before she thought. “I do not want you to start a war!”

엘레인 added in pleading tones, “We came to . . . to help you, if we can.” That was one of their reasons, and the easiest to bring up, they had decided over breakfast.

“You know about her plans for . . .” he began roughly, then made a sudden shift. “Help me? How? That is what 모이라인 says.”

에그웨인 sternly folded her arms beneath her breasts, holding the scarf tight, in the way 니나브 used to address the Village Council when she meant to have her way no matter how stubborn they were. It was too late to start over; the only thing was to go on as she had begun. “I told you not to be a fool, 랜드 al’Thor. You may have 타이런s bowing to your boots, but I remember when 니나브 switched your bottom for letting 맷 talk you into stealing a jar of apple brandy.” 엘레인 kept her face carefully composed. Too carefully; it was plain to 에그웨인 that she wanted to laugh out loud.

랜드 did not notice, of course. Men never did. He grinned at 에그웨인, close to laughing himself. “We had just turned thirteen. She found us asleep behind your father’s stable, and our heads hurt so much we didn’t even feel her switch.” That was not at all the way 에그웨인 recalled it. “Not like when you threw that bowl at her head. Remember? She’d dosed you with dogweed tea because you had been moping about for a week, and as soon as you tasted it, you hit her with her best bowl. Light, did you squeal! When was that? Two years ago come this—”

“We are not here to talk over old times,” 에그웨인 said, shifting the scarf irritably. It was thin wool, but still far too hot. Really, he did have the habit of remembering the most unfortunate things.

He grinned as if he knew what she was thinking, and went on in better humor. “You are here to help me, you say. With what? I don’t suppose you know how to make a High Lord keep his word when I’m not staring over his shoulder. Or how to stop unwanted dreams? I could surely use help with—” Eyes darting to 엘레인 and back to her, he made another abrupt shift. “What about the 고대어? Did you learn any of that in the 백색 탑?” Without waiting for an answer he began rooting through the volumes scattered across the carpet. There were more on the chairs, among the tumbled bedclothes. “I have a copy here . . . somewhere . . . of. . . .”

“랜드.” 에그웨인 raised her voice. “랜드, I cannot read the 고대어.” She shot a look at 엘레인, warning her not to admit to any such knowledge. They had not come to translate the Prophecies of the Dragon for him. The sapphires in the Daughter-Heir’s hair swayed as she nodded agreement. “We had other things to learn.”

He straightened from the books with a sigh. “It was too much to hope.” For a moment he seemed on the point of saying more, but stared at his boots. 에그웨인 wondered how he managed to deal with the High Lords in all their arrogance if she and 엘레인 put him so out of countenance.

“We came to help you with channeling,” she told him. “With the Power.” What 모이라인 claimed was supposed to be true; a woman could not teach a man to channel any more than she could teach him how to bear a child. 에그웨인 was not so sure. She had felt something woven from *세이딘*, once. Or rather, she had felt nothing, something blocking her own flows as surely as stone dammed water. But she had learned as much outside the Tower as within; surely in her knowledge there was something she could teach him, some guidance she could offer.

“If we can,” 엘레인 added.

Suspicion flashed across his face again. It was unnerving how his mood changed so quickly. “I have more chance of reading the 고대어 than you do of. . . . Are you sure this isn’t 모이라인’s doing? Did she send you here? Thinks she can convince me by some roundabout way, does she? Some twisty 에스 세다이 plot I’ll not see the point of until I am mired in it?” He grunted sourly and pulled a dark green coat from the floor behind one of the chairs, shrugging into it hastily. “I agreed to meet some more of the High Lords this morning. If I don’t keep an eye on them, they just find ways to get around what I want. They’ll learn sooner or later. I rule 티어, now. Me. The 용의 환생. I will teach them. You will have to excuse me.”

에그웨인 wanted to shake him. He ruled 티어? Well, perhaps he did, if it came to that, but she remembered a boy with a lamb nestled inside his coat, proud as a rooster because he had driven off the wolf that tried to take it. He was a shepherd, not a king, and even if he had call to give himself airs, it was no good to him that he did.

She was about to tell him as much, but before she could 엘레인 spoke up fiercely. “No one sent us. No one. We came because . . . because we care for you. Perhaps it will not work, but you can try. If I . . . if we care enough to try, you can try, too. Is it so unimportant to you that you cannot spare us an hour? For you life?”

He stopped buttoning up his coat, staring at the Daughter-Heir so intently that for a moment 에그웨인 thought he had forgotten she was there. With a shiver he pulled his eyes away. Glancing at 에그웨인, he shifted his feet and frowned at the floor. “I will try,” he muttered. “It’ll do no good, but I will. . . . What do you want me to do?”

에그웨인 drew a deep breath. She had not thought convincing him would be this easy; he had always been like a boulder buried in mud when he decided to dig his heels in, which he did far too often.

“Look at me,” she said, embracing *세다르*. She let the Power fill her as completely as it ever had, more completely, accepting every drop she could hold; it was as if light suffused every particle of her, as if the Light itself filled every cranny. Life seemed to burst inside her like 불꽃놀이. She had never before let this much in. It was a shock to realize she was not quivering; surely she could not bear this glorious sweetness. She wanted to revel in it, to dance and sing, to simply lie back and let it roll through her, over her. She made herself speak. “What do you see? What do you feel? Look at me, 랜드!”

He lifted his head slowly, still frowning. “I see you. What am I supposed to see? Are you touching the Source? 에그웨인, 모이라인 has channeled around me a hundred times, and I never saw anything. Except what she did. It doesn’t work that way. Even I know that much.”

“I am stronger than 모이라인,” she told him firmly. “She would be whimpering on the floor, or insensible, if she tried to hold as much as I hold now.” It was true, though she had never before rated the 에스 세다이’s ability so closely.

It cried out to be used, this Power pulsing through her stronger than heartblood. With this much, she could do things 모이라인 could not dream of doing. The wound in 랜드’s side that 모이라인 could never Heal completely. She did not know 치유—it was considerably more complex than anything she had ever done—but she had watched 니나브 Heal, and perhaps, with this great pool of the Power filling her, she could see something of how that could be Healed. Not to do it, of course; only to see.

Carefully she spun out hair-fine flows of Air and Water and Spirit, the Powers used for 치유, and felt for his old injury. One touch, and she recoiled, shivering, snatching back her weaving; her stomach churned as if every meal she had ever eaten wanted to come up. It seemed that all the darkness in the world rested there in 랜드’s side, all the world’s evil in a festering sore only lightly covered by tender scar tissue. A thing like that would soak up 치유 flows like drops of water on dry sand. How could he bear the pain? Why was he not weeping?

From first thought to action had taken only a moment. Shaken, and desperately hiding it, she went on without a pause. “You are as strong as I. I know it; you must be. Feel, 랜드. What do you feel?” *Light, what can Heal that? Can anything?*

“I don’t feel anything,” he muttered, shifting his feet. “Goose bumps. And no wonder. It’s not that I don’t trust you, 에그웨인, but I cannot help being nervous when a woman is channeling around me. I am sorry.”

She did not bother explaining to him the difference between channeling and merely embracing the True Source. There was so much he did not know, even compared to her own scant knowledge. He was a blind man trying to work a loom by touch, with no idea of colors or what the threads, or even the loom, looked like.

With an effort she released *세다르*, and it was an effort. Part of her wanted to cry at the loss. “I am not touching the Source now, 랜드.” She stepped closer and peered up at him. “Do you still feel goose bumps?”

“No. But that’s just because you told me.” He gave an abrupt shrug of his shoulders. “You see? I started thinking about it, and I have them again.”

에그웨인 smiled triumphantly. She did not need to look around at 엘레인 to confirm what she had already sensed, what they had agreed upon earlier for this point. “You can sense a woman embracing the Source, 랜드. 엘레인 is doing just that right now.” He squinted at the Daughter-Heir. “It doesn’t matter what you see or don’t see. *Hard Heads*

엘레인 was not certain 랜드 realized she was still in the room, the way he stared after 에그웨인 with a half-bewildered expression. Now and again he shook his head as if arguing with himself, or trying to straighten his mind. She was content to wait him out. Anything that put off the moment a while longer. She put a hand over his mouth. “I do not want to hear anything from you that you do not mean with your whole heart,” she said firmly. “Not now, or ever.”

He nodded, not as if he understood why, but at least as if he understood that she meant what she said. Straightening her hair—the strand of sapphires was tangled beyond mending without a mirror—she stepped out of his encircling arms, not without reluctance; it would be all too easy to remain there, and she had already been more forward than she had ever dreamed of before. Speaking up like that; asking for a kiss. Asking! She was not Berelain.

Berelain. Perhaps 민 had had a viewing. What 민 saw, happened, but she would not share him with Berelain. Perhaps she needed to do a bit more plain speaking. Obliquely plain, at least. “I expect you will not lack for company after I go. Just remember that some women see a man with their hearts, while others see no more than a bauble to wear, no different than a necklace or a bracelet. Remember that I will come back, and I am one who sees with her heart.” He looked confused, at first, then a little alarmed. She had said too much, too fast. She had to divert him. “Do you know what you have not said to me? You have not tried to frighten me away by telling me how dangerous you are. Don’t try now. It is too late.”

“I did not think of it.” Another thought came to him, though, and his eyes crinkled with suspicion. “Did you and 에그웨인 scheme this up between you?”

She managed to combine wide-eyed innocence with mild outrage. “How could you even consider such a thing? Do you imagine we would hand you around between us like a package? You think a good deal of yourself. There is such a thing as being overproud.” He did look confused, now. Quite satisfactory. “Are you sorry for what you did to us, 랜드?”

“I did not mean to frighten you,” he said hesitantly. “에그웨인 made me angry; she’s always been able to without half trying. That’s no excuse, I know. I said I was sorry, and I am. Look what it got me. Burned tables and another mattress ruined.”

“And for . . . the pinch?”

His face reddened again, but he faced her firmly even so. “No. No, I am not sorry for that. The two of you, talking over my head, as if I were a lump of wood with no ears. You deserved as much, both of you, and I won’t say different.”

For a moment she considered him. He rubbed his arms through his coat sleeves as she momentarily embraced *세다르*. She did not know 치유 to any degree, but she had learned bits and pieces on the edge of it. Channeling, she soothed away the hurt she had given him for the pinch. His eyes widened in surprise, and he shifted on his feet as if testing the absence of pain. “For being honest,” she told him simply.

There was a rap at the door, and Gaul looked in. At first the 아일man had his head down, but after a quick glance at them he raised it. Color flooded 엘레인’s face as she realized he had suspected that he might be interrupting something he should not see. She very nearly embraced *세다르* again and taught him a lesson.

“The 타이런s are here,” Gaul said. “The High Lords you were expecting.”

“I will go, then,” she told 랜드. “You must tell them about—taxes, was it not? Think on what I have said.” She did not say “think of me,” but she was sure the effect would be the same.

He reached out as if to stop her, but she slipped away from him. She had no intention of putting on a display in front of Gaul. The man was 아일, but what must he think of her, wearing perfume and sapphires at that hour of the morning? It required real effort not to pull the neckline of her dress up higher.

The High Lords entered as she reached the door, a cluster of graying men in pointed beards and colorful, ornate coats with puffy sleeves. They crowded out of her way with reluctant bows, their bland faces and polite murmurs not hiding their relief that she was leaving.

She glanced back once from the doorway. A tall, broad-shouldered young man in a plain green coat among the High Lords in their silks and satin stripes, 랜드 looked like a stork among peacocks, yet there was something about him, a presence that said he commanded there by right. The 타이런s recognized it, bending their stiff necks reluctantly. He thought probably they bowed just because he was the 용의 환생, and perhaps they thought so, too. But she had seen men, like Gareth Bryne, the Captain-Commander of her mother’s Guards, who could have dominated a room in rags, with no title and no one knowing their name. 랜드 might not know it, but he was such a man. He had not been when she first saw him, but he was now. She pulled the door shut behind her.

The 아일 around the entrance glanced at her, and the captain commanding the ring of Defenders in the middle of the anteroom stared uneasily, but she barely noticed them. It was done. Or at least it was begun. Four days she had before Joiya and Amico were put on that ship, four days at most to twine herself so firmly into 랜드’s thoughts that he had no room for Berelain. Or if not that, firmly enough that she stayed inside his head until she had the chance to do more. She had never thought she might do a thing like this, stalk a man like a huntress stalking a wild boar. The butterflies were still gamboling in her stomach. At least she had not let him see how nervous she was. And it occurred to her that she had not once thought of what her mother would say. With that, the flutterings vanished. She did not care what her mother said. 모르가세 had to accept her daughter as a woman; that was all there was to it.

The 아일 bowed as she moved away, and she acknowledged them with a gracious nod that would have done 모르가세 proud. Even the 타이런 captain looked at her as if he could see her new serenity. She did not think she would be troubled by butterflies again. For the 흑색 아자 perhaps, but not for 랜드.

Ignoring the High Lords in their anxious semicircle, 랜드 watched the door close behind 엘레인 with wonder in his eyes. Dreams coming true, even only this much, made him uneasy. A swim in the Waterwood was one thing, but he would never have believed a dream where she came to him like this. She had been so cool and collected, while he was tripping over his own tongue. And 에그웨인, giving his own thoughts back to him and only concerned she might hurt him. Why was it women could go to pieces or fly into a rage at the smallest thing, yet never flicker an eyelash at what left you gaping?

“My Lord Dragon?” Sunamon murmured even more diffidently than usual. Word of this morning must have spread through the Stone already; that first lot had nearly run on their way out, and it was doubtful Torean would show his face, or his filthy suggestions, anywhere 랜드 was.

Sunamon essayed an ingratiating smile, then smothered it, drywashing his plump hands, when 랜드 only looked at him. The rest pretended they did not see the burned tables, or the shattered mattress and scattered books, or the half-melted lumps over the fireplace that had been the stag and wolves. High Lords were good at seeing only what they wanted to see. Carleon and Tedosian, false self-effacement in every line of their thick bodies, surely never realized there was anything suspicious in never looking at one another. But then, 랜드 might never have noticed if not for 톰’s note, found in the pocket of a coat just back from being brushed.

“The Lord Dragon wished to see us?” Sunamon managed.

Could 에그웨인 and 엘레인 have worked it up between them? Of course not. Women did not do things like that any more than men. Did they? It had to be coincidence. 엘레인 heard that he was free and decided to speak. That was it. “Taxes,” he barked. The 타이런s did not move, but they gave the impression of stepping back. How he hated dealing with these men; he wanted to dive back into the books.

“It is a bad precedent, my Lord Dragon, lowering taxes,” a lean, gray-haired man said in an oily voice. Meilan was tall for a 타이런, only a hand shorter than 랜드, and hard as any Defender. He held himself in a stoop in 랜드’s presence; his dark eyes showed how he hated it. But he had hated it when 랜드 told them to stop crouching around him, too. None of them straightened, but Meilan especially had not liked being reminded of what he did. “The peasants have always paid easily, but if we lower their taxes, when the day comes that we raise them back to where they now are, the fools will complain as bitterly as if we had doubled the present levy. There might well be riots when that day comes, my Lord Dragon.”

랜드 strode across the room to stand before *칼란도르*; the crystal sword glittered, outshining the gilt and gemstones surrounding it. A reminder of who he was, of the power he could wield. 에그웨인. It was foolish to feel hurt because she said she no longer loved him. Why should he expect her to have feelings for him that he did not have for her? Yet it did hurt. A relief, but not a pleasant one. “You will have riots if you drive men off their farms.” Three books stood in a stack almost by Meilan’s feet. *The Treasures of the Stone of 티어, Travels in the 황무지*, and *Dealings with the Territory of Mayene*. The keys lay in those, and in the various translations of *The 카라에손 순환*, if he could only find them and fit them to the proper locks. He pushed his mind back to the High Lords. “Do you think they will watch their families starve and do nothing?”

“The Defenders of the Stone have put down riots before, my Lord Dragon,” Sunamon said soothingly. “Our own guards can keep peace in the countryside. The peasants will not disturb you, I give you my assurance.”

“There are too many farmers as it is.” Carleon flinched at 랜드’s glare. “It is the civil war in 케렌, my Lord Dragon,” he explained hurriedly. “The 케렌인 can buy no grain, and the granaries are bursting. This year’s harvest will go to waste as it is. And next year . . . ? Burn my soul, my Lord Dragon, but what we need is for some of those peasants to stop their eternal digging and planting.” He seemed to realize he had said too much, though he clearly did not understand why. 랜드 wondered whether he had any idea how food got to his table. Did he see anything but gold, and power?

“What will you do when 케렌 is buying grain again?” 랜드 said coolly. “For that matter, is 케렌 the only land that needs grain?” Why *had* 엘레인 spoken up like that? What *did* she expect of him? Fond, she said. Women could play games with words like 에스 세다이. Did she mean she loved him? No, that was plain foolishness. Overproud to a degree.

“My Lord Dragon,” Meilan said, half subservient, half as if explaining something to a child, “if the civil wars stopped today, 케렌 still could not buy more than a few bargeloads for two, even three years. We have always sold our grain to 케렌.”

Always—for the twenty years since the 아일 War. They were so bound up in what they had *always* done that they could not see what was so simple. Or would not see it. When the cabbages sprouted like weeds around Emond’s Field, it was a near certainty that bad rain or whiteworm had struck Deven Ride or Watch Hill. When Watch Hill had too many turnips, Emond’s Field would have a shortage, or Deven Ride.

“Offer it in 일리안,” he told them. What did 엘레인 expect? “Or 알타라.” He did like her, but he liked 민 as much. Or thought he did. It was impossible to sort out his feelings for either of them. “You have ships for the sea as well as riverboats and barges, and if you don’t have enough, hire them from Mayene.” He liked both women, but beyond that. . . . He had spent very nearly his whole life mooning after 에그웨인; he was not about to dive into that again until he was sure. Sure of something. Sure. If *Dealings with the Territory of Mayene* was to be believed. . . . *Stop this*, he told himself. *Keep your mind on these weasels, or they’ll find cracks to slip through, and bite you on the way*. “Pay with grain; I’m sure the First will be amenable, for a good price. And maybe a signed agreement, a treaty. . . .” That was a good word; the sort they used. “. . . pledging to leave Mayene alone in return for ships.” He owed her that.

“We trade little with 일리안, my Lord Dragon. They are vultures, and scum.” Tedosian sounded scandalized, and so did Meilan when he said, “We have always dealt with Mayene from strength, my Lord Dragon. Never with bent knee.”
랜드 took a deep breath. The High Lords tensed. It always came to this. He always tried to reason with them, and it always failed. 톰 said the High Lords had heads as hard as the Stone, and he was right. *What do I feel for her? Dreaming about her. She’s certainly pretty*. He was not sure if he meant 엘레인 or 민. *Stop this! A kiss means no more than a kiss. Stop it!* Putting women firmly out of his head, he set himself to telling these stone-brained fools what they were going to do. “First, you will cut taxes on farmers by three-quarters, and on everyone else by half. Don’t argue! Just do it! Second, you go to Berelain and ask—ask!—her price for hiring. . . .”

The High Lords listened with false smiles and grinding teeth, but they listened.

에그웨인 was considering Joiya and Amico when 맷 fell in beside her, just walking down the hallway as if he merely happened to be going the same way. He was frowning to himself, and his hair needed brushing, as if he had been scrubbing his fingers through it. Once or twice he glanced at her but did not speak. The servants they passed bowed or curtsied, and so did the occasional High Lords and Ladies, if with markedly less enthusiasm. 맷’s lip-curling stares at the nobles would have brought trouble if she had not been there, friend of the Lord. Dragon or not.

This silence was not like him, not like the 맷 she knew. Except for his fine red coat—wrinkled as if he had slept in it—he seemed no different than the old 맷, yet they were surely all different now. His quiet was unsettling. “Is last night troubling you?” she asked at last.

He missed a step. “You know about that? Well, you would, wouldn’t you. Doesn’t bother me. Wasn’t much to it. Over and done with now, anyway.”

She pretended to believe him. “니나브 and I do not see much of you.” That was a rank understatement.

“I have been busy,” he muttered with an uncomfortable shrug, looking everywhere but at her again.

“Dicing?” she asked dismissively.

“Cards.” A plump maid, curtsying with her arms full of folded towels, glanced at 에그웨인 and, apparently thinking she was not looking, winked at 맷. He grinned at her. “I’ve been busy playing cards.”

에그웨인’s eyebrows rose sharply. That woman had to be ten years older than 니나브. “I see. It must use up a great deal of time. Playing cards. Too much to spare a few moments for old friends.”

“The last time I spared you a moment, you and 니나브 tied me up with the Power like a pig for market so you could rummage through my room. Friends don’t steal from friends.” He grimaced. “Besides, you’re always with that 엘레인, with her nose in the air. Or 모이라인. I do not like—” Clearing his throat, he shot her a sideways glance. “I don’t like taking up your time. You are busy, from what I hear. Questioning 어둠의 친구들. Doing all sorts of important things, I should imagine. You know these 타이런s think you are 에스 세다이, don’t you?”

She shook her head ruefully. It was 에스 세다이 he did not like. However much of the world 맷 saw, nothing would ever change him. “It is not stealing to take back what was supposed to be a loan,” she told him.

“I don’t remember you saying anything about a loan. Aaah, what use do I have for a letter from the Amyrlin? Just get me in trouble. You could have asked, though.”

She refrained from pointing out that they had asked. She wanted neither an argument nor a sulky departure. He would not call it that, of course. This time she would let him get away with his version. “Well, I am glad you are still willing to talk to me. Was there a special reason for it today?”

He shoved his fingers through his hair and muttered to himself. What he needed was his mother to haul him off by his ear for a long talking to. 에그웨인 counseled herself to patience. She could be patient when she wanted to. She would not say a word before he did, if she burst for it.

The corridor opened into a railed colonnade of white marble, looking down on one of the Stone’s few gardens. Large white blossoms covered a few small, waxy-leafed trees and gave a scent even sweeter than the banks of red and yellow roses. A sullen breeze failed to stir the hangings on the inner wall, but it did cut the morning’s growing damp warmth. 맷 took a seat on the wide balustrade with his back against a column and one foot up in front of him. Peering down into the garden, he finally said, “I . . . need some advice.”

He wanted advice from *her*? She goggled at him. “Whatever I can do to help,” she said faintly. He turned his head to her, and she did her best to assume something like 에스 세다이 calm. “What do you want advice about?”

“I don’t know.”

It was a ten-pace drop to the garden. Besides, there were men down there weeding among the roses. If she pushed him over, he might land on one. A gardener, not a rosebush. “How am I supposed to advise you, then?” she asked in a thin voice.

“I am . . . trying to decide what to do.” He looked embarrassed; he had a right to, in her opinion.

“I hope you are not thinking of trying to leave. You know how important you are. You cannot run away from it, 맷.”

“You think I don’t know that? I don’t think I could leave if 모이라인 told me I could. Believe me, 에그웨인, I am not going anywhere. I just want to know what’s going to happen.” He gave a rough shake of his head, and his voice grew tighter. “What comes next? What’s in these holes in my memory? There are chunks of my life that aren’t even there; they don’t exist, as if they never happened! Why do I find myself spouting gibberish? People say it’s the 고대어, but it’s goose gabble to me. I want to know, 에그웨인. I have to know, before I go as crazy as 랜드.”

“랜드 is not crazy,” she said automatically. So 맷 was not trying to run away. That was a pleasant surprise; he had not seemed to believe in responsibility. But there was pain and worry in his voice. 맷 never worried, or never let anyone see it if he did. “I do not know the answers, 맷,” she said gently. “Perhaps 모이라인—”

“No!” He was on his feet in a bound. “No 에스 세다이! I mean. . . . You’re different. I know you, and you aren’t. . . . Didn’t they teach you anything in the Tower, some trick or other, something that would serve?”

“Oh, 맷, I am sorry. I am so sorry.”

His laugh reminded her of their childhood. Just so he had always laughed when his grandest expectations went astray. “Ah, well, I guess it does not matter. It’d still be the Tower, if at second hand. No offense to you.” Just so he had moaned over a splinter in his finger and treated a broken leg as if it were nothing at all.

“There might be a way,” she said slowly. “If 모이라인 says it is all right. She might.”

“모이라인! Haven’t you heard a word I said? The last thing I want is 모이라인 meddling. What way?”

맷 had always been rash. But he wanted no more than she did, to know. If only he showed a little sense and caution for once. A passing 타이런 noblewoman with dark braids coiled about her head, shoulders bare above yellow linen, bent her knee slightly, looking at them with no expression; she walked on quickly, with a stiff back. 에그웨인 watched her until she was well beyond earshot, and they were alone. Unless the gardeners, thirty feet below, counted. 맷 was staring at her expectantly.

In the end, she told him of the *ter’angreal*, the twisted doorway that held answers on its other side. It was the dangers she emphasized, the consequences of foolish questions, or those touching the Shadow, the dangers even 에스 세다이 might not know. She was more than flattered that he had come to her, but he had to show a little sense. “You must remember this, 맷. Frivolous questions can get you killed, so if you do use it, you will have to be serious for a change. And you mustn’t ask any questions that touch the Shadow.”

He had listened with greater and greater incredulity. When she was done, he exclaimed, “Three questions? You go in like Bili, I suppose, spend a night and come out ten years later with a purse that’s always full of gold and a—”

“For once in your life, 매트림 카우톤,” she snapped, “do not talk like a fool. You know very well *ter’angreal* are not stories. It’s the dangers you have to be aware of. Maybe the answers you seek are inside this one, but you must not try it before 모이라인 says you can. You must promise me that, or I promise you I will take you to her like a trout on a string. You know I can.”

He gave a loud snort. “I’d be a fool if I did try it, no matter what 모이라인 says. Walk into a bloody *ter’angreal*? It’s less I want to do with the bloody Power, not more. You can blot it right out of your mind.”

“It is the only chance I know, 맷.”

“Not for me, it isn’t,” he said firmly. “No chance at all is better than that.”

Despite his tone, she wanted to put an arm around him. Only he would likely make some joke at her expense, and try to goose her. He had been incorrigible from the day he was born. But he had come to her for help. “I’m sorry, 맷. What will you do?”

“Oh, play cards, I suppose. If anyone will play with me. Play stones with 톰. Dice in the taverns. I can still go as far as the city, at least.” His gaze strayed toward a passing maidservant, a slender, dark-eyed girl, near his own age. “I’ll find something to take up time.”

Her hand itched to slap him, but instead she said cautiously, “맷, you really aren’t thinking of leaving, are you?”

“Would you tell 모이라인, if I was?” He put up his hands to forestall her. “Well, there’s no need. I told you I wouldn’t. I’ll not pretend I’d not like to, but I won’t. Is that good enough for you?” A pensive frown crept onto his face. “에그웨인, do you ever wish you were back home? That none of this had ever happened?”

It was a startling question, coming from him, but she knew her answer. “No. Even with everything, no. Do you?”

“I would be a fool then, wouldn’t I?” he laughed. “It’s cities I like, and this one will do for now. This one will do. 에그웨인, you won’t tell 모이라인 about this, will you? About me asking for advice and all?”

“Why shouldn’t I?” she asked suspiciously. He was 맷, after all.

He gave an embarrassed hitch of his shoulders. “I’ve been keeping wider of her than I have of. . . . Anyway, I’ve been staying clear, especially when she wants to root around in my head. She might think I’m weakening. You won’t tell her, will you?”

“I won’t,” she said, “if you promise me you will not go near that *ter’angreal* without asking her permission. I shouldn’t even have told you about it.”

“I promise.” He grinned. “I won’t go near that thing unless my life depends on it. I swear.” He finished with mock solemnity.

에그웨인 shook her head. However much everything else changed, 맷 just never would.
