CHAPTER 24

![](images/00489.jpg)

*A Message Sent*

The land changed as the sun began to sink. The hills grew lower, the thickets larger. Often the toppled stone fences of what had been fields had become mounds sprouting wild hedges, or ran through long stands of oak and leatherleaf and hickory, pine and paperbark and trees 에그웨인 did not know. The few farm houses had no roofs, and trees ten or fifteen paces high grew in them here, little woods enclosed inside the stone walls; complete with twittering birds and black-tailed squirrels. The occasional rivulet caused as much talk among the 아일 as the small forests did, and the grass. They had heard tales of the wetlands, read of them in books bought from merchants and peddlers like Hadnan Kadere, but few had actually seen them since the hunt for Laman. They adapted quickly, though; the gray-brown of the tents blended well with dead leaves under the trees and with the dying grass and weeds. The camp spread over miles, marked by thousands of small cookfires in the golden dusk.

에그웨인 was more than happy to crawl into her tent once the *gai’shain* had it up. Inside the lamps were lit and a small fire burned in the firepit. Unlacing her soft boots, she tugged them off and her woolen stockings as well, and sprawled on the bright layered rugs, wriggling her toes. She wished she had a basin of water to soak her feet. She could not pretend to be as hardy as the 아일, but she was growing soft if a few hours of walking made her feet feel twice their size. Of course, water would be no problem here. Or it should not be—she remembered that shrunken stream—but surely she could even have a proper bath again.

Cowinde, meek and silent in her white robes, brought her supper, some of that pale flat bread made from *zemai* flour and in a red-striped bowl, a thick stew that she ate mechanically, though she felt more tired than hungry. She recognized the dried peppers and beans, but did not ask what the dark meat was. *Rabbit,* she told herself firmly, and hoped that it was. The 아일 ate things that would put more curl in her hair than 엘레인 had. She was willing to bet that 랜드 could not even look at what he was eating. Men were always picky eaters.

Once done with the stew, she stretched out near an ornately worked silver lamp that had a polished silver disc to reflect and increase its light. She had felt a little guilty once she realized that most of the 아일 had no light at night but their fires; few had brought lamps or oil except the 현명한 이들 and the chiefs of clans and septs. But there was no point to sitting in the dim illumination of the firepit when she could have proper light. That reminded her: the nights here would not be so drastic a contrast with the days as in the 황무지; the tent was already beginning to feel uncomfortably warm.

She channeled briefly, flows of Air to smother the fire, and dug into her saddlebags for the worn leather-bound book that she had borrowed from 아비엔다. It was a small fat volume with crowded lines of small print, hard to read except in good light, but easily portable. *The Flame, the Blade and the Heart,* it was called, a collection of tales about 비르기테 and 가이달 케인, Anselan and Barashelle, Rogosh Eagle-eye and Dunsinin, and a dozen more. 아비엔다 claimed that she liked it for the adventures and battles, and maybe she did, but every last story told of the love of a man and a woman, too. 에그웨인 was willing to admit that that was what she liked, the sometimes stormy, sometimes tender threads of undying love. To herself she would admit it, anyway. It was hardly the sort of enjoyment a woman with any pretensions to sense at all could confess publicly.

In truth she did not feel like reading any more than she had felt like eating—all she really wanted to do was bathe and sleep, and she might be willing to forgo bathing—but tonight she and Amys were to meet 니나브 in *Tel’aran’rhiod.* It would not be night yet wherever 니나브 was, on her way to 게알단, and that meant remaining awake.

엘레인 had made the menagerie sound quite exciting at their last meeting, though 에그웨인 hardly thought that 갈라드’s presence was reason enough to go haring off like that. 니나브 and 엘레인 had simply grown to like adventure, in her opinion. It was too bad about 시우안; they needed a firm hand to settle them down. Odd that she should think of 니나브 so; 니나브 had always been the one with the firm hand. But since that episode in the Tower of *Tel’aran’rhiod,* 니나브 had become less and less someone she had to struggle against.

Guiltily, she realized as she turned a page that she was looking forward to seeing 니나브 tonight. Not because 니나브 was a friend, but because she wanted to see if the effects had lingered. If 니나브 tugged at her braid, she would arch a cool eyebrow at her, and . . . *Light, I hope it’s held. If she lets out about that jaunt, Amys and Bair and Melaine will take turns skinning me, if they don’t just tell me to go.*

Her eyes kept trying to drift shut as she read, fuzzily half-dreaming the stories in the book. She could be as strong as any of these women, as strong and brave as Dunsinin or Nerein or Melisinde or even 비르기테, as strong as 아비엔다. *Would* 니나브 have sense enough to hold her tongue in front of Amys tonight? She had a vague thought of taking 니나브 by the scruff of the neck and shaking her. Silly. 니나브 was years the older. Arch an eyebrow at her. Dunsinin. 비르기테. As hardy and strong as a Maiden of the Spear.

Her head slipped down to the pages, and she tried to cradle the small book under her cheek as her breathing slowed and deepened.

She gave a start at finding herself among the great redstone columns of the Heart of the Stone, in the strange light of *Tel’aran’rhiod,* and another at realizing that she wore the *cadin’sor.* Amys would not be pleased to see her in that; not amused at all. Hastily she changed it, and was surprised when her clothes flickered back and forth between the *algode* blouse and bulky wool skirt and a fine gown of brocaded blue silk before finally settling on the 아일 garb, complete with her ivory bracelet of flames and her gold-and-ivory necklace. That indecision had not happened to her in some time.

For a moment she thought of stepping out of the World of Dreams, but she suspected she was soundly asleep, back in her tent. Very likely she would only step into a dream of her own, and she did not yet always have awareness in her dreams; without that, she could not return to *Tel’aran’rhiod.* She was not about to leave Amys and 니나브 alone together. Who knew what 니나브 would say, if Amys got her temper up? When the Wise One arrived, she would simply say that she had just arrived herself. The 현명한 이들 had always been a bit ahead of her, or arrived at the same time, before this, but surely if Amys believed she had only been there a second it would not matter.

She had almost grown accustomed to the feel of unseen eyes in this vast chamber. *Only the columns, and the shadows, and all this empty space.* Still, she hoped that Amys was not too long in coming, nor 니나브. But they would be. Time could be as strange in *Tel’aran’rhiod* as in any dream, but it had to be a good hour yet before the arranged meeting. Perhaps she had time to . . .

Suddenly she realized that she could hear voices, like faint whispers among the columns. Embracing *세다르,* she moved cautiously toward the sound, toward the place where 랜드 had left *칼란도르* beneath the great dome. The 현명한 이들 claimed that control of *Tel’aran’rhiod* was as strong as the 하나의 힘 here, but she knew her abilities with the Power far better, and trusted them more. Still hidden well back among the thick redstone columns, she stopped and stared.

It was not a pair of Black sisters, as she had feared, and not 니나브, either. Instead, 엘레인 stood near the glittering shaft of *칼란도르* rising out of the floorstone, deep in quiet conversation with as oddly dressed a woman as 에그웨인 had ever seen. She wore a short white coat of peculiar cut and wide yellow trousers gathered in folds at her ankles, above short boots with raised heels. An intricate braid of golden hair hung down her back, and she held a bow that gleamed like polished silver. The arrows in the quiver shone, too.

에그웨인 squeezed her eyes shut. First the difficulty with her dress, and now this. Just because she had been reading about 비르기테—a silver bow told the name for certain—was no reason to imagine that she saw her. 비르기테 waited—somewhere—for the 발레르의 뿔 to call her and the other heroes to the Last Battle. But when 에그웨인 opened her eyes again, 엘레인 and the oddly dressed woman were still there. She could not quite make out what they were saying, but she believed her eyes this time. She was on the point of going out to announce herself when a voice spoke, behind her.

“Did you decide to come early? Alone?”

에그웨인 whirled to face Amys, her sun-darkened face too youthful for her white hair, and leathery-cheeked Bair. Both stood with their arms folded beneath their breasts; even the way their shawls were pulled tight spoke of displeasure.

“I fell asleep,” 에그웨인 said. It was too much before time for her story to work. Even as she explained hastily about dozing off and why she had not gone back—minus the part about not wanting 니나브 and Amys to talk alone—she was surprised to feel a tinge of shame that she had intended to lie and relief that she had not. Not that the truth would necessarily save her. Amys was not as strict as Bair—not quite—but she was perfectly capable of setting her to piling up rocks the rest of the night. Many of the 현명한 이들 were great believers in useless labor for punishment; you could not tell yourself you were doing anything other than being punished while you were burying ashes with a spoon. That was provided they did not simply refuse to teach her any more, of course. The ashes would be much preferable.

She could not hold back a sigh of relief when Amys nodded and said, “It can happen. But next time, return and dream your own dreams; I could have heard what 니나브 has to say, and tell her what we know. If Melaine was not with Bael and Dorindha tonight, she would be here, as well. You frightened Bair. She is proud of your progress, and if anything happened to you . . .”

Bair did not look proud. If anything, she scowled even more deeply as Amys paused. “You are lucky Cowinde found you when she returned to clear away your supper, and was worried when she could not rouse you to move to your blankets. If I thought you had been here more than a few minutes alone . . .” The glare sharpened in dire promise for a moment, and then her voice turned grumpy. “Now I suppose we have to wait for 니나브 to arrive, just to stop you begging if we send you back. If we must, we must, but we will use the time to advantage. Concentrate your mind on—”

“It isn’t 니나브,” 에그웨인 said hastily. She did not want to know what a lesson would be like with Bair in this mood. “It is 엘레인, and . . .” She trailed off, as she turned. 엘레인, in elegant green silk suitable for a ball, was pacing up and down not far from *칼란도르.* 비르기테 was nowhere to be seen. *I did not imagine her.*

“She is here already?” Amys said, moving to where she could see, too.

“Another young fool,” Bair muttered. “Girls today have no more brains or discipline than goats.” She stalked out ahead of 에그웨인 and Amys and planted herself across *칼란도르*’s glittering shape from 엘레인, fists on hips. “You are not my pupil, 엘레인 of 안도르—though you’ve wheedled enough out of us to keep you from killing yourself here, if you are careful—but if you were, I would welt you from your toes up and send you back to your mother until you were grown enough to be let out of her sight. Which I think might take as many more years as you have lived already. I know you have been coming into the World of Dreams alone, you and 니나브. You are both fools to do it.”

엘레인 gave a start when they first appeared, but as Bair’s tirade washed over her, she drew herself up, that chilly tilt to her chin. Her gown became red and took on a finer sheen, and grew embroidery down the sleeves and across the high bodice, including rearing lions in white and golden lilies, her own sigil. A thin golden diadem rested in her red-gold curls, a single rearing lion set in moonstones above her brows. She did not yet have the best control over such things. Then again, maybe she wore exactly what she intended this time. “I do thank you for your concern,” she said regally. “Yet it is true that I am not your pupil, Bair of the Haido Shaarad. I am grateful for your instruction, but I must go my own way on the tasks given me by the 아미를린 석좌.”

“A dead woman,” Bair said coldly. “You claim obedience to a dead woman.” 에그웨인 could all but feel Bair’s hackles standing erect in anger; if she did not do something, Bair might decide to teach 엘레인 a painful lesson. The last thing they needed was that sort of squabble.

“What . . . Why are you here instead of 니나브?” She had been going to ask what 엘레인 was doing there, but that would have given Bair an opening, and maybe sounded as if she were on the Wise One’s side. What she wanted to ask was what 엘레인 had been doing talking to 비르기테. *I did not imagine it.* Maybe it had been someone dreaming she was 비르기테. But only those who entered *Tel’aran’rhiod* knowingly remained for more than minutes, and 엘레인 surely would not have been speaking with one of them. Where *did* 비르기테 and the others wait?

“니나브 is nursing a sore head.” The diadem vanished, and 엘레인’s gown became simpler, with only a few golden scrolls around the bodice.

“Is she ill?” 에그웨인 asked anxiously.

“Only with a headache, and a bruise or two.” 엘레인 giggled and winced at the same time. “Oh, 에그웨인, you would not have believed it. All four of the Chavanas had come to have supper with us. To flirt with 니나브, really. They tried flirting with me the first few days, but 톰 had a talk with them, and they stopped. He did not have any right to do that. Not that I *wanted* them to flirt, you understand. Anyway, there they were, flirting with 니나브—or trying to, because she paid them no more mind than buzzing flies—when Latelle stalked up and began hitting 니나브 with a stick, calling her all sorts of terrible names.”

“Was she hurt?” 에그웨인 was not sure which of them she meant. If 니나브’s temper was roused . . .

“Not her. The Chavanas tried to pull her off Latelle, and Taeric will likely limp for days, not to mention Brugh’s swollen lip. Petra had to carry Latelle to her wagon, and I doubt she’ll put her nose out for some time.” 엘레인 shook her head. “Luca did not know who to blame—one of his acrobats lamed and his bear trainer weeping on her bed—so he blamed everybody, and I thought 니나브 was going to box his ears as well. At least she did not channel; I thought she was going to once or twice, until she had Latelle down on the ground.”

Amys and Bair exchanged unreadable glances; this certainly was not how they expected 에스 세다이 to behave.

에그웨인 felt a little confused herself, but it was mainly over keeping up with all these people she had only heard of briefly before. Odd people, traveling with lions, dogs and bears. And an Illuminator. She did not believe this Petra could possibly be as strong as 엘레인 claimed. But then, 톰 was eating fire as well as juggling, and what 엘레인 and Juilin were doing sounded as strange, even if she was using the Power.

If 니나브 had come close to channeling . . . 엘레인 must have seen the glow of her embracing *세다르.* Whether they had a real reason to be hiding or not, they would not remain hidden long if one of them channeled and let people see it. The Tower’s eyes-and-ears would certainly hear; that sort of news traveled quickly, especially if they were not out of 아마디시아 yet.

“You tell 니나브 from me that she had best hold her temper, or I’ll have some words to say to her that she will not like.” 엘레인 looked startled—니나브 had certainly not told her what had passed between them—and 에그웨인 added, “If she channels, you can be sure 엘라이더 will hear of it as soon as a pigeon can fly to 타르 발론.” She could not say more; as it was, it brought another exchange of glances between Amys and Bair. What they really thought of a Tower divided, and an Amyrlin who as far as they knew had given orders for 에스 세다이 to be drugged, they had never let on. They could make 모이라인 look like the village gossip when they wished. “In fact, I wish I had both of you alone. If we were in the Tower, in our old rooms, I’d say a few words to the pair of you.”

엘레인 stiffened, as queenly and cool as she had been with Bair. “You may say them to me whenever you wish.”

Had she understood? Alone; away from the 현명한 이들. In the Tower. 에그웨인 could only hope. Best to change the subject and hope the 현명한 이들 were not picking over her words as carefully as she hoped that 엘레인 was. “Will this fight with Latelle cause problems?” What had 니나브 been thinking of? Back home, she would have had any woman her age who did the same up before the Women’s Circle so fast that her eyes would pop. “You must be almost to 게알단 by now.”

“Three more days, Luca says, if we are lucky. The menagerie does not move very fast.”

“Perhaps you should leave them now.”
“Perhaps,” 엘레인 said slowly. “I really would like to highwalk just once in front of . . .” With a shake of her head, she glanced at *칼란도르*; the neckline of her gown dipped precipitously, then rose again. “I do not know, 에그웨인. We could not travel much faster alone than we are traveling, and we don’t know where to go exactly, yet.” That meant 니나브 had not remembered where the Blues were gathering. If 엘라이더’s report had been right. “Not to mention that 니나브 might burst if we had to abandon the wagon and buy saddle horses, or another coach. Besides, we are both learning a great deal about the 쇼엔찬. Cerandin served as a *s’redit* handler at the Court of the Nine Moons, where the 쇼엔찬 여제 sits. Yesterday she showed us things that she took when she fled Falme. 에그웨인, she had an *a’dam.*”

에그웨인 stepped forward, her skirts brushing *칼란도르.* 랜드’s traps were not physical, whatever 니나브 seemed to think. “Can you be sure she was not a *sul’dam*?” Her voice trembled with anger.

“I am certain,” 엘레인 said soothingly. “I put the *a’dam* on her myself, and it had no effect.”

That was a little secret that the 쇼엔찬 themselves did not know, or hid well if they did. Their *다만* were women born with the spark, women who would channel eventually even if untaught. But the *sul’dam,* who controlled the *다만*—they were the women who needed to be taught. The 쇼엔찬 thought that women who could channel were dangerous animals who had to be controlled, and yet unknowingly gave many of them honored positions.

“I do not understand this interest in the 쇼엔찬.” Amys said the name awkwardly; she had never heard it until 엘레인 spoke it at their last meeting. “What they do is terrible, but they are gone. 랜드 al’Thor defeated them, and they fled.”

에그웨인 turned her back and stared at the huge polished columns running off into shadow. “Gone is not to say they will never come back.” She did not want them to see her face, not even 엘레인. “We must know whatever we can learn, in case they ever return.” They had put an *a’dam* on her in Falme. They had meant to send her over the Aryth Ocean to 쇼엔찬, to spend the rest of her life as a dog on a leash. Fury welled up in her every time she thought of them. And fear, too. The fear that if they did return, they would succeed in taking and holding her this time. That was what she could not allow them to see. The stark terror that she knew was in her eyes.

엘레인 put a hand on her arm. “We will be ready for them if they do come back,” she said gently. “They will not find us in surprise and ignorance again.” 에그웨인 patted her hand, though she wanted to clutch it; 엘레인 understood more than 에그웨인 wished, yet it was comforting that she did.

“Let us finish what we are here for,” Bair said briskly. “You need to be asleep in truth, 에그웨인.”

“We had the *gai’shain* undress you, and put you in your blankets.” Surprisingly, Amys sounded as gentle as 엘레인. “When you return to your body, you can sleep until morning.”

에그웨인’s cheeks colored. Given 아일 ways, it was as likely as not that some of those *gai’shain* had been men. She would have to speak to them about that—delicately, of course; they would not understand, and it was not a thing she could be comfortable explaining.

The fear was gone, she realized. *Apparently I’m more afraid of being embarrassed than I am of the 쇼엔찬.* It was not true, but she held to the thought.

There was really little to tell 엘레인. That they were in 케렌 finally, that Couladin had devastated Selean and ravaged the surrounding land, that the Shaido were still days ahead and moving west. The 현명한 이들 knew more than she; they had not taken to their tents straightaway. There had been skirmishes in the evening, small ones and only a few, with mounted men who quickly fled, and other men on horses who had been sighted ran without fighting. There had been no prisoners taken. 모이라인 and 란 seemed to think that the riders could have been bandits, or supporters of one or another of the Houses trying to claim the Sun Throne. All had been equally ragged. Whoever they were, word would soon spread that there were more 아일 in 케렌.

“They had to learn sooner or later” was 엘레인’s only comment.

에그웨인 watched 엘레인 as she and the 현명한 이들 faded away—to her it seemed as though 엘레인 and the Heart of the Stone became more and more attenuated—but her golden-haired friend gave no sign as to whether she had understood the message.

CHAPTER 25

![](images/00472.jpg)

*Dreams of 갈라드*

Instead of returning to her own body, 에그웨인 floated in darkness. She seemed to be darkness herself, without substance. Whether her body lay up or down or sideways from her, she did not know—there was no direction here—but she knew that it was near, that she could step into it easily. All around her in the blackness, fireflies seemingly twinkled, a vast horde fading away into unimaginable distance. Those were dreams, dreams of the 아일 in the camp, dreams of men and women across 케렌, across the world, all glittering there.

She could pick out some among the nearer and name the dreamer, now. In one way those sparkles were just as alike as fireflies—that was what had given her so much trouble in the beginning—but in another, somehow, they now seemed as individual as faces. 랜드’s dreams, and 모이라인’s, appeared muted, dimmed by the wards they had woven. Amys’ and Bair’s were bright and regular in their pulsing; they had taken their own advice, apparently. Had she not seen those, she would have been into her body in an instant. Those two could rove this darkness much more ably than she; she would not have known they were there until they pounced on her. If she ever learned to recognize 엘레인 and 니나브 in the same way, she would be able to find them in that great constellation wherever they were in the world. But tonight she did not mean to observe anyone’s dream.

Carefully she formed a well-remembered image in her mind, and she was back in *Tel’aran’rhiod,* inside the small, windowless room in the Tower where she had lived as a 수련생. A narrow bed was built against one white-painted wall. A washstand and a three-legged stool stood opposite the door, and the current occupant’s dresses and shifts of white wool hung with a white cloak on pegs. There could as easily have been none; the Tower had not been able to fill the 수련생s’ quarters in many years. The floor was almost as pale as walls and clothes. Every day the 수련생 who lived there would scrub that floor on hands and knees; 에그웨인 had done so herself, and 엘레인, in the next room. If a queen came to train in the Tower, she would start in a room like this, scrubbing the floor.

The garments were arranged differently when she glanced at them again, but she ignored that. Ready to embrace *세다르* in a heartbeat, she opened the door just enough to stick her head out. And drew a relieved breath when she found 엘레인’s head coming just as slowly out of the next doorway. 에그웨인 hoped she did not appear as wide-eyed and uncertain. She motioned hurriedly, and 엘레인 scurried across in 수련생 white that became a pale gray silk riding dress as she darted inside. 에그웨인 hated gray dresses; that was what *다만* wore.

For an instant more she stayed there, scanning the railed galleries of the 수련생s’ quarters. Layer on layer they rose, and fell as many levels to the Novices’ Court below. Not that she really expected Liandrin or worse to be out there, but it never hurt to be careful.

“I thought this was what you meant,” 엘레인 said as she shut the door. “Do you have any idea how difficult it is to remember what I can say in front of whom? Sometimes I wish we could just tell the 현명한 이들 everything. Let them know we are only 허락받은 자, and be done with it.”

“You would be done with it,” 에그웨인 said firmly. “I happen to be sleeping not twenty paces from them.”

엘레인 shivered. “That Bair. She reminds me of Lini when I’d broken something I was not supposed to touch.”

“You wait until I introduce you to Sorilea.” 엘레인 gave her a doubtful look, but then, 에그웨인 was not sure that she would have believed Sorilea herself until she met her. There was no way to do this easily. She shifted her shawl. “Tell me about meeting 비르기테. It was 비르기테, wasn’t it?”

엘레인 staggered as if hit in the stomach. Her blue eyes closed for a moment, and she took a breath that must have filled her to the toes. “I cannot talk to you about that.”

“What do you mean you can’t talk? You have a tongue. Was it 비르기테?”

“I *cannot,* 에그웨인. You must believe me. I would if I could, but I cannot. Perhaps . . . I can ask . . .” If 엘레인 had been the kind of woman to wring her hands, she would have been doing it then. Her mouth opened and closed without any words coming out; her eyes darted around the room as if seeking inspiration or aid. Taking a deep breath, she fixed an urgent blue gaze on 에그웨인. “Anything I say violates confidences I promised to hold. Even that. Please, 에그웨인. You must trust me. And you must not tell *anyone* what you . . . think you saw.”

에그웨인 forced the stern frown from her face. “I will trust you.” At least she knew now for a fact that she had not been seeing things. *비르기테? Light!* “I hope that one day you will trust me enough to tell me.”

“I *do* trust you, but . . .” Shaking her head, 엘레인 sat down on the edge of the neatly made bed. “We keep secrets too often, 에그웨인, but sometimes there is a reason.”

After a moment 에그웨인 nodded and sat next to her. “When you can,” was all she said, but her friend gave her a relieved hug.

“I told myself I was not going to ask this, 에그웨인. Just once I was not going to have my head full of him.” The gray riding dress became a shimmering green gown; 엘레인 could not possibly have been aware of how deeply the neckline swooped. “But . . . is 랜드 well?”

“He is alive and unharmed, if that is what you mean. I thought he was hard in 티어, but today I heard him threaten to hang men if they go against his commands. Not that they are bad orders—he won’t let anyone take food without paying, or murder people—but still. They were the first to hail him as He Who Comes With the Dawn; they followed him out of the 황무지 without hesitation. And he threatened them, as hard as cold steel.”

“Not a threat, 에그웨인. He is a king, whatever you or he or anyone else says, and a king or queen must dispense justice without fear of enemies or favor for friends. Anyone who does that has to be hard. Mother can make the city walls seem soft, sometimes.”

“He doesn’t have to be so arrogant about it,” 에그웨인 said levelly. “니나브 said I should remind him he’s only a man, but I’ve not figured out how yet.”

“He *does* have to remember he is only a man. But he has a right to expect to be obeyed.” There was something of a haughty tone to 엘레인’s voice, until she glanced down at herself. Then her face went crimson, and the green gown suddenly had a lace neck under her chin. “Are you sure you are not mistaking that for arrogance?” she finished in a strangled voice.

“He’s as overweening as a pig in a pea field.” 에그웨인 shifted herself on the bed; she remembered it as hard, but the thin mattress felt softer than what she slept on in the tent. She did not want to talk about 랜드. “Are you certain this fight will not cause more trouble?” A feud with this Latelle could not make their traveling easier.

“I do not think so. Latelle’s grievance against 니나브 was that all the unattached men were no longer hers to pick and choose from. Some women do think that way, I suppose. 알루드라 keeps to herself, and Cerandin wouldn’t have said boo to a goose until I started teaching her to stand up for herself, and Clarine is married to Petra. But 니나브 has made it clear that she’ll box the ears of any man who even *thinks* he can flirt with her, *and* she apologized to Latelle, so I hope that may settle it.”

“She *apologized*?”

The other woman nodded, her face as bemused as 에그웨인 knew her own must be. “I thought she *would* thump Luca when he told her she must—he doesn’t seem to think her injunction holds to him, by the way—but she did it, after grumping about for an hour. Muttering about you, actually.” She hesitated, giving 에그웨인 a sidelong look. “Did you say something to her at your last meeting? She has been . . . different . . . since then, and sometimes she talks to herself. Argues, really. About you, from the little I’ve heard.”

“I said nothing that did not have to be said.” So it was holding, whatever it was that had happened between them. Either that, or 니나브 was storing up her anger for the next time they met. She was not going to put up with the woman’s temper anymore, not now that she knew she did not have to. “You tell her from me that she is too old to be rolling about on the ground fighting. If she gets into another, I’ll have worse to say to her. You tell her that exactly. It will be worse.” Let 니나브 chew on that until next time. Either she would be mild as a lamb . . . Or else 에그웨인 would just have to carry through on her threat. 니나브 might be stronger in the Power, when she could channel, but here, 에그웨인 was. One way or another, she was finished with 니나브’s tantrums.

“I will tell her,” 엘레인 said. “You have changed, too. There seems to be something of 랜드’s attitude about you.”

It took 에그웨인 a moment to realize what she meant, helped by that amused little smile. “Don’t be silly.”

엘레인 laughed aloud and gave her another hug. “Oh, 에그웨인, you will be 아미를린 석좌 one day, when I am Queen of 안도르.”

“If there is a Tower then,” 에그웨인 said soberly, and 엘레인’s laughter faded.

“엘라이더 cannot destroy the 백색 탑, 에그웨인. Whatever she does, the Tower will remain. Perhaps she will not stay Amyrlin. Once 니나브 remembers the name of that town, I will wager that we find a Tower in exile, with every 아자 but the Red.”

“I hope so.” 에그웨인 knew she sounded sad. She wanted 에스 세다이 to support 랜드 and oppose 엘라이더, but that meant the 백색 탑 broken for sure, maybe never to be made whole again.

“I must get back,” 엘레인 said. “니나브 insists that whichever of us does not enter *Tel’aran’rhiod* remain awake, and with her headache, she needs to drink one of her herb teas and sleep. I do not know why she is so insistent. Whoever is watching can do nothing to help, and we both know enough to be perfectly safe here, now.” Her green dress flickered to 비르기테’s white coat and voluminous yellow trousers for an instant, then snapped back. “She said I wasn’t to tell you this, but she thinks that 모그헤디엔 is trying to find us. Her and me.”

에그웨인 did not ask the obvious question. Clearly it was something that 비르기테 had told them. Why did 엘레인 persist in trying to keep that secret? *Because she promised to. 엘레인 never broke a promise in her life.* “You tell her to be careful.” Small chance that 니나브 was sitting and waiting, if she thought one of the 버림받은 자들 was after her. She would be remembering that she had defeated the woman once, and she had always had more courage than sense. “The 버림받은 자들 are nothing to take lightly. And neither are 쇼엔찬, even if they are supposedly just animal trainers. You tell her that.”

“I do not suppose you would listen if I told you to be careful, too.”

She gave 엘레인 a startled look. “I am always careful. You know that.”

“Of course.” The last thing 에그웨인 saw as the other woman faded away was a very amused smile.

에그웨인 herself did not go. If 니나브 could not remember where that gathering of Blues was, perhaps she could discover it here. It was hardly a new idea: this was not her first trip to the Tower since her last meeting with 니나브. She put on a copy of Enaila’s face, with flame-colored hair to her shoulders, and an 허락받은 자’s dress with its banded hem, then formed the image of 엘라이더’s ornately furnished study.

It was as it had been before, though on every visit fewer of the vine-carved stools stood in that arc in front of the wide writing table. The paintings still hung above the fireplace. 에그웨인 strode straight to the table, pushing aside that thronelike chair with its inlaid ivory Flame of 타르 발론, so she could reach the lacquered letterbox. Lifting the lid, all fighting hawks and clouds, she began scanning parchments as fast as she could. Even so, some melted away half-read, or changed. There was no way to tell what was important and what insignificant beforehand.

Most seemed reports of failure. Still no word of where the Lord of 바쉐어 had taken his army, and a note of frustration and worry tinging the words. That name tickled the back of her mind, but with no time to waste she pushed it firmly away and snatched up another sheet. No word on 랜드’s whereabouts, either, said a cringing report filled with near panic. That was good to know, and worth the trip by itself. More than a month had passed since the last news from Tanchico by any 아자’s eyes-and-ears, and others in 타라본 had also gone silent; the writer blamed the anarchy there; rumors that someone had taken Tanchico could not be confirmed, but the writer suggested that 랜드 himself was involved. Even better, if 엘라이더 was looking in the wrong place by a thousand leagues. A confused report said that a Red sister in Caemlyn claimed to have seen 모르가세 at a public audience, but various 아자s’ agents in Caemlyn said the Queen had been in seclusion for days. Fighting in the 국경지대, possibly minor rebellions in 시엔나르 and 아라펠; the parchment was gone before she reached the reason. Pedron Niall calling in 백의단 to 아마디시아, possibly to move against 알타라. A good thing that 엘레인 and 니나브 had only another three days there.

The next parchment was about 엘레인 and 니나브. First the writer advised against punishing the agent who had allowed them to escape—엘라이더 had scratched that out in bold strokes and written “Make an example!” in the margin—and then, just when the woman began to detail the search for the pair in 아마디시아, the single sheet became a fistful, a sheaf of what seemed to be builders’ and masons’ estimates for constructing a private residence for the 아미를린 석좌 on the Tower grounds. More like a palace, by the number of pages.

She let the pages fall, and they vanished before they finished scattering across the tabletop. The lacquered box was closed again. She could spend the rest of her life here, she knew; there would always be more documents in the box, and they would always be changing. The more ephemeral something was in the waking world—a letter, a piece of clothing, a bowl that might be frequently moved—the less firm its reflection in *Tel’aran’rhiod.* She could not remain here too long; sleep while in the World of Dreams was not as restful as sleep undisturbed.

Hurrying out to the antechamber, she was about to reach for the neat piles of scrolls and parchments, some with seals, on the Keeper’s writing table, when the room seemed to flicker. Before she had time to even consider what that meant, the door opened, and 갈라드 stepped in, smiling, his brocaded blue coat fitting his shoulders perfectly, snug breeches showing the shape of his calves.

She took a deep breath, her stomach fluttering. It just was not fair for a man to have a face so beautiful.

He stepped closer, dark eyes twinkling, and brushed her cheek with his fingers. “Will you walk with me in the Water Garden?” he said softly.

“If you two wish to canoodle,” a brisk woman’s voice said, “you will not do so here.”

에그웨인 spun, wide-eyed, staring at 리안 seated behind the table with the Keeper’s stole on her shoulders and a fond smile on her copper-cheeked face. The door to the Amyrlin’s study was open, and inside 시우안 stood beside her simple, well-polished writing table, reading a long parchment, the striped stole of office on her shoulders. This was madness.

She fled without thinking of what image she was forming, and found herself gulping for breath on the Green in Emond’s Field, with the thatch-roofed houses all around, and the Winespring gushing from the stone outcrop on the broad expanse of grass. Near the swift, rapidly widening stream stood her father’s small inn, its lower floor stone, the overhanging upper whitewashed. “The only roof like it in the 두 강,” Bran al’Vere had often said of his red tiles. The large stone foundation near the Winespring Inn, a huge, spreading oak rising from its center, was far older than the inn, but some said an inn of some sort had stood there beside the Winespring Water for more than two thousand years.

*Fool.* After warning 니나브 so firmly about dreams in *Tel’aran’rhiod,* she had nearly let herself be caught in one of her own. Though it was odd that it had been 갈라드. She did dream of him, sometimes. Her face heated; she certainly did not love him, or even like him very much, but he was beautiful, and in those dreams he had been much more what she could have wished him. It was his brother 가윈 that she dreamed of more often, but that was just as silly. Whatever 엘레인 said, he had never made any feelings known to her.

It was that fool book, with all those tales of lovers. As soon as she woke in the morning she was going to give the thing back to 아비엔다. And tell her that she did not think that she read it for the adventures at all.

She was reluctant to leave, though. Home. Emond’s Field. The last place that she had really felt safe. More than a year and a half had passed since she last saw it, yet everything seemed as she remembered. Not quite everything. On the Green stood two tall poles with large banners, one a red eagle, the other an equally red wolf’s head.

Had 페린 anything to do with those? She could not imagine how. Yet he had come home, so 랜드 said, and she had dreamed of him with wolves more than once.

Enough idle standing about. It was time to—

*Flicker.*

Her mother stepped out of the inn, graying braid pulled over one shoulder. Marin al’Vere was a slim woman, still handsome, and the best cook in the 두 강. 에그웨인 could hear her father laughing inside the common room, where he was meeting with the rest of the Village Council.

“Are you still out here, child?” her mother said, gently chiding and amused. “You’ve certainly been married long enough to know you shouldn’t let your husband know you mope about waiting on him.” With a shake of her head, she laughed. “Too late. Here he comes.”

에그웨인 turned eagerly, eyes darting past the children playing on the Green. The timbers of the low Wagon Bridge thrummed as 가윈 galloped across and swung down from his saddle in front of her. Tall and straight in his gold-embroidered red coat, he had his sister’s red-gold curls, and marvelous deep blue eyes. He was not so handsome as his half-brother, of course, but her heart beat faster for him than it had for 갈라드—*For 갈라드? What?*—and she had to press her hands to her stomach in a vain attempt to still gigantic butterflies.

“Did you miss me?” he said, smiling.

“A little.” *Why did I think of 갈라드? As if I’d just seen him a moment ago.* “Now and then, when there was nothing interesting to occupy my time. Did you miss me?”

For answer, he pulled her off her feet and kissed her. She was not aware of very much else until he set her back down on unsteady legs. The banners were gone. *What banners?*

“Here he is,” her mother said, approaching with a babe wrapped in swaddling. “Here’s your son. He is a fine boy. He never cries at all.”

가윈 laughed as he took the child, held him aloft. “He does have your eyes, 에그웨인. He will be a fine one with the girls one day.”

에그웨인 backed away from them, shaking her head. There *had* been banners, red eagle and red wolf’s head. She *had* seen 갈라드. In the Tower. “NOOOOOOO!”

She fled, leaping from *Tel’aran’rhiod* to her own body. Awareness remained only long enough for her to wonder how she could possibly have been fool enough to let her own fancies nearly trap her, and then she was deep in her own safe dream. 가윈 galloped across the Wagon Bridge, swinging down. . . .

Stepping out from behind a thatch-roofed house, 모그헤디엔 wondered idly where this little village was. Not the sort of place she would expect to see banners flying. The girl had been stronger than she had thought, to escape her weaving of *Tel’aran’rhiod.* Even 란피어 could not improve on her abilities here, whatever she claimed. Still, the girl had just been of interest because she was speaking to 엘레인 Trakand, who might lead her to 니나브 al’Meara. The only reason to trap her had simply been to rid *Tel’aran’rhiod* of one who could walk it freely. It was bad enough that she must share it with 란피어.

But 니나브 al’Meara. That woman she meant to make beg to be bound in her service. She would take her in the flesh, perhaps ask the Great Lord to grant her immortality, so 니나브 could have forever to regret opposing 모그헤디엔. She and 엘레인 were scheming with 비르기테, were they? That was another she had reason to punish. 비르기테 had not even known who 모그헤디엔 was, so long ago, in the 전설의 시대, when she foiled 모그헤디엔’s finely wrought plan to lay 르웨어스 테린 by his heels. But 모그헤디엔 had known her. Only, 비르기테—Teadra, she had been then—had died before she could deal with her. Death was no punishment, no end, not when it meant living on here.

니나브 al’Meara, 엘레인 Trakand, and 비르기테. Those three she would find, and deal with. From the shadows, so that they would not know until too late. All three, without exception.

She vanished, and the banners waved on in the breeze of *Tel’aran’rhiod.*

CHAPTER 26

![](images/00209.jpg)

*Sallie Daera*

The halo of greatness, blue and gold, flickered fitfully around 로가인’s head, though he rode slumped in his saddle. 민 did not understand why it had appeared more often of late. He no longer even bothered to lift his eyes from the weeds in front of his black stallion to the low, wooded hills rolling by all around them.

The other two women rode together a little ahead, 시우안 as awkward on shaggy Bela as she had ever been, 리안 guiding her gray mare deftly, with knees more than reins. Only an unnaturally straight ribbon of ferns, poking through the leaf-covered forest floor, hinted that there had ever been a road here. The lacy ferns were withering, and the leaf mold rustled and crackled dryly under the horses’ hooves. Thickly woven branches gave a little shelter from the noonday sun, but it was hardly cool. Sweat rolled down 민’s face, despite an occasional breeze that stirred from behind them.
Fifteen days now they had ridden west and south from Lugard, guided only by 시우안’s insistence that she knew exactly where they were heading. Not that she shared her destination, of course; 시우안 and 리안 were as close-mouthed as sprung bear traps. 민 was not even sure that 리안 actually knew. Fifteen days, while towns and villages grew fewer and farther between, until finally there were none. Day by day 로가인’s shoulders had sagged a little more, and day by day the halo appeared more often. At first he had only begun muttering that they were chasing Jak o’ the Mists, but 시우안 had regained her leadership without opposition as he turned more and more inward. For the past six days he had not seemed to have the energy to care where they were going or whether they would ever get there.

시우안 and 리안 talked quietly up ahead, now. All 민 could hear was a barely audible murmur that might as well have been the wind in the leaves. And if she tried to ride closer, they would tell her to keep an eye on 로가인, or simply stare at her until only a stone-blind fool could keep her nose where it did not belong. They had done both often enough. From time to time, though, 리안 twisted in her saddle to look at 로가인.

Finally 리안 let Moonflower fall back beside his black stallion. The heat did not seem to be bothering her; not so much as a sheen of perspiration marred her coppery face. 민 reined Wildrose aside to give her room.

“It won’t be long now,” 리안 told him in a sultry voice. He did not look up from the weeds in front of his horse. She leaned closer, holding his arm for balance. Pressing against it, really. “A little while longer, Dalyn. You will have your revenge.” His eyes stayed dully on the road.

“A dead man would pay more notice,” 민 said, and meant it. She had been taking notes in her head of everything 리안 did, and talking with her of an evening, though trying not to let on why. She would never be able to behave the way that 리안 did—*not unless I had enough wine in me that I couldn’t think at all*—yet a few pointers might come in handy. “Maybe if you kissed him?”

리안 shot her a glare that could have frozen a rushing stream, but 민 merely looked back. She had never had the problems with 리안 that she did with 시우안—well, not as many, anyway—and the few difficulties had grown less since the other woman had left the Tower. Much fewer since they had begun discussing men. How could you be intimidated by a woman who had told you in dead seriousness that there were one hundred and seven different kisses, and ninety-three ways to touch a man’s face with your hand? 리안 actually seemed to believe these things.

민 had not meant it as a jibe, really, the suggestion of a kiss. 리안 had been cooing at him, giving him smiles that should have made steam rise from his ears, since the day he had had to be hauled out of his blankets instead of rising first to chivvy the rest of them. 민 did not know whether 리안 actually felt something for the man, though she did find it hard to credit even the possibility, or was just trying to keep him from giving up and dying, to keep him alive for whatever 시우안 had planned.

리안 certainly had not given up flirting with others besides him. She and 시우안 had apparently worked out that 시우안 would deal with women, 리안 with men, and so it had been ever since Lugard. Her smiles and glances had twice gotten them rooms where the innkeeper had said there were none, lowered the bill at those and three more, and on two nights earned barns instead of bushes for sleeping. They had also gotten the four of them chased off by one farmwife with a pitchfork, and a breakfast of cold porridge *thrown* at them by another, but 리안 had thought the incidents funny, if no one else did. The last few days, however, 로가인 had stopped reacting like every other man who saw her for more than two minutes. He had stopped reacting to her or anything else.

시우안 pulled Bela back stiffly, elbows out and managing to look on the point of falling off any moment. The heat was not touching her, either. “Have you viewed him today?” She hardly glanced at 로가인.

“It is still the same,” 민 said patiently. 시우안 refused to understand or believe, however many times she told her, and so did 리안. It would not have mattered if she had not seen the aura since her first viewing of it in 타르 발론. Had 로가인 been lying in the road, rasping his death rattle, she would have wagered all she had and more on a miraculous recovery, somehow. The appearance of an 에스 세다이 to Heal him. Something. What she saw was always true. It always happened. She knew the same way that she had known the first time she saw 랜드 al’Thor that she would fall desperately, helplessly in love with him, the same way she had known she would have to share him with two other women. 로가인 was destined for glory such as few men had dreamed of.

“Don’t you take that tone with me,” 시우안 said, that blue-eyed gaze sharpening. “It is bad enough we have to spoon-feed this great hairy carp to make him eat, without you going sulky as a fisher-bird in winter. I may have to put up with him, girl, but if you start giving me trouble, too, you will regret it in short order. Do I make myself clear?”

“Yes, Mara.” *At least you could have put a touch of sarcasm in it*, she thought scornfully. *You don’t have to be meek as a goose. You’ve told 리안 off to her face.* The 도마니 woman had suggested that she practice what they had been discussing on a farrier in the last village. A tall, handsome man, with strong-looking hands and a slow smile, but still . . . “I will try not to be sulky.” The worst part was that she realized she had tried to sound sincere. 시우안 had that effect. 민 could not even begin to imagine 시우안 discussing how to smile at a man. 시우안 would look a man in the eye, tell him what to do, and expect to see it done promptly. Just the way she did with everyone else. If she did anything else, as she had with 로가인, it would only be because the point did not matter enough to press.

“It is not much farther, is it?” 리안 said briskly. She saved the other voice for men. “I do not like the look of him, and if we have to stop for another night . . . Well, if he helps any less than he did this morning, I don’t know that we will be able to get him into his saddle again.”

“Not much, if those last directions I had are right.” 시우안 sounded irritated. She had asked questions at that last village, two days ago—not letting 민 hear, of course; 로가인 had showed no interest—and she did not like to be reminded of them. 민 could not understand why. 시우안 could hardly expect 엘라이더 to be behind them.

She herself hoped it was not much farther. It was hard to be sure how far south they had drifted since leaving the highway to Jehannah. Most villagers had only vague notions of where their village actually was in relation to anything except the nearest towns, but when they crossed the Manetherendrelle into 알타라, just before 시우안 took them away from the well-traveled road, the grizzled old ferryman had been studying a tattered map for some reason, a map that stretched as far as the Mountains of Mist. Unless her estimate was off, they were going to reach another wide river in not many miles. Either the Boern, which meant they were already into 게알단, where the Prophet and his mobs were, or else the Eldar, with 아마디시아 and 백의단 on the far side.

She was betting on 게알단, Prophet or no Prophet, and even that was a surprise if they really were close. Only a fool would think to find a gathering of 에스 세다이 any nearer to 아마디시아 than they had to be, and 시우안 was anything but that. Whether they were in 게알단 or 알타라, 아마디시아 had to be not many miles distant.

“온순화 would have to catch up to him now,” 시우안 muttered. “If he can only hang on a few more days . . .” 민 kept her mouth shut; if the woman would not listen, there was no use in speaking.

Shaking her head, 시우안 heeled Bela back into the lead, gripping her reins as though expecting the stout mare to bolt, and 리안 returned to silken-voiced cajoling of 로가인. Maybe she did have feelings for him; it would be no odder a choice than 민’s own.

Forested hills slid on by with never a sign of change, all trees and tangles of weeds and brambles. The ferns that marked the old road ran on, arrow-straight; 리안 had said the soil was different where the road had been, as if 민 should have known that. Squirrels with tufted ears sometimes chattered at them from a branch, and occasionally birds called. Which birds, 민 could not begin to guess. Baerlon might not be a city when compared to Caemlyn or Ilian or 티어, but she thought of herself as a city woman; a bird was a bird. And she did not care what kind of dirt a fern grew in.

Her doubts began to surface again. They had oozed up more than once after Kore Springs, but back then it had been easier to push them down. Since Lugard they had bubbled to the top more often, and she found herself considering 시우안 in ways she would never have dared, once. Not that she had the nerve to actually confront 시우안 with any of them, of course; it galled her to admit that, even to herself. But maybe 시우안 did *not* know where she was going. She could lie, since stilling broke her away from the 세 가지 맹세. Maybe she was still just hoping that if she continued searching she would find some trace of what she needed desperately to find. In a small way, a peculiar way surely, 리안 had begun making a life for herself apart from concerns of power and the Power and 랜드. Not that she had abandoned them entirely, but 민 did not think there *was* anything else for 시우안. The 백색 탑 and the 용의 환생 were the whole of her life, and she would hold to them even if she had to lie to herself.

Woodland gave way to a large village so quickly that 민 stared. Sweet-gum and oak and scrubby pine—those were trees she could recognize—running to within fifty paces of thatch-roofed houses made of rounded river stones and clinging to low hills. She was willing to wager that not so long ago the forest had grown right through. A good many trees actually stood in narrow little thickets among some of the houses, crowding against the walls, and here and there unweathered stumps stood close by the front of a house. The streets still had a look of new-turned earth, not the hard-packed surface that came from generations of feet. Men in their shirtsleeves were up laying new thatch atop three large stone cubes that had to have been inns—one actually had the remains of a faded, weathered sign dangling above the door—yet no old thatch lay anywhere that she could see. There were far too many women out and about for the number of men in sight, and far too few children playing for the number of women. The smells of midday cooking in the air were the only normal things about the place.

If the first glimpse startled 민, when she really saw what lay in front of her she nearly fell out of her saddle. The younger women, shaking blankets from a window or hurrying on some errand, wore plain woolen dresses, but no village of any size had ever contained so many women in riding dresses of silk or fine wool, in every color and cut. Around those women, and around most of the men, auras and images floated before her eyes, changing and flickering; most people rarely had anything for her viewing, but 에스 세다이 and 감시자s seldom lacked an aura for as much as an hour. The children must have belonged to Tower servants. 에스 세다이 who married were few and far between, but knowing them, they would have made every effort to bring their servants, with their families, out of any place they felt that they must flee themselves. 시우안 had found her gathering.

There was an eerie stillness as they rode into the village. No one spoke. 에스 세다이 stood without moving, watching them, and so did younger women and girls who must be 허락받은 자 or even 수련생s. Men who a moment before had been moving with wolfish grace were frozen, one hand hidden in thatch, or reaching into a doorway, doubtless where weapons were hidden. The children vanished, hurriedly herded away by the adults who had to be servants. Under all those unwinking stares, the hair on the back of 민’s neck tried to stand up.

리안 appeared uneasy, casting sidelong glances at the people they rode past, but 시우안 stayed smooth-faced and calm as she led the way straight to the largest inn, the one with the unreadable sign, and scrambled down to tie Bela to the iron ring of one of the stone hitching posts that appeared to have been only recently set upright. Helping 리안 help 로가인 to the ground—시우안 never offered a hand in getting him up or down—민 found her eyes darting around. Everyone staring, no one moving. “I never expected to be greeted like a long-lost daughter,” she murmured to the other woman, “but why isn’t anyone at least saying hello?”

Before 리안 could answer—if she meant to—시우안 said, “Well, don’t stop pulling oar with the shore in reach. Bring him on in.” She disappeared inside while 민 and 리안 were still guiding 로가인 to the door. He went easily, but when they ceased to urge him he took only one step before stopping.

The common room looked like none 민 had ever seen before. The wide fireplaces were cold, of course, and had gaps where stones had fallen out; the plaster ceiling looked rotten, with holes in it as big as her head where the lathing showed. Mismatched tables of every size and shape stood about on an age-roughened floor that several girls were sweeping. Women with ageless faces sat examining parchments, giving orders to 감시자s, a few of whom wore their color-shifting cloaks, or to other women, some of whom had to be 허락받은 자 or 수련생s. Others were too old for that, perhaps half of them graying and clearly showing their years, and there were men who were not 감시자s, too, most either darting off as though carrying messages or else fetching parchments or cups of wine to the 에스 세다이. The bustle had a satisfying air of something being done. Auras and images danced around the room, wreathing heads, so many that she had to try to ignore them before they overwhelmed her. It was not easy, but it was a trick she had had to learn when around more than a handful of 에스 세다이 at once.

Four 에스 세다이 glided forward to meet the newcomers, all grace and cool serenity in their divided skirts. For 민, seeing their familiar features was like reaching home after being lost.

셰리암’s tilted green eyes fixed immediately on 민’s face. Rays of silver and blue flashed about her fiery hair, and a soft golden light; 민 could not say what it meant. Slightly plump in her dark blue silk, at the moment she was sternness itself. “I would be happier to see you, child, if I knew how you discovered our presence here, and if I had some inkling of why you conceived the crackbrained idea of bringing him.” Half a dozen 감시자s had drifted near, hands resting on swords, eyes sharp on 로가인; he did not seem to see them at all.

민 gaped. Why were they asking *her*? “*My* crackbr—?” She had no chance to say more.

“It would be far better,” pale-cheeked Carlinya cut in icily, “if he had died as the rumors say.” It was not the ice of anger, but of cold reason. She was 백색 아자. Her ivory-colored dress looked as if it had had hard wear. For an instant 민 saw an image of a raven floating beside her dark hair; more a drawing of the bird than the bird itself. She thought it was a tattoo, but she did not know its meaning. She concentrated on faces, tried not to see anything else. “He looks nearly dead in any event,” Carlinya continued, hardly taking breath. “Whatever you thought, you have wasted your effort. But I, too, would like to know how you came to Salidar.”

시우안 and 리안 stood there exchanging smugly amused glances, while the onslaught went on. No one even *looked* at them.

미렐, darkly beautiful in green silk embroidered on the bodice with slanting lines of gold, her face a perfect oval, usually wore a knowing smile that at times could rival 리안’s new tricks. She was not smiling now as she jumped in right behind the White sister. “Speak up, 민. Don’t stand there gaping like a dolt.” She was noted for her fiery temper, even among the Greens.

“You must tell us,” Anaiya added in a more kindly voice. Exasperation tinged it, though. A blunt-featured woman, and motherly despite 에스 세다이 smoothness to her face, at the moment stroking her pale gray skirts, she looked like a mother who was trying not to reach for a switch. “We will find a place for you and these other two girls, but you must tell us how you came here.”

민 shook herself, and closed her mouth. Of course. These other two girls. She had grown so used to them as they were that she no longer thought of how much they had changed. She doubted whether any of these women had seen either since they were hauled off to the dungeons beneath the 백색 탑. 리안 looked ready to laugh, and 시우안 all but shook her head in disgust at the 에스 세다이.

“I am not the one you want to talk to,” 민 told 셰리암. *Let “these other two girls” have those stares on them for a change.* “Ask 시우안, or 리안.” They stared at her as if she were mad, until she nodded to her two companions.

Four sets of 에스 세다이 eyes shifted to the others, but there was no instant recognition. They studied and frowned and passed glances between them. None of the 감시자s took their eyes from 로가인 or their hands from their swords.

“Stilling might produce this effect,” 미렐 murmured finally. “I have read accounts that imply as much.”

“The faces are close, in many ways,” 셰리암 said slowly. “Someone could have found women who look much like them, but why?”

시우안 and 리안 did not look smug any longer. “We are who we are,” 리안 said crisply. “Question us. No impostor could know what we know.”

시우안 did not wait for questions. “My face may be changed, yet at least I know what I am doing and why. That is more than I can say for you, I’ll wager.”

민 groaned at her steely tone, but 미렐 nodded, saying, “That is 시우안 산체’s voice. It is she.”

“목소리s can be trained,” Carlinya said, still coolly calm.

“But how far can memories be taught?” Anaiya frowned sternly. “시우안—if that is who you are—on your twenty-second nameday we had an argument, you and I. Where did it occur, and what was the outcome?”

시우안 smiled confidently at the motherly woman. “During your lecture to the 허락받은 자 on why so many of the nations carved out of 아투르 호크윙’s empire after his death failed to survive. I still disagree with you on some points, by the way. The outcome was that I spent two months working three hours a day in the kitchens. ‘In the hope that the heat will overpower and diminish your ardor,’ I think you said.”

If she had thought that one answer would be sufficient, she was wrong. Anaiya had more questions, for both women, and so did Carlinya and 셰리암, who apparently had been 수련생s and 허락받은 자 with the pair. They were all about the sort of thing no impostor would be able to learn, scrapes gotten into, pranks successful and not, opinions generally held of various 에스 세다이 teachers. 민 could not believe that the women who would become the 아미를린 석좌 and the 연대기 수호자 could have dropped themselves into the soup so often, but she had the impression that this was only the tip of a buried mountain, and it appeared that 셰리암 herself might not have been far behind them. 미렐, the youngest by years, confined herself to amused comments, until 시우안 said something about a trout put into Saroiya Sedai’s bath and a 수련생 taught to mind her ways for half a year. Not that 시우안 had much room to talk of anyone minding her ways. Washing a disliked 허락받은 자’s shifts with itchweed when she was a 수련생? Sneaking out of the Tower to go fishing? Even 허락받은 자 needed permission to leave the Tower grounds except during certain hours. 시우안 and 리안 together had even chilled a bucket of water to near freezing and set it so it would douse an 에스 세다이 who had had them switched, unfairly as they saw it. From the glint in Anaiya’s eyes, it was a good thing for them that they had not been found out that time. From what 민 knew of 수련생 training, and 허락받은 자 for that matter, these women were lucky that they had been allowed to remain long enough to become 에스 세다이, much less that they still had whole hides.

“I am satisfied,” the motherly woman said at last, glancing at the others.

미렐 nodded after 셰리암 did, but Carlinya said, “There is still the question of what to do with her.” She stared right at 시우안, unblinking, and the others suddenly seemed uneasy. 미렐 pursed her lips, and Anaiya studied the floor. Smoothing her dress, 셰리암 seemed to avoid looking at the newcomers at all.

“We still know everything we knew before,” 리안 told them, her sudden frown at least half-worry. “We can be of use.”

시우안 was dark-faced—리안 had seemed amused if anything at her recounted girlhood misdeeds and penalties, but 시우안 had not liked the telling one bit—yet in contrast to her near-glare, her voice was only a little tight. “You wanted to know how we found you. I made contact with one of my agents who also works for the Blue, and she told me of Sallie Daera.”

민 did not understand that about Sallie Daera at all—who was she?—but 셰리암 and the others nodded at one another. 시우안 had done something other than tell them how, 민 realized; she had let them know that she still had access to the eyes-and-ears who had served her as Amyrlin.

“You sit over there, 민,” 셰리암 told 민, pointing to the one table not in use, in a corner. “Or are you still Elmindreda? And keep 로가인 with you.” She and the other three gathered 시우안 and 리안, herding them toward the back of the common room. Two more women in riding dresses joined them before they vanished through a new-made door of uncured boards.

Sighing, 민 took 로가인’s arm and led him to the table, sat him down on a rough bench and took a shaky ladder-back chair herself. Two of the 감시자s positioned themselves nearby, leaning against the wall. They did not appear to be watching 로가인, but 민 knew the Gaidin; they saw everything, and they could have their swords out in less than a heartbeat while sleeping.

So there were to be no open arms in welcome, even with 시우안 and 리안 recognized. Well, what did she expect? 시우안 and 리안 had been the two most powerful women in the 백색 탑; now they were not even 에스 세다이. The others very likely did not know how to behave toward them. And appearing with a gentled false Dragon. 시우안 had better not be lying or wishing about having a plan for him. 민 did not think 셰리암 and the others would be as patient as 로가인 had been.

And 셰리암, at least, had recognized her. She stood again, long enough to peer through a crack-paned window into the street. Their horses were still at the hitching posts, but one of those 감시자s who were not watching would have her before she had Wildrose’s reins untied. This last time in the Tower, 시우안 had gone to great lengths to disguise her. To no end, it seemed. She did not think any of them knew about her viewings, though. 시우안 and 리안 had held that tightly to themselves. 민 would be just as glad if it remained that way. If these 에스 세다이 learned of it, they would entangle her just as 시우안 had, and she would never reach 랜드. She was not going to be able to show off what she had learned from 리안 if they kept her on a leash here.

Helping 시우안 find this gathering, helping bring 에스 세다이 to 랜드’s aid, was all very well and important, but she still had a personal goal. Making a man who had never looked at her twice fall in love with her before he went mad. Maybe she was as mad as he was fated to be. “Then we’ll make a matched pair,” she muttered to herself.

A freckled, green-eyed girl who had to be a 수련생 stopped at her table. “Would you like something to eat or drink? There is venison stew, and wild pears. There might be some cheese, too.” She put so much effort into not looking at 로가인 that she might as well have stared pop-eyed.

“Pears and cheese sound very good,” 민 told her. The last two days had been hungry; 시우안 had managed to catch some fish in a stream, but 로가인 had done all the hunting when they had not eaten at an inn or a farm. Dried beans did not make a meal, in her opinion. “And some wine, if you have it. But first, I would like some information. Where are we, if it isn’t a secret here, too? This village is called Salidar?”

“In 알타라. The Eldar is about a mile to the west. 아마디시아 is on the other side.” The girl put on a poor imitation of 에스 세다이 mystery. “Where better to hide 에스 세다이 than where they would never be looked for?”

“We should not have to hide,” a dark, curly-haired young woman snapped, stopping. 민 recognized her, an 허락받은 자 named Faolain; she would have expected her to be in the Tower still. Faolain had never liked anyone or anything as far as 민 knew, and had often spoken of choosing the 적색 아자 when she was raised. A perfect follower for 엘라이더. “Why did you come here? With *him*! Why did *she* come?” There was no doubt in 민’s mind who she meant. “It is her fault we have to hide. I did not believe she helped 마즈림 타임 escape, but if she appears here with *him,* maybe she did.”

“That will be enough, Faolain,” a slender woman with black hair spilling down her back to her waist told the round-faced 허락받은 자. 민 thought she knew the woman in the dark golden silk riding dress. Edesina. A Yellow, she believed. “Go about your duties,” Edesina said. “And if you mean to bring food, Tabiya, do it.” Edesina did not watch Faolain’s sullen curtsy—the 수련생 gave a better and scurried away—but put a hand on 로가인’s head instead. Eyes on the table, he did not seem to notice.

To 민’s eyes, a silvery collar suddenly appeared, snug around the woman’s neck, and as suddenly seemed to shatter. 민 shivered. She did not like viewings connected to the 쇼엔찬. At least Edesina would escape somehow. Even if 민 had been willing to expose herself, there was no point in warning the woman; it would not change anything.

“It is the gentling,” the 에스 세다이 said after a moment. “He has given up on wanting to live, I suppose. There is nothing I can do for him. Not that I am sure I should if I could.” The look she gave 민 before leaving was far from friendly.
An elegant, statuesque woman in russet silk paused a few feet away, coolly examining 민 and 로가인 with expressionless eyes. Kiruna was a Green, and regal in her manner; she was a sister of the King of 아라펠, so 민 had heard, but she had been friendly to 민 in the Tower. 민 smiled, but those large dark eyes swept over her without recognition, and Kiruna glided out of the inn, four 감시자s, disparate men but all with that deadly-seeming way of moving, suddenly heeling her.

Waiting for her food, 민 hoped that 시우안 and 리안 were finding a warmer reception.
