CHAPTER 50

![](images/00387.jpg)

*To Teach, and Learn*

Some four hours later, the sweat running down 니나브’s face had very little to do with unseasonable heat, and she was wondering whether it might not have been better if Neres had gulled them. Or refused to carry them beyond Boannda. Late-afternoon sunlight slanted sharply through windows with mostly cracked panes. Clutching her skirts in blended irritation and unease, she tried to avoid looking at the six 에스 세다이 grouped around one of the sturdy tables near the wall. Their mouths moved silently as they conferred behind a screen of *세다르.* 엘레인 had her chin high, her hands folded calmly at her waist, but a tightness about her eyes and the corners of her mouth spoiled her regal air. 니나브 was not sure she wanted to know what the 에스 세다이 were saying; one stunning blow after another had knocked all her high expectations into a daze. One more shock and she thought she might scream, and she did not know whether from fury or pure hysteria.

Very nearly everything except their clothes was laid out on that table, from 비르기테’s silver arrow in front of stout Morvrin to the three *ter’angreal* before 셰리암, to the gilded coffers in front of dark-eyed 미렐. Not one of the women looked pleased. Carlinya’s face might have been carved from snow, even motherly Anaiya wore a stern mask, and 베오닌’s look of constant wide-eyed startlement had a distinctly annoyed cast. Annoyed and something more. Sometimes 베오닌 made as if to touch the white cloth spread neatly over the *cuendillar* seal, but her hand always stopped and retreated.
니나브’s eyes jerked away from the cloth. She knew exactly when things had begun to go wrong. The 감시자s who surrounded them in the woods had been proper, if cool—once she made Uno and the 시엔나르ans put up their swords, anyway. And 민’s warm greetings had been all laughter and hugs. But the 에스 세다이 and others in the streets, caught up in their own errands, had scurried along with hardly a glance for the party being escorted in. Salidar was quite crowded, with armed men drilling in nearly every open space. The first person aside from the 감시자s and 민 to pay any attention to them at all had been the lean Brown sister they were taken to, in what had once been the common room of this inn. She and 엘레인 had told the story they had agreed on to Phaedrine Sedai, or tried to. Five minutes into it, they were left standing, with strict orders not to move a foot or speak a word, even to each other. Ten more minutes, staring at one another in confusion, while all around them 허락받은 자 and white-clad 수련생s, 감시자s and servants and soldiers bustled between tables where 에스 세다이 pored over papers and briskly handed out orders, and then they had been hustled before 셰리암 and the others so quickly 니나브 did not think her shoes had touched the floor twice. That was when the grilling had begun, more suitable for captured prisoners than returning heroes. 니나브 dabbed at the perspiration on her face, but as soon as she tucked the handkerchief back up her sleeve, her hands returned to their grip on her skirts.

She and 엘레인 were not alone standing on the colorful silk carpet. 시우안, in a plain dress of fine blue wool, might have been there by choice if 니나브 had not known better, her face cool, utterly composed. She seemed lost in untroubled thought. 리안 at least watched the 에스 세다이, yet she appeared equally confident. In fact, somehow more self-confident than 니나브 remembered. The copper-skinned woman looked even more willowy, too, more supple in some fashion. Perhaps it was her scandalous dress. That pale green silk was every bit as high-necked as 시우안’s, but it clung to every curve of her, and the material only managed to be opaque by a thin hair. It was their faces that truly stunned 니나브, though. She had never expected to find either alive, and certainly never looking so very young—no more than a few years older than she if that. They did not so much as glance at one another. In truth, she thought she detected a distinct chill between them.

There was another difference about them, one that 니나브 was just beginning to recognize. If everyone including 민 had been ginger about it, no one made any real secret of the fact that they had been stilled. 니나브 could feel that lack. Perhaps it was being in a room where all the other women could channel, or perhaps it was knowing they had been stilled, but for the first time she was truly conscious of the ability in 엘레인 and the others. And its absence from 시우안 and 리안. Something had been taken from them, cut away. It was like a wound. Perhaps the worst wound a woman could suffer.

Curiosity overcame her. What sort of wound would it be? What had been cut away? She might as well make use of the waiting, and the irritation that larded itself through her nervousness. She reached out to *세다르.* . . .

“Did anyone grant you permission to channel here, 허락받은 자?” 셰리암 asked, and 니나브 gave a start, hurriedly releasing the True Source.

The green-eyed 에스 세다이 led the others back to their mismatched chairs, arranged on the carpet in a semicircle that had the four standing women as its focus. Some of them carried things from the table. They sat staring at 니나브, earlier emotion swallowed in 에스 세다이 calm. None of those ageless faces acknowledged the heat by so much as a single bead of moisture. Finally Anaiya said in a gently chiding voice, “You have been very long from us, child. Whatever you have learned in the interval, you have apparently forgotten much.”

Blushing, 니나브 curtsied. “Forgive me, 에스 세다이. I did not mean to overstep.” She hoped they thought it was shame that heated her cheeks. She *had* been away from them a long time. Just one day ago, *she* had given the orders and people jumped when she spoke. Now she was the one expected to jump. It galled.

“You tell an interesting . . . story.” Carlinya obviously believed little of it. The White sister turned 비르기테’s silver arrow over in long slender hands. “And you acquired some strange possessions.”

“The Panarch Amathera gave us many gifts, 에스 세다이,” 엘레인 said. “She seemed to think we saved her throne.” Even delivered in a perfectly level voice, that speech was a walk on thin ice. 니나브 was not the only one irritated by their fall from freedom. Carlinya’s smooth face tightened.

“You come with disturbing news,” 셰리암 said. “And some disturbing . . . things.” Her slightly tilted eyes wandered to the table, to the silvery *a’dam,* and returned firmly to 엘레인 and 니나브. Since learning what it was, what it was for, most of the 에스 세다이 had treated it like a live red adder. Most had.

“If the thing does what these children claim,” Morvrin said absently, “we need to study it. And if 엘레인 really believes she can make a *ter’angreal.* . . .” The Brown sister shook her head. Her real attention was on the flattened stone ring, all flecked and striped in red and blue and brown, that she held in one hand. The other two *ter’angreal* lay on her broad lap. “You say that this came from Verin Sedai? How is it this was never mentioned to us before?” That was not directed at 니나브 or 엘레인, but at 시우안.

시우안 frowned, but not the fierce frown 니나브 remembered. It held a touch of diffidence, as if she knew she was speaking to her superiors, and so did her voice. That was another change 니나브 could hardly believe. “Verin never told me of it. I would very much like to ask her a few questions.”

“And *I* have questions about *this*.” 미렐’s olive face darkened as she unfolded a familiar paper—why had they ever kept that?— and read aloud. “ ‘What the bearer does is done at my order and by my authority. Obey, and keep silent, at my command. 시우안 산체, Watcher of the 봉인, Flame of 타르 발론, The 아미를린 석좌.’ ” She crumpled the paper and its seal in her fist. “Hardly something to be handed out to 허락받은 자.”

“At the time, I did not know who I could trust,” 시우안 said smoothly. The six 에스 세다이 stared at her. “It was within my authority then.” The six 에스 세다이 did not blink. Her voice took on a thread of exasperated pleading. “You cannot call me to account for doing what I had to do when I had a perfect right to do it. When the boat’s sinking, you plug the hole with what you can find.”

“And why did you not tell us?” 셰리암 asked quietly, but with a hint of steel. As 수련생 감독관 she had never raised her voice, though sometimes you wished she would. “Three 허락받은 자—허락받은 자!—sent out of the Tower chasing thirteen full sisters of the 흑색 아자. Do you use babies to plug the hole in your boat, 시우안?”

“We are hardly babies,” 니나브 told her heatedly. “Several of those thirteen are dead, and we thwarted their plans twice. In 티어, we—”

Carlinya cut her off like an icy knife. “You have told us all about 티어, child. And Tanchico. And defeating 모그헤디엔.” Her mouth twisted wryly. She had already said that 니나브 had been a fool to come within a mile of one of the 버림받은 자들, that she was lucky to have escaped with her life. That Carlinya did not know how right she was—they certainly had not told everything—only made 니나브’s stomach clench tighter. “You *are* children, and lucky if we decide not to spank you. Now hold your peace until you are called on to speak.” 니나브 flushed heavily, hoping they took it for embarrassment, and held her peace.

셰리암 had never taken her eyes from 시우안. “Well? Why have you never mentioned sending three children out to hunt lions?”

시우안 drew a deep breath, but folded her hands and ducked her head penitently. “There seemed no point, 에스 세다이, with so much else of importance. I have held nothing back, when there was the faintest reason for telling. Every scrap I knew of the 흑색 아자, I told. I’ve not known where these two were or what they were up to for some time. The important thing is that they are here now, and with those three *ter’angreal.* You must realize what it means to have access to 엘라이더’s study, to her papers, if only in bits. You’d never have known that she knows where you are until it was too late, except for that.”

“We realize that,” Anaiya said, eyeing Morvrin, who was still frowning at the ring. “It is just that perhaps the means of it takes us a little by surprise.”

*“Tel’aran’rhiod,”* 미렐 breathed. “Why, it has become no more than a matter for scholarly discussion in the Tower, almost a legend. And 아일 Dreamwalkers. Who would have imagined that 아일 현명한 이들 could channel, much less this?”

니나브 wished they had been able to keep that secret—like 비르기테’s true identity and a few other things they had managed to hold back—but it was difficult to keep things from slipping out when you were being questioned by women who could bore holes in stone with a look when they wanted. Well, she supposed she should be glad they had managed to hang on to what they had. Once *Tel’aran’rhiod* had been mentioned, and that they had entered it, a mouse would have treed cats before these women stopped asking questions.

리안 took a half-step forward, not looking at 시우안. “The *important* thing is that with these *ter’angreal* you can talk to 에그웨인, and through her to 모이라인. Between them, you can not only keep an eye on 랜드 al’Thor, you should be able to influence him even in 케렌.”

“Where he went from the 아일 황무지,” 시우안 said, “where I predicted he would be.” If her eyes and words were directed at the 에스 세다이, her astringent tone was plainly meant for 리안, who grunted.

“Much good that did. Two 에스 세다이 sent off to the 황무지 chasing ducks.”

Oh, yes, there was very definitely a chill there.

“Enough, children,” Anaiya said, very much as if they really were children and she a mother used to their petty squabbles. She eyed the other 에스 세다이 meaningfully. “It will be a very good thing to be able to talk with 에그웨인.”

“If these work as claimed,” Morvrin said, bouncing the ring on one palm and fingering the other *ter’angreal* on her lap. The woman would not believe the sky was blue without proof.

셰리암 nodded. “Yes. That will be your first duty, 엘레인, 니나브. You will have a chance to teach 에스 세다이, showing us how to use them.”

니나브 curtsied, baring her teeth; they could take it for a smile if they chose. Teach them? Yes, and never get near the ring, or the others, again after. 엘레인’s curtsy was even stiffer, her face a cool mask. Her eyes rolled toward that fool *a’dam* almost longingly.

“The letters-of-rights will be useful,” Carlinya said. With all that 백색 아자 coolness and logic, testiness still showed in the way she clipped her words. “Gareth Bryne always wants more gold than we have, but with those, we may almost be able to satisfy him.”

“Yes,” 셰리암 said. “And we must take most of the coin, too. There are more mouths to feed and more backs to clothe every day, here and elsewhere.”

엘레인 gave a gracious nod, just as if they would not take the money whatever she said, but 니나브 simply waited. Gold and letters-of-rights and even *ter’angreal* were only a part.

“For the rest,” 셰리암 went on, “we are agreed that you left the Tower by command, however erroneous it was, and you cannot be held to account for it. Now that you are safely back with us, you will resume your studies.”

니나브 only breathed out slowly. It was no more than she had expected since the questioning began. Not that she liked it, but for once no one was going to be able to accuse her of having a temper. Not when in all probability it would do no good.

엘레인, though, burst out with a sharp, “But—!” Just that, before 셰리암 cut in just as sharply.

“You will resume your studies. You are both very strong, but you are not 에스 세다이 yet.” Those green eyes held them until she was sure they had taken it, and then she spoke again, her voice milder. Milder, but still firm. “You are returned to us, and if Salidar is not the 백색 탑, you may still consider it so. From what you have told us in the last hour, there is considerably more you have yet to tell.” 니나브’s breath caught, but 셰리암’s eyes slid back to the *a’dam.* “A pity you did not bring the 쇼엔찬 woman with you. That, you really should have done.” For some reason, 엘레인 blushed bright red, and looked angry at the same time. For herself, 니나브 was only relieved it was the 쇼엔찬 the woman meant. “But 허락받은 자 cannot be called to account for not thinking as 에스 세다이,” 셰리암 went on. “시우안 and 리안 will have many questions for you. You will cooperate with them, and answer to the best of your abilities. I trust I do not have to remind you not to take advantage of their present condition. Some 허락받은 자, and even some 수련생s, have thought to lay blame for events, and even take punishments into their own hands.” That mild tone became cold steel. “Those young women are now extremely sorry for themselves. Need I say more?”

니나브 was no more hasty than 엘레인 to let her know she did not, which was to say they both almost stammered in their haste to get it out. 니나브 had not thought of assigning blame—to her thinking, 에스 세다이 were all to blame—but she did not want 셰리암 angry with her. Realizing that fact drove the truth home bitterly; the days of freedom certainly were gone.

“Good. Now you may take the jewels the Panarch gave you, and the arrow—when there is time, you must tell me why she made you a gift like that—and go. One of the other 허락받은 자 will find you places to sleep. Proper dresses may be harder to come by, but they will be found. I expect you to put your . . . adventures . . . behind you, and fit smoothly back into your proper place.” Plain although unspoken was the promise that if they did not fit back in smoothly, they would be smoothed until they did. 셰리암 gave a satisfied nod when she saw they understood.

베오닌 had not said a word since the shield of *세다르* was lowered, but as 니나브 and 엘레인 made their curtsies, the Gray sister rose and strode to the table where their things were laid out. “And what of this?” she demanded in heavy 타라본er accents, whipping aside the white cloth that covered the seal on the 어둠의 존재’s prison. For a change, her large blue-gray eyes looked more angry than startled. “Are there to be no more questions about this? Do you all mean to ignore it?” The black-and-white disc lay there, next to the washleather purse, in a dozen or more pieces, fitted back together as neatly as they could be.

“It was whole when we put it in the purse.” 니나브 paused to work moisture back into her mouth. As much as her eyes had avoided the covering cloth before, they could not leave the seal now. 리안 had smirked when she saw the red dress unwrapped from around its cargo, and said . . . No, she would not run away from it, even in her head! “Why should we have thought to take special care? It’s *cuendillar*!”

“We didn’t look at it,” 엘레인 said breathlessly, “or touch it more than we had to. It felt filthy, evil.” It no longer did. Carlinya had made them each hold a piece, demanding to know what evil feeling they were talking about.

They had said the same things before, more than once, and no one paid them any heed now.

셰리암 rose and went to stand beside the honey-haired Gray. “We are ignoring nothing, 베오닌. Asking these girls more questions will do no good. They have told us what they know.”

“More questions are always good,” Morvrin said, but she had stopped fiddling with the *ter’angreal* to stare at the broken seal as hard as anyone else. It might be *cuendillar*— she and 베오닌 had each tested it and said it was—yet she had broken one fragment with her hands.

“How many of the seven still hold?” 미렐 asked softly, as if speaking to herself. “How long until the 어둠의 존재 breaks free, and the Last Battle comes?” Every 에스 세다이 did some of almost everything, according to her talents and inclinations, yet each 아자 had its own reason for being. Greens—who called themselves the Battle 아자—held themselves ready to face new Dreadlords in the Last Battle. There was almost a hint of eagerness in 미렐’s voice.

“Three,” Anaiya said unsteadily. “Three still hold. If we know everything. Let us pray that we do. Let us pray three are enough.”

“Let us pray those three are stronger than this one,” Morvrin muttered. “*퀜딜라* cannot be broken so, not and *be cuendillar.* It cannot.”

“We will discuss this in due course,” 셰리암 said. “After more immediate matters that we can do something about.” Taking the cloth from 베오닌, she covered the broken seal once more. “시우안, 리안, we have reached a decision concerning—” She stopped short as she turned and saw 엘레인 and 니나브. “Were you not told to go?” For all her outward calm, the turmoil inside showed in her forgetting their presence.

니나브 was more than ready to drop another curtsy, blurt a hurried “By your leave, 에스 세다이,” and scurry for the door. Without moving a muscle, the 에스 세다이—and 시우안 and 리안—watched her and 엘레인 go. 니나브 felt their eyes like a shove. 엘레인 stepped not a whit more slowly, for all she cast another look at the *a’dam.*

Once 니나브 had the door closed and could lean back against its unpainted wood, clutching the gilded coffer to her breasts, she took her first comfortable breath, or so it seemed, since entering the old stone inn. She did not want to think about the broken seal. Another broken seal. She would not. Those women could shear sheep with their eyes. She could almost look forward to watching their first meeting with the 현명한 이들; if she was not likely to be squarely in the middle. It had been more than difficult when she first went to the Tower, learning to do as she was told by others, to bend her neck. After long months when she gave the orders—well, once she had consulted 엘레인; usually—she did not know how she was going to learn to pull wool and scratch gravel all over again.

The common room, with its ill-patched plaster ceiling and cold stone fireplaces near collapsing, was the same beehive it had been when she first entered. No one gave her more than a glance now, and she gave them less. A small crowd awaited her and 엘레인.

톰 and Juilin, on a rough bench against the flaking plaster wall, had their heads together with Uno, who was squatting in front of them, long sword hilt rising over his shoulder. Areina and Nicola, both staring amazed at everything and trying not to show it, occupied another bench with Marigan, who was watching 비르기테 attempt to amuse Jaril and Seve by awkwardly juggling three of 톰’s colored wooden balls. Kneeling behind the boys, 민 was tickling them, whispering in their ears, but they only clung to each other, silently staring with those too-big eyes.

Only two others in the entire room were not scurrying about. Two of 미렐’s three 감시자s happened to be leaning against the wall in conversation a few paces beyond the benches, just this side of the door back to the kitchen corridor. Croi Makin, a yellow-haired young splinter of stone from 안도르 with a fine profile, and Avar Hachami, hawk-nosed and square-chinned with a thick gray-streaked mustache like down-curved horns. No one would call Hachami handsome even before his dark-eyed stare made them swallow. They were not looking at Uno or 톰 or anyone else, of course. It was only happenstance that they alone had nothing to do and had chosen just that spot to do it. Of course.

비르기테 dropped one of the balls when she saw 니나브 and 엘레인. “What did you tell them?” she asked quietly, barely glancing at the silver arrow in 엘레인’s hand. The quiver hung at her belt; but her bow was propped against the wall.

Moving closer, 니나브 carefully did not look toward Makin and Hachami. Just as carefully she lowered her voice and was sparing with emphasis. “We told them everything they asked for.”

엘레인 touched 비르기테’s arm. “They know you are a good friend who has helped us. You are welcome to stay here, just the same as Areina and Nicola and Marigan.”

Only when some of 비르기테’s tension melted did 니나브 realize how much had been there. The blue-eyed woman scooped up the fallen yellow ball and smoothly tossed all three back to 톰, who snagged them with one hand and made them vanish in a single motion. She wore the faintest of relieved grins.

“I can’t tell you how glad I am to see the pair of you,” 민 said for at least the fourth or fifth time. Her hair was longer than it had been, though still a dark cap around her head, and she looked different in some other way that 니나브 could not put a finger on. Surprisingly, freshly embroidered flowers climbed the lapels of her coat; she had always worn quite plain clothes before. “A friendly face is rare around here.” Her eyes flickered just a fraction toward the two 감시자s. “We have to settle down alone and have a long talk. I can’t wait to hear what you’ve been up to since you left 타르 발론.” Or to tell what she had been up to as well, else 니나브 missed her guess.

“I would like very much to talk to you, too,” 엘레인 said, quite seriously. 민 looked at her, then sighed and nodded, not as eager as a moment before.

톰 and Juilin and Uno came up behind 비르기테 and 민, their faces set in that way men took on when they meant to say things they thought a woman might not like to hear. Before they could open their mouths, though, a curly-haired woman in an 허락받은 자’s dress pushed between Juilin and Uno, glowering at them, and planted herself in front of 니나브.

Faolain’s dress, with its seven bands of color at the hem for the 아자s, was not quite as white as it should have been, and her dark face wore a scowl. “I am surprised to see you here, wilder. I thought you had gone running back to your village, and our fine Daughter-Heir to her mother.”

“Are you still souring milk for a hobby, Faolain?” 엘레인 asked.

니나브 kept her face pleasant. Just barely. Twice in the Tower Faolain had been set to teach her something. To put her in her place, was her own opinion. Even when teacher and pupil were both 허락받은 자, the teacher had the status of 에스 세다이 so long as the lesson lasted, and Faolain took full advantage. The curly-haired woman had spent eight years as a 수련생 and five more as 허락받은 자; she was not best pleased that 니나브 had never had to be a 수련생 at all, or that 엘레인 had worn pure white for less than a year. Two lessons from Faolain, and two trips to 셰리암’s study for 니나브, for stubbornness, temper, a list as long as her arm. She made her voice light. “I heard 시우안 and 리안 have been badly treated by someone. I think 셰리암 means to make an example to end it once and for all.” She kept her eyes steady on the other woman’s, and Faolain’s widened in alarm.

“I’ve done nothing since 셰리암—” Faolain’s mouth snapped shut, and her face colored heavily. 민 hid her mouth behind her hand, and Faolain jerked her head around, studying the other women, from 비르기테 to Marigan. She motioned brusquely to Nicola and Areina. “You two will do, I suppose. Come with me. Now. No dawdling.” They rose slowly, Areina staring warily and Nicola with fingers fretting at the waist of her dress.

엘레인 stepped between them and Faolain before 니나브 could, chin high and eyes imperious blue ice. “What do you want with them?”

“I am obeying 셰리암 Sedai’s orders,” Faolain replied. “I myself think they are too old for first testing, but I obey orders. A sister accompanies Lord Bryne’s recruiting parties, testing women even as old as 니나브.” Her sudden smile could have come from a viper. “Shall I inform 셰리암 Sedai that you disapprove, 엘레인? Shall I tell her you won’t let your *retainers* be tested?” 엘레인’s chin came down somewhat during that, but of course she could not simply back down. She needed a diversion.

니나브 touched Faolain’s shoulder. “Have they found many?”

In spite of herself, the woman’s head turned, and when she glanced back, 엘레인 was soothing Areina and Nicola, explaining that they would not be hurt, or forced into anything. 니나브 would not have gone so far. When 에스 세다이 found someone with the spark born in her like 엘레인 or 에그웨인, someone who would channel eventually whether she wanted to or not, they were quite open about bundling her into training whatever her wishes. They seemed more lenient about those who could be trained but would never touch *세다르* without it, and about wilders, those who had survived the one-in-four chance of teaching themselves, usually without knowing what they had done and often blocked in some way, as 니나브 was. Supposedly they could choose to come or stay. 니나브 had chosen to enter the Tower, but she suspected that if she had not, she still would have gone, perhaps even tied hand and foot. 에스 세다이 gave women who had the smallest chance of joining them as much choice as a lamb on a feastday.

“Three,” Faolain said after a moment. “All that effort, and they’ve found three. One a wilder.” She truly did not like wilders. “I do not know why they are so eager to find new 수련생s. The 수련생s we have can’t be raised 허락받은 자 until we regain the Tower. It is all 시우안 산체’s fault, her and 리안.” A muscle in her cheek twitched, as if she realized that remark might be thought to harass the former Amyrlin and Keeper, and she seized Areina and Nicola each by an arm. “Come along. 니나브 gave them her flattest stare and deliberately tugged her braid. 엘레인 had her chin as high as it had ever been, her blue eyes haughty enough to chip ice. 톰 and the others surely knew the signs by now; their nonsense was not going to be allowed. “If you think you are still following 랜드 al’Thor’s orders to look after us—” 엘레인 began in frosty tones at the same time that 니나브 said heatedly, “You promised to do as you were told, and I mean to see—”

엘레인 stared, at a loss for words, and 니나브 was having difficulty finding them herself. How far they had fallen. Not so much as a shifted foot in the three of them. The trouble was that she was torn. The unpainted door opened, and 시우안 stalked out, followed by 리안. Gareth Bryne, dented breastplate buckled over his plain buff-colored coat and steel-backed gauntlets tucked behind his sword belt, radiated command. Mostly gray hair and a bluff face gave him the appearance of a man who had seen everything, endured everything; a man who could endure anything.

톰’s bushy white eyebrows drew down almost as far as Uno’s had, but he never took his eyes from Bryne. “I might play a game or two,” he said finally, “once I know the stakes. As long as you understand I don’t intend to spend the rest of my life playing stones with you. I don’t like staying too long in one place anymore. My feet itch, sometimes.”

니나브 did not understand that last exchange at all. And the nerve of those men, thinking they could talk over her head—or under her nose, or whatever—without her understanding every word. Enough of them, anyway.

“A good thing he has no need for a thief-catcher,” Juilin said, eyeing 시우안 sideways, and plainly uncomfortable. 니나브 started to follow as 엘레인 hurried toward that hall to the kitchens—민 would give straight answers—but 시우안 caught her arm in an iron grip.

The 시우안 산체 who had meekly ducked her head before those 에스 세다이 was gone. No one here wore the shawl. Her voice never rose; it did not need to. She fixed Juilin with a stare that had him almost jumping out of his skin. “You watch what questions you ask, thief-catcher, or you’ll gut yourself for market.” Those cold blue eyes shifted to 비르기테 and Marigan. Marigan’s mouth twisted as if she tasted something bad, and even 비르기테 blinked. “You two find an 허락받은 자 named Theodrin and ask her about somewhere to sleep tonight. Those children look as if they should be in bed already. Well? Move your feet!” Before they had stirred a step—and 비르기테 was moving as quickly as Marigan, maybe quicker—she rounded on 니나브. “You, I have questions for. You were told to cooperate, and I suggest you do if you know what’s good for you.”

It was like being caught in a high wind. Before 니나브 knew it, 시우안 was hurrying her up rickety steps with a railing cobbled together from unpainted wood, hustling her down a rough-floored corridor to a tiny room with two cramped beds built into the wall, one above the other. 시우안 took the only stool, motioning her to sit on the lower bed. 니나브 chose to stand, if only to show she was not going to be pushed. There was not much else in the room. A washstand with a brick propping up one leg held a chipped pitcher and basin. A few dresses hung from pegs, and what appeared to be a pallet lay rolled up in one corner. 니나브 had fallen far in the space of a day, but 시우안 had fallen farther than she could imagine. She did not think she would have too much trouble with the woman. Even if 시우안 did still have the same eyes.

시우안 sniffed. “Suit yourself, then, girl. The ring. It doesn’t require channeling?”

“No. You heard me tell 셰리암—”

“Anyone can use it? A woman who can’t channel? A man?”

니나브 raised one eyebrow. This might be a lever to get what she wanted. If not, she had another. Maybe. “Do they know about this? All the talk was of showing them how it works. You were never mentioned.”

“They don’t know.” 시우안 did not appear shaken at all. She even smiled, and not pleasantly. “And they won’t. Else they’ll learn you and 엘레인 have been posing as full sisters since you left 타르 발론. 모이라인 might be letting 에그웨인 get away with it—if she hasn’t tried it, too, I don’t know a bar knot from a running hitch—but 셰리암, Carlinya . . . ? They’ll have you squealing like a spawning grunter before they’re done. Long before.”

It most certainly was. “Of course not. If I teach you anything, it’s because I want to.” She was not going to let this woman bully her. The last vestige of pity winked out. “*If* I do, I want something in return. To study you and 리안. I want to know if stilling can be Healed.”

Her other lever. Near panic had driven it right out of her head. If it existed. One glance. “What would 셰리암 say if she knew you and 리안 weren’t ready to tear out each other’s hair at all?” 시우안 just looked at her. “They think you’re tamed, don’t they? The more you snap at anybody who can’t snap back, the more they take it for proof when you leap to obey every time an 에스 세다이 coughs. Was a little cringing all it took to make them forget the two of you had worked hand-in-hand for years? Or did you convince them stilling had changed everything about you, not just your face? When they find out you’ve been scheming behind their backs, manipulating them, you’ll howl louder than any grunter. Yet there had been something in that brief look; 니나브 was sure of it. “I want to study you—and 리안—whenever I want. And 로가인.” Perhaps she could learn something there as well. Men were different; it would be like looking at the problem from another angle. Not that she would Heal him even if she discovered how. 랜드’s channeling was necessary. She was not about to loose another man on the world who could wield the Power. “If not, then you can forget about the ring, and *Tel’aran’rhiod*.” What was 시우안 after there? Probably just to revisit something that at least seemed like being 에스 세다이. 니나브 stamped firmly on momentarily rekindled pity. “And if you make any claims about us pretending to be 에스 세다이, then I’ll have no choice but to tell about you and 리안. 엘레인 and I might be uncomfortable until the truth comes out, but it will, and the truth will make you weep as long as Faolain and Emara together.”

Silence stretched. How did the other woman manage to look so cool? 니나브 had always thought it had to do with being 에스 세다이. Her lips felt dry, the only part of her that did. If she was wrong, if 시우안 was willing to put it to the test, she knew who would be weeping.

Finally, 시우안 muttered, “I hope 모이라인 has managed to keep 에그웨인’s backbone more supple than this.” 니나브 did not understand, but she hardly had time to consider it. The next instant, the other woman was leaning forward, hand outstretched. “You keep my secrets, and I will keep yours. Teach me the ring, and you can study stilling and gentling to your heart’s content.”

니나브 barely managed to hold in a relieved sigh as she clasped the offered hand. She had done it. For the first time in what seemed forever, someone had tried to bully her and failed. She almost felt ready to face 모그헤디엔. Almost.

엘레인 caught up with 민 just outside the back door of the inn and fell in beside her. 민 had what looked like two or three white shirts wadded under one arm. The sun sat on the treetops, and in the fading light the stableyard had the soft look of dirt not long turned, with a huge stump that might have belonged to an oak right in the middle. The thatch-roofed stone stable had no doors, allowing a good look at men moving among filled stalls. Surprisingly, 리안 was talking to a large man on the edge of the stable’s shadow. Roughly dressed, he looked a blacksmith, or a brawler. What was surprising was how close 리안 stood, head tilted as she stared up at him. “Don’t ask me what she’s up, to,” 민 said. “Strange people come to see 시우안 or her, and some of the men, she . . . Well, you saw.”

“Laundry,” 민 muttered, shifting the shirts irritably. “I can’t tell you how good it is to see 시우안 the mouse for once. She doesn’t know whether the eagle is going to eat her or make her a pet, but she has the same choice she gives everybody else. None!”

엘레인 quickened her pace to keep up as they crossed the stableyard. Whatever that was about, it gave no opening. “Did you know what 톰 was going to suggest? We are staying.”

“I told them you would. Not a viewing.” 민’s step slowed again as they started between the stable and a crumbling stone wall, down a dim alley of brush stubble and trampled weeds. “I just didn’t think you would give up the chance to study again. You were always eager. 니나브, too, even if she won’t admit it. I wish I’d been wrong. I’d go with you. At least, I . . .” She muttered something furious-sounding under her breath. “Those three you brought with you are trouble, and that *is* a viewing.”

There it was. The crack she needed. But instead of asking what she had intended, she said, “You mean Marigan and Nicola and Areina? How can they be trouble?” Only a fool passed over what 민 saw.

“I don’t know exactly. I only caught glimpses of aura, and just out of the corner of my eye. Never when I was looking right at them, where I might have made something out. There aren’t many who have auras all the time, you know. Trouble. Maybe they’ll carry tales. Were you up to anything you wouldn’t want the 에스 세다이 to know about?”

“Certainly not,” 엘레인 said briskly. 민 looked at her sideways, and she added, “Well, nothing we didn’t have to do. They can’t possibly know about it anyway.” This was not taking her where she wanted to go. Drawing a deep breath, she leaped off the cliff. “민, you had a viewing about 랜드 and me, didn’t you?” She went two steps before she realized the other woman had stopped.

“Yes.” It was a wary word.

“You saw that we were going to fall in love.”

“Not exactly. I saw you’d fall in love with him. I don’t know what he feels for you, only that he’s tied to you some way.”

엘레인’s mouth tightened. That was about what she had expected, but not what she wanted to hear. *“Wish” and “want” trip the feet, but “is” makes the path smoother.* That was what Lini said. You had to deal with what was, not what you wished was. “And you saw there would be someone else. Someone I’d have to . . . share . . . him with.”

“Two,” 민 said hoarsely. “Two others. And . . . And I’m one.”

Mouth already open for the next question, for a moment 엘레인 could only stare. “You?” she got out at last.

민 bristled. “Yes, me! Do you think I can’t fall in love? I didn’t want to, but I did, and that’s that.” She stalked past 엘레인 down the alleyway, and this time 엘레인 was slower to catch up.

It certainly explained a few things. How nervously 민 had always sidestepped talking about it. The embroidery on her lapels. And unless she was imagining it, 민 was wearing rouge, too. *How do I feel about it?* she wondered. She could not sort it out. “Who is the third?” she asked quietly.

“I don’t know,” 민 mumbled. “Only that she has a temper. Not 니나브, thank the Light.” She gave a weak laugh. “I don’t think I could have survived that.” Once more she gave 엘레인 a cautious sidelong look. “What does this mean between you and me? I like you. I never had a sister, but sometimes I feel like you. . . . I want to be your friend, 엘레인, and I won’t stop liking you whatever happens, but I can’t stop loving him.”

“I don’t very much like the idea of having to share a man,” 엘레인 said stiffly. That was certainly an understatement.

“Me, neither. Only . . . 엘레인, it shames me to admit it, but I will take him any way I can get him. Not that either of us has much choice. Light, he’s scrambled my whole life. Just thinking about him scrambles my brains.” 민 sounded as if she did not know whether to laugh or cry.

엘레인 exhaled slowly. Not 민’s fault. Was it better that it was 민 rather than, say, Berelain or somebody else she could not abide? *“Ta’veren,*” she said. “He bends the world around him. We are chips caught in a whirlpool. But I seem to recall you and me and 에그웨인 saying we’d never let a man come between us being friends. We will work it out somehow, 민. And when we find out who the third is . . . Well, we’ll work that out, as well. Somehow.” A *third!* Could *she* be Berelain? *Oh, blood and ashes!*

“Somehow,” 민 said bleakly. “Meanwhile, you and I are caught here in a leg trap. I know there’s another, I know I can’t do anything about it, but I had enough trouble reconciling myself to you, and . . . 케렌인 women aren’t all like 모이라인. I saw a 케렌인 noblewoman in Baerlon once. On the surface, she made 모이라인 look like 리안, but sometimes she said things, hinting. And her auras! I don’t think a man in the whole town was safe alone with her, not unless he was ugly, lame, and better yet, dead.”

엘레인 sniffed, but she managed to make her voice light. “Never you mind about that. We have another sister, you and I, one you’ve never met. 아비엔다 is keeping a close eye on 랜드, and he doesn’t go ten steps without a guard of 아일 창의 처녀들.” A 케렌인 woman? At least she had met Berelain, knew something of her. No. She was not going to fret over it like some brainless girl. A grown woman dealt with the world as it was and made the best of it. Who could it be?

They had come out into an open yard dotted with cold ashes. Huge kettles, most pitted where rust had been scrubbed away, stood against the encircling stone wall, which had been toppled in several places by trees growing up in it. Despite the shadows crossing the yard, two steaming kettles still sat on flames, and three 수련생s, hair sweat-soaked and white skirts tied up, were hard at work on scrub boards stuck into broad washpots full of soapy water.

With a glance at the shirts under 민’s arm, 엘레인 embraced *세다르*. “Let me help you with those.” Channeling to do assigned chores was forbidden—physical labor built character, so they said—but this could not be counted the same. If she swirled the shirts around in the water violently enough, there should be no reason to get their hands wet. “Tell me everything. Are 시우안 and 리안 as changed as they seem? How did you get here? Is 로가인 *really* here? And why are you laundering some man’s shirts? Everything.”

민 laughed, plainly pleased to change the subject. “ ‘Everything’ will take a week. But I’ll try. First, I helped 시우안 and 리안 get out of the dungeon 엘라이더 had stuck them in, and then . . .”

Making appropriate sounds of amazement, 엘레인 channeled Air to lift one of the boiling kettles clear of its flames. She hardly noticed the 수련생s’ incredulous stares; she was used to her own strength now, and it rarely occurred to her that she did things, without thinking, that some full 에스 세다이 could not do at all. Who was the third woman? 아비엔다 had *better* be keeping a close eye on him.

CHAPTER 51

![](images/00370.jpg)

*News Comes to 케렌*

A thin thread of blue smoke rising from the plain, short-stemmed pipe clenched in his teeth, 랜드 rested one hand on the balcony’s stone railing and looked into the garden below. Sharp shadows were lengthening; the sun was a red ball falling through a cloudless sky. Ten days in 케렌, and this seemed the first moment he had stood still when he was not asleep. Selande stood close by his side, pale face tilted up to watch him, not the garden. Her hair was not so elaborately done as that of a woman of higher rank, but it still added half a foot to her height. He tried to ignore her, but it was difficult to ignore a woman who insisted on pressing her firm bosom against your arm. The meeting had gone on long enough for him to want a moment’s break. He had known it for a mistake as soon as Selande followed him out.

“I know a secluded pool,” she said softly, “where this heat might be escaped. A sheltered pool, where nothing would disturb us.” The music of 아스모데안’s harp drifted out through the square arches behind them. Something light, cool sounding.

랜드 puffed a little more vigorously. The heat. Nothing compared to the 황무지, but . . . Autumn should be coming on, yet the afternoon felt like the depths of summer. A rainless summer. Shirt-sleeved men in the garden were spreading water from buckets, doing it late to avoid evaporation, but too much was brown or dying. The weather could not be natural. The burning sun mocked him. 모이라인 agreed, and 아스모데안, but neither knew what to do or how, any more than he did. 사마엘. 사마엘 he could do something about.

“Cool water,” Selande murmured, “and you and I alone.” She snuggled closer, though he did not see how it was possible.

He wondered when the next taunt would come. No dashing off in a temper, whatever 사마엘 did. Once his methodical buildup in 티어 was done, then he would loose the lightning. One crushing stroke to put an end to 사마엘, and add 일리안 to his bag at the same time. With 일리안, 티어 and 케렌, plus an army of 아일 big enough to overwhelm any nation in weeks, he . . .

“Would you not like to swim? I do not swim well myself, but surely you will teach me.”

랜드 sighed. For a moment he wished 아비엔다 was there. No. The last thing he wanted was a bruised Selande running screaming with her clothes half torn off.
Hooding his eyes, he looked down at her and spoke quietly around his pipe. “I can channel.” She blinked, drawing back without moving a muscle. They never understood why he would bring that up; for them it was something to be glossed over, ignored if possible. “They say I’ll go mad. But I’m not mad yet. Not yet.” He chuckled from deep in his chest, then cut it off abruptly, made his face blank. “Teach you to swim? I’ll hold you up in the water with the Power. *Saidin* is tainted, you know. 어둠의 존재’s touch. You won’t feel it, though. All around you, but you’ll not feel a thing.” Another chuckle, with a hint of a wheeze. Her dark eyes were as wide and round as they would go, her smile a sickly rictus. “Later, then. I want to be alone, to think about . . .” He bent as if to kiss her, and with a squeak, she dropped a curtsy so sudden that at first he thought her legs had collapsed.

Backing away, curtsying hurriedly at every other step, she babbled about the honor of serving him, her deepest wish to serve him, all in a voice on the brink of hysteria, until she bumped into one of the square arches. A final, half-bend of her knees, and she darted inside.

With a grimace, he turned back to the railing. Frightening women. She would have made excuses had he asked her to leave him, would have taken a command as only a temporary setback unless it was to stay out of his sight, and even then. . . . Maybe word would spread this time. He had to keep a short rein on his temper; it ran away too easily of late. It was the drought he could do nothing about, the problems that sprang up like weeds wherever he looked. A few moments more alone with his pipe. Who would rule a nation when he could have easier work, such as carrying water uphill in a sieve?

Across the garden, between two of the Royal Palace’s stepped towers, he had a view of 케렌, harshly lit and shadowed, mastering the hills more than flowing over them. His crimson flag with the ancient 에스 세다이 symbol hung limply above one of those two towers, a long copy of the Dragon Banner over the other. That one flew a dozen places in the city, including the tallest of the great unfinished towers, right in front of him. Shouting had done as little as orders there; neither 타이런s nor 케렌인 could believe he really meant that he only wanted one, and 아일 did not care about banners one way or another.

Even now, deep inside the palace, he could hear the murmur of a city jammed to bursting. Refugees from every corner of the land, more afraid to return to their homes than they were to have the 용의 환생 in their midst. Merchants seeping in, selling whatever people could afford to buy and buying whatever people could not afford to keep. Lords and armed men rallying to his banner, or to someone’s. Hunters for the Horn thinking it must be found near him; a dozen Foregaters, or a hundred, were ready to sell it to any of them. 오지어 stonemasons down from 스테딩 Tsofu to see if there was work for their fabled skills. There had even been a hundred or so 백의단, though they had galloped out as soon as it was clear the siege had been lifted. Did Pedron Niall’s ingathering of the 백의단 concern him? 에그웨인 gave him hints of things, but she saw matters from the 백색 탑, wherever she stood. The 에스 세다이 point of view was not his.

At least the wagon trains full of grain were beginning to arrive from 티어 with some regularity. Hungry people could riot. He wished he could have simply left it at being glad they were not so hungry anymore, but there it was. The bandits were fewer. And the civil war had not resumed. Yet. More good news. He had to make certain it stayed that way before he could leave. A hundred things to take care of before he could go after 사마엘. Only Rhuarc and Bael remained of the chiefs he really trusted, those who had marched from Rhuidean with him. But if the four clans who had joined him late could not be trusted on the march to 티어, could he trust them loose in 케렌? Indirian and the others had acknowledged him as *Car’a’carn,* but they knew him as little as he knew them. The message that morning might be a problem. Berelain, First of Mayene, was only a few hundred miles south of the city, on her way to join him with a small army; he had no idea how she had led it across 티어. Oddly, her letter had asked if 페린 was with him. No doubt she feared 랜드 might forget her small country if she did not remind him. It might almost be a pleasure to watch her spar with the 케렌인, the latest in a long line of Firsts who had managed to keep 티어 from swallowing their country by playing the Game of Houses. Perhaps if he put her in charge here . . . He would be taking Meilan and the other 타이런s with him when the time came. If it ever came.

This was no better than what was waiting inside. Tapping the dottle from his pipe, he ground out the tabac’s last sparks under his boot. No need to risk fire to the garden; it would go up like a torch. The drought. The unnatural weather. He realized he was snarling silently. First work on what he knew he could do something about. It took an effort to smooth his face before he went in.

아스모데안, as well dressed as any lord, with falls of lace at his neck, plucked a soothing melody from his harp in one corner, leaning against the dark severe paneling as if lounging at his leisure. The others who were sitting bobbed out of their chairs at 랜드’s appearance, and back down at his sharp gesture. Meilan, Torean and Aracome occupied carved-and-gilded chairs on one side of the deep red and gold carpet, each with a young 타이런 lord at his back, mirroring the 케렌인 on the other side. Dobraine and Maringil had a young lord apiece behind them, too, each with the front of his head shaved and powdered like Dobraine’s. A white-faced Selande stood at Colavaere’s shoulder, and trembled when 랜드 looked at her.

Schooling his face, he strode down the carpet to his own chair. That chair alone was reason to control his features. It was a new gift from Colavaere and the other two, in what they imagined was the 타이런 style. He must like 타이런 gaudiness; he ruled 티어, had sent them here. Carved 용 held it up, all sparkling red and gold with enamel and gilt, and great sunstones for their golden eyes. Two more made the arms, and others climbed the tall back. Countless craftsmen must have gone without sleep since his arrival to make the thing. He felt like a fool sitting on it. 아스모데안’s music had changed; it had a grand sound, now, a triumphal march.

And yet, there was an added wariness in those dark 케렌인 eyes watching him, a wariness reflected in the 타이런s. It had been there before he went outside, too. Perhaps in attempting to curry favor they had made a mistake that was only now dawning on them. They had all tried to ignore who he was, pretend he was simply some young lord who had conquered them, who could be dealt with and manipulated. That chair—that throne—held up in front of them who and what he really was.

“Are the soldiers moving on schedule, Lord Dobraine?” The harp faded away as soon as he opened his mouth, 아스모데안 apparently absorbed in preening it.

The leathery man smiled grimly. “They are, my Lord Dragon.” No more than that. 랜드 had no illusions that Dobraine liked him more than any of the others did, or that he would not try to gain advantage where he could, but Dobraine actually seemed ready to hold to the oath he had sworn. The colorful slashes down the chest of his coat were worn from a breastplate being buckled over them.

Maringil shifted forward on his chair, whip-slender and tall for a 케렌인, white hair almost touching his shoulders. His forehead was not shaved, and his coat, stripes nearly to his knees, bore no visible wear. “We need those men here, my Lord Dragon.” Hawk’s eyes blinked at the gilded throne, focused on 랜드 again. “There are many bandits at large in the land yet.” He shifted again, so he did not have to look at the 타이런s. Meilan and the other two were smiling faintly.

“I have set 아일 to hunting bandits,” 랜드 said. They did have orders to sweep up any brigands in their path. And to not go out of their way to find them. Even 아일 could not do that and move quickly. “I’m told that three days ago, Stone Dogs killed nearly two hundred near Morelle.” That was near the southernmost line claimed by 케렌 in recent years, halfway to the River Iralell. No need to let this lot know that those 아일 might be as far as the river by now. They could cover long distances faster than horses.

Maringil persisted, frowning uneasily. “There is another reason. Half of our land west of the Alguenya is in the hands of 안도르.” He hesitated. They all knew 랜드 had grown up in 안도르; a dozen rumors made him a son of one 안도르an House or another, even a son of 모르가세 herself, either cast off because he could channel or fled before he could be gentled. The slender man went on as if tiptoeing barefoot and blindfolded among daggers. “모르가세 does not seem to be reaching for more as yet, but what she has already must be taken back. Her heralds have even proclaimed her right to the—” He stopped abruptly. None of them knew who 랜드 meant the Sun Throne for. Maybe it was 모르가세.

Colavaere’s dark gaze had 랜드 on balance scales again; she had said little today. She would not until she learned why Selande’s face was so white.

Suddenly 랜드 was tired, of nobles balking, of all the manueyering in *Daes Dae’mar*. “안도르an claims to 케렌 will be taken care of when I am ready. Those soldiers will go to 티어. You will follow the High Lord Meilan’s good example of obedience, and I’ll hear no more on it.” He swung toward the 타이런s. “Your example is a good one, Meilan, isn’t it? And yours, Aracome? If I ride out tomorrow, I won’t find a thousand Defenders of the Stone camped ten miles south who were supposed to be on their way back to 티어 two days ago, will I? Or two thousand armsmen from 타이런 Houses?”

Those faint smiles faded with each word. Meilan became very still, dark eyes glittering, and Aracome’s narrow face went pale, whether from anger or fear it was hard to say. Torean dabbed at his lumpy face with a silk handkerchief pulled from his sleeve. 랜드 ruled in 티어, and meant to rule; *칼란도르* driven into the Heart of the Stone proved that. That was why they had not protested against his sending 타이런 soldiers to 케렌. They thought to carve new estates, perhaps kingdoms, here, far from where he ruled.

“You will not, my Lord Dragon,” Meilan said finally. “Tomorrow I will ride with you so you may see for yourself.”

랜드 did not doubt it. A rider would be dispatched south as soon as the man could arrange it, and by tomorrow those soldiers would be far on toward 티어. It would do. For now. “I am done, then. You may leave me.”

A few starts of surprise, masked so quickly they might have been imagined, and they were rising, bowing and curtsying, Selande and the young lords backing away. They had expected more. An audience with the 용의 환생 was always long, and tortuous as they saw it, with him firmly bending them the way he meant them to go, whether it was declaring that no 타이런 could claim lands in 케렌 without marrying into a 케렌인 House, or refusing to allow the expulsion of Foregaters, or making laws apply to nobles that had never applied to any but commoners before.

His eyes followed Selande for a moment. She was not the first in the last ten days. Nor the tenth, or even the twentieth. He had been tempted, at least at first. When he rejected slender, plump promptly replaced her, as tall or dark, for 케렌인 anyway, replaced short or fair. A constant search for the woman who would please him. The Maidens turned back those who tried to sneak into his quarters at night, firmly but more gently than 아비엔다 had handled the one she caught. 아비엔다 apparently took 엘레인’s ownership of him with little short of deadly seriousness. Yet her 아일 sense of humor seemed to find tormenting him very satisfying; he had seen the satisfaction on her face when he groaned and hid his face as she started undressing for the night. Thus he could have resented her deadly seriousness if he had not quickly understood what was behind that string of pretty young women.

“My Lady Colavaere.”

She stopped as soon as he spoke her name, cool-eyed and calm beneath her ornate tower of dark curls. Selande had no choice but to remain with her, though she was plainly as reluctant to stay as the others were to go. Meilan and Maringil bowed themselves out last, so intent on Colavaere and trying to puzzle out why she had been called to stay that they did not realize they were side by side. Their eyes were a perfect match, dark and predatory.

The dark-paneled door closed. “Selande is very pretty young woman,” 랜드 said. “But some prefer the company of a more mature . . . more knowledgeable . . . woman. You will sup alone with me tonight, when Second Even is rung. I look forward to the pleasure.” He waved her away before she could say anything, if she could have. Her face did not change, but her curtsy was a trifle unsteady. Selande looked purely amazed. And infinitely relieved.

Once the door had closed again, behind the two women, 랜드 threw back his head and laughed. A harsh, sardonic laugh. He was tired of the Game of Houses, so he played it without thinking. He was disgusted with himself for frightening one woman, so he frightened another. It was reason enough to laugh. Colavaere stood behind that line of young women who had been flinging themselves at him. Find a bedpartner for the Lord Dragon, a young woman whose strings she pulled, and Colavaere would have a string tied firmly to 랜드. But it was some other woman she meant to bed, and perhaps even marry, the 용의 환생. Now she would sweat all the hours until Second Even. She had to know she was pretty, if short of beautiful, and if he rebuffed all the young women she sent, perhaps it was because he wanted one with another fifteen or so years. And she would be certain she did not dare say no to the man who held 케렌 in his fist. By tonight, she should be amenable, should stop this idiocy. 아비엔다 would very likely slit the throat of any woman she found in his bed; besides, he had no time for all these easily frightened doves thinking to sacrifice themselves for 케렌 and Colavaere, There were too many problems to deal with, and no time.

*Light, what if Colavaere decides it’s worth the sacrifice?* She might. She was easily cold-blooded enough. *Then I’ll have to see that it’s cold with fear.* It would not be difficult. He could sense *세이딘* like something just beyond the edge of sight. He could feel the taint on it. Sometimes he thought that what he felt was the taint in him, now, the dregs left by *세이딘*.

He found that he was glaring at 아스모데안. The man seemed to be studying him, face expressionless. The music resumed again, like water babbling over stones, soothing. So he needed soothing, did he?

The door opened without a knock, admitting 모이라인, 에그웨인 and 아비엔다 together, the younger women’s 아일 garb framing the 에스 세다이’s pale blue. For anyone else, even Rhuarc or another chief still near the city or yet another delegation of 현명한 이들, a Maiden would have entered to announce them. These three the Maidens sent on in even if he was taking a bath. 에그웨인 glanced at “Natael” and grimaced, and the tune became lower, and for a moment intricate, perhaps a dance, before settling to what might have been the sighing of breezes. The man wore a twisted smile, directed at his harp.

“I’m surprised to see you, 에그웨인,” 랜드 said. He swung his leg over the arm of the chair. “What is it—six days you’ve been avoiding me? Have you brought me more good news? Has Masema sacked Amador in my name? Or have these 에스 세다이 you say support me turned out to be 흑색 아자? You notice I don’t ask *who* they are, or where. Not even how you know. I don’t ask you to divulge 에스 세다이 secrets, or 현명한 이들’ secrets, or whatever they are. Just give me the driblets you’re willing to dole out, and let me worry whether what you don’t care to tell me will stab me in the night.”

She looked at him calmly. “You know what you need to know. And I will not tell you what you do not need to know.” That was what she had said six days ago. She was as much 에스 세다이 as 모이라인, for all one wore 아일 garb and the other pale blue silk.

There was nothing calm about 아비엔다. She moved to stand shoulder-to-shoulder with 에그웨인, green eyes flashing, back so straight it might have been iron. He was half surprised 모이라인 did not join them, so they could all three glare at him. Her vow of obedience left a startling amount of room, it seemed, and the three seemed to have become close since his argument with 에그웨인. Not that it had been much of an argument; you could not argue very well with a woman who watched with cool eyes, never raised her voice, and after one refusal to answer declined even to acknowledge your question again.

“What do you want?” he said.

“These came for you in the last hour,” 모이라인 said, extending two folded letters. Her voice seemed to fit 아스모데안’s chime-like tune.

랜드 rose to take them suspiciously. “If they’re for me, how did they come into your hands?” One was addressed to “랜드 al’Thor” in an exact, angular hand, the other to “The Lord 용의 환생” in script flowing yet no less precise. The seals were unbroken. A second look made him blink. The two seals seemed to be the same red wax, and one bore the impression of the Flame of 타르 발론, the other a tower overlaid on what he recognized as the island of 타르 발론.

“Perhaps because of where they came from,” 모이라인 replied, “and from whom.” It was no explanation, but it was as much as he would get unless he demanded more. Even then he would have to prod her through every step. She kept her vow, but in her own way. “There are no poison needles in the seals. And no traps woven.”

He paused with his thumb against the Flame of 타르 발론—he had not thought of either—then broke it. Another Flame in red wax stood beside the signature, 엘라이더 do Avriny a’Roihan in a hasty scrawl above her titles. The rest was in the angular hand.

> *There can be no denial that you are the one prophesied, yet many will try to destroy you for what else you are. For the sake of the world, this cannot be allowed. Two nations have bent knee to you, and the savage 아일 as well, but the power of thrones is as dust beside the 하나의 힘. The 백색 탑 will shelter and protect you against those who refuse to see what must be. The 백색 탑 will see that you live to see Tarmon Gai’don. None else can do this. An escort of 에스 세다이 will come to bring you to 타르 발론 with the honor and respect you deserve. This I pledge to you.*

“She doesn’t even ask,” he said wryly. He remembered 엘라이더 well for having met her only once. A woman hard enough to make 모이라인 seem a kitten. The “honor and respect” he deserved. He would wager that the escort of 에스 세다이 just happened to number thirteen.

Passing 엘라이더’s letter back to 모이라인, he opened the other. The page was covered in the same hand that had addressed it.

> *With respect, I humbly beg to make myself known to the great Lord 용의 환생, whom the Light blesses as savior of the world.*

> *All the world must stand in awe of you, who has conquered 케렌 in one day as you did 티어. Yet be wary, I beseech you, for your splendor will inspire jealousy even in those not toiled in the Shadow. Even here in the 백색 탑 are the blind who cannot see your true radiance, which will illumine us all. Yet know that some rejoice in your coming, and will delight to serve your glory. We are not those who would steal your luster for ourselves, but rather those who would kneel to bask in your brilliance. You shall save the world, according to the Prophecies, and the world shall be yours.*

> *To my shame, I must beg you to let no one see these words, and to destroy them when once read. I stand, naked of your protection, among some who would usurp your power, and I cannot know who around you is as faithful as I. I am told that 모이라인 Damodred may be with you. She may serve you devotedly, obeying your words as law, as I will, yet I cannot know, for I remember her as a secretive woman, much given to plotting, as 케렌인 are. Yet even if you believe she is your creature, as I, I beg you to keep this missive secret, even from her. My life lies beneath your fingers, my Lord 용의 환생, and I am your servant.*

> *Alviarin Freidhen*

He read it through again, blinking, then handed it to 모이라인. She barely scanned the page before giving it to 에그웨인, who had her head over the other letter with 아비엔다. Perhaps 모이라인 already knew what they contained?

“A good thing you gave your oath,” he said. “The way you used to be, keeping everything back, I might have been ready to suspect you by now. A good thing you’re more open now.” She did not react. “What do you make of it?”

“She must have heard about your swelled head,” 에그웨인 said softly. He did not think he had been meant to hear. Shaking her head, she said more loudly, “This doesn’t sound like Alviarin at all.”

“It is her hand,” 모이라인 said. “What do *you* make of it, 랜드?”

“I think there’s a rift in the Tower, whether 엘라이더 knows it or not. I assume an 에스 세다이 can’t write a lie more easily than she can speak one?” He did not wait for her nod. “If Alviarin had been less flowery, I might have thought they were working together to pull me in. I can’t see 엘라이더 even thinking half of what Alviarin wrote, and I can’t see her having a Keeper who could write it, not if she knew.”

“You are not going to do this thing,” 아비엔다 said, 엘라이더’s letter crumpled in her hand. It was not a question.

“I am not a fool.”

“Sometimes you are not,” she said grudgingly, and made it worse by raising a questioning eyebrow to 에그웨인, who considered for a moment, then shrugged.

“Do you see anything else?” 모이라인 asked.

“I see 백색 탑 spies,” he told her dryly. “They know I hold the city.” For at least two or three days after the battle, the Shaido would have stopped anything but a pigeon going north. Even a rider who knew where to change horses, no sure thing between 케렌 and 타르 발론, could not have reached the Tower in time for these letters to come back today.

모이라인 smiled. “You learn quickly. You will do well.” For a moment she almost looked fond. “What will you do about it?”

“Nothing, except make sure that 엘라이더’s ‘escort’ doesn’t get within a mile of me.” Thirteen of the weakest 에스 세다이 could overwhelm him linked, and he did not think 엘라이더 would send her weakest. “That, and be aware that the Tower knows what I do the day after I do it. Nothing more until I know more. Could Alviarin be one of your mysterious friends, 에그웨인?”

She hesitated, and he suddenly wondered whether she had told 모이라인 any more than she had him. Was it 에스 세다이 secrets she kept, or 현명한 이들’? At last she said simply, “I do not know.”

A rap came at the door, and Somara put her flaxen head into the room. “매트림 카우톤 has come, *Car’a’carn*. He says that you sent for him.”

Four hours ago, as soon as he had learned 맷 was back in the city. What would the excuse be this time? It was time to be done with excuses. “Stay,” he told the women. 현명한 이들 made 맷 almost as uneasy as 에스 세다이 did; these three would put him off balance. He did not give a second thought to using them. He was going to use 맷, too. “Send him in, Somara.”

맷 strolled into the room grinning, as if it was a common room. His green coat hung open, and his shirt was half unlaced, exposing the silver foxhead dangling on his sweaty chest, but the dark silk scarf was draped around his neck to hide his hanging scar in spite of the heat. “Sorry if I took too long. There were some 케렌인 who thought they knew how to play cards. Doesn’t he know anything livelier?” he asked, jerking his head toward 아스모데안.

“I hear,” 랜드 said, “that every young man who can pick up a sword wants to join the Band of the Red Hand. 탈마네스 and Nalesean are having to turn them away in droves. And Daerid has doubled the number of his footmen.”

맷 paused in lowering himself into the chair Aracome had used. “It’s true. A fine lot of young . . . fellows wanting to be heroes.”

“The Band of the Red Hand,” 모이라인 murmured. “*Shen an Calhar.* A legendary group of heroes indeed, though the men in it must have changed many times in a war that lasted well over three hundred years. It is said they were the last to fall to the 트롤록s, guarding Aemon himself, when Manetheren died. Legend says a spring rose where they fell, to mark their passing, but I rather think the spring was already there.”

“I wouldn’t know about that.” 맷 touched the foxhead medallion, and his voice picked up strength. “Some fool got the name from somewhere, and they all started using it.”

모이라인 glanced at the medallion dismissively. The small blue stone hanging on the forehead seemed to catch the light and glow, though the angles were wrong. “You are very brave, it seems, 맷.” It was flatly said, and the silence that followed stiffened his face. “Very brave,” she said finally, “to lead *Shen an Calhar* across the Alguenya and south against the 안도르ans. Even braver than that, for there are rumors that you went alone to scout the way, and 탈마네스 and Nalesean had to ride hard to catch up to you.” 에그웨인 sniffed loudly in the background. “Hardly wise for a young lord leading his men.”

맷’s lip curled. “I’m no lord. I’ve more respect for myself than that.”

“But very brave,” 모이라인 said as if he had not spoken. “안도르an supply wagons burned, outposts destroyed. And three battles. Three battles, and three victories. With small loss to your own men, though outnumbered.” As she fingered a rip in the shoulder of his coat, he sank back as far the chair would allow. “Are you drawn to the thick of battles, or are they drawn to you? I am almost surprised you came back. To hear the stories, you might have driven the 안도르ans back across the Erinin had you stayed.”

“Do you think this is funny?” 맷 snarled. “If you have something to say, say it.
