“You can hardly teach me when you’re teaching 셰리암 and the others.” The silk paled; the neck was high again, surrounded by a white lace ruff, and a cap of pearls fitted close on 시우안’s hair. “Or would you rather I came after them? You claim you need *some* sleep undisturbed.”

니나브 quivered, fists clenched at her sides. 셰리암 and the others were not the worst thing stoking her anger. She and 엘레인 took turns bringing them to *Tel’aran’rhiod* two at a time, sometimes all six in one night, and even if she was the teacher they never let her forget she was 허락받은 자 and they 에스 세다이. One sharp word when they made a foolish mistake . . . 엘레인 had only been sent to scrub pots once, but 니나브’s hands were shriveled from hot, soapy water; back where her body lay sleeping they were, anyway. But they were not the worst. Nor was the fact that she barely had a moment to spare for investigating what, if anything, could be done about stilling and gentling. 로가인 was more cooperative than 시우안 and 리안 in any case, or at least more eager. Thank the Light he understood about keeping it secret. Or thought he did; he probably believed she would Heal him eventually. No, worse than that was that Faolain had been tested and raised . . . not 에스 세다이—not without the 맹세 막대, which was tight in the Tower—but to something more than 허락받은 자. Faolain wore any dress she chose now, and if she could not wear the shawl or choose an 아자, she had been given other authority. 니나브 thought she had fetched more cups of water, more books—left deliberately, she was sure!—more pins and inkjars and other useless things in the last four days than she had her entire stay in the Tower. Yet even Faolain was not the worst of all. She did not even want to remember that. Her anger could have heated a house in winter.

“What’s put a hook in your gills today, girl?” 시우안 had on a gown like those 리안 wore, only more sheer than even 리안 would ever wear in public, so thin it was hard to tell what color it was. Not the first time she had had that on today, either. What was perking around in the back of the woman’s mind? In the World of Dreams, things like these changes of clothing betrayed thoughts you might not even know you had. “You have been almost decent company until today,” 시우안 continued irritably, then paused. “Until today. I see it now. Yesterday afternoon 셰리암 assigned Theodrin to begin helping you break down that block you’ve built up. Is that what has your shift in a twist? You don’t like Theodrin telling you what to do? She’s a wilder, too, girl. If anyone can help you learn to channel without eating nettles first, she—”

“And what has you so jittery you can’t hold your dress still?” Theodrin—that was what really hurt. The failure. “Maybe it’s something I heard last night?” Theodrin was even-tempered, good-humored, patient; she said it could not be done in one session; her own block had taken months to demolish, and she had finally realized she was channeling long before going to the Tower. Still, failure hurt, and worst of all, if anyone ever discovered that she had cried like a baby in Theodrin’s comforting arms when she knew she was failing . . . “I heard you heaved Gareth Bryne’s boots at his head when he told you to sit down and polish them properly—he still doesn’t know 민 does the polishing, does he?—so he turned you upside down and—”

시우안’s full-armed slap rung her ears. For an instant she could only stare at the other woman, eyes going wider and wider. With a wordless shriek, she tried to punch 시우안 in the eye. Tried, because somehow 시우안 had tangled a fist in her hair. A moment later they were down in the dirt of the street, rolling about and screaming, flailing wildly.

Grunting, 니나브 thought she was getting the better of it even if she did not know whether she was on the top or the bottom half the time. 시우안 was trying to yank her braid out by the roots with one hand while the other pounded at her ribs or anything else it could find, but she had the other woman the same way, and 시우안’s yanking and punching were definitely growing weaker, and she herself was going to pound 시우안 senseless in another minute, then snatch her bald. 니나브 yelped as a toe caught her hard on the shin. The woman kicked! 니나브 tried to knee her, but it was not easy in skirts. Kicking was not fighting fair!

Suddenly 니나브 realized that 시우안 was shaking. At first she thought the woman was crying. Then she realized it was laughter. Pushing herself up, she brushed strands of hair out of her face—her braid was all but undone—and glared down at the other woman. “What are you laughing at? Me? If you are . . . !”

“Not at you. At us.” Still quivering with mirth, 시우안 shoved 니나브 off her. 시우안’s hair was in wild disarray, and dust covered the plain wool dress she wore now, worn-looking and neatly darned in several places. She was barefoot, too. “Two grown women, rolling around like . . . I haven’t done that since I was . . . twelve, I think. I started thinking that all we needed would be fat Cian snatching me up by an ear to tell me girls don’t fight. I heard she once knocked down a drunken printer; I don’t know why.” Something very like giggles took her for a moment, then she quieted them and stood, brushing dust from her clothes. “If we have a disagreement, we can settle it like adult women.” And in a careful tone, “Still, it might be a good idea not to discuss Gareth Bryne.” She gave a start as the worn dress became a gown, red with black-and-gold embroidery around hem and swooping neckline.

니나브 sat there staring at her. What would she have done as Wisdom if she found two women rolling around in the dirt that way? If anything, the answer kept her anger at a simmer. 시우안 still did not seem to realize that there was no need to brush away dust with your hands in *Tel’aran’rhiod.* Snatching away fingers that had been repairing her braid, 니나브 got up quickly; before she was on her feet again, her braid hung perfect over her shoulder and her good 두 강 woolens might have just been laundered.

“I agree,” she said. She would have made any two women she caught like that sorry they had been born even before she hauled them before the Women’s Circle. What was she doing lashing out with her fists like some fool man? First Cerandin—she did not want to think about that episode, but there it was—then Latelle, and now this. Was she going to get around her block by being angry all the time? Unfortunately—or perhaps fortunately—that thought did nothing for her temper. “If we have disagreements, we can . . . discuss them.”

“Which I suppose means we’ll shout at one another,” 시우안 said dryly. “Well, better that than the other.”

“We would not have to shout if you—!” Drawing a deep breath, 니나브 jerked her eyes away; this was no way to begin anew. That breath caught in her throat, and she turned her head back to 시우안 so quickly it seemed she had been shaking it. She hoped it did. Just for an instant, there had been a face in a window across the street. And there was a flutter in her belly, a bubble of fear, a burn of anger at being afraid. “I think we should go back now,” she said quietly.

“Go back! You said that vile concoction would put me to sleep for a good two hours, and we haven’t been here much more than half that.”

“Time works differently here.” Had it been 모그헤디엔? The face had vanished so quickly it could have been someone dreaming herself here for an instant. If it was 모그헤디엔, they must not—must not on any account—let her know she had been seen. They had to get away. Bubble of fear, burn of anger. “I told you. A day in *Tel’aran’rhiod* can be an hour in the waking world, or the other way round. We—”

“I’ve dipped better out of the bilge in a bucket, girl. You needn’t think you can get away with shortchanging me. You’ll teach me everything you teach the others, as agreed. We can go when I wake up.”

There was no time. If it had been 모그헤디엔. 시우안’s dress was green silk now, and the Amyrlin’s stole and her Great Serpent ring were back, but for a wonder the neckline was almost as low as anything she had worn before. The ring *ter’angreal* hung above her breasts, somehow part of a necklace of square emeralds.

니나브 moved without thinking. Her hand lashed out, snatched the necklace so hard it tore free from 시우안’s neck. 시우안’s eyes widened, but as soon as the clasp broke, she vanished, and necklace and ring melted from 니나브’s hand. For an instant she stared at her empty fingers. What happened to someone sent out of *Tel’aran’rhiod* like that? Had she sent 시우안 back to her sleeping body? Or to somewhere else? To nowhere?

Panic seized her. She was just standing there. Quick as thought she fled, the World of Dreams seeming to change around her.

She stood on a dirt street in a small village of wooden houses, none more than a single story. The White Lion of 안도르 waved from a tall staff, and a single stone dock stuck out into a broad river where a flock of long-billed birds flapped south low over the water. It all looked vaguely familiar, but it took her a moment to know where she was. Jurene. In 케렌. And that river was the Erinin. It had been here that she and 에그웨인 and 엘레인 had boarded the *Darter,* as badly misnamed as the *Riverserpent,* to continue their journey to 티어. That time seemed like something read in a book long ago.

Why had she jumped to Jurene? That was simple, and answered as soon as she thought of it. Jurene was the one place she knew well enough to leap to in *Tel’aran’rhiod* that she could be sure 모그헤디엔 did not know. They had been there for an hour, before 모그헤디엔 knew she existed, and she was sure neither she nor 엘레인 had ever mentioned it again, in *Tel’aran’rhiod* or awake.

But that left another question. The same one, in a way. Why Jurene? Why not step out of the Dream, wake up in her own bed, such as it was, if washing dishes and scrubbing floors on top of everything had not left her so weary she slept right on? *I can still step out.* 모그헤디엔 had seen her in Salidar, if that had been 모그헤디엔. 모그헤디엔 knew Salidar now. *I can tell 셰리암.* How? Admit she was teaching 시우안? She was not supposed to have her hands on those *ter’angreal* except with 셰리암 and the other 에스 세다이. How 시우안 got hold of them when she wanted, 니나브 did not know. No, she was not afraid of more hours up to her elbows in hot water. She was afraid of 모그헤디엔. Anger burned in her belly fiercely. She wished she had some goosemint out of her scrip of herbs. *I am so . . . so* bloody *tired of being afraid.*

There was a bench in front of one of the houses, overlooking dock and river. She sat down and considered her situation from every angle. It was ridiculous. The True Source was a pale thing. She channeled a flame dancing in air above her hand. *She* might look solid—to herself, anyway—but she could see the river through that scrap of fire. She tied it off, and it faded away like mist as soon as the knot was done. How could she face 모그헤디엔 when the weakest 수련생 in Salidar could match or better her strength? That was why she had fled here instead of leaving *Tel’aran’rhiod.* Afraid and angry at being afraid, too angry to think straight, to consider her own weakness.

She would step out of the Dream. Whatever 시우안’s scheme had been, it was done; she would have to take her chances right along with 니나브. The thought of more hours scrubbing floors tightened her hand on her braid. Days more likely, and maybe 셰리암’s switch besides. They might never let her near one of the dream *ter’angreal* again, or any *ter’angreal.* They would set Faolain over her instead of Theodrin. A finish to studying 시우안 and 리안, much less 로가인; maybe a finish to studying 치유.

In a fury she channeled another flame. If it was a whit stronger, she could not see it. So much for trying to crank her anger in hope it would help. “There’s nothing for it but to just tell them I saw 모그헤디엔,” she muttered, yanking her braid hard enough to hurt. “Light, they *will* give me to Faolain. I’d almost rather die!”

“But you seem to enjoy running little errands for her.”

That mocking voice pulled 니나브 up off the bench like hands on her shoulders. 모그헤디엔 stood in the street all in black, shaking her head at what she saw. With all her strength 니나브 wove a shield of Spirit and hurled it between the other woman and *세다르.* Tried to hurl it between; it was like chopping at a tree with a paper hatchet. 모그헤디엔 actually smiled before she bothered to slice 니나브’s weave, and that as casually as brushing a biteme away from her face. 니나브 stared at her as though poleaxed. After everything it came down to this. The 하나의 힘, useless. All the anger bubbling inside her, useless. All her plans, her hopes, useless. 모그헤디엔 did not bother to strike back. She did not even bother to channel a shield of her own. That was how much contempt she had.

“I was afraid you had seen me. I grew careless when you and 시우안 started trying to kill each other. With your hands.” 모그헤디엔 gave a belittling laugh. She was weaving something, lazily because there was no reason to hurry. Nyaneve did not know what it was, yet she wanted to scream. Fury seethed inside her, but fear dulled her wits, rooted her feet to the ground. “Sometimes I think you are all too ignorant even to train, you and the former *아미를린 석좌* and all the rest. But I cannot allow you to betray me.” That weave was reaching out for her. “It is time to collect you at last, it seems.”

“Hold, 모그헤디엔!” 비르기테 shouted.

니나브’s mouth dropped open. It *was* 비르기테, as she had been, in her short white coat and wide yellow trousers, intricate golden braid pulled over her shoulder, silver arrow drawn on silver bow. It was impossible. 비르기테 was no longer part of *Tel’aran’rhiod,* she was back in Salidar, making sure no one discovered 니나브 and 시우안 asleep with the sun up and began asking questions.

모그헤디엔 was so shocked, the flows she had woven vanished. Shock lasted less than a moment, though. The gleaming arrow flew from 비르기테’s bow—and evaporated. The bow evaporated. Something seemed to seize the archer, jerking her arms straight up, pulling her clear of the ground. Almost immediately she was snubbed short, pulled tight between wrists and ankles a foot above the ground.

“I should have considered the possibility of you.” 모그헤디엔 turned her back on 니나브 to move closer to 비르기테. “Do you enjoy your flesh? Without 가이달 케인?”

니나브 thought of channeling. But what? A dagger that might not even penetrate the woman’s skin? Fire that would not singe her skirts? 모그헤디엔 knew how useless she was; she was not even looking at her. If she stopped the flow of Spirit to the sleeping woman in amber, she would wake in Salidar, she could give warning. Her face twisted near to tears as she looked at 비르기테. The golden-haired woman hung there, staring defiantly at 모그헤디엔. 모그헤디엔 contemplated her in return as a woodcarver would a block of wood.

*There’s only me,* 니나브 thought. *I might as well not be able to channel at all. There’s only me.*

Lifting that first foot was like pulling it out of knee-deep mud, the second staggering step no easier. Toward 모그헤디엔. “Don’t hurt me,” 니나브 cried. “Please. Don’t hurt me.” A chill ran through her. 비르기테 was gone. A child of perhaps three or four, in short white coat and wide yellow trousers, stood there playing with a toy-sized silver bow. Flipping her golden braid back, the child aimed the bow at 니나브 and giggled, then stuck a finger in her mouth as though unsure whether she had done something wrong. 니나브 sagged to her knees. It was hard work crawling in skirts, but she did not think she could have remained standing. Somehow she managed, reaching out a pleading hand and whimpering. “Please. Don’t hurt me. Please. Don’t hurt me.” Over and over as she dragged toward the 버림받은 자들, a broken beetle scrabbling in the dirt.

모그헤디엔 watched silently, until at last she said, “Once I thought you were stronger than this. Now I find I truly like the sight of you on your knees. That is close enough, girl. Not that I think you have courage enough to try tearing *my* hair out. . . .” She seemed amused by the notion.

니나브’s hand wavered a span from 모그헤디엔. It had to be close enough. There was only her. And *Tel’aran’rhiod.* The image formed in her head, and there it was, silver bracelet on her outstretched wrist, silver leash linking it to the silver collar around 모그헤디엔’s neck. It was not just the *a’dam* she fixed in her head, but 모그헤디엔 wearing it, 모그헤디엔 and the *a’dam,* a part of *Tel’aran’rhiod* that she held in the form she wanted. She knew something of what to expect; she had worn an *a’dam*’s bracelet briefly once, in Falme. In a strange way she was aware of 모그헤디엔 in the same way she was aware of her own body, her own emotions, two sets, each distinct, but each in her own head. One thing she had only hoped, because 엘레인 insisted it was so. The thing was indeed a link; she could feel the Source *through* the other woman.

모그헤디엔’s hand leaped to the collar, shock rounding her eyes. Rage and horror. Rage more than horror, at first. 니나브 felt them almost as if they were her own. 모그헤디엔 had to know what the leash-and-collar was, yet she tried to channel anyway; at the same time 니나브 felt a slight shifting in herself, in the *a’dam,* as the other woman tried to bend *Tel’aran’rhiod* to herself. Suppressing 모그헤디엔’s attempt was simple; the *a’dam* was a link, with her in control. Knowing that made it easy. 니나브 did not want to channel those flows, so they were not channeled. 모그헤디엔 might as well have tried to pick up a mountain with her bare hands. Horror overwhelmed rage.

Getting to her feet, 니나브 fastened the proper image in her mind. She did not just imagine 모그헤디엔 leashed in the *a’dam,* she *knew* 모그헤디엔 was leashed, as firmly as she knew her own name. The sense of shifting, of her skin trying to crawl, did not go away, though. “Stop that,” she said sharply. The *a’dam* did not move, but it seemed to tremble unseen. She thought of blackwasp nettles lightly brushing the other woman from shoulders to knees. 모그헤디엔 shuddered, exhaled convulsively. “Stop it, I said, or I’ll do worse.” The shifting ceased. 모그헤디엔 watched her warily, still clutching the silver collar around her neck and with an air of being poised on her toes for flight.

비르기테—the child who was, or had been, 비르기테—stood eyeing them curiously. 니나브 formed the image of her as a grown woman, concentrated. The little girl put her finger back in her mouth and began studying the toy bow. 니나브 breathed angrily. It was hard changing what someone else was already maintaining. And on top of that, 모그헤디엔 had claimed she could make changes permanent. But what she could do, she could undo. “Restore her.”

“If you release me, I—”

니나브 thought of nettles again, and not a light brush this time. 모그헤디엔 sucked air through clenched teeth, shook like a bedsheet in a high wind.

“That,” 비르기테 said, “was the most frightening thing that has ever happened to me.” Herself once more, she wore the short coat and wide trousers, but she had no bow or quiver. “I *was* a child, but at the same time, what was me—really me—was just some fancy floating in the back of that child’s mind. And I knew it. I knew I was just going to watch what happened and play. . . .” Flipping her golden braid back over her shoulder, she gave 모그헤디엔 a hard look.

“How did you get here?” 니나브 asked. “I am grateful, you understand, but . . . how?”

비르기테 gave 모그헤디엔 a final stony stare, then opened her coat to fish in the neck of her blouse, pulling up the twisted stone ring on a leather thong. “시우안 woke up. Just for a moment, and not all the way. Long enough to grumble about you snatching this from her. When you didn’t wake right behind her, I knew something must be wrong, so I took the ring and the last of what you mixed for 시우안.”

“There was hardly any left. Only the dregs.”

“Enough to put me to sleep. It tastes horrible, by the way. After that, it was as easy as finding feather-dancers in Shiota. In some ways this is almost as if I were still—” 비르기테 cut off with another glare for 모그헤디엔. The silver bow reappeared in her hand, and a quiver of silver arrows at her hip, yet after one moment they vanished again. “Past is past, and the future is ahead,” she said firmly. “I was not truly surprised to realize there were two of you who knew they were in *Tel’aran’rhiod.* I knew the other must be her, and when I arrived and saw the pair of you . . . It seemed as if she had already captured you, but I hoped that if I distracted her, you might come up with something.”

니나브 felt a stab of shame. She had considered abandoning 비르기테. That was what she had almost come up with. The thought had only been there for a moment, rejected as soon as it came, but it had come. What a coward she was. Surely 비르기테 never even had moments when fear almost took control of her. “I . . .” A faint taste of boiled catfern and powdered mavinsleaf. “I almost ran away,” she said faintly. “I was so frightened my tongue stuck to the roof of my mouth. I almost ran away and left you.”

“Oh?” 니나브 writhed inside as 비르기테 considered her. “But you did not, did you? I should have loosed before I called out, but I’ve never felt comfortable shooting anyone from behind. Even her. Still, it all worked out. But what do we do with her now?”

모그헤디엔 certainly seemed to have overcome her fear. Ignoring the silver collar around her throat, she watched 니나브 and 비르기테 as though they were the prisoners, not she, and she was deliberating what to do with them. Except for an occasional twitch of her hands, as if she wanted to scratch where her skin held the memory of nettles, she appeared black-clad serenity. Only the *a’dam* let 니나브 know there was fear in the woman, almost a gibbering, but pushed down to a muted buzz. She wished the thing let her know what 모그헤디엔 was thinking as well as feeling. Then again, she was just as glad not to be inside the mind behind those cold dark eyes.

“Before you consider anything . . . drastic,” 모그헤디엔 said, “remember that I know much that would be useful to you. I have observed the other Chosen, peeked into their schemes. Is that not worth something?”

“Tell me, and I will consider whether it’s worth anything,” 니나브 said. What could she do with the woman?

“란피어, 그랜달, 라빈 and 사마엘 are plotting together.”

니나브 gave the leash a short tug, staggering her. “I know that. Tell me something new.” The woman was captive here, but the *a’dam* only existed so long as they were in *Tel’aran’rhiod.*

“Do you know they are drawing 랜드 al’Thor to attack 사마엘? But when he does, he will find the others as well, waiting to trap him between them. At least, he will find 그랜달 and 라빈. I think 란피어 plays another game, one the others know nothing about.”

니나브 exchanged worried glances with 비르기테. 랜드 must learn of this. He would, as soon as she and 엘레인 could speak to 에그웨인 tonight. If they could manage to put their hands on the *ter’angreal* long enough.

“That is,” 모그헤디엔 murmured, “if he lives long enough to find them.”
니나브 took hold of the silvery leash where it joined the collar and pulled the 버림받은 자들’s face close to hers. Dark eyes met her gaze flatly, but she could feel anger through the *a’dam,* and fear wriggling up and being stamped down. “You listen to me. Do you think I don’t know why you are pretending to be so cooperative? You think if you keep talking long enough, I will make some slip, and you can escape. You think the longer we talk, the harder I’ll find it to kill you.” That much was true enough. To kill somebody in cold blood, even one of the 버림받은 자들, would be hard, maybe harder than she could manage. What was she going to do with the woman? “But you understand this. I won’t allow hinting at things. If you try keeping anything back from me, I will do to you everything you ever thought of doing to me.” Dread, creeping through the leash, like bone-chilling shrieks deep in 모그헤디엔’s mind. Maybe she did not know as much about *a’dam* as 니나브 thought. Maybe she believed 니나브 could read her thoughts if she tried. “Now if you know of some threat to 랜드, something ahead of 사마엘 and the others, you tell me. Now!”

Words spilled from 모그헤디엔’s mouth, and her tongue flickered out to wet her lips continually. “Al’Thor means to go after 라빈. Today. This morning. Because he thinks 라빈 killed 모르가세. I don’t know whether he did or not, but al’Thor believes it. But 라빈 never trusted 란피어. He never trusted any of them. Why should he? He thought it all might be some trap set for him, so he has laid a trap of his own. He has set Wards through Caemlyn so if a man channels a spark he will know. Al’Thor will walk right into it. He almost certainly already has. I think he meant to leave 케렌 right after sunrise. I had no part of it. It was none of it my doing. I—”

니나브 wanted to shut her up; the fear sweat glistening on the woman’s face made her sick, but if she had to listen to that pleading voice, too . . . She started to channel, wondering whether she would be strong enough to hold 모그헤디엔’s tongue, then smiled. She was linked to 모그헤디엔, and in control. 모그헤디엔’s eyes bulged as she wove flows to stop her own mouth and tied them. 니나브 added plugs for her ears, too, before turning to 비르기테. “What do you think?”

“엘레인’s heart will break. She loves her mother.”

“I know that!” 니나브 took a breath. “I will cry with her and mean every tear, but right now I must worry about 랜드. I think she was telling the truth. I could almost feel it.” She caught the silver leash just below her bracelet and shook it. “Maybe it’s this, and maybe it was imagination. What do you believe?”

“That it’s the truth. She was never very brave unless she clearly had the upper hand, or thought she could get it. And you certainly put the fear of the Light into her.”

니나브 grimaced. 비르기테’s every word put another bubble of anger in her belly. She was never very brave except when she clearly had the upper hand. That could describe herself. She had put the fear of the Light into 모그헤디엔. She had, and she had meant every word when she said it. Boxing somebody’s ears when they needed it was one thing; threatening torture, wanting to torture, even 모그헤디엔, was something else again. And here she was trying to avoid what she knew she had to do. Never very brave except when she clearly had the upper hand. This time the bubble of anger was seeded by herself. “We have to go to Caemlyn. I do, at least. With her. I may not be able to channel strongly enough to tear paper as I am, but with the *a’dam* I can use her strength.”

“You won’t be able to affect anything in the waking world from *Tel’aran’rhiod,*” 비르기테 said quietly.

“I know! I know, but I have to do something.”

비르기테 threw back her head and laughed. “Oh, 니나브, it is such an embarrassment being associated with such a coward as you.” Abruptly her eyes widened in surprise. “There wasn’t much of your potion left. I think I am wak—” In mid-word, she was simply no longer there.

Taking a deep breath, 니나브 untied the flows around 모그헤디엔. Or made her do it; with the *a’dam* it was hard to tell which, really. She wished 비르기테 was still there. Another pair of eyes. Someone who probably knew *Tel’aran’rhiod* better than she ever could. Someone who was brave. “We are taking a trip, 모그헤디엔, and you are going to help me with every last scrap of you. If anything takes me by surprise . . . Suffice it to say, anything that happens to the one wearing this bracelet happens to the one wearing the collar. Only about tenfold.” The sickly look on 모그헤디엔’s face said she believed. Which was just as well, since it was true.

Another deep breath, and 니나브 began forming the image of the one place in Caemlyn she knew well enough to remember. The Royal Palace, where 엘레인 had taken her. 라빈 must be there. But in the waking world, not the World of Dreams. Still, she had to do something. *Tel’aran’rhiod* changed around her.

CHAPTER 55

*The Threads Burn*

랜드 stopped. A long scorch along the corridor wall marked where half a dozen costly tapestries had gone to ash. Flames licked upward on another; a number of inlaid chests and tables were only charred ruins. Not his work. Thirty paces further on, red-coated men in breastplates and helmets with barred face-guards lay contorted in death on the white floor tiles, useless swords in hands. Not his work either. 라빈 had been wasteful of his own in attempting to reach 랜드. He had been clever in his attacks, clever in his escapes, but from the moment he fled the throne room he had not faced 랜드 for more than the instant it took to strike and flee. 라빈 was strong, perhaps as strong as 랜드, and more knowledgeable, but 랜드 had the fat-little-man *angreal* in his pocket, and 라빈 had none.

The corridor was doubly familiar, once for having seen it before, once for having seen something similar.

*I walked this way with 엘레인 and 가윈 the day I met 모르가세*. The thought slithered painfully along the boundaries of the Void. He was cold in there, without emotion. *Saidin* raged and burned, but he was icy calm.

And another thought, like a stab. *She lay on a floor like this, her golden hair spread as though sleeping. 일레나 Sunhair. My 일레나*.

엘라이더 had been there that day, too. *She Foretold the pain I’d bring. She knew the darkness in me. Some of it. Enough*.

*일레나, I did not know what I was doing. I was mad! I am mad. Oh, 일레나!*

*엘라이더 knew—some—but she did not tell even all of that. Better if she had told*.

*Oh, Light, is there no forgiveness? I did what I did in madness. Is there no mercy?*

*Gareth Bryne would have killed me, had he known. 모르가세 would have ordered my death. 모르가세 would be alive, perhaps. 엘레인’s mother alive. 아비엔다 alive. 맷. 모이라인. How many alive, if I had died?*

*I have earned my torment. I deserve the final death. Oh, 일레나, I deserve death*.

*I deserve death*.

Bootsteps behind him. He turned.

They came out of a broad crossing corridor not twenty paces from him, two dozen men in breastplates and helmets and the white-collared red coats of the Queen’s Guards. Except that 안도르 had no queen now, and these men had not served her while she lived. A 미르드랄 led them, pale eyeless face like something found under a rock, overlapping plates of black armor heightening the illusion of a serpent as it moved, black cloak hanging motionless however it moved. The look of the 눈 없는 자 was fear, but fear was a distant thing in the Void. They hesitated when they saw him; then the 반쪽 인간 raised its black-bladed sword. Men who had not already drawn put hands to hilts.

랜드—he thought that was his name—channeled in a way he could not remember doing before.

Men and 미르드랄 stiffened where they stood. White frost grew thick on them, frost that smoked as 맷’s boots had smoked. The 미르드랄’s upraised arm broke off with a loud crack. When it hit the floor tiles, arm and sword shattered.

랜드 could feel the cold—yes, that was his name; 랜드—cold like a knife as he walked past and turned the way they had come. Cold, yet warmer than *세이딘*.

A man and a woman crouched against the wall, servants liveried in red and white, short of their middle years and holding each other as though for protection. Seeing 랜드—there was more to the name; not just 랜드—the man started to rise from where he had huddled away from the 미르드랄-led band, but the woman hauled him back by his sleeve.

“Go in peace,” 랜드 said, putting out a hand. Al’Thor. Yes, 랜드 al’Thor. “I’ll not hurt you, but you could be hurt if you stay.”

The woman’s brown eyes rolled up in her head. She would have collapsed in a heap if the man had not caught her, and his narrow mouth was working rapidly, as if he was praying but could not get the words out.

랜드 looked where the man was looking. His hand had stretched out of his coatsleeve far enough to bare the Dragon’s golden-maned head that was part of his skin. “I will not hurt you,” he said, and walked on, leaving them there. He had 라빈 to corner yet. 라빈 to kill. And then?

No sound but the click of his boots on the tiles. And deep in his head, a faint voice murmuring mournfully of 일레나 and forgiveness. He strained to feel 라빈 channeling, to feel the man filled with the True Source. Nothing. *Saidin* seared his bones, froze his flesh, scoured his soul, but from without it was not easy to see until you were close. A lion in high grass, 아스모데안 had said once. A rabid lion. Should 아스모데안 count among those who should not have died? Or 란피어? No. Not—

He had only a moment’s warning to throw himself flat, a hair-thin slice of time between feeling flows suddenly woven and an arm-thick bar of white light, liquid fire, slicing through the wall, ripping across like a sword through where his chest had been. Where that bar slashed, on both sides of the hallways, wall and friezes, doors and tapestries ceased to exist. Severed wall hangings and chunks of stone and plaster broken free rained to the floor.

So much for the 버림받은 자들 fearing to use balefire. Who had told him that? 모이라인. She surely had deserved to live.

마화 leaped from his hands, a brilliant white shaft streaking toward where that other bar had originated. The other failed even as his punched through the wall, leaving a purple afterimage fanning across his vision. He released his own flow. Had he done it finally?

Scrambling to his feet, he channeled Air, slamming ruined doors open so hard that the remnants ripped from the hinges. Inside, the room was empty. A sitting room, with chairs arrayed before a great marble fireplace. His balefire had taken a bite out of one of the arches leading to a small courtyard with a fountain, and another from one of the fluted columns along the walk beyond.

라빈 had not gone that way, though, and he had not died in that blast of balefire. A residue hung in the air, a fading remnant of woven *세이딘*. 랜드 recognized it. Different from the gateway he had made to Skim to Caemlyn, or the one to Travel—he knew now that was what he had done—into the throne room. But he had seen one like this in 티어, had made one himself.

He wove another now. A gateway, an opening at least, a hole in reality. It was not blackness on the other side. In fact, if he had not known the way was there, if he could not have seen the weave of it, he might not have known. There before him were the same arches opening onto the same courtyard and fountain, the same columned walk. For an instant the neatly rounded holes his balefire had made in arch and column wavered, filled, then were holes again. Wherever that gateway led, it was to somewhere else, a reflection of the Royal Palace as once it had been a reflection of the Stone of 티어. Vaguely he regretted not talking to 아스모데안 about it while he had the chance, but he had never been able to speak of that day to anyone. It did not matter. On that day he had carried *칼란도르*, but the *angreal* in his pocket had already proved enough to harry 라빈.

Stepping through quickly, he loosed the weave and hurried away across the courtyard as the gateway vanished. 라빈 would have felt that gate if he was close enough and trying. The fat little stone man did not mean he could stand and wait to be attacked.

No sign of life, except for himself and one fly. That was the way it had been in 티어, too. Stand-lamps in the hallways stood unlit, with pale wicks that had never seen a flame, yet even in what should have been the dimmest hall there was light, seemingly coming from everywhere and nowhere. Sometimes those lamps moved, too, and other things as well. Between one glance and the next, a tall lamp might have moved a foot, a vase in a niche an inch. Little things, as if someone had shifted them in the time his eyes were away. Wherever this was, it was a strange place.

It came to him, as he trotted along another colonnade, sensing for 라빈, that he had not heard the voice crying over 일레나 since he channeled balefire. Perhaps he had somehow chased 르웨어스 테린 out of his head.

*Good*. He stopped at the edge of one of the Palace gardens. The roses and whitestar bushes looked as drought-bedraggled as they would have in the real palace. On some of the white spires rising above the rooftops, the White Lion banner rippled, but which spire could change in the blink of an eye. *Good, if I don’t have to share my head with*—

He felt odd. Insubstantial. He raised his arm, and stared. He could see the garden through coatsleeve and arm as through a mist. A mist that was thinning. When he glanced down, he could see the walk’s paving stones through himself.

*No!* It was not his thought. An image began to coalesce. A tall, dark-eyed man with a worry-creased face and more white in his hair than brown. *I am Lews Ther*—

*I am 랜드 al’Thor*, 랜드 broke in. He did not know what was happening, but the faint Dragon was beginning to fade from the misty arm held in front of his face. The arm began to look darker, the fingers on his hand longer. *I am me*. That echoed in the Void. *I am 랜드 al’Thor*.

He fought to picture himself in his own mind, struggled to make the image of what he saw in the mirror every day shaving, what he saw in a stand-mirror dressing. It was a frantic fight. He had never really looked at himself. The two images waxed and waned, the older dark-eyed man and the younger with blue-gray eyes. Slowly the younger image firmed, the older faded. Slowly his arm grew more solid. His arm, with the Dragon twined around it and the heron branded into his palm. There had been times he hated those marks, but now, even enclosed within the emotionless Void, he almost grinned to see them.

Why had 르웨어스 테린 tried to take him over? To make him into 르웨어스 테린. He was sure that was who that dark-eyed man with the suffering face had been. Why now? Because he could in this place, whatever it was? Wait. It had been 르웨어스 테린 who shouted that adamant “no.” Not an attack by 르웨어스 테린. By 라빈, and not using the Power. If the man had been able to do this back in Caemlyn, the real Caemlyn, he would have. It had to be some ability he had gained here. And if 라빈 had gained it, perhaps he had, too. The image of himself had been what held him, brought him back.

He focused on the nearest rosebush, a thing a span high, and imagined it growing thin, foggy. Obediently, it melted away to nothing, but as soon as the picture in his mind was nothing, the rosebush was suddenly back, just as it had been.

랜드 nodded coldly. It had limits, then. There were always limits and rules, and he did not know them here. But he knew the Power, as much as 아스모데안 had taught him and he had taught himself, and *세이딘* was still in him, all the sweetness of life, all the corruption of death. 라빈 had to have seen him to attack. With the Power you had to see something to affect it, or know *exactly* where it was in relation to you down to a hair. Perhaps it was different here, but he did not think so. He almost wished 르웨어스 테린 had not gone silent again. The man might know this place and its rules.

Balconies and windows overlooked the garden, in some places four stories high. 라빈 had tried to . . . unmake him. He drew on the raging torrent of *세이딘* through the *angreal*. Lightnings flashed from the sky, a hundred forking silver bolts, more, stabbing at every window, every balcony. Thunder filled the garden, erupting chunks of stone. The air itself crackled, and the hair on his arms and chest tried to stand under his shirt. Even the hair on his head began to lift. He let the lightnings die. Here and there bits of shattered stone windowframe and balcony broke loose, the crash of their fall muted by the echoes of thunder still ringing in his ears.

Gaping holes peered down now where windows had. They looked like sockets in some monstrous skull, the ruined balconies like a dozen splintered mouths. If 라빈 had been at any of them, he was surely dead. 랜드 would not believe it until he saw the corpse. He wanted to see 라빈 dead.

Wearing a snarl he did not know was there, he stalked back into the palace. He had wanted to see 라빈 die.

니나브 hurled herself flat and scrambled along the hall floor as *something* slashed through the nearest wall. 모그헤디엔 slithered as fast as she, but if the woman had not, she would have hauled her by the *a’dam*. Had that been 랜드, or 라빈? She had seen bars of white fire, liquid light, like that in Tanchico, and she had no wish to be anywhere near one again. 마화 was one weave she did not know and did not want to know. *I want to Heal, burn both of these fool men, not learn a fancy way to kill!*

She levered herself up to a crouch, peered back the way they had come. Nothing. An empty Palace hallway. With a ten-foot long gash through both walls, as neat as any stoneworker could have done, and bits of tapestry lying on the floor. No sign of either man. She had not had a glimpse of either so far. Only their handiwork. Sometimes that handiwork had almost been her. A good thing that she could draw on 모그헤디엔’s anger, filter it out of the terror clawing to escape and let it seep into her. Her own was a pitiful thing that would scarcely have allowed her to sense the True Source, much less channel the flow of Spirit that kept her in *Tel’aran’rhiod*.

모그헤디엔 was hunched over on her knees, dry retching. 니나브’s mouth tightened. The woman had tried to remove the *a’dam* again. Her cooperation had faded quickly when they discovered 랜드 and 라빈 actually here in *Tel’aran’rhiod*. Well, trying to unfasten that collar when it was around your neck was its own punishment. At least 모그헤디엔 did not have anything left in her stomach this time.

“Please.” 모그헤디엔 caught at 니나브’s skirt. “I tell you, we must get away.” Stark panic made her voice painful. 모그헤디엔’s clawing terror mirrored itself on her face. “They are here in the flesh. The flesh!”

“Be quiet,” 니나브 said absently. “Unless you’ve lied to me, that is an advantage. For me.” The other woman claimed that being in the World of Dreams physically limited your control of the Dream. Or rather, she admitted it, after letting a bit of the knowledge slip. She had admitted, too, that 라빈 did not know *Tel’aran’rhiod* as well as she. 니나브 hoped that meant he did not know it as well as *she* did. That he knew more than 랜드, she did not doubt. That wool-headed man! Whatever his reason for coming after 라빈, he should never have let the man lead him here, where he did not know the rules, where thoughts could kill.

“Why will you not understand what I tell you? Even if they had only dreamed themselves here, either would be stronger than we. Here in the flesh, they could crush us without blinking. In the flesh they can draw *세이딘* more deeply than we can draw *세다르* dreaming.”

“We are linked.” Still not paying attention, 니나브 gave her braid a sharp pull. No way to tell which direction they had gone. And no warning of anything until she saw them. Somehow it still seemed unfair that they could channel without her being able to see or feel the flows. A stand-lamp that had been sliced in two was suddenly whole again, then not, just as quickly. That white fire must be incredibly powerful. *Tel’aran’rhiod* usually healed itself rapidly whatever you did to it.

“You brainless fool,” 모그헤디엔 sobbed, shaking 니나브’s skirt with both hands as if wanting to shake 니나브. “It does not matter how brave you are. We are linked, but you contribute nothing the way you are. Not a shred. It is my strength, and your madness. They are here in the flesh, not dreaming! They are using things you have never dreamed of! They will destroy us if we stay!”

“Keep your voice down,” 니나브 snapped. “Do you want to bring one of them down on us?” She looked both ways hurriedly, but the hallway was still empty. Had that been footsteps, boots? 랜드 or 라빈? One had to be approached as carefully as the other. A man in a fight for his life could strike out before he saw they were friends. Well, that she was, anyway.

“We must go,” 모그헤디엔 insisted, but she did lower her voice. She got to her feet, sullen defiance twisting her mouth. Fear and anger writhed inside her, first one stronger, then the other. “Why should I help you any further? This is madness!”

“Would you rather feel the nettles again?”

모그헤디엔 flinched, yet her dark eyes remained stubborn. “You think I will let them kill me rather than be hurt by you? You *are* mad. I will not stir from this spot until you are ready to take us away from here.”

니나브 jerked her braid again. If 모그헤디엔 refused to walk, she would have to drag her. Not a very quick way to search, with what seemed miles of Palace corridors yet to go. She should have been harsher when the woman first tried balking. In 니나브’s place, 모그헤디엔 would have killed without hesitation, or, if she thought the other useful, woven the trick of taking someone’s will, making them worship her. 니나브 had tasted that once, in Tanchico, and even had she known how it was done, she did not think she could do it to somebody else. She despised this woman, hated her with all her being. But even if she had not needed her, she could not have killed her just standing there. The trouble was, she was afraid that 모그헤디엔 knew that, too, now.

Still, a Wisdom headed the Women’s Circle—even if the Circle did not always agree—and the Women’s Circle dealt out punishments to women who broke the law or offended custom too deeply, and to men, too, for some transgressions. She might not have 모그헤디엔’s stomach for killing, for crushing people’s minds, but. . . .

모그헤디엔 opened her mouth, and 니나브 filled it with a gag of Air. Or rather she made 모그헤디엔 do it; with the *a’dam* linking them, it was like channeling herself, but 모그헤디엔 knew it was her own abilities being used like a tool in 니나브’s hand. Dark eyes glittered indignantly as 모그헤디엔’s own flows snared her arms to her sides and pulled her skirts tight around her ankles. For the rest, 니나브 used the *a’dam*, just as with the nettles, creating the sensations she wanted the other woman to feel. Not the reality; the *feel* of reality.

모그헤디엔 stiffened in her bonds as a leather strap seemed to strike her bottom. That was what it would feel like to her. Outrage and humiliation rolled through the leash. And contempt. Compared to her elaborate ways of hurting people, this seemed suitable for a child.

“When you are ready to cooperate again,” 니나브 said, “just nod.” This could not take long. She could not just stand there while 랜드 and 라빈 tried to kill one another. If the wrong one died because she avoided danger by letting 모그헤디엔 keep her there . . .

니나브 remembered a day when she was sixteen, just after she had been judged old enough to put her hair in a braid. She had stolen a plum pudding from Corin Ayellin on a dare from Nela Thane and walked out the kitchen door right into Mistress Ayellin. Adding the aftermath, sending it along the leash in a lump, made 모그헤디엔’s eyes pop.

Grimly, 니나브 did it again. *She won’t stop me short!* Again. *I will help 랜드 whatever she thinks!* Again. *Even if it kills us!* Again. *Oh, Light, she could be right; 랜드 could kill us both before he knows it’s me*. Again. *Light, I hate being afraid!* Again. *I hate her!* Again. *I hate her!* Again.

Abruptly she realized 모그헤디엔 was jerking frantically in her bonds, nodding her head so violently it seemed about to come off. For a moment, 니나브 gaped at the other woman’s tear-streaked face, then stopped what she was doing and hurriedly unraveled the flows of Air. Light, what had she done? She was not 모그헤디엔. “I take it you won’t give me any more trouble?”

“They will kill us,” the other woman mumbled faintly, and nearly unintelligibly through her sobs, but at the same time she nodded a hurried acquiescence.

Deliberately, 니나브 hardened herself. 모그헤디엔 deserved everything she had gotten and much, much more. In the Tower, one of the 버림받은 자들 would have been stilled and executed as soon as the trial could be concluded, and little evidence needed beside who she was. “Good. Now we—”

Thunder shook the entire Palace, or something very much like thunder, except that the walls rattled and dust rose off the floor. 니나브 half fell into 모그헤디엔, and they danced trying to keep their feet. Before the upheaval had faded completely, it was replaced by a roar like some monstrous fire racing up a chimney the size of a mountain. That lasted only a moment. The silence after seemed deeper than before. No. There were boots. A man running. The sound echoed down the hallway. From the north.

니나브 pushed the other woman away. “Come on.”

모그헤디엔 whimpered, but did not resist being pulled down the hall. Her eyes were huge, though, and her breath came too fast. 니나브 thought it was a good thing she had 모그헤디엔 along, and not just for access to the 하나의 힘. After all her years hiding in shadows, the Spider was such a coward she almost made 니나브 feel brave by comparison. Almost. It was only anger at her own fear that made her able to hold on to that one flow of Spirit that kept her in *Tel’aran’rhiod*, now. 모그헤디엔 was stark terror to her bones.

Pulling 모그헤디엔 behind her by the gleaming leash, 니나브 quickened her step. Chasing the fading sound of those other steps.

랜드 stepped into the round courtyard warily. Half of the white-paved circle cut into the structure rising three stories behind him; the other half was bounded by a stone semicircle atop pale columns five paces high, sticking out into yet another garden, shaded gravel walks beneath low spreading trees. Marble benches surrounded a pool with lilypads. And fish, gold and white and red.
Suddenly the benches shifted, flowed, changed into faceless manshapes, still as white and hard-looking as the stone. He had already learned the difficulty of changing something that 라빈 had altered. Lightning danced from his fingertips, shattering stone men to shards.

The air became water. Choking, 랜드 struggled to swim toward the columns; he could see the garden beyond. There must be some kind of barrier to stop all the water pouring out. Before he could channel, gold and red and white shapes were darting around him, larger than the fish in the pool had been. And with teeth. They ripped at him; blood curled up in red mist. Instinctively he flailed at the fish with his hands, but the cold part of him, deep in the Void, channeled. 마화 flared, at the barrier if there was one, at any place 라빈 might be to see this courtyard. The water roiled, throwing him around violently, as it rushed in to fill the empty tunnels carved by balefire. Flickers of gold and white and red darted at him, adding new threads of crimson to the water. Tossed about, he could not see to aim his wild bolts; they flashed in every direction. No breath left. He tried to think of air, or the water being air.

Suddenly it was. He dropped hard to the paving stones among small fish flopping about, rolled over and pushed himself up. It was all air again; even his clothes were dry. The stone ring flickered between standing untouched and lying in ruins with half the columns down. Some of the trees lay tangled atop their own stumps, then stood whole, then were fallen again. The Palace behind him had holes punched in white walls, even one through a high gilded dome above, and gashes slashed across windows, some with pierce-work stone screens. The damage all flickered, vanishing and reappearing. Not the slow, sometime shifts of before, but constant. Damage, then none, then some, then none, then all again.

Wincing, he pressed his hand to his side, to the old, half-healed wound. It stung as if his exertions had nearly torn it open. He stung all over, from a dozen or more bleeding bites. That had not changed. The bloody rips in his coat and breeches were still there. Had he managed to change the water back to air? Or had one of his frenzied bolts of balefire driven 라빈 off, or even killed him? It did not matter, unless it was the last.

Wiping blood out of his eyes, he studied the windows and balconies around the garden, the colonnade high on the far side. Or rather, he started to, but something else caught his eye. Below the colonnade, he could just make out the fading remnants of a weave. From there he could tell it was a gateway, but to see what kind and where it led, he had to be closer. Leaping over a jumble of worked stone that vanished while he was above it, he darted across the garden, dodging around trees fallen on the walkway. That residue was almost gone; he had to get close enough before it vanished completely.

Abruptly he fell, gravel scraping his palms as he caught himself. He could not see anything that might have tripped him. He felt woozy, almost as if he had been hit on the head. He tried to scramble to his feet, to reach that residue. And realized his body was writhing. Long hair covered his hands; his fingers seemed to be shrinking, drawing back into his hands. They were almost paws. A trap. 라빈 had not fled. The gateway had been a trap, and he had walked into it.

Desperation clung to the Void as he struggled to cling to himself. His hands. They were hands. Almost hands. He forced himself up. His legs seemed to bend wrong. The True Source receded; the Void shrank. Streaks of panic flared beyond the emotionless emptiness. Whatever 라빈 was trying to change him to, it could not channel. *Saidin* slipping away, thinning, thin even pulled through the *angreal*. The surrounding balconies stared down at him, empty, and the colonnade. 라빈 had to be at one of those stone-screened windows, but which? He had no strength for a hundred lightning bolts this time. One burst. He could manage that. If he did it quickly. Which window? He fought to be himself, fought to draw *세이딘* into him, welcomed every stain of the taint as evidence that he still held the Power. Staggering in a crooked circle, searching vainly, he roared 라빈’s name. It sounded like a beast’s roar.

Pulling 모그헤디엔 behind her, 니나브 rounded the corner. Ahead of her, a man vanished around the next turning, the sound of his boots echoing behind. She did not know how long she had been following those boots. Sometimes they had gone silent, and she had had to wait for them to start again to gain a direction. Sometimes when they stopped things happened; she had not seen any of it, but once the Palace had rung like a struck bell, and another time the hair on her head had tried to stand up as the air seemed to crackle, and another . . . It did not matter. This was the first time she had caught a glimpse of the man who wore those boots. She did not think it was 랜드 in that black coat. The height was right, but he was too large, too heavy in the chest.

She was running before she knew it. Her stout shoes had long since become velvet slippers for silence. If she could hear him, he could hear her. 모그헤디엔’s frenzied panting was louder than their footfalls.

니나브 reached the turn and stopped, peeking cautiously around the corner. She held *세다르*—through 모그헤디엔, but it was hers—ready to channel. There was no need. The hallway was empty. A door stood far down a wall with windows filled with arabesque-pierced stone, but she did not think he could have reached that. Nearer, another corridor ran off to the right. She hurried to that, looked warily again. Empty. But a staircase spiraled upward just beyond where the hallways met.

For a moment she hesitated. He had been hurrying somewhere. This corridor led back the way they had come. Would he have been running to go back? Up then.

Drawing 모그헤디엔 behind her, she climbed the steps slowly, straining to hear anything except the 버림받은 자들’s nearly hysterical breath and the blood pounding in her own ears. If she found herself face to face with him . . . She knew he was there already, somewhere ahead. Surprise had to be on her side.

At the first landing, she paused. The hallways here mirrored those below. They were just as empty, too, just as silent. Had he gone on up?

The stair quivered faintly beneath her feet as if the palace had been struck by a huge battering ram, then another. Again, as a bar of white fire punched through the top of one of the stone-screened windows, skewed wildly upward at an angle, then winked out as it started to slice into the ceiling.

니나브 swallowed, blinking in a vain effort to rid herself of the pale violet fan that hung across her vision in memory of the thing. That had to be 랜드, trying to strike at 라빈. If she was too close to him, 랜드 might catch her by accident. If he was flailing like that—it had had the look of flailing to her—he could catch her anywhere without knowing it.

The quivers had ceased. 모그헤디엔’s eyes shone with terror. By what 니나브 felt through the *a’dam*, it was a wonder the woman was not writhing on the floor, shrieking and frothing at the mouth. 니나브 felt a little like shrieking herself. She made herself put her foot on the next step. Up was as good a way as any. The second step was almost as hard. Slowly, though. No need to come on him too suddenly. Surprise had to be on his part. 모그헤디엔 followed like a whipped dog, shivering.

As 니나브 climbed, she embraced *세다르* as fully as she could, as much as 모그헤디엔 could handle, to the point where the sweetness of it became almost a pain. That was the warning. More, and she would approach the point where it was more than she could take in, the point where she would still herself, burn the ability to channel right out of herself. Or perhaps out of 모그헤디엔, under the circumstances. Or both of them. Any way at all, it would be disaster now. She held that point though, the . . . *life* . . . filling her a needle’s light pressure just short of breaking skin. It was as much as she could have embraced had she been channeling on her own. She and 모그헤디엔 were much the same strength in the Power; Tanchico had proved that. Was it enough? 모그헤디엔 insisted the men were stronger. 라빈, at least—모그헤디엔 knew him—and it did not seem likely 랜드 could have survived this long unless he was just as strong. It was not fair that men should have the muscles and greater strength in the Power, too. The 에스 세다이 in the Tower had always said they had been equal. It just was not—

She was babbling. Taking a deep breath, she drew 모그헤디엔 behind her off the staircase. This was as high as it went.

This hall was empty. She went to where it met the crossing corridor, peeked. And there he was. A tall black-clad man, large, with wings of white in his dark hair, peering through the curving slots of one of the stone window-screens at something below. There was sweat and effort on his face, but he seemed to be smiling. A handsome face, as handsome as 갈라드’s, but she felt no quickening of her breath for this one.

Whatever he was staring at—랜드 perhaps?—had his full attention, but 니나브 gave him no chance to notice her. It might be 랜드 down there. She could not tell whether 라빈 was channeling or not. She filled the corridor around him with fire from wall to wall, floor to ceiling, pouring into it all of *세다르* she held, fire so hot the stone itself smoked. The heat made her flinch back.

라빈 screamed in the middle of the flame—it was one flame—and staggered away from her, back to where the hallway became a columned walk. A heartbeat, less, while she still flinched, and he stood, inside the flame but surrounded by clear air. Every scrap of *세다르* she could channel was going into that inferno, but he held it at bay. She could see him through the fire; it gave everything a red cast, but she could see. Smoke rose from his charred coat. His face was a seared ruin, one eye milky white. But both eyes were malevolent as he turned them on her.

No emotion reached her along the *a’dam*’s leash, only leaden dullness. 니나브’s stomach fluttered. 모그헤디엔 had given up. Given up because death was there for them.

![](images/00211.jpg)

Fire thrust through the carved window-screens above 랜드, fingers of it filling every hole, dancing toward the colonnade. As it did, the struggle within him ceased abruptly. He was himself so suddenly it was almost a shock. He had been drawing desperately at *세이딘*, trying to hold onto some of it. Now it rushed into him, an avalanche of fire and ice that made his knees buckle, made the Void tremble with pain that shaved at it like a lathe.

And 라빈 stumbled backwards out onto the colonnade, face turned to something inside. 라빈 wreathed in fire, yet somehow standing as though untouched. If untouched now, it had not been so before. Only the size of the figure, the impossibility of it being anyone else, told 랜드 it was him. The 버림받은 자들 was a figure of char and cracked red flesh that would have strained any Healer to mend. The agony of it must have been overwhelming. Except that 라빈 would be inside the Void within that burned remnant of a man, wrapped in emptiness where the body’s pain was distant and *세이딘* close at hand.

*Saidin* raged inside 랜드, and he loosed it all. Not to Heal.

“라빈!” he screamed, and balefire flew from his hands, molten light thicker than a man, driven by all the Power he could draw.

It struck the 버림받은 자들, and 라빈 ceased to exist. The 어둠의 사냥개s in Rhuidean had become motes before they vanished, whatever kind of life they had had struggling to continue, or the Pattern struggling to maintain itself even for them. Before this, 라빈 simply . . . ceased.

랜드 let the balefire die, pushed *세이딘* away a little. Trying to blink away the purple afterimage, he stared up at the wide hole in the marble balustrade, the remains of one column a fang above it, stared at the matching hole in the Palace roof. They did not flicker, as if what he had done was too strong even for this place to mend. After everything, it seemed almost too easy. Perhaps there was something up there to convince him 라빈 was really dead. He ran toward a door.

Frantically, 니나브 threw everything into trying to close the flame tight around 라빈 once more. The thought came that she should have used lightning. She was going to die. Those horrible eyes had fixed on 모그헤디엔, not her, but she was going to die, too.

Liquid fire sliced up into the colonnade, so hot it made the fire she had made seem cool. Shock made her release her weaving, and she flung up a hand to protect her face, yet before it had raised halfway, the liquid fire was gone. So was 라빈. She did not believe he had escaped. There had been an instant, so brief she could almost have imagined it, when that white bar touched him and he became . . . mist. Just an instant. She could have imagined. But she did not believe so. She drew a shuddering breath.

모그헤디엔 had her face in her hands, weeping, trembling. The one emotion 니나브 sensed through the *a’dam* was relief so powerful it drowned anything else.

Hurried boots grated on the stairs below.

니나브 spun, took a step toward the spiral staircase. She was surprised to realize she was drinking deeply of *세다르*, holding herself ready.

That surprise faded when 랜드 climbed into sight. He was not as she remembered. His features were the same, but his face was hard. Blue ice made his eyes. The bloody rips in his coat and breeches, the blood on his face, seemed to suit that face.

The way he looked, she would not be surprised if he killed 모그헤디엔 on the spot the instant he discovered who she was. 니나브 had uses for her yet. He would recognize an *a’dam*. Without another thought she changed it, let the leash vanish, leaving only the silver bracelet on her wrist and the collar on 모그헤디엔. A moment of panic when she comprehended what she had done, then a sigh as she realized that she still felt the other woman. It worked exactly as 엘레인 had said it would. Perhaps he had not seen. She was between him and 모그헤디엔; the leash had trailed behind her.

He barely glanced at 모그헤디엔. “I thought about those flames, coming up here. I thought it might have been you or . . . Where is this? Is this where you meet 에그웨인?”

Looking up at him, 니나브 tried not to swallow. So cold, that face. “랜드, the 현명한 이들 say what you’ve done, what you are doing, is dangerous, even evil. They say you lose something of yourself if you come here in the flesh, some part of what makes you human.”

“Do the 현명한 이들 know everything?” He brushed past her and stood staring at the colonnade. “I used to think 에스 세다이 knew everything. It doesn’t matter. I don’t know how human the 용의 환생 can afford to be.”

“랜드, I . . .” She did not know what to say. “Here, let me Heal you at least.”

He held still for her to reach up and take his head in her hands. For her part, she had to suppress a wince. His fresh wounds were not serious, only numerous—what could have bitten him; she was sure most of these were bites—but the old wound, that half-healed, never-healing wound in his side, that was a sinkhole of darkness, a well filled with what she thought the taint of *세이딘* must be like. She channeled the complex flows, Air and Water, Spirit, even Fire and Earth in small amounts, that made up 치유. He did not roar and flail about. He did not even blink. He shivered. That was all. Then he took her wrists and brought her hands down from his face. She was not reluctant. His new injuries were gone, every bite and scrape and bruise, but not the old wound. Nothing had changed about that. Anything short of death should be capable of being Healed, even that. Anything!

“Is he dead?” he asked quietly. “Did you see him die?”

“He’s dead, 랜드. I saw.”

He nodded. “But there are others still, aren’t there? Other . . . Chosen.”

니나브 felt a stabbing sliver of fear from 모그헤디엔, but she did not glance back. “랜드, you must go. 라빈 is dead, and this place is dangerous for you as you are. You must go, and not come back here in the body.”

“I will go.”

He did nothing that she could see or feel—of course, she could not—but for a moment she thought the hallway behind him had . . . turned in some way. But it did not look any different. Except . . . She blinked. There was no half-gone column in the colonnade beyond him, no hole in the stone railing.

He went on as if nothing had happened. “Tell 엘레인. . . . Ask her not to hate me. Ask her . . .” Pain twisted his face. For a moment she saw the boy she had known, looking as though something precious was being ripped away from him. She reached out to comfort him, and he stepped back, his face stone again, and bleak. “란 was right. Tell 엘레인 to forget me, 니나브. Tell her I’ve found something else to love, and there’s no room left for her. He wanted me to tell you the same thing. 란 has found someone else, too. He said for you to forget him. Better never to have been born than to love us.” He stepped back again, three long steps, the hall seemed to turn dizzyingly with him in it—or part of the hall did—and he was gone.

니나브 stared at where he had been, and not at the fitfully flickering reappearance of the damage to the colonnade. 란 had told him to say *that*?

“A . . . remarkable man,” 모그헤디엔 said softly. “A very, very dangerous man.”

니나브 stared at her. Something new was coming through the bracelet to her. Fear was still there, but muted by . . . Expectation might have been the best way to describe it.

“I have been helpful, have I not?” 모그헤디엔 said. “라빈 dead, 랜드 al’Thor saved. None of it would have been possible without me.”

니나브 understood now. Hope more than expectation. Sooner or later 니나브 would have to wake. The *a’dam* would vanish. 모그헤디엔 was trying to remind her of her aid—as if it had not had to be wrenched out of her—just in case 니나브 might be steeling herself to kill before she went. “It is time for me to go, too,” 니나브 said. 모그헤디엔’s face did not alter, but fear strengthened and so did hope. A large silver cup appeared in 니나브’s hand, apparently filled with tea. “Drink this.”

모그헤디엔 edged back. “What—?”

“Not poison. I could kill you easily enough without, if that was my aim. After all, what happens to you here is real in the waking world, too.” Hope much stronger than fear now. “It will make you sleep. A deep sleep; too deep to touch *Tel’aran’rhiod*. It’s called forkroot.”

모그헤디엔 took the cup slowly. “So I cannot follow you? I will not argue.” She tipped back her head and swallowed until the cup was empty.

니나브 watched her. That much should put her down quickly. Yet a cruel streak made her speak. She knew it was cruel and did not care. 모그헤디엔 should not have any quiet rest at all. “You knew 비르기테 was not dead.” 모그헤디엔’s gaze narrowed slightly. “You knew who Faolain is.” The other woman’s eyes tried to widen, but she was already drowsy. 니나브 could feel the forkroot’s effects spreading. She concentrated on 모그헤디엔, held there in *Tel’aran’rhiod*. No easy sleep for one of the 버림받은 자들. “And you knew who 시우안 is, that she used to be the 아미를린 석좌. I’ve never mentioned that in *Tel’aran’rhiod*. Never. I’ll see you very shortly. In Salidar.”

모그헤디엔’s eyes rolled up her head. 니나브 was not sure whether it was the forkroot or a faint, but it did not matter. She released the other woman, and 모그헤디엔 winked out. The silver collar rang as it hit the floor tiles. 엘레인 would be happy about that, at least.

니나브 stepped out of the Dream.

랜드 trotted along the corridors of the Palace. There seemed to be less damage than he remembered, but he did not really look. He strode out into the great courtyard at the front of the Palace. Blasts of Air knocked the tall gates half off their hinges. Beyond lay a huge oval plaza, and what he had been searching for. 트롤록s and 미르드랄. 라빈 was dead, and the other 버림받은 자들 were elsewhere, but there were 트롤록s and 미르드랄 to kill in Caemlyn.

They were fighting, a milling mass of hundreds, perhaps thousands, surrounding something he could not see through their black-mailed numbers, as tall as a 미르드랄 on its horse. Just barely he could make out his crimson banner deep in their midst. Some swung round to face the Palace as the gates were hurled asunder.

Yet 랜드 stopped dead. Balls of fire rolled through the packed black-mailed mass, and burning 트롤록s lay everywhere. It could not be.

Not daring to hope or think, he channeled. Shafts of balefire leaped from his hands as fast as he could weave them, narrower than his little finger, precise and cut off as soon as they struck. They were much less powerful than the one he had used against 라빈 at the end, than any he had used against 라빈, but he could not risk one slicing through to those trapped in the center of all those 트롤록s. It made little difference. The first-struck 미르드랄 seemed to reverse colors, become a white-clad black shape, then it was drifting motes that vanished as its horse fled madly. 트롤록s, 미르드랄, every one that turned toward him went the same, and then he began carving into the backs of those still facing the other way, so a continuous haze of sparkling dust seemed to fill the air, renewed as it evaporated.

They could not stand against that. Bestial cries of rage turned to howls of fear, and they fled in every direction except toward him. He saw one 미르드랄 try to turn them and be trampled under, rider and horse, but the rest spurred their animals away.

랜드 let them go. He was busy staring at the veiled 아일 bursting out of their encirclement with spears and heavy-bladed knives. It was one of them carrying the banner; 아일 did not carry banners, but this one, a bit of red headband showing beneath his *shoufa*, did. There were battles going on down some of the streets leading from the plaza, too. 아일 against 트롤록s. Townsfolk against 트롤록s. Even armored men in the uniform of the Queen’s Guards against 트롤록s. Apparently some who were willing to kill a queen could not stomach 트롤록s. 랜드 only barely noticed, though. He was searching through the 아일.

There. A woman in a white blouse, one hand holding up her bulky skirts as she slashed at a fleeing 트롤록 with a short knife; an instant later flames enveloped the bear-snouted figure.

“아비엔다!” 랜드 did not know he was running until he shouted. “아비엔다!”

And there was 맷, coat torn and blood on his sword-blade spearpoint, leaning on the black shaft watching the 트롤록s flee, content to let someone else do the fighting now that that was possible. And 아스모데안, sword held awkwardly and trying to look every way at once in case any 트롤록 decided to turn back. 랜드 could sense *세이딘* in him, though weakly; he did not think much of 아스모데안’s fighting had been with that blade.

마화. 마화 that burned a thread out of the Pattern. The stronger that balefire was, the further back that burning went. And whatever that person had done *no longer had happened*. He did not care if his blast at 라빈 had unraveled half the Pattern. Not if this was the result.

He became aware of tears on his cheeks, and let *세이딘* and the Void go. He wanted to feel this. “아비엔다!” Snatching her up, he whirled her around, with her staring down at him as if he had gone mad. He did not want to put her down, but he did. So he could hug 맷. Or try to.

맷 fended him off. “What’s the matter with you? You’d think you thought we were dead. Not that we weren’t, almost. Being a general has to be safer than this!”

“You’re alive.” 랜드 laughed. He brushed back 아비엔다’s hair; she had lost her headscarf, and it hung loose around her neck. “I’m happy you’re alive. That’s all.”

He took in the plaza again, and his joy faded. Nothing could extinguish it, but the bodies lying in heaps where the 아일 had made their stand lessened it. Too many of them were not big enough to be men. There was Lamelle, veil gone and half her throat as well; she would never make him soup again. Pevin, both hands clutching the wrist-thick shaft of the 트롤록 spear through his chest and the first expression on his face 랜드 had ever seen. Surprise. 마화 had cheated death for his friends, but not for others. Too many. Too many Maidens.

*Take what you can have. Rejoice in what you can save, and do not mourn your losses too long*. It was not his thought, but he took it. It seemed a good way to avoid going mad before the taint on *세이딘* drove him to it.

“Where did you go?” 아비엔다 demanded. Not angrily. If anything, she looked relieved. “One second you were there, the next you were gone.”

“I had to kill 라빈,” he said quietly. She opened her mouth, but he put his fingers over it to silence her, then gently pushed her away. Take what you can have. “Leave it at that. He’s dead.”

Bael came limping up, *shoufa* still around his head but veil hanging down his chest. There was blood on his thigh, and on the point of his one remaining spear as well. “The Nightrunners and Shadowtwisted are running, *Car’a’carn*. Some of the wetlanders have joined the dance against them. Even some of the armored men, though they danced against us at first.” Sulin was behind him, unveiled, a nasty red gash across her cheek.

“Hunt them down however long it takes,” 랜드 said. He began walking, not sure where as long as it was away from 아비엔다. “I don’t want them loose on the countryside. Keep an eye on the Guards. I’ll find out later which of them were 라빈’s men and which . . .” He walked on, talking and not looking back. Take what you can have.
