CHAPTER 56

![](images/00483.jpg)

*Glowing Embers*

The high window had more than enough room for 랜드 to stand in it, stretching far above his head and clearing his shoulders by two feet to either side. Shirtsleeves rolled up, he stared down at one of the Royal Palace’s gardens. 아비엔다 was trailing her hand in the fountain’s redstone basin, still intrigued by so much water with no purpose but to be looked at and keep ornamental fish alive. She had been more than indignant at first, when he told her she could not go chasing 트롤록s through the streets. In fact, he was not sure she would not be down there now if not for a quiet escort of Maidens that Sulin did not think he had noticed. Neither was he supposed to have heard the white-haired Maiden remind her that she was *Far Dareis Mai* no longer and not yet a Wise One. Coatless, but wearing his hat against the sun, 맷 was sitting on the coping of the basin, talking to her. No doubt probing for what she knew of whether the 아일 were preventing people from leaving; even if 맷 did decide to accept his fate, it was unlikely he would ever stop complaining about it. 아스모데안 sat on a bench in the shade of a red myrtle tree, playing his harp. 랜드 wondered whether the man knew what had happened, or suspected. He should have no memory—for him, it never happened—but who could say what one of the 버림받은 자들 knew or could reason out?
A polite cough turned him away from the garden.

The window where he stood was a span and a half above the floor in the west wall of the throne room, the Grand Hall where Queens of 안도르 had received embassies and pronounced judgment for nearly a thousand years. It was the only place he had thought he could be sure of watching 맷 and 아비엔다 unseen and undisturbed. Rows of white columns twenty paces high marched down the sides of the hall. The light from the tall windows in the walls mingled with colored light from great windows set in the arching ceiling, windows where the White Lion alternated with portraits of early queens of the realm and scenes of great 안도르an victories. Enaila and Somara did not appear impressed.

랜드 let himself down by his fingertips. “Is there news from Bael?”

Enaila shrugged. “The hunt for 트롤록s goes on.” By her tone, the diminutive woman would have liked to be part of that. Somara’s height made her seem even shorter. “Some of the city people give aid. Most hide. The city gates are held. None of the Shadowtwisted will escape, I think, but I fear some of the Nightrunners may.” 미르드랄 were hard to kill, and just as hard to corner. Sometimes it was easy to believe the old tales that they rode shadows and could vanish by turning sideways.

“We brought you some soup,” Somara said, nodding her flaxen head toward a silver tray covered with a striped cloth, sitting on the dais that held the Lion Throne. Carved and gilded, with huge lion’s paws at the ends of its legs, the throne was a massive chair at the top of four white marble stairs, with a strip of red carpet leading up to it. The Lion of 안도르, picked out in moonstones on a field of rubies, would have stood above 모르가세’s head whenever she occupied that seat. “아비엔다 says you have not eaten yet today. It is the soup Lamelle used to make for you.”

“I suppose none of the servants have come back,” 랜드 sighed. “One of the cooks, maybe? A helper?” Enaila shook her head scornfully. She would serve her time as *gai’shain* with a good grace, if it ever came to that, but the idea of anyone spending their entire life serving someone else disgusted her.

Climbing the stairs, he squatted to twitch the cloth aside. His nose twitched, too. By the smell, whichever of them had made it was no better a cook than Lamelle had been. The sound of a man’s boots coming up the hall gave him an excuse to turn his back on the tray. With any luck, he would not have to eat it.

The man approaching up the long, red-and-white-tiled floor was certainly no 안도르man, in his short gray coat and those baggy trousers stuffed into boots turned down at the knee. Slender and only a hand taller than Enaila, he had a hooked beak of a nose and dark tilted eyes. Gray streaked his black hair and a thick mustache like down-curved horns around his wide mouth. He paused to make a leg and bow slightly, handling the curved sword at his hip gracefully despite the fact that incongruously he carried two silver goblets in one hand and a sealed pottery jar in the other.

“Forgive my intrusion,” he said, “but there was no one to announce me.” His clothes might be plain and even travel-worn, but he had what appeared to be an ivory rod capped with a golden wolf’s head thrust behind his sword belt. “I am 다브람 바쉐어, Marshal-General of 살다에아. I am here to speak with the Lord Dragon, who rumors in the city say is here in the Royal Palace. I assume that I address him?” For an instant his eyes went to the glittering 용 twining red-and-gold around 랜드’s arms.

“I am 랜드 al’Thor, Lord 바쉐어. The 용의 환생.” Enaila and Somara had moved between 랜드 and the man, each with a hand on the hilt of her long-bladed knife, poised to veil. “I am surprised to find a 살다에안 lord in Caemlyn, much less wanting to speak to me.”

“In truth, I rode to Caemlyn to speak to 모르가세, but I was put off by Lord Gaebril’s toadies—King Gaebril, I should say? Or does he still live?” 바쉐어’s tone said he doubted it, and did not care one way or the other. He did not pause. “Many in the city say 모르가세 is dead, as well.”

“They’re both dead,” 랜드 said bleakly. He sat down on the throne, his head resting against the moonstone Lion of 안도르. The throne had been sized for women. “I killed Gaebril, but not before he killed 모르가세.”

바쉐어 quirked an eyebrow. “Should I hail King 랜드 of 안도르, then?”

랜드 leaned forward angrily. “안도르 has always had a queen, and it still does. 엘레인 was Daughter-Heir. With her mother dead, she is queen. Maybe she has to be crowned first—I don’t know the law—but she is queen as far as I am concerned. I am the 용의 환생. That is as much as I want, and more. What is it you want of me, Lord 바쉐어?”

If his anger disturbed 바쉐어 at all, the man gave no outward sign. Those tilted eyes watched 랜드 carefully, but not uneasily. “The 백색 탑 allowed 마즈림 타임 to escape. The false Dragon.” He paused, then went on when 랜드 said nothing. “Queen Tenobia did not want 살다에아 troubled again, so I was sent to hunt him down once more and put an end to him. I have followed him south for many weeks. You need not fear I’ve brought a foreign army into 안도르. Except for an escort of ten, the rest I left camped in Braem Wood, well north of any border 안도르 has claimed in two hundred years. But 타임 is in 안도르. I am sure of it.”

랜드 leaned back again, hesitating. “You cannot have him, Lord 바쉐어.”

“May I ask why not, my Lord Dragon? If you wish to use 아일 to hunt him, I have no objection. My men will remain in Braem Wood until I return.”

This part of his plan he had not meant to reveal so soon. Delay could be costly, but he had intended to have a firm hold on the nations first. Yet it might as well begin now. “I am announcing an amnesty. I can channel, Lord 바쉐어. Why should another man be hunted down and killed or gentled because he can do what I can? I will announce that any man who can touch the True Source, any man who wants to learn, can come to me and have my protection. 최후의 전투 is coming, Lord 바쉐어. There may not be time for any of us to go mad before, and I would not waste one man for the risk anyway. When the 트롤록s came out of the 황무지 in the 트롤록 전쟁, they marched with Dreadlords, men and women who wielded the Power for the Shadow. We will face that again at Tarmon Gai’don. I don’t know how many 에스 세다이 will be at my side, but I won’t turn away any man who channels if he will march with me. 마즈림 타임 is mine, Lord 바쉐어, not yours.”

“I see.” It was flatly said. “You have taken Caemlyn. I hear that 티어 is yours, and 케렌 soon will be if it is not already. Do you mean to conquer the world with your 아일 and your army of men channeling the 하나의 힘?”

“If I must.” 랜드 said it just as levelly. “I’ll welcome any ruler as an ally who welcomes me, but so far all I’ve seen is maneuvering for power, or outright hostility. Lord 바쉐어, there’s anarchy in 타라본 and 아라드 도만, and not far from it in 케렌. 아마디시아 is eyeing 알타라. The 쇼엔찬—you may have heard rumors of them in 살다에아; the worst are likely true—the 쇼엔찬 on the other side of the world eyeing us all. Men fighting their own petty battles with Tarmon Gai’don on the horizon. We need peace. Time before the 트롤록s come, before the 어둠의 존재 breaks free, time to ready ourselves. If the only way I can find time and peace for the world is to impose it, I will. I don’t want to, but I will.”

“I have read *The 카라에손 순환*,” 바쉐어 said. Putting the goblets under his arm for a moment, he broke the wax seal on the jar and filled them with wine. “More importantly, Queen Tenobia has read the Prophecies, too. I cannot speak for 캔도르, or 아라펠, or 시엔나르. I believe they will come to you—not a child in the 국경지대 but knows the Shadow waits in the 황무지 to descend on us—but I cannot speak for them.” Enaila eyed the goblet he handed her suspiciously, but she climbed the stairs to hand it to 랜드. “In truth,” 바쉐어 continued, “I cannot even speak for 살다에아. Tenobia rules; I am only her general. But I think once I send a fast rider to her with a message, the return will be that 살다에아 marches with the 용의 환생. In the meanwhile, I offer you my services, and those of nine thousand 살다에안 horse.”

랜드 swirled the goblet, staring down into the dark red wine. 사마엘 in 일리안, and other 버림받은 자들 the Light alone knew where. 쇼엔찬 waiting across the Aryth Ocean, and men here ready to leap for their own advantage and profit whatever it cost the world. “Peace is far off yet,” he said softly. “It will be blood and death for some time to come.”

“It always is,” 바쉐어 replied quietly, and 랜드 did not know which statement he was speaking to. Perhaps both.

Tucking his harp under his arm, 아스모데안 drifted away from 맷 and 아비엔다. He enjoyed playing, but not for a pair who did not listen, much less appreciate. He was not sure what had happened that morning, and not sure he wanted to be sure. Too many 아일 had expressed surprise at seeing him, had claimed they had seen him dead; he did not want details. There was a long gash down the wall in front of him. He knew what made that sharp edge, that surface as slick as ice, smoother than any hand could have polished in a hundred years.

Idly—but with a shiver, too—he wondered whether being reborn in this fashion made him a new man. He did not think so. Immortality was gone. That was a gift of the Great Lord; he used that name in his head, whatever al’Thor demanded on his tongue. That was proof enough that he was himself. Immortality gone—he knew it must be imagination, yet sometimes he thought he could feel time dragging at him, pulling him toward a grave he had never thought to meet—and drawing the little of *세이딘* he could was like drinking sewage. He was hardly sorry 란피어 was dead. 라빈 either, but 란피어 especially, for what she had done to him. He would laugh when each of the others died, too, and most for the last. It was not that he had been reborn as a new man at all, but he would cling to that tuft of grass on the cliff’s brink as long as he could. The roots would give way eventually, the long fall would come, but until then he was still alive.

He pulled open a small door, intending to find his way to the pantry. There should be some decent wine. One step, and he stopped, the blood draining from his face. “You? No!” The word still hung in the air when death took him.

모르가세 blotted sweat from her face, then tucked the handkerchief back up her sleeve and readjusted her somewhat ragged straw hat. At least she had managed to acquire a decent riding dress, though even fine gray wool was still uncomfortable in this heat. Actually, 탈란보르 had acquired it. Letting her horse walk, she eyed the tall young man, riding up ahead through the trees. Basel Gill’s roundness emphasized how tall and fit 탈란보르 was. He had handed the dress to her saying it suited her better than the itchy thing she had fled the Palace in, looking down at her, never blinking, never speaking a word of respect. Of course, she herself had decided it was not safe for anyone to know who she was, especially after discovering Gareth Bryne gone from Kore Springs; why did the man have to be off chasing barnburners when she needed him? No matter; she would do as well without him. But there was something disturbing in 탈란보르’s eyes when he called her simply 모르가세.

Sighing, she glanced back over her shoulder. Hulking Lamgwin rode watching the forest, Breane at his side watching him as much as anything else. Her army had not grown a whit since Caemlyn. Too many had heard of nobles exiled for no cause and unjust laws in the capital to do more than scoff at the most casual mention of stirring a hand in support of their rightful ruler. She doubted that even knowing who spoke to them would have made a difference. So here she rode through 알타라, keeping to forest as much as possible because there seemed to be parties of armed men everywhere, rode through the forest with a scar-faced street tough, a besotted refugee 케렌인 noblewoman, a stout innkeeper who could hardly keep from kneeling whenever she glanced at him, and a young soldier who sometimes looked at her as though she had on one of those dresses she had worn for Gaebril. And Lini, of course. There was no forgetting Lini.

As if thinking of her had been a summons, the old nurse heeled her horse closer. “Better to keep your eyes ahead,” she said quietly. “ ‘A young lion charges quickest, and when you least expect it.’ ”

“You think 탈란보르 is dangerous?” 모르가세 said sharply, and Lini gave her a sidelong, considering look.

“Only the way any man can be dangerous. A fine figure of man, don’t you think? More than tall enough. Strong hands, I should think. ‘There’s no point letting honey age too long before you eat it.’ ”

“Lini,” 모르가세 said warningly. The old woman had been going on this way too often of late. 탈란보르 was a handsome man, his hands did look strong, and he had a well-turned calf, but he was young, and she was his queen. The last thing she needed was to start looking at him as a man instead of her subject and soldier. She was about to tell Lini that—and that the woman had lost her wits if she thought she was going to take up with any man ten years her junior; he had to be that—but 탈란보르 and Gill were turning back. “You hold your tongue, Lini. If you put foolish ideas into that young man’s head, I will leave you somewhere.” Lini’s snort would have earned the highest noble in 안도르 time in a cell to meditate. If she still had her throne, it would.

“Are you sure you want to do this, girl? ‘It’s too late to change your mind after you’ve jumped off the cliff.’ ”

“I will find my allies where I can find them,” 모르가세 told her stiffly.

탈란보르 reined up, sitting tall in his saddle. Sweat rolled down his face, but he seemed to ignore the heat. Master Gill tugged at the neck of his disc-covered jerkin as though he wished he could have it off.

“The wood gives way to farms just ahead,” 탈란보르 said, “but it isn’t likely anyone will recognize you here.” 모르가세 met his gaze levelly; day by day it was becoming increasingly hard to look away when he was looking at her. “Another ten miles should take us to Cormaed. If that fellow in Sehar was not lying, there will be a ferry, and we can be on the 아마디시아 side before dark. Are you certain you want to do this, 모르가세?”

The way he said her name . . . No. She was letting Lini’s ridiculous fancies take hold of her. It was the accursed heat. “I have made up my mind, young 탈란보르,” she said coolly, “and I do not expect you to question me when I have done so.”

She heeled her mount hard, letting the horse’s leap forward break their gazes apart, letting it shove past him. He could catch up to her. She would find her allies where she found them. She would have her throne back, and woe to Gaebril or *any* man who thought he could sit on it in her place.

# Lord of Chaos by Robert Jordan

## PROLOGUE

![](images/00177.jpg)

*The First Message*

디만드레드 stepped out onto the black slopes of 세이올 굴, and the gateway, a hole in reality’s fabric, winked out of existence. Above, roiling gray clouds hid the sky, an inverted sea of sluggish ashen waves crashing around the mountain’s hidden peak. Below, odd lights flashed across the barren valley, washed-out blues and reds, failing to dispel the dusky murk that shrouded their source. Lightning streaked *up* at the clouds, and slow thunder rolled. Across the slope steam and smoke rose from scattered vents, some holes as small as a man’s hand and some large enough to swallow ten men.

He released the 하나의 힘 immediately, and with the vanished sweetness went the heightened senses that made everything sharper, clearer. The absence of *세이딘* left him hollow, yet here only a fool would even appear ready to channel. Besides, here only a fool would want to see or smell or feel too clearly.

In what was now called the 전설의 시대, this had been an idyllic island in a cool sea, a favorite of those who enjoyed the rustic. Despite the steam it was bitter cold, now; he did not allow himself to feel it, but instinct made him pull his fur-lined velvet cloak closer. Feathery mist marked his breath, barely visible before the air drank it. A few hundred leagues north the world was pure ice, but Thakan’dar was always dry as any desert, though always wrapped in winter.

There was water, of a sort, an inky rivulet oozing down the rocky slope beside a gray-roofed forge. 햄mers rang inside, and with every ring, white light flared in the cramped windows. A ragged woman crouched in a hopeless heap against the forge’s rough stone wall, clutching a babe in her arms, and a spindly girl buried her face in the woman’s skirts. Prisoners from a raid down into the 국경지대, no doubt. But so few; the 미르드랄 must be gnashing their teeth. Their blades failed after a time and had to be replaced, no matter that raids into the 국경지대 had been curtailed.

One of the forgers emerged, a thick slow-moving man shape that seemed hacked out of the mountain. The forgers were not truly alive; carried any distance from 세이올 굴, they turned to stone, or dust. Nor were they smiths as such; they made nothing but the swords. This one’s two hands held a sword blade in long tongs, a blade already quenched, pale like moonlit snow. Alive or not, the forger took care as it dipped the gleaming metal into the dark stream. Whatever semblance of life it had could be ended by the touch of that water. When the metal came out again, it was dead black. But the making was not done yet. The forger shuffled back inside, and suddenly a man’s voice raised a desperate shout.

“No? No! NO!” He shrieked then, the sound dwindling away without losing intensity, as though the screamer had been yanked into unimaginably far distance. Now the blade was done.

Once more a forger appeared—perhaps the same, perhaps another—and hauled the woman to her feet. Woman, babe and child began to wail, but the infant was pulled away and shoved into the girl’s arms. At last the woman found a scrap of resistance. Weeping, she kicked wildly, clawed at the forger. It paid no more mind than stone would have. The woman’s cries vanished as soon as she was inside. The hammers began ringing again, drowning the sobs of the children.

One blade made, one making, and two to come. 디만드레드 had never before seen fewer than fifty prisoners waiting to give their mite to the Great Lord of the Dark. The 미르드랄 must be gnashing their teeth, indeed.

“Do you loiter when you have been summoned by the Great Lord?” The voice sounded like rotted leather crumbling.

디만드레드 turned slowly—how dare a 반쪽 인간 address him in that tone—but the quelling words died in his mouth. It was not the eyeless stare of its pasty-pale face; a 미르드랄’s gaze struck fear in any man, but he had rooted fear out of himself long ago. Rather, it was the black-clad creature itself. Every 미르드랄 was the height of a tall man, a sinuous imitation of a man, as alike as though cast in one mold. This one stood head and shoulders taller.

“I will take you to the Great Lord,” the 미르드랄 said. “I am 샤이다르 하란.” It turned away and began climbing the mountain, like a serpent in its fluid motion. Its inky cloak hung unnaturally still, without even a ripple.

디만드레드 hesitated before following. Halfmen’s names were always in the 트롤록s’ tongue-wrenching language. “샤이다르 하란” came from what people now named the 고대어. It meant “Hand of the Dark.” Another surprise, and 디만드레드 did not like surprises, especially not at 세이올 굴.

The entry into the mountain could have been one of the scattered vents, except that it emitted no smoke or steam. It gaped enough for two men abreast, but the 미르드랄 kept the lead. The way slanted down almost immediately, the tunnel floor worn smooth as polished tiles. The cold faded as 디만드레드 followed 샤이다르 하란’s broad back down and down, slowly replaced by increasing heat. 디만드레드 was aware of it, but did not let it touch him. A pale light rose from the stone, filling the tunnel, brighter than the eternal twilight outside. Jagged spikes jutted from the ceiling, stony teeth ready to snap shut, the Great Lord’s teeth to rend the unfaithful or the traitor. Not natural, of course, but effective.

Abruptly, he noticed something. Every time he had made this journey, those spikes had all but brushed the top of his head. Now they cleared the 미르드랄’s by two hands or more. That surprised him. Not that the height of the tunnel changed—the strange was ordinary here—but the extra space the 반쪽 인간 was given. The Great Lord gave his reminders to 미르드랄 as well as men. That extra space was a fact to be remembered.

The tunnel opened out suddenly onto a wide ledge overlooking a lake of molten stone, red mottled with black, where man-high flames danced, died and rose again. There was no roof, only a great hole rising through the mountain to a sky that was not the sky of Thakan’dar. It made that of Thakan’dar look normal, with its wildly striated clouds streaking by as though driven by the greatest winds the world had ever seen. This, men called the Pit of Doom, and few knew how well they had named it.

Even after all his visits—and the first lay well over three thousand years in the past—디만드레드 felt awe. Here he could sense the 구멍, the hole drilled through so long ago to where the Great Lord had lain imprisoned since the moment of Creation. Here the Great Lord’s presence washed over him. Physically, this place was no closer to the 구멍 than any other in the world, but here there was a thinness in the Pattern that allowed it to be sensed.

디만드레드 came as close to smiling as he ever did. What fools they were who opposed the Great Lord. Oh, the 구멍 was still blocked, though more tenuously than when he had wakened from his long sleep and broken free of his own prison in it. Blocked, but larger than when he woke. Still not so large as when he had been cast into it with his fellows at the end of the War of Power, but at each visit since waking, a little wider. Soon the blockage would be gone, and the Great Lord would reach out across the earth again. Soon would come the Day of Return. And he would rule the world for all time. Under the Great Lord, of course. And with those of the other Chosen who survived, also of course.

“You may leave now, 반쪽 인간.” He did not want the thing here to see the ecstasy overcome him. The ecstasy, and the pain.

샤이다르 하란 did not move.

디만드레드 opened his mouth—and a voice exploded in his head.

DEMANDRED.

To call it a voice was to call a mountain a pebble. It nearly crushed him against the inside of his own skull; it filled him with rapture. He sank to his knees. The 미르드랄 stood watching impassively, but only a small part of him could even notice the thing with that voice filling his brain.

DEMANDRED. HOW FARES THIS WORLD?

He was never sure how much the Great Lord knew of the world. He had been as startled by ignorance as by knowledge. But he had no doubt what the Great Lord wanted to hear.

“라빈 is dead, Great Lord. Yesterday.” There was pain. Euphoria too strong became pain quickly. His arms and legs twitched. He was sweating, now. “란피어 has vanished without a trace, just as 아스모데안 did. And 그랜달 says 모그헤디엔 failed to meet her as they had agreed. Also yesterday, Great Lord. I do not believe in coincidence.”

THE CHOSEN DWINDLE, DEMANDRED. THE WEAK FALL AWAY. WHO BETRAYS ME SHALL DIE THE FINAL DEATH. ASMODEAN, TWISTED BY HIS WEAKNESS. RAHVIN DEAD IN HIS PRIDE. HE SERVED WELL, YET EVEN I CANNOT SAVE HIM FROM BALEFIRE. EVEN I CANNOT STEP OUTSIDE OF TIME. For an instant terrible anger filled that awful voice, and—could it be frustration? An instant only. DONE BY MY ANCIENT ENEMY, THE ONE CALLED DRAGON. WOULD YOU UNLEASH THE BALEFIRE IN MY SERVICE, DEMANDRED?

디만드레드 hesitated. A bead of sweat slid half an inch on his cheek; it seemed to take an hour. For a year during the War of Power, both sides had used balefire. Until they learned the consequences. Without agreement, or truce—there had never been a truce any more than there had been quarter—each side simply stopped. Entire cities died in balefire that year, hundreds of thousands of threads burned from the Pattern; reality itself almost unraveled, world and universe evaporating like mist. If balefire was unleashed once more, there might be no world to rule.

Another point pricked him. The Great Lord already knew how 라빈 had died. And seemed to know more of 아스모데안 than he. “As you command, Great Lord, so shall I obey.” His muscles might be jerking, but his voice was rock steady. His knees began to blister from the hot stone, yet the flesh might as well have been someone else’s.

SO YOU SHALL.

“Great Lord, the Dragon can be destroyed.” A dead man could not wield balefire again, and perhaps then the Great Lord would see no need for it. “He is ignorant and weak, scattering his attentions in a dozen directions. 라빈 was a vain fool. I—”

WOULD YOU BE NAE’BLIS?

디만드레드’s tongue froze. Nae’blis. The one who would stand only a step below the Great Lord, commanding all others. “I wish only to serve you, Great Lord, however I may.” Nae’blis.

THEN LISTEN, AND SERVE. HEAR WHO WILL DIE AND WHO LIVE.

디만드레드 screamed as the voice crashed home. 티어s of joy rolled down his face.

Unmoving, the 미르드랄 watched him.

“Stop fidgeting.” 니나브 testily flipped her long braid over her shoulder. “This won’t work if you twitch around like children with an itch.”

Neither of the women across the rickety table appeared any older than she, though they were by twenty years or more, and neither was really fidgeting, but the heat had 니나브 on edge. The small windowless room seemed airless. She dripped sweat; they appeared cool and dry. 리안, in a 도마니 dress of too-thin blue silk, merely shrugged; the tall coppery-skinned woman possessed an apparently infinite store of patience. Usually. 시우안, fair and sturdy, seldom had any.
Now 시우안 grunted and resettled her skirts irritably; she used to wear fairly plain clothes, but this morning she was in fine yellow linen embroidered with a 타이런 maze around a neckline that barely missed being too low. Her blue eyes were cold as deep well water. As cold as deep well water would have been if the weather had not gone mad. Her dresses might have changed, but not her eyes. “It won’t work in any case,” she snapped. Her manner of speaking was the same, too. “You can’t patch a hull when the whole boat’s burned. Well, it’s a waste of time, but I promised, so get on with it. 리안 and I have work to do.” The pair of them ran the networks of eyes-and-ears for the 에스 세다이 here in Salidar, the agents who sent in reports and rumors of what was going on in the world.

니나브 smoothed her own skirts to soothe herself. Her dress was plain white wool, with seven bands of color at the hem, one for each 아자. An 허락받은 자’s dress. It annoyed her more than she could ever have imagined. She would much rather have been in the green silk she had packed away. She was willing to admit her acquired taste for fine clothes, privately at least, but her choice of that particular dress was only for comfort—it was thin, light—not because green seemed one of 란’s favorite colors. Not at all. Idle dreaming of the worst sort. An 허락받은 자 who put on anything except the banded white would soon learn she was a *long* step below 에스 세다이. Firmly she put all that out of her head. She was not here to fret over fripperies. He liked blue, too. No!

Delicately she probed with the 하나의 힘, first at 시우안, then 리안. In a manner of speaking, she was not channeling at all. She could not channel a scrap unless angry, could not even sense the True Source. Yet it came to the same thing. Fine filaments of *세다르*, the female half of the True Source, sifted through the two women at her weaving. They just did not originate with her.

On her left wrist 니나브 wore a slender bracelet, a simple segmented silver band. Mainly silver, anyway, and from a special source, though that made no difference. It was the only piece of jewelry she wore aside from the Great Serpent ring; 허락받은 자 were firmly discouraged from wearing much jewelry. A matching necklace snugged around the neck of the fourth woman, on a stool against the rough-plastered wall with her hands folded in her lap. Clad in a farmer’s rough brown wool, with a farmer’s worn sturdy face, she did not sweat a drop. She did not move a muscle either, but her dark eyes watched everything. To 니나브, the radiance of *세다르* surrounded her, but it was 니나브 who directed the channeling. Bracelet and necklace created a link between them, much in the way 에스 세다이 could link to combine their power. Something about “absolutely identical matrices” was involved, according to 엘레인, after which the explanation truly became incomprehensible. In truth, 니나브 did not think 엘레인 understood half as much as she pretended. For herself, 니나브 did not understand at all, except that she could feel the other woman’s every emotion, feel the woman herself, but tucked away in a corner of her head, and that all the other woman’s grasp of *세다르* was in her control. Sometimes she thought it would have been better if the woman on the stool were dead. Simpler, certainly. Cleaner.

“There’s something torn, or cut,” 니나브 muttered, wiping absently at the sweat on her face. It was just a vague impression, barely there at all, but it was also the first time she had sensed more than emptiness. It could be imagination, and the desperate wanting to find something, anything.

“Severing,” the woman on the stool said. “That was what it was called, what you name stilling for women and gentling for men.”

Three heads swiveled toward her; three sets of eyes glared with fury. 시우안 and 리안 had been 에스 세다이 until they were stilled during the coup in the 백색 탑 that put 엘라이더 on the 아미를린 석좌. Stilled. A word to cause shudders. Never to channel again. But always to remember, and know the loss. Always to sense the True Source and know you could never touch it again. Stilling could not be Healed any more than death.

That was what everyone believed, anyway, but in 니나브’s opinion the 하나의 힘 should be able to Heal anything short of death. “If you have something useful to add, Marigan,” she said sharply, “then say it. If not, keep quiet.”

Marigan shrank back against the wall, eyes glittering and fixed on 니나브. Fear and hate rolled through the bracelet, but they always did to one degree or another. Captives seldom loved their captors, even—perhaps especially—when they knew they deserved captivity and worse. The problem was that Marigan also said severing—stilling—could not be Healed. Oh, she was full of claims that anything else except death could be Healed in the 전설의 시대, that what the 황색 아자 called 치유 now was only the crudest hasty battlefield work. But try to pin her down on specifics, on even a hint of how, and you found nothing there. Marigan knew as much about 치유 as 니나브 did about blacksmithing, which was that you stuck metal in hot coals and hit it with a hammer. Certainly not enough to make a horseshoe. Or Heal much beyond a bruise.

Twisting around in her chair, 니나브 studied 시우안 and 리안. Days of this, whenever she could pry them away from their other work, and so far she had learned nothing. Suddenly she realized she was turning the bracelet on her wrist. Whatever there the gain, she hated being linked to the woman. The intimacy made her skin crawl. *At least I might learn something*, she thought. *And it couldn’t fail any worse than everything else has*.

Carefully she undid the bracelet—the clasp was impossible to find unless you knew how—and handed it to 시우안. “Put this on.” Losing the Power was bitter, but this had to be done. And losing the waves of emotion was like taking a bath. Marigan’s eyes followed the narrow length of silver as if hypnotized.

“Why?” 시우안 demanded. “You tell me this thing only works—”

“Just put it on, 시우안.”

시우안 eyed her stubbornly for a moment—Light, but the woman could be obstinate!—before closing the bracelet around her wrist. A look of wonder came onto her face immediately, then her eyes narrowed at Marigan. “She hates us, but I knew that. And there’s fear, and . . . Shock. Not a glimmer on her face, but she’s shocked to her toes. I don’t think she believed I could use this thing, either.”

Marigan shifted uneasily. So far only two who knew about her could use the bracelet. Four would give more chances for questions. On the surface she seemed to be cooperating fully, but how much was she hiding? As much as she could, 니나브 was sure.

With a sigh, 시우안 shook her head. “And I cannot. I should be able to touch the Source through her, isn’t that right? Well, I can’t. A grunter could climb trees first. I’ve been stilled, and that is that. How do you get this thing off?” She fumbled at the bracelet. “How do you bloody get it off?”

Gently 니나브 laid a hand over 시우안’s on the bracelet. “Don’t you see? The bracelet won’t work for a woman who can’t channel any more than the necklace would work on her. If I put either on one of the cooks, it would be no more than a pretty piece for her.”

“Cooks or no cooks,” 시우안 said flatly, “I cannot channel. I have been stilled.”

“But there is something there to be Healed,” 니나브 insisted, “or you’d feel nothing through the bracelet.”

시우안 jerked her arm free and stuck her wrist out. “Take it off.”

Shaking her head, 니나브 complied. Sometimes 시우안 could be as bullheaded as any man!

When she held the bracelet toward 리안, the 도마니 woman lifted her wrist eagerly. 리안 pretended to be as sanguine over having been stilled as 시우안 was—as 시우안 pretended to be—but she did not always succeed. Supposedly, the only way to survive stilling for long was to find something else to fill your life, to fill the hole left by the 하나의 힘. For 시우안 and 리안 that something was running their networks of agents, and more importantly, trying to convince the 에스 세다이 here in Salidar to support 랜드 al’Thor as the 용의 환생 without letting any of the 에스 세다이 know what they were doing. The question was whether that was enough. The bitterness on 시우안’s face, and the delight on 리안’s as the bracelet snapped shut, said that maybe nothing could ever be.

“Oh, yes.” 리안 had a brisk, clipped way of speaking. Except when talking to men, anyway; she was 도마니, after all, and of late making up for time lost in the Tower. “Yes, she really is stunned, isn’t she? Beginning to control it now, though.” For a few moments she sat silently, considering the woman on the stool. Marigan stared back warily. At last, 리안 shrugged. “I cannot touch the Source, either. And I tried to make her feel a fleabite on her ankle. If it had worked, she would have had to show something.” That was the other trick of the bracelet; you could make the woman wearing the necklace feel physical sensations. Only the sensations—there was no mark whatever you did, no real damage—but the feel of a sound switching or two had sufficed to convince Marigan that cooperation was her best choice. That and the alternative, a quick trial followed by execution.

Despite her failure, 리안 watched closely as 니나브 undid the bracelet and refastened it on her own wrist. It seemed that she, at least, had not given up completely on channeling again one day.

Regaining the Power was wonderful. Not as wonderful as drawing *세다르* herself, being filled with it, but even touching the Source through the other woman was like redoubling the life in her veins. To hold *세다르* inside was to want to laugh and dance with pure joy. She supposed that one day she would become used to it; full 에스 세다이 must. Balanced against that, linking with Marigan was a small price. “Now that we know there’s a chance,” she said, “I think—”

The door banged open, and 니나브 was on her feet before she knew it. She never thought of using the Power; she would have screamed if her throat had not closed tight. She was not the only one, but she hardly noticed 시우안 and 리안 leaping up. The fear cascading through the bracelet seemed an echo of her own.

The young woman who shut the splintery wooden door behind her took no notice of the commotion she had caused. Tall and straight in an 허락받은 자’s banded white dress, with sun-gold curls nestled on her shoulders, she looked spitting mad. Even with her face tight with anger and dripping sweat she somehow managed to look beautiful, though; it was a knack 엘레인 had. “Do you know what they’re doing? They are sending an embassy to . . . to Caemlyn! And they refuse to let me go! 셰리암 *forbade* me to mention it again. Forbade me even to *speak* of it!”

“Did you never learn to knock, 엘레인?” Straightening her chair, 니나브 sat down again. Fell, really; relief weakened her knees. “I thought you *were* 셰리암.” Just the thought of discovery cored out her middle.

To her credit, 엘레인 blushed and apologized immediately. Then spoiled it by adding, “But I don’t see why you were so goosey. 비르기테 is still outside, and you *know* she would warn you if anyone else came close. 니나브, they *must* let me go.”

“They *must* do nothing of the kind,” 시우안 said gruffly. She and 리안 were seated again, too. 시우안 sat up straight, as always, but 리안 sagged back, as flimsy as 니나브’s knees. Marigan was leaning against the wall, breathing hard, eyes closed and hands pressed hard against the plaster. Relief and stark terror surged through the bracelet in alternating jolts.

“But—”

시우안 did not allow 엘레인 another word. “Do you think 셰리암, or any of the others, will let the Daughter-Heir of 안도르 fall into the hands of the 용의 환생? With your mother dead—”

“I don’t believe that!” 엘레인 snapped.

“You don’t believe 랜드 killed her,” 시우안 went on relentlessly, “and that’s a different thing. I don’t, either. But if 모르가세 were alive, she would come forward and acknowledge him the 용의 환생. Or, if she believed him a false Dragon in spite of the proof, she’d be organizing resistance. None of my eyes-and-ears have heard a whisper of either. Not just in 안도르, but not here in 알타라 and not in 무란디.”

“They *have*,” 엘레인 forced in. “There’s rebellion in the west.”

“Against 모르가세. Against. If it’s not a rumor, too.” 시우안’s voice was flat as a planed board. “Your mother is dead, girl. Best to admit as much and get your weeping done.”

엘레인’s chin rose, a very annoying habit she had; she was the picture of icy arrogance, though most men seemed to find it attractive for some reason. “You complain continually over how long it is taking to get in touch with all of your agents,” she said coolly, “but I will set aside whether you can have heard all there is to hear. Whether my mother is alive or not, *my* place is in Caemlyn, now. I *am* Daughter-Heir.”

시우안’s loud snort made 니나브 jump. “You’ve been 허락받은 자 long enough to know better.” 엘레인 had as much potential as had been seen in a thousand years. Not as much as 니나브, if she ever learned to channel at will, but still enough to make any 에스 세다이’s eyes light up. 엘레인’s nose wrinkled—she knew very well that if she had already been on the Lion Throne, the 에스 세다이 still would have gotten her away for training, by asking if possible, by stuffing her into a barrel if necessary—and she opened her mouth, but 시우안 did not even slow down. “True, they’d not mind you taking the throne sooner than later; there hasn’t been a Queen who was openly 에스 세다이 in far too long. But they won’t let you go until you’re a full sister, and even then, because you *are* Daughter-Heir and will be Queen soon, they won’t let you near the Dragon bloody Reborn until they know how far they can trust him. Especially since this . . . *amnesty* of his.” Her mouth twisted sourly around the word, and 리안 grimaced.

니나브’s tongue curdled, too. She had been brought up to fear any man who could channel, fated to go mad and, before the Shadow-tainted male half of the Source killed him horribly, bring terror to everyone around him. But 랜드, whom she had watched grow up, was the 용의 환생, born both as a sign that the Last Battle was coming and to fight the 어둠의 존재 in that battle. The 용의 환생; humanity’s only hope—and a man who could channel. Worse, reports were that he was trying to gather others like him. Of course, there could not be many. Any 에스 세다이 would hunt down one of those—the 적색 아자 did little else—but they found few, far fewer than once, according to the records.

엘레인 was not about to give up, though. That was one admirable thing about her; she would not give up if her head were on the block and the axe descending. She stood there with her chin up, facing 시우안’s stare, which 니나브 often found hard to do. “There are two clear reasons why I should go. First, whatever has happened to my mother, she *is* missing, and as Daughter-Heir, I can calm the people and assure them the succession is intact. Second, I can approach 랜드. He trusts me. I would be *far* better than anyone the Hall chooses.”

The 에스 세다이 here in Salidar had chosen their own 탑의 회의실, a Hall-in-exile, as it were. They were supposed to be mulling over the choice of a new 아미를린 석좌, a rightful Amyrlin to challenge 엘라이더’s claim to the title and the Tower, but 니나브 had not seen much sign of it.

“So kind of you to sacrifice yourself, child,” 리안 said dryly. 엘레인’s expression did not change, yet she colored furiously; few outside this room knew, and no 에스 세다이, but 니나브 had no doubt that 엘레인’s first act in Caemlyn would be to get 랜드 alone and kiss him within an inch of his life. “With your mother . . . missing . . . if 랜드 al’Thor has you, and Caemlyn, he has 안도르, and the Hall won’t let him have any more of 안도르 than they have to, or anywhere else if they can help it. He carries 티어 and 케렌 in his pocket, and the 아일 as well, it seems. Add 안도르, and 무란디 and 알타라—with us in it—fall if he sneezes. He is growing too powerful, too fast. He might decide he doesn’t need us. With 모이라인 dead, there’s no one near him we can trust.”

That made 니나브 wince. 모이라인 was the 에스 세다이 who had brought her and 랜드 out of the 두 강 and changed their lives. Her and 랜드 and 에그웨인 and 맷 and 페린. She had wanted for so long to make 모이라인 pay for what she had done to them that losing her was like losing a piece of herself. But 모이라인 was dead in 케렌, taking 란피어 with her; she was fast becoming a legend among the 에스 세다이 here, the only 에스 세다이 to have killed one of the 버림받은 자들, much less two. The only good thing 니나브 could find in it, much as it shamed to find any good, was that now 란 was freed from being 모이라인’s 감시자. If she could ever find him.

시우안 took up immediately where 리안 left off. “We can’t afford to let the boy go sailing off with no guidance at all. Who knows what he might do? Yes, yes, I know you’re ready to argue for him, but I don’t care to hear it. I’m trying to balance a live silverpike on my nose, girl. We can’t let him grow too strong before he accepts us, and yet we don’t dare hold him back too much. And I’m trying to keep 셰리암 and the others convinced they *should* support him when half the Hall secretly don’t want anything to do with him, and the other half think in their heart of hearts that he should be gentled, 용의 환생 or not. In any case, whatever your arguments, I suggest you heed 셰리암. You won’t change any minds, and Tiana doesn’t have enough 수련생s here to keep her busy.”

엘레인’s face tightened angrily. Tiana Noselle, a Gray sister, was 수련생 감독관 here in Salidar. An 허락받은 자 had to step considerably further out of line to be sent to Tiana than did a 수련생, but by the same token, the visit was always that much more shaming and painful. Tiana might show a little kindness to a 수련생, if only a little; she felt 허락받은 자 should know better, and made sure they felt the same long before they left her small cubbyhole of a study.

니나브 had been studying 시우안, and now something popped into her head. “You knew all about this . . . embassy, or whatever it is . . . didn’t you? You two always have your heads together with 셰리암 and her little circle.” The Hall might have all the supposed authority until they chose an Amyrlin, but 셰리암 and the handful of other 에스 세다이 who had first organized the arrivals in Salidar still kept the real control of things. “How many are they sending, 시우안?” 엘레인 gasped; plainly she had not thought of this. That showed how upset she was. Usually she caught nuances 니나브 missed.

시우안 denied nothing. Since being stilled she could lie like a wool merchant, but when she decided to be open, she was as open as a slap in the face. “Nine. ‘Enough to do honor to the 용의 환생’—fish guts! an embassy to a *king* is seldom more than three!—‘but not enough to frighten him.’ If he’s learned enough to be frightened.”

“You had better hope he has,” 엘레인 said coldly. “If he hasn’t, then nine may be eight too many.”

Thirteen was the dangerous number. 랜드 was strong, perhaps as strong as any man since the Breaking, but thirteen 에스 세다이 linked could overwhelm him, shield him from *세이딘*, and take him prisoner. Thirteen was the number assigned when a man was gentled, though 니나브 had begun to think the assignment more custom than requirement. 에스 세다이 did a good many things because they always had.

시우안’s smile was far from pleasant. “I wonder why no one else thought of that? Think, girl! 셰리암 does, and so does the Hall. Only one will go near him at first, and no more after that than he’s comfortable with. But he’ll know nine came, and somebody will certainly tell him what an honor that is.”

“I see,” 엘레인 said in a small voice. “I should have known one of you would think of it. I’m sorry.” That was another good thing about her. She could be stubborn as a cross-eyed mule, but when she decided she was wrong, she admitted it as nicely as any village woman. Most unusual for a noble.

“민 will be going too,” 리안 said. “Her . . . talents may be useful to 랜드. The sisters won’t know that part, of course. She can keep her secrets.” As if that were the important thing.

“I see,” 엘레인 said again, flatly this time. She made an effort to brighten her tone, a miserable failure. “Well, I see you’re busy with . . . with Marigan. I did not mean to disturb you. Please, don’t let me interrupt.” She was gone before 니나브 could open her mouth, the door banging shut behind her.

Angrily, 니나브 rounded on 리안. “I thought 시우안 was the mean one of you, but that was vicious!”

It was 시우안 who answered. “When two women love the same man, it means trouble, and when the man is 랜드 al’Thor. . . . 빛 knows how sane he still is, or what course they might send him off on. If there’s any hair-pulling and clawing to be done, let them do it now, here.”

Without thought, 니나브’s hand found her braid and jerked it back over her shoulder. “I ought to. . . .” Trouble was, there was little she could do, and nothing to make any difference. “We’ll go on from where we left off when 엘레인 came in. But, 시우안. . . . If you ever do something like that to her again,” *or to me*, she thought, “I’ll make you sorry you—Where do you think you’re going?” 시우안 had scraped back her chair and risen, and after a glance, 리안 did the same.

“We have work,” 시우안 said curtly, already heading for the door.

“You promised to make yourself available, 시우안. 셰리암 told you to.” Not that 셰리암 thought it any less a waste of time than 시우안, but 니나브 and 엘레인 had earned rewards, and a certain amount of indulgence. Like Marigan to be their maid, to give them more time for 허락받은 자’s studies.

시우안 gave her an amused look from the door. “Maybe you’ll complain to her? And explain how you do your research? I want time with *Marigan* this evening; I have some more questions.”

As 시우안 left, 리안 said sadly, “It would be nice, 니나브, but we have to do what we *can* do. You could try 로가인.” Then she was gone, too.

니나브 scowled. Studying 로가인 had taught her even less than studying the two women. She was no longer certain she could learn anything from him at all. Anyway, the last thing she wanted was to Heal a gentled man. He made her nervous in any case.

“You bite at one another like rats in a sealed box,” Marigan said. “On the evidence, your chances are not very good. Perhaps you should consider . . . other options.”

“Hold your filthy tongue!” 니나브 glared at her. “Hold it, the Light burn you!” Fear still oozed through the bracelet, but something else as well, something almost too feeble to exist. A faint spark of hope, perhaps. “빛 burn you,” she muttered.

The woman’s real name was not Marigan, but 모그헤디엔. One of the 버림받은 자들, trapped with her own overweening pride and held prisoner in the midst of 에스 세다이. Only five women in the world knew, none 에스 세다이, but keeping 모그헤디엔 secret was purest necessity. The 버림받은 자들’s crimes made her execution as sure as the sun rising. 시우안 agreed; for every 에스 세다이 who counseled waiting, if any did, ten would demand immediate justice. Into an unmarked grave with her would go all her knowledge from the 전설의 시대, when things undreamed of today were done with the Power. 니나브 was not sure she believed half of what the woman told her of that Age. She certainly understood less than half.

Digging information out of 모그헤디엔 was not easy. Sometimes it was like 치유; 모그헤디엔 had never been interested in much that could not advance her, preferably by shortcuts. The woman was hardly likely to reveal the truth, but 니나브 suspected she had been some sort of swindler or the like before swearing her soul over to the 어둠의 존재. Sometimes she and 엘레인 just did not know the questions to ask. 모그헤디엔 seldom volunteered anything, that was certain. Even so, they had learned a great deal, and passed most on to the 에스 세다이. As results of their researches and studies as 허락받은 자, of course. They had gained a lot of credit.

She and 엘레인 would have kept knowledge of her to themselves if they could, but 비르기테 had known from the start, and 시우안 and 리안 had to be told. 시우안 had known enough of the circumstances that led to 모그헤디엔’s capture to demand a full explanation, and had the leverage to obtain one. 니나브 and 엘레인 knew some of 시우안 and 리안’s secrets; they seemed to know all of her and 엘레인’s except the truth about 비르기테. It made for a precarious balance, with the advantage to 시우안 and 리안. Besides, bits of 모그헤디엔’s revelations concerned supposed Darkfriend plots and hints of what the other 버림받은 자들 might be up to. The only way to pass those on was to make them seem to have come from 시우안 and 리안’s agents. Nothing about the 흑색 아자—hidden deep and long denied—though that interested 시우안 most. 어둠의 친구들 disgusted her, but the very idea of 에스 세다이 swearing themselves to the 어둠의 존재 was enough to screw 시우안’s anger to an icy rage. 모그헤디엔 claimed to have been afraid to go near *any* 에스 세다이, and that was believable enough. Fear was a permanent part of the woman. No wonder she had hidden in the shadows enough to be called the Spider. All in all, she was a treasure trove too valuable to give to the headsman, yet most 에스 세다이 would not see it so. Most 에스 세다이 might refuse to touch or trust anything learned from her.

Guilt and revulsion stabbed 니나브, not for the first time. Could any amount of knowledge justify keeping one of the 버림받은 자들 from justice? Turning her in meant punishment, probably dreadful, for everyone involved, not just herself, but 엘레인 and 시우안 and 리안. Turning her in meant 비르기테’s secret would come out. And all that knowledge lost. 모그헤디엔 might know nothing of 치유, but she had given 니나브 a dozen hints of what was possible, and there had to be more in her head. With those to guide her, what might she discover eventually?

니나브 wanted a bath, and it had nothing to do with the heat. “We will talk about the weather,” she said bitterly.

“You know more about controlling weather than I do.” 모그헤디엔 sounded weary, and an echo slid through the bracelet. There had been enough questions on the subject. “All I know is that what is happening is the Great—the 어둠의 존재’s work.” She had the nerve to smile ingratiatingly at the slip. “No mere human is strong enough to change that.”
It took effort for 니나브 not to grind her teeth. 엘레인 knew more about working weather than anyone else in Salidar, and she said the same. Including the 어둠의 존재 part, though any but a fool would know that, with the heat so strong when it should be coming on for snow, with no rain and the streams drying. “Then we’ll talk about using different weaves to Heal different illnesses.” The woman said that took more time than what was done now, but all the strength for it came from the Power, not from the patient and the woman channeling. Of course, she said *men* had actually been better at some kinds of 치유, and 니나브 was not about to believe that. “You must have seen it done at least once.”

She settled down to bore away for nuggets in the dross. Some knowledge was worth a great deal. She just wished she did not feel that she was digging through slime.

엘레인 did not hesitate once she was outside, only waved to 비르기테 and went on. 비르기테, her golden hair in an intricate waist-long braid, was playing with two small boys while she kept watch in the narrow alley, her bow propped against a leaning fence beside her. Or trying to play with them. Jaril and Seve stared at the woman in her odd wide yellow trousers and short dark coat, but they showed no more reaction than that. They never did, and they never spoke. They were supposed to be “Marigan’s” children. 비르기테 was happy playing with them, and a touch sad; she always liked playing with children, especially little boys, and she always felt that way when she did. 엘레인 knew it as well as she knew her own feelings.

If she had thought 모그헤디엔 had anything to do with their condition. . . . But the woman claimed they were as they had been when she picked them up for her disguise in 게알단, orphans in the street, and some of the Yellow sisters said they had simply seen too much in the riots in Samara. 엘레인 could believe it from what she herself had encountered there. The Yellow sisters said time and care would help them; 엘레인 hoped it was so. She hoped she was not allowing the one responsible to escape justice.

Reminding her that he sat on the Emond’s Field Village Council and so was a man of influence, due respect. And playing for sympathy with that staff; the thatcher was as spry as anyone half his age. He wanted something. “What do you bring me today, Master Buie?”

Cenn straightened, forgetting to prop himself up with his stick. And forgetting to keep the acrid note out of his voice. “It’s all these outlanders flooding in, bringing all sorts of things we don’t want here.” He seemed to have forgotten she was an outlander, too; most 두 강 folks had. “Strange ways, my Lady. Indecent clothes. You’ll be hearing from the women about the way those 도마니 hussies dress, if you haven’t already.” She had, as it happened, from some of them, though a momentary gleam in Cenn’s eye said he would regret it if she gave in to their demands. “Strangers stealing the food from our mouths, taking away our trade. That 타라본er fellow and his fool tile-making, for example. Taking up hands that could be put to useful work. He doesn’t care about good 두 강 people. Why, he. . . .”

Fanning herself, she stopped listening while giving every appearance of paying close attention; it was a skill her father had taught her, necessary at times like this. Of course. Master Hornval’s roof tiles would compete with Cenn’s thatchwork.

Not everyone felt as Cenn did about the newcomers. Haral Luhhan, the Emond’s Field blacksmith, had gone into partnership with a 도마니 cutler and a whitesmith from Almoth Plain, and Master Aydaer had hired three men and two women who knew furniture making and carving, and gilding as well, though there certainly was no gold lying about for that. Her chair and 페린’s were their work, and as fine as she had seen anywhere. For that matter, Cenn himself had taken on half a dozen helpers, and not all 두 강 folk; a good many roofs had burned when the 트롤록s came, and new houses were going up everywhere. 페린 had no right to make her listen to this nonsense alone.

The people of the 두 강 might have proclaimed him their lord—as well they might after he led them to victory over the 트롤록s—and he might be beginning to realize he could not change that—as he certainly should, when they bowed and called him Lord 페린 to his face right after he told them not to—yet he dug in his heels at the trappings that went with being a lord, all the things that people *expected* from their lords and ladies. Worse, he balked at the duties of a lord. 파일 knew those things exactly, as the eldest surviving child of 다브람 t’Ghaline 바쉐어, Lord of 바쉐어, Tyr and Sidona, Guardian of the 황무지border, Defender of the Heartland, Marshal-General to Queen Tenobia of 살다에아. True, she had run away to become a Hunter for the Horn—and then given that up for a husband, which sometimes still stunned her—but she remembered. 페린 listened when she explained, and even nodded his head in the proper places, but trying to make him actually do any of it was like trying to make a horse dance the sa’sara.

Cenn finally ran down in splutters, only just remembering to swallow the invective that bubbled behind his teeth.

“페린 and I chose to use thatch,” 파일 said calmly. While Cenn was still nodding in self-satisfaction, she added, “You haven’t finished it, yet.” He gave a start. “You seem to have taken on more roofs than you can handle, Master Buie. If ours isn’t done soon, I fear we will have to ask Master Hornval about his tiles.” Cenn’s mouth worked in vigorous silence; if she put a tile roof on the manor, others would follow. “I have enjoyed your discourse, but I am sure you would rather finish my roof than waste time in idle conversation, however pleasant.”

Lips thinning, Cenn glowered for a moment, then made a sketchy bow. Muttering something unintelligible except for a strangled “my Lady” at the end, he stalked out thumping the bare floor with his stick. The things people found to waste her time. 페린 was going to do his share of this if she had to tie him hand and foot.

The rest were not so provoking. A once-stout woman, her patched flower-embroidered dress hanging on her like a sack, who had come all the way from Toman Head, beyond Almoth Plain, wanted to deal in herbs and cures. Hulking Jon Ayellin rubbing his bald head and skinny Thad Torfinn twisting the lapels of his coat, disputing the boundaries of their fields. Two dark 도마니 men in long leather vests, with close-trimmed beards, miners who thought they had seen signs of gold and silver nearby on their way through the mountains. And iron, though they were less interested in that. And finally, a wiry 타라본er, a transparent veil across her narrow face and her pale hair in a multitude of thin braids, who claimed to have been a master carpetweaver and to know the making of rug looms.

The woman with an interest in herbs 파일 directed to the local Women’s Circle; if Espara Soman knew what she was about, they would find her a place under one of the village Wisdoms. With all the new people coming in, many in a bad way from the journey, not a Wisdom in the 두 강 but had an apprentice or two, and all were on the lookout for more. Maybe not exactly what Espara wanted, but where she would have to start. A few questions made it plain that neither Thad nor Jon really remembered where the boundary lay—apparently they had been arguing it since before she was born—so she directed them to split the difference. Which seemed to be what each had thought the Village Council would decide, the reason for keeping the argument between themselves so long.

The others she granted the permission they sought. They did not really need permission, but it was best to let them know where authority lay from the start. In return for her consent and enough silver to buy supplies, 파일 made the two 도마니 agree to give 페린 a tenth part of what they found, as well as to locate the iron mentioned in passing. 페린 would not like it, but the 두 강 had nothing like taxes, and a lord was expected to do things and provide things that required money. And the iron would be as useful as the gold. As for Liale Mosrara, if the 타라본er claimed more skill than she had, her enterprise would not last long, but if she did. . . . Three clothweavers already ensured that the merchants would find more than raw wool when they came down from Baerlon next year, and decent carpets would be another trade item to bring in more coin. Liale promised the first and finest from her looms to the manor, and 파일 nodded a gracious acceptance of the gift; she could give more if and when the carpets appeared. The floors did need covering. All in all, everyone seemed reasonably satisfied. Even Jon and Thad.

As the 타라본er woman backed away curtsying, 파일 stood, glad to be done, then stopped when four women entered through one of the doorways that flanked the far fireplace, all sweating in dark stout 두 강 woolens. 데이즈 콩가르, as tall as most men and wider, overtopped the other Wisdoms and thrust herself forward to take the lead here on the outskirts of her own village. Edelle Gaelin, from Watch Hill, gray-braided and slender, made it plain with her straight back and stiff face that she thought she should have Daise’s place, by virtue of age and her long time in office if no other reason. Elwinn Taron, the Wisdom of Deven Ride, was the shortest, a round woman with a pleasant motherly smile that she wore even when she was making people do what they did not want to. The last, Milla al’Azar, from Taren Ferry, trailed behind; the youngest, almost young enough to be Edelle’s daughter, she always appeared uncertain around the others.

파일 remained standing, fanning herself slowly. She truly wished 페린 there, now. Very much. These women had as much authority in their villages as the mayor—sometimes, in some ways, more—and they had to be handled carefully, with due dignity and respect. That made matters difficult. They turned into simpering girls around 페린, eager to please, but with her. . . . The 두 강 had had no nobles in centuries; they had not seen so much as a representative of the Queen in Caemlyn for seven generations. Everyone was still working out how to behave toward a lord and a lady, including these four. Sometimes they forgot she was the Lady 파일 and saw only a young woman whose marriage Daise had presided over just a few months ago. They could be all curtsies and “yes, of course, my Lady,” and right in the middle of it tell her exactly what to do about something without seeing anything at all incongruous. *You are not going to leave this to me anymore, 페린*.

They curtsied now, with varying degrees of skill, and said, “빛 shine on you, my Lady,” on top of one another.

Amenities out of the way, Daise started in before she was completely upright again. “Three more boys have run off, my Lady.” Her tone fell halfway between the respect of the words and the now-you-listen-to-me-young-woman she sometimes used. “Dav Ayellin, Ewin Finngar, and Elam Dowtry. Run off to see the world because of Lord 페린’s stories about what’s out there.”

파일 blinked in surprise. Those three were hardly boys. Dav and Elam were as old as 페린, and Ewin not really that much younger than she herself. And 페린’s stories, which he told seldom and reluctantly, were hardly the only way 두 강 youths learned about the outside world now. “I could ask 페린 to speak to you, if you wish.”

They stirred, Daise looking for him expectantly, Edelle and Milla automatically smoothing their skirts, Elwinn just as unconsciously drawing her braid over her shoulder and arranging it carefully. Abruptly they realized what they were doing and froze, not looking at one another. Or at her. The one advantage 파일 had with them was that they knew the effect her husband had on them. So many times she had seen one or another firm herself up after meeting with 페린, plainly vowing not to let it happen again; so many times she had seen resolution fly out the window at a sight of him. None was really sure whether she preferred to deal with him or with her.

“That will not be necessary,” Edelle said after a moment. “Boys running off are a bother, but only a bother.” Her tone had slid a little further from “my Lady” than Daise’s, and plump Elwinn added a smile suitable for mother to young daughter.

“As long as we’re here, my dear, we really might as well mention something else. Water. You see, some of the people are worried.”

“It hasn’t rained in months,” Edelle added, and Daise nodded.

This time 파일 did blink. They were too intelligent to think 페린 could do anything about that. “The springs are all still flowing, and 페린 has ordered more wells dug.” Actually he had only suggested it, but it had come to the same thing, fortunately. “And long before planting time, the irrigation canals from the Waterwood will be done.” That was her doing; half the fields in 살다에아 were irrigated, but no one here had ever heard of the practice. “Anyway, the rains have to come sooner or later. The canals are only in case.” Daise nodded again, slowly, and Elwinn and Edelle. But they knew all this as well as she.

“It isn’t the rain,” Milla muttered. “Not exactly, anyway. It isn’t natural. You see, none of us can Listen to the Wind.” She hunched her shoulders under the others’ sudden frowns. Plainly she was saying too much, and giving away secrets besides. Supposedly all the Wisdoms could predict the weather by Listening to the Wind; at least, they said that they all could. But even so Milla plowed on doggedly. “Well, we can’t! We look at clouds instead, and how the birds behave, and the ants and caterpillars and. . . .” Drawing a deep breath, she straightened, but still avoided the other Wisdoms’ eyes. 파일 wondered how she managed to deal with the Women’s Circle in Taren Ferry, much less the Village Council. Of course, they were as new at it as Milla; that village had lost its whole population when the 트롤록s came, and everyone there now was new. “It isn’t natural, my Lady. The first snows should have been here weeks ago, but it might as well be the middle of summer. We’re not worried, my Lady, we’re frightened! If nobody else will admit it, I will. I lie awake most nights. I haven’t slept properly in a month, and. . . .” She trailed off, color blooming in her face as she realized she might have gone too far. A Wisdom was supposed to be in control in all times; she did not run around saying she was frightened.

The others shifted their gazes from Milla to 파일. They said nothing, faces expressionless enough for 에스 세다이.

파일 understood, now. Milla had spoken simple truth. The weather was *not* natural; it was most *un*natural. 파일 often lay awake herself, praying for rain, or better still snow, trying not to think of what lurked behind the heat and drought.
