The 안도르ans did their best to ignore her too, but their pointed looks elsewhere made the attempts glaring failures. Enaila walked away as if they were invisible.

The silence lasted just moments. “My Lord Dragon is wise,” Lord Lir said with a small bow and a slight frown. The High Seat of House Baryn was blade-slender and blade-strong in a yellow coat adorned with gold braid, but too smoothly unctuous, too smooth altogether. Nothing but those occasional frowns ever sullied that surface, as if he was unaware of them, yet he was hardly the only one to give 랜드 strange looks. They all looked at the 용의 환생 in their midst with wondering disbelief sometimes. “One’s enemies usually do work together sooner or later. One must identify them before they have the chance to.”

More praise for 랜드’s wisdom flowed from Lord Henren, blocky, bald and hard-eyed, and from gray-curled Lady Carlys, with her open face and devious mind, from plump giggly Daerilla, and thin-lipped nervous Elegar, and nearly a dozen others who had held their tongues while those more powerful spoke.

The lesser lords and ladies fell silent as soon as Elenia opened her mouth once more. “There is always the difficulty of knowing your enemies before they make themselves known. It is often too late, then.” Her husband nodded sagely.

“I always say,” Naean announced, “that who does not support me, opposes me. I’ve found it a good rule. Those who hang back may be waiting until your back is turned to plant a dagger.”

This was hardly the first time they had tried to secure their own places by casting suspicion on any lord or lady not standing with them, but 랜드 wished he could stop them short of telling them to stop. Their attempts to play the Game of Houses were feeble compared to the sly maneuverings of 케렌인, or even 타이런s, and they were irritating besides, but there were thoughts he did not want them to have yet. Surprisingly, aid came from white-haired Lord Nasin, the High Seat of House Caeren.

“Another Jearom,” the man said, an obsequious smile awkward on his gaunt, narrow face. He drew exasperated looks, even from some of the minor nobles before they caught themselves. Nasin had been a little addled since the events surrounding 랜드’s coming to Caemlyn. Instead of the Star and Sword of his House, Nasin’s pale blue lapels were incongruously worked with flowers, moondrops and loversknots, and he sometimes wore a flower in his thinning hair like a country youth going courting. House Caeren was too powerful for even Jarid or Naean to push him aside, though. Nasin’s head bobbed on a scrawny neck. “Your bladework is spectacular, my Lord Dragon. You are another Jearom.”

“Why?” The word cut across the courtyard, souring the 안도르ans’ faces.

다브람 바쉐어 was certainly no 안도르an, with his tilted, almost black eyes, a hooked beak of a nose, and thick gray-streaked mustaches curving down like horns around his wide mouth. He was slender, little taller than Enaila, in a short gray coat embroidered with silver on cuffs and lapels, and baggy trousers tucked into boots turned down at the knee. Where the 안도르ans had stood to watch, the Marshal-General of 살다에아 had had a gilded chair dragged to the courtyard, and sprawled in it with a leg over one of its arms, ring-quilloned sword twisted so the hilt sat in easy reach. Sweat glistened on his dark face, but he paid it as little mind as he did the 안도르ans.

“What do you mean?” 랜드 demanded.

“All this sword practice,” 바쉐어 said easily. “And with five men? No one exercises against five. It’s foolish. Sooner or later your brains will be spilled on the ground in a melee like that, even with practice swords, and to no purpose.”

랜드’s jaw tightened. “Jearom once defeated ten.”

Shifting in his chair, 바쉐어 laughed. “Do you think you’ll live long enough to equal the greatest swordsman in history?” An angry mutter came from the 안도르ans—feigned anger, 랜드 was sure—but 바쉐어 ignored it. “You are who you are, after all.” Suddenly he moved like an uncoiling spring; the dagger drawn while shifting flashed toward 랜드’s heart.

랜드 did not move a muscle. Instead he seized *세이딘*, the male half of the True Source; it took no more thought than breathing. *Saidin* flooded into him, carrying the 어둠의 존재’s taint, an avalanche of foul ice, a torrent of reeking molten metal. It tried to crush him, to scour him away, and he rode it like a man balancing atop a collapsing mountain. He channeled, a simple weave of Air that wrapped up the dagger and stopped it an arm’s length from his chest. Emptiness surrounded him; he floated in the middle of it, in the Void, thought and emotion distant.

“Die!” Jarid shouted, drawing his sword as he ran toward 바쉐어. Lir and Henren and Elegar and every 안도르an lord had his sword out, even Nasin, though he looked about to drop his. The Maidens had wrapped their *shoufa* around their heads, black veils coming up to cover their faces to blue or green eyes as they raised long-pointed spears; 아일 always veiled before killing.

“Stop!” 랜드 barked, and everyone froze in their tracks, the 안도르ans blinking in confusion, the Maidens simply poised on their toes. 바쉐어 had not moved again beyond settling back into the chair, his leg still hooked over the arm.

Plucking the horn-hilted dagger from the air with one hand, 랜드 let go of the Source. Even with the taint twisting his belly, the taint that eventually destroyed men who channeled, letting go was difficult. With *세이딘* in him, he saw more clearly, heard more sharply. It was a paradox he did not understand, but when he was floating in that seemingly endless Void, somehow buffered against bodily feeling and emotions, every sense was magnified; without it he felt only half-alive. And some of the taint seemed to remain behind, but not the mitigating glory of *세이딘*. The deadly glory that would kill him if he wavered an inch in the struggle with it.

Turning the dagger in his hands, he walked slowly to 바쉐어. “Had I been an eyeblink slower,” he said softly, “I’d be dead. I could kill you where you sit and no law in 안도르 or anywhere else would say me wrong.” He was ready to do it, he realized. Cold rage had replaced *세이딘*. A few weeks’ acquaintance did not cover this.

The 살다에안’s tilted eyes were as calm as if he lolled in his own home. “My wife would not like that. Nor you, for that matter. 데이라 would probably take command and set out hunting 타임 again. She doesn’t approve of my agreement to follow you.”

랜드 shook his head slightly, the edge of his anger dulled a little by the man’s composure. And his words. It had been a surprise to learn that among 바쉐어’s nine thousand 살다에안 horse all of the nobles had brought their wives, and most of the other officers as well. 랜드 did not understand how a man could take his wife into danger, but it was traditional in 살다에아, except when campaigning into the 황무지.

He avoided looking at the Maidens. They were warriors to their toenails, but women, too. And he had promised not to keep them from danger, even death. He had made no promise not to flinch at it, though, and it ripped at him inside when he had to, but he kept his promises. He did what he had to do even when he hated himself for it.

With a sigh he tossed the dagger aside. “Your question,” he said politely. “Why?”

“Because you are who you are,” 바쉐어 said plainly. “Because you—and those men you’re gathering, I suppose—are what you are.” 랜드 heard feet shuffling behind him; for all they tried to, the 안도르ans could never hide their horror at his amnesty. “You can do what you did with the dagger every time,” 바쉐어 went on, putting his raised boot down and leaning forward, “but for any assassin to reach you, he has to get past your 아일. And my horsemen, for that matter. Bah! If anything gets close to you, it won’t be human.” Throwing his hands wide, he settled back again. “Well, if you want to practice the sword, do it. A man needs exercise, and relaxation. But don’t get your skull split open. Too much depends on you, and I don’t see any 에스 세다이 around to Heal you.” His mustache almost hid his sudden grin. “Besides, if you die, I don’t think our 안도르an friends will maintain their warm welcome for me and my men.”

The 안도르ans had put up their swords, but their eyes remained on 바쉐어 malevolently. Nothing to do with how close he had come to killing 랜드. Usually they kept their faces smooth around 바쉐어, for all he was a foreign general with a foreign army on 안도르an soil. The 용의 환생 wanted 바쉐어 there, and this lot would have smiled at a 미르드랄 if the 용의 환생 wanted it. But if 랜드 might turn on him. . . . No need to hide anything then. They were vultures who had been ready to feed on 모르가세 before she died, and they would feed on 바쉐어 given half a chance. And on 랜드. He could hardly wait to be rid of them.

*The only way to live is to die*. The thought came into his head suddenly. He had been told that once, in such a way he had to believe it, but the thought was not his. *I must die. I deserve only death*. He turned away from 바쉐어 clutching at his head.

바쉐어 was out of his chair in an instant, clutching 랜드’s shoulder though it was head high to him. “What is the matter? Did that blow really crack your head?”

“I am fine.” 랜드 pulled his hands down; there was never any pain in this, only the shock of having another man’s thoughts in his head. 바쉐어 was not the only one watching. Most of the Maidens were eyeing him as closely as they did the courtyard, especially Enaila and yellow-haired Somara, the tallest of them. Those two would probably bring him some sort of herb tea as soon as their duties were done, and stand over him till he drank it. Elenia and Naean and the rest of the 안도르ans were breathing hard, clutching at coats and skirts, studying 랜드 with the wide-eyed fear of people afraid they might be seeing the first signs of madness. “I am fine,” he told the courtyard. Only the Maidens relaxed, and Enaila and Somara not very far.

아일 did not care about “the 용의 환생”; to them 랜드 was the *Car’a’carn*, prophesied to unite them, and to break them. They took it in stride, though they worried about it too, and they seemed to take his channeling in stride as well, and everything that might go with it. The others—*The wetlanders*, he thought dryly—called him the 용의 환생, and never speculated on what that meant. They believed he was the rebirth of 르웨어스 테린 Telamon, the Dragon, the man who had sealed the hole into the 어둠의 존재’s prison and ended the 그림자 전쟁 three thousand years ago and more. Ended the 전설의 시대 as well, when the 어둠의 존재’s last counterstroke tainted *세이딘*, and every man who could channel began to go insane, starting with 르웨어스 테린 himself and his Hundred Companions. They called 랜드 the 용의 환생, and never suspected that some part of 르웨어스 테린 Telamon might be inside his head, as mad as the day he had begun the Time of 광기 and the 세계의 파멸, as mad as any of those male 에스 세다이 who had changed the face of the world beyond recognition. It had come on him slowly, but the more 랜드 learned of the 하나의 힘, the stronger he became with *세이딘*, the stronger 르웨어스 테린’s voice became, and the harder 랜드 had to fight to keep a dead man’s thoughts from taking him over. That was one reason why he liked sword practice; the absence of thought was a barrier to keep him himself.

“We need to find an 에스 세다이,” 바쉐어 muttered. “If those rumors are true. . . . 빛 burn my eyes, I wish we had never let that one leave.”

A good many people had fled Caemlyn in the days after 랜드 and the 아일 seized the city; the Palace itself nearly emptied overnight. There were people 랜드 would liked to have found, people who had helped him, but they had all vanished. Some still slipped away. One fleeing in those first days had been a young 에스 세다이, young enough that her face still lacked the distinctive agelessness. 바쉐어’s men sent word when they found her at an inn, but when she found out who 랜드 was, she ran screaming. Literally screaming. He never even learned her name or 아자. Rumor said another was somewhere in the city, but a hundred rumors were loose in Caemlyn now, a thousand, each less likely than the next. Definitely unlikely any would lead to an 에스 세다이. 아일 patrols had spotted several passing Caemlyn by, each plainly going somewhere in a hurry and none with any intention of entering a city occupied by the 용의 환생.

“Could I trust any 에스 세다이?” 랜드 asked. “It was just a headache. My head isn’t hard enough not to ache a little when it’s hit.”

바쉐어 snorted hard enough to stir his thick mustaches. “However hard your head is, sooner or later you’ll have to trust 에스 세다이. Without them, you’ll never bring all the nations behind you short of conquest. People look for such things. However many of the Prophecies they hear you’ve fulfilled, many will wait for the 에스 세다이 to put their stamp on you.”

“I won’t avoid fighting anyway, and you know it,” 랜드 said. “The 백의단 aren’t likely to welcome me into 아마디시아 even if 아일론 agrees, and 사마엘 certainly won’t give up 일리안 without a fight.” *사마엘 and 라빈 and 모그헤디엔 and*. . . . Harshly he forced the thought from his consciousness. It was not easy. They came without warning, and it was never easy.

A thump made him look over his shoulder. Arymilla lay in a heap on the paving stones. Karind was kneeling to pull her skirts down over her ankles and chafe her wrists. Elegar swayed as though he might join Arymilla in a moment, and neither Nasin nor Elenia appeared in much better state. Most of the rest looked ready to sick up. Mention of the 버림받은 자들 could do that, especially since 랜드 had told them that Lord Gaebril really had been 라빈. He was not sure how much they believed, but just considering the possibility was enough to unhinge the knees of most. Their shock was why they were still alive. Had he believed they had served knowingly. . . . *No*, he thought. *If they’d known, if they were all 어둠의 친구들, you’d still use them*. Sometimes he was so sick of himself that he really was ready to die.

At least he was telling the truth. The 에스 세다이 were all dying to keep it secret, the 버림받은 자들 being free; they feared that knowing would just bring more chaos and panic. 랜드 was trying to spread the truth. People might panic, but they would have time to recover. The 에스 세다이 way, knowledge and panic might come too late for recovery. Besides, people had a right to know what they faced.

“일리안 won’t hold out long,” 바쉐어 said. 랜드’s head whipped back around, but 바쉐어 was too old a campaigner to speak of what he should not where others could hear. He was just taking the talk away from the 버림받은 자들. Though if the 버림받은 자들, or anything else, made 다브람 바쉐어 nervous, 랜드 had not seen it yet. “일리안 will crack like a nut hit by a hammer.”

“You and 맷 worked out a good plan.” The basic idea had been 랜드’s, but 맷 and 바쉐어 had provided the thousand details that would make it work. 맷 more than 바쉐어.

“An interesting young fellow, 맷 카우톤,” 바쉐어 mused. “I look forward to speaking with him again. He never would say who he studied under. Agelmar Jagad? I hear you’ve both been to 시엔나르.” 랜드 said nothing. 맷’s secrets were his own; 랜드 was not really sure what they were himself. 바쉐어 tilted his head, scratched at a mustache with one finger. “He’s young to have studied under anyone. No older than you. Did he find a library somewhere? I would like to see the books he’s read.”

“You’ll have to ask him,” 랜드 said. “I don’t know.” He supposed 맷 had to have read a book sometime, somewhere, but 맷 did not have much interest in books.

바쉐어 only nodded. When 랜드 did not want to talk about something, 바쉐어 usually let it alone. Usually. “The next time you jaunt off to 케렌, why don’t you bring back the Green sister who’s there? 에그웨인 Sedai? I’ve heard the 아일 speak of her; they say she’s from your home village, too. You could trust her, couldn’t you?”

“에그웨인 has other duties,” 랜드 laughed. A Green sister. If 바쉐어 only knew.

Somara appeared at 랜드’s side with his linen shirt and his coat, a fine red wool cut in the 안도르an style, with dragons on the long collar and laurel leaves thick on the lapels and climbing the sleeves. She was tall even for an 아일 woman, maybe not quite a hand shorter than he. Like the other Maidens, she had lowered her veil, but the gray-brown *shoufa* still hid all but her face. “The *Car’a’carn* will catch a chill,” she murmured.

He doubted it. The 아일 might find this heat nothing out of the ordinary, but already sweat streamed down him nearly as hard as while working the sword. Still, he pulled the shirt over his head and tucked it in, though leaving the laces undone, then shrugged into the coat. He did not think Somara would actually try to put the clothes on him, not in front of others, but this way he would avoid lectures from her and Enaila, and very likely some of the others, along with the herb tea.

To most 아일 he was the *Car’a’carn*, and so it was with the Maidens. In public. Alone with these women who had chosen to reject marriage and the hearth in favor of the spear, matters became more complicated. He supposed he could stop it—maybe—but he owed it to them not to. Some had already died for him, and more would—he had promised, the Light burn him for it!—and if he could let them do that, he could let them do the rest. Sweat soaked through the shirt immediately and began making dark patches on the coat.
“You need the 에스 세다이, al’Thor.” 랜드 hoped 바쉐어 was half this dogged when it came to fighting; that was the man’s reputation, but he had only reputation and a few weeks to go by. “You can’t afford to have them against you, and if they don’t at least think they have a few strings tied to you, they might go that way. 에스 세다이 are tricksome; no man can know what they’ll do or why.”

“What if I tell you there are hundreds of 에스 세다이 ready to support me?” 랜드 was aware of the 안도르ans listening; he had to be careful not to say too much. Not that he knew much. What he did know was probably exaggeration and hope. He certainly doubted the “hundreds,” whatever 에그웨인 hinted.

바쉐어’s eyes narrowed. “If there’s been an embassy from the Tower, I would know, so. . . .” His voice dropped to a near whisper. “The split? The Tower has really *split*?” He sounded as if he could not believe the words coming out of his own mouth. Everyone knew 시우안 산체 had been deposed from the 아미를린 석좌 and stilled—and executed, so rumor ran—yet to most people a division in the Tower was only conjecture, and few truly believed. The 백색 탑 had remained whole, a monolith towering over thrones, for three thousand years. But the 살다에안 was a man who considered all possibilities. He went on in a true whisper, stepping close so the 안도르ans could not overhear. “It must be the rebels ready to support you. You could strike a better deal with them—they’ll need you as much as you need them, maybe more—but rebels, even 에스 세다이 rebels, won’t carry nearly the weight of the 백색 탑, certainly not with any crown. Commoners might not know the difference, but kings and queens will.”

“They’re still 에스 세다이,” 랜드 said just as quietly, “whoever they are.” *And wherever they are*, he thought dryly. *에스 세다이 . . . Servants of All . . . the Hall of the Servants is broken . . . broken forever . . . broken . . . 일레나, my love*. . . . Ruthlessly he quashed 르웨어스 테린’s thoughts. Sometimes they had actually been a help, giving him information he needed, but they were growing too strong. If he did have an 에스 세다이 there—a Yellow; they knew the most of 치유—perhaps she. . . . There had been one 에스 세다이 he trusted, though not until shortly before her death, and 모이라인 had left him a piece of advice about 에스 세다이, about every other woman who wore the shawl and the ring. “I’ll never trust any 에스 세다이,” he rasped softly. “I will use them, because I do need them, but Tower or rebel, I know they’ll try to use me, because that is what 에스 세다이 do. I’ll never trust them, 바쉐어.”

The 살다에안 nodded slowly. “Then use them, if you can. But remember this. No one resists for long going the way the 에스 세다이 want.” Abruptly he barked a short laugh. “아투르 호크윙 was the last, so far as I know. 빛 burn my eyes, maybe you’ll be the second.”

The scrape of boots announced an arrival in the courtyard, one of 바쉐어’s men, a heavy-shouldered, hatchet-nosed young fellow a head taller than his general, with a luxuriant black beard as well as thick mustaches. He walked like a man more used to a saddle under him than his own feet, but he handled the sword at his hip smoothly as he bowed. To 바쉐어, more than to 랜드. 바쉐어 might follow the 용의 환생, but Tumad—랜드 thought that was his name; Tumad Ahzkan—followed 바쉐어. Enaila and three other Maidens fastened their eyes on the new 살다에안; they did not really trust any wetlander around the *Car’a’carn*.

“There is a man has presented himself at the gates,” Tumad said uneasily. “He says. . . . It is 마즈림 타임, my Lord 바쉐어.”

**CHAPTER** **2**

![](images/00051.jpg)

*A New Arrival*

마즈림 타임. Before 랜드, other men through the centuries had claimed to be the 용의 환생. The last few years before 랜드 had seen a plague of false 용, some of whom could actually channel. 마즈림 타임 was one of those, raising an army and ravaging 살다에아 before he was taken. 바쉐어’s face did not change, but he gripped his sword hilt white-knuckle hard, and Tumad was looking at him for orders. 타임’s escape, on the way to 타르 발론 to be gentled, was the reason 바쉐어 had come to 안도르 in the first place. That was how much 살다에아 feared and hated 마즈림 타임; Queen Tenobia had sent 바쉐어 with an army to pursue the man wherever he went, however long it took, to make sure 타임 never troubled 살다에아 again.

The Maidens merely stood calmly, but that name burst among the 안도르ans like a torch tossed in dry grass. Arymilla was just being helped to her feet, yet her eyes rolled up in her head again; she would have gone down in a heap once more if Karind had not eased her to the paving stones. Elegar staggered back among the columns and bent over, retching loudly. The rest were all gasps and panic, pressing handkerchiefs to mouths and clutching at sword hilts. Even stolid Karind licked her lips nervously.

랜드 took his hand away from his coat pocket. “The amnesty,” he said, and both 살다에안s gave him a long flat look.

“What if he has not come for your amnesty?” 바쉐어 said after a moment. “What if he still claims to be the 용의 환생?” Feet shuffled among the 안도르ans; no one wanted to be within miles of where the 하나의 힘 might be used in a duel.

“If he thinks that,” 랜드 said firmly, “I will disabuse him.” He had the rarest sort of *angreal* in his pocket, one made for men, a carving of a fat little man with a sword. However strong 타임 might be, he could not stand up to that. “But if he has come for the amnesty, it is his, the same as any other.” Whatever 타임 had done in 살다에아, he could not afford to turn away a man who could channel, a man who would not have to be taught from the first steps. He needed such a man. He would turn away no one except one of the 버림받은 자들, not unless he was forced to. *디만드레드 and 사마엘, 세미르하제 and 메사나, 아스모데안 and*. . . . 랜드 forced 르웨어스 테린 down; he could not afford distractions now.

Again 바쉐어 paused before speaking, but finally he nodded and let go of his sword. “Your amnesty holds, of course. But mark me, al’Thor. If 타임 ever sets foot in 살다에아 again, he will not live to leave. There are too many memories. No command I give—nor Tenobia herself—will stop it.”

“I will keep him out of 살다에아.” Either 타임 had come here to submit to him, or else it was going to be necessary to kill him. Unconsciously 랜드 touched his pocket, pressing the fat little man through the wool. “Let’s have him in here.”

Tumad eyed 바쉐어, but 바쉐어’s short nod came so quickly that it seemed Tumad bowed in response to the spoken command. Irritation flashed in 랜드, but he said nothing, and Tumad hurried away in that slightly rolling walk. 바쉐어 folded his arms across his chest and stood with one knee bent, a portrait of a man at his ease. Those dark tilted eyes, fixed on the way Tumad had gone, made it a portrait of a man waiting to kill something.

The scuffling of feet started again among the 안도르ans, hesitant half-steps away then pulling back. Their breathing sounded as though they had run miles.

“You may leave,” 랜드 told them.

“I for one will stand at your shoulder,” Lir began just as Naean said sharply, “I will not run before—”

랜드 cut them both off. “Go!”

They wanted to show him they were unafraid, even if they were ready to soil themselves; they wanted to run, abandoning what dignity they had not already tossed at his feet. It was a simple choice. He was the 용의 환생, and currying favor meant obedience, and obedience in this case meant doing what they truly wanted. A flurry of extravagant bows and deep skirt-spreading curtsies, hurried murmurs of “By your leave, my Lord Dragon” and “As you command, my Lord Dragon,” and they were . . . not exactly scurrying out, but walking as quickly as they could manage without appearing to scurry. In the opposite direction from that in which Tumad had gone; no doubt they did not want to risk a chance encounter with 마즈림 타임 on his way in.

The waiting stretched out in the heat—it took time to bring a man through the sprawling corridors from the Palace gates—but once the 안도르ans were gone no one moved. 바쉐어 kept his gaze steady on the place 타임 would appear. The Maidens watched everywhere, but they always did, and if they looked ready to veil themselves again in an instant, they always did that too. Except for their eyes, they could have been statues.

Finally the sound of boots echoed into the courtyard. 랜드 almost reached out for *세이딘*, then held back. The man would be able to tell he held the Power as soon as he entered the court; 랜드 could not afford to appear afraid of him.

Tumad emerged into the sunlight first, then a black-haired man of well above average height whose dark face and tilted eyes, hooked nose and high cheekbones, marked him another 살다에안, though he was clean-shaven and garbed like a once prosperous 안도르an merchant lately fallen on hard times. His dark blue coat had been of fine wool trimmed in darker velvet, but wear had made the cuffs ragged, his breeches bagged at the knee, and dust coated his cracked boots. Still, he walked proudly, no mean feat with four more of 바쉐어’s men behind him, those almost straight, slightly serpentine blades bare and the points inches from his ribs. The heat hardly seemed to touch him. The Maidens’ eyes followed his progress.

랜드 studied 타임 as the man and his escort crossed the courtyard. At least fifteen years older than himself; thirty-five, then, or a few years more at most. Little was known and less written of men who could channel—it was a subject most decent people avoided—but 랜드 had learned what he could. Relatively few men actually sought it out; that was one of 랜드’s problems. Since the Breaking, most men who channeled had the ability born in them, ready to spring out as they grew into manhood. Some managed to keep madness at bay for years before 에스 세다이 found and gentled them; others were already hopelessly mad when found, at times less than a year after first touching *세이딘*. 랜드 had clung to sanity for close to two years, so far. Yet in front of him he had a man who must have managed it for ten or fifteen. That alone was worth something.

They halted a few paces before him at a gesture from Tumad. 랜드 opened his mouth, but before he could speak, 르웨어스 테린 rose up in a frenzy in his head. *사마엘 and 디만드레드 hated me, whatever honors I gave them. The more honors, the worse the hate, until they sold their souls and went over. 디만드레드 especially. I should have killed him! I should have killed them all! Scorched the earth to kill them all! Scorch the earth!*

Face frozen, 랜드 fought for his own mind. *I am 랜드 al’Thor. 랜드 al’Thor! I never knew 사마엘 or 디만드레드 or any of them! 빛 burn me, I am 랜드 al’Thor!* Like a faint echo, one more thought came from elsewhere. *빛 burn me*. It sounded like a plea. Then 르웨어스 테린 was gone, driven back into whatever shadows he lived in.

바쉐어 took advantage of the silence. “You say you’re 마즈림 타임?” He sounded doubtful, and 랜드 looked at him in confusion. Was this 타임 or not? Only a madman would claim that name if it was not his.

The prisoner’s mouth quirked in what might have been the beginning of a smile, and he rubbed his chin. “I shaved, 바쉐어.” His voice held more than a hint of mockery. “It is hot this far south, or had you not noticed? Hotter than it should be, even here. Do you want proof of me? Shall I channel for you?” His dark eyes flickered to 랜드, then back to 바쉐어, whose face was growing darker by the minute. “Perhaps not that, not now. I remember you. I had you beat at Irinjavar, until those visions appeared in the sky. But everyone knows that. What does everyone not know, that you and 마즈림 타임 will?” Focused on 바쉐어, he seemed unaware of his guards, or their swords still hovering near his ribs. “I hear you hid what happened to Musar and Hachari and their wives.” The mockery was gone; he was just relating what had happened, now. “They shouldn’t have tried to kill me under a parley flag. I trust you found them good places as servants? All they’ll really want to do now is serve and obey; they won’t be happy otherwise. I could have killed them. They all four drew daggers.”

“타임,” 바쉐어 growled, hand darting for his hilt, “you . . . !”

랜드 stepped in front of him, seizing his wrist with the blade half-drawn. The guards’ blades, Tumad’s as well, were touching 타임 now, very likely touching flesh the way they were shoved against his coat, but he did not flinch. “Did you come to see me,” 랜드 demanded, “or to taunt Lord 바쉐어? If you do it again, I’ll let him kill you. My amnesty pardons what you’ve done, but it doesn’t let you flaunt your crimes.”

타임 studied 랜드 a moment before speaking. Despite the heat, the fellow barely sweated. “To see you. You were the one in the vision in the sky. They say it was the 어둠의 존재 himself you fought.”

“Not the 어둠의 존재,” 랜드 said. 바쉐어 was not fighting him exactly, but he could feel the tension in the man’s arm. If he let go, that blade would be out and through 타임 in a heartbeat. Unless he used the Power. Or 타임 did. That had to be avoided, if it could be. He kept his grip on 바쉐어’s wrist. “He called himself Ba’alzamon, but I think he was 이샤마엘. I killed him later, in the Stone of 티어.”

“I hear you’ve killed a number of the 버림받은 자들. Should I call you my Lord Dragon? I have heard this lot use the title. Do you mean to kill all the 버림받은 자들?”

“Do you know any other way to deal with them?” 랜드 asked. “They die, or the world does. Unless you think they can be talked into abandoning the Shadow the way they abandoned the Light.” This was becoming ridiculous. Here he was, carrying on a conversation with a man who certainly had five sword points drawing blood beneath his coat while he himself held on to another man who wanted to add a sixth and draw more than a trickle. At least 바쉐어’s men were too disciplined to do more without their general’s word. At least 바쉐어 was keeping his mouth shut. Admiring 타임’s coolness, 랜드 went on as quickly as he could without seeming to be hurried.

“Whatever your crimes are, 타임, they pale beside the 버림받은 자들’s. Have you ever tortured an entire city, made thousands of people assist in breaking each other slowly, in breaking their own loved ones? 세미르하제 did that, for no more reason than that she could, to prove she could, for the pleasure of it. Have you murdered children? 그랜달 did. She called it kindness, so they would not suffer after she enslaved their parents and carried them away.” He just hoped the other 살다에안s were listening half as closely as 타임; the man had actually leaned forward slightly in interest. He hoped they did not ask too many questions about where all this came from. “Have you given people to 트롤록s to eat? All the 버림받은 자들 did—prisoners who would not turn always went to the 트롤록s, if they weren’t murdered out of hand—but 디만드레드 captured two cities just because he thought the people there had slighted him before he went over to the Shadow, and every man, woman and child went into 트롤록 bellies. 메사나 set up schools in the territory she controlled, schools where children and young people were taught the *glories* of the 어둠의 존재, taught to kill their friends who didn’t learn well enough or fast enough. I could go on. I could start from the beginning of the list and go through all thirteen names, adding a hundred crimes as bad to every name. Whatever you’ve done, it doesn’t rank with that. And now you’ve come to accept my pardon, to walk in the Light and submit to me, to battle the 어둠의 존재 as hard as you ever battled anyone. The 버림받은 자들 are reeling; I mean to hunt them all down, eradicate them. And you will help me. For that, you’ve earned your pardon. I tell you true, you’ll probably earn it a hundred times over again before the Last Battle is done.”

At last he felt 바쉐어’s arm relax, felt the man’s sword sliding back into its scabbard. 랜드 barely stopped himself from exhaling in relief. “I don’t see any reason to guard him so closely now. Put up your swords.”

Slowly, Tumad and the others began sheathing their blades. Slowly, but they were doing it. Then 타임 spoke.

“Submit? I had thought more of a compact between us.” The other 살다에안s tensed; 바쉐어 was still behind 랜드, but 랜드 could *feel* him stiffening. The Maidens did not move a muscle, except that Jalani’s hand twitched toward her veil. 타임 tilted his head, unaware. “I would be the lesser partner, of course, yet I have had years more than you to study the Power. There is much I could teach you.”

Rage rose up in 랜드 till his vision filmed red. He had spoken of things he should have no knowledge of, had probably birthed a dozen rumors about himself and the 버림받은 자들, all to make this fellow’s deeds seem less dark, and the man had the audacity to speak of *compacts*? 르웨어스 테린 raved in his head. *Kill him! Kill him now! Kill him!* For once 랜드 did not bother to quell the voice. “No compact!” he growled. “No partners! I am the 용의 환생, 타임! Me! If you have knowledge I can make use of, I will, but you will go where I say, do as I say, when I say.”

Without a pause 타임 slipped to one knee. “I submit to the 용의 환생. I will serve and obey.” The corners of his mouth quivered again in that almost smile as he rose. Tumad gaped at him.

“That fast?” 랜드 said softly. The rage was not gone; it was white hot. If he gave way, he was not sure what he would do. 르웨어스 테린 still babbled in the shadows of his head. *Kill him! Must kill him!* 랜드 pushed 르웨어스 테린 away, to a barely audible murmur. Perhaps he should not be surprised at this; strange things happened around *ta’veren*, especially one as strong as himself. That a man might change his mind in a moment, even if his course had been carved in stone, should be no great surprise. But the anger had him, and a strong streak of suspicion. “You named yourself the 용의 환생, fought battles all over 살다에아, were only captured because you were knocked unconscious, and you give up this quickly? Why?”

타임 shrugged. “What are my choices? To wander the world alone, friendless, hunted, while you rise to glory? That’s supposing 바쉐어 doesn’t manage to kill me before I can leave the city, or your 아일women don’t. Even if they don’t, the 에스 세다이 will corner me sooner or later; I doubt the Tower means to forget 마즈림 타임. Or I can follow you, and part of that glory will be mine.” For the first time he looked around, at his guards, at the Maidens, and shook his head as if he could not believe it. “I might have been the one. How could I be sure otherwise? I can channel; I’m strong. What said I was not the 용의 환생? All I had to do was fulfill just one of the Prophecies.”

“Like managing to be born on the slopes of 용산?” 랜드 said coldly. “That was the first 예언 to be met.”

타임’s mouth quirked again. It really was not a smile; it never touched his eyes. “Victors write history. Had I taken the Stone of 티어, history would have shown I was born on 용산, of a woman never touched by a man, and the heavens opened up in radiance to herald my coming. The sort of thing they say about you, now. But you took the Stone with your 아일, and the world hails you as the 용의 환생. I know better than to stand against that; you are the one. Well, since the whole loaf won’t be mine, I will settle for whatever slices fall my way.”

“You may find honors, 타임, and you may not. If you begin to fret over them, think what happened to the others who’ve done what you did. 로가인, captured and gentled; rumor says he died in the Tower. A nameless fellow beheaded in Haddon Mirk by the 타이런s. Another burned by the Murandians. Burned alive, 타임! That’s what the 일리안ers did to Gorin Rogad four years ago, as well.”

“Not a fate I would embrace,” 타임 said levelly.

“Then forget honors and remember the Last Battle. Everything I do is aimed at Tarmon Gai’don. Everything I tell you to do will be aimed at it. *You* will aim at it!”

“Of course.” 타임 spread his hands. “You are the 용의 환생. I don’t doubt that; I acknowledge it publicly. We march toward Tarmon Gai’don. Which the Prophecies say you will win. And the histories will say that 마즈림 타임 stood at your right hand.”

“Perhaps,” 랜드 told him curtly. He had lived too many prophecies to believe any of them meant exactly what they said. Or even that they ensured anything. In his opinion, prophecy set the conditions that had to be met for a thing to happen; only, meeting them did not mean the thing *would* happen, just that it *could*. Some of the conditions set in the Prophecies of the Dragon more than implied that he had to die for any chance at victory. Thinking of that did nothing for his temper. “빛 send your chance doesn’t come too soon. Now. What knowledge do you have that I need? Can you teach men to channel? Can you test a man to know whether he can be taught?” Unlike women, one man who could channel could not simply sense the ability in another. There was as much different between men and women with the 하나의 힘 as there was between men and women; sometimes it was a matter of hair-fine degree, sometimes stone versus silk.

“Your amnesty? Some fools have actually shown up to learn how to be like you and me?”

바쉐어 only stared at 타임 contemptuously, arms folded and boots spread apart, but Tumad and the guards shifted uneasily. The Maidens did not. 랜드 had no idea how the Maidens felt about the score of men who had answered his call; they never gave any sign. With the memory of 타임 as a false Dragon strong in their heads, few of the 살다에안s could hide their ill ease.

“Just answer me, 타임. If you can do what I want, say so. If not. . . .”That was the anger talking. He could not send the man away, not if every day was a struggle with him. 타임 seemed to think he would, though.

“I can do both,” he said quickly. “I have found five over the years—not that I was really looking—but only one had the courage to go beyond the testing.” He hesitated, then added, “He went mad after two years. I had to kill him before he killed me.”

Two years. “You’ve held it off a deal longer than that. How?”

“Worried?” 타임 asked softly, then shrugged. “I can’t help you. I don’t know how; I just did. I’m sane as . . .” His eyes flickered toward 바쉐어, ignoring the other man’s flat stare. “. . . as Lord 바쉐어.”

But 랜드 wondered, suddenly. Half the Maidens had returned to watching the rest of the courtyard; they were not likely to focus so deeply on one possible threat that they ignored others. The possible threat was 타임, and the second half of the Maidens still had their eyes fixed on him and 랜드 for any sign the threat was real. Any man would have to be aware of them, sudden death in their eyes, their hands. 랜드 was, and they wanted to protect him. And Tumad and the other guards still gripped their sword hilts, ready to draw again. If 바쉐어’s men and the 아일 decided to kill 타임, the man would have a hard time escaping that courtyard however he channeled, unless 랜드 helped him. Yet 타임 paid the soldiers and the Maidens no more outward attention than he did the colonnades’ columns or the paving stones beneath his boots. Bravery, real or feigned, or something else? A kind of madness?

After a moment of silence, 타임 spoke again. “You don’t trust me yet. No reason you should. Yet. In time you will. In token of that future trust, I brought you a present.” From under his worn coat he pulled a rag-wrapped bundle a little larger than a man’s two fists together.

Frowning, 랜드 took it, and his breath caught when he felt the hard shape inside. Hastily he pulled away multicolored rags, revealing a disc the size of his palm, a disc like that on the scarlet banner above the palace, half white and half black, the ancient symbol of 에스 세다이, before the 세계의 파멸. He ran his fingers across the mated teardrops.

Only seven like this had been made, of *cuendillar*. 봉인 on the 어둠의 존재’s prison, seals that held the 어둠의 존재 away from the world. He had two more, hidden away very carefully. Protected very carefully. Nothing could break *cuendillar*, not even the 하나의 힘—the lip of a delicate cup made of heartstone could scratch steel, or diamond—but three of the seven *had* been broken. He had seen them, shattered. And he had watched 모이라인 carve a thin sliver from the edge of one. The seals were weakening, the Light alone knew why or how. The disc in his hands had the hard slickness of *cuendillar*, like a blend of the finest porcelain and polished steel—but he was sure it would break if he let it fall to the stones under his feet.

Three broken. Three in his possession. Where was the seventh? Only four seals stood between humankind and the 어둠의 존재. Four, if the last was still whole. Only four, standing between humankind and the Last Battle. How well did they still hold, weakened as they were?

르웨어스 테린’s voice came up like thunder. *Break it break them all must break them must must must break them all break them and strike must strike quickly must strike now break it break it break it.* . . .

랜드 shook with the effort of fighting that voice down, forcing away a mist that clung like spiderwebs. His muscles ached as if he wrestled with a man of flesh, a giant. Handful by handful he stuffed the fog that was 르웨어스 테린 into the deepest crannies, the deepest shadows, he could find in his mind.

Abruptly he heard the words he was muttering hoarsely. “Must break it now break them all break it break it break it.” Abruptly he realized he had his hands over his head, holding the seal, ready to smash it to the white pavement. The only thing stopping him was 바쉐어, up on his toes, hands raised to grip 랜드’s arms.

“I don’t know what that is,” 바쉐어 said quietly, “but I think maybe you should wait before deciding to break it. Eh?” Tumad and the others were no longer watching 타임; they gaped wide-eyed at 랜드. Even the Maidens had shifted their eyes to him, eyes full of concern. Sulin took a half step toward the men, and Jalani’s hand was outstretched toward 랜드 as if she did not realize it.

“No.” 랜드 swallowed; his throat hurt. “I don’t think I should.” 바쉐어 stepped back slowly, and 랜드 brought the seal down just as slowly. If 랜드 had thought 타임 unflappable, he had proof to the contrary now. Shock painted the man’s face. “Do you know what this is, 타임?” 랜드 demanded. “You must, or you wouldn’t have brought it to me. Where did you find it? Do you have another? Do you know where another is?”
“No,” 타임 said, voice unsteady. Not with fear, precisely; more like a man who had felt a cliff unexpectedly crumbling under him and had somehow found himself back on solid ground. “That is the only one I. . . . I’ve heard all sorts of rumors since I escaped the 에스 세다이. Monsters leaping out of thin air. Strange beasts. Men talking to animals, and the animals talking back. 에스 세다이 going mad like we’re supposed to. Whole villages going mad, killing each other. Some could be true. Half what I know to be true is no less insane. I heard some of the seals have been broken. A hammer could break that one.”

바쉐어 frowned, stared at the seal in 랜드’s hands, then gasped. He understood.

“Where did you find it?” 랜드 repeated. If he could find the last. . . . Then what? 르웨어스 테린 stirred, but he refused to listen.

“In the last place you would expect,” 타임 replied, “which I suppose is the first place to look for the others. A decaying little farm in 살다에아. I stopped for water, and the farmer gave it to me. He was old, with no children or grandchildren to pass it on to, and he thought I was the 용의 환생. He claimed his family had guarded it more than two thousand years. Claimed they were kings and queens during the 트롤록 전쟁, and nobles under 아투르 호크윙. His tale could have been true. No more unlikely than finding that in a hut only a few days ride from the 황무지border.”

랜드 nodded, then stooped to gather up the rags. He was used to the unlikely happening around him; it had to happen elsewhere, sometimes. Hurriedly rewrapping the seal, he handed it to 바쉐어. “Guard this carefully.” *Break it!* He squashed the voice hard. “Nothing must happen to it.”

바쉐어 took the bundle reverently in both hands. 랜드 was unsure whether the man’s bow was for him or the seal. “For ten hours or ten years, it will be safe until you require it.”

For a moment 랜드 studied him. “Everybody’s waiting for me to go mad, afraid of it, but not you. You must have thought I finally was, just now, but you weren’t afraid of me even then.”

바쉐어 shrugged, grinning behind his gray-streaked mustaches. “When I first slept in a saddle, Muad Cheade was Marshal-General. The man was as mad as a hare in spring thaw. Twice every day he searched his bodyservant for poison, and he drank nothing but vinegar and water, which he claimed was sovereign against the poison the fellow fed him, but he ate everything the man prepared for as long as I knew him. Once he had a grove of oaks chopped down because they were looking at him. And then insisted they be given decent funerals; he gave the oration. Do you have any idea how long it takes to dig graves for twenty-three oak trees?”

“Why didn’t somebody do something? His family?”

“Those not mad as he was, or madder, were afraid to look at him sideways. Tenobia’s father wouldn’t have let anyone touch Cheade anyway. He might have been insane, but he could outgeneral anyone I ever saw. He never lost a battle. He never even came close to losing.”

랜드 laughed. “So you follow me because you think I can out-general the 어둠의 존재?”

“I follow you because you are who you are,” 바쉐어 said quietly. “The world must follow you, or those who survive will wish themselves dead.”

Slowly 랜드 nodded. The Prophecies said he would break nations and bind them together. Not that he wanted to, but the Prophecies were his only guide to how to fight the Last Battle, how to win it. Even without them, he thought the binding together was necessary. 최후의 전투 would not be just him against the 어둠의 존재. He could not believe that; if he was going mad, he was not yet mad enough to believe he was more than a man. It would be mankind against 트롤록s and 미르드랄, too, and every sort of 그림자태생 the 황무지 could vomit out, and 어둠의 친구들 rising out of their hiding places. There would be other dangers on that road to Tarmon Gai’don, and if the world was not united. . . . *You do what must be done*. He was not sure whether that was himself or 르웨어스 테린, but it was the truth, as far as he could see.

Walking quickly to the nearest colonnade, he spoke over his shoulder to 바쉐어. “I am taking 타임 to the farm. Do you want to come along?”

“The farm?” 타임 said.

바쉐어 shook his head. “Thank you, no,” he said dryly. He might not allow any nerves to show, but 랜드 and 타임 together were probably as much as he could take; he certainly avoided the farm. “My men are growing soft policing the streets for you. I mean to put some of them back into their saddles properly for a few hours. You were going to inspect them this afternoon. Has that changed?”

“What farm?” 타임 said.

랜드 sighed, suddenly weary. “No, that hasn’t changed. I will be there if I can.” It was too important to change, though none but 바쉐어 and 맷 knew; he could not let anyone else think it more than a casual matter, a useless ceremony for a man growing taken with the pomp of his position, the 용의 환생 going out to be cheered by his soldiers. He had another visit to make today, too, one that everyone would think he was trying to keep secret. It might even stay secret, from most, but he had no doubt that those he wanted to learn of it, would.

Taking up his sword from where it stood against one of the narrow columns, he buckled it on over his undone coat. The belt was unadorned dark boarhide, just like the scabbard and the long hilt; the buckle was ornate, a finely worked dragon of etched steel inlaid with gold. He should get rid of that buckle, find something plain. He could not bring himself to do it, though. It had been a gift from 아비엔다. Which was the reason he should rid himself of it. He could never think his way out of that circle.

Something else waited there for him, too, a two-foot length of spear with a green-and-white tassel below the sharp head. He hefted it as he turned back to the courtyard. One of the Maidens had carved the short shaft with 용. Some people were already calling it the Dragon Scepter, especially Elenia and that lot. 랜드 kept the thing close to remind himself that he might have more enemies than those he could see.

“What farm are you talking about?” 타임’s voice grew harder. “Where is it you mean to take me?”

For a long moment 랜드 studied the man. He did not like 타임. Something in the fellow’s manner would not allow it. Or maybe something in himself. For so long he had been the only man who could even think of channeling without looking over his shoulder in a sweat for 에스 세다이. Well, it seemed a long time, and at least the 에스 세다이 would not try to gentle him, not now that they knew who he was. Could it be as simple as that? Jealousy that he was no longer unique? He did not think so. Apart from everything else, he would welcome more men who could channel walking the earth unmolested. Finally he would stop being a freak. No, it would not go that far, not this side of Tarmon Gai’don. He was unique; he was the 용의 환생. Whatever his reasons, he just did not like the man.

*Kill him!* 르웨어스 테린 shrieked. *Kill them all!* 랜드 pushed the voice back down. He did not have to like 타임, only to use him. And trust him. That was the hard part.

“I’m taking you where you can serve me,” he said coldly. 타임 did not flinch or frown; he merely watched and waited, the corners of his mouth twitching for one moment in that almost smile.
