Neither of these rings worked quite as well as the original, though they did work. 엘레인 was getting a little better at that; of four attempts to produce a copy, only one had been a failure. A *much* better average than with the things she made from scratch. But what if one of her failures did worse than simply not work, or not work very well? 에스 세다이 had been stilled studying *ter’angreal*. Burned out, it was called when it happened by accident, yet it was just as final. 니나브 did not think so, of course but 니나브 would not be satisfied till she Healed somebody three days dead.
엘레인 turned the ring in her fingers. What it did was simple enough to understand, but the “how” still escaped her. “How” and “why” were the keys. With the rings she thought the pattern of colors had as much to do with it as the shape—anything other than the twisted ring did nothing, and the one that had turned out solid blue just gave you horrific nightmares—but she was not sure how to reproduce the original’s red, blue and brown. Yet the fine structure of her copies was the same, the way the tiniest bits of them, too small to see or even detect without the 하나의 힘, were arranged. Why should the *colors* matter? There seemed to be one common thread in those tiny structures for *ter’angreal* that required channeling to work, and another for those that simply made use of the Power—stumbling on that was what allowed her to even attempt to make original *ter’angreal—*but there was so much she did not know, so much she was guessing at.

“Are you going to sit there all night?” 니나브 asked dryly, and 엘레인 gave a start. Setting one of the pottery cups back on the table, 니나브 arranged herself on her bed, hands folded across her middle. “You *were* the one who mentioned not keeping them waiting. For myself, I don’t mean to give those biddies an excuse to chew my tailfeathers.”

Hastily 엘레인 slipped the speckled ring—it was not really stone anymore, though it had started out that way—onto a cord that she tied around her own neck. The second pottery cup also held a tincture of herbs that 니나브 had prepared, slightly sweetened with honey to negate a bitter taste. 엘레인 drank about half, from past experience enough to help her sleep even with a headache. Tonight was one of those nights she could not afford to dally.

Stretching out on the cramped bed, she channeled briefly to extinguish the candle, then flapped her shift to produce a little cool. Well, a stir in the air, anyway. “I wish 에그웨인 would get better. I am tired of the scraps 셰리암 and the rest of them toss us. I want to know what is happening!”

She had touched on a hazardous topic, she realized. 에그웨인 had been injured a month and a half ago in 케렌, on the day 모이라인 and 란피어 died. The day 란 vanished.

“The 현명한 이들 say she *is* getting better,” 니나브 murmured sleepily in the dark. For once she did not sound as if she had followed the path to 란. “That’s what 셰리암 and her little circle say, and they have no reason to lie even if they could.”

“Well, I wish I could look over 셰리암’s shoulder tomorrow night.”

“As well wish—” 니나브 stopped for a yawn. “As well wish the Hall will choose you Amyrlin while you’re about it. You might have that one, granted. By the time they choose anyone, we’ll both be gray-haired enough for the job.”

엘레인 opened her mouth to reply, but with the other woman’s example, it turned into a yawn too. 니나브 began to snore, not loudly, but with dogged persistence. 엘레인 let her eyes drift shut, but her thoughts tried to remain focused in spite of herself.

The Hall certainly was being dilatory, the 의석자들 meeting for less than an hour some days and often not at all. To talk to one, you would think she saw no urgency, though of course the 의석자들 for the six 아자s—there were no Reds in Salidar, of course—did not tell other 에스 세다이 what they discussed in session, much less an 허락받은 자. They certainly had cause for dispatch. If their intentions remained secret, their gathering surely no longer did. 엘라이더 and the Tower would not ignore them forever. Beyond that, the 백의단 were still only a few miles away in 아마디시아, and rumors had begun of 용worn right here in 알타라. 빛 alone knew what 용worn might get up to if 랜드 had no control over them. The Prophet was a good example—or rather a horrid one. Riots, homes and farms burned, people murdered for not showing enough fervor in support of the 용의 환생.

니나브’s snoring sounded like cloth ripping, but in the distance. Another yawn cracked 엘레인’s jaws; she turned on her side and snuggled into the thin pillow. Reasons for dispatch. 사마엘 sat in 일리안, and it was only a few hundred miles to the 일리안er border, far too close with one of the 버림받은 자들. 빛 alone knew where the other 버림받은 자들 were, or what they were scheming. And 랜드; they had to be concerned about 랜드. He was not a danger, of course. He could never be that. But he *was* the key to everything; the world truly did bend itself around him now. She *would* bond him, somehow. 민. She and the embassy had to be more than halfway to Caemlyn by now. No snows to slow them. Another month yet for them to arrive. Not that she was concerned about 민 going to 랜드. What was the girl thinking of? 민. Sleep slid over her, and she slid into *Tel’aran’rhiod . . .*

. . . and found herself standing in the main street of silent night-shrouded Salidar, with the moon gibbous overhead. She could see quite clearly, more so than moonlight alone would have allowed. There was always a sense of light in the World of Dreams, from everywhere and nowhere, as if the darkness itself had some dark glow. But then, dreams were like that, and this was a dream, if not any ordinary dream.

The village here reflected the real Salidar, but in strange facsimile, more still than even night would make it. Every window was dark, and an air of emptiness hung heavily, as if no one occupied any of the buildings. Of course, no one did, here. A nightbird’s reedy cry was answered by another, then a third, and something made a faint rustling noise as it skittered away in the odd half-light, but the stables would be empty, and the picket lines outside the village, and the clearings where sheep and cattle had been gathered. Wild creatures there would be in plenty, but none domesticated. Details changed between one glance and the next; the thatch-roofed buildings remained the same, yet a water barrel would be in a slightly different place, or gone, a door that had stood open was closed. The more ephemeral a thing was in the real world, the more its position or condition might change, the less firm its reflection.

Occasionally motion flickered in the dark street, someone appearing and vanishing after a few steps, or even floating across the ground as if flying. Many people’s dreams could touch *Tel’aran’rhiod*, but only briefly. Which was lucky for them. Another property of the World of Dreams was that what happened to you here was still real when you woke. If you died here, you did not wake. A strange reflection. Only the heat was the same.

니나브 stood there in an 허락받은 자’s white dress with the banded hem, impatient beside 시우안 and 리안. She had the silver bracelet, too, though it would not work from here to the waking world; it still held 모그헤디엔, but 니나브, out of her body, would not be feeling anything through it. 리안 was regally slim, though in 엘레인’s opinion her barely opaque 도마니 gown of thin silk detracted from her elegance. The color kept shifting, too; that sort of thing happened until you learned what you were doing here. 시우안 was better. She wore a simple dress of blue silk, with a scooped neck just low enough to show the twisted ring on a necklace. On the other hand, lace trim sometimes appeared on the dress and the necklace changed from a plain silver chain to elaborate pieces with rubies or firedrops or emeralds set in gold, with earrings to match, then back to the plain chain.

That was the original ring hanging around 시우안’s neck; she appeared as solid as any of the buildings. To herself, 엘레인 looked just as solid, but she knew that to the others she seemed slightly misty, like 니나브 and 리안. You almost thought you might see the moonlight through them. That was what using a copy did. She could sense the True Source, but as she was, *세다르* felt tenuous; if she tried to channel, that would be meager too. With the ring 시우안 wore, it would not be so, but that was the price of having secrets someone else knew and you did not dare have exposed. 시우안 trusted the original more than 엘레인’s copies, so she wore it—or sometimes 리안 did—while 엘레인 and 니나브, who could use *세다르*, made do.

“Where are they?” 시우안 demanded. Her neckline swooped up and down. The dress was green, now, the necklace a strand of fat moonstones. “It’s bad enough they want to stick an oar into my work and row as they please; now they make me wait.”

“I do not know why it upsets you for them to come along,” 리안 told her. “You like watching them make mistakes. They do not know half of what they think they do.” For a moment her gown slid dangerously close to transparency; a close torque of fat pearls appeared around her neck and vanished. She did not notice. She had even less experience here than 시우안.

“I need some real sleep,” 시우안 muttered. “Bryne tries to run me breathless. But I have to wait on the pleasure of women who’ll spend half the night remembering how to walk. Not to mention being lumbered with these two.” She frowned at 엘레인 and 니나브, then rolled her eyes skyward.

니나브 gripped her braid firmly, a sure indication of temper working. For once, 엘레인 agreed with her wholeheartedly. It was more than difficult being a teacher with pupils who thought they knew more than they did and were far more likely to call down the teacher than the teacher was to get away with calling them down. Of course, the others were far worse than 시우안 or 리안. Where *were* the others?

Movement appeared up the street. Six women, surrounded by the glow of *세다르*, who did not vanish. As usual, 셰리암 and the rest of her council had dreamed themselves into their own bedchambers and walked out. 엘레인 was not sure how far they understood the attributes of *Tel’aran’rhiod* yet. In any case, they often insisted on doing things their own way even when there was a better. Who could know better than an 에스 세다이?

The six 에스 세다이 truly were beginners in *Tel’aran’rhiod*, and their dresses changed every time 엘레인 looked at them. First one was wearing the embroidered 에스 세다이 shawl, fringed in the color of her 아자 and with the white Flame of 타르 발론 a bold teardrop on the back, then four were, then none. Sometimes it was a light traveling cloak, as to keep dust off, with the Flame on back and left breast. Their ageless faces showed no signs of the heat, of course—에스 세다이 never did—and no sign they were aware of how their clothes were changing, either.

They were as misty as 니나브 or 리안. 셰리암 and the others put more faith in dream *ter’angreal* that required channeling than in the rings. They just did not seem willing to believe that *Tel’aran’rhiod* had nothing to do with the 하나의 힘. At least 엘레인 could not tell which were using her copies. Somewhere about them three would have a small disc of what had once been iron, scribed on both sides with a tight spiral and powered by a flow of Spirit, the only one of the Five Powers that could be channeled in your sleep. Except here, anyway. The other three would be carrying small plaques once amber, with a sleeping woman worked inside each. Even if she had all six *ter’angreal* in front of her, 엘레인 would not have been able to pick out the two originals; those copies had gone very well. Just the same, it was still copying.

As the 에스 세다이 came down the dirt street together, she heard the tail end of their conversation, though she could not make head nor foot of it.

“. . . will scorn our choice, Carlinya,” fiery-haired 셰리암 was saying, “but they will scorn any choice we make. We might as well stay by our decision. You do not need me to list reasons again.”

Morvrin, a stout Brown sister with gray-streaked hair, snorted. “After all our work with the Hall, we would have a hard time changing their minds now.”

“As long as no ruler scoffs, why should we care?” 미렐 said heatedly. The youngest of the six, not many years 에스 세다이, she sounded decidedly irritated.

“What ruler would dare?” Anaiya asked, much like a woman asking what child would dare track mud on her carpets. “In any case, no king or queen knows enough of what passes among 에스 세다이 to understand. Only the sisters’ opinions need concern us, not theirs.”

“What worries me,” Carlinya replied coolly, “is that if she is easily guided by us, she may be as easily guided by others.” The pale, almost black-eyed White was always cool, some would say icy.

Whatever they were talking about, it was nothing they wanted to discuss in front of 엘레인 or the others; they fell silent just before reaching them.

시우안 and 리안’s reaction to the newcomers had been to turn their backs on each other sharply, as if they had been having words interrupted by the 에스 세다이’s arrival. For 엘레인’s part, she quickly checked her dress. It was the proper banded white. She did not know how she felt about that, appearing in the right dress without thought; she would have wagered that 니나브 had had to change her garb after appearing. But then, 니나브 was far more intrepid than she, struggling against limits that she herself acquiesced to. How could she ever manage to rule 안도르? If her mother was dead. If.

셰리암, slightly plump and with high cheekbones, turned tilted green eyes on 시우안 and 리안. For a moment she wore a blue-fringed shawl. “If you two cannot learn to get along, I vow I’ll send both of you to Tiana.” It had the sound of something said often and no longer really meant.

“You worked together long enough,” 베오닌 said in her heavy 타라본er accent. A pretty Gray with honey-colored hair in a multitude of braids, she had blue-gray eyes that constantly looked startled. Nothing surprised 베오닌, though. She would not believe the sun came up in the morning until she saw for herself, yet if one morning it did not, 엘레인 doubted that 베오닌 would turn a hair. It would just confirm that she had been right to demand proof. “You can and must work together again.”

베오닌 sounded as if she had said that so often that she hardly thought of it. All the 에스 세다이 were long since used to 시우안 and 리안. They had begun handling them as they might have managed two girls who could not stop squabbling. 에스 세다이 did have a tendency to see anyone who was not as a child. Even these two who once had been sisters.

“Send them to Tiana or don’t,” 미렐 snapped, “but don’t talk about it.” 엘레인 did not think the darkly beautiful woman was angry at 시우안 or 리안. Perhaps not at anyone or anything in particular. She had a volatile temper remarkable even among Greens. Her golden yellow silk dress became high-necked, but with an oval cutout that exposed the tops of her breasts; she wore a peculiar necklace, too, like a wide silver collar supporting three small daggers, hilts nestling in her cleavage. A fourth dagger appeared and was gone so quickly it might have been imagination. She eyed 니나브 up and down as if searching for fault. “Are we going to the Tower, or aren’t we? If we are going to do this, we might as well accomplish something useful while we are about it.”

엘레인 knew why 미렐 was angry, now. When she and 니나브 first came to Salidar, they had been meeting 에그웨인 in *Tel’aran’rhiod* every seven days to share what they had learned. Which had not always been easy, since 에그웨인 was always accompanied by at least one of the 아일 dreamwalkers she was studying with. Meeting without a Wise One or two had taken some pains. In any case, all that ended when they reached Salidar. These six 에스 세다이 of 셰리암’s council had taken over the meetings, when they had had only the three original *ter’angreal* and little more knowledge of *Tel’aran’rhiod* than how to reach it. That had been just when 에그웨인 was injured, which left 에스 세다이 facing 현명한 이들, two sets of proud resolute women, each suspicious of what the other wanted, neither willing to yield an inch or bow her neck a hair.

Of course, 엘레인 did not know what went on at those meetings, but she had her own experiences to go by, and fragments dropped here and there by 셰리암 and the others.

에스 세다이 were sure they could learn anything once they knew there was something to be learned, usually required the respect due a queen, and always expected to be told what they wanted to know without delays or quibbles. They had apparently demanded answers about everything, from what 랜드 was planning to when 에그웨인 would be well enough to return to the World of Dreams, to whether it was possible to spy on people’s dreams in *Tel’aran’rhiod* or to enter the World of Dreams physically, or bring someone into the dream against their will. They had even asked more than once whether it was possible to affect the real world by what you did in the dream, a pure impossibility they apparently doubted. Morvrin had read a little about *Tel’aran’rhiod*, enough to come up with plenty of questions, though 엘레인 suspected 시우안 supplied her share. She thought 시우안 was angling to attend the meetings herself, but the 에스 세다이 seemed to think it concession enough to allow her to use the ring as an aid in her work with the eyes-and-ears. 에스 세다이 interference in that work was what upset her.

As for the 아일. . . . 현명한 이들—the dreamwalkers, at least, 엘레인 was aware from her own encounters, not only knew just about everything there was to know about the World of Dreams, but looked on it almost as a private preserve. They did not like anyone coming there in ignorance, and had a rough way of dealing with what they saw as foolishness. Besides which, they were a closemouthed lot, apparently fiercely loyal to 랜드, unwilling to say much more than that he was alive, or that 에그웨인 would return to *Tel’aran’rhiod* when she was well enough, and more than unwilling to answer questions they considered improper. Which last could mean that they did not believe the questioner knew enough yet to hear the answer, or that question or answer or both somehow violated their strange philosophy of honor and obligation. 엘레인 knew little more of *ji’e’toh* than that it existed, and that it made for very peculiar, very touchy behavior.

All in all, it was a recipe for disaster, and 엘레인 thought it very probably was served up fresh every seven days, at least from the 에스 세다이 point of view.

셰리암 and the other five had required lessons every night in the beginning, but now there were only two times they did so. The night before meeting the 현명한 이들, as if to hone their skills one last time before a contest. And the night after, usually tight-mouthed, as if to work out what had gone wrong and how to counter it. 미렐 was probably already seething over tomorrow night’s disaster. There surely would be one of some kind.

Morvrin turned to 미렐 and opened her mouth, but suddenly there was another woman among them. It took 엘레인 a moment to recognize Gera, one of the cooks, in those ageless features. Wearing a green-fringed shawl with the Flame of 타르 발론 on her back and weighing no more than half what she really did, Gera raised an admonitory finger to the 에스 세다이—and was gone.

“So those are her dreams, are they?” Carlinya said coolly. Her snow-white silk dress grew sleeves that hung in points over her hands, and a high tight neck under her chin. “Someone should speak to her.”

“Leave over, Carlinya,” Anaiya chuckled. “Gera’s a good cook. Let her have her dreams. I can see the attraction myself.” Abruptly she became slimmer and taller. Her features did not really alter; she wore the same plain, motherly face as always. With a laugh she changed back. “Can’t you see the fun in something for once, Carlinya?” Even Carlinya’s sniff was cool.

“Clearly,” Morvrin said, “Gera saw us, but will she remember?” Her dark, steely eyes were thoughtful. Her dress, plain dark wool, held the steadiest among the six. Details shifted, but so subtly that 엘레인 could not really say what was different.

“Of course she will,” 니나브 said acerbically. She had explained this before. Six 에스 세다이 looked at her, eyebrows rising, and she moderated her voice. A little. She hated scrubbing pots, too. “If she remembers the dream, she will. But only as a dream.”

Morvrin frowned. She ran 베오닌 a close second in wanting proof. 니나브’s long-suffering expression was going to get her in trouble, whatever her tone. Before 엘레인 could say anything to take the 에스 세다이’s attention from 니나브, though, 리안 spoke up with an expression close to a simper.

“Don’t you think we should go, now?”

시우안 snorted contemptuously at the timidity, and 리안 cut her eyes at her sharply. “Yes, you’ll want to have as much time in the Tower as possible,” 시우안 said, diffident in turn, and 리안 sniffed.

They really did it very well. 셰리암 and the others never suspected that 시우안 and 리안 were not simply two stilled women clinging to a purpose that might keep them alive, clinging to the edge of what they had been. Two women childishly at one another’s throats all the time. The 에스 세다이 should have remembered that 시우안 had had the reputation of a strong-willed and devious manipulator, and to a lesser extent so had 리안. Had they presented a unified front, or shown their true faces, the six would have remembered, and looked hard at everything the pair said. But divided, spitting rancor in each other’s face, all but groveling to the 에스 세다이 and plainly not even aware of it. . . . When one was reluctantly forced to agree with what the other said, it lent extra weight. When one objected on obviously frivolous grounds, so did that. 엘레인 knew they used the pretense to guide 셰리암 and the others toward supporting 랜드. She just wished she knew what else they used it for.

“They’re right,” 니나브 said firmly, giving 시우안 and 리안 a disgusted look. Their pretence irked 니나브 no end: 니나브 would not have groveled for her life. “You should know by now that the longer you spend here, the less real rest you get. Sleep while you are in *Tel’aran’rhiod* doesn’t do as much good as ordinary sleep. Now, remember that if you see anything out of the ordinary, you need to be careful.” She truly did hate repeating herself—the fact showed clearly in her voice—but with these women, 엘레인 had to admit it was too often necessary. If only 니나브 did not sound as if she were talking to dim-witted children. “When somebody dreams themselves into *Tel’aran’rhiod* like Gera, but they’re having a nightmare, sometimes the nightmare survives, and those are very dangerous. Avoid anything that looks unusual. And try to control your thoughts this time. What you think of here can become real. That 미르드랄 that popped out of nowhere last time might have been a leftover nightmare, but I think one of you let her mind wander. You were talking about the 흑색 아자, if you’ll remember, and discussing whether they were letting 그림자태생 into the Tower.” As if that were not bad enough, she had to add, “You won’t impress the 현명한 이들 tomorrow night if you drop a 미르드랄 into the middle of everything.” 엘레인 winced.

“Child,” Anaiya said gently, adjusting the blue-fringed shawl that was suddenly looped over her arms, “you have been doing very good work, but that doesn’t excuse a peevish mouth.”

“You have been given a number of privileges,” 미렐 said, not at all gently, “but you seem to forget that they *are* privileges.” Her frown should have been enough to make 니나브 quake. 미렐 had been increasingly hard on 니나브 the past weeks. She had her shawl on, too. They all did, a bad sign.

Morvrin snorted bluntly. “When I was 허락받은 자, any girl who spoke to an 에스 세다이 that way would have spent the next month scrubbing floors, if she was due to be raised 에스 세다이 the next day.”

엘레인 spoke up hurriedly, hoping she could forestall their own disaster. 니나브 had put on what she probably thought was a conciliatory face, but she looked sulky and stubborn. “I am sure she didn’t mean anything, 에스 세다이. We have been working very hard. Please forgive us.” Adding herself might help, since she had done nothing. It might also have them both scrubbing floors. At least it made 니나브 look at her. And think, apparently, since her features smoothed into something that did seem appeasing and she made a curtsy and stared at the ground as though abashed. Maybe she really was. Maybe. 엘레인 rushed on as if 니나브 had made a formal apology and had it accepted. “I know you all do want to spend as much time as possible at the Tower, so perhaps we shouldn’t wait any longer? If you will all visualize 엘라이더’s study, just as you saw it last time?” 엘라이더 was never called the Amyrlin in Salidar, and in the same way the Amyrlin’s study in the 백색 탑 had its name shifted. “Everyone fix it in your minds, so we all arrive together.”

Anaiya was the first to nod, but even Carlinya and 베오닌 let themselves be diverted.

It was unclear whether the ten of them moved or *Tel’aran’rhiod* moved around them. It could have been either from the little 엘레인 really understood; the World of Dreams was almost infinitely malleable. One moment they were standing in the street in Salidar, the next in a large and ornate room. The 에스 세다이 gave satisfied nods, still inexperienced enough to be pleased at anything that worked as they thought it should.

As surely as *Tel’aran’rhiod* reflected the waking world, this room reflected the power of the women who had occupied it over the last three thousand years. The gilded stand-lamps were unlit, but there was light, in the odd way of *Tel’aran’rhiod* and dreams. The tall fireplace was golden marble from 캔도르, the floor polished redstone from the Mountains of Mist. The walls had been paneled a relatively short time ago—a mere thousand years—in pale wood, oddly striped and carved with marvelous beasts and birds that 엘레인 was sure had come straight out of the carver’s imagination. Gleaming pearly stone framed tall arched windows that let onto the balcony overlooking the Amyrlin’s private garden; that stone had been salvaged from a nameless city submerged in the Sea of Storms during the 세계의 파멸, and no one had ever found its like elsewhere.

Each woman who used that room put her own mark on it, if only for the time of her possession, and 엘라이더 was no different. A heavy thronelike chair, an ivory Flame of 타르 발론 cresting the high back, stood behind a massive writing table ornately carved in triple-linked rings. The tabletop was bare except for three boxes of 알타라n lacquerwork, each precisely the same distance from the next. A plain white vase stood atop a severe white plinth against one wall. The vase held roses, the number and color changing at every look, but always arranged with a harsh rigidity. Roses, at this time of year, in this weather! The 하나의 힘 had been *wasted* to make them grow. 엘라이더 had done the same when she was advisor to 엘레인’s mother.

Above the fireplace hung a painting in the new style, on stretched canvas, of two men fighting among clouds, hurling lightning. One man had a face of fire, and the other was 랜드. 엘레인 had been at Falme; the painting was not too far from the truth. A tear in the canvas across 랜드’s face, as though something heavy had been thrown at it, had been mended almost invisibly. Plainly 엘라이더 wanted a constant reminder of the 용의 환생, and just as plainly she was not happy having to look at it.
“If you will excuse me,” 리안 said before all the satisfied nodding was done, “I must see if my people have received my messages.” Every 아자 except the White had a network of eyes-and-ears scattered across the nations, and so did a good many individual 에스 세다이, but 리안 was rare, perhaps unique, in that as Keeper she had created a net in 타르 발론 itself. No sooner had she spoken than she vanished.

“She should not be wandering about alone here,” 셰리암 said in an exasperated voice. “니나브, go after her. Stay with her.”

니나브 gave her braid a tug. “I don’t think—”

“Very often you do not,” 미렐 cut her off. “For once do as you are told, when you are told, 허락받은 자.”

Exchanging wry glances with 엘레인, 니나브 nodded, visibly suppressing a sigh, and disappeared. 엘레인 had little sympathy. Had 니나브 not indulged her irritation back in Salidar it might have been possible to explain that 리안 could be anywhere in the city, that it would be almost impossible to find her, and that she had been venturing into *Tel’aran’rhiod* alone for weeks.

“Now to see what we can learn,” Morvrin said, but before anyone could move, 엘라이더 was behind the writing table, glaring.

An unyielding stern-faced woman, handsome rather than beautiful, and dark of hair and eye, 엘라이더 wore a blood-red dress, with the striped stole of the 아미를린 석좌 about her shoulders. “As I have Foretold,” she intoned. “The 백색 탑 will be reunited under me. Under *me*!” She pointed harshly to the floor. “Kneel, and ask forgiveness of your sins!” With that, she was gone.

엘레인 let out a long breath, and was gratified to realize she was not the only one.

“A Foretelling?” 베오닌’s forehead creased thoughtfully. She did not sound worried, but she might well have. 엘라이더 did have the Foretelling, if fitfully. When the Foretelling laid hold of a woman and she knew a thing would happen, it did.

“A dream,” 엘레인 said, and was surprised at how steady her voice was. “She’s asleep and dreaming. No wonder if she dreams everything to her liking.” *Please, Light, let it only be that*.

“Did you notice the stole?” Anaiya asked no one in particular. “It had no blue stripe.” The Amyrlin’s stole was supposed to have one stripe for each of the seven 아자s.

“A dream,” 셰리암 said flatly. She sounded unafraid, but she had her blue-fringed shawl on again and was clutching it around her. So was Anaiya.

“Whether it is or not,” Morvrin said placidly, “we may as well do what we came for.” Not much could frighten Morvrin.

The abrupt stir of activity at the Brown sister’s words made it suddenly clear how still everyone had gone. She, Carlinya and Anaiya glided swiftly out to the anteroom, where the Keeper’s worktable would be. That was Alviarin Freidhen, under 엘라이더; a White, strangely, though the Keeper *always* came from the Amyrlin’s own 아자.

시우안 stared after them testily. She claimed there was often more to be learned from Alviarin’s papers than from 엘라이더’s, for Alviarin sometimes seemed to know more than the woman she supposedly served, and twice 시우안 had found evidence that Alviarin had countermanded 엘라이더’s orders, apparently without repercussions. Not that she had told 엘레인 or 니나브 what orders. There were definite limits to 시우안’s sharing.

셰리암, 베오닌 and 미렐 gathered at 엘라이더’s desk, opened one of the lacquered boxes, and began rifling through the papers inside. 엘라이더 kept her recent correspondence and reports there. The box, worked in golden hawks fighting among white clouds in a blue sky, would suddenly shut again every time one of them let go of the lid, until they remembered to hold it open, and the papers themselves changed even as they were being read. Paper truly was ephemeral. Amid vexed *tsks* and annoyed sighs, the 에스 세다이 persevered.

“Here’s a report from Danelle,” 미렐 said, hastily scanning a page. 시우안 tried to join them—Danelle, a young Brown, had been part of the cabal that deposed her—but 베오닌 gave her a sharp frown that sent her back to a corner grumbling to herself. 베오닌 had returned her attention to the box and its documents before 시우안 had taken three steps; the other two women never noticed. 미렐 went right on talking. “She says that 맷tin Stepaneos accepts wholeheartedly, Roedran is still trying to take every side, while Alliandre and Tylin want more time to consider their answers. There’s a note here in 엘라이더’s hand. ‘Press them!’ ” She clicked her tongue as the report melted into air in her hand. “It did not say about what, but there can be only two possibilities to take in those four.” 맷tin Stepaneos was King of 일리안 and Roedran of 무란디, while Alliandre was Queen of 게알단 and Tylin of 알타라. The subject had to be 랜드 or the 에스 세다이 opposing 엘라이더.

“At least we know our emissaries still have as good a chance as 엘라이더’s,” 셰리암 said. Of course, Salidar had sent none to 맷tin Stepaneos; Lord Brend of the Council of Nine, 사마엘, was the true power in 일리안. 엘레인 would have given a pretty to know what 엘라이더 proposed that 사마엘 was willing to support, or at least let 맷tin Stepaneos say that he would support. She was sure the three 에스 세다이 would have given as much, but they just went on snatching documents out of the lacquerwork box.

“The arrest warrant for 모이라인, it is still in force,” 베오닌 said, shaking her head as the sheet in her hand suddenly turned to a fat sheaf. “She does not yet know 모이라인 is dead.” Grimacing at the pages, she let them fall; they scattered like leaves, and melted into air before settling. “엘라이더 still means to build herself a palace, too.”

“She would,” 셰리암 said dryly. Her hand jerked as she took in what appeared to be a short note. “Shemerin has run away. The *허락받은 자* Shemerin.”

All three glanced at 엘레인 before turning back to the box, which they had to open again. None made any comment on what 셰리암 had said.

엘레인 very nearly ground her teeth. She and 니나브 had told them 엘라이더 was reducing Shemerin, a Yellow sister, to the 허락받은 자, but of course they had not believed. An 에스 세다이 could be made to do penance, she might be cast out, but she could not be demoted short of stilling. Only, it seemed that 엘라이더 was doing exactly as that, whatever Tower law said. Maybe she was rewriting Tower law.

A number of things they had told these women had not really been believed. Such young women, 허락받은 자, could not know enough of the world to know what could be and what not. Young women were credulous, gullible; they might well see and believe what was not there at all. It was an effort not to stamp her foot. An 허락받은 자 took what 에스 세다이 wished to hand out and did not ask for what 에스 세다이 did not choose to give. Such as apologies. She kept her face smooth and her smoldering inside.

시우안 felt under no such restraints. Most of the time she did not. When the 에스 세다이 were not looking at her, she bathed them all in a glower. Of course, if one of the three glanced in her direction, her face became meek acceptance in a twinkling. She was very practiced at that. A lion survives by being a lion, she had once told 엘레인, and a mouse by being a mouse. Even so, 시우안 made a poor and reluctant mouse.

엘레인 thought she detected worry in 시우안’s eyes. This task had been 시우안’s since she proved to the 에스 세다이 that she could use the ring safely—after secret lessons for her and 리안 from 니나브 and 엘레인, true—and a prime source of information. It took time to reestablish contact with eyes-and-ears scattered across the nations, and redirect their reports from the Tower to Salidar. If 셰리암 and the others meant to take this over, 시우안 might be less useful. In the history of the Tower no network of agents had ever been run by any but a full sister until 시우안 came to Salidar with her knowledge of the Amyrlin’s eyes-and-ears, and the 청색 아자’s that she had run before becoming Amyrlin. 베오닌 and Carlinya were openly reluctant to depend on a woman who was no longer one of them, and the others were not far behind. Truth to tell, they were none of them comfortable around a woman who had been stilled.

There really was nothing for 엘레인 to do, either. The 에스 세다이 might call this a lesson, they might even think of it so, but she knew from past experience that if she tried to do any teaching without being asked, she would have her nose snapped off in short order. She was there to answer any questions they might have and nothing more. She thought of a stool—it appeared, the legs carved in vines—and sat down to wait. A chair would have been more comfortable, but it might occasion comment. An 허락받은 자 sitting too comfortably was often considered an 허락받은 자 with not enough to do. After a moment 시우안 made herself an almost identical stool. She gave 엘레인 a tight smile—and the 에스 세다이 backs a scowl.

The first time 엘레인 had visited this room in *Tel’aran’rhiod*, there had been a semicircle of such stools, a dozen or more, in front of the heavily carved table. Each visit since had seen fewer, and now none. She was sure that indicated something, though she could not imagine what. She was sure 시우안 thought so, too, and very likely had puzzled out a reason, but if she had, she had not shared it with 엘레인 or 니나브.

“The fighting in 시엔나르 and 아라펠 is dying down,” 셰리암 murmured half to herself, “but still nothing here to say why it began. Skirmishes only, yet Bordermen do not fight one another. They have the 황무지.” She was 살다에안, and 살다에아 was one of the 국경지대.

“At least the 황무지 is still quiet,” 미렐 said. “Almost too quiet. It cannot last. A good thing that 엘라이더 has plenty of eyes-and-ears through the 국경지대.” 시우안 managed to combine a wince with a glare at the 에스 세다이. 엘레인 did not think she had managed yet to make contact with any of her agents in the 국경지대; they lay a long way from Salidar.

“I would feel better if the same could be said of 타라본.” The page in 베오닌’s hand grew longer and wider; she glanced at it, sniffed, and tossed it aside. “The eyes-and-ears in 타라본, they are still silent. All of them. The only word she has of 타라본 is rumors from 아마디시아 that 에스 세다이 are involved in the war.” She shook her head at the absurdity of committing such rumors to paper. 에스 세다이 did not involve themselves in civil wars. Not openly enough to be detected, at any rate. “And there are no more than a handful of confused reports from 아라드 도만, it seems.”

“We will know about 타라본 soon enough ourselves,” 셰리암 said soothingly. “A few more weeks.”

The search went on for hours. There was never any shortage of documents; the lacquered box never emptied. In fact, the stack inside sometimes increased with the removal of a paper. Of course, only the shortest held steady long enough to be read in full, but occasionally a letter or report that had already been scanned would come out of the box again. Long stretches passed in silence, yet some documents elicited comment; a few the 에스 세다이 discussed. 시우안 began stringing a cat’s-cradle between her hands, apparently paying no attention at all. 엘레인 wished she could do the same, or better yet read—a book appeared on the floor at her feet, *The Travels of Jain Farstrider*, before she made it go away—but women who were not 에스 세다이 were granted more leeway than those training to be. Still, she learned a few things by listening.

에스 세다이 involvement in 타라본 was not the only rumor that had found its way to 엘라이더’s writing table. Pedron Niall’s ingathering of the 백의단 was rumored to have as its goal everything from seizing the throne of 아마디시아—which he certainly had no need of—to crushing the wars and anarchy in 타라본 and 아라드 도만, to *supporting* 랜드. 엘레인 would believe that when the sun rose in the west. There were reports of strange occurrences in 일리안 and 케렌—there might have been others, but those were the ones they saw—villages taken by madness, nightmares walking in daylight, two-headed calves that talked, 그림자태생 appearing out of thin air. 셰리암 and the other two passed over those lightly; the same sort of stories drifted to Salidar from parts of 알타라 and 무란디 and across the river from 아마디시아. The 에스 세다이 dismissed them as hysteria among people learning of the 용의 환생. 엘레인 was not so sure. She had seen things they had not, for all their years and experience. Her mother was rumored to be raising an army in the west of 안도르—under the ancient flag of Manetheren, of all things!—as well as being held prisoner by 랜드 and fleeing to every nation imaginable, including the 국경지대 and 아마디시아, which last was purely *un*imaginable. Apparently the Tower believed none of it. 엘레인 wished she knew what to believe.

She stopped fretting over where her mother really was when she heard 셰리암 mention her name. Not speaking to her; reading hurriedly from a square sheet of paper that became a long parchment with three seals at the bottom. 엘레인 Trakand was to be located and returned to the 백색 탑 at all costs. If there was any more bungling, those who failed would “envy the Macura woman.” That made 엘레인 shiver; on their way to Salidar a woman named Ronde Macura had come within an eyelash of sending her and 니나브 back to the Tower like bundles of wash to the laundry. The ruling house of 안도르, 셰리암 read, was “the key,” which made as little sense. The key to what?

None of the three 에스 세다이 so much as glanced in her direction. They just exchanged glances and went on with what they were doing. Perhaps they had forgotten her, but then again, perhaps not. 에스 세다이 did what they did. If she was to be shielded from 엘라이더, that was an 에스 세다이 decision, and if they decided for some reason to hand her to 엘라이더 bound hand and foot, that was their choice too. *“The pike does not ask the frog’s permission before dining*,” as she remembered Lini saying.

엘라이더’s response to 랜드’s amnesty was evident in the condition of the report. 엘레인 could almost see her crumpling the sheet of paper in her fist, starting to rip it apart, then coldly smoothing it out and adding it to the box. 엘라이더’s rages were almost always cold. She had not written anything on that document, but scrawled biting words on another, enumerating the 에스 세다이 in the Tower, made clear she was almost ready to declare publicly that any who did not obey her order to return were traitors. 셰리암 and the other two discussed the possibility calmly. However many sisters intended to obey, some would have far to travel; some might not even have received the summons yet. In any case, such a decree would confirm to the world all the rumors of a divided Tower. 엘라이더 must be near panic to consider such a thing, or else maddened beyond reason.

A sliver of cold slid down 엘레인’s backbone, and nothing to do with whether 엘라이더 was fearful or engaged. Two hundred ninety four 에스 세다이 in the Tower, supporting 엘라이더. Nearly one-third of all 에스 세다이, almost as many as had gathered in Salidar. It might be that the best that could be expected was for the rest to split down the middle as well. After a great rush in the beginning, the numbers coming into Salidar had slowed to a trickle. Perhaps the flow to the Tower had dwindled as well. It could be hoped.

For a time they did their searching in silence, then 베오닌 exclaimed, “엘라이더, she has sent emissaries to 랜드 al’Thor.” 엘레인 leaped to her feet, and barely held her tongue at a clutching gesture from 시우안, spoiled a little by her failure to make the cat’s-cradle disappear first.

셰리암 reached for the single sheet, but it became three before her hand touched it. “Where is she sending them?” she asked at the same time 미렐 asked, “When did they leave 타르 발론?” Serenity hung on by its fingernails.

“To 케렌,” 베오닌 said. “And I did not see when, if it was mentioned. But they certainly will go on to Caemlyn as soon as they discover where he is.”

Even so, that was good; it might take a month or more to travel from 케렌 to Caemlyn. The Salidar embassy would reach him first, surely. 엘레인 had a ragged map tucked away beneath her mattress back in Salidar, and every day she marked off how far she thought they might have traveled toward Caemlyn.

The Gray sister was not finished. “It seems that 엘라이더, she means to offer him support. And an escort to the Tower.” 셰리암’s eyebrows rose.

“That is preposterous.” 미렐’s olive cheeks darkened. “엘라이더 was Red.” An Amyrlin was of all 아자s and none, yet no one could simply abandon where they came from.

“That woman will do anything,” 셰리암 said. “He might find the 백색 탑’s support attractive.”

“Perhaps we can send a message to 에그웨인 through the 아일 women?” 미렐 suggested in a doubtful tone.

시우안 gave a loud, and very phony, cough, but 엘레인 had had all she could stand. Warning 에그웨인 was vital, of course—엘라이더’s people would surely drag her back to the Tower if they discovered her in 케렌, and not to a pleasant reception—but the rest . . . ! “How can you think 랜드 would listen to anything 엘라이더 says? Do you think he does not know she was 적색 아자, and what that means? They aren’t going to offer him support, and you know it. We have to warn him!” There was a contradiction in that, and she knew it, but worry had hold of her tongue. If anything happened to 랜드, she would die.

“And how do you suggest that *we* do that, 허락받은 자?” 셰리암 asked coolly.

엘레인 was afraid she must look like a fish, with her mouth hanging open. She had not a clue what answer to give. She was saved suddenly by distant screaming, followed by wordless shouts from the anteroom. She was closest to the door, but she ran through with the others on her heels.

The room was empty except for the Keeper’s writing table, with its piles of papers and stacks of scrolls and documents, and a row of chairs against one wall where 에스 세다이 would sit while waiting to speak to 엘라이더. Anaiya, Morvrin and Carlinya were gone, but one of the tall outer doors was still swinging shut. A woman’s frantic screams rolled through the narrowing opening. 셰리암, 미렐 and 베오닌 almost knocked 엘레인 down in their haste to reach the hall. They might have appeared misty, but they felt solid enough.

“Be careful,” 엘레인 shouted, yet there was really nothing to do but gather her skirts and follow as quickly as possible with 시우안. They stepped into a scene from nightmare. Literally.

Some thirty paces to their right, the tapestry-hung corridor suddenly widened into a stony cavern that seemed to stretch forever, lit in dim patches by the red glow of scattered fires and braziers. There were 트롤록s everywhere, great manlike shapes, their all-too-human faces distorted by bestial muzzles and snouts and beaks, sporting horns or tusks or feathered crests. Those in the distance appeared more indistinct than the nearest, only half-formed, while the nearest were giants twice as tall as a man, even larger than any real 트롤록, all clad in leather and black spiked mail, howling and capering around cookfires and cauldrons, racks and strange spiked frames and metal shapes.

It really was a nightmare, though larger than any 엘레인 had heard of from 에그웨인 or the 현명한 이들. Once freed of the mind that created them, such things sometimes drifted through the World of Dreams and sometimes latched on to a particular spot. 아일 dreamwalkers destroyed each as a matter of course whenever they found one, but they—and 에그웨인—had told her the best thing to do was avoid any she saw altogether. Unfortunately, Carlinya apparently had not listened when she and 니나브 passed that on.

The White sister was bound and hanging by her ankles from a chain that disappeared into darkness overhead. To 엘레인’s eyes the glow of *세다르* still surrounded her, but Carlinya writhed frantically and screamed as she was slowly lowered headfirst toward a great bubbling black kettle of boiling oil.

Even as 엘레인 ran into the corridor, Anaiya and Morvrin halted at the border where hallway abruptly became cavern. For all of a heartbeat, they halted, then suddenly their hazy forms seemed to elongate toward the boundary, like smoke drawn into a chimney. No sooner had they touched it than they were inside, Morvrin shouting as two 트롤록s turned great iron wheels that stretched her out tighter and tighter, Anaiya dangling by her wrists as 트롤록s danced about her, flogging her with metal-tipped whips that tore long rents in her dress.

“We must link,” 셰리암 said, and the glow surrounding her merged with that around 미렐 and 베오닌. Even so, it did not come near the brightness of that around a single woman in the waking world, a woman who was not a misty dream.

“No!” 엘레인 shouted urgently. “You mustn’t accept it as real. You must treat it as—” She seized 셰리암’s arm, but the flow of Fire the three had woven, tenuous even with them linked, touched the dividing line between dream and nightmare. The weave vanished there as if the nightmare had absorbed it, and in the same instant the three 에스 세다이 became drawn out, mist caught in a wind. They had time only for startled yells before they touched the boundary and vanished. 셰리암 reappeared inside, her head sticking up from a dark metal bell shape. 트롤록s turned handles and jerked levers on the outside, and 셰리암’s red hair flailed wildly as she shrieked in rising crescendos. Of the other two there was no sign, but 엘레인 thought she could hear more screaming in the distance, someone wailing “No!” over and over, another shrieking for help.

“Do you remember what we told you about dispelling nightmares?” 엘레인 asked.

Eyes fixed on the scene in front of her, 시우안 nodded. “Deny its reality. Try to fix things in your mind as they would be without it.”

That had been 셰리암’s mistake, all the 에스 세다이’s mistake probably. By trying to channel against the nightmare they had accepted it as real, and that acceptance had pulled them into it as surely as walking in, leaving them helpless unless they remembered what they had forgotten. Which they showed no sign of doing. The climbing shrieks augered into 엘레인’s ears.

“The corridor,” she muttered, trying to form in her head how it had been when she saw it last. “Think of the corridor the way you remember it.”

“I’m trying, girl,” 시우안 growled. “It isn’t working.”

엘레인 sighed. 시우안 was right. Not a line of the scene before them so much as wavered. 셰리암’s head was almost vibrating above the metal shroud that enclosed the rest of her. Morvrin’s howls came in strained pants; 엘레인 almost thought she could hear the woman’s joints being pulled apart. Carlinya’s hair, hanging below her, was almost touching the roiling surface of the hot oil. Two women were not enough. The nightmare was too big.

“We need the others,” she said.

“리안 and 니나브? Girl, if we knew where to find them, 셰리암 and the rest would be dead before. . . .” She trailed off, staring at 엘레인. “You don’t mean 리안 and 니나브, do you? You mean 셰리암 and. . . .” 엘레인 only nodded; she was too frightened to speak. “I don’t think they can hear us from here, or see us. Those 트롤록s haven’t even glanced our way. That means we have to try from inside.” 엘레인 nodded again. “Girl,” 시우안 said in a toneless voice, “you have a lion’s courage, and maybe a fisherbird’s sense.” With a heavy sigh, she added, “But I don’t see any other way myself.”

엘레인 agreed with her about everything except the courage. If she had not had her knees locked, she would have been in a heap on the floor tiles, patterned in all the colors of the 아자s. She realized she had a sword in her hand, a great gleaming length of steel, absolutely useless even had she known how to wield it. She let it fall, and it vanished before reaching the floor. “Waiting isn’t helping anything,” she muttered. Much longer, and the little courage she had managed to scrape together would surely evaporate.

Together she and 시우안 stepped toward the boundary. 엘레인’s foot touched that dividing line, and suddenly she felt herself being pulled in, sucked like water through a tube.

One instant she was standing in the hallway, staring at the horrors, the next she was lying on her belly on rough gray stone, wrists and ankles tightly tied in the small of her back, and the horrors were all around her. The cavern stretched endless in every direction; the Tower corridor no longer seemed to exist. Screams filled the air, echoing from rocky walls and a ceiling dripping stalactites. A few paces from her a huge black cauldron stood steaming over a roaring fire. A boar-snouted 트롤록, complete with tusks, was tossing in lumps that seemed to be unidentifiable roots. A cookpot. 트롤록s ate anything. Including people. She thought of her hands and feet free, but the coarse rope still dug into her flesh. Even the pale shadow of *세다르* had vanished; the True Source no longer existed for her, not here. A nightmare in truth, and she was well and truly caught.

시우안’s voice cut through the screams in a pained moan. “셰리암, listen to me!” 빛 alone knew what was being done to her; 엘레인 could not see any of the others. Only hear them. “This is a dream! *Aah . . . aaaaaaah!* Th-think how it should be!”

엘레인 took it up. “셰리암, Anaiya, everybody, listen to me! You must think of the corridor as it was! As it really is! This is only real as long as you believe it!” She set the image of the corridor in her head firmly, colored tiles in ordered rows and gilded stand-lamps and brilliant woven tapestries. Nothing changed. The screams still echoed. “You must think of the corridor! Hold it in your minds, and it will be real! The six 에스 세다이 vanished.

*The Storm Gathers*

니나브 woke the next morning at first light feeling grumpy. She had a sense of bad weather coming, yet a glance out of the window revealed not a single cloud marring the still gray sky. Already the day promised to be another oven. Her shift was sweat-damp and twisted from tossing and turning. “They think they know everything,” 니나브 muttered disparagingly. “I told them about nightmares. I warned them, and last night was not the first time.” It made no difference that all six sisters had been Healed before she so much as got back from *Tel’aran’rhiod*. Much too easily it could have ended much worse—because they thought they knew it all. The irritated tugs she gave her braid delayed redoing it for the day. The *a’dam* bracelet sometimes caught on her hair, too, but she was not about to take it off. It was 엘레인’s turn to wear it today, but she was just as likely to leave it on a peg on the wall. Worry tickled through the bracelet, and the inevitable fear, but more than anything else, frustration. Doubtless “Marigan” was already helping with breakfast; having to do chores seemed to grate at her more than being a prisoner did. “That was good thinking on your part, 엘레인. You didn’t say how you ended up in it yourself after trying to warn everybody else.”

Still scrubbing with her facecloth, 엘레인 shuddered. “It wasn’t so hard to think of it. A nightmare that size needed all of us to handle. Maybe they learned a little humility. Maybe their meeting with the 현명한 이들 tonight won’t be so bad.”

니나브 nodded to herself. As she had thought. Not about 셰리암 and the others; 에스 세다이 would find humility when goats flew on wings, and a day before the 현명한 이들 at that. About 엘레인. She had probably let herself be caught in the nightmare, though the girl would never admit it. 니나브 was not sure whether 엘레인 thought taking credit for bravery was boasting or whether she simply did not realize how brave she was. Either way, 니나브 was torn between admiration for the other woman’s courage and a wish that just once 엘레인 would acknowledge it. “I thought I saw 랜드.” That brought the facecloth down.

“Was he there in the flesh?” That was dangerous, according to the 현명한 이들; it risked losing some part of what made you human. “You warned him about that.”

“When did he start listening to sense? I only glimpsed him. Maybe he just touched *Tel’aran’rhiod* in a dream.” Unlikely, that. He apparently hedged his dreams with wards so strong she did not think he could reach the World of Dreams any other way than in the flesh, not even if he had been a Dreamwalker *and* had one of the rings. “Maybe it was somebody who looked a little like him. As I said, I only saw him for a moment, in the square in front of the Tower.”

“I should be there with him,” 엘레인 muttered. Emptying the basin into the night jar, she moved aside to let 니나브 reach the washstand. “He *needs* me.”

“What he needs is what he has always needed.” 니나브 glowered as she refilled the basin from the pitcher. She did hate washing in water that had stood all night. At least it was not cold; there was no such thing as cold water anymore. “Somebody to box his ears once a week on general principles and keep him on the straight and narrow.”

“It isn’t fair.” A clean shift going over 엘레인’s head muffled the words. “I worry about him all the time.” Her face popped out the top, looking more worried than indignant whatever her tone, and she pulled a banded white dress from one of the pegs. “I even worry about him in my *dreams*! It was just not the same when you did not see the documents yourself. All very well to learn 엘라이더 finally knew about 랜드’s amnesty, but what did she mean to do about it? Proof the Tower was approaching rulers might actually be good news; it might light a fire under the Hall. 모그헤디엔 straightened, opening her mouth, but 니나브 silenced her with a firm look—and a conspicuous touch to the *a’dam* bracelet on her wrist—and she resumed work. Immense shame and outright fury surged through the *a’dam*.

니나브 managed a smile for Nildra and murmured something, she was not sure what, then stalked off to one of the communal kitchens to find breakfast. 미렐, again. She wondered if the Green had taken against her personally for some reason. She wondered if she was going to harvest a permanently sour stomach from keeping 모그헤디엔. It was easy enough to get a clay mug full of tea with honey and a bun hot from the oven, but once she had them, she walked while she ate. Sweat beaded on her face. Even at that early hour heat was building and the air dry. The rising sun formed a dome of molten gold above the forest.

The dirt streets were full, as usual when there was light to see. 에스 세다이 glided past serenely, ignoring dust and heat, mysterious-faced on mysterious errands, often with 감시자s heeling them, cold-eyed wolves vainly pretending to be tame. There were soldiers everywhere, usually marching or riding in blocks, though 니나브 did not understand why they were allowed to crowd the streets so when they had camps in the woods. Children darted about, often aping the soldiers with sticks for swords and pikes. White-clad 수련생s trotted through the throng about their chores. Servants moved somewhat more slowly, women with armloads of sheets for 에스 세다이s’ beds or baskets of bread from the kitchens, men leading ox-carts piled with firewood, hauling chests or shouldering whole sheep carcasses for the kitchens. 니나브 kept moving. An 허락받은 자’s day was supposedly her own for the most part, unless she was teaching 수련생s, to be used studying what she chose to, alone or with an 에스 세다이, but an 허락받은 자 who appeared to be doing nothing could be snapped up by any 에스 세다이. Every time she became aware of the heavy gold ring nestling between her breasts she thought, *He has to be alive. Even if he’s forgotten me, Light, just let him be alive*. Which last, of course, only made her angrier. If al’란 Mandragoran so much as let forgetting her cross his mind, she would set him straight. He had to be alive. 감시자s often died avenging their 에스 세다이—it was as sure as the sun coming up that no 감시자 would let anything stand in the way of that retribution—but there was no way for 란 to avenge 모이라인 any more than if she had fallen off a horse and broken her neck. She and 란피어 had killed one another. He *had* to be alive. And why should she feel guilty over 모이라인’s death? True, it had freed 란 for her, but she had had nothing to do with it. The broad common room had been cleared and furnished like a reception room; its plaster walls and high ceiling had been patched, a few bright tapestries had been hung, and a few colorful rugs lay scattered on a floor that no longer looked precisely splintered but still did not want to hold a polish. The shaded interior actually seemed cool after the street. Cooler, at least. It was also in use.

로가인 stood insolently in front of one of the wide unlit fireplaces, the tails of his gold-embroidered red coat shoved behind his back, under the watchful gaze of Lelaine Akashi, her blue-fringed shawl marking the occasion as formal. Two men and a woman resplendent in embroidered silks and gold jewelry, all three graying, and one of the men nearly bald and wearing a square-cut beard and long mustache to make up for it. Small wonder; the only news more shocking would have been for the 에스 세다이 to admit the 흑색 아자 really did exist. All in all, only a few were brought to hear 로가인, yet every one of that handful was chosen for the power of the House they led. Houses that now would lend their support to the 에스 세다이 in Salidar, if not always openly, or at worst, withhold support from 엘라이더.
“Javindhra sent me word when more 에스 세다이 came,” 로가인 said, “the ones hunting me, and where they would be, so I could come on them before they knew.” Lelaine’s serene, ageless features hardened for a moment, and Burin’s hand drifted toward his sword hilt. The bearded man was staring at 로가인 so hard it was plain he was making himself do it. “에스 세다이, what of his followers? Perhaps he was safe in the Tower, but he was captured a good many leagues closer to where we stand.”

“They were not all killed or captured,” the gaunt-faced lord put in right behind him. “Most escaped, melted away. I know my history, 에스 세다이. Raolin Darksbane’s followers dared attack the 백색 탑 itself after he was taken, and Guaire Amalasan’s as well. We remember too well 로가인’s army marching across our lands to want it to come again, to rescue him.”

“You need have no fear of that.” Lelaine eyed 로가인 with a brief smile, as a woman might a fierce dog she knew tamed to her leash. “He has no more desire for glory, only to make some small restitution for the harm he did. Besides which, I doubt many of his former followers would come if he did call, not after he was carried to 타르 발론 in a cage and gentled.” Her light laugh was echoed by the 알타라ns, but only after a moment, and weakly. 로가인’s face was an iron mask.

Abruptly Lelaine noticed 니나브 just inside the doorway, and her eyebrows rose. She had exchanged pleasant words with 니나브 more than once, and praised her and 엘레인’s supposed discoveries, but she could be as quick as any other 에스 세다이 to call down an 허락받은 자 who put a foot wrong.

니나브 dropped a curtsy, gesturing with the clay mug, now empty of tea. “Pardon me, Lelaine Sedai. I must take this back to the kitchen.” She darted out into the baking street before the 에스 세다이 could say a word.

Luckily, 미렐 was nowhere in sight now. 니나브 was in no mood for yet another lecture on showing responsibility or holding her temper or any one of a dozen fool things. An even better piece of luck, 시우안 was standing not thirty paces away, facing Gareth Bryne in the middle of the street with the passing throng parting around them. You are a smaller man than I ever thought, Gareth Bryne. Do you expect me to trail after you like a camp follower when the army marches, hoping for more of your *compliments*? And you will *not* address me so, as *woman*! It sounds like ‘Here, dog!’ ”

A vein started throbbing on Bryne’s temple. “It pleases me that you keep your word, *시우안*. And if the army ever does march, I expect you to continue keeping it. In one heartbeat 시우안 went from fiery rage to icy calm. “That is no part of my oath.” You might have thought her a young 에스 세다이, standing there straight-backed with that coolly arrogant defiance, one who had not worked with the Power long enough to take on agelessness. “I will not spy for you. The change in Bryne was as lightning quick. “You would be an enemy worth crossing swords with,” he chuckled admiringly. “You would be a better. . . .” That fast the chuckle faded back into a glower. “The Hall, is it? 니나브 stepped closer. No one in the street was paying them any mind beyond a glance in passing, but she lowered her voice anyway. “What are they planning about him? Abruptly 리안 was there, and 니나브 might as well not have spoken. 시우안 and 리안 glared at one another, stiff-backed as two strange cats in a small room.

리안 sniffed, and her curls swung as she tossed her head. A sneer twisted her lips, yet her words did not match expression or tone. “I tried to talk them out of it,” she spat, but softly. “Only they had not listened to you enough to even consider it. You won’t be meeting the 현명한 이들 tonight.”

니나브 almost threw up her hands in frustration. Talking as if she were not there, as if she did not know exactly what they were talking about. There was no sign of 로가인 or Burin or the 알타라n nobles. The Blue sister shifted her shawl. “They are not what they were, of course, but one would think they could retain a little decorum. It will not do if they actually come to hair-pulling in the street.”

“Sometimes people just rub one another the wrong way,” 니나브 said. 시우안 and 리안 worked so hard to maintain their fiction, the least she could do was support it. How she hated people sneaking up on her.

Lelaine eyed 니나브’s hand on her braid, and she snatched it away. Too many knew about that habit; a habit she had tried hard to break. But what the 에스 세다이 said was “Not when it impinges on the dignity of 에스 세다이, child. “I thought the room was empty, 에스 세다이,” 니나브 said hastily. “I’m sorry. I hope I did not disturb you.” That was no answer—she could hardly say she had been hiding from 미렐—but the slender Blue only met her eyes for a moment.

“What do you think 랜드 al’Thor will do, child?”

니나브 blinked in confusion. “에스 세다이, I haven’t seen him in half a year. All I know is what I’ve heard here. Is the Hall . . . ? 에스 세다이, what has the Hall decided about him?”

Scrutinizing 니나브’s face, Lelaine pursed her lips. Those dark eyes, seeming to see inside your head, were quite unsettling. “A remarkable coincidence. You come from the same village as the 용의 환생, and so does that other girl, 에그웨인 al’Vere. Great things were expected when she became a 수련생. Do you have any idea where she is?” She did not wait for an answer. “And the other two young men, 페린 Aybara and 맷 카우톤. Both *ta’veren* as well, so I understand. Remarkable, indeed. There was a hint of compassion in her voice, and a tinge of contempt too. Those not 에스 세다이 were less, after all, and 시우안 and 리안’s ruse had definitely painted them among the least. What *had* been done complicated the whole thing, though. Stilling was rare. Before 시우안 and 리안, no woman had been tried and stilled in one hundred and forty years, and none burned out in at least a dozen. A stilled woman usually tried to get as far from 에스 세다이 as she could. No doubt if Lelaine had been stilled, she would want to forget being 에스 세다이 if she could. No doubt she would like to forget that 시우안 and 리안 had been, too, that all that had been taken away from them. If they could be seen as two women never able to channel, never 에스 세다이, a good many 에스 세다이 would be more comfortable.

“셰리암 Sedai has given me permission to try,” 니나브 said as firmly as she dared to a full sister. Lelaine held her eyes until she let her gaze drop. Her knuckles whitened around her braid before she could let go, but she kept her face smooth. Trying to trade stares with an 에스 세다이 was a woolhead’s trick for an 허락받은 자.

“We are all fools sometimes, child, yet a wise woman learns to limit how often. 니나브 dropped a curtsy, but it was being made to the 에스 세다이’s back before she reached the bottom of it. Safe from Lelaine’s eyes, she glowered at the woman. Cut her *hair*? She lifted her braid and shook it at the retreating 에스 세다이. That she had waited until it was safe made her furious, though if she had not waited she would almost certainly be on her way to join 모그헤디엔 at the laundry, with a stop to see Tiana on the way. Months sitting here in Salidar doing nothing—for all practical purposes it seemed she was, no matter what she and 엘레인 managed to pull out of 모그헤디엔—amid 에스 세다이 who did nothing except talk and wait while the world went on its way to ruin without them, and Lelaine thought she should cut her hair!
