*To Understand a Message*

그랜달 managed not to stare as she entered the room, but her streith gown went dead black before she could control herself and return it to a blue mist. 사마엘 had done enough to make anyone doubt that this chamber was in the Great Hall of the Council in 일리안. But then, she would be very surprised if anyone but he ever penetrated this far uninvited into “Lord Brend’s” apartments.

The air was pleasantly cool; in one corner rose the hollow cylinder of an exchanger. Glowbulbs, bright and steady, stood oddly in heavy gold candleholders, giving much better illumination than candles or oil lamps ever could. A small music box sat on the marble mantelpiece, producing from its memory the soft strains of a sound-sculpture that very likely had not been heard outside this room in well over three thousand years. And she recognized several of the artworks on the walls.

She paused in front of Ceran Tol’s “Tempo of Infinity.” Not a copy. “One might think you had looted a museum, 사마엘.” It was hard to keep the envy from her voice, and when she saw his faint smile, she realized she had failed.

Filling two silver-chased goblets with wine, he handed her one. “Only a stasis box. I suppose people tried to save what they could in the last days.” His smile pulled at that awful scar across his face as he beamed around the chamber, with especial fondness for the zara board projecting its field of still-transparent boxes in the air; he had always liked the more violent games. Of course, a zara board meant his stasis box had been filled by someone who followed the Great Lord; possession of a single once-human playing piece had meant imprisonment at the least on the other side. What else had he found?

Sipping her wine—and suppressing a sigh; it was from the here and now; she had hoped for a delicate Satare or one of the exquisite Comolads—she stroked her gown with beringed fingers. “I found one as well, but beyond streith, it contained the most appalling collection of useless rubbish.” After all, since he had invited her here and let her see this, it was a time for confidences. Small confidences.

“How sad for you.” Again that faint smile. He *had* found something more than playthings and pretties. “On the other hand,” he went on, “think how awful it would have been to open a box and rouse a nest of cafar, say, or a jumara, or one of 아지노르’s other little creations. Did you know there are jumara loose in the 황무지? Full-grown, though they’ll never transform now. They call them 벌레s.” He laughed so hard at that, he shook.

그랜달 smiled a good deal more warmly than she felt inside, though if her gown changed color, it was by a hair. She had had an unpleasant, in fact almost fatal, experience with one of 아지노르’s creations. The man had been brilliant in his way, but mad. None but a madman would have made the *gholam.* “You seem in very good mood.”

“Why should I not be?” he said expansively. “I all but have my hands on a cache of *angreal* and who can say what else. Do not look so surprised. Of course I’ve known that the rest of you have been trying to look over my shoulder in hopes I will lead you to it. Well, it will do you no good. Oh, I will share, but after it’s mine, and after I have first choice.” Sprawling in a heavily gilded chair—or perhaps it was solid gold; that would be like him—he balanced one boot atop the toe of the other and stroked his golden beard. “Besides, I sent an emissary to al’Thor. And the answer was favorable.”

그랜달 almost spilled her wine. “It was? I heard that he killed your messenger.” If her knowing that much shook him, he held it in. He even smiled.

“Al’Thor killed no one. Andris went there to die; do you think I wanted to wait on couriers, or *pigeons*? How he died told me al’Thor’s answer.”

“Which was?” she said carefully.

“A truce between us.”

Icy fingers seemed to dig into her scalp. It could not be true. Yet he looked more at ease than she had seen him since waking. “르웨어스 테린 would never—”

“르웨어스 테린 is long dead, 그랜달.” The interruption was amused, even mocking. No anger at all.

She covered a deep breath by pretending to drink. Could it be true? “His army is still gathering in 티어. I have seen it. That hardly looks like a truce to me.”

사마엘 laughed outright. “It takes time to redirect an army. Believe me, it will never move against me.”

“You think not? One or two of my little friends say he wants you dead because you killed some of his pet Maidens. Were I you, I would be thinking about somewhere less conspicuous, somewhere he might not find me.” Not a flicker of an eyelid out of him. It was as if all the strings that usually moved him had been cut.

“What should it matter a few Maidens died?” The look on his face was truly puzzled. “It was battle; soldiers die in battle. Al’Thor may be a farmer, but he has generals to fight his battles and explain matters. I doubt he even noticed.”

“You really never have looked at these people. They have changed as much as the land, 사마엘. Not just the 아일. In some ways, the rest have changed much more. Those soldiers were women, and to 랜드 al’Thor, that makes a difference.”

He shrugged dismissively, and she suppressed contempt, kept the streith steady in a calm fog. He had never understood that you must understand people to make them do as you wished. 강제 was all very well, but you could not use 강제 on the entire world.

She wondered whether the stasis box had been this cache that he claimed he would put his hands on soon. If he had even one *angreal.* . . . If he did, she would find out, but probably not before he let her. “I suppose we shall see how much wiser the primitive 르웨어스 테린 has become, then.” She raised a doubting eyebrow, managed a smile of her own. No reaction. Where had he found this leash for his temper? 르웨어스 테린’s name alone should have been enough to loose it. “If he fails to chase you out of 일리안 like a cosa scampering up a tree, perhaps—”

“That might be waiting too long,” he cut in smoothly. “Too long for you, that is.”

“Is that supposed to be a threat, 사마엘?” Her gown shifted to a pale rose, but she let it stay. Let him be aware she was angry. “I thought you learned long ago that threatening me is a mistake.”

“No threats, 그랜달,” he replied calmly. All of his pressure points had gone numb; nothing seemed to shift him out of that amused coolness. “Merely facts. Al’Thor will not attack me, and I will not attack him. And of course, I agreed not to aid any other Chosen should al’Thor find them. All very much in accordance with the Great Lord’s commands, wouldn’t you say?”

“Of course.” She kept her face smooth, but the streith had gone a deeper rose, losing some of its mistiness. In part the color was still anger. There was more to this, but how was she to find out?

“Which means,” he continued, “that on the Day of Return, I will very likely be the only one remaining to face al’Thor.”

“I doubt he will manage to kill all of us,” she said acidly, but acid churned in her stomach, as well. Too many of the Chosen had died. 사마엘 *had* found a way to stand aside until the last; it was the only explanation.

“You think not? Not even if he learns where you all are?” That smile deepened. “I am sure I know what 디만드레드 is scheming, but where is he hiding? Where is 세미르하제? 메사나? What about 아스모데안 and 란피어? 모그헤디엔?”
Those cold fingers returned, imprinting themselves on her skull. He would not lounge there and talk this way—he would not dare suggest what he was suggesting—unless. . . . “아스모데안 and 란피어 are dead, and I am sure 모그헤디엔 must be, too.” She was surprised to hear her own voice, hoarse and unsteady. Wine did not seem to dampen her dry throat.

“And the others?” It was just a question; his voice was not in the slightest insistent. It sent a shiver through her.

“I’ve told you what I know, 사마엘.”

“Which is nothing. When I am Nae’blis, I will choose who stands just below me. That one will have to be alive to receive the Great Lord’s touch.”

“Are you saying you have been to 세이올 굴? That the Great Lord promised you . . . ?”

“You will know all when it is time, and not before. But a small advice, 그랜달. Prepare now. Where are they?”

Her mind worked furiously. He must have had that promise. He must. But why him? No, there was no time for speculation. The Great Lord chose as he wished. And 사마엘 knew where she was, at least. She could flee 아라드 도만, establish herself elsewhere; it would not be difficult. Giving up the little games she played there, and even the larger games that might have to be abandoned, would be a small loss compared with having al’Thor—or 르웨어스 테린—come after her. She had no intention of ever confronting him directly; if 이샤마엘 and 라빈 had fallen to him, she was not about to risk his strength, not head-on. 사마엘 *must* have had the promise. If he died now. . . . He was certainly holding *세이딘*—he would be mad to say these things otherwise—and he would feel the instant she embraced *세다르.* She would be the one to die. He must have had it. “I . . . do not know where 디만드레드 or 세미르하제 is. 메사나 . . . 메사나 is in the 백색 탑. That is all I know. I swear it.”

A tightness in her chest loosened when he finally nodded. “You will find the others for me.” It was not a question. “All of them, 그랜달. If you want me to believe anyone dead, show me a corpse.”

She very much wished she dared turn him into a corpse. Her gown rippled through violent shades of red, echoing the anger and fear and shame that rippled through her uncontrollably. Very well, let him think her cowed for the moment. If he fed 메사나 to al’Thor, if he fed them all to al’Thor, so be it, so long as that kept al’Thor from her own throat. “I will try.”

“Do more than try, 그랜달. More than try.”

When 그랜달 was gone, the gateway back to her palace in 아라드 도만 closed, 사마엘 let the smile dissolve on his face. His jaws ached from holding it. 그랜달 thought too much; she was so used to making others act for her that she failed to think of acting for herself. He wondered what she would say if she ever discovered that he had manipulated her as deftly as she had manipulated so many fools in her time. He would wager everything that she never saw his real purpose. So, 메사나 was inside the 백색 탑. 메사나 in the Tower, and 그랜달 in 아라드 도만. Had 그랜달 been able to see his face then, she would have known real fear. Whatever happened, 사마엘 intended to be the one still standing on the Day of Return, to be named Nae’blis and defeat the 용의 환생.

**CHAPTER** **24**

![](images/00161.jpg)

*An Embassy*

Turning away from the musicians on the street corner, a perspiring woman puffing at a long flute and a red-faced man plucking a nine-string bittern, 에그웨인 threaded her way through the crowd with a light heart. The sun stood high in the sky, molten gold, and the paving stones were hot enough to burn through the soles of her soft boots. Sweat dripped from her nose, her shawl felt like a heavy blanket even looped loosely over her elbows, and there was enough dust in the air that she already wanted to wash, yet she smiled. Some people eyed her askance, when they thought she was not looking, which almost made her laugh. That was how they looked at 아일. People saw what they expected to see, and they saw a woman in 아일 garb, never noticing her eyes or her height.

Hawkers and peddlers cried their wares, competing against the shouts of butchers and candlemakers, the rattle and clatter from silversmiths’ and potters’ shops, the squeal of ungreased axles. Rough-tongued wagon drivers and men walking alongside ox-carts loudly contested the way with dark-lacquered sedan chairs and sober coaches with House sigils on the doors. There were musicians everywhere, along with tumblers and jugglers. A knot of pale women in riding dresses, carrying swords, swaggered by, imitating how they imagined men behaved, laughing too raucously and pushing their way in a manner that would have started a dozen fights in a hundred paces had they been men. A blacksmith’s hammer rang on his anvil. In general a babble and hum of bustle hung in the air, the noise of a city that she had almost forgotten among the 아일. Perhaps she had missed it.

She did laugh then, right there in the street. The first time she had heard the noise of a city, it had nearly stunned her. Sometimes it seemed that wide-eyed girl had been someone else.

A woman working her bay mare through the crowd turned to look at her curiously. The horse had small silver bells tied in her long mane and tail, and the woman had more bells in the dark hair that hung halfway down her back. Pretty, she could not have been much older than 에그웨인, but she had a hardness to her face, and a sharp eye, and no fewer than six knives at her belt, one nearly as large as an 아일’s. A Hunter for the Horn, no doubt.

A tall handsome man in a green coat, two swords on his back, watched the woman ride on. He was probably another. They seemed to be everywhere. As the crowd swallowed the woman on the bay, he turned and saw 에그웨인 looking at him. Smiling with sudden interest, he squared broad shoulders and started toward her.

Hastily 에그웨인 put on her coldest face, tried to combine Sorilea at her sternest with 시우안 산체, the stole of the 아미를린 석좌 around her shoulders.

He stopped, looking surprised. As he turned away, she distinctly heard him growl, “Flaming 아일.” She could not help laughing again; he must have heard despite the noise, because he stiffened, shaking his head. But he did not look back.

The source of her good mood was twofold. One was the 현명한 이들 finally agreeing that walking in the city provided as much exercise as walking around it outside the walls. Sorilea in particular did not seem to understand why she wanted to spend a minute more than she had to among throngs of wetlanders, especially cramped inside walls. Mostly, though, she felt good because they had told her that now the headaches that had puzzled them so were completely gone—she had not been able to hide them altogether—she could return to *Tel’aran’rhiod* soon. Not in time for the next meeting, three nights off, but before the one after.

That was a relief in more ways than one. An end to having to sneak into the World of Dreams. An end to laboriously working everything out for herself. An end to being terrified the 현명한 이들 would catch her and refuse to teach her any more. An end to needing to lie. It was necessary—she could not afford to waste time; there was too much to learn, and she could not believe she would have time to learn it all—but they would never understand.

아일 dotted the crowd, both in *cadin’sor* and in *gai’shain* white. The *gai’shain* went where they were sent, yet the others might well be inside the walls for their first time, and quite possibly their last. The 아일 really did not seem to like cities, though a good many had come in six days ago, to see Mangin hang. It was said he put the noose around his own neck, and made some 아일 joke about whether the rope would break his neck or his neck the rope. She had heard several 아일 repeat the joke, but never a comment about the hanging. 랜드 had liked Mangin; she was sure of it. Berelain had informed the 현명한 이들 of the sentence as though telling them their wash would be ready the next day, and the 현명한 이들 had listened the same way. 에그웨인 did not think she would ever understand 아일. She was very much afraid she did not understand 랜드 anymore. As for Berelain, 에그웨인 understood her all too well; that one was only interested in men who were alive.

With thoughts like those, it took an effort to regain her good mood. The city was certainly no cooler than outside the walls—in fact, with no breeze and people so close, it might have been hotter—and nearly as dusty, but at least she was not trudging along with nothing to look at but the ashes of Foregate. A few more days and she would be able to learn again, to really learn. That put a smile back on her face.

She stopped near a wiry, damp-faced Illuminator; it was easy to tell what he was, or had been. His thick mustaches were not covered by the diaphanous veil 타라본ers often wore, but baggy breeches, embroidered on the legs, and an equally loose shirt embroidered across the chest marked him well enough. He was selling finches and warblers in crudely made cages. With their chapter house burned by the Shaido, a number of Illuminators were trying to find the means to return to 타라본.

“I have it from the most reliable source,” he was telling a handsome graying woman in a plainly cut dark blue dress. A merchant, no doubt, catching a jump on those waiting for better times in 케렌. “The 에스 세다이,” the Illuminator confided, leaning over a caged bird to whisper, “they are divided. The 에스 세다이, they are at war. With one another.” The merchant nodded agreement.

에그웨인 stopped pretending to consider a green-headed finch and moved on, though she had to hop out of the way of a round-faced gleeman, striding along with self-important flourishes of his patch-covered cloak. Gleemen knew very well that they were among the few wetlanders welcome in the 황무지; 아일 did not intimidate them. At least, they pretended so.

That rumor troubled her. Not that the Tower had split apart—that could not have been kept secret much longer—but talk of war between 에스 세다이. Knowing that 에스 세다이 were set against 에스 세다이 was like knowing one part of her family was set against another, just barely tolerable for knowing the reasons, yet the thought that it might come to more. . . . If only there were some way to Heal the Tower, to make it whole again without bloodshed.

A little farther down the street, a perspiring Foregate woman who might have been pretty if her face were cleaner was dispensing rumor along with ribbons and pins from a tray hung from a neckstrap. She wore a blue silk dress, slashed with red in the skirt, that had been made for a shorter woman; the heavily worn hem was high enough to show her stout shoes, and holes in the sleeves and bodice showed where embroidery had been picked out. “I tell you a fact,” she informed the women picking over her tray, “there has been 트롤록s seen around the city. Ah, yes, that green will set off your eyes. Hundreds of 트롤록s and. . . .”

에그웨인 barely paused. If there had been even one 트롤록 anywhere near the city, the 아일 would have known long before it became street gossip. She wished the 현명한 이들 gossiped. Well, they did, sometimes, but only about other 아일. As far as 아일 were concerned, nothing about wetlanders was very absorbing. Being able to pop into 엘라이더’s study in *Tel’aran’rhiod* whenever she wanted and read the woman’s letters had accustomed her to knowing what was happening in the world, though.

Abruptly 에그웨인 realized she was looking around differently, looking at people’s faces. There were 에스 세다이 eyes-and-ears in 케렌 as surely as she was sweating. 엘라이더 must receive a report a day by pigeon from 케렌, if not more. Tower spies, 아자 spies, spies for individual 에스 세다이. They were everywhere, often where and who you least suspected. Why were those two tumblers just standing there? Were they catching their breath, or watching her? They sprang back into action, one leaping up to a handstand on the other’s shoulders.

A spy for the 황색 아자 had once tried to bundle 엘레인 and 니나브 off to 타르 발론, on orders issued by 엘라이더. 에그웨인 did not actually know that 엘라이더 wanted her as well, but assuming anything else would be very foolish. 에그웨인 could not make herself believe that 엘라이더 would forgive anyone who had worked closely for the woman she deposed.

For that matter, some of the 에스 세다이 in Salidar probably had eyes-and-ears here too. If word ever reached them of “에그웨인 Sedai of the 녹색 아자. . . .” It could be anybody. That skinny woman in the shop door, apparently studying a bolt of dark gray cloth. Or the blowsy woman lolling beside the tavern door, flapping her apron at her face. Or that fat fellow with his pushcart full of pies—Why was he looking at her so strangely? She very nearly headed for the nearest city gate.

It was the fat fellow who stopped her, or rather the way he suddenly tried to cover his pies with his hands. He was staring at her because she had been staring at him. He was probably afraid an 아일 “savage” was going to take some of his wares without paying.

에그웨인 laughed weakly. 아일. Even people who looked her in the face assumed she was 아일. A Tower agent who was looking for her would walk right past. Feeling a good deal better, she went back to meandering through the streets, listening where she could.

The trouble was, she had grown used to knowing things just weeks, or even days, after they happened, and with a certainty that they had happened. Rumor might cross a hundred miles in a day or take a month, and it birthed ten daughters every day. Today she learned that 시우안 had been executed because she unearthed the 흑색 아자, that 시우안 *was* 흑색 아자 and still alive, that the 흑색 아자 had driven those 에스 세다이 who were not Black from the Tower. They were not new tales, only variations on old. One new story, spreading like fire in a summer meadow, was that the Tower had been behind all the false 용; that made her so angry she stalked away stiff-backed every time she heard it. Which meant she did a good bit of stiff-backed stalking. She heard that 안도르ans in Aringill had declared some noblewoman queen—Dylin, Delin, the name varied—now that 모르가세 was dead, which might be true, and that 에스 세다이 were running around 아라드 도만 doing very improbable things, which was certainly untrue. The Prophet was Coming to 케렌; the Prophet had been crowned King of 게알단—no, 아마디시아; the 용의 환생 had killed the Prophet for blasphemy. The 아일 were all leaving; no, they meant to settle and stay. Berelain was to be crowned on the Sun Throne. A skinny little man with shifty eyes nearly got himself beaten by his listeners outside a tavern for saying that 랜드 was one of the 버림받은 자들, but 에그웨인 stepped into that without thought.

“Have you no honor?” she demanded coldly. The four coarse-faced men who had been on the point of grabbing the skinny fellow blinked at her. They were 케렌인, not all that much taller than she, but much bulkier, with the broken noses and sunken knuckles of brawlers, yet she held them where they stood with her sheer intensity. That and the presence of 아일 in the street; they were not fool enough to become rough with an 아일 woman, as they thought, in those circumstances. “If you must face a man for what he says, face him one at a time, in honor. This is not battle; you shame yourselves to go four at one.”

They stared at her as if she were mad, and slowly her face reddened. She hoped they thought it anger. Not how dare you pick on someone weaker, but how dare you not let him fight you one by one? She had just lectured them as if they followed *ji’e’toh.* Of course, if they did, there would have been no need to lecture.

One of the men ducked his head in a sort of half-bow. His nose was not only crooked, the tip was missing. “Uh . . . he is gone now . . . uh. . . . Mistress. Can we go too?”

It was true; the skinny man had used her interference to vanish. She felt a flash of contempt. Running because he feared to face four. How could he bear the shame? Light, she was doing it again.

She opened her mouth to say that of course they could—and nothing came out. They took her silence for assent, or maybe excuse, and hurried away, but she barely noticed them go. She was too busy staring at the back of a mounted party making its way up the street.

She did not recognize the dozen or so green-cloaked soldiers forcing a path through the crowd, but who they escorted was a different matter. She could only see the backs of the women—five or six, she thought, between the soldiers—just parts of their backs, but that was more than enough. Much more. The women wore light dustcloaks, pale linen in shades of brown, and 에그웨인 found herself staring right at what seemed to be a pure white disc embroidered on the back of one of those cloaks. Only the stitching picked out the white Flame of 타르 발론 from the border signifying the 백색 아자. She caught a glimpse of green, of red. Red! Five or six 에스 세다이, riding toward the Royal Palace, where a copy of the Dragon banner waved fitfully atop a stepped tower alongside one of 랜드’s crimson flags bearing the ancient 에스 세다이 symbol. Some called *that* the Dragon banner, and others al’Thor’s banner, or even the 아일 banner, and a dozen other names besides.

Wriggling through the crowd, she followed them maybe twenty paces, then stopped. A Red sister—at least one Red that she had seen—had to mean this was the long-expected embassy from the Tower, the one 엘라이더 had written would escort 랜드 to 타르 발론. More than two months since that letter arrived by a hard-riding courier; this party must have left not long behind.

They would not find 랜드—not unless he had slipped in unannounced; she had decided that he had somehow rediscovered the Talent called 이동, but that put her no closer to knowing how it was done—yet whether they found 랜드 or not, they must not find 에그웨인. The best she could expect was to be hauled up short as an 허락받은 자 out of the Tower with no full sister to oversee her, and that could be expected only if 엘라이더 really was not hunting for her. Even then they would haul her back to 타르 발론, and 엘라이더; she had no illusions that she could resist five or six 에스 세다이.

With a last look after the receding 에스 세다이, she gathered her skirts and began to run, dodging between people, sometimes caroming off them, ducking under the noses of teams pulling wagons or carriages. Angered shouts followed her. When she at last dashed through one of the tall square-arched city gates, the hot wind hit her in the face. Unhindered by buildings, it carried sheets of dust that made her cough, but she kept running, all the way back to the Wise One’s low tents.

To her surprise a sleek gray mare, saddle and bridle worked and fringed with gold, stood outside Amys’ tent, in the charge of a *gai’shain* who kept his eyes down except when patting the spirited animal. Ducking inside, she found the rider, Berelain, sipping tea with Amys and Bair and Sorilea, all stretched out on bright, tasseled cushions. A white-robed woman, Rodera, knelt to one side, meekly waiting to refill cups.

“There are 에스 세다이 in the city,” 에그웨인 said as soon as she was inside, “heading toward the Sun Palace. It must be 엘라이더’s embassy to 랜드.”

Berelain rose gracefully; 에그웨인 had to admit, if grudgingly, that the woman was graceful. And her riding dress was decently cut, for even she was not fool enough to go riding in the sun in her usual garb. The others rose with her. “I must return to the palace, it seems,” she sighed. “빛 knows how they will feel about no one there to greet them. Amys, if you know where Rhuarc is, could you send a message for him to meet me?”

Amys nodded, but Sorilea said, “You should not depend on Rhuarc so much, girl. 랜드 al’Thor gave 케렌 to you to tend. Let most men have a finger, and they will have the whole hand before you know. Let a clan chief have a finger, and he will have the entire arm.”

“It is true,” Amys murmured. “Rhuarc is the shade of my heart, but it is true.”

Pulling slim riding gloves from behind her belt, Berelain began tugging them on. “He reminds me of my father. Too much so, sometimes.” For an instant she grimaced ruefully. “But he gives very good advice. And he knows when to loom, and how much. I think even 에스 세다이 must be impressed by Rhuarc staring at them.”

Amys laughed in her throat. “He is impressive. I will send him to you.” She kissed Berelain lightly on the forehead and each cheek.

에그웨인 stared; that was how a mother kissed her son or daughter. What *was* going on between Berelain and the 현명한 이들? She could not ask, of course. Such a question would be shaming to her and to the 현명한 이들. To Berelain too, though Berelain would not know it, and 에그웨인 would not mind shaming Berelain until her hair fell out.

As Berelain turned to leave the tent, 에그웨인 put a hand on the woman’s arm. “They must be handled carefully. They’ll not be friendly toward 랜드, but the wrong words, a wrong move, could make them open enemies.” That was true enough, but not what she needed to say. She would rather have her tongue torn out than ask a favor of Berelain.

“I have dealt with 에스 세다이 before, 에그웨인 Sedai,” the other woman said dryly.

에그웨인 refrained from drawing a deep breath. 아비엔다 jerked free. “No! He thought he had hidden it, but his face must have changed. 아비엔다 slowly trailed off and stood there staring at him, breathing hard. Padan Fain sat with his feet up on a hassock, studying the beauty of new-breaking sunlight glittering on the curved blade of the dagger that he turned over and over in his hands. Carrying it at his belt was not enough; from time to time he simply had to handle it. The large ruby set in the pommel shone with a deep malevolence. The dagger was part of him, or he of it. *Fire and Spirit*

Not that it did much good—sweat popped out again right away—but she wanted to look her best inside. She wanted to look cool, serene, dignified. Small chance of that. To top it off, her weather sense was nagging at her; the molten sun should have been hidden by roiling black clouds and threatening bolts of lightning.

The 감시자s lounging out front did not look like guards at first glance, but they were. They reminded her of the 아일 she had seen in the Stone of 티어; they probably looked like wolves even when asleep. A bald, square-faced man, no taller than she but nearly as wide as he was tall, trotted out of the Little Tower and down the street, the hilt of the sword on his back thrusting up over his shoulder. Even he—Jori, bonded to Morvrin—managed it.

Top-knotted Uno passed, threading his horse through the crowd and hardly seeming to acknowledge the heat despite the steel plates and mail that covered him from the shoulders down. He twisted in his saddle to watch her with his good eye, and her face darkened. 비르기테 *had* talked. Every time the man saw her he was obviously waiting for her to ask him for horses. She was almost ready to. Even 엘레인 could not say they were doing any good. Well, she could, and did, but she should not.

Uno rode out of sight around a corner, and 니나브 sighed. She was just trying to put off going inside. 미렐 might be there. Blotting her face again, she frowned at her wrinkled hand—today would be the eleventh scrubbing pots, with twenty-nine more to go; twenty-nine!—and went in.

It was slightly cooler in what had been the common room when the Little Tower was an inn, offering a little relief to her aching head. Everyone called it “the waiting room” now. No time had been wasted for repairs here. The fireplaces had stones missing, and lathing showed through holes in the plaster. Areina and Nicola were working brooms with another 수련생, but making little impression on the age-roughened floor; Areina wore a scowl, but, then, she was never pleased at having to do chores with the 수련생s. No one went choreless in Salidar. At the far end of the room Romanda was speaking with two slender, aged 에스 세다이—their faces might be ageless, but their hair was white—plainly new arrivals by the thin dustcloaks still hanging down their backs. No sign of 미렐, which brought a sigh of relief; the woman raked 니나브 over the coals at every opportunity, then raked her the other way! 에스 세다이 sat at tables, mismatched but carefully arranged in rows, working over parchments or issuing orders to 감시자s and servants, but fewer than the first time she had seen the room. Only the 의석자들 and their servants lived on the floors above now; everyone else had been removed to make space for 에스 세다이 to work in. The Little Tower had taken on attributes of the 백색 탑, the precise formality above all. When 니나브 first saw this room it had had a bustle about it, an air of something being done. A false air, then. Now it seemed almost slow, but it was the feel of the 백색 탑.

Approaching one of the tables, not the nearest, she curtsied carefully. “Pardon, 에스 세다이, but I was told 시우안 and 리안 are here. Could you tell me where to find them?”

Brendas’ pen stopped moving and she looked up with cool dark eyes. 니나브 had chosen her instead of someone nearer the door because Brendas was one of the few 에스 세다이 who had never grilled her about 랜드. Besides, once, when 시우안 was Amyrlin, 시우안 had chosen Brendas as one who could be trusted. That had nothing to do with this, but 니나브 found small comforts where she could.

“They are with some of the 의석자들, child.” Brendas’ voice was chimes, as emotionless as her pale face. Whites seldom showed emotion, but Brendas never showed any.

니나브 stifled an irritated sigh. If 의석자들 had them reporting on their eyes-and-ears, they might not be free for hours yet. Maybe not for the rest of the day. By then she would be head-down among the pots. “Thank you, 에스 세다이.”

Brendas stopped her curtsy with a gesture. “Did Theodrin make any progress with you yesterday?”

“No, 에스 세다이.” If her voice was bit tight, a touch curt, she had reason. Theodrin had said she meant to try everything, and apparently she really did mean everything. Yesterday’s effort had involved sipping wine to relax her, only somehow 니나브 had ended up taking more than just a few sips. She did not think she would ever forget being carried back to her room singing—singing!—or remember without going red in the face. Brendas had to know. Everyone had to know. 니나브 wanted to writhe.

“I only ask because your studies seem to be suffering. I’ve heard several sisters remark that you appear to have reached the end of your remarkable discoveries. Your extra chores might be the problem—but 엘레인 reveals something new every day, even with teaching her classes and working at the pots. A number of sisters are wondering whether they might not be able to help you more than Theodrin can. If we took it in turns, working you all day every day might prove more fruitful than these informal sessions with someone who is, after all, little more than 허락받은 자 herself.” It was all delivered in a level tone without the slightest accusation, yet 니나브’s face heated as if she had been shouted at.

“I’m sure Theodrin will find the key any day, 에스 세다이,” she almost whispered. “I will try harder, 에스 세다이.” Bobbing a hurried curtsy, she whirled around before Brendas could stop her again. With the result that she bumped into one of the two white-haired newcomers. They looked enough alike to be sisters in truth, almost mirror images of one another, with fine bones and long patrician faces.

The bump was more of a brush, really, and she did try to apologize, but the 에스 세다이 fixed her with a stare to do a hawk proud. “Watch where you are going, 허락받은 자. In my day, an 허락받은 자 who tried to trample 에스 세다이 would have had hair whiter than mine by the time she finished scrubbing floors.”

The other touched her arm. “Oh, do let the child go, Vandene. We have work to do.”

Vandene directed a sharp sniff at 니나브, but allowed herself to be led outside.

Waiting a moment to let them leave, 니나브 saw 셰리암 come out of one of the meeting rooms with 미렐, Morvrin and 베오닌. 미렐 saw her, too, and started in her direction, but only a step before 셰리암 and Morvrin each put a hand on the Green sister’s arms and spoke quickly and softly, with many a glance at 니나브. Still talking, the four crossed the room and disappeared through another door.

니나브 waited until she was back in front of the Little Tower before giving her braid a firm, deliberate tug. They had met the 현명한 이들 last night. Guessing why the others had stopped 미렐 from speaking was easy enough. If 에그웨인 had finally been there in the Heart of the Stone, she was not to be told. 니나브 al’Meara was in disgrace. 니나브 al’Meara was scrubbing pots like a 수련생 when she might have been at least a step higher than 허락받은 자. 니나브 al’Meara was getting nowhere with Theodrin, and all her marvelous discoveries had dried up. 니나브 al’Meara would never be 에스 세다이. She had known it was a mistake to start funneling everything from 모그헤디엔 through 엘레인. She had known it!

Her tongue tried to curl up at the memory of a vile taste. Boiled catfern and powdered mavinsleaf. An antidote she had used on many a child who would not stop lying. All right; she *had* been the one to suggest it herself, but it was still a mistake. 에스 세다이 were no longer talking about her innovations; they talked about the lack of them. 에스 세다이 who had never taken more than a passing interest in her block were now caught up in how to break it down. She could not win. One way or another she was going to end up with 에스 세다이 examining her from hair to toenails, sunup to sundown.

She yanked harder on her braid, hard enough to hurt her scalp, and the way her head felt, that did nothing for her temper. A soldier in an archer’s flat helmet and padded jerkin slowed to look at her curiously, but she gave him such a stare of refined malevolence that he stumbled over his own feet and quickly lost himself in the throng. *Why* did 엘레인 have to be so stubborn?

A man’s hands closed on her shoulders, and she whirled about with words that would rip his head from his neck. They died on her tongue.

톰 Merrilin grinned down at her through his long white mustaches, sharp blue eyes twinkling in his gnarled face. “By the look of you, 니나브, I could almost think you were angry, but I know you have such a sweet disposition people ask you to dabble your fingers in their tea.”

Juilin Sandar was there beside him, the lean fellow looking carved from dark wood, leaning on his thumb-thick bamboo staff. Juilin was 타이런, not 타라본er, but he still wore that ridiculous flat-topped conical red cap, even more battered than she had last seen it. He snatched it off when she glanced at him. Both men were dusty and travel-worn, their faces gaunt, though neither had been particularly fleshy to begin with. They looked as if they had spent the weeks since leaving Salidar sleeping in their clothes when they were not in the saddle.

Before 니나브 could open her mouth, they were hit by a human storm. 엘레인 flung herself at 톰 so hard he staggered. He of course put his hands under her arms and hoisted her, whirling her around in a circle like a child despite his slight limp. He was laughing when he set her down again, and so was she. She reached up and tugged at one of his mustaches, and they fell to laughing even harder. He examined her hands, as wrinkled as 니나브’s, asking what sort of trouble she had dived into without him to keep her on the straight and narrow, and she replied that she had no need of anyone to tell her what to do, only she spoiled it by blushing, and giggling, and biting her lip.

니나브 took a deep breath. Sometimes the pair of them took playing at father and daughter entirely too far. Sometimes 엘레인 seemed to think she was about ten, and so did 톰. “I thought you had a 수련생 class this morning, 엘레인.”

The other woman glanced at her sideways, then gathered herself in an attempt at decorum that came too late, and set about straightening her banded dress. “I asked Calindin to take it,” she said casually. “I thought I might keep you company. And I’m glad I did,” she added with a grin for 톰. “Now we can hear everything you learned in 아마디시아.”

니나브 sniffed. Keep her company indeed. She did not remember everything about yesterday, but she remembered 엘레인 laughing while getting her undressed and putting her to bed with the sun not yet all the way down. And she was sure she remembered the woman asking whether she wanted a bucket of water to cool her head.

톰 noticed nothing; most men were blind, though he was sharp enough usually. “We will have to be quick,” he said. “Now 셰리암’s drained us dry, she means to have us report to some of the 의석자들 in person. Luckily, it boils down well enough. There aren’t enough 백의단 along the Eldar to keep a mouse from crossing, if he had drums and trumpets to announce him a day ahead. Except for a strong force on the 타라본 border and the men he has trying to hold back the Prophet in the north, Niall seems to be gathering every last Whitecloak around 아마디시아, and 아일론 is pulling in his soldiers, too. Talk of Salidar had started in the streets before we left, but if Niall has even thought about the place twice, I could find not a hint of it anywhere.”

“타라본,” Juilin muttered, studying his cap. “All ill country for anyone who doesn’t know how to take care of herself, or so we heard.”

니나브 was not sure which of the two was best at dissembling, but she was sure either could lie to your face to make a wool merchant blue with envy. And right then, she was sure they were hiding something.

엘레인 saw more than that. Gripping 톰’s lapel, she peered up at him. “You heard something about Mother,” she said calmly, and it was not a question.

톰 knuckled his mustaches. “There are a hundred rumors on every street in 아마디시아, child, each wilder than the last.” His gnarled leathery face was pure innocence and openness, but the man had not been innocent the day he was born. “It’s said the whole 백색 탑 is here in Salidar, with ten thousand 감시자s ready to cross the Eldar. It’s said 에스 세다이 have captured Tanchico, and 랜드 has wings he uses to fly around in the night, and—”

“톰?” 엘레인 said.

He snorted, glaring at Juilin and 니나브 as though this were their fault. “Child, it’s just a rumor, as crazed as any we heard. I could not confirm anything, and believe me, I tried. I meant not to mention it. It just stirs up your pain. Let it pass, child.”

“톰.” Much firmer. Shifting his feet, Juilin looked as if he wished he were somewhere else. 톰 just looked grim.

“Well, if you must hear it. Everybody in 아마디시아 seems to think your mother is in the Fortress of the Light, that she’s going to lead an army of 백의단 back to 안도르.”

엘레인 shook her head, laughing softly. “Oh, 톰, do you think I would worry over something like that? Mother would never go to the 백의단. I could wish she had. I could wish she was alive to. Even though it violates everything she ever taught me—bringing foreign soldiers into 안도르; and 백의단!—I could wish it. But if wishes were wings . . .” Her smile was sad, but it was a muted sadness. “I have done my grieving, 톰. Mother is dead, and I must do my best to be worthy of her. She would never have gone running after ridiculous rumors, or wept over them either.”

“Child,” he said awkwardly.

니나브 wondered what if anything he himself felt about 모르가세’s death. Hard as it was to believe, he had been 모르가세’s lover once, when she was young and 엘레인 little more than a babe. Back then he must not have looked as though he had been left to dry in the sun too long. 니나브 knew little more of how or why it ended than that he had slipped out of Caemlyn with an arrest warrant at his heels. Not the mark of a love to be told in the stories. At the moment he certainly appeared concerned only with whether 엘레인 was telling the truth or hiding her hurt, with patting her shoulder and stroking her hair. If 니나브 had not wished they would just once snap at one another like normal people, she would have thought it a pretty picture.

A throat clearing broke up the vignette. “Master Merrilin?” Tabitha said, spreading her white dress in a quick curtsy. “Master Sandar? 셰리암 Sedai says the 의석자들 are ready to receive you. She says you were not supposed to leave the Little Tower.”

“The Little Tower, is it?” 톰 said dryly, eyeing the former inn. “엘레인, they can’t keep us forever. When we’re done, you and I can discuss . . . whatever you wish.” Motioning Tabiya to lead, he marched inside, his limp obvious, the way it was when he was tired. Juilin squared his shoulders and followed as though walking to a gallows; he was 타이런, after all.

니나브 and 엘레인 stood there, neither quite looking at the other.

Finally, 니나브 said, “I was not—” at the same time that 엘레인 said, “I should not—” They cut off together, and moments passed in fidgeting with skirts and blotting faces.

“It is too hot to just stand here,” 니나브 said at last.

It was unlikely that the 의석자들 who were hearing 시우안 and 리안’s reports would stop to hear 톰 and Juilin’s. They split such things among them. That left 로가인, much as she wished it did not. She would not learn anything. But it was better than twiddling her thumbs until a dozen 에스 세다이 descended on her with an hourly schedule.

With a sigh she started down the street. 엘레인 came along as though she had been invited. That helped 니나브 find the anger she was going to need. Abruptly she realized that 엘레인’s wrists were bare.

“Where is the bracelet?” she asked softly. No one in the street would understand if they heard, but caution once forgotten could be forgotten once too often. “Where is Marigan?”

“The bracelet is in my pouch, 니나브.” 엘레인 stepped aside to let a high-wheeled cart pass, then joined 니나브 again behind the cart. “Marigan is doing our laundry, with about twenty other women around her. And groaning every time she moves. She said something she didn’t think 비르기테 would hear, and 비르기테. . . . I *had* to take the thing off, 니나브. 비르기테 had the right, and it *hurt.* I told Marigan to say she fell down some stairs.”

니나브 sniffed, but her heart was not in it. She had not been wearing the bracelet much of late. Not because she could not hand over anything she dug out as her own. She was still sure 모그헤디엔 knew *something* about 치유 even if she did not realize it herself—nobody could be that blind—and there was the trick of detecting a man’s channeling that 모그헤디엔 kept saying they almost had right. The truth of it was, she was afraid she might do far worse than 비르기테 had if she had any more contact with the woman than was absolutely necessary. Maybe it was the way satisfaction seemed to underlie everything else even when 모그헤디엔 was groaning from the fed-back pain of 니나브 trying to master that detection. Maybe it was remembering how afraid she had been, alone with the woman without the bracelet. Maybe growing disgust at keeping one of the 버림받은 자들 from judgment. Maybe some of all of it. What she did know was that she had to make herself put on the bracelet now, and that whenever she saw 모그헤디엔’s face, she wanted to pound it with her fists.

“I should not have laughed,” 엘레인 said. “I am sorry I did.”

니나브 stopped dead so suddenly that a horseman had to jerk his reins to keep from riding over her. He shouted something before the crowd carried him away, but shock muffled his words beyond hearing. Not shock at the apology. At what she had to say. The right thing to say. The truth.

Unable to look at 엘레인, she started walking again. “You had every right to laugh. I. . . .” She swallowed hard. “I made a complete fool of myself.” She had. A few sips, Theodrin said; a cup. And she emptied the pitcher. If you were going to fail, better to have some other reason than that you just could not do it. “You should have sent for that bucket and dunked my head until I could recite *The Great Hunt of the Horn* without a mistake.” She risked a glance from the corner of her eye. Small spots of color rested in 엘레인’s cheeks. So there had been mention of a bucket.

“It could happen to anyone,” the other woman said simply.

니나브 felt her own cheeks heating. When it had happened to 엘레인, she had dunked the girl to wash away the wine. “You should have done whatever you needed to . . . to sober me.”

It was quite the oddest argument 니나브 could remember, with her insisting she had been a total fool and deserved whatever came of it, while 엘레인 made excuse after excuse for her. 니나브 did not understand why it felt so refreshing, taking all the blame on herself that way. She could not recall ever doing that before, not without hedging as far as she was able. She very nearly got angry with 엘레인 for not agreeing that she had been a childish buffoon. It lasted until they reached the small thatched house on the edge of the village where 로가인 was kept.

“If you don’t stop this,” 엘레인 said finally, “I vow I’ll send for a bucket of water right this instant.”

니나브 opened her mouth, then closed it again. Even in this newfound euphoria of admitting she had been wrong, that was going too far. Feeling this good, she could not face 로가인. Feeling this good, it would be useless anyway, without 모그헤디엔 and the bracelet she definitely felt too fine to put on. She glanced at the two 감시자s standing guard beside the stone-linteled door. They were not close enough to hear, but she still pitched her voice low. “엘레인, let’s go. Tonight.” With 톰 and Juilin in Salidar, there was no need to ask Uno to find horses. “Not to Caemlyn, if you don’t want. To Ebou Dar. Merilille will never find that bowl, and 셰리암 will never let us go find it. What do you say? Tonight?”

“No, 니나브. What good can we do 랜드 if they take us for runaways? Which is what we’d be. You promised, 니나브. You promised, if we found something.”

“I promised if we found something we could use. All we’ve found is this!” 니나브 thrust her shriveled hands under the other woman’s nose.

The firmness slid from 엘레인’s face, and her voice; she pursed her lips and studied the ground. “니나브, you know I told 비르기테 we were staying. Well, it seems she told Uno that under no circumstances was he to provide you with a horse unless she said so. She told him you were thinking of running away. I didn’t find out until it was too late.” Her head tossed irritably. “If this is what having a 감시자 is like, I don’t know why anybody wants one.”

니나브 thought her eyes might burst from indignation. So *that* was why he had been staring at her. Euphoria vanished in a heat of—well, partly anger, partly humiliation. The man *knew*; he thought she. . . . Wait. For a moment she frowned at 엘레인, then decided not to voice the question that had come to mind. Was 니나브 the only name 비르기테 had mentioned to Uno, or was 엘레인 perhaps included? 엘레인 had found herself quite an adopted family. In 톰, an indulgent father who wanted to teach her everything he knew, and in 비르기테, an older sister who thought it was her job to keep the younger from breaking her neck riding horses she could not handle yet.

“In that case,” she said flatly, “let’s see what I can learn from 로가인.”

It was a small house, only two rooms, but thick stone walls made it relatively cool. 로가인 was in his shirtsleeves, smoking a pipe and reading by a window. The 에스 세다이 were taking good care of him. The chairs and tables were as fine as anything in Salidar—nothing elaborate, but well made, though nothing matched anything else—and a scroll-woven red-and-gold carpet covered much of a floor that was swept so clean 니나브 doubted he did the sweeping.

He set his book down when they entered, seemingly not at all put out by the lack of a knock. Rising leisurely, he tapped out his pipe, donned his coat and only then made a smooth leg. “It is good to see you again after so long. I thought you had forgotten me. Will you join me in some wine? The 에스 세다이 keep me on short supply, but what they do let me have is not bad at all.”

The offer of wine would have been enough—니나브 barely suppressed a wince—if she had needed more. Thinking of Uno, the fact that he was male was enough. No need to pull up any of her anger from the Little Tower. Thinking of it added its bit, though. The True Source was suddenly there, an unseen warmth just out of sight. She opened herself, and *세다르* flooded her; if what she had felt earlier was euphoria, this was beyond ecstasy. She *was* surrendering to it, burn Theodrin!

“Sit down,” she told him coldly. “I’ll have no chatter out of you. Answer when you’re spoken to, and otherwise hold your tongue.”
로가인 only shrugged and complied, meek as a puppy. No, not meek; that smile was pure insolence. Part came from his feelings toward 에스 세다이, 니나브 was certain, and part. . . . He watched 엘레인 take another chair, arranging her skirts with a studied care, and even if 니나브 had not seen what he was looking at, she would have known it was a woman. There was no smirking about it, no leering, just. . . . 니나브 did not know what, only that he directed the same at her, and she was suddenly very much aware that she was a woman and he a man. Maybe it was just that he was handsome and had broad shoulders, but she liked to think better of herself. Of course that was not it.

Clearing her throat, she wove filaments of *세다르* into him, Air and Water, Fire and Earth, Spirit. All the elements of 치유, but used now to probe. It would have helped to lay her hands on him, but she could not bring herself to do that. Bad enough to touch him with the Power. He was healthy as a bull and almost as strong, nothing wrong with him in the slightest—except for the hole.

It was not really a hole, more a feeling that what seemed continuous was not, that what seemed smooth and straight was really skirting around an absence. She knew that sensation well, from the early days, back when she thought she might really learn something. It still made her skin crawl.

He looked up at her intently. She did not remember moving closer. His face was fixed in a mask of brazen contempt; she might not be 에스 세다이, but she was the next thing to it.

“How can you do all of that at once?” 엘레인 asked. “I could not keep track of half of it.”

“Hush,” 니나브 murmured. Hiding the effort required, she took 로가인’s head in her hands roughly. Yes. It was better with physical contact, the impressions sharper.

She directed the full flow of *세다르* into where the hole should have been—and was almost surprised to find an emptiness. Of course, she still did not expect to learn anything. Men were as different from women in the Power as they were in flesh, maybe more so. She might as well study a rock to find out about fish. It was hard to keep her thoughts on what she was doing, knowing she was only going through motions, killing time as it were.

*What is 미렐 going to say? Would she keep back a message from 에그웨인?* That emptiness, so small she could pass right over it, was vast once she slipped the flows inside, immense enough to swallow them all. *If only I could talk to 에그웨인. I’ll wager once she knows the Tower is sending an embassy to 랜드, and the 에스 세다이 here are just sitting on their hands, she’ll help me convince 엘레인 we’ve done all we can here.* Vast emptiness; nothingness. What about what she had found in 시우안 and 리안, the feel of something cut? She was sure it was real, however faint. Men and women might be different, but maybe. . . . *All I need to do is talk to her somehow. She’ll see that 랜드 would be better off with us there. 엘레인 will listen to her; 엘레인 thinks 에그웨인 knows 랜드 better than anybody else.* There it was. Something cut. Just an impression, but the same as in 시우안 and 리안. *So how do I find her? If only she’d pop into our dreams again. I’ll bet I can talk her into joining us. The three of us would do much better with 랜드. Together, we could tell him what we learn in* Tel’aran’rhiod, *keep him from making some wool-headed mistake with the 에스 세다이. She’ll see that.* Something about that cut. . . . If it was bridged with Fire and Spirit, so. . . .

It was the slight widening of 로가인’s eyes that told her what she had done. Breath froze in her throat. She backed away from him so fast she stumbled over her skirt.

“니나브,” 엘레인 said, sitting up straight, “what is the mat—?”

A heartbeat, and 니나브 had all of *세다르* she could hold redirected into a shield. “Go find 셰리암,” she said hurriedly. “Nobody else but 셰리암. Tell her. . . .” She drew a deep breath that seemed like her first in hours; her heart was speeding to beat galloping horses. “Tell her I’ve Healed 로가인.”
