**CHAPTER** **36**

![](images/00161.jpg)

*The Amyrlin Is Raised*

에그웨인 raised her head from the pillows and looked around, for a moment surprised to find herself in a canopied bed in a large room. Early-morning light spilled in at the windows, and a plumply pretty woman in a simple gray wool dress was setting a large white pitcher of hot water on the washstand. Chesa had been introduced to her last night as her maid. The Amyrlin’s maid. A covered tray already sat beside her comb and brush on a narrow table beneath a mirror with a silver-worked frame. The smell of hot bread and stewed pears drifted in the air.

Anaiya had prepared the room for 에그웨인’s arrival. The furnishings still did not match, but they were the best Salidar had to offer, from the padded armchair upholstered in green silk to the stand-mirror in the corner with all its gilding intact to the ornately carved wardrobe where her belongings now hung. Unfortunately, Anaiya’s taste seemed to run heavily to frothy lace and frills. Both thickly bordered the canopy of the bed and the drawn-back bed curtains, and one or the other decked the table and its stool, the arms and legs of the padded chair, the coverlet 에그웨인 had tossed on the floor and the thin silk sheet that had followed. The curtains at the windows were lace, too. 에그웨인 put her head back down. Lace edged the pillows as well. The room made her feel she might drown in lace.
There had been a great deal of talk after 셰리암 and the others brought her here to what they called the Little Tower, almost all of it on their side. They were not really interested in what she thought 랜드 was up to, or what Coiren and the others might want. There was an embassy on its way to Caemlyn under Merana, who knew what to do, though they were rather vague about exactly what that was. For the most part, they did the talking, she the listening, her questions brushed aside. The answers to some were unimportant, she was told, for now anyway; those that were answered got a quick gloss before they went on to what was important. Embassies had been sent off to every ruler, each one named in turn, with an explanation of why he or she was absolutely vital to Salidar’s cause, which it seemed every one was. They did not quite say everything would fail if even one ruler went against them, but the emphasis they laid on every one said it for them. Gareth Bryne was building an army that would eventually be strong enough to prosecute their—her—claims against 엘라이더, if it came to that. They did not seem to think it would, despite 엘라이더’s demand that they return to the Tower; they seemed to believe that once word of 에그웨인 al’Vere’s elevation to the 아미를린 석좌 was spread, 에스 세다이 would come to her, even some of those in the Tower now, enough that 엘라이더 would have no choice but to step down on demand. The 백의단 were twiddling their thumbs for some reason, so Salidar was as safe as anywhere for as long as was necessary. That 로가인 had been Healed as well as 시우안—and 리안; of course she would have been Healed if she was here; it was just a surprise to find out she was—came up almost in passing.

*“Nothing to worry you there,” 셰리암 said soothingly. She stood over 에그웨인, who sat in the padded armchair, with the others in an arc around her. “The Hall will argue whether to gentle him again until old age relieves us of the problem.”*

*에그웨인 tried to stifle another yawn—it was getting late—and Anaiya said, “We need to let her sleep. Tomorrow is almost as important as tonight was, child.” Abruptly she laughed to herself softly. “Mother. Tomorrow is important too, Mother. We will send Chesa to help you get ready for bed.”*

Even after they left, going to bed was not easy. While Chesa was still undoing 에그웨인’s dress, Romanda appeared with a number of suggestions for the Amyrlin, delivered in a firm no-nonsense voice, and no sooner did she go than Lelaine came, as if the Blue Sitter had been waiting for the Yellow’s departure. Lelaine had her own helpful counsel, given with 에그웨인 sitting up in bed after Chesa was gently but firmly put out of the room. It was not a bit like Romanda’s advice—neither was much like 셰리암’s—and came with a warm, even affectionate, smile, but with just as much certainty that 에그웨인 would need a little guidance in her first months. Neither woman exactly said that she could guide 에그웨인 to what was best for the Tower better than 셰리암, or that 셰리암 and her little circle might try to tug in too many directions, or that they might give bad advice, but the strong implications were there. Romanda and Lelaine also each hinted that the other might have her own agenda, one that undoubtedly would cause untold misery.

By the time 에그웨인 channeled the last lamp out, she expected a sleep full of nightmares. In fact there were only two that she remembered the next morning. In one she was Amyrlin—에스 세다이, but without taking the oaths—and everything she did led to disaster. That wakened her bolt upright, just to get away, yet she was sure it was not a dream with meaning. It was much the same as one of her experiences inside the *ter’angreal* where she had been tested for 허락받은 자; as far as anyone knew, those had no connection to reality. Not to this reality. The other was the sort of foolishness she expected; she knew enough about her own dreams now to know that, even if she had to wake herself finally to escape that one as well. 셰리암 had snatched the stole from her shoulders, and then everyone was laughing at her and pointing at the fool who really believed a girl of barely eighteen years could be Amyrlin. Not just the 에스 세다이, but all the 현명한 이들, and 랜드 and 페린 and 맷, 니나브 and 엘레인, almost everyone she had ever met, while she stood there naked, desperately trying to put on an 허락받은 자’s dress that might have fit a ten-year-old child.

“Now, you can’t be lying abed all day, Mother.”

에그웨인 opened her eyes.

Chesa had an expression of mock severity on her face and a twinkle in her eye. At least twice 에그웨인’s age, at their first meeting she had fallen straight into the blend of respect and familiarity that could be expected of an old retainer. “The 아미를린 석좌 can’t be lying slugabed, not today of all days.”

“The last thing in my mind.” Scrambling stiffly from the bed, 에그웨인 stretched before pulling off her sweaty shift. She could not wait until she had worked long enough with the Power to stop sweating. “I’ll wear the blue silk with the white morning-stars along the neckline.” She noticed Chesa very carefully not looking as the woman handed her a fresh shift. The effects of meeting her *toh* had faded somewhat, but she still appeared faintly bruised. “I had an accident before I got here,” she said, hurriedly thrusting her head through the new shift.

Chesa nodded in sudden understanding. “Horses are wicked, untrustworthy beasts. You’ll never get me on one, Mother. A good sturdy cart is ever so much safer. If I fell off a horse like that, I’d never let on to a soul. Nildra would say such things, and Kaylin. . . . Oh, you’d never believe the things some women can say the moment your back is turned. Of course, it’s different for the 아미를린 석좌, but that’s what I’d do.” Holding the wardrobe door open, she glanced sideways at 에그웨인 to see whether she understood.

에그웨인 smiled at her. “People are people, low or high,” she said gravely.

Chesa beamed for an instant before bringing out the blue dress. Anaiya might have chosen her, but she was the 아미를린 석좌’s maid, and her loyalty was to the 아미를린 석좌. And she was right about today’s importance, too.

Eating quickly—despite Chesa’s murmurs to herself about how gulping food always upset the stomach; the warm milk with honey and spices was sovereign for settling a nervous stomach—에그웨인 scrubbed her teeth and washed hurriedly, let Chesa take a few licks at her hair with the brush and dressed as fast as the woman could get the blue silk over her head. Settling the seven-striped stole on her shoulders, she paused to look in the stand-mirror. Stole or no stole, she did not look very much like the 아미를린 석좌. *But I am. This is no dream.*

In the large room below, the tables stood as empty as they had in the night. Only the 의석자들 were there, wearing their shawls and clustered according to 아자, and 셰리암 standing alone. They quieted as 에그웨인 descended the stair, curtsied when she reached the bottom. Romanda and Lelaine eyed her sharply, then turned away, very obviously not looking at 셰리암, and resumed their conversations. When 에그웨인 remained silent, the others did the same. Occasionally one of them glanced at her. Even in whispers their voices sounded too loud. There was silence outside; utter stillness. 에그웨인 plucked her handkerchief from her sleeve and patted her face. None of *them* sweated a drop.

셰리암 came to stand beside her. “It will go well,” she said softly. “Just remember what you are to say.” That was another thing they had gone over in detail last night; 에그웨인 had a speech to deliver this morning.

에그웨인 nodded. It was strange. Her stomach should have been turning over, her knees shaking. They were not, and she could not understand.

“There is no need to be anxious,” 셰리암 said. She sounded as if she thought 에그웨인 was, and meant to soothe her, but before she could open her mouth again, Romanda spoke loudly.

“It is time.”

In a rustle of skirts the 의석자들 lined up according to age, with Romanda in the lead this time, and marched outside. 에그웨인 moved to just short of the door. Still no flutters. Maybe Chesa was right about the warm milk.

Silence still, then Romanda’s voice, too loud for nature. “We have an 아미를린 석좌.”

에그웨인 stepped outside into a heat she would not have expected until later in the day. As her foot left the stoop, it landed on a platform woven of Air. The lines of 의석자들 stretched out to either side of her, each Sitter glowing with the light of *세다르.*

“에그웨인 al’Vere,” Romanda intoned, her voice carried by weaves of the Power, “the Watcher of the 봉인, the Flame of 타르 발론, the 아미를린 석좌.”

They lifted her high as Romanda spoke, raising the Amyrlin in truth, until she stood just below the thatched roof, standing on thin air it would seem to any but a woman who could channel.

There were plenty to see her outlined by the rising sun; a second weave made the light into a shimmering weave around her. Men and women packed the street. The crowd disappeared around corners. Every doorway was filled, every window, every rooftop except that of the Little Tower itself. A roar erupted that very nearly drowned out Romanda, waves of cheering that rolled across the village. 에그웨인 scanned the crowd searching for 니나브 and 엘레인, but she could not find them in that sea of upturned faces. An age seemed to pass before there was quiet enough for her to speak. The weave that had carried Romanda’s voice shifted to her.

They had prepared her speech, 셰리암 and the others, a weighty exhortation she might have been able to deliver without blushing if she was twice her age, or better yet three times. She had made a few changes on her own. “We are gathered together in a quest for truth and justice that will not end until the false Amyrlin 엘라이더 is removed from the place she usurped.” The only change in that was “will not” for “cannot,” but she thought it stronger and better. “As Amyrlin, I will lead you in that quest, and I will not falter, as I know you will not.” And that was quite enough exhortation; in any case, she had no intention of remaining up here long enough to repeat everything they wanted said. It all amounted to what she already had said anyway. “As my 연대기 수호자, I name 셰리암 Bayanar.”

That produced a much smaller cheer; a Keeper was not an Amyrlin, after all. 에그웨인 glanced down, waiting until she saw 셰리암 hurry outside, still draping her shoulders with the stole of the Keeper, blue to show she had been raised from the 청색 아자. It had been decided not to make a copy of the Amyrlin’s staff, topped with a golden flame, that the Keeper carried; until the true staff was recovered from the 백색 탑, they would have to do without. 셰리암 had been expecting a much longer wait, and she looked at 에그웨인 with open exasperation. In the lines of 의석자들, Romanda and Lelaine wore no expression at all; each had had her own very strong suggestion for Keeper, and needless to say, neither had been 셰리암.

에그웨인 drew breath and turned back to the waiting crowd. “In honor of this day, I hereby decree that all 허락받은 자 and 수련생s are absolved of penances and punishments.” That was customary, and produced shouts of glee only from white-clad girls and a few 허락받은 자 who forgot themselves. “In honor of this day, I hereby decree that Theodrin Dabei, Faolain Orande, 니나브 al’Meara and 엘레인 Trakand are from this moment raised to the shawl, full sisters and 에스 세다이.” A sort of questioning silence greeted that, with here and there a murmur. It was not according to custom at all; far from it. But it was said, and a good thing Morvrin had happened to mention Theodrin and Faolain. Time to return to what they had written out for her. “I hereby decree this a day of feasting and celebration. Let no work be done but what is necessary for enjoyment. May the Light shine on you all, and the Creator’s hand shelter you.” That last was swallowed by a tumultuous roar that overwhelmed the weave carrying her words. Some people began dancing in the street right there and then, though there was hardly room for them to move.

The platform of Air descended perhaps a trifle more quickly than it had risen. The 의석자들 were staring at her when she stepped off, and the glow of *세다르* began winking out among them almost before she touched ground.

셰리암 darted up to take 에그웨인’s arm, smiling at the stone-faced 의석자들. “I must show the Amyrlin her study. Forgive me.” 에그웨인 would not exactly have said 셰리암 hustled her inside, but then again, she would not exactly have said she did not. She did not think 셰리암 would actually try to drag her, but it seemed best to gather her skirts with her free hand and take longer strides so as not to find out.

Her study, at the back of the waiting room, turned out to be somewhat smaller than her bedroom, with two windows, a writing table, a straight-backed chair behind it and two more in front. Nothing else. The beetle-riddled wall panels had been waxed to a dull shine, but the tabletop was quite bare. There was a piece of flowered carpet on the floor.

“Forgive me if I was abrupt, Mother,” 셰리암 said, releasing her arm, “but I thought we should speak privately before you spoke to any of the 의석자들. They all had a hand in writing your speech, and—”

“I know I made a few changes,” 에그웨인 said with a bright smile, “but I felt such a mudgin standing up there with all that to say.” *All* of them had a hand? No wonder it had sounded like a pompous old woman who could not stop talking. She almost laughed. “Anyway, I said what had to be said, the heart of it. 엘라이더 must be removed, and I will lead them to do it.”

“Yes,” 셰리암 said slowly, “but there might be a few questions about some of the other . . . changes. Theodrin and Faolain will certainly be raised 에스 세다이 as soon as we have the Tower and the 맹세 막대 back, and very likely 엘레인, but 니나브 still can’t light a candle unless she yanks her braid at people first.”

“That was exactly the point I wished to raise,” Romanda said, coming in without knocking. “Mother,” she added after a distinct pause. Lelaine shut the door behind them, nearly in the faces of several other 의석자들.

“It seemed necessary,” 에그웨인 said, widening her eyes. “I thought of it last night. I’ve been raised 에스 세다이 without being tested or taking the 세 가지 맹세, and if I was the only one, it would just point me out. With four others, I won’t seem quite so odd anymore. Not to people here, at least. 엘라이더 might try to make something of it when she hears, but most folk know so little about 에스 세다이, they won’t know what to believe anyway. It is the people here who matter most. They must have confidence in me.”

Anyone but 에스 세다이 would have gaped at her. As it was, Romanda very nearly spluttered.

“That may be so,” Lelaine began sharply, giving her blue-fringed shawl a jerk, then stopped. It was so. More, the 아미를린 석좌 had publicly decreed those women 에스 세다이. The Hall might be able to keep them 허락받은 자—or whatever Theodrin and Faolain were, in their cases—but the Hall could not erase memories, and it would not stop everyone knowing they had gone against the Amyrlin on her first day. A great deal that would do for confidence.

“I hope, Mother,” Romanda said in a tight voice, “that you will consult the Hall first the next time. Going against custom can have unexpected consequences.”

“Going against law can have unfortunate ones,” Lelaine said bluntly, tacking on a belated, “Mother.” That was nonsense, or close to it. The conditions for being raised 에스 세다이 were set in law, true, but the Amyrlin could decree almost anything she wished. Still, a wise Amyrlin did not jump into fights with the Hall when they could be avoided.

“Oh, I will consult in the future,” 에그웨인 told them earnestly. “But it did seem the right thing to do. Please, would you excuse me now? I really do need to speak with the Keeper.”

They practically quivered. Their curtsies were slight, their parting words perfectly correct so far as the words went, but muttered in Romanda’s case, and in Lelaine’s, sharp enough to cut.

“You handled that very well,” 셰리암 said when they were gone. She sounded surprised. “But you must remember the Hall can make problems for any Amyrlin. One reason I am your Keeper is so that I can advise you, and keep you away from that sort of problem. You should ask me about any decrees you want to make. And if I’m not at hand, 미렐 and Morvrin and the others. We are here to help you, Mother.”

“I understand, 셰리암. I promise to listen carefully to whatever you say. I’d like to see 니나브 and 엘레인, if that is possible.”

“It should be,” 셰리암 said, smiling, “though I may have to pull 니나브 away from a Yellow physically. 시우안 is coming to teach you about the etiquette of being Amyrlin—there is a great deal of it to learn—but I’ll tell her to come a little later.”

에그웨인 stared at the door after 셰리암 had gone. Then she turned and stared at the table. Absolutely bare. Not a report to be read, no records to study. Not so much as pen and ink to write a note, much less a decree. And 시우안 coming to teach her etiquette.

When a timid tap came at the door, she was still standing there. “Come,” she said, wondering whether it was 시우안, or perhaps a servant with a snack of honeycakes, already cut into suitably small pieces.

니나브 poked her head in hesitantly, then was pushed into the room by 엘레인. Side by side, they made perfect deep curtsies, spreading white, banded skirts wide and murmuring, “Mother.”

“Please don’t do that,” 에그웨인 said. Actually, it was more of a wail. “You’re the only two friends I have, and if you start. . . .” Light, she was almost ready to cry!

엘레인 reached her first by a hair, throwing her arms around her. 니나브 was silent, fiddling nervously with a slim silver bracelet, but not 엘레인. “We’re still your friends, 에그웨인, but you *are* the 아미를린 석좌. Light, remember I told you one day you’d be the Amyrlin when I was. . . .” 엘레인 grimaced faintly. “Well, in any case, you *are.* We can’t just walk up to the Amyrlin and say, ‘에그웨인, does this dress make me look fat?’ It would not be proper.”

“Yes it would,” 에그웨인 said stoutly. “Well, in private,” she allowed after a moment. “When we’re alone, I *want* you to tell me a dress makes me look fat, or . . . or whatever you want.” Smiling at 니나브, she tugged the woman’s thick braid gently. 니나브 gave a start. “And I want you to pull that at me, if you feel like it. I need somebody who is 에그웨인’s friend and doesn’t see this . . . this *bloody* stole all the time, or I will go crazy. Speaking of dresses, why are you still in those? I thought sure you could be changed by now.”

니나브 did pull at her braid then. “That Nisao told me it must be some sort of mistake and dragged me off. She said she wasn’t going to waste her turn just for a celebration.” The sounds of it were beginning to rise outside, a general hum just loud enough to penetrate the stone walls, and a faint thread of music.

“Well, it was no mistake,” 에그웨인 said. Nisao’s turn? Well, she was not going to ask now; 니나브 was not happy about it, and 에그웨인 wanted this to be as happy an occasion as it could. Dragging the chair from behind the table, she saw two plump patchwork cushions on the seat and smiled. Chesa. “We are going to sit here and talk, and then I will help you find the two best dresses in Salidar. Tell me about these discoveries of yours. Anaiya mentioned them, and 셰리암, but I could not make them hold still long enough to give me any details.”

Almost as one, the pair paused in the act of sitting and exchanged glances. Unaccountably, they seemed reluctant to talk of anything but 니나브’s 치유 시우안 and 리안—니나브 repeated three times rather anxiously that 치유 로가인 had been an accident—and 엘레인’s work with *ter’angreal.* Those were remarkable feats, especially 니나브’s, but there was only so much they could say, and there were only so many times 에그웨인 could tell them how marvelous what they had done was and how much she envied them. Trying to demonstrate did not last long; 에그웨인 had no real feel for 치유, especially not this complicated tapestry 니나브 wove without thought, and though she had an affinity for metals and very good strength in both Fire and Earth, 엘레인 lost her almost immediately. Of course they wanted to know what life was like among the 아일. From the startled blinks and shocked laughs, abruptly cut off, she was not sure they believed everything she told them, and she certainly did not tell everything. The 아일 led naturally into 랜드. Both women stared all through her rendition of his meeting with the 에스 세다이. They agreed that he was wading waters deeper than he knew and needed someone to guide him before he stepped into a hole. 엘레인 thought 민 might help with that, once the embassy reached Caemlyn—this was the first 에그웨인 knew 민 was with him, or had been in Salidar—though in truth, 엘레인 seemed rather halfhearted. And she muttered something truly peculiar, as if it were a truth she did not like hearing.

“민 is a better woman than I am.” For some reason, that got a sympathetic look from 니나브. “I wish *I* were there,” 엘레인 went on in a stronger voice. “To guide him, I mean.” She looked from 에그웨인 to 니나브, red touching her cheeks. “Well, that, too.” 니나브 and 에그웨인 began laughing so hard they nearly fell out of their chairs, and 엘레인 joined in almost immediately.

“There’s one good thing to tell, 엘레인,” 에그웨인 said breathlessly, still trying to recover. Then she realized exactly what she was going to say, and why. Light, what a mire she had stepped into, and while laughing! “I’m sorry about your mother, 엘레인. You don’t know how I wished I could offer my condolences before this.” 엘레인 looked confused, as well she might. “The point is, 랜드 means to give you the Lion Throne *and* the Sun Throne.” To her surprise, 엘레인 sat up very straight.

“He does, does he?” she said in a cool flat voice. “He intends to give them to me.” Her chin rose slightly. “I have some claim to the Sun Throne, and if I choose to make it, I will do so in my own right. As for the Lion Throne, 랜드 al’Thor has no right—none!—to *give* me what is mine already.”

“I’m sure he didn’t mean it that way,” 에그웨인 protested. *Did he?* “He loves you, 엘레인. I know he does.”

“If only it were that simple,” 엘레인 muttered, whatever that was supposed to mean.

니나브 sniffed. “Men always say they didn’t mean it that way. You would think they spoke a different language.”

“When I put my hands on him again,” 엘레인 said firmly, “I will teach him to speak the right language. *Give* me!”

It was all 에그웨인 could do not to laugh again. The next time 엘레인 laid hands on 랜드 she would be too busy hunting a secluded spot to teach him anything. This was very like old times. “Now you’re 에스 세다이, you can go to him any time you want. Nobody can stop you.” A quick look passed between the pair.

“The Hall isn’t letting anyone just pick up and leave,” 니나브 said. “And even if she could, we found something I think is more important.”

엘레인 nodded vigorously. “I think so, too. I’ll admit, the first thought I had when I heard you announced Amyrlin was that now maybe 니나브 and I could go find it. Well, the second; the first was a sort of stunned joy.”

에그웨인 blinked in confusion. “You found something. But now you need to find it.” Leaning forward in their chairs, they answered eagerly and almost on top of one another.

“We found it,” 엘레인 said, “but only in *Tel’aran’rhiod*.”

“We used need,” 니나브 added. “We certainly needed *something*.”

“It’s a bowl,” 엘레인 continued, “a *ter’angreal*, and I think it might be strong enough to change the weather.”

“Only, the bowl is somewhere in Ebou Dar, in an awful, tangled warren of streets with no signs or anything to help. The Hall sent a letter to Merilille, but she’ll never find it.”

“Especially since she is supposed to be busy convincing Queen Tylin that the *real* 백색 탑 is here.”

“We told them it needed a man in the channeling.” 니나브 sighed. “Of course, that was before 로가인, though I don’t think they would trust him.”

“It doesn’t really need a man,” 엘레인 said. “We just wanted to make them believe they *needed* 랜드. I don’t know how many women it does need; maybe a full circle of thirteen.”

“엘레인 says it’s very powerful, 에그웨인. It could make the weather right again. I’d welcome that just to get my weather sense straight again.”

“The bowl *can* make it right, 에그웨인.” 엘레인 exchanged happy looks with 니나브. “All you have to do is send us to Ebou Dar.”

The flood receded, and 에그웨인 leaned back in her chair. “I will do what I can. Maybe there’ll be no objection, now that you’re 에스 세다이.” She had the feeling there would be, though. Raising them had seemed such a bold stroke, but she was beginning to believe it was not quite so simple.

“What you can?” 엘레인 said incredulously. “You are the 아미를린 석좌, 에그웨인. You give a command, and 에스 세다이 jump.” She flashed a quick grin. “Say ‘jump,’ and I’ll prove it.”

Grimacing, 에그웨인 shifted on the cushions. “I’m the Amyrlin, but. . . . 엘레인, 셰리암 doesn’t have to think very hard to recall a 수련생 named 에그웨인, staring goggle-eyed at everything and being sent to rake the New Garden walks for eating apples after bedtime. She means to lead me by the hand, or maybe push me by the scruff of my neck. Romanda and Lelaine both wanted to be Amyrlin, and they see that 수련생 too. They intend to show me where to put my feet as much as 셰리암 does.”

니나브 frowned worriedly, but 엘레인 was pure indignation. “You can’t let them get away with trying to . . . to *bully* you. You are the *Amyrlin.* The Amyrlin tells the Hall what to do, not the other way around. You have to stand up and make them *see* the 아미를린 석좌.”

에그웨인’s laugh had a touch of bitterness. Had it only been last night that she was so defiant about being bullied? “That will take a little time, 엘레인. You see, I finally understood why they chose me. Part is for 랜드, I think. Maybe they believe he’ll be more amenable if he sees me wearing the stole. The other part is *because* they remember that 수련생. A woman—no; a girl!—who’s so used to doing as she’s told that there will be no trouble making her do as they want.” She fingered the striped stole around her neck. “Well, whatever their reasons, they chose me Amyrlin, and since they did, I mean to *be* Amyrlin, but I have to be careful, at first anyway. Maybe 시우안 made the Hall jump every time she frowned”—she wondered whether that had ever been true—“but if I try that, I might just be the first Amyrlin ever deposed the day after she was raised.”

엘레인 looked dumbfounded, but 니나브 nodded slowly. Perhaps being Wisdom and dealing with the Women’s Circle back home had given her more insight into how the 아미를린 석좌 and the 탑의 회의실 actually worked together than all of 엘레인’s training to be Queen.
“엘레인, once word spreads and rulers know about me, I can begin making the Hall realize they chose an Amyrlin, not a puppet, but until then, they really could take this stole away as fast as they gave it. I mean, if I’m not really Amyrlin, then it isn’t hard to push me aside. There might be a few mutters, but I have no doubt they could smooth those over fast enough. If anyone outside Salidar ever heard somebody named 에그웨인 al’Vere was raised Amyrlin, it would just be one of those peculiar rumors that grow up around 에스 세다이.”

“What are you going to do?” 엘레인 asked quietly. “You are not going to accept it meekly.” That made 에그웨인 smile wholeheartedly. It was not a question, but a firm statement of fact.

“No, I am not.” She had listened to a number of 모이라인’s lectures to 랜드 about the Game of Houses. Back then, she had thought the Game absurd, and worse than underhanded. Now she hoped she could remember everything she had heard. The 아일 always said, “Use the weapons you have.”

“It may help that they’re trying to fit me for three different leashes. I can pretend to be pulled by one or another, depending on which is closest to what I want to do. Once in a while I can just do what I want, the way I did raising you two, but not very often yet.” Squaring her shoulders, she met their gazes levelly. “I would like to say I raised you because you deserved it, but the truth is, I did it because you’re my friends, and because I hope as full sisters you can help me. I certainly don’t know who else I can trust except you two. I will send you to Ebou Dar as soon as I can, but before and after, you are who I can discuss things with. I know you will tell me the truth. That trip to Ebou Dar may not take as long as you might think. You two have made all sorts of discoveries, so I hear, but if I can puzzle a few things out, I may have one of my own.”

“That will be wonderful,” 엘레인 said, but she sounded almost absentminded.

*When Battle Begins*

The silence was very peculiar, and 에그웨인 did not understand at all. 엘레인 looked at 니나브, then they both looked at 니나브’s slim silver bracelet. 니나브 shifted her gaze to 에그웨인, wide-eyed, and quickly put it on the floor.

“I have a confession,” she said in a near whisper. Her voice never rose, but words spilled out in a rush. “I captured 모그헤디엔.” Without raising her eyes, she lifted her wrist with the bracelet. “This is an *a’dam.* We’re holding her prisoner, and nobody knows. Except 시우안 and 리안 and 비르기테. And now you.”

“We had to,” 엘레인 said, leaning forward urgently. “They’d have executed her, 에그웨인. I know she deserves it, but her head is full of knowledge, things we hardly dream of. That’s where all of our *discoveries* came from. Except 니나브’s 치유 시우안 and 리안 and 로가인, and my *ter’angreal.* They would have killed her without waiting to learn anything!”

Questions whirled through 에그웨인’s head dizzyingly. They had captured one of the 버림받은 자들? How? 엘레인 had made an *a’dam*? 에그웨인 shivered, barely able to look at the thing. It looked nothing like the *a’dam* she knew far too well. Even with that, how had they managed to keep one of the 버림받은 자들 hidden among so many 에스 세다이? One of the 버림받은 자들, prisoner. Not tried and executed. As suspicious as 랜드 had become, if he ever discovered that, he would never trust 엘레인 again.

“Bring her here,” she managed to say hollowly. 니나브 bounced out of her chair and ran. The noises of celebration, laughter and music and song, swelled for a moment before the door banged shut behind her. 에그웨인 rubbed her temples. One of the 버림받은 자들. “That is quite a secret to keep.”

엘레인’s cheeks colored. Why under the Light . . . ? Of course.

“엘레인, I have no intention of asking about . . . anybody I’m not supposed to know about.”

The golden-haired woman actually jumped. “I . . . I may be able to talk. Later. Tomorrow. Maybe. 에그웨인, you have to promise me you won’t say anything—not to anybody!—unless I say so. No matter what you . . . what you see.”

“If that’s what you want.” 에그웨인 did not understand why the other woman was so agitated. Not really. 엘레인 had a secret that 에그웨인 shared, only 에그웨인 had found out by accident, and ever since they had both been pretending it was still 엘레인’s secret alone. She had met with 비르기테, the hero out of legend, in *Tel’aran’rhiod*; maybe she still did. Wait, that was what 니나브 had said. 비르기테 knew about 모그헤디엔. Did she mean the woman waiting in *Tel’aran’rhiod* for the 발레르의 뿔 to call her back? *니나브* knew the secret that 엘레인 had refused to admit to 에그웨인 even when she was caught out? No. This was not going to turn into a round of accusations and denials.

“엘레인, I am the Amyrlin—really the Amyrlin—and I already have plans. The 현명한 이들 who channel handle a good many of their weaves differently from 에스 세다이.” 엘레인 already knew about the 현명한 이들, though come to think of it, 에그웨인 did not know whether the 에스 세다이 did; the other 에스 세다이, now. “Sometimes what they do is more complicated or more crude, but at times it’s simpler than we were taught in the Tower and works just as well.”

“You want 에스 세다이 to study with the 아일?” 엘레인’s mouth quirked in amusement. “에그웨인, they’ll *never* agree to that, not if you live a thousand years. I suppose they’ll want to test 아일 girls for 수련생s when they find out, though.”

Shifting on her cushions, 에그웨인 hesitated. 에스 세다이 studying with the 현명한 이들. As apprentices? It would never happen, but Romanda and Lelaine especially might benefit from a little *ji’e’toh*. And 셰리암, and 미렐, and. . . . She found a more comfortable way to sit and gave up her fancies. “I doubt the 현명한 이들 will agree to 아일 girls becoming 수련생s.” They might have once, possibly, but certainly not now. Now it would be as much as 에그웨인 could expect for them to speak civilly to 에스 세다이. “I thought some sort of association. 엘레인, there are fewer than a thousand 에스 세다이. If you include those who remain in the 황무지, I think there are more 현명한 이들 who can channel than there are 에스 세다이. Maybe many more. Anyway, they don’t miss a one with the spark born in her.” How many women had died on this side of the Dragonwall, because they suddenly could channel, maybe without realizing what they were doing at all, and had no one to teach them? “I want to bring in more women, 엘레인. What about women who can learn, but no 에스 세다이 found them before they were thought too old for 수련생s? I say, if she wants to learn, let her try, even if she’s forty or fifty or her grandchildren have grandchildren.”

엘레인 hugged herself laughing. “Oh, 에그웨인, the 허락받은 자 will just love teaching *those* 수련생 classes.”

“They’ll have to learn how,” 에그웨인 said firmly. She did not see the problem. 에스 세다이 had always said you could be too old for a 수련생, but if you wanted to learn. . . . They had changed their minds partway already; in the crowd she had seen faces older than 니나브’s above 수련생 white. “The Tower has always been severe about excluding people, 엘레인. If you aren’t strong enough, you’re put out. Refuse to take a test, and you’re sent away. Fail a test, and out. They should be allowed to stay if they want.”

“But the tests are to make sure you’re strong enough,” 엘레인 protested. “Not just in the 하나의 힘; in yourself. Surely you don’t want 에스 세다이 who will break the first time they come under pressure? Or 에스 세다이 who can barely channel?”

에그웨인 sniffed. Sorilea would have been put out of the Tower without ever being tested for 허락받은 자. “Maybe they can’t be 에스 세다이, but that doesn’t mean they are useless. After all, they’re already trusted to use the Power with at least some discretion, or they wouldn’t be sent off into the world. My dream is for every woman who can channel to be connected to the Tower somehow. Every last one.”

“The Windfinders?” 엘레인 winced when 에그웨인 nodded.

“You didn’t betray them, 엘레인. I can’t believe they kept their secret as long as they did.”

엘레인 sighed heavily. “Well, what’s done is done. ‘You can’t put honey back in the comb.’ But if your 아일 get special protection, the Sea Folk should too. Let the Windfinders teach their girls. No Sea Folk women bundled off by 에스 세다이 whatever they will.”

“Done.” 에그웨인 spat on her palm and held out her hand, and after a moment 엘레인 spat on hers and grinned as they clasped to seal the bargain.

Slowly that grin faded. “Is this about 랜드 and his amnesty, 에그웨인?”

“In part. 엘레인, how could the man be so . . . ?” There was no way to finish that, and no answer anyway. The other woman nodded a touch sadly, in understanding or agreement or both.

The door opened, and a sturdy woman in dark wool appeared, a silver tray in her hands with three silver cups and a long-necked silver wine pitcher. Her face was worn, a farmwife’s face, but her dark eyes glittered as she studied 에그웨인 and 엘레인 with a shifting gaze. 에그웨인 had just a moment to feel surprise that the woman wore a close-fitting silver necklace despite her drab dress, and then 니나브 entered behind heir, shutting the door. She must have run like the wind, because she had found time to exchange the 허락받은 자’s dress for a dark blue silk embroidered with golden scrolls around the neckline and hem. It was not nearly so low-cut as what Berelain wore, but still considerably lower than 에그웨인 expected to see on 니나브.

“This is ‘Marigan,’ ” 니나브 said, drawing her braid over her shoulder in a practiced motion. Her Great Serpent ring shone golden on her right hand.

에그웨인 started to ask why she emphasized the name so, then abruptly realized that “Marigan’s” necklace was a match for the bracelet on 니나브’s wrist. She could not help staring. The woman certainly did not look anything like she expected one of the 버림받은 자들 to look. She said as much, and 니나브 laughed.

“Watch, 에그웨인.”

She did more than watch; she nearly leaped out of her chair, and she did embrace *세다르*. As soon as 니나브 spoke, the glow had surrounded “Marigan.” Only for an instant, but before it faded, the woman in the plain wool dress changed completely. Actually they were rather small changes, but they added up to a different woman, handsome rather than beautiful but not at all worn, a woman who was proud, even regal. Only the eyes remained the same, glittering, but no matter how they shifted, 에그웨인 could believe this woman was 모그헤디엔.

“How?” was all she said. She listened carefully as 니나브 and 엘레인 explained about weaving disguises and inverting weaves, but she watched 모그헤디엔. She *was* proud, and full of herself, full of being herself again.

“Put her back,” 에그웨인 said when the explanations were done. Again the glow of *세다르* lasted only moments, and once it faded, there were no weaves that she could see. 모그헤디엔 was plain and worn again, a country woman who had led a hard life and looked older than her years. Those black eyes glittered at 에그웨인, filled with hate, and maybe self-loathing as well.

Realizing she still held *세다르*, 에그웨인 felt foolish for a moment. Neither 니나브 nor 엘레인 had embraced the Source. But then, 니나브 was wearing that bracelet. 에그웨인 stood, never taking her gaze from 모그헤디엔, and held out her hand. If anything, 니나브 seemed eager to have the thing off her wrist, which 에그웨인 could understand.

Handing the bracelet over, 니나브 said, “Put the tray on the table, Marigan. And be on your best behavior. 에그웨인 has been living with the 아일.”

에그웨인 turned the silver band over in her hands and tried not to shiver. Cunning work, segmented so cleverly it almost appeared solid. She had been on the other end of an *a’dam* once. A 쇼엔찬 device, with a silver leash connecting necklace and bracelet, but still the same. Her stomach roiled as it had not facing the Hall or the crowd; it stewed as though trying to make up for being still before. Deliberately she closed the length of silver around her wrist. She had some idea of what to expect, but she still almost jumped. The other woman’s emotions were laid out before her, her physical state, all gathered in one fenced-off portion of 에그웨인’s mind. Mainly there was pulsing fear, but the self-loathing she had thought she saw swelled nearly as strongly. 모그헤디엔 did not like her present appearance. Maybe she especially did not like it after a short return to her own.

에그웨인 thought of who it was she was looking at; one of the 버림받은 자들, a woman whose name had been used to frighten children for centuries, a woman whose crimes deserved death a hundred times over. She thought of the knowledge in that head. She made herself smile. It was not a pretty smile; she did not mean it to be, but she did not think she could have made it one if she tried. “They’re right. I have been living with the 아일. So if you expect me to be as gentle as 니나브 and 엘레인, put it out of your mind. Set just one foot wrong with me, and I’ll make you beg for death. Only, I won’t kill you. The fear leaped so high it drowned everything else and bulged against the fence. Standing in front of the table, 모그헤디엔 clutched her skirts white-knuckle tight and trembled visibly. 니나브 and 엘레인 were looking at 에그웨인 as if they had never seen her before. Light, did they expect her to be polite to one of the 버림받은 자들? Sorilea would stake the woman out in the sun to bring her to heel, if she did not simply slit her throat out of hand.

에그웨인 moved closer to 모그헤디엔. The other woman was taller, but she cowered back against the table, knocking over the winecups on their tray and rocking the pitcher. 에그웨인 made her voice cold; it did not have far to go. “The day I detect one lie out of you is the day I execute you myself. Now. I have considered traveling from one place to another by boring a hole, so to speak, from here to there. A hole through the Pattern, so there’s no distance between one end and the other. How well will that work?”

“Not at all, for you or any woman,” 모그헤디엔 said, breathless and quick. The fear that boiled inside was plain on her face now. “That is how men Travel.” The capital was plain; she was speaking of one of the lost Talents. “If you try, you will be sucked into. . . . I don’t know what it is. The space between the threads of the Pattern, maybe. I don’t think you would live very long. I know you would never come back.”

“이동,” 니나브 muttered disgustedly. “We never thought of 이동!”

“No, we didn’t.” 엘레인 sounded no more pleased with herself. “I wonder what else we never thought of.”

에그웨인 ignored them. “Then how?” she asked softly. A quiet voice was always better than shouting.

모그헤디엔 flinched as though she had shouted anyway. “You make the two places in the Pattern identical. I can show you how. It takes a little effort, because of the . . . the necklace, but I can—”

“Like this?” 에그웨인 said, embracing *세다르*, and wove flows of Spirit. This time she was not trying to touch the World of Dreams, but she expected something much the same if it worked. What she got was quite different.

The thin curtain she wove did not produce the shimmering effect, and it lasted only a moment before snapping together in a vertical line that was suddenly a slash of silvery blue light. Stone spires and sharp cliffs loomed over a dusty yellow-clay plain cut by fissures and dotted with a few scrub bushes that had a thorny look even at a distance.

에그웨인 very nearly stared. That was the 아일 황무지 halfway between Cold Rocks Hold and the valley of Rhuidean, a spot where it was very unlikely there would be anyone to see—or be hurt; 랜드’s precautions with his special room in the Sun Palace had suggested she take some too—but she had only hoped to reach it, and she had been sure it would be seen through a shimmering curtain.

“Light!” 엘레인 breathed. “Do you know what you’ve done, 에그웨인? Do you? I think I can do it. If you repeat the weave again, I know I’ll remember.”

“Remember what?” 니나브 practically wailed. “How did she do it? Oh, curse this *cursed* block! 엘레인, kick my ankle. Please?”

모그헤디엔’s face had gone very still; uncertainty rolled through the bracelet almost as heavily as fear. Reading emotions was hardly like reading words on a page, but those two were clear. “Who . . . ?” 모그헤디엔 licked her lips. “Who taught you that?”

에그웨인 smiled as she had seen 에스 세다이 smile; at least, she hoped it conveyed mystery. “Never be too sure I don’t already know the answer,” she said coolly. “Remember. Lie to me once.” Suddenly it occurred to her how this must sound to 니나브 and 엘레인. They had captured the woman, held her captive in the most impossible circumstances, pried all sorts of information out of her. Turning to them, she gave a small, rueful laugh. “I *am* sorry. I didn’t mean to just take over.”

“Why should you be sorry?” 엘레인 wore a broad smile. “You are *supposed* to take over, 에그웨인.”

니나브 gave her braid a yank, then glared at it. “Nothing seems to work! Why can’t I get angry? Oh, you can keep her forever, for all of me. We couldn’t take her to Ebou Dar, anyway. *Why* can’t I get angry? Oh, blood and bloody ashes!” Her eyes went wide as she realized what she had said, and she clapped a hand over her mouth.

에그웨인 glanced at 모그헤디엔. The woman was busily setting the winecups upright again and pouring wine with a smell of sweet spices, but something had come through the bracelet while 니나브 was talking. Shock, perhaps? Maybe she would prefer the mistresses she knew to one who threatened death in almost her first breath.

A firm knock sounded at the door, and 에그웨인 hastily released *세다르*; the opening to the 황무지 vanished. “Come.”

시우안 took one step into the study and stopped, taking in 모그헤디엔, the bracelet on 에그웨인’s wrist, 니나브 and 엘레인. Shutting the door, she made a curtsy as minimal as anything from Romanda or Lelaine. “Mother, I’ve come to instruct you in etiquette, but if you would rather I returned later . . . ?” Her eyebrows rose, calmly questioning.

“Go,” 에그웨인 told 모그헤디엔. If 니나브 and 엘레인 were willing to let her run loose, the *a’dam* must limit her, if not as much as one with a leash. Facing 시우안, she folded her arms beneath her breasts. “This won’t do, 시우안. I know everything. Daughter.”

시우안 tilted her head. “Sometimes knowing gives no advantage whatsoever. Sometimes it only means sharing the danger.”

“You can’t expect me to become somebody else overnight,” the woman muttered grumpily.

에그웨인 suspected 니나브 and 엘레인 could help with what she had to do, but if she was really going to be Amyrlin, she had to do it alone. “엘레인, I know you want to get out of that 허락받은 자’s dress. Why don’t you do that? And then see what you find out about lost Talents. 니나브, you do the same.”

A look passed between them, then they glanced at 시우안 and rose to make perfect curtsies, respectfully murmuring, “As you command, Mother.” There was no evidence of any impression on 시우안; she stood watching 에그웨인 with a wry expression while they left.

에그웨인 embraced *세다르* again, briefly, to slide her chair back into place behind the table, then adjusted her stole and sat. For a long moment she regarded 시우안 silently. “I need you,” she said at last. “You know what it is to be Amyrlin, what the Amyrlin can and cannot do. You know the 의석자들, how they think, what they want. I need you, and I mean to have you. 셰리암 and Romanda and Lelaine may think I still wear 수련생 white under this stole—maybe they all do—but you are going to help me show them differently. 시우안 regarded her, then gave a slight shake of her head and laughed softly. “They made a very bad mistake, didn’t they? Of course, I made it first. The plump little grunter for the table turns out to be a live silverpike as long as your leg.” Spreading her skirts wide, she made a deep curtsy, inclining her head. “Mother, please allow me to serve, and advise.”

“So long as you know it’s only advice, 시우안. I have too many people already who think they can tie strings to my arms and legs. I won’t put up with it from you.”

“I’d as soon try tying strings to myself,” 시우안 said dryly. “You know, I never really liked you. Maybe it was because I saw too much of myself in you.”

“In that case,” 에그웨인 said in just as dry a tone, “you can call me 에그웨인. When we’re alone. Now sit down and tell me why the Hall is still sitting here, and how I can get them moving.”

시우안 started to pull one of the chairs over before remembering she could move it with *세다르* now. “They are sitting because once they move, the 백색 탑 really is broken. As for how to get them moving, my advice. . . .” Her advice took a long time. Some of it went along lines 에그웨인 had already thought of, and all of it seemed good.

In her room in the Little Tower, Romanda poured mint tea for three other 의석자들, only one a Yellow. The room was in the back, but the sounds of festival penetrated; Romanda ignored them studiously. These three had been ready to support her for the 아미를린 석좌; voting for the girl had been as much a way to keep Lelaine from being raised as anything else. Lelaine would burn if she ever knew that. Now that 셰리암 had her child Amyrlin installed, these three were still willing to listen. Especially after the business of raising 허락받은 자 to the shawl by decree. That had to be 셰리암’s doing; she and her little clique had pampered all four; it had been their notion to lift Theodrin and Faolain above the other 허락받은 자, and they had suggested it for 엘레인 and 니나브 as well at one time. In a house halfway across Salidar, Lelaine was serving chilled wine to four 의석자들, only one from her own 청색 아자. *Saidar* laced the room against listeners. The sounds of celebration made her smile. The four women with her had suggested she try for the 아미를린 석좌 herself, and she had not been reluctant, but a failure would have meant Romanda being raised instead, which would have pained Lelaine as much as being exiled. How Romanda would gnash her teeth if she ever learned they had all voted for the child just to keep the stole from Romanda’s own shoulders. That farce of raising 허락받은 자 to 에스 세다이 by the girl’s decree! 셰리암’s head must have swollen to madness. As the talk went on, Lelaine began to wonder where Delana was. She should have been there by now.

Delana sat in her room, staring at Halima perched on the edge of Delana’s bed. The name Aran’gar was never to be used; sometimes Delana was afraid Halima would know if she even thought it. The ward against eavesdropping was small, enclosing just the pair of them. “That is madness,” she managed at last. “Don’t you understand? If I continue to try supporting every faction, they will catch me out sooner or later!”

“Everyone must take some risks.” The firmness of the woman’s voice belied the smile on that lush mouth. “And you will continue to press for gentling 로가인 again. That, or killing him.” A slight grimace actually made the woman more beautiful somehow. “If they ever brought him out of that house, I would attend to it myself.”

Delana could not imagine how, but she would not doubt the woman until she failed. “What I don’t understand is why you are so afraid of a man with six sisters shielding him from sunup to sunup.”

Halima’s green eyes blazed as she leaped to her feet. “I am not afraid, and don’t you ever suggest it! I want 로가인 severed or dead, and that is all you have to know. Do we understand one another?”

Not for the first time Delana considered killing the other woman, but as always she had a sinking certainty that she would be the one to die. Somehow Halima knew when she embraced *세다르*, even if Halima could not channel herself. The worst of it was the possibility that because Halima needed her, she would not kill her; Delana could not imagine what she might do instead, but the very vagueness of the threat made her shudder. She should be able to kill the woman right there, right then. “Yes, Halima,” she said meekly, and hated herself for it.

“So good of you,” 시우안 murmured, holding her cup for Lelaine to add a small splash of brandy in her tea. The sun was sinking toward the horizon, giving the light a reddish cast, but the streets outside were still raucous. “You have no idea how tiring it is trying to teach that girl etiquette. She seemed to think as long as she behaves like a *Wisdom* from back home, everything will be fine. The Hall is supposed to be the Women’s Circle or some such thing.”

Lelaine made sympathetic noises over her own tea. “You say she was complaining about Romanda?”

시우안 shrugged. “Something about Romanda insisting we stay here instead of marching for 타르 발론, as near as I could make out. Light, the girl has a temper like a fisherbird in mating season. I almost wanted to take her by the shoulders and shake her, but of course, she does wear the stole, now. Well, once I finish my lectures I’m done with her. Do you remember . . . ?”
Smiling inside, 시우안 watched Lelaine drinking it all in with the tea. Only the first sentence had really been important. The bit about a temper was her own addition, but it might make some of the 의석자들 walk a little more carefully around 에그웨인. Besides, she suspected it might be true. She would never be Amyrlin again herself, and she was fairly certain that trying to manipulate 에그웨인 would be as futile as trying to manipulate herself had been, and as painful, yet teaching an Amyrlin to be Amyrlin. . . . She looked forward to that as much as she had anything in a long time. 에그웨인 al’Vere would be an Amyrlin to make thrones tremble.

“But what about my block?” 니나브 said, and Romanda frowned at her. They were in Romanda’s room in the Little Tower, and this was when Romanda was supposed to have her according to the schedule the Yellows had set up. The music and laughter outside seemed to irritate the Yellow.

“You weren’t so eager earlier. I heard that you told Dagdara you were 에스 세다이 too and she could find a lake and douse her head.”

Heat rose in 니나브’s face. Trust her temper to get in the way. “Maybe I just realized that being 에스 세다이 doesn’t mean I can channel any more easily than before.”

Romanda sniffed. “에스 세다이. You have a long way to go for that, whatever. . . . Very well, then. Something we haven’t tried before. Jump up and down on one foot. And talk.” She sat down in a carved armchair near the bed, still frowning. “Gossip, I think. Talk about light things. For instance, what was it the Amyrlin said Lelaine wanted to talk about?”

For a moment 니나브 stared back indignantly. Jump on one foot? That was ridiculous! Still, she was not really here about her block anyway. Lifting her skirts, she began jumping. “에그웨인 . . . the Amyrlin . . . didn’t say much. Something about having to stay put in Salidar. . . .” This had better work, or 에그웨인 was going to hear a few choice words, Amyrlin or no.

“I think this one will work better, 셰리암,” 엘레인 said, handing over a twisted blue-and-red flecked ring of what had been stone this morning. In truth, it was no different from any other she had made. They stood apart from the crowd, at the mouth of a narrow alley lit by the red sun. Behind them fiddles squealed and flutes sang.

“Thank you, 엘레인.” 셰리암 tucked the *ter’angreal* into her belt pouch without even looking at it. 엘레인 had caught 셰리암 in a pause from dancing, her face a little flushed beneath all that cool 에스 세다이 serenity, but the clear green gaze that had made 엘레인’s knees shake as a 수련생 was fixed on her face. “Why do I get the feeling this is not your only reason for coming to see me?”

엘레인 grimaced, twisting the Great Serpent ring on her right hand. The right hand; she just had to remember she was 에스 세다이 too, now. “It’s 에그웨인. The Amyrlin, I guess I should say. She’s worried, 셰리암, and I was hoping you could help her. You are the Keeper, and I did *not* know who else to go to. I don’t have the straight of it completely. You know how 에그웨인 is; she wouldn’t complain if her *foot* was cut off. It’s Romanda, I think, though she did mention Lelaine. One or both have been at her, I think, about staying here in Salidar, about not moving yet because it’s too dangerous.”

“That is good advice,” 셰리암 said slowly. “I don’t know about dangerous, but that is the advice I would give her myself.”

엘레인 spread her hands in a helpless shrug. “I know. She told me you did, but. . . . She didn’t *say* it right out, but I think she’s a little afraid of those two. I *know* she’s Amyrlin now, but I think they make her feel a 수련생. I think she’s afraid if she does what they want—even if it *is* good advice—they will expect her to do the same next time. I think. . . . 셰리암, she is afraid she won’t be *able* to say no the next time if she says yes now. And . . . and I am afraid of it, too. 셰리암, she’s the Amyrlin *Seat*; she shouldn’t be under Romanda’s thumb, or Lelaine’s, or anybody’s. You are the *only* one who can help her. I do not know how, but you *are*.”

셰리암 was quiet so long that 엘레인 began to think the other woman was going to tell her every word was ludicrous. “I will do what I can,” 셰리암 said at last.

엘레인 stifled a relieved sigh before she realized it would not have mattered.

Leaning forward, 에그웨인 rested her arms along the sides of the copper tub and let Chesa’s chatter flow over her as the woman scrubbed her back. She had dreamed of a real bath, but actually sitting in the soapy water, scented with a floral oil, felt strange after 아일 sweat tents. She had taken her first step as Amyrlin, marshaled her outnumbered army and begun her attack. She remembered hearing Rhuarc say once that when battle began, a battle leader no longer had any real control of events. Now all she could do was wait. “Even so,” she said softly, “I think the 현명한 이들 would be proud.”

*A Sudden Chill*

The blazing sun still climbed behind him, and 맷 was glad his broad-brimmed hat gave a little shade on his face. This 알타라n forest was winter-bare and more than winter-brown, with pines and leatherleafs and other evergreens looking sere, and oak and ash and sweetgum naked. Noon yet to come, the worst heat beyond that, and already the day was like riding through an oven. His coat was slung atop his saddlebags, but sweat made his fine linen shirt cling. Pips’ hooves crunched on dead ferns and fallen leaves thick atop the leaf mold, and the Band moved in a crackle from the forest floor. Few birds appeared, quick flashes between the branches, and not a squirrel. There were flies, though, and bitemes, as if this were the heart of summer instead of less than a month to the Feast of Lights. No different from what he had seen back on the Erinin, really, but finding it here too made him uneasy. Was the whole world really burning up?

아비엔다 strode along beside Pips with her bundle on her back, apparently unconcerned by dying trees or biting flies, and making considerably less noise than the horse despite her skirts. Her eyes scanned the surrounding trees as though she did not trust the Band’s scouts and flankers to keep them out of an ambush. She had not accepted a ride once, which he had not expected anyway, seeing how 아일 felt about riding, but she had made no trouble either, unless sharpening her knife every time they halted could be considered provocative. There had been the incident with 올버, of course. Riding the high-stepping gray gelding 맷 had found him among the remounts, 올버 kept a wary eye on her. He had tried to stick his belt knife in her the second night, shouting about 아일 killing his father. Of course, she only took it away from him, but even after 맷 cuffed him and tried to explain the difference between Shaido and other 아일—something 맷 was not all that sure he understood himself—올버 glared at her constantly. He did not like 아일. For 아비엔다’s part, 올버 seemed to make her uneasy, which 맷 did not understand at all.

The trees stood tall enough to have allowed a breeze to stir under the sparse canopy overhead, but the Red Hand banner hung limp, and so did the two he had dug out once 랜드 put them through that gateway into a night-covered meadow, a Dragon banner, the red-and-gold shape hidden in white folds, and one of those the Band called Al’Thor’s Banner, the ancient 에스 세다이 symbol also thankfully wrapped inside. A grizzled senior bannerman had the Red Hand, a fellow with narrow eyes and more scars than Daerid who insisted on actually carrying the banner a part of each day, which few bannermen did. 탈마네스 and Daerid had supplied second squadmen for the other two, fresh-faced young men who had shown themselves steady enough for a little responsibility.

Three days they had come across 알타라, three days in forest without sight of a single 용worn—or anyone else for that matter—and 맷 hoped to stretch their loneliness at least through this fourth before reaching Salidar. Aside from 에스 세다이, there was the problem of how to keep 아비엔다 from 엘레인’s throat. He had few doubts why she kept sharpening that knife; the edge glittered like gemstones. He was very much afraid he was going to end taking the 아일 woman to Caemlyn under guard, with the bloody Daughter-Heir demanding he hang her every step of the way. 랜드 and his bloody women! In 맷’s view, anything that slowed the Band and kept him from the stew he expected in Salidar was to the good. Halting early and marching late helped. So did the supply wagons at the rear, slow as they were in the forest. But the Band could ride only so slowly. All too soon Vanin was sure to find something.

As if thinking his name had been a summons, the fat scout appeared through the trees ahead with four riders. He had gone out before dawn with six.

맷 raised a clenched fist, signaling a halt, and murmurs passed down the column. His first order on leaving the gateway had been “no drums, no trumpets, no flutes and no bloody singing,” and if there had been a few glum faces in the beginning, after the first day in that wooded terrain, where you could never see clearly more than a hundred paces and seldom so far, no one objected at all.

Resting his spear across his saddle, 맷 waited until Vanin pulled up and casually knuckled his forehead. “You found them?”

The balding man leaned to one side in his saddle to spit through a gap in his teeth. He was sweating so much he looked to be melting. “I found them. Eight or ten miles west. *Possibilities*
