“Of course you are, 맷.” She made it sound the most obvious thing in the world. Which it was, if you only thought. “You go where 랜드 sends you. What else are you but 용worn? But if you listen to me, I can stop them from putting *your* head on a pike. Actually, I don’t think Lord Bryne would use a pike—he always complains he doesn’t have enough—but I am sure he would figure out something.”

맷 looked at the other two women, and 에그웨인 compressed her lips for an instant. She had made herself plain, but he appeared to be hunting for a clue to what she was talking about. 엘레인 gave him back a tight smile and a decisively confirming nod. She might not see where 에그웨인 was going, yet she knew she was not talking for the sound of her voice. 니나브, still struggling to keep a severe face and tugging at her braid, only glared at him, but maybe that was even better. Though she was beginning to sweat; 니나브 lost concentration when she grew angry.

“Now, listen, 에그웨인,” 맷 said. Then again, maybe neither response was really enough. He managed to combine a reasonable tone with indulgence in the most offensive way possible. “If you want to call yourself Amyrlin, you can call yourself Amyrlin. 랜드 would welcome you with open arms in Caemlyn even if you don’t bring all these 에스 세다이 to him, but I know he will be overjoyed if you do. Whatever your problems are with 엘라이더, he can work them out. She knows he’s the 용의 환생. Light, you remember her letter. Why, you will have your 백색 탑 all mended before you can say Jak o’ the Wisps. No battles. No bloodshed. You know you don’t want bloodshed, 에그웨인.”

That she did not. Once the first blood was shed between Salidar and 타르 발론, it would be difficult to make the Tower whole again. Once the first 에스 세다이 blood was shed, it might be impossible. Still, 엘라이더 had to be brought down, and 에그웨인 would do what she had to do. She just did not like it. And she did not like 맷 telling her what she knew, liked it the less so for being right. Definitely the less so in that tone. It was a real effort to keep her hands still on the table. She wanted to stand and box his ears.

“However I deal with 랜드,” she said coolly, “you can be sure it will not be by leading 에스 세다이 to swear fealty to him or any other man.” Cool, and not at all arguing; a calm statement of simple facts. “How I deal with 엘라이더 is my concern, and none of yours. If you have any sense at all, 맷, you will keep your mouth shut as long as you are in Salidar and walk small. You start telling other 에스 세다이 what 랜드 is going to do just as soon they kneel to him, and you might not like the answers you get. Talk about carrying me off, or 니나브 or 엘레인, and you will be *very* lucky not to get a sword through you.”

He jerked upright with a glare. “I’ll talk to you again when you’re ready to listen to reason, 에그웨인. Is 톰 Merrilin around?” She gave a curt nod. What did he want with 톰? Probably to douse himself in wine. Well, good luck to him finding a tavern here. “When you’re ready to listen,” he repeated grimly, and stalked—limped—to the door.

“맷,” 엘레인 said, “I would not try to leave were I you. Getting into Salidar is much easier than getting out.”

He grinned at her insolently, and the way he eyed her up and down, he was lucky 엘레인 did not slap him hard enough to loosen all his teeth. “You, my fine Lady, I am taking back to Caemlyn if I have to tie you up in a package to hand to 랜드, burn me if I don’t. And I will bloody well leave when I choose.” His bow was mocking, to 엘레인 and to 에그웨인. 니나브 got only a glower and another shake of his finger.

“How *can* 랜드 have such a low, insufferable lout for a friend?” 엘레인 asked no one in particular before the door was well closed behind him.

“His language has certainly slipped downhill,” 니나브 grumbled darkly, tossing her head so her braid swung over her shoulder. 에그웨인 thought she might be afraid she would pull it out by the roots if she did not put it out of reach.

“I should have let him do as he wanted, 니나브. You have to remember you’re 에스 세다이 now. You can’t go around kicking people, or boxing their ears, or thumping them with sticks.” 니나브 stared at her, mouth working, face growing redder and redder. 엘레인 began assiduously studying the carpet.

With a sigh, 에그웨인 folded the striped stole and laid it on the table to one side. That was her way of making sure 엘레인 and 니나브 remembered they were alone; sometimes the stole made them start talking to the 아미를린 석좌 instead of 에그웨인 al’Vere. As usual, it worked. 니나브 took a very deep breath.

Before she could speak, though, 엘레인 said, “Do you mean to join him and this Band of the Red Hand to Gareth Bryne?”

에그웨인 shook her head. The 감시자s said there were six or seven thousand in 맷’s Band now, more than she remembered from 케렌, and a considerable number, if not nearly so many as those two captured men claimed, but Bryne’s soldiers truly would not take kindly to 용worn. Besides, she had her own scheme, which she explained while they drew the other chairs to the table. It was very like sitting in a kitchen talking. She moved the stole farther over.

“That is brilliant.” 엘레인’s grin said she meant it. But then, 엘레인 always said what she meant. “I didn’t think the other would work either, but this really is *brilliant*.”

니나브 sniffed irritably. “What makes you think 맷 will go along? He’ll stick a pole through the spokes just for the fun of it.”

“I think he made a promise,” 에그웨인 said simply, and 니나브 nodded. Slowly, reluctantly, but she nodded. 엘레인 looked lost, of course; she did not know him. “엘레인, 맷 does exactly as he pleases; he always has.”

“No matter how many turnips he had to peel for it,” 니나브 muttered, “or how often he was switched.”

“Yes, that is 맷,” 에그웨인 sighed. He had been the most irresponsible boy in Emond’s Field, maybe in the 두 강. “But if he gives his word, he keeps it. And I think he promised 랜드 to see you back in Caemlyn, 엘레인. You notice he retreated to asking me”—in a way he had—“but you he never changed a hair on. I think he’ll try to stay as close to you as your belt pouch. But we won’t let him even see you unless he does as we want.” She paused. “엘레인, if you want to go with him, you can. To 랜드, I mean. As soon as we squeeze all of the good out of 맷 and his Band.”

엘레인 hardly hesitated before shaking her head, and she shook it firmly. “No, Ebou Dar is too important.” That had been one victory, surprisingly won with a mere suggestion. 엘레인 and 니나브 were to join Merilille at Tylin’s court. “At least if he stays close, I’ll have a few days to try for a look at the *ter’angreal* he is carrying. It has to be that, 에그웨인. Nothing else could explain it.”

에그웨인 could only agree. She had simply meant to wrap him up in Air where he stood, just a gentle reminder of who he was trying to manhandle, but the flows touched him, and melted. That was the only way to explain it. They ceased to exist where they touched him. She still felt the shock of that moment, remembering, and she realized she was not the only one suddenly adjusting skirts that needed no adjusting.

“We could have some 감시자s turn out his pockets.” 니나브 sounded more than satisfied with the image. “We’ll see how Master 맷 카우톤 likes that.”

“If we take things away from him,” 에그웨인 said patiently, “don’t you think he might balk when we start telling him what to do?” 맷 had never taken orders very well, and his usual response to 에스 세다이 and the 하나의 힘 was to take the first chance to slip away. Maybe his promise to 랜드 would stop that—there *had* to be one; nothing else explained his behavior—but she was not going to risk it. 니나브 nodded, rather grudgingly.

“Maybe. . . .” Tapping her fingers on the table, 엘레인 stared at nothing thoughtfully for a moment. “Maybe we could take him to Ebou Dar. That way, I might have a better chance at the *ter’angreal.* Though if it stops *세다르*, I can’t see how I’ll *ever* manage to study it.”

“Take that young ruffian along!” 니나브 sat up straight. “You can’t mean it, 엘레인. He would make every day a misery; he’s very good at that. He’ll never do what he’s told. Besides, he will never stand still for it. He’s so wrapped up in taking you to Caemlyn, you could not budge him from it with a prybar and a team of horses.”

“But if he means to keep an eye on me until I reach Caemlyn,” 엘레인 told her, “he’ll have no choice but to go. It is perfect.”

“It might not be a bad idea,” 에그웨인 put in while 니나브 was searching for another argument. Sending them after the bowl still seemed right, but the more she thought of where they would have to search, the more she worried. “A few soldiers might be a very good idea, unless you’ve picked out 감시자s without letting me know. 톰 and Juilin are all very well, and 비르기테, but it is a rough place you’re going.”

“A *few* soldiers might be well enough,” 엘레인 said, coloring slightly. “So long as they know to follow orders.”

니나브 did not quite glance at 엘레인, but there was a distinct pause before she shook her head irascibly. “We’re hardly going to be fighting duels, 에그웨인, however touchy these Ebou Dari are. 톰 and Juilin will do quite well enough. Myself, I think all these stories we’ve been hearing are just meant to make us decide to give it over.” Everybody had heard tales of Ebou Dar since word had spread that they were going; Chesa had heard several, each more pitiful and horrific than the last, strangers killed for a wrong glance before they could blink, women widowed and children orphaned over a word, *women* fighting in the streets with knives. “No, if we could survive Tanchico with just 톰 and Juilin, and Liandrin and some of her Black sisters around in the bargain, we will do very well in Ebou Dar without 맷 카우톤 or any soldiers either. 맷 commanding soldiers! He never even remembered to milk his father’s cows unless he was put on the stool and handed the bucket.”

에그웨인 gave a faint sigh. Any mention of 비르기테 did that; they started as if goosed, then either stammered around her or else went on as if she had not been mentioned at all. One look had convinced 에그웨인 that the woman following 엘레인 and 니나브 about—especially 엘레인, for some reason—was the woman she had seen in *Tel’aran’rhiod.* 비르기테 of the legends, the archer who never missed, one of the dead heroes awaiting the call of the 발레르의 뿔. A dead hero, not a live woman walking the streets of Salidar, but the same woman nonetheless. 엘레인 still had provided no explanation, only a careful, embarrassed mumble about not being able to talk of what they had agreed not to talk of. 비르기테 herself, the hero of legends, turned the other way or went down alleys if she saw 에그웨인 coming. Ordering the woman to her study and demanding an explanation was out of the question; she had promised, after all, no matter how much a fool the situation made her feel. Anyway, there hardly seemed any harm. She just wished she knew the why of it. And the how.

Putting 비르기테 out of her mind for the moment, she leaned across the table toward 니나브. “Perhaps we can’t make 맷 take orders exactly, but wouldn’t it be fine to watch him smolder over having to be your bodyguard?”

“It would certainly be worthwhile,” 엘레인 said thoughtfully, “if 랜드 really has made him a general. Mother often said the best men were reluctant to take orders, and always worth teaching to. I can’t see 맷 as one of the best—Lini says ‘Fools only listen to themselves’—but if we can teach him enough that he doesn’t make a *complete* fool of himself where there is nobody to rescue him, we will be doing 랜드 a large favor. Besides, I need *time* if I am to study that *ter’angreal*.”

에그웨인 tried not to smile; 엘레인 always caught on so quickly. Then again, she probably was going to try teaching 맷 to sit up straight. That would be something to see. She liked 엘레인, and admired her strength, but she would bet on 맷 in that contest. By a whisker.

니나브 gave ground stubbornly. 맷 was wrongheaded; he would say “down” if they said “up” just to spite them. He could make trouble nailed up inside a barrel. They constantly would have to be dragging him out of taverns and gambling dens. Toward the end she was reduced to claiming that 맷 would probably pinch 엘레인 the first time her back was turned, and 에그웨인 knew they were overcoming her objections. 맷 certainly gave a lot of time to chasing after women, which 에그웨인 could hardly approve, but 니나브 surely knew as well as she that for all of looking when and how he should not, he seemed to have an uncanny knack for picking women who wanted to be chased, even the most unlikely. Unfortunately, just when she was sure that 니나브 was about to give in, a knock at the door announced 셰리암.

셰리암 did not wait on permission to enter; she never did. Cool-eyed in her blue stole, she paused to gaze at 니나브 and 엘레인. Second to the Amyrlin or not, the Keeper had no real authority over 에스 세다이 except what the Amyrlin chose to give her, and most assuredly none to dismiss anyone from the Amyrlin’s presence, yet that look was clearly a dismissal.

엘레인 rose smoothly, making a deep formal curtsy to 에그웨인. “If you will excuse me, Mother, I should go find 아비엔다.”

니나브, on the other hand, locked eyes with 셰리암 until 에그웨인 cleared her throat and slipped the striped stole back into place on her shoulders.

Flushing, 니나브 bobbed to her feet. “I should go, too. Janya said she would talk to me about lost Talents.”

The recovery of those Talents was not proving as easy as 에그웨인 had hoped. The sisters were willing enough to talk; the problem was in making 모그헤디엔 understand what was meant by a vague description or sometimes only a name, then hoping she really knew something. All very well to know, for example, that Aligning the 맷rix made metals stronger, but the woman knew less of metals than of 치유, and what under the Light was Spinning Earthfire, or for that matter, Milking 티어s?

모그헤디엔 seemed eager to help, desperate to, especially since 시우안 taught the trick of ignoring heat. Apparently she had lied to 니나브 and 엘레인 about that. Convinced 에그웨인 would take that for her “one lie,” the woman had groveled on her knees, weeping and begging, teeth chattering, kissing the hems of their skirts. Eager to help or not, it had raised her fear to new heights. The constant sickening rain of sniveling terror was just too much. Despite her intentions, the *a’dam* bracelet lay in 에그웨인’s pouch now. She would have given it to 니나브 now—and glad to be rid of it—but handing the thing back and forth in front of others would occasion comment sooner or later.

Instead, she said, “니나브, it might be best for you to avoid 맷 until his temper cools.” She was not sure that 맷 would really carry out his threat, but if anyone could goad him to it, 니나브 could, and there would be no convincing her after that. “Or at least make sure you only talk to him with a great many people around. Perhaps a few 감시자s.”

니나브 opened her mouth; then after a moment closed it again; her cheeks paled a little and she swallowed. “Yes. Yes, I think that might be best, Mother.”

셰리암 watched the door close with a small frown that she still wore when she turned to 에그웨인. “There were hard words, Mother?”

“Only what you expect when old friends meet after a long time. 니나브 remembers 맷 as a scamp, but he isn’t ten anymore, and he resents it.” Bound by the Oath against lying, 에스 세다이 had carried the half-truth, the quarter-truth and the implication to arts. Useful arts, in 에그웨인’s opinion. Especially with 에스 세다이. The 세 가지 맹세 did no one any favors, least of all 에스 세다이.

“It’s hard sometimes to remember that people change.” Taking a chair without being asked, 셰리암 arranged her blue silk skirts carefully. “I assume whoever commands the 용worn sent young 맷 with a message from 랜드 al’Thor? I hope you said nothings he might take as a promise, Mother. An army of 용worn not ten miles distant faces us with a delicate situation. It will not help if their commander believes we are going back on pledges.”

에그웨인 studied the other woman a moment. Nothing fazed 셰리암. Not that she let anyone see, at least. 셰리암 knew quite a lot about 맷; so did several other sisters in Salidar. Could that be used to press him in the right direction, or would it make him bolt? *맷 for later*, she thought firmly. *셰리암 now.* “Would you ask someone to bring tea, 셰리암? I feel a trifle thirsty.”

셰리암’s face altered only slightly, just a tightening around those tilted eyes so small that it barely disturbed her apparent serenity. 에그웨인 could almost see the question wanting to pop out, though. What had she said to 맷 that she did not want to talk about? What promises had she made that 셰리암 was going to have to rescue her from without losing ground to Romanda or Lelaine?
All 셰리암 did was say a few words to someone outside, and when she regained her seat, 에그웨인 gave her no opportunity to open her mouth. Instead, she hit her right between the eyes. So to speak. “It seems 맷 is the commander, 셰리암, and in a way, the army is the message. Apparently, 랜드 would like us all to come to him in Caemlyn. There was some mention of oaths of fealty.”

셰리암’s head came up, eyes widening. Only partly in outrage at such a suggestion, though. There was a definite tinge of . . . well, in anyone but an 에스 세다이, 에그웨인 would have called it fear. Very understandable, if so. If she had promised that—and she *was* from the same village; one of her *uses* as Amyrlin was that she had grown up with 랜드—it would be a bottomless mire to get out of. Word would spread no matter what 셰리암 did; some of the Hall might well blame it on her, or use it as a pretext, anyway. Romanda and Lelaine were not the only 의석자들 to have cautioned 에그웨인 about following 셰리암’s advice without consulting the Hall. In truth, Delana was the only one who really seemed to support 셰리암 fully, but she counseled listening to Romanda and Lelaine as well, as if it were really possible to go in three directions at once. And even could the Hall be managed, once news of the promise reached 랜드, and of its withdrawal, he would be ten times harder to handle. A hundred times.

에그웨인 only waited until 셰리암’s lips parted, then spoke first again. “Of course, I told him it was ridiculous.”

“Of course.” 셰리암’s voice was not quite as steady as it had been. Very good.

“But you are quite right. The situation is delicate. It’s such a pity. Your advice on how to deal with Romanda and Lelaine was good, but I don’t think increasing preparations to move will be enough now.”

Romanda had cornered her and grimly lectured her on haste leading to ruin; Gareth Bryne’s army must be made larger, large enough for news of its size to intimidate 엘라이더. And by the way, Romanda could not emphasize strongly enough once again that the embassies to rulers *must* be recalled; none but 에스 세다이 should be allowed to learn any more of troubles in the Tower than could be avoided. Lelaine cared about neither Lord Bryne’s army nor rulers—both were irrelevant—though she did counsel caution and waiting. The proper approaches to 에스 세다이 still in the Tower would surely yield dividends; 엘라이더 could be removed from the 아미를린 석좌 and 에그웨인 installed in such a fashion that none but a very few sisters would ever be certain what had actually happened. In time, the fact that the 백색 탑 had ever been broken would be taken for no more than a country tale. It might even have worked, if they had had enough time. If waiting did not give 엘라이더 just as much chance to work on sisters here.

The other difference with Lelaine was she had said everything with a smile that would have done very well for a pet 수련생 or 허락받은 자 she was very proud of. 에그웨인’s rediscovery of 이동 caused a lot of 에스 세다이 to smile, though only a handful were strong enough to make a gateway larger than they could put an arm through and most not even that. Romanda wanted to use gateways to remove the 맹세 막대 and certain other items—에그웨인 was not told exactly what—from the Tower so they could make true 에스 세다이 in Salidar while depriving 엘라이더 of the ability; surely 에그웨인 wanted to be truly 에스 세다이. Lelaine agreed about that last, but not about using gateways in the Tower; there was too much chance they might be detected, and if those in the Tower learned to Travel, too much advantage would be lost. Those points had carried considerable weight with the Hall, which did not please Romanda at all.

셰리암 had smiled too, over agreeing with Lelaine about something, but she was not smiling now. “Mother, I am not sure I understand,” she said, much too tolerantly. “Preparations are certainly enough to show the Hall you will not be bullied. Moving before everything is in place could be disastrous.”

에그웨인 managed to put on a disingenuous expression. “I understand, 셰리암. I don’t know what I would do without your advice.” How she looked forward to the day she could stop this. 셰리암 would make a very good Keeper—she might even have made a good Amyrlin—but 에그웨인 was going to enjoy the day she could teach the woman that she *was* Keeper, not Amyrlin. 셰리암 *and* the Hall. “It’s just that now 맷 has this army of 용worn on our doorstep. What will Lord Bryne do? Or some of his soldiers, on their own? Everybody talks about how he wanted to send men to hunt these 용worn who are supposed to be burning villages. I know he has been told to keep a tight rein on them, but. . . .”

“Lord Gareth will do exactly as we—as you—command, and no more.”

“Perhaps.” He was not so happy with that tight rein as 셰리암 believed. 시우안 spent a great deal of time with Gareth Bryne for all her grumbling about the man, and he told her things. 에그웨인 could not afford to give away 시우안’s allegiance, though. “I hope the same can be said for every one of his soldiers. We cannot move west into 아마디시아, but I thought perhaps we could go downriver, to Ebou Dar. Maybe by gateway. Surely 에스 세다이 are welcome there. Lord Bryne could camp outside the city. Moving would emphasize that we aren’t going to accept 랜드’s . . . offer, if it can be called that. And if we are going to make more preparations, I’m sure we would find everything much easier to accomplish in a large city, with roads and ships in and out of the harbor.”

셰리암’s control slipped again, to the extent of a breathiness in her voice. “Ebou Dar is not so welcoming as that, Mother. A few sisters are quite different from a few hundred, with an army at their backs. Mother, even a hint of that might make Tylin think we meant to seize the city. Tylin, and a good many 알타라n nobles who would like nothing better than an excuse to topple her and take the Throne of the Winds for themselves. A tangle of that kind would ruin us with every ruler. No, Mother, it is quite out of the question.”

“But do we dare remain here now? 맷 won’t do anything, but all it needs is a handful of Lord Bryne’s soldiers deciding to take matters into their own hands.” 에그웨인 frowned at her skirts, smoothed them as if thinking worriedly, then sighed. “The longer we sit and do nothing with an army of 용worn staring at us, the worse it will be. I won’t be surprised to hear rumors they mean to attack us, and people saying we should do for them first.” If this did not work, there would be rumors. 니나브 and 엘레인 and 시우안 and 리안 would see to that. It would be dangerous, but she could find some way to make 맷 retreat before sparks flew if it came to that. “Why, the way rumors spread, I wouldn’t be surprised if half of 알타라 thinks *we* are 용worn in under a month.” That was one rumor she would have stopped if she knew how. The Hall no longer brought nobles to see 로가인 since he was Healed, but Bryne’s recruiters still went out, and parties of 에스 세다이 hunting new 수련생s, and men to make the long trek to the nearest villages with their carts and wagons to buy food. A hundred paths for that rumor to take, and it only needed one. “셰리암, I can’t help feeling we are in a box, and if we don’t get out of it, nothing good will come. Nothing at all good.”

“The answer is to send the 용worn away,” 셰리암 said, not so patiently as before. “I regret letting 맷 out of our hands again, but I fear there’s no answer for it. You’ve told him the *offer* is refused; tell him to go.”

“I wish it were that simple. I don’t think he will for asking, 셰리암. He implied he was to wait right where he is until something happens. He could be expecting orders from 랜드, or even 랜드 himself. There was a rumor in 케렌 that he’s taken to sometimes 이동 with some of those men he’s gathered. The ones he’s teaching to channel? I do not know what we will do if that happens.”

셰리암 stared at her, breathing quite heavily for someone with such calm features.

A scratching at the door was followed by Tabiya with a beaten silver tray. Not catching the mood, she fussed about setting the green porcelain teapot and cups just so, the silver honeypot and small pitcher of cream and lace-edged linen napkins, until 셰리암 finally snapped at her so fiercely to be about her work that Tabiya squeaked and dropped a wide-eyed curtsy that nearly put her head on the floor and ran.

For a moment 셰리암 busied herself smoothing her skirts while she regained her composure. “Perhaps,” she said finally, reluctantly, “it might be necessary for us to leave Salidar after all. Sooner than I could wish.”

“But the only way left is north.” 에그웨인 widened her eyes. Light, but she hated this! “It will seem we’re moving toward 타르 발론.”

“I know that,” 셰리암 almost snapped. Drawing breath, she moderated her tone. “Forgive me, Mother. I feel a little. . . . I do not like being forced into things, and I fear 랜드 al’Thor has forced our hand before we are ready.”

“I will speak quite severely when I see him,” 에그웨인 said. “I can hardly think what I would do without your advice.” Perhaps she could find a way to send 셰리암 to study with the 현명한 이들 as an apprentice. He had never puzzled out what would make an 아일 decide not to come in. Chiefs, 현명한 이들 and Maidens had walked in on him in his smallclothes, in his bed, his bath. Green eyes regarded 민 neutrally.

This time 민 made no effort to get up. In fact, from the way she was lying against him, head pressed against his chest, breathing slowly, he was not sure she might not be falling asleep. After all, she had said she had reached Caemlyn in the night. Suddenly he became conscious of his hand fitted in the hollow of her waist, and moved it firmly to the arm of the chair. She sighed almost regretfully and snuggled against him. Going to sleep without a doubt.

“I have news,” Melaine said, “and I am uncertain which is the most important. 에그웨인 has gone from the tents. She goes to a place called Salidar, where there are 에스 세다이. These are the 에스 세다이 who may uphold you. At her asking, we did not speak to you of them before, but now I will tell you they are froward, undisciplined, contentious and full of themselves beyond reason.” Her tone was heated toward the end, and her head was thrust forward.

So one of the dreamwalkers in 케렌 had spoken to Melaine in her dreams. That was about all he knew of the dreamwalkers’ skills, and while it could have been useful, they were seldom willing to put it at his disposal. What was different was all that about froward and so forth. Most 아일 behaved as if they thought 에스 세다이 might strike them, believed they would deserve it if so, and intended to take the blow without flinching. Even 현명한 이들 spoke of 에스 세다이 respectfully if at all. Clearly a few things had changed. All he said, though, was “I know.” If Melaine had any intention of telling him why, she would without his asking. If she did not, asking would get no answers. “About 에그웨인, and Salidar too. There are nine from Salidar in Caemlyn right now. 민 here came with them.” 민 stirred on his chest and murmured something. 르웨어스 테린 was grumbling again, just too low to make out, and 랜드 was glad of the distraction. 민 felt . . . good. She would be offended to the sky if she knew. Then again, considering her promise to make him pay, she might laugh. Maybe. She could be quicksilver at times.

Melaine showed no surprise at his knowledge, not even shifting her shawl. Since marrying Bael she seemed to have—“calmed” was not quite the right word; it was much too placid for Melaine—grown less excitable. “That was my second news. You must be wary of them, 랜드 al’Thor, and use a firm hand. They will respect nothing else.” Most definitely a change.

“You will have two daughters,” 민 murmured. “Twins like mirrors.”

If Melaine had been unsurprised before, she made up for it now. Her eyes went wide, and she gave a start that nearly lifted her from the floor. “How could you . . . ?” she began incredulously, then stopped to gather herself. Even so, she went on in a breathless voice. “I myself was uncertain I was with child until this morning. How could you know?”

민 did get up then, giving him a look he knew all too well. It was his fault for some reason. She was not entirely without flaws, if small ones. Fussing with her coat, she looked everywhere except at Melaine, and when her gaze fell on him again, it was a variation of the first look. He had gotten her into this; it was up to him to get her out.

“It is all right, 민,” he said. “She’s a Wise One, and I expect she knows things that would curl your hair.” Except that already was curly. How did women do that, anyway? “I am sure she will promise to keep your secret, and you can trust her promise.” Melaine almost stumbled over her tongue promising.

Just the same, 랜드 received another look before 민 sat down beside Melaine. Reproachful, maybe. How *did* she expect him to get her out of it? Melaine would not forget because he asked, but she would keep a promise, and a secret. She had kept enough from him.

For all her reluctance, once 민 began she gave a much fuller explanation than she had ever given him at one time, perhaps helped by the other woman’s constant questions, and Melaine’s changing attitude as well. It was as if Melaine began to feel that 민’s ability made her an equal of sorts, not at all a wetlander.

“It is remarkable,” Melaine said at last. “Like interpreting the dream without dreaming. Two, you say? Both girls? Bael will be so pleased. Dorindha has given him three sons, but we both know he would like a daughter.” 민 blinked and gave her head a hard shake. Of course; she could not know about sister-wives.

From there the two of them passed quickly on to childbirth itself. Neither had ever borne a child, but each had helped midwives.

랜드 cleared his throat loudly. It was not that any of the details bothered him. He had helped ewes lamb, mares foal and cows calve. What was irritating was that they sat there with their heads together as though he had ceased to exist. Neither looked around until he cleared his throat again, loud enough that he wondered whether he had strained something.

Melaine leaned closer to 민 and spoke in a whisper that could have been heard in the next room. “Men always faint.”

“And always at the worst possible time,” 민 agreed in the same tone.

What would they think if they could have seen him in 맷’s father’s barn, blood and birthing fluids to his shoulders and three ribs cracked where he had been kicked because the mare had never foaled before and was frightened? A fine colt that had been, and the mare had not kicked at all the next time.

“Before I faint,” he said wryly, joining them on the carpet, “perhaps one of you would like to say some more about the 에스 세다이?” He would have stood up or sat on the floor before this had his lap not been full. Among the 아일, only chiefs had chairs, and a chief’s chair was only used for things like pronouncing judgments or receiving the submission of an enemy.

Both women were suitably chastened. Neither said anything, but there was ample shifting of shawl, adjusting of coat and not quite meeting his eye. All that vanished once they got down to talking. 민 held tenaciously to her opinion that the 에스 세다이 from Salidar meant no harm to 랜드 and might give aid, suitably handled, which was with all respect in public and in private her reporting to 랜드 every whisper she overheard. “I’m not being a traitor, you understand, Melaine. I knew 랜드 before any 에스 세다이 except 모이라인, really, and the truth of it is, he took my loyalty long before she died.”

Melaine did not think 민 a traitor, quite the contrary, and seemed to think even better of her. 현명한 이들 did have their own version of the 아일 view of spies. But she argued that with notable exceptions, 에스 세다이 could be trusted as far as Shaido, which was to say not until they had been taken captive and made *gai’shain.* She did not exactly suggest captivity for the 에스 세다이 at The Crown of Roses, but she did not miss far. “How can you trust them, 랜드 al’Thor? I think they have no honor, except for 에그웨인 al’Vere, and she—” Melaine twitched her shawl again. “When an 에스 세다이 shows me she has as much honor as 에그웨인, I will trust her, and not before.”

For his part, 랜드 listened more than spoke, and saying no more than a dozen or so words, learned a great deal. Answering Melaine’s arguments, 민 ran through the embassy name by name, listing what each woman had said about support for 랜드, and in truth admitting that all was not exactly rosy. Merana Ambrey and Kairen Stang, a Blue, were both 안도르an, and for all that 에스 세다이 supposedly forsook all allegiances save the 백색 탑, perhaps because they were estranged from the Tower, they worried that 랜드 sat in Caemlyn and might have murdered 모르가세. Rafela Cindal, also 청색 아자, might be pleased with the changes 랜드 had made in 티어, where once channeling had been outlawed and a girl found able to learn was hurried out of the country, but she said little, and 모르가세 worried her too. Seonid Traighan, a Green, mulled over every rumor from her native 케렌 and kept her own counsel, and Faeldrin Harella, the second Green sister, sometimes compared 용worn atrocities in 알타라 and 무란디 to what 용worn had done in 타라본, refusing even to talk about the fact that civil war had ripped her land apart before the first man had sworn to the Dragon there. No matter how Melaine pressed, though, 민 insisted that every one of those 에스 세다이 acknowledged 랜드 to be the 용의 환생 and asked her most carefully, all through the journey from Salidar, what he was like and how he could best be approached without either offending or frightening him.

랜드 grunted at that—that they were worried about frightening him—but Melaine began insisting that if most of the women in the embassy had so much reason to be against 랜드, then the embassy as a whole surely could not be trusted far enough to fetch dung for the fire. 민 spared him an apologetic grimace and rushed on. 아라드 도만 had seen as much of 용worn as 타라본, as well as its own civil war, but Demira Eriff, of the 갈색 아자, only talked of two things really: meeting 랜드, and the rumor that he had started some sort of school in 케렌; no man who started a school could be all bad in Demira’s eyes. 베렌icia Morsad, a Yellow sister from 시엔나르, had heard from 시엔나르ans in Salidar that 랜드 had been received in 팔 다라 by the great captain Lord Agelmar Jagad, an honor that seemed to carry considerable weight with her; Lord Agelmar would hardly have received a ruffian, a fool or a scoundrel. It weighed almost as heavily with Masuri Sokawa; she was a Brown, from 아라펠, which bordered 시엔나르. Finally there was Valinde Nathenos, who according to 민 showed an eagerness very unlike the 백색 아자 to have 랜드 drive 사마엘 out of 일리안; a promise of that, a promise even to try, and 민 would not be surprised to see Valinde offer him an oath of fealty. Melaine expressed disbelief, even rolling her eyes; she had never seen an 에스 세다이 with that much sense, an attitude 랜드 found more than surprising considering that she would probably laugh in his face if he asked for such an oath. 민 maintained that it was true, though, whatever the other woman said.

“I will show them as much respect as I can without kneeling,” 랜드 told 민 when she finally ran down. For Melaine, he added, “And until they show proof of goodwill, I’ll trust them not one jot.” He thought that should please them both, since each got what she wanted, but from the frowns he received, it pleased neither.

After all that arguing, he half-expected the pair to be at one another’s throats, but it seemed that Melaine’s pregnancy and 민’s viewing had created a bond. When they stood, the women were all smiles and hugs, and Melaine said, “I did not think I would like you, 민, but I do, and I will name one of the girls after you, because you knew of her first. I must go to tell Bael so he will not be jealous that 랜드 al’Thor knew before him. May you always find water and shade, 민.” To 랜드, she added, “Watch these 에스 세다이 closely, 랜드 al’Thor, and give 민 your protection when she needs it. They will harm her if they learn she is sworn to you.” Of course, she left with exactly the ceremony with which she had arrived, a nod of the head.

Which left him alone with 민 again. Which felt awkward for some reason.

**CHAPTER** **42**

*The 검은 탑*

랜드 and 민 stood looking at one another, not moving, until finally he said, “Would you like to come out to the farm with me?”

She gave a little start at the sound of his voice. “The farm?”

“It’s a school, really. For the men who come for the amnesty.”

민’s face paled. “No, I don’t think. . . . Merana will be waiting to hear from me. And I should let them know your rules as soon as possible. Any one of them could wander into the Inner City without knowing, and you wouldn’t want. . . . I really ought to go.”

He did not understand. Without meeting even one of the students, she was afraid of them, men who could channel, men who wanted to channel. In anyone else it would be understandable, but he could channel, and she was ready to rough his hair and poke his ribs and call him names to his face. “Do you want an escort back to The Crown of Roses? There really are footpads, even by daylight. Not many, but I would not like anything to happen to you.”

Her laugh was a bit unsteady. She truly was upset over the farm. “I took care of myself while you were tending sheep, farmboy.” Abruptly she had a knife in either hand; a flourish, and they went back up her sleeves, not quite so smoothly as they had come out. In a much more sober tone, she said, “You must take care of yourself, 랜드. Rest. You look tired.” Startlingly, she went a-tiptoe and stretched her head up to brush his lips with a kiss. “It is good to see you too, sheepherder.” And with another laugh, this one delighted, she slipped out.

Muttering to himself, 랜드 put his coat back on and went into his bedchamber to fetch his sword from the back of the wardrobe, a dark, rose-carved thing tall enough and wide enough for four men’s clothes. He really was turning into a randy goat. 민 was just having her fun. He wondered how long she intended to keep teasing him for one slip of the tongue.

A cloth bag of moderate size, clinking when he lifted it from under his stockings in a drawered chest inlaid with lapis, went into one coat pocket, and a much smaller, velvet bag went in atop his *angreal.* The silversmith who had made the contents of the larger had been more than happy to work for the 용의 환생 and had tried to refuse payment for the honor of it. The goldsmith who had made the single piece in the other bag had required four times what 바쉐어 said the work was worth, and a pair of Maidens to stand over him until it was done.
This trip to the farm had been in 랜드’s mind for some time already. He did not like 타임, and 르웨어스 테린 would surge around the man, but he could not go on avoiding the place. Especially not now. So far as he knew, 타임 had done well at keeping the students out of the city—at least, 랜드 had heard of no incidents, and he would have—but news of Merana and the embassy would reach the farm eventually, by the supply carts or with new students, and in the way of rumors, nine 에스 세다이 would become nine Red sisters, or ninety, hunting men to gentle. Whether the result of that would be students running off in the night or students coming into Caemlyn to strike the first blow, he had to quell it before it began.

Caemlyn held too many rumors of 에스 세다이 already as it was, another reason he had planned to go out. Alanna and Verin and the 두 강 girls had grown into half the Tower, by the word in the streets, and there were plenty of other tales of 에스 세다이 sneaking into the city, sneaking through the gates in the night. That story of an 에스 세다이 치유 stray cats was so prevalent he could almost believe in her himself, but all 바쉐어’s efforts to track the tale down provided as much substance as the tale that the women who escorted the 용의 환생 everywhere were really 에스 세다이 in disguise.

Unconsciously 랜드 turned, staring at a wall banded with white reliefs of lions and roses, staring beyond it. Alanna was no longer at Culain’s Hound. She was on edge; had she not been 에스 세다이, he would have said her nerves were jagged. Once last night he had wakened, sure she was weeping; the feel had been that strong. Sometimes he almost found himself forgetting she was there—until something like her waking him happened. He supposed you really could grow used to anything. This morning Alanna was . . . eager, as well; eager seemed the best word. He would wager all of Caemlyn that the plumb line from his eyes to her ran straight to The Crown of Roses. He would wager Verin was with her. Not nine 에스 세다이. Eleven.

르웨어스 테린 murmured uneasily. It was the sound of a man wondering whether his back was against a wall. 랜드 wondered, too. Eleven, and thirteen could take him as easily as scoop up a child. If he gave them the chance. 르웨어스 테린 began laughing softly, a hoarse weeping sort of laugh; he had drifted again.

For a moment 랜드 considered Somara and Enaila, then opened a gateway right there above the blue-and-gold-patterned carpet in his bedchamber. Sullen as they were this morning, one of them was sure to blurt something before the visit to the farm was done, and remembering his previous visits, he did not want the students all looking over their shoulders for fear of twenty or so Maidens. That sort of thing did little for a man’s confidence, and they needed confidence if they were to survive.

타임 was right on one point; holding on to *세이딘*, a man knew he was alive, and it went beyond heightened senses. Despite the. 어둠의 존재’s taint, despite the feel of oily offal staining your bones, when the Power was trying to melt you where you stood, freeze you till you shattered, when one misstep or one moment of weakness meant death—Light, you knew you were alive. Still, he pushed the Source away as soon as he was through the gateway, and not only to rid himself of the taint before his stomach emptied itself; it seemed worse than it had been, more vile, if that was possible. His real reason for abandoning the Power was that he did not think he dared face 타임 with *세이딘* in him and 르웨어스 테린 in his head.

The clearing was browner than he remembered, more leaves crackling under his boots and still fewer on the trees. Some of the pines were completely yellow, and a number of leatherleafs stood dead, gray and bare. But if the clearing had changed, the farm was altered almost beyond recognition.

The farmhouse looked in much better repair with its new thatch, and the barn had certainly been rebuilt entirely; it was much larger than before and did not lean at all. Horses filled a large corral beside the barn, and the pens of cows and sheep had been moved farther away. The goats were penned now as well, and neat rows of coops held the chickens. The forest had been cleared back. Over a dozen long white tents made a row beyond the barn, and nearby stood the frames for two buildings much larger than the farmhouse, where a cluster of women sat outside doing their sewing and watching a score of children roll hoops and toss balls and play with dolls. The biggest change was the students, most in close-fitting high-collared black coats and few sweating. There must have been well over a hundred, of all ages. 랜드 had had no idea 타임’s recruiting trips had gone this well. The feel of *세이딘* seemed to fill the air. Some men practiced weaves, setting fire to stumps or shattering stones or snaring each other in coils of Air. Others channeled to haul water, the buckets gripped with Air, or to push dung carts from the barn, or stack firewood. Not everyone was channeling. Henre Haslin had a line of bare-chested men under his eye, working the forms with practice swords. With only a fringe of white hair and a bulbous red nose, Haslin sweated more than his students, and doubtless was wishing for his wine, but he watched and corrected as sharply as when he was Master of the Sword for the Queen’s Guards. Saeric, a gray-haired Red Water Goshien with no right hand, had two shirtless rows under his stony eyes. One was kicking as high as their heads, pivot and kick, then pivot and kick with the other foot, over and over; the other punched the air in front of them as fast they could. All in all, it was a far cry from the pitiful handful 랜드 had seen the last time.

A black-coated man just short of his middle years planted himself in front of 랜드. He had a sharp nose and a sneering mouth. “And who are you?” he demanded in a 타라본er accent. “I suppose you have come to the 검은 탑 to learn, yes? You should have waited in Caemlyn for the wagon to bring you. You could have had another day to enjoy that fine coat.”

“I am 랜드 al’Thor,” 랜드 said quietly. Quietly so as not to let out a sudden surge of anger. Civility cost nothing, and if this fool did not decide it was cheap at the price soon. . . .

If anything, the sneer deepened. “So you are him, are you?” He looked 랜드 up and down insolently. “You do not look so grand to me. I think that I myself could—” A flow of Air solidified just before it clipped him under the ear, and he collapsed in a heap.

“Sometimes we need a hard discipline,” 타임 said, coming to stand over the man on the ground. His voice was almost jolly, but his dark tilted eyes stared close to murder at the man he had clubbed. “You cannot tell a man he has the power to make the earth shake, then expect him to walk small.” 용s climbing the sleeves of his black coat glittered in the sunlight; thread-of-gold would do for the one, but what could make the blue shine so? Abruptly he raised his voice. “키스만! Rochaid! Drag Torval away and douse him until he wakes. No 치유, mind you. Maybe an aching head will teach him to mind his tongue.”

Two men in black coats, younger than 랜드, came running and bent over Torval, then hesitated, glancing at 타임. After a moment, 랜드 felt *세이딘* fill them; flows of Air lifted a limp Torval, and the pair trotted away with him floating between them.

*I should have killed him long ago*, 르웨어스 테린 panted. *I should have . . . should have. . . .* There was a stretching toward the Source.

*No, burn you!* 랜드 thought. *No, you don’t! You’re only a bloody voice!* With a fading wail 르웨어스 테린 fled.

랜드 took a slow breath. 타임 was looking at him, wearing that almost-smile. “You teach them 치유?”

“The little I know, first thing. Even before how not to sweat to death in this weather. A weapon loses its utility if it’s going to be laid up with the first wound. As it is, I have had one kill himself drawing too deeply and three burn themselves out, but no one has died from a sword yet.” He managed to put a good deal of contempt into the word “sword.”

“I see,” 랜드 said simply. One dead and three burned out. Did 에스 세다이 lose that many in the Tower? But then, they went slowly. They could afford to go slowly. “What is this 검은 탑 the fellow was talking about? I don’t like the sound of it, 타임.” 르웨어스 테린 was mumbling and moaning again, just short of making words.

The hawk-nosed man shrugged, studying the farm and the students with a proprietory pride. “A name the students use. You could not go on calling this just ‘the farm.’ They certainly did not feel right about it; they wanted something more. The 검은 탑 to balance the 백색 탑.” He tilted his head, looking at 랜드 almost sideways. “I can suppress it, if you wish. It is easy enough to take a word from men’s lips.”

랜드 hesitated. Easy enough to take a word from their lips perhaps, but not from their minds. It did have to be called something. He had not thought of that. Why not the 검은 탑? Though looking at the farmhouse and the framing—larger, but only wood—the name did make him smile. “Let it stand.” Maybe the 백색 탑 had begun as humbly. Not that the 검은 탑 would ever have time to grow into anything to rival the White. That erased his smile, and he looked at the children sadly. He was playing as much as they, pretending there was a chance of building something that might last. “Assemble the students, 타임. I have a few things to say to them.”

He had come expecting to gather them round him, and then seeing their numbers, maybe to speak from the back of the rickety cart that now seemed to have vanished. 타임 had a platform for making addresses, though, a plain block of black stone dressed and polished so finely that it shone like a mirror in the sunlight, with two steps cut into the back. It stood in an open area beyond the farmhouse, the ground beaten bare and flat and hard around it. The women and children gathered to one side to watch and listen.

From the block, 랜드 had a chance to see clues to how far 타임’s recruiting had ranged. Jahar Narishma, whom 타임 had pointed out, the young man with the spark, had dark eyes as big as a girl’s, a pale face filled with confidence, and hair in two long braids with silver bells on the ends. Actually, 타임 had said he came from 아라펠, but 랜드 recognized a 시엔나르an’s shaved head and topknot on another man, and two with the transparent veils often worn by men and women alike in 타라본. There were tilted eyes from 살다에아 and pale, short fellows from 케렌. One old man had a beard oiled and cut to a point in imitation of a 타이런 lord, which he assuredly was not with that creased leathery face, and no fewer than three wore beards that left their upper lips bare. He hoped 타임 had not roused 사마엘’s interest by recruiting into 일리안. He had expected mainly younger men, but fresh faces like Eben’s and Fedwin’s were balanced by gray or balding heads, some even more grizzled than Damer. Now that he thought of it, though, there was no mystery, no reason there should not be as many grandfathers who could be taught as boys.

He did not know how to make speeches, but he had thought long and hard over what he wanted to say. Not the first part, but that was quickest done, with luck. “You’ve all probably heard stories that the Tower . . . the 백색 탑 . . . has divided. Well, it’s true. There are some rebel 에스 세다이 who might just decide to follow me, and they’ve sent emissaries. Nine of them, sitting in Caemlyn right now and waiting my pleasure. So when you hear about 에스 세다이 in Caemlyn, don’t believe any rumors. You know why they are here, and you can laugh in the face of the fellow with the rumor.”

There was no reaction. They just stood there staring up at him, hardly seeming to blink. 타임 looked wry, very wry. Touching the larger bag in his pocket, 랜드 went on with the part he had labored over.

“You need a name. In the 고대어, 에스 세다이 means Servants of All, or something very close. The 고대어 doesn’t translate easily.” For himself, he knew only a few words, some from 아스모데안, a handful from 모이라인, some that had seeped through from 르웨어스 테린. 바쉐어 had provided what he needed, though. “Another word in the 고대어 is *asha’man.* It means guardian, or guardians. Or defender, and maybe a couple of other things; I told you, the 고대어 is very flexible. Guardian seems to be best, though. Not just any defender or guardian, though. You could not call a man who defended an unjust cause *asha’man*, and never one that was evil. An *asha’man* was a man who defended truth and justice and right for everyone. A guardian who would not yield even when hope was gone.” 빛 knew, hope would go when Tarmon Gai’don came, if not before. “That is what you are here to become. When you finish your training, you will be Asha’man.”

Murmurs rustled like leaves in a breeze, the name being repeated, but they died quickly. Attentive faces peered up at him; he could almost see ears pricking for his next words. At least that was a little better than before. The cloth bag gave off a faint clinking as he took it from his coat pocket.

“에스 세다이 begin as 수련생s, then become 허락받은 자, then finally full 에스 세다이. You will have degrees, too, but not like theirs. There will be no putting out or sending away among us.” Send away? Light, he would do everything short of tying them hand and foot to stop anyone who wanted to go if he could channel at all. “When a man first comes to the 검은 탑 . . .” He did not like that name. “. . . he will be called a soldier, because that is what he becomes when he joins us, what you all became, a soldier to fight the Shadow, and not just the Shadow, but anyone who opposes justice or oppresses the weak. When a soldier reaches a certain stage in his skills, he will be called 헌신자, and wear this.” From the bag he took one of the badges the silversmith had made, a small gleaming silver sword, perfect with its long hilt and slanting quillons and slightly curved blade. “타임.”

타임 walked to the block stiffly, and 랜드 bent to pin the silver sword to the tall collar of his coat. It seemed to shine even more brightly against the pitch-black wool. 타임’s face had as much expression as the stone beneath 랜드’s boots. 랜드 handed him the bag, whispering, “Give these to whoever you think is ready. *The Color of Trust*
