“No,” Katerine said, toying idly with the fringe on her shawl. “What you need to learn, it has been decided, is humility. The Amyrlin has heard of your foolish refusal to curtsy to sisters. In her opinion, it’s the last symbol of your defiant nature, and so you are to receive a new form of instruction.”

에그웨인 felt a moment of fear. “What kind of instruction?” she said, keeping her voice even.

“Chores and work,” Katerine said.

“I already do chores, just like the 수련생s.”

“You mistake me,” Katerine said. “From now on, *all* you will do is chores. You are to report to the kitchens immediately—you will spend every afternoon working there. In the evenings, you will scrub floors. In the mornings you will report to the groundsmaster and work the gardens. This will be your life, those same three activities every day—five hours at each one—until you give up your foolish pride and learn to curtsy to your betters.”

It was an end to 에그웨인’s freedom, what little she had. There was glee in Katerine’s eyes.

“Ah, so you understand,” Katerine said. “No more visiting sisters in their quarters, wasting their time as you practice weaves that you have already mastered. No more laziness; now you will work instead. What think you of that?”

It wasn’t the difficulty of the work that worried 에그웨인—she didn’t mind the chores she did each day. It was the lack of contact with other sisters that would ruin her. How would she mend the 백색 탑? Light! It was a disaster.

She gritted her teeth and forced down her emotion. She met Katerine’s eyes, saying, “Very well. Let us go.”

Katerine blinked. She’d obviously expected a tantrum, or at least a fight. But this was not the time. 에그웨인 turned her step toward the kitchens, leaving the quarters of the Whites behind. She couldn’t let them know how effective this punishment was.

She forced down her panic as she walked, the cavernous hallways of the inner Tower lined with bracketed lamps, long and sinuous, like the heads of serpents spouting tiny flames up toward the stone ceiling. She could deal with this. She *would* deal with this. They would not break her.

Perhaps she should work for a few days, then pretend that she had been humbled. Should she give the curtsy 엘라이더 demanded? It was a simple thing, really. One curtsy, and she could go back to her more important duties.

*No,* she thought. *No, that would not be the end of it. I’d lose the moment I gave that first curtsy*. Giving in would prove to 엘라이더 that 에그웨인 could be broken. Curtsying would begin a descent into destruction. Soon, 엘라이더 would decide that 에그웨인 needed to start using honorifics for the 에스 세다이. The false Amyrlin would send 에그웨인 back to work detail, knowing it had been effective before. Would 에그웨인 bend there too? How long before any credibility she had ended up forgotten, trampled into the tiles of the Tower hallways?

She could not bend. The beatings had not changed her behavior; work detail must not change her either.

Three hours of working the kitchens did little to improve her mood. Laras, the hefty Mistress of Kitchens, had set 에그웨인 at scrubbing out one of the ovenlike fireplaces. It was dirty, grimy work, not conducive to thinking. Not that there were many ways out of her situation.

에그웨인 knelt back on her heels, raising an arm and wiping her brow. The arm came away smeared with soot. 에그웨인 sighed softly, her mouth and nose protected by a damp cloth to keep her from breathing too much ash. Her breath was hot and stuffy against her face, and her skin was sticky with sweat. The drops that fell from her face were stained with black soot; through the cloth she could smell the dull, crusty scent of ash that had been burned over and over and over again.

The fireplace was a large square construction of burned red bricks. It was open on both sides and more than large enough to crawl into—which was exactly what 에그웨인 had to do. Dark crusts built up on the inside of the flue and chimney, and they needed to be scrubbed free lest they clog the chimney or break free and fall into the food. Outside in the dining room, 에그웨인 could hear Katerine and Lirene chatting and laughing with each other. The Reds periodically poked heads in to check on her, but her real supervisor was Laras, who was scrubbing pots on the other side of the room.

에그웨인 had changed into a work dress for the duty. While it had once been white, it had been repeatedly used by 수련생s cleaning the fireplaces, and the soot had been ground into the fibers. Patches of gray stained the cloth, like shadows.

She rubbed the small of her back, got back on her hands and knees, and crawled farther into the fireplace. Using a small wooden scrape, she worked clumps of ash free from seams between the bricks, then gathered it up and deposited it in brass buckets, the rims of which were powdered white and gray with ash. Her first task had been to dig out all of the loose soot and pile it into the buckets. Her hands were so blackened from the work she worried that the most furious scrubbing wouldn’t get them clean. Her knees ached, and they seemed a strange counterpart to her backside, which still stung from her regular morning beating.

She continued, scratching with her scrape at a blackened section of brick, dimly lit by the lantern she’d left burning in a corner inside the fireplace. She itched to use the 하나의 힘; but the Reds outside would sense her channeling, and she’d discovered that her afternoon dose of forkroot had been uncharacteristically strong, leaving her unable to channel as much as a trickle. In fact, it had been strong enough to leave her drowsy, which made the work even harder.

Was this to be her life? Trapped inside a fireplace, scrubbing at bricks nobody saw, locked away from the world? She couldn’t stand up to 엘라이더 if everyone forgot about her. She coughed quietly, the sound echoing against the inside of the fireplace.

She needed a plan. Her only recourse seemed to be to use the sisters who were trying to root out the 흑색 아자. But how to visit them? Without being trained by sisters, she had no way to escape her Red handlers by entering the domains of other 아자s. Could she sneak away somehow while doing labor? If her absence were discovered, she’d probably end up in an even *worse* situation.

But she couldn’t let her life be dominated by this menial labor! 최후의 전투 was approaching, the 용의 환생 ran free, and the 아미를린 석좌 was on her hands and knees cleaning fireplaces! She gritted her teeth, scrubbing furiously. The soot had been baked on for so long that it formed a glossy black patina on the stone. She’d never get it all off. She just needed to make sure it was clean enough that none would break free.

Reflected in that glossy patina, she saw a shadow move across the opening of the far side of the fireplace. 에그웨인 immediately reached for the Source—but, of course, she found nothing. Not with forkroot clouding her mind. But there was *definitely* someone outside the fireplace, crouching down, moving quietly. . . .

에그웨인 gripped the scrape in one hand, slowly reaching down with the other to grab the brush she’d been using to scoop up ash. Then she spun.

Laras froze, peeking into the fireplace. The Mistress of Kitchens wore a large white apron, stained with a few soot marks itself. Her pudgy round face had seen its share of winters; her hair was starting to gray, and lines creased the sides of her eyes. Leaning over as she was, her jowls formed a second, third and fourth chin, and she gripped the side of the fireplace opening with a thick-fingered hand.

에그웨인 relaxed. Why had she been so certain that someone had been sneaking up on her? It was just Laras coming to check on her.

Yet why had the woman moved so silently? Laras glanced to the side, eyes narrowing. Then she raised a finger to her lips. 에그웨인 felt herself tense again. What was going on?

Laras backed out of the fireplace, waving for 에그웨인 to follow. The Mistress of Kitchens moved on light feet, far quieter than 에그웨인 would have thought possible. Assistant cooks and scullions clanged away in other parts of the kitchen, but none were directly visible. 에그웨인 crept free of the fireplace, tucking the scrape into her belt and wiping her hands on her dress. She pulled the cloth free from her face, breathing sweet, soot-free air. She took a deep breath, and received a harsh glare from Laras, followed by another finger to the lips.

에그웨인 nodded, following Laras through the kitchens. In a few moments she and 에그웨인 stood in a pantry, thick with the scent of dried grains and aging cheeses. The tiles gave way to more durable brickwork here. Laras shoved aside a few sacks, then pulled open a piece of the floor. It was a wooden trapdoor, capped with shaved brickwork on the top to make it seem part of the floor. It revealed a small, rock-walled chamber underneath the pantry, large enough to hold a person, though a tall man would be cramped.

“You wait here until night,” Laras said in a low voice. “I can’t get you out right now, not with the Tower fluttery as a yard full of hens when the fox is about. But the garbage goes out late at night, and I’ll hide you among the girls who unload it. A dockworker will take you to a small boat and row you across the river. I have some friends among the guard; they’ll turn the other way. Once you reach the other side, it’s up to you what you do. I’d advise against going back to those fools who made you their puppet. Find some place to lie low until this all blows over, then come back and see if whoever’s in charge will take you in. Isn’t likely it will be 엘라이더, the way things are going. . . .”

에그웨인 blinked in surprise.

“Well,” the heavyset woman said. “In you go.”

“I—”

“No time for jabbering!” Laras said, as if she weren’t the one doing all of the talking. She was obviously nervous, the way she kept glancing about and tapping her foot. But she’d obviously *also* done this sort of thing before. Why was the simple cook in the 백색 탑 so skilled at sneaking, so handy with a plan to get 에그웨인 out of the fortified and besieged city? And why did she have a bolt-hole in the kitchens in the first place? Light! How had she created it?

“Don’t worry about me,” Laras said, eyeing 에그웨인. “I can handle myself. I’ll keep all of the kitchen servants away from where you were working. Those 에스 세다이 only check on you every half-hour or so—and since they just checked a minute ago, it will be a while before they look in again. When they *do* check, I can plead ignorance and everyone will assume you slipped out of the kitchens. We’ll soon have you out of the city and nobody will be the wiser.”

“Yes,” 에그웨인 said, finally finding her tongue, “but *why*?” She had assumed that, after helping 민 and 시우안, Laras wouldn’t be eager to help another fugitive.

Laras looked back at her, in the woman’s eyes a determination as hard as any 에스 세다이’s. 에그웨인 certainly had overlooked this woman! Who was she really?

“I won’t be a party to the breaking of a girl’s spirit,” Laras said sternly. “Those beatings are shameful! Fool 에스 세다이. I’ve served loyally these years, I have, but now they’ve told me that you’re to be worked as hard as I can push you, indefinitely. Well, I can see when a girl has moved away from being instructed and into being beaten down. I won’t have it, not in my kitchens. Light burn 엘라이더 for thinking she could do such a thing! Execute you or make you a 수련생, I don’t care. But this breaking is unacceptable!”

The woman stood, setting hands on hips, a puff of flour rising from her apron. Oddly, 에그웨인 found herself considering the offer. She’d denied 시우안’s offer to save her, but if she fled now, she would return to the rebel camp having freed herself. That would be far superior to being rescued. She could get away from all this, away from the beatings, away from the drudgery.

To do what? To sit on the outside and watch the Tower collapse?

“No,” she said to Laras. “Your offer is very kind, but I can’t take it. I’m sorry.”

Laras frowned. “Now, you listen—”

“Laras,” 에그웨인 interrupted, “one does not take that tone with an 에스 세다이, no matter that one is the Mistress of Kitchens.”

Laras hesitated. “Fool girl. You ain’t 에스 세다이.”

“Accept it or not, I still can’t go. Unless you intend to try stuffing me into that hole yourself—gagging and tying me to keep me from crying out, followed by escorting me across the river in person—then I suggest letting me return to my work.”

“But why?”

“Because,” 에그웨인 said, glancing back at the fireplace. “Someone has to fight her.”

“You can’t fight like this,” Laras said.

“Each day is a battle,” 에그웨인 said. “Each day I refuse to bend means something. Even if 엘라이더 and her Reds are the only ones who know it, that’s something. A small something, but more than I could do from the outside. Come. I’ve still got two hours of work left.”

She turned and began to walk back toward the fireplace. A reluctant Laras closed the hatch on her hidden chamber, then joined her. The woman made much more noise now as she walked, brushing against counters, her footfalls sounding on the bricks. Curious how she’d been able to be so quiet when she wanted to.

A flash of red cloth, like the blood of a dead rabbit in the snow, moved through the kitchens. 에그웨인 froze as Katerine, wearing a dress with crimson skirts and yellow trim, spotted her. The Red’s mouth was thin-lipped, her eyes narrow. Had she seen 에그웨인 and Laras walk off?

Laras froze.

“I see now what I was doing wrong,” 에그웨인 quickly said to the Mistress of Kitchens, eyeing a second hearth, which lay near where they had been standing in the pantry. “Thank you for showing it to me. I’ll be more careful now.”

“See that you are,” Laras said, shaking out of her shock. “Otherwise, you’ll see what a *real* punishment is like, not those halfhearted paddlings the 수련생 감독관 gives. Now back to work with you.”

에그웨인 nodded, hurrying back toward the fireplace. Katerine held up a hand to forestall her. 에그웨인’s heart thumped traitorously.

“No need,” Katerine said. “The Amyrlin has demanded that the 수련생 attend her tonight at dinner. I told the Amyrlin that one day of work would hardly break someone as foolishly stubborn as this child, but she is insistent. I guess you are to be given your first chance to prove your humility, child. I suggest you take it.”

에그웨인 glanced down at her blackened hands and soiled dress.

“Go, run,” Katerine said. “Wash up and clean yourself. The Amyrlin will not be kept waiting.”
Washing up proved to be nearly as difficult as cleaning the fireplace. The soot had stained her hands much in the way it had the work dress. 에그웨인 spent the better part of an hour washing in a tub full of lukewarm water, trying to make herself presentable. Her fingernails were ragged from scraping the bricks, and it seemed that each time she rinsed her hair, she washed out an entire bucket’s worth of soot flakes.

However, she was glad for the chance. She rarely had much time for bathing; usually she could not stop for more than a quick scrub. As she rinsed and scrubbed in the small, gray-tiled bathing chamber, she considered her next step.

She had turned down the opportunity to flee. That meant she had to work with 엘라이더 and her Reds, the only sisters she saw. But could they be made to see their errors? She wished she could send the whole lot of them for penance and be rid of them.

But no. She was Amyrlin; she represented all 아자s, including the Red. She couldn’t treat them as 엘라이더 had treated the Blues. They were the most antagonistic toward her, but that meant a greater challenge. She seemed to be making some headway with Silviana, and hadn’t Lirene Doirellin admitted that 엘라이더 had made serious mistakes?

Maybe the Reds weren’t the only ones she could influence. There were always chance meetings with other sisters in the hallways. If one of them approached her to speak, the Reds couldn’t very well tow her away. They would show some decorum, and that would give 에그웨인 a chance to interact a bit with other sisters.

But how to treat 엘라이더 herself? Was it wise to let the false Amyrlin continue to think that 에그웨인 was nearly cowed? Or was it time to make a stand?

By the end of her bath, 에그웨인 felt a great deal cleaner and a great deal more confident. Her war had taken a serious turn for the worse, but she could still fight. She ran a hurried brush through her wet hair, threw on a new 수련생 dress—my, how good it felt to have the soft, clean fabric on her skin!—and left to join her handlers.

They escorted her up to the Amyrlin’s chambers. 에그웨인 passed several groups of sisters, and she held herself carefully erect for their benefit. The handlers took her through the Red sector of the Tower, the tiles on the floor shifting to a pattern of red and charcoal. There were more people walking about here, women in their shawls, servants bearing the Flame of 타르 발론 on their chests. Never any 감시자s; that always felt strange to 에그웨인, since they were so common in other parts of the Tower.

A long climb and a few twists later, they arrived at 엘라이더’s quarters. 에그웨인 checked her skirts unconsciously. She had determined during the walk that she needed to approach 엘라이더 with silence, just as she had last time. Riling her further would only lead to more restrictions. 에그웨인 would not debase herself, but neither would she go out of her way to insult 엘라이더. Let the woman think as she wished.

A servant opened the door, leading 에그웨인 in, and into the dining chamber. There, she was shocked by what she found. She had assumed she’d attend 엘라이더 alone, or maybe with Meidani. 에그웨인 hadn’t for a moment considered that the dining room would be filled with women. There were five, one from each 아자 save the Red and the Blue. And each woman was a Sitter. 유키리 was there, as was 도신, both from the clandestine hunters of the 흑색 아자. Ferane was there, though she seemed surprised to see 에그웨인; had the White not known about this dinner earlier, or had she simply not mentioned it?

Rubinde, of the 녹색 아자, sat beside Shevan of the Brown, a sister whom 에그웨인 had been wanting to meet. Shevan was one of those who supported negotiating with the rebel 에스 세다이, and 에그웨인 hoped to be able to nudge her more toward helping unify the 백색 탑 from within.

There wasn’t a Red sister at the table other than 엘라이더. Was that because the Red 의석자들 were all out of the Tower? Perhaps 엘라이더 thought the room balanced with her there, as she still thought of herself as Red, although she wasn’t supposed to.

It was a long table, crystal goblets sparkling and reflecting light from the ornate bronze standlamps, running along the walls painted a rusty red-yellow in color. Each woman wore a fine gown in the color of her 아자. The room smelled of succulent meats and steamed carrots. The women chatted. Amicable, but forced. Tense. They didn’t want to be there.

Across the room, 도신 nodded to 에그웨인, almost in respect. It was an indication of something. “I’m here because you said that this sort of thing was important,” it seemed to say. 엘라이더 sat at the head of the table, wearing a red dress with full sleeves, uncut garnets trimming them and the bodice, her face bearing a satisfied smile. Servants bustled back and forth, pouring wine and bringing food. Why had 엘라이더 called a dinner of 의석자들? Was this an attempt to heal the rifts in the 백색 탑? Had 에그웨인 misjudged her?

“Ah, good,” 엘라이더 said, noticing 에그웨인. “You’ve finally arrived. Come here, child.”

에그웨인 did so, walking through the room, the last few 의석자들 catching notice of her. Some seemed confused, others made curious, by her presence. As she walked, 에그웨인 realized something.

This one evening could easily undo all that she’d worked for.

If the 에스 세다이 here saw her subserviently waiting on 엘라이더, 에그웨인 would lose integrity in their eyes. 엘라이더 had declared that 에그웨인 was cowed—but 에그웨인 had proven otherwise. If she bent to 엘라이더’s will here, even a little, it would be seen as proof.

Light burn the woman! Why had she invited so many of the women that 에그웨인 had been working to influence? Was it simple happenstance? 에그웨인 joined the false Amyrlin at the head of the table, and a servant handed her a crystal pitcher of glistening red wine. “You are to keep my cup full,” 엘라이더 said. “Wait there, but don’t come too close. I’d rather not have to smell the soot on you from your punishments this afternoon.”

에그웨인 clenched her jaw. Smell the soot? After an hour of scrubbing? Doubtful. From the side, she could see the satisfaction in 엘라이더’s eyes as she sipped her wine. Then 엘라이더 turned to Shevan, who sat in the chair to 엘라이더’s right. The Brown was a lanky woman, with knobbed arms and an angular face, like a person made of gnarled sticks. Her eyes were thoughtful as she studied her hostess.

“Tell me, Shevan,” 엘라이더 said. “Do you still insist on those foolish talks with the rebels?”

Shevan responded. “The sisters must be given a chance to reconcile.”

“They’ve had their chance,” 엘라이더 said. “Honestly, I expected more of a Brown. You’re behaving doggedly, without a whit of understanding how the real world works. Why, even Meidani agrees with me, and she’s a Gray! You know how *they* are.”

Shevan turned away, seeming more disturbed than before. Why did 엘라이더 invite them to dinner, if only to insult them and their 아자s? As 에그웨인 watched, the Red turned her attention to Ferane, and complained to her about Rubinde, a Sitter from the Green who also resisted 엘라이더’s efforts to end the talks. As she spoke, she raised her cup to 에그웨인, tapping it. 엘라이더 had barely taken a few sips.

에그웨인 ground her teeth, filling the cup. The others had seen her do labor before—why, she’d cracked walnuts for Ferane. This wouldn’t ruin her reputation, not unless 엘라이더 forced her to abase herself somehow.

But what was the point of this dinner? 엘라이더 didn’t seem to be making any attempt to bring the 아자s together. If anything, she was prying those rifts wider, the way she was dismissing those who disagreed with her. Occasionally, she would have 에그웨인 refill her cup, but it never had room for more than a sip or two.

Slowly, 에그웨인 began to understand. This dinner wasn’t about working with the 아자s. It was about bullying the 의석자들 into doing as 엘라이더 felt they should. And 에그웨인 was simply there to be shown off! This was all about proving to the others how much power 엘라이더 had—she could take someone that others had named Amyrlin, put a 수련생 dress on her and send her to penance every day.

에그웨인 felt herself grow angry again. Why could 엘라이더 always stir her emotions? Soup bowls were removed and plates of steamed, buttered carrots were brought, a hint of cinnamon striking the air. 에그웨인 had not been given dinner, but she felt too sick to care about eating.

*No,* she thought, steeling herself. *I will not end this early, like last time. I will endure. I am stronger than 엘라이더. I’m stronger than her madness.*

The conversation continued, 엘라이더 making insulting comments to the others, sometimes with intent, sometimes with apparent unawareness. The others steered the talk away from the rebels and toward the strangely overcast skies. Eventually, Shevan mentioned a rumor about the 쇼엔찬 working with 아일 far to the south.

“The 쇼엔찬 again?” 엘라이더 said with a sigh. “You needn’t worry about them.”

“My sources say otherwise, Mother,” Shevan said stiffly. “I think we need to pay close attention to what they are doing. I have had some sisters ask this child about her experience with them, which has been extensive. You should hear the things they do to 에스 세다이.”

엘라이더 laughed a tinkling, melodic laugh. “Surely you know how the child is prone to exaggerate!” She glanced at 에그웨인. “Have you been spreading lies for your friend, the fool al’Thor? What did he tell you to say about these invaders? They are working for him, are they not?”

에그웨인 didn’t respond.

“Speak,” 엘라이더 said, gesturing with her cup. “Tell these women you have been speaking lies. Confess or I’ll have you in penance again, girl.”

The penance she would take for not speaking would be better than suffering 엘라이더’s rage at contradicting her. Silence was the path to victory.

And yet, as 에그웨인 glanced down the long mahogany table, set with bright white Sea Folk porcelain and flickering red candles, she saw five pairs of eyes studying her. She could see their questions. 에그웨인 had spoken boldly to them when alone, but would she hold to her assertions now, faced by the most powerful woman in the world? A woman who held 에그웨인’s life in her hands?

Was 에그웨인 the Amyrlin? Or was she just a girl who liked to pretend?

*Light burn you, 엘라이더,* she thought, gritting her teeth, seeing that she had been wrong. Silence wouldn’t lead to victory, not in front of these women. *You are* not *going to like how this proceeds.*

“The 쇼엔찬 are not working for 랜드,” 에그웨인 said. “And they are a severe danger to the 백색 탑. I have spread no lies. To say otherwise would be to betray the 세 가지 맹세.”

“You haven’t taken the 세 가지 맹세,” 엘라이더 said sternly, turning toward her.

“I have,” 에그웨인 said. “I’ve held no 맹세 막대, but it isn’t the Rod that makes my words true. I have spoken the words of the oaths in my heart, and to me they are more dear, for I have nothing forcing me to hold to them. And by that oath holding me, I tell you again. I am a Dreamer, and I have Dreamed that the 쇼엔찬 will attack the 백색 탑.”

엘라이더’s eyes flared for a moment, and she gripped her fork until her knuckles whitened. 에그웨인 held her eyes, and finally 엘라이더 laughed again. “Ah, stubborn as ever, I see. I shall have to tell Katerine that she was right. You’ll have penance for your exaggerations, child.”

“These women know I don’t speak lies,” 에그웨인 said calmly. “And each time you insist that I do, you lower yourself in their eyes. Even if you disbelieve my Dream, you *must* admit that the 쇼엔찬 are a threat. They leash women who can channel, using them as weapons with a kind of twisted *ter’angreal*. I have felt the collar on my neck. I still feel it, sometimes. In my dreams. My nightmares.”

The room fell still.

“You *are* a foolish child,” 엘라이더 said, obviously trying to pretend that 에그웨인 was no threat. She should have turned to look at the eyes of the others. If she had, she’d have seen the truth. “Well, you have forced my hand. You will kneel before me, child, and beg forgiveness. Right now. Otherwise, I will lock you away alone. Is that what you want? Don’t think that the beatings will stop, however. You’ll still get your daily penance, you’ll just be thrown back into your cell after each one. Now, kneel and beg forgiveness.”

The 의석자들 glanced at one another. There was no backing down now. 에그웨인 *wished* it hadn’t come to this. But it had, and 엘라이더 had demanded a fight.

It was time to give her one. “And if I do not bow before you?” 에그웨인 asked, meeting the woman’s eyes. “What then?”

“You *will* kneel, one way or another,” 엘라이더 growled, embracing the Source.

“You’ll use the Power on me?” 에그웨인 asked calmly. “Do you have to resort to that? Have you no authority without channeling?”

엘라이더 paused. “It is within my rights to discipline one who isn’t showing proper respect.”

“And so you will *make* me obey,” 에그웨인 said. “Is this what you will do to everyone in the Tower, 엘라이더? An 아자 opposes you, and it is disbanded. Someone displeases you, and you try to destroy her right to be 에스 세다이. You will have every sister bowing down before you by the end of this.”

“Nonsense!”

“Oh?” 에그웨인 asked. “And have you told them about your idea for a new oath? Sworn on the 맹세 막대 by every sister, an oath to obey the Amyrlin and support her?”

“I—”

“Deny it,” 에그웨인 said. “Deny that you made the statement. Will the Oaths let you?”

엘라이더 froze. If she were Black, she *could* deny it, 맹세 막대 or not. But either way, Meidani could substantiate what 에그웨인 had said.

“It was idle talk,” 엘라이더 said. “Just speculation, thoughts spoken out loud.”

“There is often truth in speculation,” 에그웨인 said. “You locked the 용의 환생 himself in a box; you just threatened to do the same to me, in front of all of these witnesses. People call him a tyrant, but you are the one destroying our laws and ruling by fear.”

엘라이더’s eyes opened wide, her anger visible. She seemed . . . shocked. As if she couldn’t understand how she’d gone from disciplining an unruly 수련생 into debating an equal. 에그웨인 saw the woman begin to weave a thread of Air. That had to be stopped. A gag of Air would end this debate.

“Go ahead,” 에그웨인 said calmly. “Use the Power to silence me. As Amyrlin, shouldn’t you be able to *talk* an opponent into obedience, rather than resorting to force?”

Out of the corner of her eye, 에그웨인 saw diminutive 유키리, of the Gray, nod at that comment.

엘라이더’s eyes flared in anger as she dropped the thread of Air. “I don’t need to rebut a mere 수련생,” 엘라이더 snapped. “The Amyrlin doesn’t explain herself to one such as you.”

“ ‘The Amyrlin understands the most complex of creeds and debates,’ ” 에그웨인 said, quoting from memory. “ ‘Yet in the end, she is the servant of all, even the lowest of laborers.’ ” That had been said by Balladare Arandaille, the first Amyrlin to be raised from the 갈색 아자. She’d used the words in her last writings before her death; those writings had been an explanation of her reign and what she had done during the Kavarthen wars. Arandaille had felt that once a crisis was passed, it was the moral duty of an Amyrlin to explain herself to the common people.

Sitting beside 엘라이더, Shevan nodded appreciatively. The quote was somewhat obscure; 에그웨인 blessed 시우안’s quiet training in the wisdom of the former Amyrlins. Much of what she’d said had come from the secret histories, but there had been a number of nuggets from women such as Balladare as well.

“What is this nonsense you’re sputtering?” 엘라이더 spat.

“What did you intend to do with 랜드 al’Thor once you captured him?” 에그웨인 said, ignoring the comment.

“I don’t—”

“You’re not answering *me*,” 에그웨인 said, nodding to the table of women, “but *them*. Have you explained yourself, 엘라이더? What were your plans? Or will you dodge this question just as you have the others I’ve asked?”

엘라이더’s face was turning red, but she calmed herself with some effort. “I would have kept him secure, and well shielded, here in the Tower until it was time for the Last Battle. That would have prevented him from causing the suffering and chaos he’s created in many nations. It was worth the risk of angering him.”

“ ‘As the plow breaks the earth shall he break the lives of men, and all that was shall be consumed in the fire of his eyes,’ ” 에그웨인 said. “ ‘The trumpets of war shall sound at his footsteps, the ravens feed at his voice, and he shall wear a crown of swords.’ ”

엘라이더 frowned, taken aback.

“*The 카라에손 순환*, 엘라이더,” 에그웨인 said. “When you had 랜드 locked away to be kept ‘secure,’ had he yet taken 일리안? Had he yet worn what he was to name the Crown of Swords?”

“Well, no.”

“And how did you expect him to fulfill the prophecies if he was hidden away in the 백색 탑?” 에그웨인 said. “How was he to cause war, as the prophecies say he must? How was he to break the nations and bind them to him? How could he ‘slay his people with the sword of peace’ or ‘bind the nine moons to serve him’ if he was locked away? Do the prophecies say that he will be ‘unfettered’? Do they not speak of the ‘chaos of his passing’? How can anything pass at all if he is kept in chains?”

“I. . . .”

“Your logic is astounding, 엘라이더,” 에그웨인 said coldly. At that, Ferane smiled slyly; she was probably thinking yet again that 에그웨인 would fit well in the 백색 아자.

“Bah,” 엘라이더 said, “you ask meaningless questions. The prophecies would *have* to have been fulfilled. There was no other way.”

“So you’re saying that your attempt to bind him was destined to fail.”

“No, not at all,” 엘라이더 said, red-faced again. “We shouldn’t be bothering with this—it’s not for you to decide upon. No, we should be talking about your rebels, and what *they’ve* done to the 백색 탑!”

A good turn of the conversation, an attempt to put 에그웨인 on the defensive. 엘라이더 wasn’t completely incompetent. Just arrogant.

“I see *them* trying to heal the rift between us,” 에그웨인 said. “We cannot change what has happened. We can’t change what you did to 시우안, even if those with me did discover a method of 치유 her stilling. We can only move forward and try our best to smooth the scars. What are you doing, 엘라이더? Refusing talks, trying to bully the 의석자들 into withdrawing? Insulting 아자s that are not your own?”

도신, of the Yellow, gave a quiet murmur of agreement. That drew 엘라이더’s eyes, and she fell silent for a moment, as if realizing that she had lost control of the debate. “Enough of this.”

“Coward,” 에그웨인 said.

엘라이더’s eyes flared wide. “How *dare* you!”

“I dare the truth, 엘라이더,” 에그웨인 said quietly. “You are a coward and a tyrant. I’d name you Darkfriend as well, but I suspect that the 어둠의 존재 would perhaps be embarrassed to associate with you.”

엘라이더 screeched, weaving in a flash of Power, slamming 에그웨인 back against the wall, toppling the pitcher of wine from her hands. It shattered on a patch of wooden floor beside the rug, throwing a spray of bloodlike liquid across the table and half of its occupants, staining the white tablecloth with a smear of red.

“You name *me* Darkfriend?” 엘라이더 screamed. “You are the Darkfriend. You and those rebels outside, who seek to distract me from doing what must be done.”

A blast of woven Air slammed 에그웨인 against the wall again, and she dropped to the ground, hitting shards of the broken pitcher that sliced open her arms. A dozen switches beat her, ripping her clothing. Blood seeped from her arms, and it began to splash into the air, smirching the wall as 엘라이더 beat her.

“엘라이더, stop it!” Rubinde said, standing, green dress swishing. “Are you mad?”

엘라이더 turned, panting. “Do *not* tempt me, Green!”

The switches continuing to beat 에그웨인. She bore it silently. With effort, she stood up. She could feel her face and arms swelling already. But she maintained a calm gaze at 엘라이더.

“엘라이더!” Ferane yelled, standing. “You violate Tower law! You *cannot* use the Power to punish an initiate!”

“I *am* Tower law!” 엘라이더 raved. She pointed at the sisters. “You mock me. I know you do it. Behind my back. You show me deference when you see me, but I know what you say, what you whisper. You ungrateful fools! After what I’ve done for you! Do you think I’ll suffer you forever? Take this one as an example!”

She spun, pointing at 에그웨인, then stumbled back in shock to find 에그웨인 calmly watching her. 엘라이더 gasped softly, raising a hand to her breast as the switches beat. They could all see the weaves, and they could all see that 에그웨인 did not scream, although her mouth was not gagged with Air. Her arms dripped blood, her body was beaten before them, and yet she found no reason to scream. Instead, she quietly blessed the 아일 현명한 이들 for their wisdom.

“And what,” 에그웨인 said evenly, “am I to be an example of, 엘라이더?”

Her battle from within the Tower was at an end, one way or another.

“My Lord,” Grady said, rubbing his weathered face, “I don’t think you understand.”

“Then explain it to me,” 페린 said. He stood on a hillside, looking down over the huge gathering of refugees and soldiers. Mismatched tents of many different designs—tan, single-peaked 아일 structures; colorful large 케렌인 ones; two-tipped tents of basic design—sprang up as the people prepared for the night.

The Shaido 아일, as hoped, had not given chase. They had let 페린’s army withdraw, though his scouts said that they had now moved in to investigate the city. Either way, it meant 페린 had time. Time to rest, time to limp away, time—he’d hoped—to use gateways to transport away most of these refugees.

Light, but it was a big group. Thousands upon thousands of people, a nightmare to coordinate and administer to. His last few days had been filled with an endless stream of complaints, objections, judgments and papers. Where did Balwer find so much paper? It seemed to satisfy many of the people who came to 페린. Judgments and the settlement of disputes seemed so much more official to them when a piece of paper outlined them. Balwer said 페린 would need a seal.

The work had been distracting, which was good. But 페린 knew he couldn’t push aside his problems for long. 랜드 pulled him northward. 페린 *had* to march for the Last Battle. Nothing else mattered.

And yet, that very single-mindedness in him—ignoring everything but his objective—had been the source of much trouble during his hunt for 파일. He had to find a balance, somehow. He needed to decide for himself if he wanted to lead these people. He needed to make peace with the wolf inside himself, the beast that raged when he went into battle.

But before he could do any of that, he needed to get the refugees home. That was proving a problem. “You’ve had time to rest now, Grady,” 페린 said.

“The fatigue is only one part of it, my Lord,” Grady said. “Though, honestly, I *still* feel as if I could sleep a week’s time.”

He *did* look tired. Grady was a stalwart man, with the face of a farmer and the temperament of one, too. 페린 would trust this man to do his duty before most lords he’d known. But Grady could be pushed only so far. What did it do to a man, to have to channel so much? Grady had bags beneath his eyes, and his face was pale despite his tanned skin. Though he was still a young man, he’d started to go gray.

*Light, but I used this man too hard,* 페린 thought. *Him and Neald both*. That had been another effect of 페린’s single-mindedness, as he was beginning to see. What he’d done to Aram, how he’d allowed those around him to go without leadership. . . . *I have to fix this. I have to find a way to deal with it all.*

If he didn’t, he might not *get* to the Last Battle.

“Here’s the thing, my Lord.” Grady rubbed his chin again, surveying the camp. The various contingents—Mayeners, Alliandre’s guard, the 두 강 men, the 아일, the refugees from various cities—all camped separately, in their own rings. “There are some hundred thousand people who need to get home. The ones that will leave, anyway. Many say they feel safer here, with you.”

“They can give over wanting that,” 페린 said. “They belong with their families.”

“And the ones whose families are in 쇼엔찬 lands?” Grady shrugged. “Before the invaders came, many of these people would be happy to return. But now . . . Well, they keep talking about staying where there’s food and protection.”

“We can still send the ones who want to go,” 페린 said. “We’ll travel lighter without them.”

Grady shook his head. “That’s the thing, my Lord. Your man, Balwer, he gave us a count. I can make a gateway big enough for about two men to walk through at once. If you figure them taking one second to go through . . . Well, it would take hours and hours to send them all. I don’t know the number, but he claimed it would be days’ worth of work. And he said that his estimates were probably too optimistic. My Lord, I could barely keep a gateway open an hour, with how tired I am.”

페린 gritted his teeth. He’d have to get those numbers from Balwer himself, but he had a sinking feeling that Balwer would be right.

“We’ll keep marching, then,” 페린 said. “Moving north. Each day, we’ll have you and Neald make gateways and return some of the people to their homes. But don’t tire yourselves.”

Grady nodded, eyes hollow from fatigue. Perhaps it would be best to wait a few more days before starting the process. 페린 nodded a dismissal to the 헌신자, and Grady jogged back down into camp. 페린 remained on the hillside, inspecting the various sections of the camp as the people prepared for the evening meal. The wagons sat at the center of the camp, laden with food that—he feared—would run out before he could reach 안도르. Or should he go around to 케렌? That was where he had last seen 랜드, though his visions of the man made it seem he wasn’t in either country. He doubted the Queen of 안도르 would welcome him with open arms, after the rumors about him and that blasted Red Eagle banner.

페린 left that problem alone for the moment. The camp seemed to be settling in. Each ring of tents sent representatives to the central food depot to claim their evening rations. Each group was in charge of its own meals; 페린 just oversaw the distribution of materials. He made out the quartermaster—a 케렌인 named Bavin Rockshaw—standing on the back of a wagon, dealing with each representative in turn.

Satisfied with his inspection, 페린 walked down into the camp, passing through the 케렌인 tents on the way to his own tents, which were with the 두 강 men.

He took his enhanced senses for granted, now. They had come along with the yellowing of his eyes. Most people around him didn’t seem to notice those anymore, but he was starkly reminded of the contrast when he met anyone new. Many of the 케렌인 refugees, for instance, paused in their labors setting up tents. They watched him as he passed, whispering, “Goldeneyes.”

He didn’t much care for the name. Aybara was the name of his family, and he bore it proudly. He was one of the few who could pass it on. 트롤록s had seen to that.

He shot a glance at a nearby group of the refugees, and they hastily turned back to pounding in tent stakes. As they did, 페린 passed a couple of 두 강 men—Tod al’Caar and Jori Congar. They saw him and saluted, fists to hearts. To them, 페린 Goldeneyes wasn’t a person to fear, but one to respect, although they did still whisper about that night he’d spent in Berelain’s tent. 페린 wished he could escape the shadow of *that* event. The men were still enthusiastic and energized by their defeat of the Shaido, but it hadn’t been too long ago that 페린 had felt he wasn’t welcome among them.

Still, for the moment, these two seemed to have set aside that displeasure. Instead, they saluted. Had they forgotten that 페린 had grown up with them? What of the times when Jori had made sport of 페린’s slow tongue, or the times when he’d stopped by the forge to brag about which girls he’d managed to steal a kiss from?

페린 just nodded back. No use in digging up the past, not when their allegiance to “페린 Goldeneyes” had helped rescue 파일. Though, as he left them, his too-keen ears caught the two of them chatting about the battle, just a few days past, and their part of it. One of them still smelled like blood; he hadn’t cleaned his boots. He probably didn’t even notice the bloodstained mud.

Sometimes, 페린 wondered if his senses weren’t actually any better than anyone else’s. He took the time to notice things that others ignored. How could they miss that scent of blood? And the crisp air of the mountains to the north? It smelled of home, though they were many leagues from the 두 강. If other men took the time to close their eyes and pay attention, would they be able to smell what he did? If they opened those eyes and looked closer at the world around them, would men call their eyes “keen” as they did 페린’s?

No. That was just fancy. His senses *were* better; his kinship with the wolves had changed him. He hadn’t thought of that kinship in a while—he’d been too focused on 파일. But he’d stopped feeling so self-conscious about his eyes. They were part of him. No use grumbling about them.

And yet, that rage he felt when he fought . . . that loss of control. It worried him, more and more. The first time he’d felt it had been that night, so long ago, fighting 백의단. For a time, 페린 hadn’t known if he was a wolf or a man.

And now—during one of his recent visits to the wolf dream—he’d tried to kill 호퍼. In the wolf dream, death was final. 페린 had almost lost himself that day. Thinking of it awakened old fears, fears he’d shoved aside. Fears relating to a man, behaving like a wolf, locked in a cage.

He continued down the pathway to his tent, making some decisions. He’d pursued 파일 with determination, avoiding the wolf dream as he’d avoided all of his responsibilities. He’d claimed that nothing else had mattered. But he knew that the truth was much more difficult. He’d focused on 파일 because he loved her so much, but—in addition—he’d done so because it had been convenient. Her rescue had been an excuse to avoid things like his discomfort with leadership and the blurred truce between himself and the wolf inside of himself.

He had rescued 파일, but so many things were still wrong. The answers might lie in his dreams.

It was time to return.

셰리암 raised an eyebrow. “엘라이더 has 이동.”

셰리암 nodded. “We found out when Ashmanaille was sent to collect from 캔도르.” Tributes were one of the main sources of income for 에그웨인’s 에스 세다이. “The chief clerk was quite livid,” Ashmanaille said in her no-nonsense voice. “ ‘I already paid your money this month,’ he told me. ‘I gave it to a woman who came not one day gone. The woman bore a letter from the Amyrlin herself, sealed properly, which told me to give the money *only* to a member of the 적색 아자.’ ”

“This doesn’t say for certain 엘라이더 has 이동,” Romanda noted from inside the tent. “The Red sister could have gotten to 캔도르 by other means.”

Ashmanaille shook her head. “They saw a gateway made. The chief clerk discovered an accounting error and sent a scribe out after 엘라이더’s delegation to give them a few extra coins. The man described what he saw *perfectly*. The horses were riding through a black hole in the air. It stunned him so deeply that he called for the guard—but by then 엘라이더’s people were already gone. I interrogated him myself.”

“I dislike trusting the word of one man,” said Moria, sitting near the front of the group.

“The chief clerk described in detail the woman who took the money from him,” Ashmanaille said. “I am confident that it was Nesita. Perhaps we could discover if she is in the Tower? That would give us further proof.”

Others raised objections, but 시우안 ceased to listen closely. Perhaps this was a very clever ruse intended to distract them, but they couldn’t take that chance. Light! Was she the only one with a head on her shoulders?

She grabbed the nearest 수련생, a mousy girl who was probably older than she looked—she’d have to be, since she looked no older than nine. “I need a courier,” 시우안 informed her. “Fetch one of the messengers Lord Bryne left at the camp for running news to him. *Quickly*.”

The girl yelped, dashing away.

“What was that about?” 셰리암 asked.

“Saving our lives,” 시우안 said, glaring at the crowding 수련생s. “All right!” she growled. “Enough gawking! If your classes are postponed because of this fiasco, then find some work to do. Any 수련생 still standing on this walkway in ten seconds will find herself doing penance until she can’t count straight!”

That initiated a mass exodus of white, the families of women bustling away with hurried steps. In moments, only the small group of 허락받은 자 remained, along with 셰리암 and 시우안. The 허락받은 자 cringed when 시우안 glanced at them, but she said nothing. Part of the privilege of being an 허락받은 자 was increased freedom. Besides, as long as 시우안 could move without bumping someone, she was satisfied.

“Why wasn’t this meeting Sealed to the Flame in the first place?” she asked 셰리암.

“I don’t know,” 셰리암 admitted, glancing into the large tent. “It’s daunting news, if it’s true.”

“This was bound to occur eventually,” 시우안 said, though she was nowhere near that calm on the inside. “News of 이동 has to be spreading.”

*What happened?* she thought. *They didn’t break 에그웨인, did they? Light send it wasn’t her or 리안 who was forced to give up this secret. 베오닌. It had to be her. Burn it all!*

She shook her head. “Light send that we can keep 이동 secret from the 쇼엔찬. When they *do* assault the 백색 탑, we’ll want at least that advantage.”

셰리암 eyed her, skepticism showing. Most of the sisters didn’t believe 에그웨인’s Dreaming of the attack. Fools—they wanted to catch the fish, but didn’t want to gut it. You didn’t raise a woman to Amyrlin, then treat her warnings lightly.

시우안 waited impatiently, tapping her foot, listening to the conversation inside the tent. Just as she was beginning to wonder if she’d need to send another 수련생, one of Bryne’s couriers trotted up to the tent on horseback. The ill-tempered brute he was riding was midnight black with white just above the hooves, and it snorted at 시우안 as the rider pulled up short, wearing a neat uniform and close-cropped brown hair. Did he *have* to bring that creature with him?

“에스 세다이?” the man asked, bowing to her from horseback. “You have a message for Lord Bryne?”

“Yes,” 시우안 said. “And you’ll see it delivered with *all haste*. You understand me? All of our lives could depend on it.”

The soldier nodded sharply.

“Tell Lord Bryne . . .” 시우안 began. “Tell him to watch his flanks. Our enemy has been taught the method we used to get here.”

“It shall be done.”

“Repeat it back to me,” 시우안 said.

“Of course, 에스 세다이,” the slender man said, bowing again. “Just so you know, I have been a messenger in the general’s command for over a decade. My memory—”

“Stop,” 시우안 interrupted. “I don’t care how *long* you’ve been doing this. I don’t care how good your memory is. I don’t care if, by some twist of fate, you’ve been asked to run this *very same message* a thousand times before. You *will* repeat it back to me.”

“Um, yes, 에스 세다이. I’m to tell the Lord General to watch his flanks. Our enemy has been taught the method we used to get here.”

“Good. Go.”

The man nodded.

“Now!”

He reared that awful horse and galloped out of the camp, cloak flapping behind him.

“What was *that* about?” 셰리암 asked, glancing away from the proceedings inside the Hall.

“Making certain we don’t wake up with 엘라이더’s army surrounding us,” 시우안 said. “I’ll bet I’m the only one who thought to warn our general that the enemy may have just undone our biggest tactical advantage. So much for a siege.”

셰리암 frowned, as if she hadn’t considered that. She wouldn’t be alone. Oh, some would think of Bryne, and would be planning to send word to the general eventually. But for many, the catastrophe here *wasn’t* the fact that 엘라이더 could now move her armies to flank them, or that now Bryne’s siege was useless. The catastrophe would be more personal for them: the knowledge they’d worked to keep secret had fallen into the hands of others. 이동 was *theirs*, and now 엘라이더 had it! Very 에스 세다이. Indignation first, implication second.

Or perhaps 시우안 was just feeling bitter. Someone inside the tent finally thought to call for the meeting to be Sealed to the Flame, and so 시우안 withdrew, stepping off the walkway and onto the hard-packed earth. Novices scuttled this way and that, heads bowed to avoid her eyes, though they were quick to curtsy. *I haven’t been doing a very good job of acting weak today,* 시우안 thought with a grimace.

The 백색 탑 was crumbling. The 아자s weakened one another with petty infighting. Even here, in 에그웨인’s camp, more time was spent politicking than preparing for the coming storm.

And 시우안 was partially responsible for those failures.
엘라이더 and her 아자 certainly bore the lionfish’s share of the blame. But would the Tower have split in the first place if 시우안 had fostered cooperation between the 아자s? 엘라이더 hadn’t had *that* long to work. Every rift that appeared in the Tower could likely be traced back to tiny cracks during 시우안’s tenure as Amyrlin. If she’d been more of a mediator among the factions of the 백색 탑, could she have pounded strength into the bones of these women? Could she have kept them from turning on one another like razorfish in a blood frenzy?

The 용의 환생 was important. But he was only one figure in the weaving of these final days. It was too easy to forget that, too easy to watch the dramatic figure of legend and forget everyone else.

She sighed, picking up her laundry and—out of habit—checking to make certain everything was there. As she did so, a figure in white approached her from one of the branching pathways. “시우안 Sedai?”

시우안 looked up, frowning. The 수련생 before her was one of the strangest in the camp. Nearly seventy years old, Sharina had the weathered, creased face of a grandmother. She kept her silver hair up in a bun, and while she walked without a stoop, there was a certain distinct *weight* to her. She had seen so much, done so much, passed so many years. And unlike an 에스 세다이, Sharina had *lived* all of those years. Working, raising a family, even burying children.

She was strong in the power. Remarkably so; she would wear the shawl for certain, and as soon as she did, she’d be far above 시우안. For now, though, Sharina curtsied deeply. She gave an almost perfect show of deference. Of all of the 수련생s, she was known to complain the least, make the least trouble, and study the most assiduously. As a 수련생, she understood things that most 에스 세다이 had never learned—or had forgotten the moment they took the shawl. How to be humble when necessary, how to take a punishment, how to know when you needed to learn rather than pretend you already knew. *If only we had a few score more of her,* 시우안 thought, *and a few score less 엘라이더s and Romandas.*

“Yes, child?” 시우안 asked. “What is it?”

“I saw you picking up that wash, 시우안 Sedai,” Sharina said. “And I thought that perhaps I should carry it for you.”

시우안 hesitated. “I wouldn’t want you to tire yourself.”

Sharina raised an eyebrow in a very un-수련생-like expression. “These old arms carried loads twice that heavy back and forth from the river just last year, 시우안 Sedai, juggling three grandchildren all the way. I think I’ll be all right.” There was something in her eyes, a hint that her offer was not all it seemed to be. This one was adept at more than just 치유 weaves, it appeared.

Curious, 시우안 let the aged woman take the basket. They began to walk down the pathway toward the 수련생s’ tents.

“It’s curious,” Sharina said, “that such a large disturbance could be caused by such a seemingly simple revelation, wouldn’t you say, 시우안 Sedai?”

“엘라이더’s discovery of 이동 *is* an important revelation.”

“And yet nowhere near as important as the ones rumored to have come during the meeting a few months back, when that man who can channel visited. Odd that this should create such a scene.”

시우안 shook her head. “The thinking of crowds is often odd at first consideration, Sharina. Everyone is still talking about that Asha’man visit, and they’re thirsty for more. So they react with excitement at the chance to hear something else. In that way, the great revelations can come in secret, but then cause lesser ones to be received in an explosion of anxiety.”

“One could put that observation to good use, I should think.” Sharina nodded to a group of 수련생s as they passed. “If one wanted to cause worry, that is.”

“What are you saying?” 시우안 asked, eyes narrowing.

“Ashmanaille reported first to Lelaine Sedai,” Sharina said softly. “I’ve heard that Lelaine was the one who let the news slip. She spoke it out loud in the hearing of a family of 수련생s while calling for the Hall to meet. She also deflected several early calls for the meeting to be Sealed to the Flame.”

“Ah,” 시우안 said. “So *that’s* why!”

“I relate only hearsay, of course,” Sharina explained, pausing in the shade of a scraggly blackwood tree. “It is probably just foolishness. Why, an 에스 세다이 of Lelaine’s stature would *know* that if she let information slip in the hearing of 수련생s, it would soon pass to all willing ears.”

“And in the Tower, every ear is willing.”

“Exactly, 시우안 Sedai,” Sharina said, smiling.

Lelaine had wanted to create a menagerie of a meeting—she’d wanted 수련생s listening in, and every sister in the camp joining in the discussion. Why? And why was Sharina confiding her very un-수련생-like opinions?

The answer was obvious. The more threatened the women in the camp felt—the more danger they saw from 엘라이더—the easier it would be for a firm hand to seize control. Though the sisters were indignant now over the mere loss of a closely guarded secret, they would soon realize the danger that 시우안 had already seen. Soon there would be fear. Worry. Anxiety. The siege would never work, not now that the 에스 세다이 inside it could Travel wherever and whenever they wished. Bryne’s army at the bridges had become useless.

Unless 시우안 missed her guess, Lelaine would be making certain that everyone else noticed the implications, too.

“She wants us scared,” 시우안 said. “She wants a crisis.” It was clever. 시우안 should have seen this coming. The fact that she hadn’t—and the fact that she’d gotten no wind of Lelaine’s plans—also whispered an important fact. The woman might not trust 시우안 as deeply as she seemed to. Blast!

She focused on Sharina. The gray-haired woman stood patiently, waiting as 시우안 worked through what she’d revealed.

“Why did you tell me this?” 시우안 asked. “For all you know, I’m Lelaine’s lackey.”

Sharina raised her eyebrows. “Please, 시우안 Sedai. These eyes aren’t blind, and they see a woman working very hard to keep the Amyrlin’s enemies occupied.”

“Fine,” 시우안 said. “But you are still exposing yourself for very little reward.”

“Little reward?” Sharina asked. “Excuse me, 시우안 Sedai, but what do you suppose my fate will be if the Amyrlin doesn’t return? No matter what she says now, we can sense Lelaine Sedai’s true opinions.”

시우안 hesitated. Though Lelaine now played the part of 에그웨인’s pious advocate, not too long ago she had been as displeased as everyone else over the too-old 수련생s. Few liked it when traditions changed.

Now that the new 수련생s had been entered into the 수련생 book, it would be very difficult to put them out of the Tower. But that didn’t mean the 에스 세다이 would continue to let older women in. Beyond that, there was a good chance that Lelaine—or whoever ended up with the 아미를린 석좌—would find a way to delay or disrupt the progression of the women who had been accepted against tradition. That would certainly include Sharina.

“I will let the Amyrlin know of your actions here,” 시우안 said. “You will be rewarded.”

“My reward will be 에그웨인 Sedai’s return, 시우안 Sedai. Pray it be swift. She entangled our fate with her own the moment she took us in. After what I’ve seen, and what I’ve felt, I have no intention of stopping my training.” The woman hefted the basket. “I assume you wish these washed and returned to you?”

“Yes. Thank you.”

“I am a 수련생, 시우안 Sedai. It is my duty and my pleasure.” The elderly woman bowed in respect and continued on down the path, walking with a step younger than her years.

시우안 watched her go, then stopped another 수련생. Another messenger to Bryne. Just in case. *Hurry up, girl,* 시우안 thought to 에그웨인, glancing toward the spire of the 백색 탑. *Sharina isn’t the only one whose fate is entangled with yours. You’ve got us all wound up in that net of yours.*

**C*HAPTER** **19**

Gambits

Chaos. The entire world was chaos.

투온 stood on the balcony of her audience hall in the palace of Ebou Dar, hands clasped behind her back. In the palace grounds—flagstones washed white, like so many surfaces in the city—a group of 알타라n armsmen in gold and black practiced formations beneath the watchful eyes of a pair of her own officers. Beyond them, the city proper rose, white domes banded with colors spreading alongside tall, white spires.

Order. Here in Ebou Dar, there was order, even in the fields of tents and wagons outside the city. 쇼엔찬 soldiers patrolled and kept the peace; there were plans to clean out the Rahad. Just because one was poor was not a reason—or an excuse—to live without law.

But this city was just a tiny, tiny pocket of order in a world of tempest. 쇼엔찬 itself was broken by civil war, now that the 여제 had died. The 코렌 had come, but recapturing these lands of 아투르 호크윙 progressed slowly, stalled by the 용의 환생 in the east and 도마니 armies in the north. She still waited to hear news of Lieutenant-General Turan, but the signs were not good. Galgan maintained that they might be surprised at the outcome, but 투온 had seen a black dove the hour she was informed of Turan’s predicament. The omen had been clear. He would not return alive.

Chaos. She glanced to the side, where faithful 카레데 stood in his thick armor, colored blood-red and a deep green, nearly black. He was a tall man, square face nearly as solid as the armor he wore. He had fully two dozen 죽음감시대s with him this day—the day after 투온’s return to Ebou Dar—along with six 오지어 Gardeners, all standing along the walls. They lined the sides of the high-ceilinged, white-pillared room. 카레데 sensed the chaos, and did not intend to let her be taken again. Chaos was the most deadly when you made assumptions about what it could and couldn’t infect. Here in Ebou Dar, it manifested in the form of a faction intent on taking 투온’s own life.

She had been dodging assassinations since she could walk, and she had survived them all. She anticipated them. In a way, she thrived because of them. How were you to know that you were powerful unless assassins were sent to kill you?

Suroth’s betrayal, however . . . Chaos, indeed, when the leader of the Forerunners herself turned traitor. Bringing the world back into order was going to be very, very difficult. Perhaps impossible.

투온 straightened her back. She had not thought to become 여제 for many years yet. But she would do her duty.

She turned away from the balcony and walked back into the audience chamber to face the crowd awaiting her. Like the others of the Blood, she wore ashes on her cheeks to mourn the loss of the 여제. 투온 had little affection for her mother, but affection was not needed for an empress. She provided order and stability. 투온 had only begun to understand the importance of these things as the weight had settled on her shoulders.

The chamber was wide and rectangular, lit with candelabras between the pillars and the radiant glow of sunlight through the wide balcony behind. 투온 had ordered the room’s rugs removed, preferring the bright white tiles. The ceiling bore a painted mural of fishers at sea, with gulls in the clear air, and the walls were a soft blue. A group of ten *da’covale* knelt before the candelabras to 투온’s right. They wore filmy costumes, waiting for a command. Suroth was not among them. The 죽음감시대 saw to her, at least until her hair grew out.

As soon as 투온 entered the room, all of the commoners bowed on knees with foreheads to the ground. Those of the Blood knelt, bowing their heads.

Across from the *da’covale*, on the other side of the hall, 란elle and Melitene knelt in dresses emblazoned with silver lightning bolts in red panels on their skirts. Their leashed *다만* knelt facedown. 투온’s kidnapping had been unbearable to several of the *다만*; they had taken to inconsolable weeping during her absence.

Her audience chair was relatively simple. A wooden seat with black velvet on the arms and back. She sat down, wearing a pleated gown of the deepest sea blue, a white cape fluttering behind her. As soon as she did, the people in the room rose from their positions of adulation—all save the *da’covale*, who remained kneeling. 셀루시아 stood and stepped up beside the chair, her golden hair in a braid down her right side, the left side of her head shaven. She did not wear the ashes, since she was not of the Blood, but the white band on her arm indicated that she—like the entire Empire—mourned the loss of the 여제.

Yuril, 투온’s secretary and secretly her Hand, stepped up to the other side of the chair. The 죽음감시대s moved in subtly around her, dark armor glittering faintly in the sunlight. They had been particularly protective of her lately. She didn’t blame them, recent events considered.

*Here I am,* 투온 thought, *surrounded by my might,* 다만 *on one side and 죽음감시대 on the other. And yet I feel no safer than I did with 매트림*. How odd, that she should have felt safe with him.

Directly in front of her, lit by indirect sunlight from the open balcony behind, was a collection of the Blood, Captain-General Galgan highest of them. He wore armor this day, the breastplate painted a deep blue, nearly dark enough to be black. His powdery white hair ran in a crest with the sides of his head shaven, and was plaited to his shoulders, for he was of the High Blood. With him were two members of the low Blood—Banner-General Najirah and Banner-General Yamada—and several commoner officers. They waited patiently, carefully not meeting 투온’s eyes.

A gathering of other members of the Blood stood several steps behind, to witness her acts. Wiry Faverde Nothish and long-faced Amenar Shumada led them. They were both important—important enough to be dangerous. Suroth wouldn’t be the only one who saw opportunity in these times. If 투온 were to fall, practically anyone could become 여제. Or Emperor.

The war in 쇼엔찬 would not end quickly; but when it did, the victor would undoubtedly raise him- or herself to the Crystal Throne as well. And then there would be two leaders of the 쇼엔찬 제국, divided by an ocean, united in desire to conquer one another. Neither could allow the other to live.

*Order,* 투온 thought, tapping the black wood of her armrest with a blue-lacquered fingernail. *Order must emanate from me. I will bring the calm airs to those beset by storms.*

“셀루시아 is my Truthspeaker,” she announced to the room. “Let it be published among the Blood.”

The statement was expected. 셀루시아 bowed her head in acceptance, though she had no desire for any appointment other than to serve and protect 투온. She would not welcome this position. But she was also honest and straightforward; she would make an excellent Truthspeaker.

At least this time, 투온 could be certain that her Truthspeaker wasn’t one of the 버림받은 자들.

Did she believe Falendre’s story, then? It stretched plausibility; it sounded like one of 매트림’s fanciful tales of imaginary creatures that lurked in the dark. And yet, the other *sul’dam* and *다만* had corroborated Falendre’s tale.

Some facts, at least, seemed straightforward. Anath had been working with Suroth. Suroth—after some persuasion—had admitted that she had met with one of the 버림받은 자들. Or, at least, she thought she had. She hadn’t known that the 버림받은 자들 was the same as Anath, but she seemed to find the revelation believable.

Whether or not she really was 버림받은 자들, Anath had met with the 용의 환생, imitating 투온. And had then tried to kill him. *Order,* 투온 thought, keeping her face still. *I represent order*.

투온 gestured rapidly to 셀루시아, who was still 투온’s 목소리—and her shadow—even with the added responsibility of Truthspeaker. When ordering those far beneath herself, 투온 would first pass the words to 셀루시아, who would speak them.

“You are required to send him in,” 셀루시아 said to a *da’covale* beside the throne. He bowed himself to the ground, touching head to the floor, then hurried to the other end of the large room and opened the door.

Beslan, King of 알타라 and High Seat of House Mitsobar, was a slender youth with black eyes and hair. He had the olive skin common to the 알타라n people, but he had taken to wearing clothing like that favored by the Blood. Loose trousers of yellow and a high-collared coat that came down only to the middle of his chest, a yellow shirt underneath. The Blood had left a clear passage down the middle of the room, and Beslan walked through it, eyes lowered. Upon reaching the supplication space before the throne, he went down on his knees, then bowed low. The perfect image of a loyal subject, except for the thin golden crown on his head.

투온 gestured to 셀루시아.

“You are bidden to rise,” 셀루시아 said.

Beslan rose, though he kept his gaze averted. He was a fine actor.

“The Daughter of the Nine Moons expresses her condolences to you for your loss,” 셀루시아 said to him.

“I give the same to her for her loss,” he said. “My grief is but a candle to the great fire felt by the 쇼엔찬 people.”

He was *too* servile. He was a king; he was not required to bow himself so far. He was the equal of many of the Blood.

She could almost have believed he was just being submissive before the woman who would soon become 여제. But she knew too much of his temperament, through both spies and hearsay.

“The Daughter of the Nine Moons wishes to know the reason you have ceased holding court,” 셀루시아 said, watching 투온’s hands move. “She finds it distressing that your people cannot have audience with their king. Your mother’s death was as tragic as it was shocking, but your kingdom needs you.”

Beslan bowed. “Please have her know that I did not think it appropriate to elevate myself above her. I am uncertain how to act. I meant no insult.”

“Are you certain that is the true reason?” 셀루시아 목소리d. “It is not, perhaps, because you are planning a rebellion against us, and do not have time for your other duties?”

Beslan looked up sharply, eyes wide. “Your Majesty, I—”

“You need not speak any further lies, child of Tylin,” 투온 said directly to him, causing gasps of surprise from the assembled Blood. “I know of the things you have said to General Habiger and your friend, Lord Malalin. I know of your quiet meetings in the basement of The Three Stars. I know of it all, King Beslan.”

The room fell silent, Beslan bowed his head for a moment. Then, surprisingly, he rose to his feet and stared her directly in the eyes. She wouldn’t have thought the soft-spoken youth had it in him. “I will not allow my people to—”

“I would still my tongue if I were you,” 투온 interrupted. “You stand on sand as it is.”

Beslan hesitated. She could see the question in his eyes. Wasn’t she going to execute him? *If I intended to kill you,* she thought, *you would be dead already, and you would never have seen the knife*.

“쇼엔찬 is in upheaval,” 투온 said, regarding him. He appeared shocked at the words. “Oh, did you think I would ignore it, Beslan? I am not content to stare at the stars while my empire collapses around me. The truth must be acknowledged. My mother is dead. There is no empress.

“However, the forces of the 코렌 are *more* than sufficient to maintain our positions here on this side of the ocean, 알타라 included.” She leaned forward, trying to project a sense of *control*, of *firmness*. Her mother had been able to do so at all times. 투온 did not have her mother’s height, but she would need that aura. Others had to feel safer, more secure, simply by entering her presence.

“In times such as these,” 투온 continued, “threats of rebellion cannot be tolerated. Many will see opportunity in the Empire’s weakness, and their divisive squabbling—if left unchecked—would prove the end of us all. Therefore, I must be firm. Very firm. With those who defy me.”

“Then why,” Beslan said, “am I still alive?”

“You started planning your rebellion *before* events in the Empire were made known.”

He frowned, dumbfounded.

“You began your rebellion when Suroth led here,” 투온 said, “and when your mother was still queen. Much has changed since then, Beslan. Very much. In times like these, there is potential for great accomplishment.”

“You must know I have no thirst for power,” Beslan said. “The freedom of my people is all I desire.”

“I do know it,” 투온 said, clasping her hands before her, lacquered nails curling, elbows on the armrests of her chair. “And that is the other reason you are still alive. You rebel not out of lust for station, but out of sheer ignorance. You are misguided, and that means you can change, should you receive the proper knowledge.”

He looked at her, confused. *Lower your eyes, fool. Don’t make me have you strapped for insolence!* As if he had heard her thoughts, he averted his eyes, then lowered them. Yes, she had judged correctly regarding this one.
