A Force of Light

민 sat quietly, watching 랜드 dress. His motions were tense and careful, like the steps of a performer walking the high rope at a menagerie. He did up the left cuff on his crisp white shirt with slow, deliberate fingers. The right cuff was already done up; his servants saw to that.

It was approaching evening outside. Not quite dark yet, though the shutters were closed in preparation. 랜드 reached for a gold and black coat, sliding on one sleeve, then the other. Then did the buttons one after another. He had no trouble with these; he was growing practiced at working with only one hand. Button after button. First, second, third, fourth. . . .

민 felt like screaming.

“Do you want to talk about it?” she asked.

랜드 did not turn from the mirror. “About what?”

“The 쇼엔찬.”

“There will be no peace,” he said, straightening his coat collar. “I have failed.” His tone was emotionless, yet somehow taut.

“It’s all right to be frustrated, 랜드.”

“Frustration is pointless,” he said. “Anger is pointless. Neither emotion will change facts, and the fact is that I have no more time to waste on the 쇼엔찬. We will have to risk an attack from behind by riding to the Last Battle without stability in 아라드 도만. It is not ideal, but it is what must happen.”

The air shimmered above 랜드, and a mountain appeared there. Viewings were so common around 랜드 that 민 usually forced herself to ignore them unless they were new—though she did spend time some days trying to pick them all out and sort through them. This one was new, and it caught her attention. The towering mountain was blasted out on one side, making a jagged hole down the slope. 용산? It was cloaked in dark shadows, as if shaded by clouds high above. That was odd; whenever she’d seen the mountain, it had reached higher than the clouds themselves.

용산 in shadows. It would be important to 랜드 in the future. Was that a tiny prick of light shining from the heavens down onto the point of the mountain?

The viewing vanished. Though 민 knew what some of them meant, this one baffled her. She sighed, leaning back in the red-cushioned chair. Her books lay scattered on the floor; she’d been dedicating more and more time to her studies, partly because she felt 랜드’s sense of urgency, and partly because she didn’t know what else to do. She liked to think that she was capable of taking care of herself. And she’d begun to think of herself as a last defense for 랜드.

민 had discovered just how useful she was as a “line of defense.” She’d been about as useful as a child! In fact, she’d been a hindrance, a tool for 세미르하제 to use against him. She’d been indignant when 랜드 had suggested sending her away, giving him a tongue-lashing for even suggesting it. Send her away! To keep her safe? That was foolishness! She could take care of herself.

So she had thought. Now she saw that he’d been right.

That made her sick. So she studied and tried to stay out of his way. He’d changed on that day, as if something bright had turned off inside of him. A lamp flickering out, its oil gone, leaving only the casing. He looked at her differently, now. When those eyes of his studied her, did they see only a liability?

She shivered, trying to shove that thought from her mind.

랜드 put on his boots, then did up their buckles.

He stood, reaching for the sword which leaned against his clothing chest. The black scabbard, with its lacquered red and gold dragon, sparkled in the light. Such a strange weapon those scholars had found beneath the submerged statue. The sword felt so *old*. Was 랜드 wearing it today as a symbol of something? A sign, perhaps, that he was riding to battle?

“You’re going after *her*, aren’t you?” 민 found herself asking. “그랜달.”

“I have to fix what problems I can,” 랜드 said, pulling the ancient sword from the sheath and checking the blade. There was no heron mark, but the fine steel blade glistened in the lamplight, showing the undulating lines of its folded metal. It had been Power-forged, he claimed. He seemed to know things about it he did not share.

랜드 snapped the blade into the black scabbard, looking at her. “Fix the problems you can, don’t fret over the ones you cannot. It was something Tam once told me. 아라드 도만 will have to survive against the 쇼엔찬 on its own. The last thing I can do for the people here is remove one of the 버림받은 자들 from their soil.”

“She might be waiting for you, 랜드,” 민 said. “Did it occur to you that the boy 니나브 found was a plant? Intended to be discovered, to lead you into a trap?”

He hesitated, then shook his head. “He was genuine, 민. 모그헤디엔 might have considered a trick like that, but not 그랜달. She’d be too worried about being traced. We have to move quickly, before word reaches her that she has been compromised. I must strike now.”

민 stood.

“Are you coming, then?” 랜드 asked, looking surprised.

She flushed. *What if things go as poorly with 그랜달 as they did with 세미르하제? What if I become a tool against him again?*

“Yes,” she said, just to prove to herself that she wasn’t giving up. “Of course I’m coming. Don’t think you can leave me behind!”

“I wouldn’t dream of it,” he said flatly. “Come.”

She’d expected more of an argument.

From the night stand he picked up the statuette of a man holding aloft a globe. He turned the *ter’angreal* in his hand, inspecting it, then looked up at 민, as if in challenge. She said nothing.

He tucked the statuette into the oversized pocket of his coat, then strode from the room, ancient, Power-forged sword belted to his waist.

민 hurried after 랜드. He glanced at the pair of Maidens guarding the door. “I go to battle,” he said to them. “Bring no more than twenty.”

The Maidens exchanged a brief moment of handtalk; then one loped ahead and the other tailed 랜드 as he marched down the hallway. 민 hurried up beside him, heart thumping, her boots loud on the floorboards. He had rushed off like this to fight 버림받은 자들 before, but usually he took more time to plan. He’d maneuvered 사마엘 for months before striking at 일리안. He’d had barely a single day to decide what do with 그랜달!

민 checked her knives, making certain they were secure in her sleeves, but it was just a nervous habit. 랜드 reached the end of the hallway, then strode down the stairs, his face still calm, his step quick but not hurried. Yet he seemed like a thunderstorm, contained and wrapped up, somehow bound and channeled toward a single goal. How she wished he’d just explode and lose his temper, the way he used to! He’d exasperated her then, but he’d never frightened her. Not as he did now, with those icy eyes she couldn’t read, that aura of danger. Since the incident with 세미르하제, he spoke of doing “whatever he had to” regardless of cost, and she knew that he must seethe at having failed to convince the 쇼엔찬 to ally with him. What would that combination of failure and determination lead him to do?

At the bottom of the wide staircase, 랜드 spoke to a servant. “Fetch for me 니나브 Sedai and Lord Ramshalan. Bring them to the sitting room.”

Lord Ramshalan? The overstuffed man from Lady Chadmar’s former circle? “랜드,” 민 said quietly, reaching the bottom of the stairs, “what are you planning?”

He said nothing. He strode through the white marble entryway, entering the sitting room, which was decorated in deep reds to contrast with the white floor. He did not sit, but remained standing with his arms behind his back, studying the map of 아라드 도만 he’d ordered placed on the wall. The aged map hung where a fine oil painting once had, and seemed completely out of place in the room.

On the map, there was a black ink mark at the edge of a small lake to the southeast. 랜드 had placed it there the morning after Kerb died. It marked Natrin’s Barrow.

“It was a fort, once,” 랜드 said absently.

“The city where 그랜달 is hiding?” 민 said, walking up beside him.

He shook his head. “It’s not a city. I’ve sent scouts. It’s just a solitary structure, built long ago to watch the Mountains of Mist and guard against incursion through the passes by Manetheren. It hasn’t been used for military purposes since the 트롤록 전쟁; there’s hardly need to worry about invasion from 두 강 people who don’t even remember the name Manetheren.”

민 nodded. “Though, 아라드 도만 did get invaded by a shepherd from the 두 강.”

Once that would have made him smile. She kept forgetting that he didn’t do that anymore.

“A few centuries back,” 랜드 said, eyes narrowed in thought, “the king of 아라드 도만 seized Natrin’s Barrow back in the name of the throne. For some time before, it had been occupied by a minor noble family from Toman Head who had been trying to set up their own new kingdom. That happens on Almoth Plain occasionally. The 도마니 king liked the location, and used the fortress as a palace instead.

“He spent a great deal of time there, so much, in fact, that several of his merchant enemies gained too much power in Bandar Eban. The King fell, but his successors also used the fortress, and it became a popular retreat for the Crown when the King needed relaxation. The practice dwindled during the last hundred years or so, until it was granted to a distant cousin of the King about fifty years back. Their family has used it ever since. Among the general 도마니 populace, Natrin’s Barrow has been largely forgotten.”

“Except by 알살람?” 민 asked.

랜드 shook his head. “No. I doubt he knew of it at all. I learned this history from the royal archivist, who had to search for hours to locate the name of the family using the place. There has been no contact with them for months, though they used to visit towns on occasion. The few farmsteaders in the area say that someone new seems to be living in the palace, though nobody knows where the former owner went. They seem surprised that they’ve never thought about how odd that is.”

He eyed her. “This is exactly the sort of location 그랜달 would choose as her center of power. It’s a jewel—a forgotten fortress of beauty and power, ancient and regal. Close enough to Bandar Eban for her to have a hand in ruling 아라드 도만, but far enough away to be defensible and secluded. I made a mistake in my searches for her—I assumed she’d want a beautiful manor with gardens and grounds. I should have realized; it isn’t just beauty that she collects, but prestige. A magnificent fortress for kings fits her just as much as an elegant manor house. Particularly since this one is more palace than fort now.”

Footsteps in the entryway behind drew 민’s attention, and a few seconds later a servant ushered in 니나브 and the foppish Ramshalan, with his pointed beard and thin mustache. Today he had tiny bells at the end of the beard and wore a black velvet beauty mark on his cheek, also in the shape of a bell. He wore a loose silk costume of green and blue, the sleeves drooping, ruffled shirt poking out beneath. 민 didn’t care what fashion dictated, the man looked ridiculous. Like a disheveled peacock.

“My Lord called for me?” Ramshalan said, bowing extravagantly toward 랜드.

랜드 didn’t turn away from the map. “I have a puzzle for you, Ramshalan,” he said. “I want to know what you think.”

“Please, don’t hesitate, my Lord!”

“Then tell me this: How do I outthink an enemy I know is smarter than I am?”

“My Lord.” Ramshalan bowed a second time, as if worried that 랜드 hadn’t noticed the first one. “Surely you seek to trick me! There is nobody more intelligent than yourself.”

“I wish that were true,” 랜드 said softly. “I face some of the most crafty people who have ever lived. My current foe understands the minds of others in a way that I cannot hope to match. So how do I defeat her? She will vanish the moment I threaten her, running to one of a dozen other refuges she is sure to have set up. She won’t fight me head-on, yet if I destroy her fortress in a surprise attack, I risk letting her slip away and never knowing if I’ve finished her.”

“A problem indeed, my Lord,” Ramshalan said. He looked confused.

랜드 nodded, as if to himself. “I have to peer into her eyes, see into her soul, and know that it’s *her* that I face and not some decoy. I have to do that without frightening her into running. How? *How* can I kill a foe who is more clever than myself, a foe who is impossible to surprise, yet who is also unwilling to confront me?”

Ramshalan looked overwhelmed by those demands. “I. . . . My Lord, if your foe is that clever, then perhaps your best course of action is to request the aid of someone *more* clever?”

랜드 turned to him. “An excellent suggestion, Ramshalan. Perhaps I’ve already done just that.”

The man swelled. *He thinks that’s why 랜드 summoned him!* 민 realized. She had to hide her smile with a turn of the head and a raised hand.

“If *you* had an enemy such as this, Ramshalan, what would you do?” 랜드 asked. “I grow impatient. Give me an answer.”

“I’d make an alliance, my Lord,” Ramshalan said without pausing for another second. “Anyone that powerful would make a better friend than foe, I say.”

*Idiot,* 민 thought. *If your enemy is that crafty and ruthless, an alliance will only end with an assassin’s dagger in your back.*

“Another excellent suggestion,” 랜드 said softly. “But I am still intrigued by the first comment you made. You said I need allies who are smarter than I am, and that is true. It is time for you to be off, then.”

“My Lord?” Ramshalan said.

“You are to be my emissary,” 랜드 said, waving his hand. A gateway suddenly split the air on the far side of the room, shearing through the fine rug at the floor. “Too many of the 도마니 bloodborn are hiding, scattered through the country. I would have them as my allies, but it would be a drain on my time to seek each one in person. Fortunately, I have you to go on my behalf.”

Ramshalan looked excited about the prospect. Through the gateway, 민 could see towering pines, and the air on the other side was cold and crisp. 민 turned and glanced at 니나브—dressed in blue and white again. The 에스 세다이 watched the exchange with calculating eyes, and 민 could read her own emotions in 니나브’s expression. What was 랜드’s game?

“Beyond that gateway,” 랜드 said, “you will find a hill leading down to an ancient palace which is inhabited by a minor 도마니 merchant family. It is the first of many places I shall send you. Go in my name and seek those who rule the keep. See if they are willing to support me, or if they even know about me. Offer them rewards for allegiance; since you have proven yourself clever, I will let you determine the terms. I haven’t the mind for those sorts of negotiations myself.”

“Yes, my Lord!” the man said, swelling further, though he did eye the gateway with concern, distrustful—like most people—of the 하나의 힘, particularly when wielded by a man. If it were opportune, this man would switch loyalties as quickly as he had when Lady Chadmar had fallen. What was 랜드 thinking, sending a popinjay like this to meet with 그랜달?

“Go,” 랜드 said.

Ramshalan took a few hesitant steps toward the gateway. “Er, my Lord Dragon, could I perhaps have something in the way of an escort?”

“No need to frighten or alarm the people there,” 랜드 said without turning from the map. Cold air continued to blow through the gateway. “Go quickly and return, Ramshalan. I will leave the gateway open until you are back. My patience is not limitless, and there are many I could turn to for this mission.”

“I. . . .” The man seemed to calculate the risks. “Of course, Lord Dragon.” He took a deep breath and walked through the portal, his steps uncomfortable, like those of a house cat venturing out into a puddle of water. 민 found herself feeling sorry for the man.

Fallen needles crackled as Ramshalan moved off into the forest. A breeze hissed through the trees; it was an odd sound to hear while standing in the comfort of the mansion. 랜드 left the gateway open, still staring at his map.

“All right, 랜드,” 니나브 demanded after a few minutes, her arms folded. “What game is this?”

“How would *you* beat her, 니나브?” 랜드 asked. “She won’t be goaded into fighting me, like 라빈 or 사마엘 were. She won’t be easily trapped either. 그랜달 understands people better than anyone. Twisted she may be, but she *is* crafty, and should not be underestimated. Torhs Margin made that mistake, I recall, and you know his fate.”

민 frowned. “Who?” she asked, looking at 니나브. The 에스 세다이 shrugged.

랜드 glanced at them. “I believe in history he was known as Tohrs the Broken.”

Again, 민 shook her head. 니나브 joined her. Neither was deeply versed in history, true, but 랜드 acted as if they should know this name. 랜드’s face hardened, and he blushed just faintly, turning away from them. “The question remains,” he said, voice soft but tense. “How would you fight her, 니나브?”

“I don’t care to play your games, 랜드 al’Thor,” 니나브 replied with a huff. “You’ve obviously already decided what you intend to do. Why ask me?”

“Because what I am about to do should frighten me,” he said. “It doesn’t.”

민 shivered. 랜드 nodded to the Maidens standing in the doorway. Moving lightly, they crossed the room, leaped through the gateway, and spread through the pine forest, quickly vanishing from sight. All twenty together made less noise than Ramshalan had.

민 waited. On the other side of the gateway, a distant sun was hidden from sight, giving a late-afternoon light to the shadowed forest floor. After a few moments, white-haired Nerilea stepped into view and nodded to 랜드. All clear.

“Come,” 랜드 said, and walked to the gateway. 민 followed, though 니나브—breaking into a trot—beat her to the gateway.

They stepped out onto a carpet of brown pine needles, dirtied from a long slumber beneath the vanished winter snows. Branches nudged one another in the breeze, and the mountain air was more chilly than the breeze had indicated. 민 wished for a cloak, but there wasn’t time to go fetch one. 랜드 strode directly through the forest, 니나브 trotting up to him and speaking in a low voice.

니나브 wouldn’t get anything useful out of 랜드, not when he was in this kind of mood. They would just have to see what he revealed. 민 caught sight of some 아일 in the woods, but only brief glimpses when they obviously weren’t taking care to hide. They certainly had taken well to life in the wetlands. How did a people raised in the 황무지 know so instinctively how to hide in a forest?

Up ahead, the trees broke. 민 hastened to join 랜드 and 니나브, who had stopped at the top of a gently sloping ridge. Here, they could see over the forest, and the trees continued down below like a sea of green and brown. The pines parted at the shores of a small mountain lake, caught in a triangular depression of the land.

Atop a ridge of its own, high above the water, was an impressive white stone structure. Rectangular and tall, it was built in the form of several towers stacked atop one another, each one slightly thinner than the one beneath. That gave the palace an elegant shape—fortified, yet palatial. “It’s beautiful,” she said breathlessly.

“It was built during a different time,” 랜드 said. “A time when people still thought that the majesty of a structure lent it strength.”

The palace was distant, but not so distant that 민 couldn’t make out the figures of men walking the battlements on guard, halberds at their shoulders, breastplates reflecting the late sunlight. A late party of hunters rode in through the gates, a fine buck deer lashed to the packhorse, and a group of workers chopped at a fallen tree nearby, perhaps for firewood. A pair of serving women in white carried poles, bucket at each end, up from the lake, and lights were winking on in windows the length of the structure. It was a living, working estate bundled up in a single massive building.

“Do you think Ramshalan found his way?” 니나브 said, arms folded, obviously trying not to look impressed.

“Even a fool like him could not miss that,” 랜드 said, eyes narrowing. He still carried the statuette in his pocket. 민 wished he had left the thing behind. It made her uncomfortable, the way he fingered it. Caressed it.

“So you sent Ramshalan to die,” 니나브 said. “What will that accomplish?”

“She won’t kill him,” 랜드 said.

“How can you be sure of that?”

“It isn’t her way,” 랜드 said. “Not when she can use him against me.”

“You don’t expect her to believe that story you told him,” 민 said. “About sending him out to test the allegiance of the 도마니 lords?”

랜드 slowly shook his head. “No. I hope for her to believe something of that tale, but I do not expect it. I meant what I said about her, 민—she’s more crafty than I am. And I fear that she knows me far better than I know her. She will compel Ramshalan and pull from him that entire conversation we had. From there, she will find a way to use that conversation against me.”

“How?” 민 asked.

“I don’t know. I wish I did. She’ll think of something clever, then infect Ramshalan with a very subtle 강제 that I won’t be able to anticipate. I’ll be left with the choice to keep him nearby and see what he does, or to send him away. But of course, she will think of that as well, and whatever I do will set in motion her other plans.”

“You make it sound as if you can’t win,” 니나브 said, frowning. She didn’t seem to notice the chill at all. In fact, neither did 랜드. Whatever that “trick” about ignoring cold and heat was, 민 had never been able to figure it out. They claimed it had nothing to do with the power, but if that were so, why were 랜드 and the 에스 세다이 the only ones who could manage it? The 아일 didn’t seem to be bothered by the cold either, but they didn’t count. They never seemed bothered by regular human concerns, though they could be very touchy about the most random and insignificant things.

“We can’t win, you say?” 랜드 asked. “Is that what we’re trying to do? Win?”

니나브 raised an eyebrow. “Do you not answer questions anymore?”

랜드 turned, looking at 니나브. Standing on the other side of him, 민 couldn’t see what was in his face, but she could see 니나브 grow pale. It was her own fault. Couldn’t she sense how on edge 랜드 was? Perhaps 민’s chill didn’t just come from the cold. She moved up close to him, but he didn’t put his arm around her as he might once have. When he finally turned away from 니나브, the 에스 세다이 slumped slightly, as if she had been dangling, held up by his gaze.

랜드 did not speak for some time, and so they waited quietly on the mountain ridge as the distant sun made its way toward the horizon. Shadows lengthened, fingers stretching away from the sun. Down below, by the fortress walls, a group of grooms began walking some horses to give them exercise. More lights had been lit in the fortress windows. How many people did 그랜달 have in there? Scores, if not hundreds.

A crashing sound in the brush suddenly drew 민’s attention; it was accompanied by curses. She jumped as the noise cut off quite abruptly.

A small group of 아일 approached a few moments later, leading a disheveled Ramshalan, his fine clothing stuck with needles and scratched from branches. He dusted himself off, then took a step toward 랜드.

The Maidens held him back. He glanced at them, cocking his head. “My Lord Dragon?”

“Is he infected?” 랜드 asked of 니나브.

“By what?” she asked.

“그랜달’s touch.”

니나브 walked over to Ramshalan and looked at him for a moment. She hissed and said, “Yes. 랜드, he’s under a heavy 강제. There are a lot of weaves here. Not as bad as the chandler’s apprentice, or maybe just more subtle.”

“I say,” Ramshalan said, “my Lord Dragon, what is going on? The lady of the castle down there was quite friendly—she is an ally, my Lord. You have nothing to fear from her! Very refined, I must say.”
“Is that so?” 랜드 asked quietly. It was growing dark, sun setting behind the distant mountains. Besides the dim evening light, the only illumination came from the still-open gateway behind them. It shone with lamplight, an inviting portal back to warmth, away from this place of shadow and coldness.

랜드’s voice sounded so hard. Worse than 민 had ever heard it before.

“랜드,” she said, touching his arm. “Let’s go back.”

“I have something I must do,” he said, not looking at her.

“Think about it some more,” 민 said. “At least take some advice. We can ask Cadsuane, or—”

“Cadsuane held me in a box, 민,” he said very softly. His face was clasped in shadow, but as he turned toward her, his eyes reflected the light from the open gateway. Orange and red. There was an edge of anger to his tone. *I shouldn’t have mentioned Cadsuane,* she realized. The woman’s name was one of the few things that could still get emotion out of him.

“A box, 민,” 랜드 whispered. “Though Cadsuane’s box had walls that were invisible, it was as binding as any that ever held me. Her tongue was far more painful a rod than any that was taken to my skin. I see that now.”

랜드 pulled away from 민’s touch.

“What is the purpose of all this?” 니나브 demanded. “You sent this man to suffer a 강제, *knowing* what it would do to him? I won’t watch another man squirm and die because of this! Whatever she has compelled him to do, I won’t remove it! It will be your own fault if it brings your death.”

“My Lord?” Ramshalan asked. The growing terror in his voice put 민 on edge.

The sun set; 랜드 was now just a silhouette. The fortress was only a black profile with lanterns lighting the holes in its walls. 랜드 stepped up to the lip of the ridge, removing the access key from his pocket. It started to glow just faintly, a red light coming from its very heart. 니나브 inhaled sharply.

“Neither of you were there when *칼란도르* failed me,” he said into the night. “It happened twice. Once I tried to use it to raise the dead, but I got only a puppeted body. Once I tried to use it to destroy the 쇼엔찬, but I caused as much death among my own armies as I caused among theirs.

“Cadsuane told me that the second failure came from a flaw in *칼란도르* itself. It cannot be controlled by a lone man, you see. It only works if he’s in a box. *칼란도르* is a carefully enticing leash, intended to make me surrender willingly.”

The access key’s globe burst alight with a more brilliant color, seeming crystalline. The light within was scarlet, the core brilliant and bright. As if someone had dropped a glowing rock into a pool of blood.

“I see a different answer to my problems,” 랜드 said, voice still almost a whisper. “Both times *칼란도르* failed me, I was being reckless with my emotion. I allowed temper to drive me. I can’t kill in anger, 민. I have to keep that anger inside; I must channel it as I channel the 하나의 힘. Each death must be deliberate. Intentional.”

민 couldn’t speak. Couldn’t phrase her fears, couldn’t find the words to make him stop. His eyes remained in the darkness, somehow, despite the liquid light he held before him. That light hurled shadows away from his figure, as if he was the point of a silent explosion. 민 turned to 니나브; the 에스 세다이 watched with wide eyes, mouth slightly open. She couldn’t find words either.

민 turned back to 랜드. When he’d been close to killing her with his own hand, she hadn’t feared him. But then, she’d known that it wasn’t 랜드 hurting her, but 세미르하제.

But this 랜드—hand aflame, eyes so intent yet so dispassionate—terrified her.

“I’ve done it before,” he whispered. “I once said that I didn’t kill women, but it was a lie. I murdered a woman long before I faced 세미르하제. Her name was Liah. I killed her in Shadar Logoth. I struck her down, and I called it mercy.”

He turned to the fortress palace below.

“Forgive me,” he said, but it didn’t seem directed at 민, “for calling this mercy as well.”

Something impossibly bright formed in the air before him, and 민 cried out, backing away. The air itself seemed to warp, as if pulling away from 랜드 in fear. Dust blew from the ground in a circle around him, and the trees groaned, lit by the brilliant white light, the pine needles rattling like a hundred thousand insects scrambling over one another. 민 could no longer make out 랜드, only a blazing, brilliant *force* of light. Pure power, gathered, making the hairs on her arms rise with the force of its nebulous energy. In that moment, she felt as if she could understand what the 하나의 힘 was. It was there, before her, made incarnate in the man 랜드 al’Thor.

And then, with a sound like a sigh, he released it. A column of pure whiteness exploded from him and burned across the silent night sky, illuminating the trees below it in a wave. It moved as quick as a snap of the fingers, striking the wall of the distant fortress. The stones came alight, as if they were breathing in the force of the energy. The entire fortress glowed, transforming into living light, an amazing, spectacular palace of unadulterated energy. It was beautiful.

And then it was gone. Burned from the landscape—and the Pattern—as if it had never been there. The entire fortress, hundreds of feet of stone and everyone who had lived in it.

Something hit 민, something like a shocking wave in the air. It wasn’t a physical blast, and it didn’t make her stumble, but it twisted her insides about. The forest around them—still lit by the glowing access key in 랜드’s hands—seemed to warp and shake. It was as if the world itself were groaning in agony.

It snapped back, but 민 could still feel that tension. In that instant, it seemed as if the very substance of world had been near to breaking.

“What have you done?” 니나브 whispered.

랜드 didn’t reply. 민 could see his face again, now that the enormous column of balefire had vanished, leaving behind only the glowing access key. He was in ecstasy, mouth agape, and he held the access key aloft before himself as if in victory. Or in reverence.

Then he gritted his teeth, eyes opening wide, lips parted as if he were under great pressure. The light flashed once, then immediately vanished. All became dark. 민 blinked in the sudden darkness, trying to get her eyes to adjust. The powerful image of 랜드 seemed burned into her vision. Had he really done what she thought he had? Had he burned away an entire fortress with balefire?

All those people. Men returning from the hunt . . . women carrying water . . . soldiers on the walls . . . the grooms outside . . .

They were *gone*. Burned from the Pattern. Killed. Dead forever. The horror of it made 민 stumble back, and she pressed her back against a tree to keep herself upright.

So many lives, ended in an instant. Dead. Destroyed. By 랜드.

A light appeared from 니나브, and 민 turned, seeing the 에스 세다이 illuminated by the warm, soft glow of a globe above her hand. Her eyes seemed almost afire with a light of their own. “You are out of control, 랜드 al’Thor,” she declared.

“I do what must be done,” he said, speaking now from the shadows. He sounded exhausted. “Test him, 니나브.”

“What?”

“The fool,” 랜드 said. “Is her 강제 still there? Is 그랜달’s touch gone?”

“I hate what you just did, 랜드,” 니나브 snarled. “No. ‘Hate’ isn’t strong enough. I *loathe* what you’ve done. What has happened to you?”

“Test him!” 랜드 whispered, voice dangerous. “Before condemning me, let us first determine if my sins have achieved anything beyond my own damnation.”

니나브 breathed in deeply, then glanced at Ramshalan, who was still held in the grip of several 아일 Maidens. 니나브 reached out and touched his forehead, concentrating. “It’s gone,” she said. “Erased.”

“Then she is dead,” 랜드 said from the darkness.

*Light!* 민 thought, realizing what he’d done. *He didn’t use Ramshalan as a courier, or as bait. He used the man as a way of proving to himself that 그랜달 was dead.* 마화 burned someone out of the Pattern completely, making it so that their most recent actions never occurred. Ramshalan would remember visiting 그랜달, but her 강제 no longer existed. In a way, she’d been killed *before* Ramshalan had visited her.

민 felt at her neck, where the bruises of 랜드’s hand on her neck hadn’t yet faded.

“I don’t understand,” Ramshalan said, his voice nearly a squeak.

“How do you fight someone smarter than yourself?” 랜드 whispered. “The answer is simple. You make her think that you are sitting down across the table from her, ready to play her game. Then you punch her in the face as hard as you can. You have served me well, Ramshalan. I will forgive you for boasting to Lords Vivian and Callswell that you could manipulate me however you wished.”

Ramshalan slumped in shock, and the Maidens let him fall to his knees. “My Lord!” he said. “I had too much wine that night, and—”

“Hush,” 랜드 said. “As I said, you have served me well this day. I will not execute you. You will find a village two days’ walk to the south.”

With that, 랜드 turned; to 민’s eyes, he was just a shadow rustling in the forest. He walked to the gateway and stepped through. 민 hurried to follow him, and 니나브 did likewise. The Maidens came last, leaving Ramshalan kneeling stupefied in the forest. When the last Maiden was through the gateway, the portal slid closed, cutting off the sounds of Ramshalan whimpering in the dark.

“What you have done is an abomination, 랜드 al’Thor,” 니나브 said as soon as the gateway was closed. “There looked to have been dozens, maybe hundreds, of people living in that palace!”

“Each one made into an idiot by 그랜달’s 강제,” 랜드 replied. “She never lets anyone close to her without destroying their mind first. The boy she sent to work the jail barely knew a fraction of the torture most of her pets receive. She leaves them without ability to think or act—all they can do is kneel and adore her, perhaps run errands at her command. I did them a favor.”

“A favor?” 니나브 asked. “랜드, you used balefire! They were burned out of existence!”

“As I said,” 랜드 replied softly. “A favor. Sometimes, I wish the same blessing for myself. Good night, 니나브. Sleep as well you can, for our time in 아라드 도만 is at an end.”

민 watched him go, wishing to sprint after him, but holding herself back. Once he was gone from the room, 니나브 slumped into one of the room’s maroon chairs, sighing and leaning her head against her hand.

민 felt like doing the same. Until that moment, she hadn’t realized just how drained she was. Being around 랜드 lately did that to her, even when he wasn’t engaged in activities as terrible as the ones this night.

“I wish 모이라인 were here,” 니나브 muttered softly, then froze, as if surprised to have heard herself say that.

“We have to do something, 니나브,” 민 said, looking at the 에스 세다이.

니나브 nodded absently. “Maybe.”

“What do you mean by that?”

“Well, what if he’s right?” 니나브 asked. “Wool-headed fool though he is, what if he really *does* have to be like this to win? The old 랜드 could never have destroyed an entire fortress full of people to kill one of the 버림받은 자들.”

“Of course he couldn’t have,” 민 said. “He still *cared* about killing then! 니나브, all those lives . . .”

“And how many people would still be alive now if he’d been this ruthless from the start?” 니나브 asked, looking away. “If he’d been capable of sending his followers into danger as he did Ramshalan? If he’d been able to strike without worrying about whom he would have to kill? If he’d ordered his troops into 그랜달’s fortress, her followers would have resisted fanatically, and they would have ended up dead anyway. And she would have escaped.

“This might be what he has to be. 최후의 전투 is nearly upon us, 민. *최후의 전투!* Can we dare send a man to fight the 어둠의 존재 who won’t sacrifice for what needs to be done?”

민 shook her head. “Dare we send him as he is, with that look in his eyes? 니나브, he’s stopped caring. Nothing matters to him anymore but defeating the 어둠의 존재.”

“Isn’t that what we want him to do?”

“I. . . .” She stopped. “Winning won’t be winning at all if 랜드 becomes something as bad as the 버림받은 자들 . . . We—”

“I understand,” 니나브 said suddenly. “Light burn me, but I do, and you’re right. I just don’t like the answers those conclusions are giving me.”

“What conclusions?”

니나브 sighed. “That Cadsuane was right,” she said. Nearly under her breath, she added, “Insufferable woman.” She stood up. “Come on. We need to find her and discover what her plans are.”

민 stood, joining 니나브. “You’re certain she *has* plans? 랜드 was harsh with her. Maybe she’s just staying with us to watch him flounder and fail without her.”

“She has plans,” 니나브 said. “If there’s one thing we can count on with that woman, it’s that she’s scheming. We just have to convince her to let us in on it.”

“And if she won’t?” 민 asked.

“She will,” 니나브 said, looking at the place where 랜드’s gateway had split the rug. “Once we tell her about tonight, she will. I dislike the woman, and I suspect she returns the emotion, but neither of us can handle 랜드 alone.” She pursed her lips. “I worry we won’t be able to handle him together. Let’s go.”

민 followed. “Handle” 랜드? That was another problem. 니나브 and Cadsuane were both so concerned with *handling* that they failed to see that it might be best to *help* him instead. 니나브 cared for 랜드, but she saw him as a problem to be fixed, rather than a man in need.

And so 민 accompanied the 에스 세다이 out of the mansion. They walked into the dark courtyard—니나브 making a globe of light—and hurried around the back, past the stable and toward the gatekeeper’s cottage. They passed Alivia on the way; the former *다만* looked disappointed. Likely, she’d been turned away by Cadsuane and the others again—Alivia spent a great deal of time trying to get the 에스 세다이 to train her in new weaves.

They finally reached the gatekeeper’s cottage—at least, the gatekeeper’s cottage was what it *had* been until Cadsuane prevailed upon him to move out. It was a single-story, thatch-roofed structure of painted yellow wood. Light shone out between the shutters on the windows.

니나브 stepped up to the front and knocked on the sturdy oak door; it was answered shortly by Merise. “Yes, child?” the Green asked, as if intentionally trying to goad 니나브.

“I have to speak with Cadsuane,” 니나브 growled.

“Cadsuane *Sedai*, she has no business with you right now,” Merise said, moving to close the cottage door. “Return tomorrow, and perhaps she will see you.”

“랜드 al’Thor just burned an entire palace full of people from existence with balefire,” 니나브 said, loud enough to be heard by those inside the cottage. “I was with him.”

Merise froze.

“Let her in,” Cadsuane’s voice said from inside. Reluctantly, Merise pulled open the door. Inside, 민 saw Cadsuane sitting on some cushions on the floor with Amys, Bair, Melaine and Sorilea. The front room—the main room—of the cottage was decorated with a simple brown rug on the floor, mostly obscured by the seated women. A gray stone fireplace burned with a calm flame at the back, the wood nearly consumed, the fire low. A stool sat in the corner, with a pot of tea on it.

니나브 barely gave the 현명한 이들 a glance. She pushed her way into the cottage, and 민 followed more hesitantly.

“Tell us of this event, child,” Sorilea said. “We felt the world warping from here, but did not know what had caused it. We assumed it to be the 어둠의 존재’s work.”

“I’ll tell you,” 니나브 said, then took a deep breath, “but I want to be a part of your plans.”

“We shall see,” Cadsuane said. “Relate your experience.”

민 took a seat on a wooden stool at the side of the room as 니나브 gave her account of Natrin’s Barrow. The 현명한 이들 listened, tight-lipped. Cadsuane just nodded occasionally. Merise, face full of horror, refilled cups of tea from the pot on the stool—by the smell it was Tremalking black—then set it to hang by the fire. 니나브 finished, still standing.

*Oh, 랜드,* 민 thought. *This must be tearing you apart inside.* But she could feel him through the bond; his emotions seemed very cold.

“You were wise to come to us with this, child,” Sorilea said to 니나브. “You may withdraw.”

니나브’s eyes opened wide with anger. “But—”

“Sorilea,” Cadsuane said calmly, cutting 니나브 off. “This child could be of use to our plans. She is still close to the al’Thor boy; he trusted her enough to take her with him this evening.”

Sorilea glanced toward the other 현명한 이들. Aged Bair and sun-haired Melaine both nodded. Amys seemed thoughtful, but did not object.

“Perhaps,” Sorilea said. “But can she be obedient?”

“Well?” Cadsuane asked of 니나브. They all seemed to be ignoring 민. “Can you?”

니나브’s eyes were still wide with anger. *Light,* 민 thought. *니나브?* Obey *Cadsuane and the others? She’s going to explode at them!*

니나브 tugged on her braid with a white-knuckled grip. “Yes, Cadsuane Sedai,” she said through clenched teeth. “I can.”

The 현명한 이들 seemed surprised to hear her speak the words, but Cadsuane nodded again, as if she’d expected that response. Who could expect 니나브 to be so . . . well, reasonable?

“Sit down, child,” Cadsuane said with a wave of the hand. “Let’s see if you *can* follow orders. You might be the only one of the current crop who is salvageable.” That made Merise flush.

“No, Cadsuane,” Amys said. “Not the only one. 에그웨인 has much honor.”

The other two 현명한 이들 nodded.

“What is the plan?” 니나브 said.

“Your part in it is—” Cadsuane began.

“Wait,” 니나브 said. “My part? I want to hear the whole thing.”

“You’ll hear when we’re ready to tell you,” Cadsuane said curtly. “And don’t make me regret my decision to speak in your behalf.”

니나브 forced her mouth shut, eyes aflame. But she did not snap at them.

“Your part,” Cadsuane continued, “is to find 페린 Aybara.”

“What good will that do?” 니나브 asked, then added, “Cadsuane Sedai.”

“That is our business,” Cadsuane said. “He has been traveling in the south recently, but we can’t discover exactly where. The al’Thor boy might know where he is. Find out for us, and perhaps I’ll explain the point.”

니나브 nodded reluctantly, and the others turned to a discussion of how much strain from balefire the Pattern could take before unraveling completely. 니나브 listened in silence, obviously trying to glean more about Cadsuane’s plan, though there didn’t seem to be many clues.

민 only half-listened. Whatever the plan, someone would need to watch out for 랜드. His deed this day would be destroying him inside, no matter what he proclaimed. There were plenty of others worrying about what he would do at the Last Battle. It was her job to get him to that Last Battle alive and sane, with his soul in one piece.

Somehow.

**C*HAPTER** **38**

![](images/00279.jpg)

News in **Tel’aran’rhiod**

“에그웨인, see reason,” 시우안 said, faintly translucent because of the *ter’angreal* ring she had used to enter *Tel’aran’rhiod.* “What good can you do, rotting in that cell? 엘라이더 will see that you’re never let free, not after what you said you did at that dinner.” 시우안 shook her head. “Mother, sometimes you just have to face truth. You can only repair a net so many times before you need to toss the thing aside and weave a new one.”

에그웨인 sat on a three-legged stool in the corner of the room, the front part of a cobbler’s shop. She’d chosen the location at random, just in case, eschewing a location in the 백색 탑 itself. The 버림받은 자들 knew that 에그웨인 and the others walked the World of Dreams.

With 시우안, 에그웨인 could be more relaxed, more her real self. The two of them both understood that 에그웨인 was now the Amyrlin and 시우안 her lesser, but at the same time, they shared a bond. A camaraderie due to the station they both had filled. That bond, strangely, had turned into something akin to friendship.

At the moment, 에그웨인 was nearly ready to strangle her friend. “We’ve been over this,” she said firmly. “I *cannot* flee. Each day I spend imprisoned—but do not break—is another blow to 엘라이더’s rule. If I disappear before her trial, it will undermine everything we’ve worked for!”

“The trial will be a sham, Mother,” 시우안 said. “And if it isn’t, the punishment will be light. From what you’ve told me, she didn’t break any bones when she beat you—why, she didn’t break the skin.”

That was true. 에그웨인’s bleeding had been from broken glass, not 엘라이더’s stripes.

“Even a formal censure from the Hall will undermine her,” 에그웨인 said. “My resistance, my refusal to break my imprisonment, means something. The 의석자들 themselves come to visit me! If I were to flee, it would look as though I’d given in to 엘라이더.”

“Didn’t she declare you a Darkfriend?” 시우안 asked pointedly.

에그웨인 hesitated. Yes, 엘라이더 had done that. But she didn’t have proof for it.

Tower law was intricate, and sorting out the proper punishments and interpretations could be complicated. The 세 가지 맹세 would have prevented 엘라이더 from using the 하나의 힘 as a weapon, and so 엘라이더 must have *thought* that what she was doing wasn’t a violation. Either she had gone farther than she’d planned, or she saw 에그웨인 as a Darkfriend. She could argue for either position to defend herself; the latter would relieve her of the most guilt, but the former would be much easier to prove.

“She could succeed at having you convicted,” 시우안 said, apparently thinking along the same lines. “You would be slated for execution. What then?”

“She won’t succeed. She hasn’t any proof that I am a Darkfriend, and so the Hall will never allow it.”

“And if you’re wrong?”

에그웨인 hesitated. “Very well. If the Hall decides that I am to be executed, I will let you get me out. But not until then, 시우안. Not until then.”

시우안 snorted. “You might not have an opportunity, Mother. If 엘라이더 cows them, she will act quickly. The woman’s punishments can be swift as a stormwind, take you unaware. I know *that* for certain.”

“If that happens,” 에그웨인 said pointedly, “my death would be a victory. 엘라이더 would be the one who gave up, not I.”

시우안 shook her head, muttering, “Stubborn as a mooring post.”

“We are finished with that discussion, 시우안,” 에그웨인 said sternly.

시우안 sighed, but said nothing further. She seemed to have too much nervous energy to sit, and ignored the stool on the other side of the room, instead going to stand by the shop window to 에그웨인’s right.

The cobbler’s salesroom showed signs of great traffic. A stout counter divided the room in half, the wall behind pocketed with dozens of shoe-sized nooks. At times, most of these were stuffed with sturdy work shoes of leather or canvas, laces hanging down the front or buckles gleaming in the phantom light of *Tel’aran’rhiod*. Yet each time 에그웨인 glanced at the wall, the shoes had shifted, some vanishing, others appearing. They must not stay long in their cubbyholes in the real world, for they left only vague images behind in the world of dreams.

The front half of the shop was crowded with stools for customers to use. The shoes on the back wall were of different designs and patterns, along with test shoes for sizing. A person came into the shop, tried on the sizing shoes, then picked a style. The cobbler—or, likely, his assistants—would then craft a pair for later pickup. The wide glass windows at the front proclaimed the name of the cobbler in white painted letters to be Naorman Mashinta, and a smaller number “three” had been painted beside the name. This was the third generation of Mashintas to run the shop. Not uncommon at all among townsfolk. In fact, the part of 에그웨인 that was still influenced by the 두 강 found it odd that anyone would consider leaving their parent’s trade for another, unless they were a third or fourth child.

“Now that we’ve dealt with the obvious,” 에그웨인 said, “what news is there?”

“Well,” 시우안 said, leaning on the window and staring out at the eerily empty 타르 발론 street. “An old acquaintance of yours recently arrived in camp.”

“Really?” 에그웨인 asked absently. “Who?”

“가윈 Trakand.”

에그웨인 started. That was impossible! 가윈 had sided with 엘라이더’s faction during the rebellion. He wouldn’t have come over to the rebel side. Had he been captured? But that wasn’t how 시우안 had phrased it.

For a moment, 에그웨인 was a trembling girl, caught in the power of his whispered promises. She managed to keep her form locked into that of the Amyrlin, however, and forced her thoughts back to the moment, driving herself to be casual as she responded. “가윈?” she asked. “How odd. I wouldn’t have thought to find him there.”

시우안 smiled. “That was nicely handled,” she said. “Though you paused too long, and when you did ask for him, you were overly uninterested. That made you easy to read.”

“Light blind you,” 에그웨인 said. “Another test? Is he really there?”

“I hold to the oaths, thank you,” 시우안 said, affronted. 에그웨인 was one of the few who knew that, as a result of her stilling and 치유, 시우안 had been released from the 세 가지 맹세. But, like 에그웨인, she chose not to lie anyway.

“Either way,” 에그웨인 said, “I should think that the time for testing me has passed.”

“Everyone you meet will always be testing you, Mother,” 시우안 said. “You must be prepared for surprises; at any moment someone could throw one at you just to see how you respond.”

“Thank you,” 에그웨인 said coldly. “But I really don’t need the reminder.”

“Don’t you?” 시우안 said. “Sounds a little like something 엘라이더 would say.”

“That’s unfair!”

“Prove it,” 시우안 said smugly.

에그웨인 forced herself to be calm. 시우안 was right. Better to take the advice, particularly when it was good advice, than to complain. “You are right, of course,” 에그웨인 said, smoothing out her dress across her knees as she also smoothed the frustration from her face. “Tell me more of 가윈’s arrival.”

“I don’t know much more,” 시우안 confessed. “I really should have mentioned it yesterday, but our meeting was cut short.” They were meeting more often now—each night of 에그웨인’s imprisonment—but yesterday something had awakened 시우안 before they had finished talking. A bubble of evil in the rebel camp, she had reported, involving tents coming alive and trying to strangle people. Three had died, one of them 에스 세다이.

“Anyway,” 시우안 continued, “가윈 hasn’t said much that I could hear. I think he’s here because he heard that you were captured. He arrived with a spectacular flurry, but now he stays in Bryne’s command post, visiting the 에스 세다이 regularly. He’s mulling over something; keeps going to speak to Romanda and Lelaine.”

“That’s troubling.”

“Well, they *are* the obvious power in camp,” 시우안 said. “Save when 셰리암 and the others can wrench some authority away. Things haven’t gone well without you; the camp needs leadership. Actually, we crave it, as a starving fisherman craves a catch. 에스 세다이 are a people of order, I suppose. It—”

She stopped herself. Likely, she had been about to bully 에그웨인 again to accept rescue. She glanced at 에그웨인, then continued. “Well, it will be good for us when you return, Mother. The longer you stay away, the stronger the factions become. You can almost see the lines down the middle of the camp now. Romanda on one side, Lelaine on the other, with a shrinking slice that doesn’t want to take sides.”

“We *cannot* afford another division,” 에그웨인 said. “Not among ourselves; we have to prove stronger than 엘라이더.”
“At least our splits aren’t along the lines of 아자,” 시우안 said defensively.

“Factions and breaks,” 에그웨인 said, getting up. “Infighting and squabbling. We are better than this, 시우안. Tell the Hall that I wish to meet with them. Perhaps in two days. Tomorrow, you and I should meet again.”

시우안 nodded hesitantly. “Very well.”

에그웨인 eyed her. “You think it unwise?”

“No,” 시우안 said. “I worry about how hard you’re pushing yourself. The Amyrlin needs to learn to ration her strength; some in your place have failed not because they lacked the capacity for greatness, but because they stretched that capacity too thin, sprinting when they should have walked.”

에그웨인 refrained from pointing out that 시우안 herself had spent much of her tenure as Amyrlin sprinting at a breakneck speed. But it could very well be argued that 시우안 *had* stretched herself too thin, and had fallen as a result. Who better to speak on the dangers of such activities than one who had been burned by them so deeply?

“The advice is appreciated, daughter,” 에그웨인 said. “But really, there is little to worry about. My days are spent in solitude, with the occasional beating to provide spice. These meetings at night help me survive.” She shivered, glancing away from 시우안, out the window toward the dirty, vacant street.

“Is it difficult to endure?” 시우안 asked softly.

“The cell is narrow enough for me to touch opposite walls at once,” 에그웨인 said. “And isn’t very long, either. When I lie down, I have to bend my knees to fit. I can’t stand, since the ceiling is so low it makes me stoop, and I can’t sit without pain, for they no longer Heal me between beatings. The straw is old and itches. The door is thick and the cracks don’t allow in much light. I wasn’t aware that the Tower *had* cells such as this one.” She glanced back at 시우안. “Once I am upheld fully as Amyrlin, this room and any like it will be removed, the doors ripped out and the cells themselves filled with bricks and mortar.”

시우안 nodded. “We’ll make certain of it.”

에그웨인 turned away again, and noticed with shame that she’d let her gown shift to the *cadin’sor* of an 아일 Maiden, complete with spears and bow at her back. She forced the clothing back, taking a deep breath. “No person should be kept in such a manner,” she said, “not even. . . .”

시우안 frowned as 에그웨인 trailed off. “What was that?”

에그웨인 shook her head. “It just occurred to me. This is what it must have been like for 랜드. No, worse. The stories say he was locked in a box smaller than my cell. At least I can spend part of the evenings chatting with you. He had nobody. He was without the belief that his beatings meant something.” Light send that she didn’t have to endure as long as he had. Her imprisonment had only been a few days so far.

시우안 fell silent.

“Regardless,” 에그웨인 said, “I have *Tel’aran’rhiod*. During the days, my body is captive, but my soul is free at night. And each day I endure is another proof that 엘라이더’s will is *not* law. She cannot break me. Her support from the others is eroding. Trust me.”

시우안 nodded. “Very well,” she said, rising. “You *are* Amyrlin.”

“Of course I am,” 에그웨인 said absently.

“No, 에그웨인,” 시우안 said. “I meant that from the heart.”

에그웨인 turned, surprised. “But you’ve always believed in me!”

시우안 raised an eyebrow.

“At least,” 에그웨인 said, “from fairly near the beginning.”

“I always believed you had potential,” 시우안 corrected. “Well, you’ve fulfilled it. Some of it at least. Enough of it. However this storm blows through, you’ve proven one thing. You *deserved* the place you hold. Light, girl, you may end up being the best Amyrlin this world has known this side of 아투르 호크윙’s reign!” She hesitated. “And that’s not an easy thing for me to admit, mind you.”

에그웨인 took 시우안’s arms, smiling. Why, 시우안 almost looked teary-eyed with pride! “All I did was get myself locked in a cell.”

“And you did it like an Amyrlin, 에그웨인,” 시우안 said. “But I should be getting back. Some of us can’t spend our days relaxing the way you can. We need real sleep, otherwise we’re likely to fall unconscious in our washwater.” She grimaced, releasing herself from 에그웨인’s hands.

“You could just tell him to—”

“Now, I’ll have none of that,” 시우안 said, wagging a finger at 에그웨인. Had she forgotten that she’d just been complimenting 에그웨인’s stature as an Amyrlin? “I gave my word, and I’ll be fish guts before I’ll break it.”

에그웨인 blinked. “I wouldn’t dream of making you,” she said, covering a smile as she noticed that 시우안’s shadowy form now had a bright red ribbon in its hair. “Off with you, then.”

시우안 nodded sharply, then sat down and closed her eyes. She faded slowly from *Tel’aran’rhiod*.

에그웨인 hesitated, watching the area where 시우안 had been. It was probably time to return to normal dreaming, letting her mind restore itself. But returning to her normal dreams would be a step toward waking, and when she woke she would find only that cramped dungeon and its stuffy darkness. She longed to stay in the World of Dreams just a little longer. She thought of visiting 엘레인’s dreams to ask for a meeting . . . but no, that would take too much time, assuming 엘레인 could make her dream *ter’angreal* work. She rarely could, these days.

She found herself stepping away from 타르 발론, the cobbler’s shop vanishing around her.

She appeared in the rebel 에스 세다이 camp. A foolish place to visit, perhaps. If there were 어둠의 친구들 or 버림받은 자들 in the World of Dreams, they could very well be studying this camp and looking for information, much as 에그웨인 sometimes visited the Amyrlin’s study in *Tel’aran’rhiod* to search for clues on 엘라이더’s plans. But 에그웨인 needed to come here. She didn’t question why; she simply felt that it was true.

The streets of the camp were muddy, worn in ruts from passing wagons. Once just a field, the area had been appropriated by the 에스 세다이 and turned into . . . something. Part a place of war, with Bryne’s soldiers camped in a ring about them. Part town, though no town had ever boasted such a complement of 에스 세다이, 수련생s and 허락받은 자. Part monument to the weakness of the 백색 탑.

에그웨인 walked the camp’s main thoroughfare, where weeds had been trampled to mud, then mud worn into a road. Walkways lined it, and tents covered the flat land beyond. There were no people, only the occasional fleeting glimpse of a sleeper who had stumbled into *Tel’aran’rhiod*. Here, a brief flash of a woman in a fine green gown. A dreaming 에스 세다이, perhaps, though it was just as likely to be a serving maid imagining herself to be a queen. There, a woman in white—a woman with stringy blond hair who was far too old to be a 수련생. That no longer mattered. The 수련생 book should have long ago been opened to all. The 백색 탑 was too weak to turn down any source of strength.

Both women were gone almost as quickly as they appeared. Few dreamers stayed long in *Tel’aran’rhiod*; to remain longer, one needed either a particular skill like 에그웨인’s or a *ter’angreal* like the ring 시우안 used. There was a third way. Getting caught up in a living nightmare. There were none of the latter about, thank the Light.

The camp seemed strange to be so deserted. 에그웨인 had long since stopped being unnerved by the eerie lack of people in *Tel’aran’rhiod*. But this camp was different somehow. It looked as a war camp might after all of the soldiers had been slaughtered on the battlefield. Deserted, yet still a banner to proclaim the lives of those who had occupied it. 에그웨인 felt as if she could see the division that 시우안 had talked about, tents clumped together like bunches of sprouting flowers.

With individuals removed, she could see the patterns and the troubles they bespoke. 에그웨인 might denounce 엘라이더 for the rifts among the 아자s in the 백색 탑, but 에그웨인’s own 에스 세다이 were beginning to fracture as well. Well, three 에스 세다이 could hardly gather without two of them making an alliance. It was healthy to have the women planning and preparing; the trouble was when they began to regard others of their kind as enemies, rather than just rivals.

시우안 was right, unfortunately. 에그웨인 could not spend much more time setting her hopes on reconciliation. What if the 백색 탑 *didn’t* unseat 엘라이더? What if, despite 에그웨인’s progress, the rifts between the 아자s never healed? What then? Go to war?

There was another option, one that none of them had brought up: that of giving up on reconciliation permanently. Setting up a second 백색 탑. It would mean leaving the 에스 세다이 broken, perhaps forever. 에그웨인 shuddered at the prospect, and her skin itched, rebelling against the thought.

But what if she had no other choice? She had to consider the ramifications, and she found them daunting. How could they encourage the Kin or the 현명한 이들 to tie themselves to the 에스 세다이 if the 에스 세다이 themselves were not unified? The two 백색 탑s would become opposed forces, confusing the leaders of men as rival Amyrlins tried to use nations for their own purposes. Allies and enemies alike would lose their awe of the 에스 세다이, and kings very well might start up their own centers for women talented in channeling.

에그웨인 steeled herself, walking on the muddy road, the tents along the way changing, their flaps open, then closed, then open again in the strange ephemeral way of the World of Dreams. 에그웨인 felt the Amyrlin’s stole appear around her neck, too heavy, as if woven with lead weights.

She *would* bring the 백색 탑 에스 세다이 to her side. 엘라이더 *would* fall. But if not . . . then 에그웨인 would do what was necessary in order to preserve the people, and the world, in the face of Tarmon Gai’don.

She stepped away from the camp, the tents, ruts, and empty streets vanishing. Again, she wasn’t certain where her mind would take her. 이동 in the World of Dreams this way—letting *need* direct her—could be dangerous, but it could also be very illuminating. In this case, she looked not for an object, but for knowledge. What did she need to know, what did she need to see?

Her surroundings blurred, then snapped back straight. She stood in the middle of a small camp, fire smoldering in a firepit before her, a tiny tongue of smoke curling toward the sky. That was odd. Fire was usually too fleeting to reflect in *Tel’aran’rhiod*. There were no actual flames, despite the smoke and the orange glow warming the smooth riverstones that ringed the pit. She glanced upward, toward the too-dark, stormy sky. That silent storm was another irregularity for the World of Dreams, though it had become so common lately that she hardly noticed it anymore. Could anything be called regular for this place?

With shock, she noticed colorful wagons around her, green, red, orange and yellow. Had they been there a moment before? She was in a large clearing set inside a forest of phantom white aspen. The underbrush was thick, where spindly wild grass poked fingers out in jagged patches. An overgrown road meandered through the trees to her right; the colorful wagons sat in a ring around the fire. Bright paints colored the sides of the boxy vehicles, which had roofs and walls like tiny buildings. Oxen did not reflect in the World of Dreams, but plates, cups and spoons appeared, then vanished from places beside the firepit or on the seats of the wagons.

It was a camp of the 이동 People, the Tuatha’an. Why this place? 에그웨인 walked idly around the firepit, looking at the wagons, the coats of paint kept fresh and free of cracks or stains. This caravan was much smaller than the one she and 페린 had visited so long ago, but it had much the same feel. She could almost hear the flutes and drums, could almost imagine those flickers from the firepit to be the shadows of dancing men and women. Did the Tuatha’an still dance, with that sky so full of gloom, the winds so full of ill news? What place was there for them in a world preparing for war? 트롤록s cared nothing for the Way of the Leaf. Did this group of Tuatha’an seek to hide from the Last Battle?

에그웨인 settled herself on the side steps of a wagon, which was turned to face the nearby firepit. For a moment, she let her gown change to that of a simple, woolen 두 강 dress of green, much like the one she’d worn during her time visiting the 이동 People. She stared into those nonexistent flames, remembering and pondering. What had become of Aram, Raen and Ila? But she would not break, particularly not while she could spend the nights in *Tel’aran’rhiod*. 에그웨인 shook her head. 엘라이더 was more competent than 에그웨인 had assumed. She’d seen that the imprisonment wasn’t working and had found a scapegoat to punish instead. “Hello, 에그웨인,” Verin said, taking a sip from a steaming cup of tea. “My! I was beginning to wonder if I’d have to break into that cell of yours in order to speak with you.”

She froze, glancing at Verin.

That had been a lie. *Verin could speak lies.*

“Yes, I thought that might get your attention,” Verin said, smiling. “You should sit down. We have much to discuss and little time in which to do it.”

A Visit from Verin Sedai

“I compliment you on what you’ve done here, 에그웨인,” Verin said. “I’ve followed some little of the foolishness going on between the 에스 세다이 factions, though I decided not to get involved personally.
