He seemed so emotionless, but she had seen the beast get free and roar at her. It was coiled inside him, and if he didn’t let his emotions out soon, they would devour him from the inside.

But how to make him see reason? She had prepared argument after argument—each of them distinctly reasoned and calmly explained—during their time in 티어. 랜드 had ignored all of them, spending the last two days meeting with his generals and planning strategy for the Last Battle.

Each day brought 란 one step closer to a fight he couldn’t win. Each day made her more anxious; several times, she’d nearly abandoned 랜드 and ridden for the north. If 란 was going to fight an impossible battle, then she longed to be at his side. But she stayed. Light take 랜드 al’Thor, she stayed. What good would it do to help 란, only to let the world fall into Shadow because of a stubborn sheepherder’s stubborn . . . *stubbornness*!

She gave her braid a solid yank. The jeweled bracelets and rings on her hands glittered in the faint sunlight—the sky was cloudy, of course, just as it had been for weeks. Everyone tried to ignore how unnatural that was, but 니나브 could still feel that storm building to the north.

Such a short time left until 란 reached the Gap! Light send that he was slowed down by the 말키에르i who had come to support him in his ride. Light send that he was not alone. Thinking of him, riding into the 황무지, facing the army of 그림자태생 who infested his homeland. . . .

“We *have* to attack there,” 니나브 said. “이투랄데 says that the 황무지 is swarming with 트롤록s. 어둠의 존재 is gathering his forces. You can bet that the bulk of them will be at the Gap, where it’s easiest to get through and strike at 안도르 and 케렌!”

“That is exactly why we will not attack at the Gap, 니나브,” 랜드 said, voice cold and even. “We cannot let the enemy dictate our battlefield. The last thing we want to do is fight where *they* want us to, or where they expect us to.” He turned eyes northward. “Yes, let them gather. They seek me, and I shall not deliver myself. Why fight at Tarwin’s Gap? It makes the best sense to jump most of our armies right to 세이올 굴.”

“랜드,” she said, trying to sound reasonable. Couldn’t he see that she was reasonable? “There is no way that 란 has been able to gather a large enough force to hold back a mass assault by the 트롤록s, particularly not with most of the Borderlander armies doing Light only knows what down here. He’ll be overrun, and the 트롤록s will invade!”

Mention of the Borderlanders made 랜드’s face tighten; they rode to meet with their messengers. “The 트롤록s will invade,” 랜드 repeated.

“Yes!”

“Good,” 랜드 said. “It will keep them occupied as I do what needs to be done.”

“And 란?” 니나브 asked.

“His attack will be well placed.” 랜드 nodded. “He will draw my enemies’ attention to 말키에르 and the Gap, and it will make them think that I am there. 그림자태생 can’t move through gateways, so they can’t move as quickly as I can. By the time they’ve engaged 란, I’ll be past them and attacking directly at the 어둠의 존재’s heart.

“I don’t plan to abandon the southern lands, not at all. When the 트롤록s punch through the Gap, they will break up into fists to invade. That’s when my forces will hit them, led by 바쉐어, 이동 by gateway to strike at each group of 트롤록s from the sides or behind. That way, we can pick the best battlefields to suit our needs.”

“랜드,” 니나브 said, her anger fading to horror. “란 will die!”

“Then who am I to deny him that?” 랜드 said. “We all deserve the chance to find peace.”

니나브 found her mouth hanging open. He actually believed that! Or he was convincing himself to believe it, at least.

“My duty is to kill the 어둠의 존재,” 랜드 said, as if to himself. “I kill him, then I die. That is all.”

“But—”

“That is enough, 니나브.” 랜드 spoke softly in that dangerous voice of his. He would not be pressed further.

니나브 sat back, stewing, trying to decide how to press him on the topic. Light! He would leave the people of the 국경지대 to suffer and die in the 트롤록 invasions? The people there wouldn’t care if the 어둠의 존재 had been defeated—they would be cooking in stewpots. That would leave 란 and the 말키에르i to fight alone, a tiny force to resist the might of every monster that the 황무지 could spit out.

The 쇼엔찬 would wage their war to the south and the west. The 트롤록s would attack from the north and the east. The two would meet, eventually. 안도르 and the other kingdoms would be turned into a massive battleground, the people there—good people, like those in the 두 강—would have no chance against such warfare. They’d be crushed.

So what could she do to change it? She had to come up with a new strategy to influence 랜드. Everything, in her heart, pointed at protecting 란. She had to get him help!

The group rode through open grassland spotted occasionally with farms. They passed one on the right, a solitary farmstead not unlike many back in the 두 강. Yet, in the 두 강, she’d never seen a farmer watch travelers with such open hostility. The red-bearded man in dirtied trousers, with sleeves rolled nearly to his shoulders, leaned against a half-finished fence, his axe laid casually—but very visibly—on the logs beside him.

His field had seen better years; though the soil had been neatly plowed and harrowed, the furrows had spat forth only the smallest of sprouts. The field was spotted with empty patches where seeds had inexplicably refused to take root, and the plants that *were* growing had a yellowish cast to them.

A group of younger men were pulling a stump free from a neighboring field, yet to 니나브’s practiced eye, they weren’t actually trying to get any work done. They didn’t have the harness hooked to their ox, and they hadn’t loosened the stump in the earth by digging about it. Those lengths of wood lying in the grass were too stout and smoothly worked to be the shafts of tools. Quarterstaffs. It was almost an amusing display—considering the fact that 랜드 had two hundred 아일 with him—but it said something. These men expected trouble and were preparing for it. No doubt they could feel the storm themselves.

This area, close to trade routes and within reach of 티어, was relatively safe from bandits. It was also just far enough north to avoid being caught in squabbles between 일리안 and 티어. This should have been a place where farmers didn’t need to turn good lumber into quarterstaffs, nor watch strangers with eyes that expected attack.

That wariness would serve them well when the 트롤록s reached them—assuming the 쇼엔찬 hadn’t conquered them and pressed them into their armies by that point. 니나브 tugged her braid again.

Her mind turned back to 란. She had to do something! But 랜드 wasn’t seeing sense. That left only Cadsuane’s mysterious plan. Fool woman, refusing to explain it. 니나브 had made the first step, offering an alliance, and how had Cadsuane reacted? With presumptuous arrogance, of course. How dare she welcome 니나브 into her little group of 에스 세다이 like a child who had been wandering in the woods!

How would 니나브’s task—discovering where 페린 was—help 란? During the past week, 니나브 had pressed Cadsuane for more information, but had failed. “Perform this task well, child,” Cadsuane had said, “and perhaps we shall give you more responsibility in the future. You’ve proven yourself willful at times, and we can’t have that.”

니나브 sighed. Find out where 페린 was. How was she supposed to do that? The 두 강 folk had been of little use. Many of their men were traveling with 페린, but they hadn’t been seen for some time. They were in the south somewhere, 알타라 or 게알단, likely. But that left a large area to search.

She should have known that the 두 강 would not provide an easy answer. Cadsuane had obviously already tried reaching 페린 herself, and must have failed. That’s why she’d given the task to 니나브. Had 랜드 sent 페린 on some secret mission?

“랜드?” she said.

He was muttering roughly to himself.

She shivered. “랜드,” she said more sharply.

He stopped muttering, then glanced at her. She thought she could see the anger hidden there, deep within him, a flash of annoyance at her interruption. Then it was gone, replaced by the frighteningly cool control. “Yes?” he asked.

“Do you . . . know where 페린 is?”

“He has tasks set before him and performs them,” 랜드 said, turning away. “Why do you wish to know?”

Best not to mention Cadsuane. “I’m still worried about him. And about 맷.”

“Ah,” 랜드 said. “You are particularly unaccustomed to lying, aren’t you, 니나브?”

She felt her face flush in embarrassment. When had he learned to read people so well! “I *am* worried about him, 랜드 al’Thor,” she said. “He has a peaceful, unassuming nature—and always did let his friends push him around too much.”

There. Let 랜드 think about *that*.

“Unassuming,” 랜드 said musingly. “Yes, I suppose he is still that. But peaceful? 페린 is no longer too . . . peaceful.”

So he had been in touch with 페린 recently. Light! How had Cadsuane known, and how had 니나브 missed those communications? “랜드, if you have 페린 working on something for you, then why have you kept it secret? I deserve to—”

“I haven’t been meeting with him, 니나브,” 랜드 said. “Calm yourself. There are simply things that I know. We are connected, 페린, myself and 맷.”

“How? What do you—”

“That is all I will say on it, 니나브,” 랜드 interrupted, slicing into her sentence with soft words.

니나브 settled back, gritting her teeth again. The other 에스 세다이 spoke of being in control of their emotions, but obviously they didn’t have to deal with 랜드 al’Thor. 니나브 could be calm too, if she weren’t expected to manage the most bullheaded fool of a man who had ever put on a pair of boots.

They rode in silence for a time, the overcast sky hanging above them like a distant field of graymoss peat. The meeting place with the Borderlanders was a nearby crossroads. They could have Traveled directly there, but the Maidens had prevailed upon 랜드 to arrive a short distance out and approach more carefully. 이동 was extremely convenient, but it also could be dangerous. If your enemies knew where you would appear, you could open a gateway and find yourself ambushed by a line of archers. Even sending scouts through the gateway first wasn’t as safe as 이동 to a spot where nobody was expecting you.

The 아일 learned, and adapted, quickly. Surprising, really. The 황무지 was terribly unvaried; every part looked just about the same. Of course, she *had* overheard some 아일 guards saying something similar about the wetlands.

This particular crossroads hadn’t been important in years. If Verin or one of the other Brown sisters had been there, they’d likely have been able to explain exactly why. All 니나브 knew was that the kingdom which had once held this land had fallen long ago, and the only remnant was the independent city of Far Madding. 시간의 수레바퀴 turned. The most grand of kingdoms fell, rusted and eventually changed into lazy fields, ruled only by farmers determined to grow a particularly good crop of barley. It had happened to Manetheren, and it had happened here. Great highways that had once transported legions now dwindled to obscure country roads in need of maintenance.

As they continued, 니나브 let Moonlight fall back from 랜드’s position. That placed her riding near Narishma, with his dark, braided hair, bells tinkling on the ends. He wore black, like most Asha’man, and the Sword and Dragon twinkled on his collar. He’d changed in the months since being bonded as a 감시자. She could no longer look at him and see a boy. This was a man, with the grace of a soldier, the careful eyes of a 감시자. A man who had seen death and fought 버림받은 자들.

“You’re a Borderlander, Narishma,” 니나브 said. “Do you have any idea why the others left their posts?”

He shook his head, scanning the landscape. “I was a cobbler’s son, 니나브 Sedai. I know not the ways of lords and ladies.” He hesitated. “Besides, I’m not a Borderlander anymore.” The implication was clear. He would protect 랜드, no matter what other allegiances tugged at him. A very 감시자-like way of thought.

니나브 nodded slowly. “Do you have any idea what we’re riding into?”

“They’ll keep their word,” Narishma said. “A Borderlander would sooner die than break his word. They promised to send a delegation to meet with the Lord Dragon. They’ll do just that. I wish we’d been allowed to bring our 에스 세다이, though.”

Reports held that the Borderlander army included thirteen 에스 세다이. A dangerous number: the number needed to still a woman or gentle a man. Thirteen women in a circle could shield the most powerful of channelers. 랜드 had insisted that the delegation that came to meet him include no more than four of those thirteen 에스 세다이; in return, he promised to bring no more than four channelers. Two Asha’man—Narishma and Naeff—니나브 and 랜드 himself.

Merise and the others had thrown the 에스 세다이 equivalent of a fit—it involved a lot of downturned lips and questions like “Are you certain you want to do that?”—when 랜드 had forbidden them to come.

니나브 noted Narishma’s tense posture. “You don’t look as if you trust them.”

“A Borderlander’s place is guarding the Border,” Narishma said. “I was a cobbler’s son, and yet I was trained with the sword, spear, bow, axe and sling. Even before joining the Asha’man, I could best four out of five trained southern soldiers in a duel. We *live* to defend. And yet they left. Now, of all times. With thirteen 에스 세다이.” He glanced at her with those dark eyes of his. “I want to trust them. I know them for good people. But good people can do the wrong thing. Particularly when men who can channel are involved.”

니나브 fell silent. Narishma had a point, though what cause would the Borderlanders have to harm 랜드? They’d fought the encroachment of the 황무지 and its 그림자태생 for centuries, and the struggle against the 어둠의 존재 was imprinted on their very souls. They wouldn’t turn against the 용의 환생.

The Borderlanders had a special honor about them. It could be frustrating, true, but it was who they were. 란’s reverence for his homeland—particularly when many other 말키에르i had abandoned their identity—was part of what she loved about him. *Oh, 란. I’ll find someone to help you. I won’t let you ride into the Shadow’s jaws alone.*

As they neared a small green hill, several 아일 returned from scouting. 랜드 pulled the group to a halt, waiting for the *cadin’sor*-clad scouts to pad up to him, several wearing the red headbands marked with the ancient symbol of the 에스 세다이. The scouts weren’t winded, despite the fact that they’d run all the way ahead to the meeting place and then back.

랜드 leaned forward in his saddle. “Did they do as I asked? Did they bring no more than two hundred men, no more than four 에스 세다이?”

“Yes, 랜드 al’Thor,” said one of the scouts. “Yes, they kept to your requirements admirably. They have great honor.”

니나브 recognized the strange 아일 brand of humor in the tone of the man’s response.

“What?” 랜드 asked.

“One man, 랜드 al’Thor,” the 아일 scout said. “That is all that their ‘delegation’ consists of. He’s a short little thing of a man, though he looks like he knows how to dance the spears. The crossroads is behind this hill.”

니나브 looked ahead. Indeed, now that she knew to look, she could see another road running up from the south, presumably meeting with theirs just beyond the hill.

“What manner of trap is this?” Naeff asked, riding up beside 랜드, his lean, warrior’s face concerned. “An ambush?”

랜드 held up a hand for silence. He kicked his gelding into motion, and the scouts kept up without a word of complaint. 니나브 was nearly left behind; Moonlight was a far more placid animal than she would have chosen for herself. She’d have words with the stable master when she returned to 티어.

They rounded the hillside, finding a dusty square of ground, scarred by old firepits where caravans had stopped for the night. A roadway smaller than the one they’d been using twisted up to the north and down to the south. A solitary 시엔나르an man stood in the center, where roads met, watching the oncoming procession. His shoulder-length gray hair hung loose around a lean face which complemented his wiry build. His round face was lined with marks of age; his eyes were small, and he seemed to be squinting.

*Hurin?* she thought with surprise. 니나브 hadn’t seen the thief-taker since he’d accompanied her and a group of others back to the 백색 탑 following the events at Falme.

랜드 reined in his horse, allowing 니나브 and the Asha’man to catch up. 아일 fanned out like leaves blown before a gust of wind, taking up watchful positions around the crossroads. She was fairly certain that both of the Asha’man had seized the Source, and likely 랜드 had as well.

Hurin shuffled uncomfortably. He looked much as 니나브 remembered him. A tad more gray in the hair, but wearing the same simple brown clothing, with a sword-breaker and a shortsword at his waist. He had tied a horse to a fallen log nearby. The 아일 watched it suspiciously, as others might watch a pack of guard dogs.

“Why, Lord 랜드!” Hurin called, voice uneven. “It *is* you! Well, you’ve certainly come up in the world, I must say. Good to—”

He cut off as he was raised from the ground. He made an “urk” of surprise, being turned on unseen weaves of Air. 니나브 suppressed a shiver. Would seeing men channel ever stop bothering her?

“Who chased after you and me, Hurin,” 랜드 called, “the time when we were trapped in that distant shadow land? What nationality of men did I fell with the bow?”

“Men?” Hurin asked, voice almost a squawk. “Lord 랜드, there were no men in that place! None that we met, beyond Lady Selene, that is. All I remember are those frog beasts, the same ones folk say those 쇼엔찬 ride!”

랜드 spun Hurin around in the Air, regarding him with cold eyes. Then he urged his mount closer. 니나브 and the Asha’man did as well.

“You don’t believe that I’m me, Lord 랜드?” Hurin asked as he hung in the air.

“I take very little as it is presented to me, these days,” 랜드 said. “I assume the Borderlanders sent you because of our familiarity?”

Hurin nodded, sweating. 니나브 felt a stab of pity for the man. He was absolutely devoted to 랜드. They had spent a lot of time together, chasing down Fain and the 발레르의 뿔. On the return trip to 타르 발론, she’d seldom been able to stop Hurin from gossiping about this or that grand feat that 랜드 had accomplished. Being treated this way by the man he idolized was probably very unsettling for the lean thief-taker.

“Why only you?” 랜드 asked quietly.

“Well,” Hurin said, sighing. “They did tell you—” He hesitated, seeming distracted by something. He sniffed audibly. “Now that . . . that’s strange. Never smelled that before.”

“What?” 랜드 asked.

“I don’t know,” Hurin said. “The air . . . it smells like a lot of death, a lot of violence, only not. It’s darker. More terrible.” He shuddered visibly. Hurin’s ability to smell violence was one of those oddities that the Tower couldn’t explain. Not something related to the Power, yet obviously not quite natural either.

랜드 didn’t seem to care what Hurin smelled. “Tell me why they sent only you, Hurin.”

“I was saying, Lord 랜드. See, this here, we’re to discuss *terms*.”

“Terms regarding your armies moving back where they belong,” 랜드 said.

“No, Lord 랜드,” Hurin said uncomfortably. “Terms for setting up a *real* meeting with them. That part in their letter was kind of vague, I guess. They said you might be angry to find only me here.”

“They were wrong,” 랜드 said, voice softer. 니나브 found herself straining to hear him, leaning forward.

“I no longer feel anger, Hurin,” 랜드 said. “It serves me no useful function. Why would we need ‘terms’ to meet together? I presumed that my offer to bring only a small force would be acceptable.”

“Well, Lord 랜드,” Hurin said, “you see, they really *want* to meet with you. I mean, we came all this way—marched through the bloody winter itself, my pardon, 에스 세다이. But it was the bloody *winter*! And a bad one, although it took a long time getting to us. Anyways, we did that coming for you, Lord 랜드. So you see, they want to meet with you. Very badly.”

“But?”

“But, well, last time you were in Far Madding there was—”

랜드 held up a finger. Hurin quieted, and all grew still. Even the horses seemed to hold their breaths.

“The Borderlanders are in Far Madding?” 랜드 asked.

“Yes, Lord 랜드.”

“They want to meet with me there?”

“Yes, Lord 랜드. You’ll have to come inside the protection of the Guardian, you see, and—”

랜드 waved a curt hand, cutting off Hurin. A gateway opened immediately. It didn’t appear to lead to Far Madding, however; it just led back a short distance, to the road where 랜드 and the others had been riding a short time before.

랜드 released Hurin, gesturing for the 아일 to let the man mount, then moved Tai’daishar through the gateway. What was going on? Everyone else followed. Once through, 랜드 created another gateway, this one opening into a small wooded hollow. 니나브 thought she recognized it; this was where they had stopped following their visit to Far Madding with Cadsuane.

*Why the first gateway?* 니나브 thought, confused. And then it occurred to her. One didn’t need to learn an area to Travel a short distance from it—and 이동 *to* a place taught someone that location well enough to create gateways from it.

So by 이동 a short hop first, 랜드 memorized the location well enough to create gateways wherever he wanted—while skipping the time needed to learn the area! It was extremely clever, and 니나브 felt herself blushing that she hadn’t seen the possibility before. How long had 랜드 known of this trick? Had memory of it come from that . . . voice in his head?

랜드 rode Tai’daishar out into the hollow, the horse’s hooves stirring fallen leaves as he worked his way through the underbrush. 니나브 followed, trying to urge her docile mare to keep up with 랜드. That stablemaster was going to hear from her for certain. His ears would burn when she was through with him!

Hurin trotted his horse out as well, and the 아일 loped along, subtly keeping him surrounded. They had their faces veiled, spears or bows in hand. Past the trees and underbrush, 랜드 stopped Tai’daishar, looking across the open meadow toward the ancient city of Far Madding.

It wasn’t large, not by the measure of the Great Cities. Nor was it beautiful, not when compared with the 오지어-built wonders 니나브 had seen. But it was big enough, and it was certainly home to fine architecture and ancient relics. Set upon an island in a lake, it was actually faintly reminiscent of 타르 발론. Three broad bridges crossed the calm waters, and were the only means of entering the city.
A very large army was encamped around the lake, perhaps covering more ground than Far Madding itself. 니나브 counted dozens of different pennons marking dozens of different houses. There were lines upon lines of horses, and tents like rows of summer crops, carefully planted and organized, awaiting harvest. The Borderlander army.

“I’ve heard of this place,” Naeff said, riding up, close-cropped, dark brown hair ruffling in the wind. He narrowed his eyes, rectangular face dissatisfied. “It’s like a *stedding*, only not as safe.”

Far Madding’s massive *ter’angreal*—known as the Guardian—created invisible protective bubbles that blocked people from touching the 하나의 힘. That could be worked around through the use of a very specialized *ter’angreal*, one of which 니나브 happened to be wearing. But it would help only slightly.

The army looked close enough to be within the bubble that prevented men from channeling, which extended about a mile out around the city.

“They will know we’ve come,” 랜드 said softly, eyes narrowed. “They’ll have been waiting for it. They expect me to ride into their box.”

“Box?” 니나브 asked hesitantly.

“The city is a box,” 랜드 said. “The whole city and the area round it. They want me where they can control me, but they don’t understand. Nobody controls me. Not anymore. I’ve had enough of boxes and prisons, of chains and ropes. Never again will I put myself into the power of another.”

Still staring at the city, he reached to its place on his saddle and removed the statuette of a man holding aloft a globe. 니나브 felt a sharp chill. Did he have to bring *that* with him everywhere he went?

“Perhaps they need to be taught,” 랜드 said. “Given encouragement to do their duty and obey me.”

“랜드. . . .” 니나브 tried to think. She couldn’t let this happen again!

The access key began to glow faintly. “They want to capture me,” he said softly. “Hold me. Beat me. They did it once in Far Madding already. They—”

“랜드!” 니나브 said sharply.

He stopped, looking at her, seeing her as if for the first time.

“These are not slaves with their minds already burned away by 그랜달. That is an entire city full of innocent people!”

“I wouldn’t harm the people of the city,” 랜드 said, voice emotionless. “That army deserves the demonstration, not the city. A rain of fire upon them, perhaps. Or lightning to strike and bite.”

“They have done nothing other than ask you to meet with them!” 니나브 said, edging her horse closer to him. That *ter’angreal* sat like a viper in his hand. Once, it had cleansed the Source. If only it had melted away as the female one had!

She wasn’t certain what would happen if he aimed a weave into the protective bubble of Far Madding, but she suspected it would still work. The Guardian didn’t stop weaves from being made; 니나브 had been able to craft weaves just fine, when she’d drawn upon her Well.

Either way, she knew that she had to stop 랜드 from turning his anger—or whatever it was he felt—upon his allies. “랜드,” she said softly. “If you do this, there will be no turning back.”

“There’s already no turning back for me, 니나브,” he said, his eyes intense. Those eyes shifted, sometimes seeming gray, sometimes blue. Today, they looked iron gray. He continued, voice flat. “My feet started on this path the moment Tam found me crying on that mountain.”

“You don’t have to kill anyone today. Please.”

He turned to look back at the city. Slowly, mercifully, the access key stopped glowing. “Hurin!” he barked.

*He must be close to fraying,* 니나브 thought. *His anger is slipping out in his voice.*

The thief-taker rode up to the front of the group. The 아일 kept their distance, however. “Yes, Lord 랜드?”

“Return to your masters inside of their box,” 랜드 said, voice under control again. “You are to give them a message for me.”

“What message, Lord 랜드?”

랜드 hesitated, then slipped the access key back in its place. “Tell them that it will not be long before the 용의 환생 rides to battle at 세이올 굴. If they wish to return to their posts with honor, I will provide them with transport back to the 황무지. Otherwise, they can remain here, hiding. Let them explain to their children and grandchildren why *they* were hundreds of leagues away from their posts when the 어둠의 존재 was slain and the prophecies fulfilled.”

Hurin looked shaken. “Yes, Lord 랜드.”

With that, 랜드 turned his horse about and rode back toward the clearing. 니나브 followed, too slowly. Beautiful though Moonlight was, she’d have traded the beautiful mare in an instant for a biddable, dependable 두 강 horse like Bela.

Hurin stayed behind. He still looked shaken. His reunion with “Lord 랜드” had obviously been far from what he expected. 니나브 gritted her teeth as the trees obscured her view of him. Inside the clearing, 랜드 had opened another gateway, a direct gateway to 티어.

They rode out into the 이동 ground prepared outside the Stone of 티어’s stableyards. The air was hot and muggy in 티어, despite the overcast sky, and thick with the sounds of men training and gulls shrieking. 랜드 rode out to where stablehands waited, then dismounted, his face unreadable.

As 니나브 climbed off of Moonlight and handed the reins to a ruddy-faced stable worker, 랜드 walked past her. “Look for a statue,” he said.

“What?” she asked with surprise.

He glanced back at her, stopping. “You asked where 페린 was. He’s camped with an army beneath the shade of an enormous fallen statue shaped like a sword stabbing the earth. I’m certain scholars here can tell you where it is; it’s very distinctive.”

“How . . . how do you know that?”

랜드 just shrugged. “I just do.”

“Why tell me?” she asked, walking alongside him across the yard of packed earth. She hadn’t expected him to give up the information—he had gotten into the habit of holding onto whatever he knew, even if that knowledge was meaningless.

“Because,” he said, striding toward the keep, voice growing almost too soft to hear, “I . . . have a debt to you for caring when I cannot. If you seek 페린 out, tell him that I will soon need him.”

With that, he left her.

니나브 stood in the horse yard, watching him go. There was a wet scent to the air, the smell of new rain, and she could feel that she’d missed a sprinkle. Not enough to clear the air or muddy the ground, but enough to leave wetted sections of stone in shaded corners. To her right, men galloped and exercised horses beneath the dun sky, riding across sandy earth between pickets. The Stone was the only fortress she knew of with exercise areas for cavalry—but, then, the Stone was far from ordinary.

The rumble of hoofbeats was like the sound of a distant storm, and she found herself glancing northward. The storm there felt *closer* than it had before. She’d assumed it was gathering in the 황무지, but now she wasn’t so certain.

She took a deep breath, then hastened to the keep. She passed Defenders in their immaculate uniforms, the upper arm portions ribbed and puffy, breastplates smooth and curved. She passed stableboys, each probably dreaming of one day wearing that same uniform, but for now only leading horses back to the stables for hay and currying. She passed dozens of servants in linens, doubtless far more comfortable than 니나브’s maroon wool.

The keep itself was a towering rock of a structure, sheer walls broken only by windows. Except that she could still spot the place where 맷 had destroyed a section of stone with his Illuminator’s 불꽃놀이 when coming to rescue 니나브 and the others from their imprisonment. Fool boy. Where was he? She hadn’t seen him in . . . in quite a long time. Since Ebou Dar had fallen to the 쇼엔찬. In a way, she felt as though she’d abandoned him, though she’d never admit that. Why, she’d embarrassed herself enough in front of the Daughter of the Nine Moons when she’d defended that scoundrel! She still didn’t know what had come over her.

맷 could care for himself. He was probably carousing in some inn while the rest of them worked to save the world—drinking himself silly and playing at dice. 랜드 was another matter. He’d been so much easier to deal with when he’d continued to act like other men—stubborn and immature, but predictable. This new 랜드 with the cold emotions and the cold voice was truly unnerving.

The narrow corridors of the Stone were still unfamiliar to 니나브, and she often got lost. Her disorientation wasn’t helped by the fact that hallways and walls sometimes changed places. She’d tried to discount such tales as superstitious nonsense, but the day before, she’d woken to discover that her room had indeed suddenly and mysteriously *moved*. Her door had opened to a smooth wall of the same seamless rock as the Stone itself. She’d been forced to escape through a gateway, and had been shocked to learn that her window looked out from a location two stories higher than it had the previous night!

Cadsuane said it was the 어둠의 존재’s touch on the world, causing the Pattern to unravel. Cadsuane said a lot of things, and few of them were things that 니나브 wished to hear.

니나브 got lost twice as she wove her way through the corridors, but she eventually arrived at Cadsuane’s room. At least 랜드 hadn’t forbidden his stewards to grant her rooms. 니나브 knocked—she’d learned that she’d better—then entered.

The 에스 세다이 from Cadsuane’s group—Merise and Corele—sat in the room, knitting and sipping tea, trying to look like they were *not* waiting on the infernal woman’s whims. Cadsuane herself was speaking quietly with 민, whom she had all but appropriated in recent days. 민 herself didn’t seem to mind, perhaps because it wasn’t easy to spend time with 랜드 these days. 니나브 felt a stab of sympathy for the girl. 니나브 only had to deal with 랜드 as a friend; all of this would be much harsher on the one who shared his heart.

All eyes turned toward 니나브 as she closed the door. “I think I’ve found him,” she announced.

“Who is that, child?” Cadsuane said, leafing through one of 민’s books.

“페린,” 니나브 said. “You were right; 랜드 did know where he was.”

“Excellent!” Cadsuane said. “You did well; it appears that you *can* be of use.”

니나브 wasn’t certain which annoyed her more—the backhanded compliment, or the fact that her heart swelled with pride at hearing it. She was no girl, without her braid, to be stroked by this woman’s words!

“Well?” Cadsuane looked up from the book. The others remained silent, though 민 did shoot 니나브 a congratulatory smile. “Where is he?”

니나브’s opened her mouth to reply before she caught herself. What was it about this woman that made her want to obey? It wasn’t the 하나의 힘 or anything to do with it. Cadsuane simply projected the air of a stern, but fair, grandmother. The type you never spoke back to, but who would give you some baked sweets in reward for sweeping the floor when told.

“First, I want to know why 페린 is important.” 니나브 stalked into the room and took the only remaining seat, a painted wooden stool. When she sat, she found herself sitting a few inches below eye level. Like a student before Cadsuane. She almost stood up, but realized that would draw more attention.

“Phaw!” Cadsuane said. “You’d hold this knowledge back, even if it means the lives of those you hold dear?”

“I want to know what I’ve gotten myself into,” 니나브 said stubbornly. “I want to know that this information isn’t going to end up hurting 랜드 further.”

Cadsuane snorted. “You presume to think that I’d *hurt* the fool boy?”

“I’m not going to presume otherwise,” 니나브 snapped. “Not until you *tell* me what you are doing.”

Cadsuane closed the book—*Echoes of His Dynasty*—and looked perturbed. “Will you at least tell me how the meeting with the Borderlanders went?” she asked. “Or is that information held for ransom as well?”

Did she think she’d distract 니나브 that easily? “It went poorly, as one might expect,” she said. “They’ve hunkered down outside Far Madding and refuse to meet with 랜드 unless he comes within range of the Guardian, cutting himself off from the Source.”

“Did he take it well?” Corele asked from her cushioned bench at the side of the room. She smiled faintly; she seemed to be the only one who thought the changes in 랜드 were amusing, rather than terrifying. But, then, she *was* one of the women who had bonded an Asha’man at practically the first opportunity.

“Did he take it well?” 니나브 repeated flatly. “That depends. Does pulling out that blasted *ter’angreal* and threatening to rain down fire on the army strike you as ‘Taking it well’?”

민 paled. Cadsuane raised an eyebrow.

“I stopped him,” 니나브 said. “But just barely. I don’t know. It . . . it might be getting too late to do anything to change him.”

“That boy *will* laugh again,” Cadsuane said quietly, but intensely. “I didn’t live this long to fail now.”

“What does it matter?” Corele said.

니나브 turned in shock.

“Well?” Corele set down her mending. “What *does* it matter? We’re obviously going to succeed.”

“Light!” 니나브 said. “What gave you *that* idea?”

“We’ve just spent all afternoon drilling this girl about her visions.” Corele nodded to 민. “They always come true, and she’s seen things that obviously can’t happen until *after* the Last Battle. So we know that 랜드 is going to defeat the 어둠의 존재. 패턴 has already decided it. We can stop worrying.”

“No,” 민 said. “You’re wrong.”

Corele frowned. “Child, are you saying that you lied about the things you’ve seen?”

“No,” 민 said. “But if 랜드 loses, there *is* no Pattern.”

“The girl is correct.” Cadsuane sounded surprised. “What this child sees are weavings in the Pattern from a time still distant—but if the 어둠의 존재 wins, he will *destroy* the Pattern entirely. This is the only way the visions could fail to occur. The same holds for other prophecies and Foretellings. Our victory is by no means sure.”

That stilled the room. They weren’t playing at village politics or national dominance. At stake was creation itself.

*Light. Can I withhold this information if there’s any* chance *of it helping 란?* It wrenched her heart to think of him, and she had few options. In fact, 란’s only hope seemed to rest in the armies 랜드 could marshal and the gateways his people could form.

랜드 had to change. For 란. For them all. And she had no idea what to do other than, unfortunately, to trust Cadsuane. 니나브 swallowed her pride and spoke. “Do you know the location of a statue of an enormous sword, fallen to the earth as if stabbing it?”

Corele and Merise glanced at each other in confusion.

“The hand of the *amahn’rukane*.” Cadsuane turned from 민 with a raised eyebrow. “The full statue was never finished, from what scholars can tell. It rests near the Jehannah Road.”

“페린 is camping in its shadow.”

Cadsuane pursed her lips. “I assumed he would go eastward, toward lands al’Thor has captured.” She took a deep breath. “All right. We are going for him *right now*.” She hesitated, then glanced at 니나브. “In answer to your question earlier, child, 페린 actually isn’t important to our plans.”

“He isn’t?” 니나브 asked. “But—”

Cadsuane raised a finger. “There are people with him who are *vital.* One in particular.”

**C*HAPTER** **45**

![](images/00302.jpg)

The Tower Stands

에그웨인 walked slowly through the rebel camp, wearing a crimson gown, its skirts divided for riding. The color raised not a few eyebrows. Considering what the 적색 아자 had done, these 에스 세다이 weren’t likely to wear the hue. Even the camp’s serving women had noticed, selling their red and maroon dresses or cutting them up for rags.

에그웨인 had asked for the crimson specifically. In the Tower, sisters had formed the habit of wearing only their own 아자’s color, and the practice had helped fuel the division. While it was good to be proud of your 아자 affiliation, it was dangerous to begin assuming that you couldn’t trust anyone wearing other colors.

에그웨인 was all 아자s. Today, the red symbolized many things to her. The impending reunification with the 적색 아자. A reminder of the division that needed to be righted. A sign of the blood that would be spilled, the blood of good men who fought to defend the 백색 탑.

The blood of the dead 에스 세다이, beheaded not an hour ago by 에그웨인’s order.

시우안 had found her Great Serpent ring; it felt very good to have it on her finger again.

The sky was an iron gray, and the scent of dirt rose into the air, accompanying the bustling motion around the camp. Women hurriedly washed clothing, as if they were late in getting their patrons ready for a festival. Novices ran—literally ran—from lesson to lesson. 에스 세다이 stood about with arms folded, eyes ready to burn any who didn’t keep up the tempo.

*They sense the tension of the day,* 에그웨인 thought. *And can’t help but be made anxious by it.* The night before, with its attack by the 쇼엔찬. Followed by the return of the Amyrlin, who had spent the morning cleansing the 에스 세다이. And now afternoon, and the beating drums of war.

She doubted that Bryne’s own camp was in such a state. He’d have his men ready for attack; he probably could have assaulted the 백색 탑 at a moment’s notice on any given day of the siege. His soldiers would decide this war. 에그웨인 would *not* have her 에스 세다이 riding into battle, wriggling around their oaths not to use the Power to kill. They would wait here, to be called only for 치유.

Or called if the 백색 탑 sisters joined the fight in earnest. Light send that 엘라이더 saw wisdom in forbidding that. If the 에스 세다이 turned the Power against one another, it would be a dark day indeed.

*Can this day grow any darker?* 에그웨인 wondered. Many of the 에스 세다이 she passed in the camp gave her looks of respect, awe, and a little horror. After a long absence, the Amyrlin had returned. And she had brought destruction and judgment in her wake.

Over fifty Black Sisters had been stilled, then executed. 에그웨인 felt sick, thinking of their deaths. 셰리암 had seemed almost relieved when her turn came, though she’d soon begun to struggle, sobbing and desperate. She’d confessed to several disturbing crimes, as if hoping that her willingness to speak would gain her amnesty.

They’d placed her head on the block and taken it off, just like the others. That scene would always be vivid in 에그웨인’s mind—her former Keeper, lying with her head pressed against the stump, blue dress and fiery red hair suddenly bathed in warm golden light as a thinner section of clouds moved in front of the sun. Then the silvery axe, falling to claim her head. Perhaps the Pattern would be kinder to her next time she was allowed a thread in its great tapestry. But perhaps not. Death was not an escape from the 어둠의 존재. 셰리암’s horror at the end indicated that she might have been thinking that very thing as the axe took her head.

Now 에그웨인 understood fully how the 아일 could laugh at a simple beating. Would that she could go through a few days beneath the rod rather than have to order the execution of women she had liked and worked with!

Some of the 의석자들 had argued for interrogation instead of execution, but 에그웨인 had been insistent. Fifty women were far too many to shield and guard, and now that they knew stilling could be Healed, that wasn’t an option. No, history proved how slippery and dangerous members of the Black could be, and 에그웨인 was tired of worrying about what *could* happen. She had learned with 모그헤디엔 that there was a price to be paid for greed, if just greed for information. She and the others had been too eager—too proud of the “discoveries” they’d made—to see the world rid of one of the 버림받은 자들.

Well, she would not allow a similar mistake here. The law was known, the Hall had made its judgment, and it had not been done in secret. Verin had died to stop these women, and 에그웨인 would see that her sacrifice meant something.

*You did well, Verin. So very well.* Every 에스 세다이 in the camp had been made to swear the 세 가지 맹세 over again, and only three members of the Black had been discovered beyond the ones Verin had located. Her research had been thorough.

The Blacks’ 감시자s were under guard. They would have to be sorted through at a later date, when attention could be given to separating those who were really Black from those who were just enraged by the loss of their 에스 세다이. Most of them would seek death, even the innocent ones. Perhaps the innocent could be convinced to remain alive long enough to throw themselves into the Last Battle.

Nearly twenty of the Black sisters on Verin’s list had still escaped, despite all of 에그웨인’s precautions. She wasn’t certain how they had known. Bryne’s guards had caught some weaker ones trying to flee, and soldiers had fallen to delay them. But many had still escaped.

No use crying over that. Fifty Black were dead; that was a victory. A frightening one. But a victory nonetheless.

And so she walked through the camp, in riding boots and a dress of red, brown hair free to stream in the wind and tied with crimson ribbons to mark the streams of blood she had shed not an hour before. She did not blame the sisters around her for their sly glances, their masked concern, their fear. And their respect. If there had been any doubt that 에그웨인 was Amyrlin, it had been dispelled. They accepted her, they feared her. And she would never quite fit in with them again. She was separate, and always would be.

A determined figure in blue made her way through the tents and approached 에그웨인. The dignified woman curtsied appropriately, though since they were walking so quickly, 에그웨인 didn’t stop to let her kiss the Great Serpent ring. “Mother,” Lelaine said, “Bryne sends word that all is at ready for the assault. He says that the western bridges would be the ideal point of attack, though he suggests that gateways be employed to send a flanking force of his men behind the 백색 탑 lines. He asks if this would be possible.”

It wasn’t using the Power as a weapon, but it was close. A fine distinction. But being 에스 세다이 was *about* fine distinctions. “Tell him I will make the gateway myself,” she said.

“Excellent, Mother,” Lelaine said, bowing her head, the perfect, loyal attendant. It was remarkable, how quickly the woman’s bearing toward 에그웨인 had changed. She must have realized that her only choice was to attach herself to 에그웨인 completely and give up on her attempts to secure power. This way, she didn’t look like a hypocrite and would perhaps gain position through 에그웨인. Assuming 에그웨인 was able to stabilize herself as a powerful Amyrlin.

It was a good assumption.

Lelaine must have been frustrated by Romanda’s change of temperament. The Yellow waited beside the road ahead, as if on cue. She wore a dress after the color of her 아자, hair back in a stately bun. She curtsied as 에그웨인 reached her and barely spared a glance for Lelaine before falling into position on 에그웨인’s right, away from Lelaine. “Mother,” Romanda said, “I have made the inquires you requested. There has been no contact with those sent to the 검은 탑. Not a whisper.”

“Does this strike you as odd?” 에그웨인 asked.

“Yes, Mother. With 이동 they should have been there and back by now. They should have at least sent word. This silence is disturbing.”

Disturbing indeed. Even worse, that delegation contained Nisao, 미렐, Faolain *and* Theodrin. Each of the women had sworn fealty to 에그웨인. An unsettling coincidence. The departure of Faolain and Theodrin was particularly suspicious. Supposedly, they had gone because they had no 감시자s, but the sisters in the camp didn’t consider those two full 에스 세다이—though nobody would dare say such to 에그웨인 directly.

Why had those four, out of the hundreds of 에스 세다이 in the camp, been placed in the delegation? Was it mere coincidence? It stretched plausibility. But what did it mean, then? Had someone intentionally sent away those loyal to 에그웨인? If so, why not send 시우안? Was this perhaps 셰리암’s work? The woman had confessed to several things before her execution, but this hadn’t been one of them.

Either way, something was happening with those Asha’man. The 검은 탑 would need to be dealt with.

“Mother,” Lelaine said, drawing her attention back. The Blue didn’t glance at her rival. “I have other news.”

Romanda sniffed quietly.

“Speak,” 에그웨인 said.

“셰리암 wasn’t lying,” Lelaine said. “The *ter’angreal* used for dreams are gone. All of them.”

“How is this possible?” 에그웨인 demanded, letting a hint of her anger slip out.

“셰리암 was Keeper, Mother,” Lelaine said quickly. “We kept the *ter’angreal* together, as is custom in the 백색 탑, under guard. But . . . well, what reason would those guards have had to turn 셰리암 away?”

“And what do you suppose she was planning to tell us?” 에그웨인 asked. “This theft could not have been kept hidden for long.”

“I don’t know, Mother,” Lelaine said, shaking her head. “The guards said that 셰리암 seemed . . . flustered . . . when she took the *ter’angreal*. This was just last night.”

에그웨인 clenched her teeth, thinking of 셰리암’s final spilled confessions. The theft of the *ter’angreal* had been far from the most shocking tidbit she’d mentioned. 엘레인 would be livid; she had made all of the copies that were stolen. While none of her copies worked as well as the original, they worked well enough. She would not be happy that they were in the hands of a 버림받은 자들.

“Mother,” Lelaine said, more softly. “What of 셰리암’s . . . other claim?”

“That one of the 버림받은 자들 is in the 백색 탑, impersonating an 에스 세다이?” 에그웨인 said. 셰리암 claimed she’d given the *ter’angreal* to this . . . person.

Lelaine and Romanda walked silently, both staring forward, as if speculation were too daunting.

“Yes, I suspect that she is right,” 에그웨인 said. “They infiltrated not only our camp, but the aristocracies of 안도르, 일리안 and 티어. Why not the 백색 탑 as well?” She didn’t add that Verin’s book confirmed the presence of one of the 버림받은 자들. It seemed best to keep the extent of Verin’s notes secret.

“I wouldn’t worry about it too much,” 에그웨인 said. “With the assault on the Tower, and our return, it seems likely that the 버림받은 자들—whoever she is—will find it prudent to slip away and find an easier target for her scheming.”

Lelaine and Romanda didn’t seem comforted by that comment. The three of them reached the edge of the 에스 세다이 camp, where mounts awaited them, as well as a large group of soldiers and one Sitter from each of the 아자s, other than the Blue and Red. There wasn’t a Blue because Lelaine was the only one remaining in camp; the reason there wasn’t a Red was obvious. This was part of why 에그웨인 had chosen to wear red, a subtle hint that all 아자s should be represented in the action they were about to take. It was for the good of all.

As 에그웨인 mounted, she noticed that 가윈 was following her, again, at a respectful distance. Where had he come from? They hadn’t spoken since the early morning. As she mounted, so did he, and as she turned to ride out of camp with Lelaine, Romanda, the 의석자들 and the soldiers, 가윈 followed at a safe distance. 에그웨인 wasn’t certain what to do with him yet.
The army camp was mostly deserted. Tents sat empty, ground trampled by feet and hoofs, hardly any soldiers remaining behind. 에그웨인 embraced the Source soon after leaving their camp, and she held to it, ready with weaves should someone attack her during the ride. She still didn’t trust that 엘라이더 wouldn’t use a gateway to interfere with the assault. True, the false Amyrlin probably had her hands full with the aftermath of the 쇼엔찬 attack. But expectations like that one—assuming that she was safe—were what had gotten 에그웨인 captured in the first place. She was Amyrlin. She couldn’t risk herself. It was frustrating, but she knew that an end had come to her days of solitary action, striking out as she saw fit. She could have been killed, rather than captured, all those weeks ago. The Salidar rebellion would have floundered, and 엘라이더 would have continued as Amyrlin.

So it was that her force rode up to the battle lines outside the village of Darein. The 백색 탑 still smoldered, a wide field of smoke trailing up in a ring from the center of the island, shrouding the white spire. Even from a distance, the scars of the 쇼엔찬 attack were evident on the building. Blackened holes, like spots of corruption on an otherwise healthy apple. The Tower almost seemed to groan as she looked at it. It had stood for so long, had seen so much. Now it had been wounded so deeply that it still bled a day later.

And yet it stood. Light bless them, it *stood*. It rose high, wounded but sound, pointing toward a sun hidden by clouds above. It stood defiant of those who would break it, within and without.

Bryne and 시우안 waited for 에그웨인 at the back of the army. A disparate couple they were. The battle-hardened general, with temples of gray and a face like an unyielding piece of armor. Strong, made of lines. And beside him 시우안, the diminutive woman in pale blue, her face lovely, looking young enough to be Bryne’s granddaughter, for all the fact that they were near the same age.

시우안 made a horseback curtsy as 에그웨인 approached, and Bryne saluted. His eyes were still troubled. He seemed ashamed of his part in the rescue, though 에그웨인 bore him no grievance. He was a man of honor. If he had been bullied into coming along to protect foolhardy 시우안 and 가윈, then Bryne was to be commended for keeping them alive.

As 에그웨인 joined them, she noted that 시우안 and Bryne were riding close together. Had 시우안 finally admitted her attraction to the man? And . . . there was a certain familiar grace to Bryne now. It was slight enough that she could have just been seeing things, but coupled with the relationship between the two. . . .

“You’ve taken another 감시자, at last?” 에그웨인 asked 시우안.

The woman narrowed her eyes. “Aye,” she said.

Bryne did seem surprised, and a tad ashamed.

“Do your best to keep her out of trouble, General,” 에그웨인 said, staring 시우안 in the eyes. “She has been in quite a bit of it lately. I have half a mind to give her to you to use as a foot soldier. I believe that the military organization might be good for her, and remind her that sometimes, *obedience* overrides initiative.”

시우안 wilted, glancing away.

“I haven’t decided what to do with you yet, 시우안,” 에그웨인 said in a softer voice. “But my anger has been kindled. And my trust has been lost. You will need to soothe the first and stoke the second if you wish to enter my confidence again.”

She turned from 시우안 to the general, who looked sick. Probably from being forced to feel 시우안’s shame.

“You are to be commended for your bravery, letting her bond you, General,” 에그웨인 said, turning to Bryne. “I realize that keeping *her* from trouble is a nearly impossible charge, but I have confidence in you.”

The general relaxed. “I shall do my best, Mother,” he said. Then he turned his horse, glancing along the rows of soldiers. “There is something you should see. If you will?”

She nodded, turning her horse and riding beside him down the roadway. The village was cobbled here, the population evacuated, the main thoroughfare lined with thousands of Bryne’s soldiers. 시우안 accompanied 에그웨인, and 가윈 followed. Lelaine and Romanda stayed with the other 의석자들 at a wave of 에그웨인’s hand. Their newfound obedience was proving useful, particularly since they had apparently decided that they would now be trying to outdo one another for 에그웨인’s approval. Likely, they were both vying to be her new Keeper, now that 셰리암 was gone.

The general led 에그웨인 to the front lines, and 에그웨인 prepared a weave of Air just in case an arrow was shot in her direction. 시우안 eyed her, but said nothing at the precaution. It shouldn’t have been needed—Tower Guards would never fire on an 에스 세다이, not even in a conflict like this one. However, the same couldn’t be said of 감시자s, and accidents *did* happen. It would be very convenient for 엘라이더 if a stray arrow took her rival in the throat.

They made their way through the village, finally coming to a stop near the Darein Bridge, a majestic white construction that spanned the river to 타르 발론. Here was the thing Bryne wanted her to see: Gathered just west of the high point of the bridge, bunkered down behind a blockade of stones and large logs, was a force of Tower Guard. They looked to be about three hundred strong. Across the river, more soldiers stood atop the walls. They brought the total to no more than a thousand.

Bryne’s assault force here was ten thousand strong.

“Now, I know it was never numbers that were keeping us from attacking,” Bryne said. “But the Tower Guard should be able to field more men than that, particularly with conscriptions out of the city proper. I doubt they’ve been spending these months carving pegs by the fire and reminiscing about old times. If Chubain has half a mind, he’s been training a new set of recruits.”

“So where is everyone?” 에그웨인 asked.

“Light only knows, Mother,” Bryne said, shaking his head. “We’ll lose some men getting past that force, but not many. It will be a rout.”

“Could the 쇼엔찬 have really hurt them *that* much?”

“I don’t know, Mother,” Bryne said. “It was bad last night. A lot of fire, a lot of men dead. But I’d have pegged the cost at hundreds, not thousands. Perhaps the Tower Guard is clearing out rubble and stopping the fires, but I still think they’d have gathered a larger force when they saw me forming up here. I’ve taken a spyglass to those lads over there, and I’ve noted more than one set of bleary red eyes.”

에그웨인 sat thoughtfully, glad for the breeze blowing in along the river from downstream. “You haven’t questioned the wisdom of this assault, General.”

“It’s not my habit to question where I’m pointed, Mother.”

“And your thoughts on the matter, if asked?”

“If asked?” Byrne said. “Well, attacking makes tactical sense. We’ve lost 이동 as an edge, and if our enemy can resupply at will and send envoys in and out whenever they want, then what’s the purpose of a siege? It’s time to either attack or pack up and leave.”

에그웨인 nodded. And yet, she found herself hesitating. That ominous smoke in the sky, the maimed Tower, the frightened soldiers without reinforcements. It all seemed to whisper a warning.

“How long can we wait before you absolutely *must* begin this assault, General?” she asked.

He frowned, but didn’t question her. He glanced at the sky. “It’s getting late. An hour, perhaps? After that, it will be too dark. With numbers this favorable, I’d rather not add the randomness of a night battle to the mix.”

“We wait, then, for an hour,” 에그웨인 said, settling back on her mount. The others seemed confused, but they said nothing. The 아미를린 석좌 had spoken.

What was she waiting for? What were her instincts telling her? 에그웨인 thought on it as the minutes extended, eventually realizing what had made her pause. Once this step had been taken, there was no turning back. The 백색 탑 had suffered the previous night; it was the first time an enemy force had used the 하나의 힘 against it. 에그웨인’s assault would be another first: the first time one group of 에스 세다이 had led troops in battle against another group. There had been fights between factions in the Tower before; clashes between one 아자 and another, some turning to bloodshed, like what had happened after 시우안’s ousting. The Secret Histories mentioned such events.

But never had the dissension extended beyond the doors of the Tower itself. Never had 에스 세다이 led troops across those bridges. To do so now would attach the event forever to 에그웨인’s tenure as Amyrlin. Whatever else she achieved, it would likely be overshadowed by this day.

She had hoped to liberate and unite. Instead, she would turn to war and subjugation. If it had to be so, then she would give the command. But she wanted to wait until the last possible moment. If that meant a grim hour beneath the overcast sky, horses snorting as they sensed their riders’ tension, then so be it.

Bryne’s hour came and passed. 에그웨인 hesitated for a few minutes longer—as long as she dared. No relief came to the poor soldiers standing on the bridge. They just stared out behind their little barricade, resolute.

Reluctantly, 에그웨인 turned to give the command.

“Here now.” Bryne leaned forward in his saddle. “What is this?”

에그웨인 turned back to the bridge. Distantly, just barely visible, a procession was coming over the top. Had she waited too long? Had the 백색 탑 sent reinforcements? Had she cost the lives of her men by her stubborn reluctance?

But no. That group wasn’t soldiers, but women in skirts. 에스 세다이!

에그웨인 held up her hand, staying any attacks by her soldiers. The procession rode directly up to the Tower Guard fortification. A moment later, a woman in a gray dress stepped out in front of the blockade, accompanied by a single 감시자. 에그웨인 squinted, trying to make out the woman’s features, and Bryne hastily handed her his spyglass. 에그웨인 accepted it thankfully, but had already recognized the woman. Andaya Forae, one of the new 의석자들 to the Hall chosen after the split. 회색 아자. That implied a willingness to negotiate.

The glow of power surrounded the woman, and 시우안 hissed, causing several nearby soldiers to raise their bows. Again 에그웨인 held up a hand. “Bryne,” she said sternly, “I will *not* have the first shot fired until I give permission.”

“Stand down, men!” Bryne bellowed. “I’ll have your hides if you so much as nock an arrow!” The men snapped their bows back down from the ready.

The distant woman used a weave 에그웨인 couldn’t make out, and then spoke in a voice that was obviously amplified. “We would speak with 에그웨인 al’Vere,” Andaya said. “Is she in attendance?”

에그웨인 made her own weave to amplify her voice. “I am here, Andaya. Tell the others with you to come out so that I can see them.”

Surprisingly, they obeyed the command. Nine more women filed out, and 에그웨인 studied each one. “Ten 의석자들,” she said, handing Bryne back his spyglass and releasing her weave so that she could speak without her words being projected. “Two from each 아자 except the Blue and the Red.”

“That’s promising.” Bryne rubbed his chin.

“Well, they could be here to demand my surrender,” 에그웨인 noted. “All right,” she said, amplifying her voice with the Power again. “What do you wish of me?”

“We have come,” Andaya said. She hesitated. “We have come to inform you that the Hall of the 백색 탑 has chosen to raise you to the 아미를린 석좌.”

시우안 gasped in shock, and Bryne cursed quietly to himself. Several of the soldiers muttered about it being a trap. But 에그웨인 just closed her eyes. Dared she hope? She’d assumed that her unwanted rescue had come too soon. But if she’d laid enough groundwork before being taken by 시우안 and 가윈. . . .

“What of 엘라이더?” 에그웨인 demanded, opening her eyes, her voice booming across the expanse. “Have you deposed yet another Amyrlin?”

The other side was silent for a moment. “They’re conferring.” Bryne had raised his spyglass.

Andaya spoke a moment later. “엘라이더 do Avriny a Roihan, Watcher of the 봉인, the Flame of 타르 발론, the 아미를린 석좌 . . . was taken in the raid last night. Her whereabouts are unknown. She is presumed dead or otherwise unable to fulfill her duties.”

“By the Light!” Bryne lowered the glass.

“No more than she deserved,” 시우안 muttered.

“No woman deserves that,” 에그웨인 said to 시우안 and Bryne. Absently she raised fingers to her neck. “Better she had died.”

Bryne said, “This could be a trap.”

“I don’t see how,” 시우안 said. “Andaya is bound by the oaths. She wasn’t on your list of Black, was she, 에그웨인?”

에그웨인 shook her head.

“I’m still hesitant, Mother,” Bryne said.

에그웨인 restored her weave. “You will let my army enter? You will accept the other 에스 세다이 back in fellowship and will reinstate the 청색 아자?”

“We anticipated these demands,” Andaya said. “They will be met.”

There was silence, the only sound that of the waters lapping against their banks below.

“Then I accept,” 에그웨인 said.

“Mother,” 시우안 said cautiously. “This might be rash. Perhaps you should speak with—”

“It is not rash,” 에그웨인 released her weave and felt a surge of hope. “It is what we’ve wanted.” She eyed 시우안. “Besides. Who are you to lecture me on being rash?” 시우안 looked down. “General, prepare your men to cross, and bring the 의석자들 at the back forward. Send runners back to the 에스 세다이 camp with the news, and make certain your men at the other bridges know to stand down.”

“Yes, Mother.” Bryne wheeled his horse about and gave the necessary orders.

Taking a deep breath, 에그웨인 kicked her horse into motion onto the bridge. 시우안 muttered a fisher’s curse and followed. 에그웨인 could hear 가윈’s horse following as well, then a squad of soldiers obeying a curt command from Bryne.

에그웨인 rode across the waters, hair blowing out behind her, laced with red ribbons. She felt an odd sense of moment—a weight of realization—as she considered what they had all just avoided. It was soon replaced with growing satisfaction and joy.

Her white mare bucked her head slightly, brushing a silky mane across 에그웨인’s hands. On the bridge, the 의석자들 turned to make their way into the city. The Tower rose just ahead. Wounded. Bleeding.

But it still stood. Light, it *stood*!

**C*HAPTER** **46**

![](images/00227.jpg)

To Be Forged Again

After crossing the bridge to 타르 발론 as a victor, the day nearly became a blur for 에그웨인. She hastened to the 백색 탑, 시우안 and 가윈 barely managing to keep up with her. At the Tower, 에그웨인 was met by a group of servants; the 의석자들 themselves were waiting in the Hall for 에그웨인.

The servants led her to an unadorned, wood-paneled chamber set with a pair of leather-padded chairs. 에그웨인 had never been here before; it appeared to be a kind of waiting room near the Hall. It smelled of leather, and a small brazier burned coals in the corner.

Soon, a short, toadlike Brown sister named Lairain entered and instructed 에그웨인 on the proper way to go about the ceremony. The little curly-haired woman seemed completely indifferent to the importance of the moment, and 에그웨인 had never met her before. Likely, she was one of the Browns who spent her life roaming the back library stacks, and only surfaced once a century or so to recite instructions to prospective Amyrlins. 에그웨인 listened carefully; she’d gone through the ceremony once, but it was very complex.

She could still remember her nervousness on that day, months ago, when she’d been raised in Salidar. Back then, she’d still been confused as to what was happening. Her? Amyrlin?

That hesitation was gone. She did not really worry about getting the ceremony wrong. It was only a ceremony, and the important decision had already been made. As 에그웨인 listened to Lairain, she heard 시우안 arguing outside the doors with one of the sisters, claiming that 에그웨인 had already been raised, and that this ceremony wasn’t needed. 에그웨인 quieted Lairain with a raised hand and called out to 시우안.

시우안 peeked in the door.

“I was raised by the rebels, 시우안,” 에그웨인 said sternly. “These women deserve the chance to stand for me as well. Otherwise, I will never have a claim to their loyalty. The ceremony must be performed again.”

시우안 scowled, but nodded. “Very well.”

Lairain opened her mouth to continue instructions, but 에그웨인 silenced her with another motion, earning a huff. “What news have you, 시우안?”

“Well,” 시우안 said, cracking the door a little wider, “Bryne moved most of his troops across the bridges, and has relieved the Tower Guard from their positions at the fortifications, sending them in—along with a number of his own squads—to help put out flareups around the city. The 쇼엔찬 set some homes on fire to cover their retreat as they fled.”

That explained the lack of troops at the barricade—that, along with the knowledge that the Hall was busy debating whether or not to raise 에그웨인. They likely didn’t realize how close they’d come to war.

“What do you want to do with the sisters from your camp?” 시우안 asked. “They’re starting to wonder.”

“Tell them to gather in front of the Sunset Gate,” 에그웨인 said. “Have them stand in ranks by 아자, with 의석자들 in a line at the front. Once I am finished with the ceremony, I will greet them and formally accept their apology for their rebellion and welcome them back into the Tower.”

“Accept their *apology*?” 시우안 asked incredulously.

“They rebelled against the Tower, 시우안,” 에그웨인 said, looking at her. “Whatever the need of what they did, there is reason for apology.”

“But you were with them!”

“I no longer represent just them, 시우안,” 에그웨인 said firmly. “I represent the Tower. The entire Tower. And the Tower needs to know that the rebels regret the division. They needn’t lie and say that they wished they had stayed, but I think it *is* appropriate for them to express sorrow over the hardships the division caused. I will acquit them, and we can get on with healing.”

“Yes, Mother,” 시우안 said in resignation. 에그웨인 caught sight of Tesan standing behind, the woman nodding her 타라본er-braided head at 에그웨인’s words.

에그웨인 let Lairain continue her instructions, then repeated back to her the lines she would have to say and the actions she’d have to take. When the Brown was satisfied, 에그웨인 rose, pulled open the door and found that 시우안 had left to relay her orders. Tesan stood in the hallway outside, arms folded, regarding 가윈. He leaned against the wall a short distance away, his hand resting on the pommel of his sheathed sword.

“Your 감시자?” Tesan asked of 에그웨인.

She regarded 가윈, and was forced to confront a whole mess of emotions. Anger, affection, passion and regret. What a strange mix. “No,” she said. She stared 가윈 in the eyes. “What I am going to do next you cannot be part of, 가윈. Wait here.”

He opened his mouth to object, thought better of it, then stood up stiffly and bowed. That gesture felt even more insolent than an argument would have.

에그웨인 sniffed softly—yet loud enough for him to hear—then allowed Tesan to lead her to the 탑의 회의실. The Hall: both a place and a group of people. For they were one, just as the 아미를린 석좌 was a person, yet was also the chair in which she sat.

She stopped before the doors to the Hall, the dark wood inlaid with the silver Flame of 타르 발론, and felt her heart flutter rebelliously. 시우안 suddenly appeared, with a pair of slippers, gesturing at 에그웨인’s riding boots. Of course; the Hall floor was delicately painted. She changed into the slippers; 시우안 took her boots away. There was no need to be nervous! *I’ve been here before,* she thought suddenly. *Not just in Salidar. In my testing. I’ve faced this door, confronted the women beyond. In my testing . . .*

A gong suddenly sounded; it seemed loud enough to shake the entire Tower, ringing to warn that an Amyrlin was about to be raised. The gong rang again, then again, and those ornate doors swung open. Yes, this was a different experience entirely from the one she’d had back in that humble wooden building where she’d been raised by the Salidar 에스 세다이. In many ways, her performance in Salidar had been but a rehearsal.

The doors finished opening, and 에그웨인 stifled a gasp. The grand, domed room beyond now had a blasted hole—a gaping emptiness—directly across from the entrance. It looked out at 용산. The chamber wasn’t as damaged as some had been in the 쇼엔찬 attack; the rubble was minimal, and the destruction had barely reached past that outer wall. The raised platform still ran around the outside of the room, and the chairs it held were undamaged. Eighteen of them, in clusters of three, each painted and cushioned to declare the 아자 of its inhabitant.

The 아미를린 석좌 stood by the far wall, directly in front of the broken wall, its back to the sprawling landscape beyond and distant 용산. If the 쇼엔찬 blast had gone a few feet farther inward, the Seat would have been destroyed. Thank the Light, it was unmarred.

에그웨인 could faintly smell paint in the air. Had they hurriedly had the Seat repainted to bear all seven colors again? If so, they’d worked quickly. They hadn’t had time to replace the seats of the Blue 의석자들, however.

에그웨인 noted 사에린, 도신 and 유키리 sitting with their respective 아자s. 세인 was there as well, regarding 에그웨인 with those calculating blue eyes. How much power had these four women wielded in these events? Square-faced Suana, of the Yellow, was smiling openly in satisfaction as she regarded 에그웨인, and while most of the faces bore the serene, unemotional faces of 에스 세다이, 에그웨인 sensed approval in their postures. Or, at least, a lack of hostility. More than just the 흑색 아자 hunters had been behind this decision.

사에린 stood up from her chair in the Brown section. “Who comes before the 탑의 회의실?” she asked in a ringing voice.

에그웨인 hesitated, still looking over the 의석자들, their seats arranged around the outer platform, equally spaced. Too many of those chairs were empty. There were only two Green 의석자들; Talene had fled weeks ago. The Gray were missing Evanellein, who had vanished earlier in the day. Velina and Sedore were gone as well. That didn’t bode well; those two were on Verin’s list of 흑색 아자. Had they been warned? Did Evanellein’s disappearance mean Verin had missed her?

There were no Red sisters either. With a start, 에그웨인 remembered that Duhara had left the Tower some weeks before—nobody knew why, but some said it had been on a mission for 엘라이더. Perhaps she was about 흑색 아자 business. The other two red 의석자들, Javindhra and 페바라, had vanished mysteriously.

That left eleven 의석자들. Not enough to raise an Amyrlin by the old laws of the Tower—but those had been revised with 엘라이더’s disbanding of the Blue. Fewer 의석자들 meant fewer women needed to raise an Amyrlin, and now only eleven were required. It would have to do. At least each and every Sitter currently in the Tower knew of this event; it wasn’t in secret, like 엘라이더’s raising. And 에그웨인 could be reasonably certain no Black 의석자들 would stand for her.

사에린 cleared her throat, glancing at 에그웨인 uncertainly, and called again, “Who comes before the 탑의 회의실?”

Tesan leaned in from the side, as if to hiss the proper response to 에그웨인. 에그웨인, however, cut her off by holding up a hand.

There was something 에그웨인 had been considering, something audacious. Yet it was appropriate. She knew that it was. She could *feel* that it was. “The 적색 아자 is in disgrace?” she asked quietly of Tesan.

The White nodded, braided hair brushing the sides of her face. “The Reds, you needn’t worry about them,” she said in her light 타라본er accent. “Following 엘라이더’s disappearance, they retreated back to their quarters. The 의석자들 here, they worried that the Red would choose new 의석자들 quickly and send them to this proceeding. I believe some . . . curt missives from the 탑의 회의실 were enough to cow them.”

“And Silviana Brehon? Still imprisoned?”

“She is, as far as I know, Mother,” Tesan said, slipping for a moment and using the title, though 에그웨인 hadn’t been formally raised by the Hall yet. “Don’t worry, 리안—she has been freed. We had her escorted out to stand with the other rebels, awaiting your forgiveness.”

에그웨인 nodded thoughtfully. “Have Silviana brought here, to the 탑의 회의실, immediately.”

Tesan’s brow wrinkled. “Mother, I don’t think this is the time—”

“Just do it,” 에그웨인 hissed, then turned to face the Hall. “One who comes obediently, in the Light,” she pronounced in a firm voice.

사에린 relaxed. “Who comes before the 탑의 회의실?”

“One who comes humbly, in the Light,” 에그웨인 responded. She stared at each of the 의석자들. A firm hand. She would have to be firm. They needed leadership.

“Who comes before the 탑의 회의실?” 사에린 finished.

“One who comes at the summons of the Hall,” 에그웨인 said, “obedient and humble in the Light, asking only to accept the will of the Hall.”

The ceremony proceeded, each of the 의석자들 stripping to the waist to prove she was a woman. 에그웨인 did the same, and barely gave a blush at the thought of 가윈, who had clearly thought she should bring him along to the event.

“Who stands for this woman?” 사에린 asked after the 의석자들 had re-dressed. 에그웨인 had to remain stripped to the waist for now, and the cool breeze through the broken wall was chill on her skin. “And pledges for her, heart for heart, soul for soul, life for life?”

유키리, 세인 and Suana stood quickly. “I so pledge,” each of them announced.

The first time 에그웨인 had experienced this ceremony, she had been in shock. At each step, she’d been terrified she’d make an error. Worse, she’d been terrified that it would all turn out to be a ruse or a mistake.

That fear was gone. As the ritual questions were asked—as 에그웨인 stepped forward three steps and knelt on the smooth floor, repainted by 엘라이더’s order with only six colors spiraling out of the mark of the Flame of 타르 발론—에그웨인 saw through the pomp and looked at the core of what was happening. These women were terrified. As had been the women in Salidar. The 아미를린 석좌 was a force of stability, and they reached for it.

Why had she been chosen? Both times, it seemed the same answer. Because she was the only one they could all agree upon. There were smiling faces in this group. But they were the smiles of women who had succeeded in keeping rivals off of the Seat. Either that, or they were the smiles of women who were relieved that *someone* was stepping up to take leadership. And, perhaps, there were some who smiled because they weren’t the ones who had to take the Seat. Its recent history had been fraught with danger, dissension, and two dramatic tragedies.

Originally, in Salidar, 에그웨인 had thought the women were being idiots. She was more experienced now, and hopefully wiser as well. She could see that they hadn’t been fools. They’d been 에스 세다이—covering their fear by being overly cautious, yet brazen at the same time. Choosing someone they wouldn’t mind seeing fall. Taking a risk, but not putting themselves in direct danger.

These women were doing the same. They covered their fear with smooth faces and acts of control. When the time came for the 의석자들 to stand in her support, 에그웨인 was not surprised that all eleven rose to their feet. Not a single dissent. There would be no foot washing during this ceremony.

No, she was not surprised. They knew that there was no other option, not with an army on their doorstep, not with 엘라이더 as good as dead. The 에스 세다이 thing to do was act as if there had never been any argument. The consensus must be reached.
사에린 looked surprised that nobody had chosen to remain seated, if only to prove that she would not be bullied. In fact, more than one of the 의석자들 seemed surprised, and 에그웨인 suspected that they were regretting their decision to stand up so quickly. One could gain some measure of power by being the only person who remained seated, forcing 에그웨인 to wash her feet and ask for permission to serve. Of course, that also could have singled the woman out, and earned her the dislike of the new Amyrlin.

The women slowly took their seats. 에그웨인 needed no guidance, and none was offered. She rose and strode across the hall, her slippered feet silent on the painted stone of the Flame. A gust of wind blew through the room, ruffling shawls, blowing across 에그웨인’s bare skin. It said something for the strength of the Hall that they had chosen to meet here, despite the dizzying view out of the far wall.

사에린 met 에그웨인 at the Seat. The olive-skinned 알타라n began to button 에그웨인’s bodice with careful fingers, then reverently lifted the Amyrlin’s stole from the Seat. It was the one with all seven colors, recovered from wherever 엘라이더 had discarded it. 사에린 regarded 에그웨인 for a moment, hefting the stole, as if judging it.

“Are you certain you want to bear this weight, child?” 사에린 asked in a very soft voice. This was not part of the ceremony.

“I bear it already, 사에린.” 에그웨인’s reply was almost a whisper. “엘라이더 cast it aside when she tried to slice it and divide it as she wished. I took it up and have carried it since. I would bear it to my death. And will.”

사에린 nodded. “I think that might be why you deserve it,” she said. “I doubt anything in the histories will compare to the days ahead. I suspect that, in the future, scholars will look back on our days and judge them to be more difficult—more trying of mind, body and soul—than the Time of 광기 or the Breaking itself.”

“Then it’s a good thing the world has us, isn’t it?” 에그웨인 asked.

사에린 hesitated, then nodded. “I suppose it is at that.” She raised the stole and set it upon 에그웨인’s shoulders. “You are raised to the 아미를린 석좌!” she declared, the voices of the other 의석자들 joining in, “In the glory of the Light, that the 백색 탑 may endure forever. 에그웨인 al’Vere, the Watcher of the 봉인, the Flame of 타르 발론, the *아미를린 석좌*!”

에그웨인 turned to regard the group of women, then sat down in the chair. She felt as if she had returned home after a very long journey. The world bowed beneath the stress of the 어둠의 존재’s touch, but it felt a little more right—a little more secure—the moment she took her place.

The women arranged themselves before her in order of age, with 사에린 at the very end. One at a time they curtsied deeply before her, asked her permission to serve, then kissed her Great Serpent ring and stepped aside. As they did so, 에그웨인 noticed that Tesan had finally returned. She peeked in to be certain everyone was dressed, then returned a moment later leading a group of four guards with the Flame of 타르 발론 burning white on their chests. 에그웨인 suppressed a sigh. They’d brought Silviana in chains, it appeared.

After kissing her ring, the 의석자들 returned to their chairs. There was some little more to the ceremony, but the important part was through with. 에그웨인 was Amyrlin, really and truly, at long last. She had waited so long for this moment.

Now it was time for some surprises.

“Release the prisoner’s chains,” 에그웨인 said.

Reluctantly, the soldiers outside the room did as demanded, the metal clinking. The 의석자들 turned with confused expressions.

“Silviana Brehon!” 에그웨인 declared, standing up. “You may approach the 아미를린 석좌.”

The soldiers stepped aside and allowed Silviana to enter. Her red dress had once been fine, but she had not been well treated by 엘라이더’s confinement. Her black hair—normally kept in a bun—was instead coarsely braided. Her dress was rumpled, the knees dirty. And yet her square face was serene.

Surprisingly, she knelt before 에그웨인 after walking across the room. 에그웨인 lowered her hand and let the woman kiss her ring.
