The 의석자들 watched, confused that 에그웨인 had broken the ceremony. “Mother,” 유키리 finally asked. “Is this the best time to be dispensing judgment?”

에그웨인 withdrew her hand from the kneeling Silviana and looked directly at 유키리, then turned her gaze across the waiting 의석자들. “You all bear a great deal of shame,” she said.

Stiff-faced 에스 세다이 raised eyebrows and opened eyes wider. They seemed angry. They had no right! Their anger was nothing beside hers.

“This,” 에그웨인 said, gesturing toward the broken wall. “You bear responsibility for this.” She pointed at Silviana, still kneeling. “You bear responsibility for *this*. You bear responsibility for the way our sisters regard one another in the halls, and you bear responsibility for letting the Tower remain so long in division. Many of you bear responsibility for that division on the first place!

“You are a *disgrace*. The 백색 탑—the pride of the Light, the power for stability and truth since the 전설의 시대—has nearly been shattered because of you.”

Eyes bugged out, and a few women choked in shock. “엘라이더—” one began.

“엘라이더 was a madwoman, and you all know it!” 에그웨인 said sternly, standing tall, staring them down. “You knew it these last few months as she worked unwittingly to destroy us. Light, many of you probably knew it when you *raised* her in the first place!

“There have been foolish Amyrlins before, but none have come as close to tearing down the entire Tower! *You* are a check upon the Amyrlin. *You* are to keep her from doing things like this! *You* allowed her to disband an entire 아자? What were you *thinking*? How is it that you allowed the Tower to fall so far? And when the *용의 환생* himself walks the land, no less!

“You should have removed 엘라이더 the moment you heard of her disastrous attempt to confine 랜드 al’Thor. You should have removed her when you saw how her bickering and pettiness was turning 아자s against one another. And you should *certainly* have removed her when she refused to do what was needed to bring the Tower together again, whole as one!”

에그웨인 looked down the lines of sisters, staring at each one in turn, meeting each set of eyes until they looked away. None dared hold her gaze for long. Finally, she saw shame begin to peek through their masks. As well it should!

“None of you would stand up to her,” 에그웨인 spat. “You *dare* call yourself the 탑의 회의실? You who were cowed? You who were too frightened to do what was needed? You who were too caught up in your own squabbles and politicking to *see* what was needed?”

에그웨인 looked down at Silviana. “Only one woman in this room was willing to stand up for what she knew to be right. Only one woman dared defy 엘라이더, and she accepted the price of doing so. And you think I brought this woman here to exact *vengeance* on her? Are you really so blinded that you think I’d punish the only person in the entire Tower who did anything of decency these last few months?”

They were all looking down, now. Even 사에린 wouldn’t meet her eyes.

Silviana looked up at her.

“You did your duty, Silviana,” 에그웨인 said. “And you did it well. Rise.”

The woman stood. She looked haggard, eyes puffy from lack of sleep, and 에그웨인 suspected she was having trouble standing. Had anyone seen to bringing her food or water during the chaos of the last few days?

“Silviana,” 에그웨인 said, “a new Amyrlin has been raised. And, it shames me to say, it was done with subterfuge similar to 엘라이더’s raising. Of the seven 아자s, only five were represented. The Blue I know would support me, were they here. But the Red were not even given a chance to voice their dissent or approval.”

“There are good reasons for that, Mother,” Silviana said.

“That may be true,” 에그웨인 said, “but it all but ensures that my reign will be marked with tension between myself and the Red. They will perceive ill will where there is none, and I will lose the strength of hundreds of women. Women that will be sorely needed.”

“I . . . don’t see any way around that, Mother,” Silviana said, honestly.

“I do,” 에그웨인 said. “Silviana Brehon, I would have you as my 연대기 수호자. Let it not be said that I spurned the Red.”

Silviana blinked in surprise. There were a few gasps from the 의석자들, though 에그웨인 did not mark whose they were.

She stared Silviana in the eyes. Just a short time ago, this woman had had 에그웨인 over the side of the desk, paddling her at 엘라이더’s command. But Silviana now knelt; she had done so without needing an order. She accepted the Hall’s authority to raise 에그웨인. Did she accept 에그웨인 herself?

에그웨인’s offer would place her on a difficult and dangerous road. The Reds might see it as a betrayal. What would Silviana’s response be? 에그웨인 blessed the trick that kept her from sweating, otherwise she knew that drops would have been trickling down the sides of her face.

“I would be honored, Mother,” Silviana said, kneeling again. “Truly honored.”

에그웨인 let out a breath. Her task of reuniting the fractured 아자s would be difficult—but if the Reds saw her as an enemy, it would be nearly impossible. With Silviana on her side, she would have an envoy to the Reds who would not be rejected. Hopefully.

“This will be a difficult time for the 적색 아자, daughter,” 에그웨인 said. “Their nature has always been to capture men who can channel, but reports claim that *세이딘* is cleansed.”

“There will still be rogue channelers, Mother,” Silviana said. “And men are not to be trusted.”

*Someday, we will have to move beyond that last sentiment,* 에그웨인 thought. *But for now, it is true enough to let stand.* “I didn’t say that your purpose would vanish, only that it would change. I see great things for the 적색 아자 in the future—an expanding of vision, a renewal of duty. I am pleased to have you at my side to help guide them.”

에그웨인 looked up at the 의석자들, who were watching in stunned silence. “I’d order you all to do penance,” 에그웨인 said, “save for the fact that I know some of you, at least, were working behind the scenes to stop the crumbling of the 백색 탑. You didn’t do enough, but you did something. Beyond that, I think that the penance we often demand of ourselves is ridiculous. What is physical pain to 에스 세다이?”

에그웨인 took a deep breath. “And I am not guiltless either. I share some of your shame, for it was during my tenure that these disasters occurred. I sided with the rebels, allowed myself to be raised by them because it was the only choice. But that choice still gives me culpability.

“Bear your shame, 의석자들, but bear it with determination. Do not let it break you. The time for healing has begun, and there is no longer any use in pointing fingers. You failed. But you are all that we have. *We* are all that the world has.”

The women began to look up.

“Come,” 에그웨인 said, striding through the room, Silviana smoothly falling into step beside her. “Let us greet the rebels.”

They passed through the hallways of the Tower, which still smelled of smoke and were strewn with rubble in places. 에그웨인 tried not to look at the bloodstains. The 의석자들 followed behind, clustering in 아자 groups, despite 에그웨인’s recent chastisement. There would still be a lot of work to heal them.

“Mother,” Silviana said quietly as they walked, “I can only assume that you had a Keeper already, among the rebels. Do you intend to maintain two of us?” Her tense voice revealed what she thought of such an unconventional arrangement.

“No,” 에그웨인 said. “My previous Keeper was executed for being of the 흑색 아자.”

Silviana paled. “I see.”

“We can’t dance around these things, Silviana,” 에그웨인 said. “I received a very important visitor just before my . . . rescue. She was of the Black, and betrayed to me the names of other Black sisters. I have confirmed each of those who were among the rebel 에스 세다이 through use of the 맹세 막대.”

“The 맹세 막대?” Silviana exclaimed.

“Yes,” 에그웨인 said as they entered a stairwell. “I was given it last night by an ally in the Tower. Though, it occurs to me that we’ll have to move the room with the *ter’angreal*. And keep the location secret and constantly warded. It won’t be long before every sister with sufficient power knows the weave for 이동, and I wouldn’t put it past many of them—including those I trust—to ‘borrow’ *angreal* now and again.”

“Yes, Mother,” Silviana said. Then, in a quieter voice. “I’m going to have to get used to a lot of things changing, I suspect.”

“I’m afraid so,” 에그웨인 said. “Not the least of which will be the need to choose a proper 수련생 감독관, one who can deal with hundreds of new initiates—many of whom are not of the standard age. I’ve already begun the process of accepting for training any woman, no matter how old, who shows some measure of ability with channeling. I suspect that before long, the 백색 탑 will be bursting at the seams with 수련생s.”

“I shall consider suggestions for a replacement quickly then, Mother,” Silviana said.

에그웨인 nodded in approval. Romanda and Lelaine would undoubtedly be livid when they discovered what 에그웨인 had done in choosing Silviana, but the more she considered it, the more satisfied 에그웨인 was. Not just because Silviana was Red, but because she was so capable. 사에린 would have been a fair choice, but many would have seen her as being 에그웨인’s guide, and perhaps the real power behind the Seat. Picking a Blue would have been too divisive for the current state of the Tower. And besides, with an Amyrlin who was one of the rebels—nobody would soon forget that, no matter what 에그웨인 said or did—it would go a long way toward healing relations to have a Keeper who had been a loyalist.

Before long, they reached the Tower’s Great Square, on the east side of the building. The square was filled—as per her orders—by women in ranks by 아자. 에그웨인 had chosen this position because of the tall steps leading up to the Tower, topped by a spacious landing. She stood there, back to the majestically carved doors. It was a perfect location from which to address a crowd.

It was also situated between the wings, which had taken the worst damage during the attack the previous night. The east wing still smoldered; the dome had collapsed; one of the walls had fallen in. However, from this vantage, the Tower itself was relatively free of scars, and neither of the gaping holes was directly visible.

에그웨인 could see faces lining the lower windows. 에스 세다이 and 수련생s alike watched her. It seemed that in addition to the rebels, 에그웨인 had an opportunity to address the majority of the remaining occupants of the Tower. She made a weave to enhance her voice. Not to booming levels, but enough to let her be heard both from behind and below.

“Sisters,” she said, “daughters. I have been raised properly to the 아미를린 석좌. Both sides of this conflict have chosen me. Both followed the prescribed methods, and both now accept me as their Amyrlin. It is time to join together again.

“I will not pretend that our division did not take place. We of the 백색 탑 are sometimes too eager to forget those facts we don’t want to acknowledge. This one cannot be hidden, not from us who lived it. We were divided. We nearly came to war with one another. We have disgraced ourselves.

“You rebels before me have done something terrible. You have shattered the Tower and raised up a rival Amyrlin. For the first time, troops have been marshaled by 에스 세다이 against 에스 세다이. I led those troops. I know of this shame.

“Necessary or not, it *is* a shame. And so it is that I require your admission of guilt. You must take responsibility for your crimes, even those performed in the name of the greater good.”

She looked down at the 에스 세다이 below. If her action of forcing them into ranks—then making them wait upon her will—hadn’t made them aware of her attitude, then perhaps her words would.

“You did not come here in glory,” 에그웨인 said to them. “You did not come here victorious. For there *is* no victory, and could have been no victory, when sister fought sister and 감시자 died to 감시자.” She noted 시우안 standing near the front of the ranks and met her eyes across the distance. 리안 was there, too, looking disheveled from her long imprisonment, but standing erect.

“Mistakes have been made on both sides,” 에그웨인 said. “And we will all have to work hard to repair what we have done. It is said by blacksmiths that a sword can never be whole again once it has been shattered. It must be completely reforged, the metal melted down to slag, then reworked and re-formed.

“These next few months will be our re-forming. We have been broken, then torn down nearly to roots. 최후의 전투 approaches, and before it arrives, I mean to see that we are once again a sword forged with strength, whole and unbroken! I will make demands of you. They will be harsh. They will stretch you to the limits of what you think you can bear. I will take these burned holes and fill them! Accommodations will have to be made, for between us there are far too many 의석자들 for the Hall, not to mention five too many 아자 heads. Some of you will have to step down and bow yourselves in humility before those you dislike.

“These days will test you! I will force you to work with those you saw as enemies just hours ago. You will march alongside those who spurned you, or hurt you, or hated you.

“But we are stronger than our weaknesses. The 백색 탑 stands, and we shall stand with it! We *will* become one again. We will be an assembly that tales will tell of! When I am finished with you, it will not be written that the 백색 탑 was weak. Our divisions will be forgotten in the face of our victories. We will be remembered not as the 백색 탑 who turned against itself, but as the 백색 탑 who stood strong in the face of the Shadow. These days will be *legendary*!”

Cheers burst out, mostly from 수련생s and soldiers, as the 에스 세다이 were too reserved for that sort of behavior. Generally. Some younger ones did call out, caught up in the moment. Thankfully, those cheers came from both sides. 에그웨인 let them roar for a moment, then raised her arms, quieting them.

“Let it go forth across the land!” she shouted. “Let it be spoken of, let it be relied upon, and let it be remembered. The 백색 탑 is whole and complete. And no one—man, woman or creation of the Shadow—will see us divided again!”

The cheers were nearly deafening this time, and surprisingly, more 에스 세다이 joined in. 에그웨인 lowered her hands.

She hoped they would still cheer her in the months to come. There was a great deal of work to be done.

**C*HAPTER** **47**

![](images/00286.jpg)

The One He Lost

랜드 did not return to his rooms immediately. The failed meeting with the Borderlanders had left him feeling unhinged. Not because of their tricky attempt to pull him into Far Madding—that was frustrating, but it was not unexpected. People always tried to control and manipulate him. The Borderlanders were no different.

No, it was something else that had unsettled him, something he couldn’t quite define. And so he stalked through the Stone of 티어, two 아일 Maidens trailing behind him, his presence startling servants and unnerving Defenders.

The corridors twisted and turned. The walls—where unadorned by tapestry—were the color of wet sand, but they were far stronger than any rock 랜드 knew, alien and strange; each smooth span a reminder that this place was not natural.

랜드 felt the same way. He had the form of a human. Indeed, he had the mannerisms and history of one. But he was a thing that no human—not even he himself—could understand. A figure of legend, a creation of the 하나의 힘, as unnatural as a *ter’angreal* or a fragment of *cuendillar*. They dressed him up like a king, just as they dressed these corridors with tasseled gold and red rugs. Just as they hung the walls with those tapestries, each one depicting a famous 타이런 general. Those decorations were intended for beauty, but they were also intended to obscure. The patches of naked wall highlighted how alien the place was. Rugs and tapestries made it all feel more . . . human. Just as giving 랜드 a crown and a fine coat allowed them to accept him. Kings were supposed to be a little different. Never mind his much more alien nature, hidden beneath the crown. Never mind his heart of a man long dead, his shoulders created to bear the weight of prophecy, his soul crushed by the needs, wants and hopes of a million people.

Two hands. One to destroy, the other to save. Which had he lost?

It was easy to go astray in the Stone. Long before the Pattern had begun to unravel, these twisting corridors of brown rock had been misleading. They were designed to befuddle attackers. Intersections came unexpectedly; there were few landmarks, and the inner corridors of the keep didn’t have windows. The 아일 said they had been impressed with how difficult it had been to seize the Stone. It hadn’t been the Defenders who had impressed them, but the sheer scope and layout of the monstrous building.

Fortunately, 랜드 had no particular goal. He simply wanted to walk.

He had *accepted* what he needed to be. Why was he so bothered by it, then? A voice deep down—one not in his head, but in his heart—had begun to disagree with what he did. It was not loud or violent like 르웨어스 테린’s; it just whispered, like a forgotten itch. Something is wrong. Something is wrong. . . .

*No!* he thought. *I must be strong. I have finally become what I must be!*

He stopped in the corridor, teeth gritted. In his deep coat pocket, he carried the access key. He fingered it, its contours cold and smooth. He didn’t dare leave it to the care of a servant, no matter how trusted.

*Hurin,* he realized. *That’s what is bothering me. Seeing Hurin.*

He resumed walking, straightening his back. He had to be strong—or at least appear strong—at all times.

Hurin was a relic from an earlier life. Days when 맷 had still mocked 랜드’s coats, days when 랜드 had hoped that he’d marry 에그웨인 and somehow return to the 두 강. He had traveled with Hurin and 로이알, determined to stop Fain and get back 맷’s dagger, to prove that he was a friend. That had been a much simpler time, although 랜드 hadn’t known it. He’d have wondered if anything could grow more complicated than thinking his friends hated him.

The colors shifted in his vision. 페린 walking through a dark camp, that stone sword looming in the air above him. The vision changed to 맷, who was still in that city. It was Caemlyn? Why could he be near 엘레인, when 랜드 had to remain so far away? He could barely feel her emotions through the bond. He missed her so. Once they had stolen kisses from one another in the halls of this very fortress.

*No,* he thought. *I am strong.* Longing was an emotion he mustn’t feel. Nostalgia got him nowhere. He tried to banish both, ducking into a stairwell and moving down the steps, working his body, trying to make his breath come in gasps.

*Do we run from the past, then?* 르웨어스 테린 asked softly. *Yes. That is well. Better to run than to face it.*

랜드’s time with Hurin had ended at Falme. Those days were indistinct in his mind. The changes that had come upon him then—realizing that he had to kill, that he could never return to the life he had loved—were things he could not dwell on. He’d headed out toward 티어, almost delirious, separated from his friends, seeing 이샤마엘 in his dreams.

That last one was happening again.

랜드 burst out onto one of the lower floors of the keep, breathing deeply. His Maidens followed him, not winded. He strode down the hallway and into a massive chamber with rows of pillars, stout and broad, wider than a man could wrap his arms around. The Heart of the Stone. Several Defenders came to attention and saluted as 랜드 passed them.

He walked to the center of the Heart. Once, *칼란도르* had hung here, glistening with light. The crystal sword was now in Cadsuane’s possession. Hopefully, she hadn’t bungled that and lost *it* as she had the male *a’dam*. 랜드 didn’t really care. *칼란도르* was inferior; to use it, a man had to subject himself to the will of a woman. Besides, it was powerful, but not nearly as powerful as the 초에단 칼. The access key was a much better tool. 랜드 stroked it quietly, regarding the place where *칼란도르* had once hung.

This had always bothered him. *칼란도르* was the weapon spoken of in the prophecies. The 카라에손 순환 said that the Stone would not fall until *칼란도르* was wielded by the 용의 환생. To some scholars, that passage had implied that the sword would *never* be wielded. But the prophecies did not work that way—they were made to be fulfilled.

랜드 had studied the Karaethon 예언. Unfortunately, teasing out its meaning was like trying to untie a hundred yards of tangled rope. With one hand.

Taking the Sword That Cannot Be Touched was one of the first major prophecies that he had fulfilled. But was his taking of *칼란도르* a meaningless sign, or was it a step? Everyone knew the prophecy, but few asked the question that should have been inevitable. Why? *Why* did 랜드 have to take up the sword? Was it to be used in the Last Battle?

The sword was inferior as a *sa’angreal*, and he doubted that it was intended to be used simply as a sword. Why did the prophecies not speak of the 초에단 칼? He had used *those* to cleanse the taint. The access key gave 랜드 power well beyond what *칼란도르* could provide, and that power came with no strings. The statuette was freedom, but *칼란도르* was just another box. Yet talk of the 초에단 칼 and their keys was absent from the prophecies.

랜드 found that frustrating, for the prophecies were—in a way—the grandest and most stifling box of them all. He was trapped inside of them. Eventually, they would suffocate him.

*I told them . . .* 르웨어스 테린 whispered.

*Told them what?* 랜드 demanded.

*That the plan would not work,* 르웨어스 테린 said, voice very soft. *That brute force would not contain him. They called my plan brash, but these weapons they created, they were too dangerous. Too frightening. No man should hold such Power . . .*

랜드 struggled with the thoughts, the voice, the memories. He couldn’t recall much at all of 르웨어스 테린’s plan to Seal the 어둠의 존재’s prison. The 초에단 칼—had they been built for that purpose?

Was that the answer? Had 르웨어스 테린 made the wrong choice? Why, then, was there no mention of them in the prophecies?

랜드 turned to leave the empty chamber. “Guard this place no more,” he said to the Defenders. “There is nothing here of worth. I’m not sure if there ever was.”

The men looked shocked, mortified, like children just chastised by a beloved father. But there was a war coming, and he wouldn’t leave soldiers behind to defend an empty room.

랜드 gritted his teeth and strode into a hallway. *칼란도르*. Where had Cadsuane hidden it? He knew she’d taken rooms in the Stone, again pushing the limits of his exile. He would have to do something about that. Cast her from the Stone, perhaps. He hurried up the stone steps, then left the stairwell on a random floor, continuing to *move*. Sitting now would drive him mad.

He worked so hard to keep from being tied with strings, but at the end of the day, the prophecies would see that he did what he was supposed to. They were more manipulative, more devious, than any 에스 세다이.
His anger welled up inside him, raging against its constraints. The quiet voice deep within shivered at the tempest. 랜드 leaned his left arm against the wall, bowing his head, teeth gritted.

“I will be strong,” he whispered. And yet, the anger would not go away. And why should it? The Borderlanders defied him. The 쇼엔찬 defied him. The 에스 세다이 pretended to obey him, yet dined with Cadsuane behind his back and danced at her command.

Cadsuane defied him most of all. Staying right near him, flouting his words of command and twisting his intentions. He pulled out the access key, fingering it. 최후의 전투 loomed, and he spent what little time he had riding to meetings with people who insulted him. 어둠의 존재 was unraveling the Pattern more each day, and those sworn to protect the borders were hiding in Far Madding.

He glanced around, breathing deeply. Something about this particular hallway seemed familiar. He wasn’t certain why; it looked like all of the others. Rugs of gold and red. An intersection of hallways ahead.

Maybe he shouldn’t have let the Borderlanders survive their defiance. Perhaps he should go back and see that they learned to fear him. But no. He didn’t need them. He could leave them for the 쇼엔찬. That Borderlander army would serve to slow his enemies here in the south. Perhaps that would keep the 쇼엔찬 from his flanks while he dealt with the 어둠의 존재.

But . . . was there, perhaps, a way to stop the 쇼엔찬 for good? He looked down at the access key. Once he had tried to use *칼란도르* to fight the foreign invaders. He hadn’t yet understood why the sword was so difficult to control: only after his disastrous assault had Cadsuane explained what she knew about it. 랜드 needed to be in a circle with two women before he could safely wield the sword that was not a sword.

That had been his first major failure as a commander.

But he had a better tool now. The most powerful tool ever created; surely no human could hold more of the 하나의 힘 than he had when cleansing *세이딘*. Burning 그랜달 and Natrin’s Barrow away had required only a fraction of what 랜드 could summon.

If he turned *that* against the 쇼엔찬, then he could go to the Last Battle with confidence, no longer worried about what was creeping along behind him. He had given them their chance. Several chances. He had warned Cadsuane, told her that he’d bind the Daughter of the Nine Moons to him. One way . . . or another.

It would not take long.

*There,* 르웨어스 테린 said. *We stood there.*

랜드 frowned. What was the madman babbling about? He glanced around. The wide hallway’s floor was tiled in red and black patterns. A few tapestries fluttered on the walls. With shock, 랜드 realized that several of them depicted *him*, taking the Stone, holding *칼란도르*, killing 트롤록s.

*Fighting the 쇼엔찬 wasn’t our first failure,* 르웨어스 테린 whispered. *No, our first failure happened here. In this hallway.*

Exhausted, following the battle with the 트롤록s and 미르드랄. His side throbbing. The Stone still ringing with the cries of the wounded. Feeling he could do anything. *Anything.*

Standing above the corpse of a young girl. Just a child. *칼란도르* glowing in his fingers. The body suddenly jerked.

모이라인 had stopped him. Bringing life to the dead was beyond him, she’d said.

*How I wish she was still here,* 랜드 thought. He had often been frustrated with her, but she—more than anyone else—had seemed to grasp just what it was he was expected to do. She’d made him more willing to do it, even when he’d been angry with her.

He turned away. 모이라인 had been right. He could not bring life to those who were dead. But he was *very* good at bringing death to those who lived. “Gather your spear-sisters,” 랜드 called over his shoulder to his 아일 guards. “We are going to battle.”

“Now?” one of them asked. “It is nightfall!”

*Have I been walking that long?* 랜드 thought with surprise. “Yes,” he said. “The darkness won’t matter; I shall create light enough.” He fingered the access key, feeling a thrill and a horror at the same time. He had driven the 쇼엔찬 back into the ocean once. He would do so again. Alone.

Yes, he would drive them back—at least, the ones he left alive.

“Go!” he shouted at the Maidens. They left him, loping down the hallway. What had happened to his control? The ice had grown thin lately.

He walked back to the stairway and climbed a few flights up toward his rooms. The 쇼엔찬 would know his fury. They dared to provoke the 용의 환생? He offered them peace, and they *laughed* at him?

He threw open the door to his rooms, silencing the eager Defenders on guard outside with a sharply upraised hand. He was not in the mood for their prattle.

He stormed inside, and was annoyed to find that the guards had allowed someone inside. An unfamiliar figure stood with his back to 랜드, looking out the open balcony doors. “What—” 랜드 began.

The man turned. It was *not* a stranger. Not a stranger at all.

It was Tam. His father.

랜드 stumbled back. Was this an apparition? Some twisted trick of the 어둠의 존재? But no, it was Tam. There was no mistaking the man’s kindly eyes. Though he was a head shorter than 랜드, Tam had always seemed more solid than the world around him. His broad chest and steady legs could not be moved, not because he was strong—랜드 had met many men of greater strength during his travels. Strength was fleeting. Tam was *real*. Certain and stable. Just looking at him brought comfort.

But comfort clashed with who 랜드 had become. His worlds met—the person he had been, the person he had become—like a jet of water on a white-hot stone. One shattering, the other turning to steam.

Tam stood, hesitant, in the balcony doorway, lit by two flickering lamps on stands in the room. 랜드 understood Tam’s hesitation. They were not blood father and son. 랜드’s blood father had been Janduin, clan chief of the Taardad 아일. Tam was just the man who had found 랜드 on the slopes of 용산.

Just the man who had raised him. Just the man who had taught him everything he knew. Just the man 랜드 loved and revered, and always would, no matter what their blood connection.

“랜드.” Tam’s voice was awkward.

“Please,” 랜드 said through his shock. “Please sit.”

Tam nodded. He closed the balcony doors, then walked forward and took one of the chairs. 랜드 sat, too. They stared across the room at one another. The stone walls were bare; 랜드 preferred them unornamented with tapestries or paintings. The rug was yellow and red, and so large it reached to all four walls.

The room felt too perfect. A vase of freshly cut dara lilies and calima blossoms sat there, right where it should. Chairs in the center, arranged too correctly. The room didn’t look *lived* in. Like so many places he stayed, it wasn’t home. He hadn’t truly had a home since he’d left the 두 강.

Tam sat in one chair, 랜드 in another. 랜드 realized he still had the access key in his hand, so he set it on the sun-patterned rug before him. Tam glanced at 랜드’s stump, but said nothing. He clenched his hands together, probably wishing he had something to work on. Tam was always more comfortable talking about uncomfortable things when he had something to do with his hands, whether it be checking the straps on a harness or shearing a sheep.

*Light,* 랜드 thought, feeling a sudden urge to enfold Tam in a hug. Familiarity and memories flooded back into his mind. Tam delivering brandy to the Winespring Inn for Bel Tine. The pleasure Tam took in his pipe. His patience and his kindness. His unexpected heron-mark sword. *I know him so well. And yet I’ve rarely thought of him recently.*

“How . . .” 랜드 said. “Tam, how did you get here? How did you find me?”

Tam chuckled quietly. “You’ve been sending nonstop messengers to all the great cities these last few days, telling them to marshal their armies for war. I think a man would have to be blind, deaf *and* drunk not to know where to find you.”

“But my messengers haven’t gone to the 두 강!”

“I wasn’t in the 두 강,” Tam said. “Some of us have been fighting alongside 페린.”

*Of course,* 랜드 thought. 니나브 must have contacted 페린—the colors swirled—she was so worried about him and 맷. It would have been easy for Tam to come back with her.

Was 랜드 really having this conversation? He had given up on returning to the 두 강, on ever seeing his father again. It felt so good, despite the awkwardness. Tam’s face held more lines than it had before, and the few determined streaks of black in his hair had finally given in and gone silver, but he was the same.

So many people had changed around 랜드—맷, 페린, 에그웨인, 니나브—it was a wonder to meet someone from his old life who was the same. Tam, the man who had taught 랜드 to seek the void. Tam was a rock that seemed to him stronger than the Stone itself.

랜드’s mood darkened slightly. “Wait. 페린 has been using 두 강 folk?”

Tam nodded. “He needed us. That boy’s put on a balancing act to impress any menagerie performer. What with the 쇼엔찬 and the Prophet’s men, not to mention the 백의단 and the queen—”

“The queen?” 랜드 said.

“Aye,” Tam said. “Though she says she’s not queen anymore. 엘레인’s mother.”

“She *lives*, then?” 랜드 asked.

“She does, little thanks to the 백의단,” Tam said with distaste.

“Has she seen 엘레인?” 랜드 asked. “You mentioned 백의단—how did he run into 백의단?” Tam began to answer, but 랜드 held up his hand. “No. Wait. I can get a report from 페린 when I wish it. I will not have our time together spent with you acting the messenger.”

Tam smiled faintly.

“What?” 랜드 asked.

“Ah, son,” he said, shaking his head, broad hardworking hands clasped before him, “they’ve really done it. They’ve gone and made a king out of you. What happened to the gangly boy, so wide-eyed at Bel Tine? Where’s the uncertain lad I raised all those years?”

“He’s dead,” 랜드 said immediately.

Tam nodded slowly. “I can see that. You . . . must know then. . . . About. . . .”

“That you’re not my father?” 랜드 guessed.

Tam nodded, looking down.

“I’ve known since the day I left Emond’s Field,” 랜드 replied. “You spoke of it in your fever dreams. I refused to believe it for a time, but I was eventually persuaded.”

“Yes,” Tam said. “I can see how. I. . . .” He gripped his hands together tightly. “I never meant to lie to you, son. Or, well, I guess I shouldn’t call you that, should I?”

*You can call me son,* 랜드 thought. *You are my father. No matter what some may say.* But he couldn’t force the words out.

The 용의 환생 couldn’t have a father. A father would be a weakness to be exploited, even more than a woman like 민. Lovers were expected. But the 용의 환생 had to be a figure of myth, a creature nearly as large as the Pattern itself. He had difficulty getting people to obey as it was. What would it do if it were known that he kept his father nearby? If it were known that the 용의 환생 relied upon the strength of a shepherd?

The quiet voice in his heart was screaming.

“You did well, Tam,” 랜드 found himself saying. “By keeping the truth from me, you likely saved my life. If people had known that I was a foundling, and discovered near 용산 no less—well, word would have spread. I might very well have been assassinated as a child.”

“Oh,” Tam said. “Well, then, I’m glad I did it.”

랜드 picked up the access key—it too brought him comfort—then stood. Tam hastily joined him, acting more and more like just another retainer or servant.

“You have done a great service, Tam al’Thor,” 랜드 said. “By protecting and raising me, you have ushered in a new Age. The world owes you a debt. I will see that you are cared for the rest of your life.”

“I appreciate that, my Lord,” Tam said. “But it isn’t necessary. I have what I need.”

Was he hiding a grin? Perhaps it *had* been a pompous speech. The room felt stifling, and 랜드 turned, crossing the fine rug and throwing open the balcony doors again. The sun had indeed set, and darkness had fallen on the city. A crisp ocean breeze blew across him as he stepped out to the balcony railing, into the night.

Tam stepped up beside him.

“I’m afraid I lost your sword,” 랜드 found himself saying. It felt foolish.

“That’s all right,” Tam said. “I don’t know that I ever deserved the thing anyway.”

“Were you really a blademaster?”

Tam nodded. “I suppose. I killed a man who was one, did it in front of witnesses, but I’ve never forgiven myself for it. Though it needed doing.”

“The ones that need to be done often seem the ones that we least like to have to do.”

“That’s the truth if I’ve ever heard it,” Tam said, sighing softly, leaning on the balcony railing. Lit windows were beginning to shine in the darkness below. “It’s so strange. My boy, the 용의 환생. All of those stories I heard when traveling the world, I’m part of them.”

“Think how it feels for me,” 랜드 said.

Tam chuckled. “Yes. Yes, I suppose you understand exactly what I mean, don’t you? Funny, isn’t it?”

“Funny?” 랜드 shook his head. “No. Not, that. My life isn’t my own. I’m a puppet for the Pattern and the prophecies, made to dance for the world before having my strings cut.”

Tam frowned. “That’s not true, son. Er, my Lord.”

“I can’t see it any other way.”

Tam crossed his arms on the smooth stone railing. “I guess I can understand. I remember some of those emotions myself, during the days when I was a soldier. You know that I fought against 티어? You’d think I would have painful memories, coming here. But one enemy often comes to seem like another. I don’t bear any grudges.”

랜드 rested the access key on the railing, but held it tightly. He did not lean down; he remained straight-backed.

“A soldier doesn’t have a lot of choices for his own destiny either,” Tam said, tapping softly on the railing with an idle finger. “More important men make all the decisions. Men, well, I guess men like you.”

“But my choices are made for me by the Pattern itself,” 랜드 said. “I have *less* freedom than the soldiers. You could have run, deserted. Or at least gotten out by legal means.”

“And you can’t run?” Tam asked.

“I don’t think the Pattern would let me,” 랜드 said. “What I do is too important. It would just force me back in line. It has done so a dozen times already.”

“And would you really *want* to run?” Tam asked.

랜드 didn’t reply.

“I could have left those wars. But, at the same time, I couldn’t have. Not without betraying who I was. I think it’s the same for you. Does it matter if you *can* run, when you know that you’re not going to?”

“I’m going to die at the end of this,” 랜드 said. “And I have no choice.”

Tam stood up straight, frowning. In an instant, 랜드 felt that he was twelve years old again. “I won’t have talk like that,” Tam said. “Even if you’re the 용의 환생, I won’t listen to it. You *always* have a choice. Maybe you can’t pick where you are forced to go, but you still have a choice.”

“But how?”

Tam laid a hand on 랜드’s shoulder. “The choice isn’t always about *what* you do, son, but *why* you do it. When I was a soldier, there were some men who fought simply for the money. There were others who fought for loyalty—loyalty to their comrades, or to the crown, or to whatever. The soldier who dies for money and the soldier who dies for loyalty are both dead, but there’s a *difference* between them. One death meant something. The other didn’t.

“I don’t know if it’s true that you’ll need to die for this all to play out. But we both know you aren’t going to run from it. Changed though you are, I can see that some things are the same. So I won’t stand any whining on the subject.”

“I wasn’t whining—” 랜드 began.

“I know,” Tam said. “Kings don’t whine, they deliberate.” He seemed to be quoting someone, though 랜드 had no idea who. Oddly, Tam gave a brief chuckle. “It doesn’t matter,” Tam continued. “랜드, I think you can survive this. I can’t imagine that the Pattern won’t give you some peace, considering the service you’re doing for us all. But you’re a soldier going to war, and the first thing a soldier learns is that you might die. You may not be able to choose the duties you’re given. But you *can* choose why you fulfill them. Why do you go to battle, 랜드?”

“Because I must.”

“That’s not good enough,” Tam said. “To the crows with that woman! I wish she’d come to me sooner. If I’d known—”

“What woman?”

“Cadsuane Sedai,” Tam said. “She brought me here, said that I needed to talk to you. I’d stayed away, previously, because I thought the last thing you needed was your father stomping across your field!”

Tam continued, but 랜드 stopped listening.

Cadsuane. Tam had come because of *Cadsuane*. It wasn’t because Tam had noticed 니나브 and taken the opportunity. Not because he’d just wanted to check on his son. But because he’d been *manipulated* into coming.

Would the woman never leave 랜드 alone!

His emotions seeing Tam were so strong that they had worn away the ice. Too much affection was like too much hatred. Either one made him *feel*, which was something he could not risk.

But he had. And suddenly, *feeling* nearly overcame him. He shuddered, turning away from Tam. Had their conversation all been another one of Cadsuane’s games? What was Tam’s part in it?

“랜드?” Tam asked. “I’m sorry. I shouldn’t have brought up the 에스 세다이. She said you might be angry if I mentioned her.”

“What else did she say?” 랜드 demanded, spinning back toward Tam. The stout man took a hesitant step backward. Night air blew around them, lights from the city dots below.

“Well,” Tam said, “she told me that I should talk about your youth, remind you of better times. She thought—”

“She manipulates me!” 랜드 said softly, meeting Tam’s eyes. “And she manipulates you. Everyone ties their strings to me!”

The rage boiled inside. He tried to shove it back, but it was *so* difficult. Where was the ice, the quiet? Desperately, 랜드 sought the void. He tried pouring all of his emotions into the flame of a candle, as Tam had taught so long ago.

*Saidin* was waiting there. Without thought, 랜드 seized it, and in doing so was overwhelmed with those emotions he thought he’d abandoned. The void shattered, but somehow *세이딘* remained, struggling against him. He screamed as the nausea hit him, and he threw his anger against it in defiance.

“랜드,” Tam said, frowning. “You should know better than—”

“*BE SILENT!*” 랜드 bellowed, throwing Tam to the floor with a flow of Air. 랜드 wrestled with his rage on one side and *세이딘* on the other. They threatened to crush him between them.

*This* was why he needed to be strong. Couldn’t they see? How could a man laugh when confronted by forces like these?

“I am the 용의 환생!” 랜드 roared at *세이딘*, at Tam, at Cadsuane, at the Creator himself. “I will not be your pawn!” He pointed at Tam with the access key. His father lay on the stone floor of the balcony. “You come from Cadsuane, pretending to show me affection. But you unwind another of her strings to tie about my throat! Can I not be free of you all?”

He had lost control. But he didn’t care. They wanted him to feel. He would *feel*, then! They wanted him to laugh? He would laugh as they burned!

Screaming at them all, he wove threads of Air and Fire. 르웨어스 테린 howled in his head, *세이딘* tried to destroy both of them, and the quiet voice inside 랜드’s heart vanished.

A prick of light grew in front of 랜드, sprouting from the center of the access key. The weaves for balefire spun before him, and the access key grew brighter as he drew in more power.

By that light, 랜드 saw his father’s face, looking up at him.

Terrified.

*What am I doing?*

랜드 began to shake, the balefire unraveling before he had time to loose it. He stumbled backward in horror.

*What am I DOING?* 랜드 thought again.

*No more than I’ve done before,* 르웨어스 테린 whispered.

Tam continued to stare at him, face shadowed by the night.

*Oh, Light,* 랜드 thought with terror, shock and rage. *I am doing it again. I am a monster.*

Still holding tenuously to *세이딘*, 랜드 wove a gateway to Ebou Dar, then ducked through, fleeing from the horror in Tam’s eyes.

**C*HAPTER** **48**

![](images/00290.jpg)

Reading the Commentary

민 sat in Cadsuane’s small room, waiting—with the others—to hear the result of 랜드’s meeting with his father. A low fire burned in the fireplace and lamps at each corner of the room lent light to the women, who worked at various busying activities—embroidery, darning, and knitting—to keep their minds off of the wait.

민 was past regretting her decision to make an alliance with Cadsuane. Regret had come early, during the first few days when Cadsuane had kept 민 close, asking after every viewing she had had about 랜드. The woman was meticulous as a Brown, writing down each vision and answer. It was like being in the 백색 탑, again!

민 wasn’t certain why 니나브’s submission to Cadsuane had given the woman license to interrogate 민, but that was how Cadsuane seemed to interpret it. Mix that with 민’s discomfort around 랜드 lately and her own desire to figure out just what Cadsuane and the 현명한 이들 were planning, and she seemed to spend practically all of her time in the woman’s presence.

Yes, regret had come and gone. 민 had moved on to resignation, tinged with a hint of frustration. Cadsuane knew quite a bit about the material 민 was studying in her books, but the woman doled out her knowledge like cloudberry jam, a little reward for good behavior, always hinting that there was more to come. That kept 민 from fleeing.

She *had* to find the answers. 랜드 needed them.

With that thought in mind, 민 leaned back on her cushioned bench and reopened her current book, a work by Sajius that was simply titled *Commentary on the Dragon*. One line in it teased at her, a sentence mostly ignored by those who had written commentary. *He shall hold a blade of light in his hands, and the three shall be one.*

The commentators felt it was too vague compared with other passages, like 랜드 taking the Stone or 랜드’s blood being spilled on the rocks of 세이올 굴.

She tried not to think about that last one. The important thing was that many of the prophecies—with a little consideration and thought—generally made sense. Even the lines about 랜드 being marked by the 용 and the Herons made sense, looking at it now.

But what of this line? A blade of light almost certainly meant *칼란도르*. But what of the “three shall be one”? Some few scholars claimed that “the three” were three great cities—티어, 일리안 and Caemlyn. Or, if one happened to be a scholar from 케렌, then they were said to be 티어, 일리안 and 케렌. The problem was that 랜드 had united far more than three cities. He’d conquered Bandar Eban as well, not to mention the fact that he would need to bring the Borderlanders to his banner.

But he was ruler—or near to it—in three kingdoms. He’d given up 안도르, but 케렌, 일리안 and 티어 were directly beneath his control, even if he personally wore only one crown. Maybe this passage did mean what the scholars said, and 민 was chasing nothing.

Were her studies as useless as the protection she’d thought to offer 랜드? *민,* she told herself, *self-pity will get you nowhere.* All she could do was study, think and hope.

“This is wrong,” she found herself saying out loud.

She heard Beldeine’s softly derisive snort from across the room. 민 looked up, frowning.

The women who had sworn to 랜드—Erian, Nesune, Sarene and Beldeine—had found themselves less welcome in his presence as he had grown less trusting of 에스 세다이. The only one he regularly allowed to see him was 니나브. It wasn’t odd, then, that the others had found their way to Cadsuane’s “camp.”

And what of 민’s own relationship with 랜드? She was still welcome in his presence; that hadn’t changed. But there was something wrong, something *off*. He put up walls when she was near—not to keep her out, but to keep the real him in. As if he was afraid of what the real him would do, or could do, to those he loved. . . .

*He’s in pain again,* she thought, feeling him through the bond. *Such anger.* What was going on? She felt a spike of fear, but shoved it down. She had to trust in Cadsuane’s plan. It was a good one.

Corele and Merise—almost constant attendants of Cadsuane these days—continued their embroidery in matching chairs by the hearth. Cadsuane had suggested the work to them to keep their hands busy while they waited. It seemed the ancient 에스 세다이 rarely did anything without intending to teach someone a lesson.

Of the 에스 세다이 sworn to 랜드, only Beldeine was there at the moment. Cadsuane sat near 민, perusing her own book. 니나브 walked back and forth, up and down, occasionally tugging on her braid. Nobody spoke of the tension in the room.

What *were* 랜드 and Tam discussing? Would 랜드’s father be able to turn him?

The chamber was cramped. With three chairs on the rug beside the hearth, a bench along the wall, and 니나브 crossing back and forth before the door like a spotted hound, there was barely room to move. The smooth stone walls made the place feel like a box, and there was only one window, open to the night air, behind Cadsuane. Light shone from the coals in the hearth and the lamps. The 감시자s were speaking in low tones in the adjoining room.

Yes, it was cramped, but considering her banishment, Cadsuane was lucky to have rooms in the Stone at all.

민 sighed and turned back to *Commentary on the Dragon*. That same phrase popped out at her again. *He shall hold a blade of light in his hands, and the three shall be one.* What did it mean?

“Cadsuane,” 민 said, holding up the book. “I think the interpretation of this phrase is wrong.”

Again, Beldeine let out a small—almost imperceptible—sniff of disdain.

“You have something to say, Beldeine?” Cadsuane asked, not looking up from her own book, a history called *The Proper Taming of Power*.

“Not in so many words, Cadsuane Sedai,” Beldeine replied lightly. The Green had a face that some might have called pretty, bearing traces of her 살다에안 heritage. Young enough to not yet have the ageless face, she often seemed to try too hard to prove herself.

“You obviously thought *something* when 민 spoke, Beldeine,” Cadsuane replied, turning a page. “Out with it.”

Beldeine flushed slightly—one noticed these things, if one spent a lot of time with 에스 세다이. They *did* have emotional reactions, they were just subtle. Unless, of course, the 에스 세다이 in question was 니나브. Although she’d grown better at controlling her emotions, she . . . well, she was still 니나브.

Beldeine said, “I simply think that the child is amusing in the way she pokes through those tomes, as if she were a scholar.”

민 would have taken that as a challenge from most people, but from Beldeine, the words were matter-of-fact.

Cadsuane turned another page. “I see. 민, what was it you were saying to me?”

“Nothing important, Cadsuane Sedai.”
“I didn’t ask if it was important, girl,” Cadsuane said briskly. “I asked you to repeat yourself. Out with it.”

민 sighed. Nobody could humiliate one more soundly than an 에스 세다이, for they did it without malice. 모이라인 had explained it to 민 once in simple terms: Most 에스 세다이 felt it was important to establish control when there was no great conflict, so that if a crisis *did* happen, people would know where to look.

It was very frustrating.

“I said,” 민 repeated, “that a passage is wrong. I’m reading commentary on the 카라에손 순환. Sajius claims that this line about the three becoming one speaks of the unification of three kingdoms beneath the Dragon’s banner. But I think he’s wrong.”

“And why,” Cadsuane said, “is it that you think you know more than a respected scholar of the prophecies?”

“Because,” 민 said, bristling, “the theory doesn’t make sense. 랜드 only really holds one crown. There *might* have been a good argument here if he hadn’t given away 티어 to 달린. But the theory doesn’t hold any longer. I think the passage refers to some way he has to use *칼란도르*.”

“I see,” Cadsuane said, turning yet another page in her own book. “That is a very unconventional interpretation.” Beldeine smiled thinly, turning back to her embroidery. “Of course,” Cadsuane added, “you are quite right.”

민 looked up.

“It was that very passage that led me to investigate *칼란도르*,” Cadsuane continued. “Through a great deal of searching I discovered that the sword could only be used properly in a circle of three. That is likely the ultimate meaning of the passage.”

“But that would imply that 랜드 had to use *칼란도르* in a circle sometime,” 민 said, looking at the passage again. He’d never done so, as far as she knew.

“It would,” Cadsuane said.

민 felt a sudden thrill. A hint, perhaps. Something that 랜드 didn’t know, that might help him! Except . . . Cadsuane had already known it. So 민 hadn’t discovered anything of real import after all.

“I should think,” Cadsuane said, “that an acknowledgment is due. Bad manners are not to be tolerated, after all.”

Beldeine looked up from her needlework, face dark. Then, unexpectedly, she stood and left the room. Her 감시자, the youthful Asha’man Karldin, followed quickly from the side chamber, crossing the room with the 에스 세다이 and following Beldeine out into the hallway outside. Cadsuane gave a sniff, then turned back to her book.

The door closed, and 니나브 eyed 민 before returning to her pacing. 민 could read a lot in that glance. 니나브 was annoyed that nobody else seemed nervous. She was frustrated that they hadn’t found some way to listen in on 랜드 and Tam’s conversation. And she was obviously terrified for 란. 민 understood. She felt similarly about 랜드.

And . . . what was that vision that was suddenly hovering above 니나브’s head? She was kneeling over someone’s corpse in a posture of grief. The viewing was gone a moment later.

민 shook her head. That hadn’t been a viewing she could interpret, so she let it pass. She couldn’t waste her time trying to unravel all of those. For instance, the black knife that spun around Beldeine’s head recently could mean anything.

She focused on the book. So . . . 랜드 was to use *칼란도르* as part of a circle, then? The three becoming one? But for what reason and with whom? If he was to fight the 어둠의 존재, then it didn’t make sense for him to be in a circle with someone else in control, did it?

“Cadsuane,” she said. “This is still wrong. There’s more here. Something we haven’t discovered.”

“About *칼란도르*?” the woman asked.

민 nodded.

“I suspect so as well,” Cadsuane replied. How odd to hear her being frank! “But I haven’t been able to determine *what*. If only that fool boy would revoke my exile, we could get on with more important—”

The door to Cadsuane’s room slammed open, causing Merise to jump in shock. 니나브 hopped back from the door—it had nearly hit her.

Standing in the doorway was a very angry Tam al’Thor. He glared at Cadsuane. “What have you done to him?” he demanded.

Cadsuane lowered her book. “I have done *nothing* to the boy, other than to encourage him toward civility. Something, it seems, other members of the family could learn as well.”

“Watch your tongue, 에스 세다이,” Tam snarled. “Have you seen him? The entire *room* seemed to grow darker when he entered. And that face—I’ve seen more emotion in the eyes of a corpse! What has happened to my son?”

“I take it,” Cadsuane said, “that the reunion did not go as hoped?”

Tam took a deep breath, and the anger seemed to suddenly flow out of him. He was still firm, his eyes displeased, but the rage was gone. 민 had seen 랜드 take control of himself that quickly, before things had started to go wrong in Bandar Eban.

“He tried to kill me,” Tam said in a level voice. “My own son. Once he was as gentle and faithful a lad as a father could hope for. Tonight, he channeled the 하나의 힘 and turned it against me.”

민 raised her hand to her mouth, feeling a panicked terror. The words brought back memories of 랜드 looming over her, trying to kill her.

But that hadn’t been him! It had been 세미르하제. Hadn’t it? *Oh, 랜드,* she thought, understanding the pain she’d felt through the bond. *What have you done?*

“Interesting,” Cadsuane said, her voice cold. “And did you speak the words I prepared for you?”

“It’s all right, Wisdom,” Tam said. He looked at Cadsuane. 민 had seen her treat others like this, including 랜드. He had always grown frustrated, and others she did it to were prone to bellowing.

Tam stared her in the eyes. “I’ve known men who, when challenged, always turn to their fists for answers. I’ve never liked 에스 세다이; I was happy to be rid of them when I returned to my farm. A bully is a bully, whether she uses the strength of her arm or other means.”

“Now,” 니나브 said, as if she’d been the one to defuse the exchange, “perhaps we can get back to what is important. Tam al’Thor, I’d have expected you of all people to handle this better. Didn’t we warn you that 랜드 had grown unstable?”

“This is irrelevant,” Cadsuane said. “You realize, child, that might have been our last opportunity to save your son?”

“This is what you get for being wool-headed and ignoring what you are told!” 니나브 interjected.

The room fell still.

“What happened, then?” 니나브 asked.

“He . . . seemed to be distracted by something, suddenly,” Tam said. “He took that little statue and dashed through the gateway.”

Cadsuane raised an eyebrow. “And did you see, by chance, where that gateway took him?”

“I’m not certain,” Tam admitted. “It was dark, though I thought. . . .”

“I don’t know about that last part,” Tam said. “But it *did* look like Ebou Dar.”

“Light preserve us,” Corele whispered.

Just Another Man

He’d spent long enough with the 아일 to pick up some of their disdain for the Tinkers. Yet that disdain warred with his knowledge that the Tuatha’an—in many ways—followed more true, traditional 아일 ways. 랜드 could *remember* what it was like to live as they had. In the visions of Rhuidean, he had followed the Way of the Leaf. He’d also seen the 전설의 시대. He’d lived those lives, the lives of others, for a few brief moments.

He walked along the packed streets of the muggy city, still in something of a daze. Last night, he had traded his fine black coat to a Tinker for a common brown cloak, ragged on the bottom and stitched in places. Ebou Dar. It was a busy, bulging city, split in half by its large river. 랜드 walked the west side, through squares edged with beautiful statues and streets lined with row upon row of white houses, many several stories high. He often passed men fighting with fists or knives, and nobody making any effort to break them apart. He ignored them all. Instead, he thought on the Tinkers. Tinkers were safe here, but 랜드’s own father wasn’t safe in his empire. 랜드’s friends feared him; he had seen it in 니나브’s eyes.

The people here weren’t afraid. 쇼엔찬 officers moved through the crowds, wearing those insectlike helms. The people made way for them, but out of respect. When 랜드 heard commoners speaking, they were glad for the stability. They actually praised the 쇼엔찬 for conquering them!

랜드 crossed a short, canal-spanning bridge. Small boats idled down the waterway, boatmen calling greetings to one another. 랜드 stopped and leaned against another white building, this one a farrier’s shop. He raised his stump to his head, trying to clear his mind.

He didn’t want to confront what he had nearly done back in the Stone. He didn’t want to confront what he *had* done: weaving Air and shoving Tam to the ground, threatening him; raving.

랜드 couldn’t focus on that. He had not come to Ebou Dar to gawk like a farmboy. He had come to destroy his enemies! They defied him; they needed to be eliminated. For the good of all nations.

The 용의 환생 walked among this people, and they did not know him. He unwrapped the access key, just another foreigner, standing on the muddy bridge. After destroying the palace, he would have to be quick. He’d send off bursts of balefire to destroy the ships in the harbor, then use something more mundane to rain fire on the city itself, throw it into a panic. The chaos would delay his enemies’ reaction. After that, he would Travel to the garrisons at the city gates and destroy them. He vaguely remembered scout reports of supply camps to the north, well stocked with both soldiers and foodstuffs. He would destroy them next.

From there, he’d need to move on to Amador, then to Tanchico and others. He’d Travel quickly, never remaining in one place long enough to be caught by the 버림받은 자들. A flickering light of death, like a burning ember, flaring to life here, then there. Many would die, but most would be 쇼엔찬. Invaders.

He stared down at the access key. Then he seized *세이딘*.

The sickness washed across him more powerfully than it ever had before. The force of it knocked him to the ground like a physical blow. He cried out, barely noticing when he hit the stones. He groaned, gripping the access key, curling around it. His insides seemed to burn, and he turned his head, rolling onto his shoulder and vomiting onto the bridge.

But he held on to *세이딘*. He needed the power. The succulent, beautiful power. Even the stench of his own vomit seemed more real to him, more sweet, for the power within him.

He opened his eyes. People were gathered around him, concerned. A 쇼엔찬 patrol was approaching. Now was the time. He had to strike.

Screaming in frustration, 랜드 made a gateway, causing the people to jump back in shock. He stumbled to his feet and threw himself through, scrabbling on all fours, as the 쇼엔찬 soldiers drew swords and yelled unfamiliar words.

랜드 landed on a large stone disc of black and white, the air around him a void of darkness. The portal closed behind, locking Ebou Dar away, and the disc began to move. It floated through the void, lit by some strange ambient light. 랜드 curled up on the disc, cradling the access key, breathing deeply.

*Why can’t I be strong enough?* He didn’t know if the thought was his or if it was 르웨어스 테린’s. The two were the same. *Why can’t I do what I must?*

The disc traveled for a short time, the only sound in the void that of his breathing. The disc looked like one of the seals to the 어둠의 존재’s prison, split with a sinuous line dividing the black from the white. 랜드 lay directly atop it. They called the black half the Dragon’s Fang. To the people, it symbolized evil. Destruction.

But 랜드 was *necessary* destruction. Why had the Pattern pushed him so hard if he didn’t need to destroy? Originally, he had tried to avoid killing—but there had been little chance of that working. Then he’d made himself avoid killing women. That had proven impossible.

He was destruction. He just had to accept that. *Someone* had to be hard enough to do what was necessary, didn’t they?

A gateway opened, and he stumbled to his feet, clutching the access key. He stepped from the 스키밍 platform and out onto an empty meadow. The place where he’d fought the 쇼엔찬 once with *칼란도르*. And failed.

He stood on the very point of 용산, the lone peak that had erupted where 르웨어스 테린 had killed himself three thousand years before. To think.

**C*HAPTER** **50**

![](images/00286.jpg)

Veins of Gold

Wind blew around 랜드 as he sat at the top of the world. His weaving of Air and Fire had melted away the snow around him, exposing a jagged gray-black tip of rock about three paces wide. The peak was like a broken fingernail jutting into the sky, and 랜드 sat atop it. As far as he could tell, it was the very tip of 용산. Perhaps the highest point in the world.

He sat upon his small outcropping, the access key sitting on the rock in front of him. The air was thin here, and he’d had trouble breathing until he’d found a way to weave Air so that it compressed slightly around him. Like the weave that warmed him, he wasn’t certain how he’d done it. He vaguely remembered 아스모데안 trying to teach him a similar weave, and 랜드 hadn’t been able to get it right. Now it came naturally. 르웨어스 테린’s influence, or his own growing familiarity with the 하나의 힘?

용산’s broken, open mouth lay several hundred feet beneath him, to the left. The scents of ash and sulphur were pungent, even at this distance. The maw was black with ash and red from molten rock and blazing fires.

He still held to the Source. He didn’t dare let go. This last time he’d seized it had been the worst he could remember, and he feared that the sickness would overpower him if he tried again.

He had been here for hours. And yet he did not feel tired. He stared at the *ter’angreal*. Thinking.

What was he? What was the 용의 환생? A symbol? A sacrifice? A sword, meant to destroy? A sheltering hand, meant to protect?

A puppet, playing a part over and over again?

He was angry. Angry at the world, angry at the Pattern, angry at the Creator for leaving humans to fight against the 어둠의 존재 with no direction. What right did any of them have to demand 랜드’s life of him?

Well, 랜드 had offered that life to them. It had taken him a great while to accept his death, but he *had* made his peace. Wasn’t that enough? Did he have to be in pain until the end?

He had thought that if he made himself hard enough, it would take away the pain. If he couldn’t feel, then he couldn’t hurt.

The wounds in his side pulsed in agony. For a time, he’d been able to forget them. But the deaths he had caused rubbed his soul raw. That list starting with 모이라인. Everything had begun to go wrong at her death. Before that, he’d still had hope.

Before that, he’d never been put in a box.

He understood what would be required of him, and he’d changed in the ways he thought he needed. Those changes were to keep him from being overwhelmed. Die to protect people he didn’t know? Chosen to save mankind? Chosen to force the kingdoms of the world to unite behind him, destroying those who refused to listen? Chosen to cause the deaths of thousands who fought in his name, to hold those souls upon his shoulders, a weight that must be borne? What man could do these things and remain sane? The only way he had seen had been to cut off his emotions, to make himself *cuendillar*.

But he had failed. He hadn’t been able to stamp his feelings out. The voice inside had been so small, but it had pricked at him, like a needle making the smallest of holes in his heart. Even the smallest of holes would let the blood leak free.

Those holes would bleed him dry.

The quiet voice was gone now. It had vanished when he’d thrown Tam to the floor and nearly killed him. Without that voice, did 랜드 dare continue? If it was the last remnant of the old 랜드—the 랜드 who had believed that he knew what was right and what was wrong—then what did its silence mean?

랜드 picked up the access key and stood up, boots scraping stone. It was midday, though the sun still lay hidden behind the clouds. Below, he could see hills and forests, lakes and villages.

“And what if I don’t *want* the Pattern to continue?” he bellowed. He stepped forward, right to the edge of the rock, clutching the access key to his chest.

“We live the same lives!” he yelled at them. “Over and over and over. We make the same mistakes. Kingdoms do the same *stupid* things. Rulers fail their people time and time again. Men continue to hurt and hate and die and kill!”

Winds buffeted him, whipping at his brown cloak and his fine 타이런 trousers. But his words carried, echoing across the broken rocks of 용산. It was cold and crisp, the air new. His weave kept him warm enough to survive, but it did not stop the chill. He hadn’t wanted it to.

“What if I think it’s all meaningless?” he demanded with the loud voice of a king. “What if I don’t *want* it to keep turning? We live our lives by the blood of others! And those others become forgotten. What *good* is it if everything we know will fade? Great deeds or great tragedies, neither means anything! They will become legends, then those legends will be forgotten, then it will all start over again!”

The access key began to glow in his hands. The clouds above seemed to grow darker.

랜드’s anger beat in rhythm with his heart, demanding to be set free.

“What if *he* is right?” 랜드 bellowed. “What if it’s better for this all to end? What if the Light was a lie all along, and *this* is all just a punishment? We live again and again, growing feeble, dying, trapped forever. We are to be tortured for all time!”
Power flooded into 랜드 like surging waves filling a new ocean. He came to life, glorying in *세이딘*, not caring that the display must be brilliantly visible to men everywhere who could channel. He felt himself alight with the Power, like a sun to the world below.

“NONE OF THIS MATTERS!”

He closed his eyes, drawing in more and more power, feeling as he had only twice before. Once when he had cleansed *세이딘*. Once when he had created this mountain.

Then he drew in more.

He knew that much power would destroy him. He had stopped caring. Fury that had been building in him for two years finally boiled free, unleashed at long last. He spread his arms out wide, access key in his hand. 르웨어스 테린 had been right to kill himself and create 용산. Only he hadn’t gone far enough.

랜드 could remember that day. The smoke, the rumbling, the sharp pains of a 치유 bringing him back to lucidity as he lay in a broken palace. But those pains had paled compared with the agony of realization. Agony from seeing the beautiful walls scarred and broken. From seeing the piles of familiar corpses, tossed to the floor like discarded rags.

From seeing 일레나 a short distance away, her golden hair spread out on the ground around her.

He could *feel* the palace around him shaking from the earth’s own sobs. Or was that 용산, throbbing from the immense power he had drawn into himself?

He could smell the air thick with blood and soot and death and *pain*. Or was that just the scent of a dying world, spread before him?

The winds began to whip at him, spinning, enormous clouds above twisting upon themselves, like ancient leviathans passing in the profound black deep.

르웨어스 테린 had made a mistake. He had died, but had left the world alive, wounded, limping forward. He’d let the Wheel of Time keep turning, rotating, *rotting* and bringing him back around again. He could not escape it. Not without ending everything.

“Why?” 랜드 whispered to the twisting winds around him. The Power coming to him through the access key was greater than he’d held when cleansing *세이딘*. Perhaps greater than any man had ever held. Great enough to unravel the Pattern itself and bring final peace.

“Why do we have to do this again?” he whispered. “I have already failed. She is dead by my hand. Why must you make me live it *again*?”

Lightning cracked above, thunder buffeting him. 랜드 closed his eyes, perched above a drop that plummeted thousands of feet downward, in the middle of a tempest of icy wind. Through his eyelids, he could sense the blazing light of the access key. The Power he held inside dwarfed that light. He was the sun. He was fire. He was life and death.

Why? Why must they do this over and over? The world could give him no answers.

랜드 raised his arms high, a conduit of power and energy. An incarnation of death and destruction. He would end it. End it all and let men rest, finally, from their suffering.

Stop them from having to live over and over again. Why? Why had the Creator done this to them? *Why?*

*Why do we live again?* 르웨어스 테린 asked, suddenly. His voice was crisp and distinct.

*Yes,* 랜드 said, pleading. *Tell me. Why?*

*Maybe . . .* 르웨어스 테린 said, shockingly lucid, not a hint of madness to him. He spoke softly, reverently. *Why? Could it be . . . Maybe it’s so that we can have a second chance.*

랜드 froze. The winds blew against him, but he could not be moved by them. The Power hesitated inside him, like the headsman’s axe, held quivering above the criminal’s neck. *You may not have a choice about which duties are given you,* Tam’s voice, just a memory, said in his mind. *But you can choose* why *you fulfill them.*

*Why, 랜드? Why do you go to battle? What* is *the point?*

*Why?*

All was still. Even with the tempest, the winds, the crashes of thunder. All was still.

*Why?* 랜드 thought with wonder. *Because each time we live, we get to love again.*

That was the answer. It all swept over him, lives lived, mistakes made, love changing everything. He saw the entire world in his mind’s eye, lit by the glow in his hand. He remembered lives, hundreds of them, thousands of them, stretching to infinity. He remembered love, and peace, and joy, and hope.

Within that moment, suddenly something amazing occurred to him. *If I live again, then she might as well!*

That’s why he fought. That’s why he lived again, and that was the answer to Tam’s question. *I fight because last time, I failed. I fight because I want to fix what I did wrong.*

*I want to do it right this time.*

The Power within him reached a crescendo, and he turned it upon itself, drove it through the access key. The *ter’angreal* was connected to a much greater force, a massive *sa’angreal* to the south, built to stop the 어둠의 존재. Too powerful, some had said. Too powerful ever to use. Too frightening.

랜드 used its own power upon it, crushing the distant globe, shattering it as if in the grip of a giant’s hands.

The 초에단 칼 exploded.

The Power winked out.

The tempest ended.

And 랜드 opened his eyes for the first time in a very long while. He knew—somehow—that he would never again hear 르웨어스 테린’s voice in his head. For they were not two men, and never had been.

He regarded the world beneath him. The clouds above had finally broken, if only just above him. The gloom dispersed, allowing him to see the sun hanging just above.

랜드 looked up at it. Then he smiled. Finally, he let out a deep-throated laugh, true and pure.

It had been far too long.

Bathed in Light
