알루드라 cocked her head at him. *Maybe if I smiled more when I made jokes,* he thought idly, leaning against the side of the barricade. *Then they’d understand what I meant.* That, of course, raised the question: Did he want people to understand? It was often more amusing the other way. Besides, smiling was so *garish.* Where was the subtlety? And…

And he was *really* having trouble focusing. He blinked at 알루드라, whose face had grown concerned in the torchlight.

“What about my face?” 탈마네스 raised a hand to his cheek. Blood. The 미르드랄. Right. “Just a cut.”

“And the veins?”

“Veins?” he asked, then noticed his hand. Tendrils of blackness, like ivy growing beneath the skin, had wound down his wrist and across the back of his hand toward the fingers. They seemed to be growing darker as he watched. “Oh, that. I’m dying, unfortunately. Terribly tragic. You wouldn’t happen to have any brandy, would you?”

“I—”

“My Lord!” a voice called.

탈마네스 blinked, then forced himself to turn about, leaning on the spear. “Yes, Filger?”

“More 트롤록s, my Lord. Lots of them! They’re filling in behind us.”

“East gates?” Guybon called. “Maybe a half-hour march. We need to head further down the hill.”

“탈마네스,” 알루드라 said, stepping in. “용’ eggs and powder, we have few of them left. We will need the supplies from Baerlon. Today, if you set up the dragons ... A few shots for each dragon, this is all I can give you.”

Dennel nodded. “용 aren’t meant to make up frontline units all by themselves, my Lord. They need support to keep the enemy from coming too close and destroying the weapons. We can man those dragons, but we won’t last long without infantry.”

“That’s why we’re running,” 탈마네스 said. He turned, took a step, and was so woozy he almost fell. “And I believe ... I believe I’ll need a horse…”

모그헤디엔 stepped onto a platform of stone floating in the middle of an open sea. Glassy and blue, the water rippled in the occasional breeze, but there were no waves. Neither was there land in sight.

모리딘 stood at the side of the platform, hands clasped behind his back. In front of him, the sea burned. The fire gave off no smoke, but it was hot, and the water near it hissed and boiled. Stone flooring in the middle of an endless sea. Water that burned. 모리딘 always *had* enjoyed creating impossibilities within his dreamshards.

“Sit,” 모리딘 said to her, not turning.

She obeyed, choosing one of the four chairs suddenly arranged near the center of the platform. The sky was deep blue, cloudless, and the sun hung at about three-quarters of the way to its zenith. How long had it been since she’d seen the sun in *Tel’aran’rhiod*? Lately, that omnipresent black storm had blanketed the sky. But, then, this wasn’t completely *Tel’aran’rhiod.* Nor was it 모리딘’s dream, but a… melding of the two. Like a temporary lean-to built off the side of the dream world. A bubble of merged realities.

모그헤디엔 wore a gown of black and gold, lacework on the sleeves faintly reminiscent of a spider’s web. Only faintly. One did well not to overuse a theme.

As she sat, 모그헤디엔 tried to exude control and self-confidence. Once, both had come easily for her. Today, trying to capture either was like trying to snatch dandelion seeds from the air, only to have them dance away from her hand. 모그헤디엔 gritted her teeth, angry at herself. She was one of the *Chosen*. She had made kings weep, armies tremble. Her name had been used by generations of mothers to frighten their children. And now…

She felt at her neck, found the pendant hanging there. It was still safe. She knew it was, but touching it brought her calmness.

“Do not grow too comfortable wearing that,” 모리딘 said. A wind blew across him, rippling the pristine ocean surface. On that wind she heard faint screams. “You are not completely forgiven, 모그헤디엔. This is a probation. Perhaps when you fail next, I will give the mindtrap to 디만드레드.”

She sniffed. “He would toss it aside in boredom. 디만드레드 wants only one thing. Al’Thor. Anyone who does not lead him toward his goal is unimportant to him.”

“You underestimate him,” 모리딘 said softly. “The Great Lord is pleased with 디만드레드. Very pleased. You, however . . ”

모그헤디엔 sank down in her chair, feeling her tortures anew. Pain such as few in this world had ever known. Pain beyond what a body should be able to endure. She held to the *cour’souvra* and embraced *세다르.* That brought some relief.

Before, channeling in the same room as the *cour’souvra* had been agonizing. Now that she, rather than 모리딘, wore the pendant, it was not so. *Not just a pendant,* she thought, clutching it. *My soul itself.* Darkness within! She had never thought that she, of all people, would find herself subject to one of these. Was she not the spider, careful in all that she did?

She reached her other hand up, clasping it over the one that held the pendant. What if it fell, what if someone took it? She wouldn’t lose it. She *couldn’t* lose it.

*This is what I have become?* She felt sick. *I have to recover. Somehow.* She forced herself to let go of the mindtrap.

최후의 전투 was upon them; already, 트롤록s poured into the southern lands. It was a new 그림자 전쟁, but only she and the other Chosen knew the deeper secrets of the 하나의 힘. The ones she hadn’t been forced to give up to those horrible women…

*No, don’t think about that.* The pain, the suffering, the *failure.*

In this war, they faced no Hundred Companions, no 에스 세다이 with centuries of skill and practice. She would prove herself, and past errors would be forgotten.

모리딘 continued to stare at those impossible flames. The only sounds were that of the fire and of the water that boiled near it. He would eventually explain his purpose in summoning her, wouldn’t he? He had been acting increasingly strange, lately. Perhaps his madness was returning. Once, the man named 모리딘—or 이샤마엘, or Elan Morin Tedronai—would have delighted in holding a *cour’souvra* for one of his rivals. He would have invented punishments, thrilled in her agony.

There had been some of that at the start; then ... he had lost interest. He spent more and more time alone, staring into flames, brooding. The punishments he had administered to her and 신데인 had seemed almost routine.

She found him more dangerous this way.

A gateway split the air just to the side of the platform. “Do we really need to do this every other day, 모리딘?” 디만드레드 asked, stepping through and into the World of Dreams. Handsome and tall, he had jet hair and a prominent nose. He gave 모그헤디엔 a glance, noting the mindtrap on her neck before continuing. “I have important things to do, and you interrupt them.”

“There are people you need to meet, 디만드레드,” 모리딘 said softly. “Unless the Great Lord has named you Nae’blis without informing me, you *will* do as you are told. Your playthings can wait.”

디만드레드’s expression darkened, but he did not object further. He let the gateway close, then moved to the side, looking down into the sea. He frowned. What was in the waters? She hadn’t looked. She felt foolish for not having done so. What had happened to her caution?

디만드레드 walked to one of the chairs near her, but did not sit. He stood, contemplating 모리딘 from behind. What *had* 디만드레드 been doing? During her period bound to the mindtrap, she had done 모리딘’s bidding, but had never found an answer to 디만드레드.

She shivered again, thinking of those months under 모리딘’s control. *I will have vengeance.*

“You’ve let 모그헤디엔 free,” 디만드레드 said. “What of this… 신데인?”

“She is not your concern,” 모리딘 said.

모그헤디엔 had not failed to notice that 모리딘 still wore 신데인’s mindtrap. 신데인. It meant “last chance” in the 고대어, but the woman’s true nature was one secret that 모그헤디엔 *had* discovered. 모리딘 himself had rescued 란피어 from *Sindhol*, freeing her from the creatures that feasted upon her ability to channel.

In order to rescue her, and of course to punish her, 모리딘 had slain her. That had allowed the Great Lord to recapture her soul and place it in a new body. Brutal, but very effective. Precisely the kind of solution the Great Lord preferred.

모리딘 was focused on his flames, and 디만드레드 on him, so 모그헤디엔 used the chance to slip out of her seat and walk to the edge of the floating stone platform. The water below was completely clear. Through it she could see people very distinctly. They floated with their legs chained to something deep below, arms bound behind them. They swayed like kelp.

There were thousands of them. Each of them looked up at the sky with wide, horrified eyes. They were locked in a perpetual state of drowning. Not dead, not allowed to die, but constantly gasping for air and finding only water. As she watched, something dark reached up from below and pulled one of them down into the depths. Blood rose like a blooming flower; it caused the others to struggle all the more urgently.

모그헤디엔 smiled. It did her good to see someone other than herself suffering. These might simply be figments, but it was possible that they were ones who had failed the Great Lord.
Another gateway opened at the side of the platform, and an unfamiliar woman stepped through. The creature had alarmingly unpleasant features, with a hooked yet bulbous nose and pale eyes that were off center with one another. She wore a dress that tried to be fine, of yellow silk, but it only served to highlight the woman’s ugliness.

모그헤디엔 sneered and returned to her seat. Why was 모리딘 admitting a stranger to one of their meetings? This woman could channel; she must be one of those useless women who called themselves 에스 세다이 in this Age.

*Granted,* 모그헤디엔 thought, sitting, *she* is *powerful* How had 모그헤디엔 missed noticing one with this talent among the 에스 세다이? Her sources had picked out that wretched lightskirt 니나브 almost immediately, yet they’d missed this hag?

“This is who you wish us to meet?” 디만드레드 said, lips turning down.

“No,” 모리딘 said absently. “You’ve met Hessalam before.”

Hessalam? It meant… “without forgiveness” in the 고대어. The woman met 모그헤디엔’s eyes proudly, and there was something familiar about her stance.

“I have things to be about, 모리딘,” the newcomer said. “This had better be—”

모그헤디엔 gasped. The tone in that voice…

“Do not take that tone with me,” 모리딘 cut in, speaking softly, not turning. “Do not take it with any of us. Currently, even 모그헤디엔 is favored more than you.”

“*그랜달?”* 모그헤디엔 asked, horrified.

“Do not use that name!” 모리딘 said, spinning on her, the burning water flaring up. “It has been stripped from her.”

그랜달—Hessalam—sat down without looking again at 모그헤디엔. Yes, the way the woman carried herself was right. It *was* her.

모그헤디엔 almost chortled with glee. 그랜달 had always used her looks as a bludgeon. Well, now they were a bludgeon of a different type. How perfect! The woman must be positively *writhing* inside. What had she done to earn such a punishment? 그랜달’s stature—her authority, the myths told about her—were all linked to her beauty. What now? Would she have to start searching for the most horrid people alive to keep as pets, the only ones who could compete with her ugliness?

This time, 모그헤디엔 did laugh. A quiet laugh, but 그랜달 heard. The woman shot her a glare that could have set a section of the ocean aflame all on its own.

모그헤디엔 returned a calm gaze, feeling more confident now. She resisted the urge to stroke the *cour’souvra. Bring what you will, 그랜달*, she thought. *We are on level footing now. We shall see who ends this race ahead.*

A stronger wind blew past, and ripples started to rise around them, though the platform itself remained secure. 모리딘 let his fire die out, and nearby, waves rose. 모그헤디엔 could make out bodies, little more than dark shadows, inside those waves. Some were dead. Others struggled for the surface, their chains removed, but as they neared the open air, something always towed them back down again.

“We are few, now,” 모리딘 said. “We four, and the one who is punished most, are all that remain. By definition, that makes us the strongest.”

*Some of us are,* 모그헤디엔 thought. *One of us was slain by al’Thor, 모리딘, and required the Great Lord’s hand to return him.* Why had 모리딘 never been punished for his failure? Well, it was best not to look too long for fairness in the Great Lord’s hand.

“Still, we are too few.” 모리딘 waved a hand, and a stone doorway appeared on the side of the platform. Not a gateway, just a door. This was 모리딘’s dreamshard; he could control it. The door opened, and a man strode through it and out onto the platform.

Dark-haired, the man had the features of a 살다에안—a nose that was faintly hooked, eyes that tilted. He was handsome and tall, and 모그헤디엔 recognized him. “The leader of those fledgling male 에스 세다이? I know this man, Mazri—”

“That name has been discarded,” 모리딘 said. “Just as each of us, upon being Chosen, discarded what we were and the names men called us. From this moment on, this man shall be known only as M’Hael. One of the Chosen.”

“Chosen?” Hessalam seemed to choke on the word. “This *child*? He—” She cut off.

It was not their place to debate if one was Chosen. They could argue among themselves, even plot, if they did so with care. But questioning the Great Lord… that was not allowed. Ever.

Hessalam said no more. 모리딘 would not dare call this man Chosen if the Great Lord had not decided it. There was no argument to be made. Still, 모그헤디엔 shivered. 타임… M’Hael… was said to be strong, perhaps as strong as the rest of them, but elevating one from this Age, with all of their ignorance. ... It galled her to consider that this M’Hael would be regarded as her equal.

“I see the challenge in your eyes,” 모리딘 said, looking at the three of them, “though only one of you was foolish enough to start voicing it. M’Hael has earned his reward. Too many of our number threw themselves into contests with al’Thor when he was presumed to be weak. M’Hael instead earned 르웨어스 테린’s trust, then took charge of the training of his weapons. *He* has been raising a new generation of Dreadlords to the Shadow’s cause. What do the three of you have to show for your work since being released?”

“You will know the fruits I have harvested, 모리딘,” 디만드레드 said, voice low. “You will know them in bushels and droves. Just remember my requirement: I face al’Thor on the field of battle. His blood is mine, and no one else’s.” He met each of their eyes in turn, then finally those of M’Hael. There seemed to be a familiarity to them. The two had met before.

*You will have competition with that one*, *디만드레드,* 모그헤디엔 thought. *He wants al’Thor nearly as much as you do.*

디만드레드 had been changing lately. Once, he wouldn’t have cared who killed 르웨어스 테린—so long as the man died. What made 디만드레드 insist on doing the deed himself?

“모그헤디엔,” 모리딘 said. “디만드레드 has plans for the war to come. You are to assist him.”

‘*Assist* him?” she said. “I—”

“Do you forget yourself so quickly, 모그헤디엔?” 모리딘’s voice was silky. “You will do as you are told. 디만드레드 wants you watching over one of the armies that now lacks proper monitoring. Speak a single word of complaint, and you will realize that the pain you have known up to now is but a shadow of true agony.”

Her hand went to the *cour’souvra* at her neck. Looking into his eyes, she felt her authority evaporate. *I hate you,* she thought. *I hate you more for doing this to me in front of the others.*

“The last days are upon us,” 모리딘 said, turning his back on them. “In these hours, you will earn your final rewards. If you have grudges, put them behind you. If you have plots, bring them to completion. Make your final plays, for this… this is the end.”

탈마네스 lay on his back, staring up at a dark sky. The clouds above seemed to be reflecting light from below, the light of a dying city. That was wrong. Light came from above, didn’t it?

He’d fallen from the horse not long after starting for the city gate. He could remember that, most of the time. Pain made it hard to think. People yelled at one another.

*I should have ... I should have taunted 맷 more,* he thought, a hint of a smile cracking his lips. *Stupid time to be thinking of such things. I have to*… *have to find the dragons. Or did we find them already… ?*

“I’m telling you, the bloody things don’t work like that!” Dennel’s voice. “They’re not bloody 에스 세다이 on wheels. We can’t make a wall of fire. We can send these balls of metal hurtling through the 트롤록s.”

“They explode.” Guybon’s voice. “We could use the extras like I say.”

탈마네스’ eyes drifted closed.

“The balls explode, yes,” Dennel said. “But we have to launch them first. Setting them all in a row and letting the 트롤록s run over them wont do much.”

A hand shook 탈마네스’ shoulder. “Lord 탈마네스,” Melten said. “There is no dishonor in letting it end now. I know the pain is great. May the last embrace of the mother shelter you.”

A sword being drawn. 탈마네스 steeled himself.

Then he found that he really, *really* didn’t want to die.

He forced his eyes open and held up a hand to Melten, who stood over him. Jesamyn hovered nearby with arms folded, looking worried.

“Help me to my feet,” 탈마네스 said.

Melten hesitated, then did so.

“You shouldn’t be standing,” Jesamyn said.

“Better than being beheaded in honor,” 탈마네스 grumbled, gritting his teeth against the pain. Light, was that his hand? It was so dark, it looked as if it had been charred in a fire. “What… what is going on?”

“We're cornered, my Lord,” Melten said grimly, eyes solemn. He thought them all as good as dead. “Dennel and Guybon are arguing over placement of the dragons for a last stand. 알루드라 is measuring the charges.”

탈마네스, finally standing, sagged against Melten. Before him, two thousand people clustered in the large city square. They huddled like men in the wilderness seeking one another’s warmth on a cold night. Dennel and Guybon had set up the dragons in a half-circle bowed outward, pointing toward the center of the city, refugees behind. The Band was now committed to manning the dragons; three pairs of hands were needed to operate each weapon. Almost all of the Band had had at least some training.

The buildings nearby had caught fire, but the light was doing strange things. Why didn’t it reach the streets? Those were all too dark. As if they’d been painted. Like…

He blinked, clearing the tears of pain from his eyes, realization dawning. 트롤록s filled the streets like ink flowing toward the half-circle of dragons that were pointed at them.

Something held the 트롤록s back for the moment. *They’re waiting until they are all together for a rush,* 탈마네스 thought.

Calls and snarls came from behind. 탈마네스 pivoted, then clutched Melten’s arm as the world lurched. He waited for it to steady. The pain… the pain was actually dulling. Like glowing flames running out of fresh coal. It had feasted upon him, but there wasn’t much left of him for it to eat.

As things steadied, 탈마네스 saw what was creating the snarls. The square they were in adjoined the city wall, but the townspeople and soldiers had kept their distance from the wall, for it was coated with 트롤록s, like a thick grime. They raised weapons in the air and roared down at the people.

“They throw down spears at anyone who comes too close, Melten said. “We’d been hoping to reach the wall, then follow it along to the gate, but we can’t—not with those things up there raining death upon us. All other routes are cut off.”

알루드라 approached Guybon and Dennel. “Charges, I can set under the dragons,” she said to them; softly, but not as softly as she should have. “These charges, they will destroy the weapons. They may hurt the people in an unpleasant way.”

“Do it,” Guybon said very softly. “What the 트롤록s would do is worse, and we cannot allow the dragons to fall into the Shadow’s hands. That’s why they’re waiting. Their leaders are hoping that a sudden rush will give them time to overwhelm us and seize the weapons.”

“They’re moving!” a soldier called from beside the dragons. “Light, they’re coming!”

That dark slime of 그림자태생 bubbled down the streets. Teeth, nails, claws, too-human eyes. The 트롤록s came from all sides, eager for the kill. 탈마네스 struggled to draw breath.

On the walls, the calls grew excited. *We’re surrounded,* 탈마네스 thought.

*Pressed back against the wall, caught in a net. We…*

Pressed back against the wall.

“Dennel!” 탈마네스 shouted over the din. The captain of dragons turned from his line, where men waited with burning punks for the call to launch the one volley they’d have.

탈마네스 took a deep breath that made his lungs burn. “You told me that you could level an enemy bulwark in only a few shots.”

“Of course,” Dennel called. “But we're not trying to enter . . ” He trailed off.

*Light,* 탈마네스 thought. *We’re all so exhausted. We should have seen this.* “You in the middle, Ryden’s dragon squad, about-face!” 탈마네스 screamed. “The rest of you, stay in position and fire at the oncoming 트롤록s! Move, move, *mover*

The dragoners sprang into motion, Ryden and his men hastily turning their weapons about, wheels creaking. The other dragons began to fire a pattern of shot that sprayed through the streets entering the square. The booms were deafening, causing refugees to scream and cover their ears. It sounded like the end of the world. Hundreds, thousands of 트롤록s went down in pools of blood as dragons’ eggs exploded in their midst. The square filled with white smoke that poured from the mouths of the dragons.

The refugees behind, already terrified by what they had just witnessed, shrieked as Ryden’s dragons turned on them, and most of them fell to the ground in fright, clearing a path. A path that exposed the 트롤록-infested city wall. Ryden’s line of dragons bowed inward like a cup, the reverse formation of those firing into the 트롤록s behind, so that the tubes were pointed at the same section of city wall.

“Give me one of those bloody punks!” 탈마네스 shouted, holding out a hand. One of the dragoners obeyed, passing him a flaming brand with a glowing red tip. He pushed away from Melten, determined to stand on his own for the moment.

Guybon stepped up. The man’s voice sounded soft to 탈마네스’ strained ears. “Those walls have stood for hundreds of years. My poor city. My poor, poor city.”

“It’s not your city any longer,” 탈마네스 said, raising his flaming brand high in the air, defiant before a wall thick with 트롤록s, a burning city to his back. “It’s theirs.”

탈마네스 swiped the brand down in the air, leaving a trail of red. His signal ignited a roar of dragonfire that echoed throughout the square.

트롤록s—pieces of them, at least—blew into the air. The wall under them exploded like a stack of children’s blocks kicked at a full run. As 탈마네스 wavered, his vision blackening, he saw the wall crumble outward. When he toppled, slipping into unconsciousness, the ground seemed to tremble from the force of his fall.

**CHAPTER 1**

*Eastward the Wind Blew*

시간의 수레바퀴 turns, and Ages come and pass, leaving memories that become legend. Legend fades to myth, and even myth is long forgotten when the Age that gave it birth comes again. In one Age, called the Third Age by some, an Age yet to come, an Age long past, a wind rose in the Mountains of Mist. The wind was not the beginning. There are neither beginnings nor endings to the turning of the Wheel of Time. But it was *a* beginning.

Eastward the wind blew, descending from lofty mountains and coursing over desolate hills. It passed into the place known as the Westwood, an area that had once flourished with pine and leatherleaf. Here, the wind found little more than tangled underbrush, thick save around an occasional towering oak. Those looked stricken by disease, bark peeling free, branches drooping. Elsewhere needles had fallen from pines, draping the ground in a brown blanket. None of the skeletal branches of the Westwood put forth buds.

North and eastward the wind blew, across underbrush that crunched and cracked as it shook. It was night, and scrawny foxes picked over the rotting ground, searching in vain for prey or carrion. No spring birds had come to call, and—most telling—the howls of wolves had gone silent across the land.

The wind blew out of the forest and across Taren Ferry. What was left of it. The town had been a fine one, by local standards. Dark buildings, tall above their redstone foundations, a cobbled street, built at the mouth of the land known as the 두 강.

The smoke had long since stopped rising from burned buildings, but there was little left of the town to rebuild. Feral dogs hunted through the rubble for meat. They looked up as the wind passed, their eyes hungry.

The wind crossed the river eastward. Fiere, clusters of refugees carrying torches walked the long road from Baerlon to Whitebridge despite the late hour. They were sorry groups, with heads bowed, shoulders huddled. Some bore the coppery skin of 도마니, their worn clothing displaying the hardships of crossing the mountains with little in the way of supplies. Others came from farther off. 타라본ers with haunted eyes above dirty veils. Farmers and their wives from northern 게알단. All had heard rumors that in 안도르, there was food. In 안도르, there was hope.

So far, they had yet to find either.

Eastward the wind blew, along the river that wove between farms without crops. Grasslands without grass. Orchards without fruit.

Abandoned villages. Trees like bones with the flesh picked free. Ravens often clustered in their branches; starveling rabbits and sometimes larger game picked through the dead grass underneath. Above it all, the omnipresent clouds pressed down upon the land. Sometimes, that cloud cover made it impossible to tell if it was day or night.

As the wind approached the grand city of Caemlyn, it turned northward, away from the burning city—orange, red and violent, spewing black smoke toward the hungry clouds above. War had come to 안도르 in the still of night. The approaching refugees would soon discover that they’d been marching toward danger. It was not surprising. Danger was in all directions. The only way to avoid walking toward it would be to stand still.

As the wind blew northward, it passed people sitting beside roads, alone or in small groups, staring with the eyes of the hopeless. Some lay as they hungered, looking up at those rumbling, boiling clouds. Other people trudged onward, though toward what, they knew not. 최후의 전투, to the north, whatever that meant. 최후의 전투 was not hope. 최후의 전투 was death. But it was a place to *be,* a place to *go.*

In the evening dimness, the wind reached a large gathering far to the north of Caemlyn. This wide field broke the forest-patched landscape, but it was overgrown with tents like fungi on a decaying log. Tens of thousands of soldiers waited beside campfires that were quickly denuding the area of timber.

The wind blew among them, whipping smoke from fires into the faces of soldiers. The people here didn’t display the same sense of hopelessness as the refugees, but there was a dread to them. They could see the sickened land. They could feel the clouds above. They knew.

The world was dying. The soldiers stared at the flames, watching the wood be consumed. Ember by ember, what had once been alive turned to dust.

A company of men inspected armor that had begun to rust despite being well oiled. A group of white-robed 아일 collected water—former warriors who refused to take up weapons again, despite their *toh* having been served. A cluster of frightened servants, sure that tomorrow would bring war between the 백색 탑 and the 용의 환생, organized stores inside tents shaken by the wind.

Men and women whispered the truth into the night. *The end has come. The end has come. All will fall. The end has come.*

Laughter broke the air.

Warm light spilled from a large tent at the center of the camp, bursting around the tent flap and from beneath the sides.

Inside that tent, 랜드 al’Thor—the 용의 환생—laughed, head thrown back.

“So what did she do?” 랜드 asked when his laughter subsided. He poured himself a cup of red wine, then one for 페린, who blushed at the question.

*He’s become harder,* 랜드 thought, *but somehow he hasn’t lost that innocence of his. Not completely.* To 랜드, that seemed a marvelous thing. A wonder, like a pearl discovered in a trout. 페린 was strong, but his strength hadn’t broken him.

“Well,” 페린 said, “you know how Marin is. She somehow manages to look at even *Cenn* as if he were a child in need of mothering. Finding 파일 and me lying there on the floor like two fool youths… well, I think she was torn between laughing at us and sending us into the kitchen to scrub dishes. Separately, to keep us out of trouble.”

랜드 smiled, trying to picture it. 페린—burly, solid 페린—so weak he could barely walk. It was an incongruous image. 랜드 wanted to assume his friend was exaggerating, but 페린 didn’t have a dishonest hair on his head. Strange, how much about a man could change while his core remained exactly the same.

“Anyway,” 페린 said after taking a drink of wine, “파일 picked me up off the floor and set me on my horse, and the two of us pranced about looking important. I didn’t do much. The fighting was accomplished by the others—I’d have had trouble lifting a cup to my lips.” He stopped, his golden eyes growing distant. “You should be proud of them, 랜드. Without Dannil, your father and 맷’s father, without all of them, I wouldn’t have managed half what I did. No, not a tenth.”

“I believe it.” 랜드 regarded his wine. 르웨어스 테린 had loved wine. A part of 랜드—that distant part, the memories of a man he had been—was displeased by the vintage. Few wines in the current world could match the favored vintages of the 전설의 시대. Not the ones he had sampled, at least.

He took a small drink, then set the wine aside. 민 still slumbered in another part of the tent, sectioned off with a curtain. Events in 랜드’s dreams had awakened him. He had been glad for 페린’s arrival to take his mind off what he had seen.

*Mierin*… No. He would not let that woman distract him. That was probably the point of what he had seen.

“Walk with me,” 랜드 said. “I need to check on some things for tomorrow.”

They went out into the night. Several Maidens fell into step behind them as 랜드 walked toward Sebban Balwer, whose services 페린 had loaned to 랜드. Which was fine with Balwer, who was prone to gravitate toward those holding the greatest power.

“랜드?” 페린 asked, walking beside him with a hand on *Mah’alleinir.* “I’ve told you about all of this before, the siege of the 두 강, the fighting… Why ask after it again?”

“I asked about the events before, 페린. I asked after what happened, but I did not ask after the people it happened to.” He looked at 페린, making a globe of light for them to see by as they walked in the night. “I need to remember the *people.* Not doing so is a mistake I have made too often in the past.”

The stirring wind carried the scent of campfires from 페린’s nearby camp and the sounds of smiths working on weapons. 랜드 had heard the stories: Power-wrought weapons discovered again. 페린’s men were working overtime, running his two Asha’man ragged, to make as many as possible.

랜드 had lent him as many more Asha’man as he could spare, if only because—as soon as they’d heard—he’d had dozens of Maidens presenting themselves and demanding Power-wrought spearheads. *It only makes sense, 랜드 al’Thor,* Beralna had explained. *His smiths can make four spearheads for every sword.* She’d grimaced saying the word “sword,” as if it tasted like seawater.

랜드 had never tasted seawater. 르웨어스 테린 had. Knowing facts like that had greatly discomforted him once. Now he had learned to accept that part of him.

“Can you believe what has happened to us?” 페린 asked. “Light, sometimes I wonder when the man who owns all these fancy clothes is going to walk in on me and start yelling, then send me out to muck the stables for being too bigheaded for my collar.”

“수레바퀴 weaves as the Wheel wills, 페린. We've become what we needed to become.”

페린 nodded as they walked on the path between tents, lit by the glow of the light above 랜드’s hand.

“How does it… feel?” 페린 asked. “Those memories you’ve gained?”

“Have you ever had a dream that, upon waking, you remembered in stark clarity? Not one that faded quickly, but one that stayed with you through the day?”

“Yes,” 페린 said, sounding oddly reserved. “Yes, I can say that I have.”

“It’s like that,” 랜드 said. “I can remember being 르웨어스 테린, can remember doing what he did, as one remembers actions in a dream. It *was* me doing them, but I don’t necessarily like them—or think I’d take those actions if I were in my waking mind. That doesn’t change the fact that, in the dream, they seemed like the right actions.”

페린 nodded.

“He’s me,” 랜드 said. “And I’m him. But at the same time, I’m not.”

“Well, you still seem like yourself,” 페린 said, though 랜드 caught a slight hesitation on the word “seem.” Had 페린 been about to say “smell” instead? “You haven’t changed *that* much.”

랜드 doubted he could explain it to 페린 without sounding mad. The person he became when he wore the mantle of the 용의 환생… that wasn’t simply an act, wasn’t simply a mask.

It was who he was. He had not changed, he had not transformed. He had merely *accepted.*

That didn’t mean he had all of the answers. Despite four hundred years of memories nestled in his brain, he still worried about what he had to do. 르웨어스 테린 hadn’t known how to seal the 구멍. His attempt had led to disaster. The taint, the Breaking, all for an imperfect prison with seals that were now brittle.

One answer kept coming to 랜드. A dangerous answer. One that 르웨어스 테린 hadn’t considered.

What if the answer *wasn’t* to seal the 어둠의 존재 away again? What if the answer, the final answer, was something else? Something more permanent. *Yes,* 랜드 thought to himself for the hundredth time. *But is it possible?* They arrived at the tent where the clerks worked, the Maidens fanning out behind them, 랜드 and 페린 entering. The clerks were up late, of course, and they didn’t look surprised to see 랜드 enter.

“My Lord Dragon,” Balwer said, bowing stiffly from where he stood beside a table of maps and stacks of paper. The dried-up little man sorted his papers nervously, one knobby elbow protruding from a hole in his oversized brown coat.

“Report,” 랜드 said.

“Roedran will come,” Balwer said, his voice thin and precise. “The Queen of 안도르 has sent for him, promising him gateways made by those Kinswomen of hers. Our eyes in his court say he is angry that he needs her help to attend, but is insistent that he needs to be at this meeting—if only so he doesn’t look left out.”

Balwer sputtered. “Nobody—”

“She’ll have someone, Balwer,” 랜드 said with a smile. “She all but taught me how to do this, after all. No matter. After tomorrow, my intentions will be manifest for all. Secrets won’t be needed.”

*None save the ones I keep closest to my own heart.*

The shaking of the ground came suddenly. Clerks grabbed stacks of papers, holding them down and crying out as furniture crashed to the ground around them. Outside, men shouted, barely audible over the sound of trees breaking, metal clanging. The land groaned, a distant rumble.

랜드 felt it like a painful muscle spasm.

Thunder shook the sky, distant, like a promise of things to come. The shaking subsided. The clerks remained holding their stacks of paper, as if afraid to let go and risk them toppling.

*It’s really here,* 랜드 thought. *I’m not ready*—*we’re not ready—but it’s here anyway.*

He had spent many months fearing this day. Ever since 트롤록s had come in the night, ever since 란 and 모이라인 had dragged him from the 두 강, he had feared what was to come.

최후의 전투. The end. He found himself unafraid now that it had come. Worried, but not afraid.

*I’m coming for you,* 랜드 thought.
“Tell the people,” 랜드 said to his clerks. “Post warnings. Earthquakes will continue. Storms. Real ones, terrible ones. There will be a Breaking, and we cannot avoid it. 어둠의 존재 will try to grind this world to dust.”

The clerks nodded, shooting concerned glances at one another by lamplight. 페린 looked contemplative, but nodded faintly, as if to himself.

랜드 frowned, resting his hand on Laman’s sword at his waist.

“It could just be plans for tomorrow,” 페린 said.

“True,” 랜드 said. “Let me know if you discover anything, Balwer. Thank you. You do well here.”

The man stood taller. In these last days—days so dark—every man looked for something useful to do. Balwer was the best at what he did, and was confident in his own abilities. Still, it did no harm to be reminded of the fact by one who employed him, particularly if his employer was none other than the 용의 환생.

랜드 left the tent, 페린 following.

Pregnant. Pregnant with *his* children. Light! He had only just learned of it. Why hadn’t she been the one to tell him?

The answer was simple. 엘레인 could feel 랜드’s emotions as he felt hers. She would have been able to feel how he had been, recently. Before 용산. Back when…

Well, she wouldn’t have wanted to confront him with a pregnancy when he’d been in such a state. Beyond that, he hadn’t exactly made himself easy to find.

*I’m going to be a father, he thought, not for the first time. Yes, 르웨어스 테린 had had children, could remember them and his love for them. It wasn’t the same.*

He, 랜드 al’Thor, would be a father. Assuming he won the Last Battle.

“They wouldn’t have awakened 엘레인 without good reason,” he continued, returning to task. “I’m worried, not because of what might have happened, but because of the potential distraction. Tomorrow will be an important day. If the Shadow has any inkling of tomorrow’s importance, it will try whatever it can to keep us from meeting, from unifying.”

페린 scratched at his beard. “I have people close to 엘레인. People who keep watch on things for me.”

The night felt too quiet. 에그웨인, in her tent, worked on a letter to 랜드. She was not certain if she would send it. Sending it was not important. Writing it was about organizing her thoughts, determining what she wished to say to him.

가윈 pushed his way into the tent again, hand on his sword, 감시자 cloak rustling.

가윈 cocked an eyebrow at his sister. “I'm surprised you are awake.

엘레인 smiled fondly. Light, but she was smitten. I *can rely on her, can’t*

*I?* It was hard to tell with 엘레인 these days. The woman’s ploy with the Kinswomen.…

“We have unfortunately found nothing pertinent in your library *ter’angreal.”* The statue of the smiling bearded man had nearly caused a riot in the Tower; every sister had wanted to read the thousands of books that it held. “All of the books seem to have been written before the 구멍 was opened. *“The 카라에손 순환”* 엘레인 asked, curious. “ And light shall fail, and dawn shall not come, and still the captive rails.’ The captive is the 어둠의 존재?

I think so,” 에그웨인 said. “The Prophecies are never clear. 랜드 intends to enter the Last Battle and break the seals immediately, but that is a dreadful idea. We have an extended war ahead of us. Freeing the 어둠의 존재 now will strengthen the forces of the Shadow and weaken us.

“If it is to be done—and I still don’t know that it has to be—we should wait until the last possible moment. At the very least, we need to discuss it. 랜드 has been right about many things, but he has been *wrong,* too. This is not a decision he should be allowed to make alone.”

엘레인 shuffled through the sheets of paper, then stopped on one of them. “ ‘His blood shall give us the Light…’ ” She rubbed the page with her thumb, as if lost in thought. “ ‘Wait upon the Light.’ Who added this note?”

“The sisters who gathered these for me came to the same conclusion that I have,” 에그웨인 said. “There may be a time to break the seals, but that time is not at the start of the Last Battle, whatever 랜드 thinks. We must wait for the right moment, and as the Watcher of the 봉인, it is my duty to choose that moment. I won’t risk the world on one of 랜드’s overly dramatic stratagems.”

“He has a fair bit of gleeman in him,” 엘레인 said, again fondly. “Your argument is a good one, 에그웨인. Make it to him. He will listen to you. He does have a good mind, and can be persuaded.”

에그웨인 suddenly sensed a spike of alarm from 가윈. She glanced over to see him turning. Hoofbeats outside. His ears weren’t any better than 에그웨인’s, but it was his job to listen for things like this.

에그웨인 embraced the True Source, causing 엘레인 to do likewise. 비르기테 already had the tent flaps open, hand on her sword.

A frazzled messenger leaped from horseback outside, eyes wide. She scrambled into the tent, 비르기테 and 가윈 falling in beside her immediately, watching in case she came too close.

She didn’t. “Caemlyn is under attack, Your Majesty,” the woman said, gasping for breath.

The 이동 ground was not far from 엘레인’s tent. A crowd had gathered, but men and women made way for the Amyrlin and Queen. In moments the two of them reached the front.

A group of men in bloodied clothing trudged through the open gateway, pulling carts laden with 엘레인’s new weapons, the dragons. Many of the men seemed near collapse. They smelled of smoke, and their skin was blackened by soot. Not a few of them slumped unconscious as 엘레인’s soldiers grabbed the carts, which were obviously meant for horses to pull, to help them.

“Go,” 에그웨인 said to 가윈, weaving her own gateway—one to the 이동 grounds in the 백색 탑 camp nearby. “Send for as many 에스 세다이 as we can rouse. Tell Bryne to ready his soldiers, tell them to do as 엘레인 orders and send them through gateways to the outskirts of Caemlyn. We will show solidarity with 안도르.”

가윈 nodded, ducking through the gateway. 에그웨인 let it vanish, then joined 엘레인 near the gathering of wounded, confused soldiers. Sumeko, of the Kinswomen, had taken charge of seeing that 치유 was given to those in immediate danger.

Once we ... we escaped . . ” He seemed pained by something. “Once we escaped through the hole in the city wall, we found that several mercenary bands were making their way around the city toward the gate that Lord 탈마네스 had left defended. “Give your reward to the men of the Band, Your Majesty. It was their work. And please, if you can do anything for Lord 탈마네스…” He gestured to the fallen man whom several members of the Band had just carried through the gateway.

엘레인 knelt beside him, and 에그웨인 joined her. At first, 에그웨인 assumed that 탈마네스 was dead, with his skin blackened. Then he drew a ragged breath.

“에그웨인?” 엘레인 asked softly.

“Do what you can for him,” 에그웨인 said, standing and rushing away. She pushed through the confused crowd, following the voice. Was that… yes, *there.* She found an open gateway at the edge of the 이동 grounds, 에스 세다이 in a variety of clothing hurrying through to see to the wounded. 가윈 had done his work well.

니나브 was asking, quite loudly, who was in charge of this mess. 에그웨인 approached her from the side and grabbed her by the shoulder, surprising her.

니나브 drew in a sharp breath, then went to her knees and pushed 엘레인 gently aside. 니나브 Delved 탈마네스, then froze, eyes wide.

“니나브?” 에그웨인 said. “Can you—”

An *explosion* of weaves burst from 니나브 like the sudden light of a sun coming out from behind clouds. 니나브 wove the Five Powers together in a column of radiance, then sent it driving into 탈마네스’ body.

에그웨인 left her to her work. Perhaps it would be enough, though he looked far gone. 빛 willing, the man would live. She had been impressed with him in the past. He seemed precisely the type of man that the Band—and 맷—needed.

엘레인 was near the dragons and was questioning a woman with her hair in braids. That must be 알루드라, who had created the dragons. 에그웨인 walked up to the weapons, resting her fingers on one of the long bronze tubes. She had been given reports on them, of course. Some men said they were like 에스 세다이, cast in metal and fueled by the powders from 불꽃놀이.

More and more refugees poured though the gateway, many of them townspeople. “Light,” 에그웨인 said to herself. “There are too many of them. We cant house all of Caemlyn here at Merrilor.”

엘레인 finished her conversation, leaving 알루드라 to inspect the wagons. It appeared that the woman wasn’t willing to rest for the night and see to them in the morning. 엘레인 walked toward the gateways.

“The soldiers say the area outside the city is secure,” 엘레인 said, passing 에그웨인. “I’m going through to have a look.”

“엘레인…” 비르기테 said, coming up behind her.

“We’re going! Come on.”

에그웨인 left the Queen to it, stepping back to supervise the work. Romanda had taken charge of the 에스 세다이 and was organizing the injured, separating them into groups depending on the urgency of their wounds.

As 에그웨인 surveyed the chaotic mix, she noticed a pair of people standing nearby. A woman and man, 일리안ers by the looks of them. “What do you two want?”

The woman knelt before her. The fair-skinned, dark-haired woman had a firmness to her features, despite her tall, slender build. “I am Leilwin,” she said in an unmistakable accent. “I was accompanying 니나브 Sedai when the call for 치유 was raised. We followed her here.”

“You’re 쇼엔찬,” 에그웨인 said, startled.

쇼엔찬. 에그웨인 still held the 하나의 힘. Light, not *every* 쇼엔찬 she met was dangerous to her; still, she would not take chances. As some members of the Tower Guard came through one of the gateways, 에그웨인 pointed to the 쇼엔찬 pair. “Take these somewhere safe and keep watch on them. I’ll deal with them later.”

에그웨인 returned to 니나브, who still knelt beside 탈마네스. The sickness had retreated from the man’s skin, leaving it pale. “Take him somewhere to rest,” 니나브 said tiredly to several watching members of the Band. “I’ve done what I can.”

She looked up at 에그웨인 as the men carried him away. “Light,” 니나브 whispered, “that took a lot out of me. Even with my *angreal.* I’m impressed that 모이라인 managed it with Tam, all that time ago…” There seemed to be a note of pride in 니나브’s voice.

She had wanted to heal Tam, but could not—though, of course, 니나브 had not known what she had been doing at the time. She had come a long, long way since then.

“Is it true, Mother?” 니나브 asked, rising. “About Caemlyn?”

에그웨인 nodded.

“This is going to be a long night,” 니나브 said, looking at the wounded still pouring through the gateways.

“And a longer tomorrow,” 에그웨인 said. “Here, let us link. I’ll lend you my strength.”

니나브 looked shocked. “Mother?”

“You are better at 치유 than I.” 에그웨인 smiled. “I may be Amyrlin, 니나브, but I am still 에스 세다이. Servant of all. My strength will be of use to you.”

니나브 nodded and they linked. The two of them joined the group of 에스 세다이 that Romanda had set 치유 the refugees with the worst wounds.

“파일 has been organizing my network of eyes-and-ears,” 페린 said to 랜드 as the two of them hurried toward 페린’s camp. “She might be there with them tonight. I’ll warn you, I’m not certain she likes you.”

*She would be a fool to like me,* 랜드 thought. *She probably knows what I’m going to require of you before this is over.*

An amazing piece of work. 랜드 kept intending to ask whether it was one of the Power-wrought weapons his Asha’man had been making— “But 랜드, you’re not. You don’t seem at all crazy to me.”

랜드 smiled, and a thought fluttered at the edge of his mind. “I *am* mad, 페린. My madness is these memories, these impulses. 르웨어스 테린 tried to take over. I was two people, fighting over control of myself. And one of them was completely insane.”

“Light,” 페린 whispered, “that sounds horrible.”

“It wasn’t pleasant. But… here’s the thing, 페린. I’m increasingly certain that I needed these memories. 르웨어스 테린 was a good man. I was a good man, but things went wrong—I grew too arrogant, I assumed I could do everything myself. I needed to remember that; without the madness… without these memories, I might have gone charging in alone again.”

“So you are going to work with the others?” 페린 asked, looking up toward where 에그웨인 and the other members of the 백색 탑 were camped. “This looks an *awful* lot like armies gathering to fight one another.

I’ll make 에그웨인 see sense,” 랜드 said. “I’m right, 페린. We need to break the seals. I don’t know why she denies this.”

“She’s the Amyrlin now.” 페린 rubbed his chin. “She’s Watcher of the 봉인, 랜드. It’s up to her to make sure they’re cared for.”

“랜드,” 페린 said, “that’s the most reasonable thing anyone has said on this topic. Have you explained it that way to 에그웨인?”

페린 stopped walking, his face lit by the glow of 랜드’s Power-summoned orb. His camp, beside 랜드’s, contained a force as large as any on the field. 랜드 still found it incredible that 페린 had gathered so many, including—of all things—the 백의단. 랜드’s eyes-and-ears indicated that everyone in 페린’s camp seemed loyal to him. Even the 현명한 이들 and 에스 세다이 with him were more inclined to do what 페린 said than not.

Sure as the wind and the sky, 페린 had become a king. A different kind of king than 랜드—a king of his people, who lived among them. 랜드 couldn’t take that same path. 페린 could be a man. 랜드 had to be something more, for a little time yet. He had to be a symbol, a force that everyone could rely upon.

That was terribly tiring. Not all of it was physical fatigue, but instead something deeper. Being what people needed was wearing on him, grinding as surely as a river cut at a mountain. In the end, the river would always win.

“I’ll support you in this, 랜드,” 페린 said. “But I want you to promise me that you won’t let it come to blows. I won’t fight 엘레인. Going up against the 에스 세다이 would be worse. We can’t afford to squabble.”

“There won’t be fighting.”

“Promise me.” 페린’s face grew so hard, one could have broken rocks against it. “Promise me, 랜드.”

“I promise it, my friend. I’ll bring us to the Last Battle united.”

“That’ll do, then.” 페린 walked into his camp, nodding to the sentries. 두 강 men, both of them—Reed Soalen and Kert Wagoner. They saluted 페린, then eyed 랜드 and bowed somewhat awkwardly.

Reed and Kert. He’d known them both—Light, he’d looked up to them, as a child—but 랜드 had grown accustomed to people he’d known treating him as a stranger. He felt the mantle of the 용의 환생 harden upon him.

“My Lord Dragon,” Kert said. “Are we ... I mean…” He gulped and looked at the sky, and the clouds that seemed to be—despite 랜드’s presence—creeping in on them. “Things look bad, don’t they?”

“The storms are often bad, Kert,” 랜드 said. “But the 두 강 survives them. Such it will do again.”

“But . . ” Kert said again. “It looks bad. Light burn me, but it does.”

“It will be as the Wheel wills,” 랜드 said, glancing northward. “Peace, Kert, Reed,” 랜드 said softly. “The Prophecies have nearly all been fulfilled. This day was seen, and our tests are known. We do not walk into them unaware.”

He hadn’t promised them they would win or that they would survive, but both men stood up straighter and nodded, smiling. People liked to know that there was a plan. The knowledge that someone was in control might be the strongest comfort that 랜드 could offer them.

“That’s enough bothering the Lord Dragon with your questions,” 페린 said. “Make sure you guard this post well—no dozing, Kert, and no dicing.”

Both men saluted again as 페린 and 랜드 passed into the camp. There was more cheer here than there was in other camps on the Field. The campfires seemed faintly brighter, the laughter faintly louder. It was as if the 두 강 folk had managed, somehow, to bring *home* with them.

“You lead them well,” 랜드 said softly, moving quickly beside 페린, who nodded toward those out at night.

“They shouldn’t need me to tell them what to do, and that’s that.” However, when a messenger came running into camp, 페린 was immediately in charge. He called the spindly youth by name and, seeing the boy’s flushed face and trembling legs—he was frightened of 랜드—페린 pulled him aside and spoke softly, but firmly, with him.

페린 sent the boy off to find Lady 파일, then stepped over. “I need to talk to 랜드 again.”

“You’re talking to—”

“I need the real 랜드, not the man who’s learned to talk like an 에스 세다이.”

랜드 sighed. “It really *is* me, 페린,” he protested. “I’m more me than I’ve been for ages.”

“Yes, well, I don’t like talking to you when your emotions are all masked.”

A group of 두 강 men passed and saluted. He felt a sudden spike of cold solitude at seeing those men and knowing he could never be one of them again. It was hardest with the 두 강 men. But he did let himself be more… relaxed, for 페린’s sake.

“So, what was it?” he asked. “What did the messenger say?”

“You were right to be worried,” 페린 said. “랜드, Caemlyn has fallen. It’s overrun with 트롤록s.”

랜드 felt his face grow hard.

“You’re not surprised,” 페린 said. “You’re worried, but not surprised.

No, I’m not,” 랜드 admitted. “I thought it would be the south where they struck—I’ve heard word of 트롤록 sightings there, and I’m half-certain that 디만드레드 is involved. He has never been comfortable without an army. But Caemlyn… yes, it’s a clever strike. I told you they would try to distract us. If they can undercut 안도르 and draw her away, my alliance grows much shakier.”

페린 glanced at where 엘레인’s camp was set up right beside that of 에그웨인. “But wouldn’t it be good for you if 엘레인 ran off? She’s on the other side of this confrontation.”

“There is no other side, 페린. There is *one* side, with a disagreement on how that side should proceed. If 엘레인 isn’t here to be part of the meeting, it will undermine everything I’m trying to accomplish. She’s probably the most powerful of all the rulers.”

랜드 could feel her, of course, through the bond. Her spike of alarm let him know that she’d received this information. Should he go to her? Perhaps he could send 민. She had gotten up, and was moving away from the tent where he’d left her. And—

He blinked. 아비엔다. She was here, at Merrilor. She hadn’t been here moments ago, had she? 페린 glanced at him, and he didn’t bother to wipe the shock from his face.

“We can’t let 엘레인 leave,” 랜드 said.

“Not even to protect her homeland?” 페린 asked, incredulous.
“If the 트롤록s have already taken Caemlyn, then it’s too late for 엘레인 to do anything meaningful. 엘레인’s forces will focus on evacuation. She doesn’t need to be there for that, but she *does* need to be here. Tomorrow morning.”

How could he make certain she stayed? 엘레인 reacted poorly to being told what to do—all women did—but if he implied…

“랜드,” 페린 said, “what if we sent in the Asha’man? All of them? We could make a fight of it at Caemlyn.”

“No,” 랜드 said, though the word hurt. “페린, if the city really is overrun—I’ll send men through gateways to be certain—then it’s lost. Taking back those walls would take far too much effort, at least right now. We *cannot* let this coalition break apart before I have a chance to forge it together. Unity will preserve us. If each of us goes running off to put out fires in our homelands, then we will lose. That’s what this attack is about.”

“I suppose that’s possible . . 페린 said, fingering his hammer.

“The attack might unnerve 엘레인, make her more eager to act,” 랜드 said, considering a dozen different lines of action. “Perhaps this will make her more vulnerable to agreeing with my plan. This could be a good thing.” 페린 frowned.

*How quickly I’ve learned to use others.* He had learned to laugh again. He had learned to accept his fate, and to charge toward it smiling. He had learned to be at peace with who he had been, what he had done.

That understanding would not stop him from using the tools given him. He needed them, needed them all. The difference now was that he would see the people they were, not just the tools he would use. So he told himself.

“I still think we should do something to help 안도르,” 페린 said, scratching his beard. “How did they sneak in, do you think?”

“By Waygate,” 랜드 said absently.

페린 grunted. “Well, you said that 트롤록s can’t Travel through gateways; could they have learned how to fix that?”

“Pray to the Light they haven’t,” 랜드 said. “The only 그림자태생 they managed to make that could go through gateways were *gholam*, and 아지노르 wasn’t foolish enough to make more than a few of *those.* No, I’d bet against 맷 himself that this was the Caemlyn Waygate. I thought she had that thing guarded!”

“If it *was* the Waygate, we can do something,” 페린 said. “We can’t have 트롤록s rampaging in 안도르; if they leave Caemlyn, they’ll be at our backs, and that will be a disaster. But if they’re coming in at a single point, we might be able to disrupt their invasion with an attack on that point.” 랜드 grinned.

“What’s so funny?”

“At least I have an excuse for knowing and understanding things no youth from the 두 강 should.”

페린 snorted. “Go jump in the Winespring Water. You really think this is 디만드레드?”

“It’s exactly the sort of thing he’d try. Separate your foes, then crush them one at a time. It’s one of the oldest strategies in warfare.”

디만드레드 himself had discovered it in the old writings. They’d known nothing of war when the 구멍 had first opened. Oh, they’d *thought* they understood it, but it had been the understanding of the scholar looking back on something ancient, dusty.

Of all those to turn to the Shadow, 디만드레드’s betrayal seemed the most tragic. The man could have been a hero. *Should* have been a hero.

*I’m to blame for that*, *too,* 랜드 thought. *If I’d offered a hand instead of a smirk, if I'd congratulated instead of competed. If I’d been the man then that I am now. . .*

Never mind that. He had to send to 엘레인. The proper course was to send help for evacuating the city, Asha’man and loyal 에스 세다이 to make gateways and free as many people as possible—and to make certain that for now, the 트롤록s remained in Caemlyn.

“Well, I guess those memories of yours are good for something, then,” 페린 said.

“Do you want to know the thing that twists my brain in knots, 페린?” 랜드 said softly. “The thing that gives me shivers, like the cold breath of the Shadow itself? The taint is what made me mad *and* what gave me memories from my past life. They came as 르웨어스 테린 whispering to me. But that very insanity is the thing giving me the clues I need to win. Don’t you see? If I win this, it will be the *taint itself* that led to the 어둠의 존재’s fall.”

페린 whistled softly.

*Redemption,* 랜드 thought. *When I tried this last time, my madness destroyed us.* *This time, it will save us.*

“Go to your wife, 페린,” 랜드 said, glancing at the sky. “This is the last night of anything resembling peace you shall know before the end. I’ll investigate and see how bad things are in 안도르.” He looked back at his friend. “I will not forget my promise. *Unity* must come before all else. I lost last time precisely because I threw unity aside.”

페린 nodded, then rested a hand on 랜드’s shoulder. “빛 illumine you.”

“And you, my friend.”
