**CHAPTER 2**

![](images/00109.jpg)

*The Choice of an 아자*

페바라 did her very best to pretend that she was not terrified.

If these Asha’man had known her, they’d have realized that sitting still and quiet was not her natural state. She retreated to basic 에스 세다이 training: *appearing* in control when she felt anything but.

She forced herself to rise. Canler and 에마린 had withdrawn to visit the 두 강 lads and make sure they were going about in pairs. That left only her and 안드롤 again. He quietly tinkered with his leather straps as the rain continued outside. He used two needles at once to stitch, crossing the holes on either side. The man had the concentration of a master craftsman.

페바라 strolled over, causing him to look up sharply when she drew close. She smothered a smile. She might not look it, but she could move silently, when necessary.

She stared out of the windows. The rain had grown worse, splashing curtains of water against the glass. “After so many weeks of *looking* as if it would storm at any moment, it finally comes.”

“Those clouds had to break open eventually,” 안드롤 said.

“The rain doesn’t feel natural,” she said, hands clasped behind her. She could feel the coldness through the glass. “It doesn’t ebb and flow. Just the same steady torrent. A great deal of lightning, but very little thunder.

“You think it’s one of those?” 안드롤 asked. He didn’t need to say what “those” meant. Earlier in the week, common people in the Tower—none of the Asha’man—had begun bursting into flame. Just… flame, inexplicably. They’d lost some forty people. Many still blamed a rogue Asha’man, though the men had sworn nobody had been channeling nearby.

She shook her head, watching a group of people trudge past on the muddy street outside. She had been one of those, at first, who had called the deaths the work of an Asha’man gone mad. Now she accepted these events, and other oddities, as something far worse.

The world was unraveling.

She needed to be strong. 페바라 herself had devised the plan of bringing women here to bond these men, though Tarna had suggested it. She couldn’t let them discover how disturbing she found it to be trapped in here, facing down enemies who could force a person to the Shadow. Her only allies men who, only months ago, she would have pursued with diligence and gentled without remorse.

She sat down on the stool 에마린 had used earlier. “I would like to discuss this ‘plan’ you are developing.”

“I’m not sure I’ve actually developed one yet, 에스 세다이.”

“I might be able to offer some suggestions.”

“I wouldn’t say no to hearing them,” 안드롤 said, though he narrowed his eyes.

“What’s wrong?” she asked.

“Those people outside. I don’t recognize them. And…”

She looked back out the window. The only light came from buildings, shining an occasional red-orange glow into the drenched night. The passersby still moved very slowly down the street, in and out of the light of windows.

“Their clothing isn’t wet,” 안드롤 whispered.

With a chill, 페바라 realized he was right. The man at the front walked with a wide-brimmed, drooping hat on his head, but it didn’t break the rain or stream water. His rustic clothing was untouched by the downpour. And the dress of the woman beside him wasn’t blowing at all in the wind. Now 페바라 saw that one of the younger men was holding his hand behind him, as if pulling the reins of a pack animal—but there was no animal there.

페바라 and 안드롤 watched in silence until the figures passed too far into the night to be seen. Visions of the dead were growing increasingly common.

“You said you had a suggestion?” 안드롤’s voice trembled.

“I… Yes.” 페바라 tore her eyes away from the window. “So far, 타임’s focus has been on the 에스 세다이. My sisters have all been taken. I am the last.”

“You’re offering yourself as bait.”

“They *will* come for me,” she said. “It is only a matter of time.”

안드롤 fingered the leather strap and looked pleased with it. “We should sneak you out.”

“Is that so?” she said, eyebrow raised. “I have been elevated to the position of maiden in need of rescue, have I? Very valiant of you.”

He blushed. “Sarcasm? From an 에스 세다이? I wouldn’t have thought I’d hear that.”

페바라 laughed. “Oh my, 안드롤. You really don’t know *anything* about us, do you?”

“Honestly? No. I’ve avoided your kind for most of my life.”

“Well, considering your… innate tendencies, perhaps that was wise.”

“I couldn’t channel before.”

“But you suspected. You came here to learn.”

“I was curious,” he said. “It’s something I hadn’t tried before.”

*Interesting,* 페바라 thought. *Is that what drives you then, leatherworker? What has set you drifting on the winds, from place to place?*

“I suspect,” she said, “you have never tried jumping off a cliff before. The fact that you haven’t done something shouldn’t *always* be a reason to try it.”

“Actually, I have jumped off a cliff. Several of them.”

She raised an eyebrow at him.

“The Sea Folk do it,” he explained. “Off into the ocean. The braver you are, the higher the cliff you choose. And you have changed the topic of the conversation again, 페바라 Sedai. You are quite skilled at that.”

“Thank you.”

“The reason,” he said, holding up a finger, “that I suggested we sneak you out is because this isn’t your battle. You shouldn’t have to fall here.”

“It isn’t because you want to hurry an 에스 세다이 away, out of meddling in your business?”

“I came to you for help,” 안드롤 said. “I don’t want to be rid of you; I’ll happily use you. However, if you fall here, you do so in a fight that is not your own. That isn’t fair.”

“Let me explain something to you, Asha’man,” 페바라 said, leaning in. “This *is* my fight. If the Shadow takes this tower, it will mean terrible things for the Last Battle. I have accepted responsibility for you and yours; I will not turn away from it so easily.”

“You’ve accepted responsibility’ for us? What does that mean?”

*Ah, perhaps I shouldn’t have shared that.* Still, if they were going to be allies, perhaps he needed to know.

“The 검은 탑 needs guidance,” she explained.

“So that’s the point of bonding us?” 안드롤 asked. “So we can be… corralled, like stallions to be broken?”

“Don’t be a fool. Surely you admit the value of the 백색 탑’s experience.”

“I’m not sure I’d say that,” 안드롤 said. “With experience comes a determination to be set in your ways, to avoid new experiences. You 에스 세다이 all assume that the way things have been done is the only way to do them. Well, the 검은 탑 will not be subject to you. We can look after ourselves.”

“And you’ve done a *wonderful* job of that so far, haven’t you?”

“That was unfair,” he said softly.

“Perhaps it was,” she admitted. “I’m sorry.”

“Your motivations don’t surprise me,” he said. “What you were doing here was obvious to the weakest of soldiers. The question I’ve had is this: Why, of all women, did the 백색 탑 send *Red* sisters to bond us?”

“Who better? Our entire lives have been dedicated to dealing with men who can channel.”

“Your 아자 is doomed.”

“Is that so?”

“You exist to hunt down men who can channel,” he said. “To gentle them. See them… disposed of. Well, the Source is cleansed—”

“So you all say.”

“It *is* cleansed, 페바라. All things come and pass, and the Wheel turns. It was once pure, so it must someday be pure again. It has happened.”

*And the way you look at shadows, 안드롤? Is that a sign of purity? The way that 날람 mutters in unknown languages? Do you think we don't notice such things?*

“You have two choices, as an 아자,” 안드롤 continued. “You can either continue to hunt us—ignoring the proof that we offer, that the Source is cleansed—or you can give up on being 적색 아자.”

“Nonsense. Of all 아자s, the Reds should be your greatest ally.”

“You exist to destroy us!”

“We exist to make certain that men who can channel do not accidentally hurt themselves or those around them. Would you not agree that is a purpose of the 검은 탑 as well?”

“I suppose that might be part of it. The only purpose I have been told was that we are to be a weapon for the 용의 환생, but keeping good men from hurting themselves without proper training is important as well.”

“Then we can unite on that idea, can we not?”

“I would like to believe that, 페바라, but I’ve seen the way you and yours look at us. You see us as ... as some stain that needs to be cleansed, or poison to be bottled.”

페바라 shook her head. “If what you say is true, and the Source is cleansed, then changes *will* come, 안드롤. The 적색 아자 and the Asha’man will grow together in common purpose, over time. I’m willing to work with you now, here.”

“Contain us.”

“Guide you. Please. Trust me.”

He studied her by the light of the room’s many lamps. He did have a sincere face. She could see why the others followed him, though he was weakest among them. He had a strange mixture of passion and humility. If only he hadn’t been one of. . . well… what he was.

“I wish I could believe you,” 안드롤 said, looking away. “You’re different from the others, I’ll admit. Not like a Red at all.”

“I think you’ll find we’re more varied than you suppose,” 페바라 said. “There isn’t one single motive that makes a woman choose the Red.”

“Other than hatred of men.”

“If we hated you, would we have come here looking to bond you?” That was a sidestep, in truth. Though 페바라 herself did not hate men, many Reds did—at the very least, many regarded men with suspicion. She hoped to change that.

“에스 세다이 motivations are odd sometimes,” 안드롤 said. “Everyone knows that. Anyway, different though you are from many of your sisters, I’ve seen that look in your eyes.” He shook his head. “I won’t believe you’re here to help us. No more than I believed that the 에스 세다이 who hunted down male channelers really thought they were helping the men. No more than I believe a headsman thinks he’s doing a criminal a favor by killing him. Just because a thing needs to be done doesn’t make the one doing it a friend, 페바라 Sedai. I’m sorry.”

He turned back to his leather, working by the close light of a lantern on the table.

페바라 found her annoyance rising. She’d almost had him. She *liked* men; she had often thought 감시자s would be useful. Couldn’t the fool recognize a hand extended across the chasm when he saw it?

*Calm yourself, 페바라*, she thought. *You won’t get anywhere if anger rules you.* She needed this man on her side.

“That will be a saddle, won’t it?” she said.

“Yes.”

“You’re staggering the stitches.”

“It’s my own method,” he said. “Helps prevent rips from spreading. I think it looks nice, too.”

“Good linen thread, I assume? Waxed? And do you use a single lacing chisel for those holes, or a double? I didn’t get a good look.”

He glanced at her, wary. “You know leatherworking?”

“From my uncle,” she said. “He taught me a few things. Let me work in the shop, when I was little.”

“Maybe I’ve met him.”

She fell still. For all 안드롤’s comments that she was good at steering a conversation, she had blundered this one directly into places she didn’t like to go.

“Well?” he asked. “Where does he live?”

“Back in 캔도르.”

“You’re *캔도리”* he asked, surprised.

“Of course I am. Don’t I look it?”

“I just thought I could pick out any accent,” he said, pulling a pair of stitches tight. “I’ve been there. Maybe I do know your uncle.”

“He’s dead,” she said. “Murdered by 어둠의 친구들.”

안드롤 fell silent. “I’m sorry.”

“It’s been over a hundred years now. I miss my family, but they’d be dead by now even if the 어둠의 친구들 hadn’t killed them. Everyone I knew back home is dead.”

“My sorrow is deeper, then. Truly.”

“It is long past,” 페바라 said. “I can remember them with fondness without having the pain intrude. But what of your family? Siblings? Nieces, nephews?”

“A smattering of each group,” 안드롤 said.

“Do you ever see them?”

He eyed her. “You’re trying to engage me in friendly conversation to prove that you don’t feel awkward around me. But I’ve seen how you 에스 세다이 look at people like me.”

“I—”

“Say you don’t find us repulsive.”

“I hardly think what you do should be—”

“Straight answer, 페바라.”

“Very well, fine. Men who can channel *do* discomfort me. You make me itch all over, and it has only grown worse the longer I’ve been here, surrounded by you.”

안드롤 nodded in satisfaction at having pulled it from her.

“However,” 페바라 continued, “I feel this way because it has been ingrained in me over decades of life. What you do is terribly unnatural, but you yourself do *not* disgust me. You are just a man trying to do your best, and I hardly think that is worthy of disgust. Either way, I am willing to look beyond my inhibitions in the name of common good.”

“That’s better than I could have expected, I suppose.” He looked back toward the rain-splattered windows. “The taint is cleansed. This isn’t unnatural any longer. I wish ... I wish I could just *show* you, woman.” He looked toward her sharply. “How does one form one of those circles you mentioned?”

“Well,” 페바라 said, “I’ve never actually done it with a male channeler, of course. I did some reading before coming down here, but much of what we have is hearsay. So much has been lost. To start with, you must put yourself on the edge of embracing the Source, then open yourself to me. That is how we establish the link.”

“All right,” he said. “You’re not holding the Source, however.”

It was downright unfair, that a man could tell when a woman was holding the 하나의 힘 and when she wasn’t. 페바라 embraced the Source, flooding herself with the sweet nectar that was *세다르.*

She reached out to link with 안드롤 as she would with a woman. That was how one was supposed to begin, according to the records. But it was not the same. *Saidin* was a torrent, and what she had read was true; she could do nothing with the flows.

“It’s working; my power is flowing into you.”

“Yes,” 페바라 said. “But when a man and woman link, the man must be in control. You must take the lead.”

“How?” 안드롤 asked.

“I don’t know. I’ll try to pass it. You *must* control the flows.”

He eyed her, and she prepared herself to pass control to him. Instead, he somehow *seized* it. She was caught in the tempestuous link, yanked—as if by her hair—right in.

The force of it nearly made her teeth rattle, and it felt as if her skin was being pulled off. 페바라 closed her eyes, breathed deeply, and did not let herself fight back. She had wanted to try this; it could be useful. But she couldn’t help a moment of sheer panic.

She was linked with a *male channeler*,; one of the most feared things the land had ever known. Now he had control of her, completely. Her Power flowed through her, washing over him, and 안드롤 gasped.

“So much…” he said. “Light, you’re strong.”

She allowed herself a smile. The link brought with it a storm of awareness. She could feel 안드롤’s emotions. He was as fearful as she was. He was also *solid.* She’d imagined that being linked to him would be terrible, because of his madness, but she sensed none of it.

But *세이딘*… that liquid fire that he wrestled with, like a serpent that was trying to consume him. She pulled back. Was it tainted? She wasn’t certain she could tell. *Saidin* was so different, so alien. Reports from the early days fragmented, spoke of the taint like an oil slick upon a river. Well, she could see a river—more a stream, really. It appeared that 안드롤 had been honest with her, and wasn’t very powerful. She could not sense any taint— but then again, she did not know what to look for.

“I wonder . .” 안드롤 said. “I wonder if I can make a gateway with this power.”

“관문s don’t work in the 검은 탑 anymore.”

“I know,” he said. “But I keep feeling that they’re just beyond my fingertips.”

페바라 opened her eyes, looking at him. She could feel his honesty within the circle, but creating a gateway required a *lot* of the 하나의 힘, at least for a woman. 안드롤 would have to be orders of magnitude too weak for that weave. Could it require a different level of strength for a man?

He reached out a hand, using her Power somehow, mixed with his own. She could feel him pulling the 하나의 힘 through her. 페바라 tried to maintain her composure, but she did not like him having control. She could do nothing!

“안드롤,” she said. “Release me.”

“It’s wonderful…” he whispered, eyes unfocused as he stood up. “Is this what it feels like, to be one of the others? Those with strength in the Power?”

He drew more of her power and used it. Objects in the room began to rise into the air.

“안드롤!” Panic. It was the panic she’d felt after hearing that her parents were dead. She hadn’t known this sense of horror in over a hundred years, not since taking the test for her shawl.

He had control of her channeling. Absolute control. She began to gasp, trying to reach for him. She could not use *세다르* without him releasing it back to her—but he could use it against her. Images of him using her own strength to tie her in Air ran through her mind. She could not end the link. Only he could.

He noticed, suddenly, and his eyes widened. The circle vanished like a wink of the eye, and her power was her own again. Without thinking, she lashed out. This would not happen again. *She* would have the control. The weaves sprang from her before she knew what she was doing.

안드롤 fell to his knees, hand sweeping across his table as he threw his head back, brushing tools and scraps of leather to the floor. He gasped. “What have you done?”

“타임 said we could pick any of you,” 페바라 muttered as she realized what she *had* done. She’d bonded him. The reverse, after a fashion, of what he’d done to her. She tried to calm her thundering heart. An awareness of him blossomed in the back of her mind, like what they’d known in the circle, but somehow more personal. Intimate.

“타임 is a monster!” 안드롤 growled. “You know that. You take his word on what you can do, and you do it without my permission?”

“I… I…”

안드롤 clenched his jaw, and 페바라 immediately felt *something.* Something alien, something strange. It felt like looking at herself. Feeling her emotions circled back on her endlessly.

Her *self* melded with *his* for a seeming eternity. She knew what it was like to be him, think his thoughts. She saw his life in the blink of an eye, was absorbed by his memories. She gasped and fell to her knees in front of him.

It faded. Not completely, but it faded. It felt like swimming a hundred leagues through boiling water, and only now emerging, having forgotten what it was like to have normal sensations.

“Light . .” she whispered. “What was that?”

He lay on his back. When had he fallen? He blinked, looking up at the ceiling. “I saw one of the others do it. Some of the Asha’man bond their wives.”

“You *bonded* me?” she said, horrified.

He groaned, rolling over. “You did it to me first.”

She realized, with horror, that she could still feel his emotions. His self. She could even understand some of what he was thinking. Not the actual thoughts, but some impressions of them.

He was confused, worried and… curious. He was curious about the new experience. *Foolish man!*

She’d hoped that the two bonds would have somehow canceled one another out. They did not. “We have to stop this,” she said. “I’ll release you. I vow it. Just… just release me.”

“I don’t know how,” he said, standing up and breathing in deeply. “I’m sorry.”

He was telling the truth. “That circle was a bad idea,” she said. He offered a hand to help her to her feet. She stood on her own without accepting it.

“I believe it was *your* bad idea before it was mine.”

“So it was,” she admitted. “It isn’t my first one, but it might be one of my worst.” She sat down. “We need to think through this. Find a way to—”

The door to his shop slammed open.

안드롤 spun, and 페바라 embraced the Source. 안드롤 had grabbed his stitching groover in one hand like a weapon. He’d also seized the 하나의 힘. She could sense that molten force within him—weak because of his lack of talent, like a single small jet of magma, but still burning and hot. She could feel his awe. So it was the same for him as it was for her. Holding the 하나의 힘 felt like opening your eyes for the first time, the world coming to life.

Fortunately, neither weapon nor the 하나의 힘 was needed. Young Evin stood in the doorway, raindrops dribbling down the sides of his face. He shut the door and hurried to 안드롤’s workbench.

“안드롤, it—” He froze, seeing 페바라.

“Evin,” 안드롤 said. “You’re alone.”

“I left 날람 to watch,” he said, breathing in and out. “It was important, 안드롤.”

“We are *never* to be alone, Evin,” 안드롤 said. “Never. Always in pairs. No matter the emergency.”

“I know, I know,” Evin said. “I’m sorry. It’s just—the news, 안드롤.” He glanced at 페바라.

“Speak,” 안드롤 said.

“웰린 and his 에스 세다이 are back,” Ewan said.

페바라 could feel 안드롤’s sudden tension. “Is he… one of us, still?”

Evin shook his head, sick. “He’s one of them. Probably Jenare Sedai is, too. I don’t know her well enough to tell for sure. 웰린, though… his eyes aren’t his own any longer, and he now serves 타임.”

안드롤 groaned. 웰린 had been with 로가인. 안드롤 and the others had been holding to the hope that although 메자르 had been taken, 로가인 and 웰린 were still free.

“로가인?” 안드롤 whispered.

“He isn’t here,” Evin said, “but 안드롤, 웰린 says 로가인 will come back soon—and that he’s met with 타임, and they have reconciled their differences. 웰린 is promising that 로가인 will come tomorrow to prove it. 안드롤… that’s it. We have to admit it now. They have him.”

페바라 could feel 안드롤’s agreement, and his horror. It mirrored her own.

아비엔다 moved through the darkened camps silently.

So many groups. There had to be at least a hundred thousand people gathered here at the Field of Merrilor. All waiting. Like a breath taken in and held before a great leap.
The 아일 saw her, but she did not approach them. The wetlanders didn’t notice her, save for a 감시자 who spotted her as she skirted the 에스 세다이 camp. That camp was a place of motion and activity. Something had happened, though she caught only fragments. A 트롤록 attack somewhere?

She listened enough to determine that the attack was in 안도르, in the city of Caemlyn. There was worry the 트롤록s would leave the city and rampage across the land.

She needed to know more; would the spears be danced tonight? Perhaps 엘레인 would share news with her. 아비엔다 moved silently out of the 에스 세다이 camp. Stepping softly in these wet lands, with their lush plants, presented different challenges than the Three-fold 란d did. There, the dry ground was often dusty, which could muffle footsteps. Here, a dry twig could inexplicably be buried beneath wet grass.

She tried not to think about how dead that grass seemed. Once, she’d have considered those browns lush. Now, she knew these wetland plants should *not* look so wan and… and hollow.

Hollow plants. What was she thinking? She shook her head and crept through the shadows out of the 에스 세다이 camp. She briefly contemplated sneaking back to surprise that 감시자—he’d been hiding in a moss-worn cleft in the rubble of an old, fallen building and watching the 에스 세다이 perimeter—but discarded the idea. She wanted to get to 엘레인 and ask her for details on the attack.

아비엔다 approached another busy camp, ducked beneath the leafless branches of a tree—she didn’t know what type, but its limbs spread wide and high—and slipped inside the guard perimeter. A pair of wetlanders in white and red stood on “watch” near a fire. They didn’t come close to spotting her, though they did jump up and level polearms toward a thicket a good thirty feet away when an animal rustled in it.

아비엔다 shook her head and passed them.

Forward. She needed to keep moving forward. What to do about 랜드 al’Thor? What were his plans for tomorrow? These were other questions she wanted to ask 엘레인.

The 아일 needed a purpose once 랜드 al’Thor finished with them. That was clear from the visions. She had to find a way to give this to them. Perhaps they should return to the Three-fold 란d. But… no. No. It tore her heart, but she had to admit that if the 아일 did so, they would be going to their graves. Their death, as a people, might not be immediate, but it would come. The changing world, with new devices and new ways of fighting, would overtake the 아일, and the 쇼엔찬 would never leave them alone. Not with women who could channel. Not with armies full of spears that could, at any time, invade.

A patrol approached. 아비엔다 drew some fallen brown undergrowth over herself for camouflage, then lay down flat beside a dead shrub and remained perfectly still. The guards walked two handspans from her.

*We could attack the 쇼엔찬 now,* she thought. *In my vision, the 아일 waited nearly a generation to attack—and that let the 쇼엔찬 strengthen their position.*

The 아일 already spoke of the 쇼엔찬 and the confrontation that must inevitably come. The 쇼엔찬 would force it, everyone whispered. Except, in her vision, years had passed with the 쇼엔찬 failing to attack. Why? What could possibly have held them back?

아비엔다 rose and crept across to the pathway the guards had taken. She took out her knife and rammed it down into the ground. She left it there, right beside a lantern on a pole, clearly visible even to wetlander eyes. Then she slipped back into the night, hiding near the back of the large tent that was her goal.

She crouched low and practiced her silent breathing, using the rhythm to calm herself. There were hushed, anxious voices inside the tent. 아비엔다 did her best not to pay attention to what they were saying. It wouldn’t be proper to eavesdrop.

As the patrol passed again, she stood up. When they cried out, having found her dagger, she slipped around to the front of the tent. There, avoiding the attention of guards distracted by the commotion, she lifted the flap and stepped inside the tent behind them.

Some people sat at a table on the far side of the very large tent, huddled around a lamp. They were so busy with their conversation that they did not see her, so she settled down near some cushions to wait.

It was very hard not to listen in, now that she was so close.

“. . . *must* send our forces back!” one man barked. “The fall of the capital is a symbol, Your Majesty. A *symbol!* We cannot let Caemlyn go or the entire nation will collapse into chaos.”

“You underestimate the strength of the 안도르an people,” said 엘레인. She looked very much in control, very strong, her red-gold hair practically glowing in the lamplight. Several of her battle commanders stood behind her, lending authority and a sense of stability to the meeting. 아비엔다 was pleased to see the fire in her first-sister’s eyes.

“I have been to Caemlyn, Lord Lir,” 엘레인 continued. “And I have left a small force of soldiers there to watch and give warning if the 트롤록s leave the city. Our spies will use gateways to sneak through the city and find where the remaining 트롤록s are herding captives, and then we can mount rescue operations if the 트롤록s continue to hold the city.”

“But the city itself!” Lord Lir said.

“Caemlyn is lost, Lir,” Lady Dyelin snapped. “We’d be fools to try to mount any kind of assault now.”

엘레인 nodded. “I have held conference with the other High Seats, and they agree with my assessment. For now, the refugees who escaped are safe—I sent them on along toward Whitebridge with guards. If there are people alive within, we will try to rescue them with gateways, but I will *not* commit my forces to an all-out attack on Caemlyn’s walls.”

“But—”

“Taking the city again would be fruitless,” 엘레인 said, voice hard. “I know full well the damage that can be done to an army assaulting those walls! 안도르 will not collapse because of the loss of one city, no matter how important a city.” Her face was a mask, her voice as cold as good steel.

“The 트롤록s will eventually leave the city,” 엘레인 continued. “They gain nothing by holding it—they will starve themselves out, if nothing else. Once they leave, we can fight them—and on far fairer ground. If you wish, Lord Lir, you may visit the city yourself and see that what I say is true. The soldiers there could use the inspiration of a High Seat.”

Lir frowned, but nodded. “I think I will.”

“Then go knowing my plan. We will begin sending in scouts before the night is through, trying to find pens of civilians to save, and *아비엔다, what in the name of a bloody goat's left stone are you doing!”*

아비엔다 looked up from trimming her fingernails with her second knife. *Bloody goat’s left stone*? That was a new one. 엘레인 always knew the most interesting curses.

The three High Seats at the table jumped up, scrambling, throwing down chairs and reaching for swords. 엘레인 sat in her place, eyes and mouth wide.

“It is a bad habit,” 아비엔다 admitted, slipping her knife back into her boot. “My nails were growing long, but I should not have done it in your tent, 엘레인. I am sorry. I hope I did not offend.”

“I’m not talking about your flaming nails, 아비엔다,” 엘레인 said. “How… when did you arrive? Why didn’t the guards announce you?”

“They didn’t see me,” 아비엔다 said. “I didn’t wish to make a fuss, and wetlanders can be touchy. I thought they might turn me away, now that you are Queen.” She smiled as she said the last part. 엘레인 had much honor; the way of becoming a leader among the wetlanders was different from proper ways—things could be so backward over here—but 엘레인 had handled herself well and obtained her throne. 아비엔다 couldn’t have been more proud of a spear-sister who had taken a clan chief *gai’shain.*

“They didn’t . .” 엘레인 said. Suddenly, she was smiling. “You crept through the *entire camp*, to my tent at the center, and then slipped inside and sat down not five feet from me. And nobody saw.”

“I didn’t wish to make a fuss.”

“You have a strange way of not making a fuss.”

엘레인’s companions did not react with such calm. One of the three, young Lord Perival, gazed around him with worried eyes, as if searching for other intruders.

“My Queen,” Lir said. “We must punish this breach in security! I will find the men who were lax in their duty and see that they—”

“Peace,” 엘레인 said. “I will speak to my guards and suggest they keep their eyes a little more open. Still, guarding the front of a tent is a silly precaution—and always has been—as someone can just cut their way into the back.”

“And ruin a good tent?” 아비엔다 said, lips turning down. “Only if we had blood feud, 엘레인.”

“Lord Lir, you may go inspect the city—from a good distance—if you wish,” 엘레인 said, standing. “If any of the rest of you wish to accompany him, you may. Dyelin, I will see you in the morning.”

“Very well,” the lords said in turn, then walked from the tent. Both kept distrustful eyes on 아비엔다 as they left. Dyelin just shook her head before following them, and 엘레인 sent her battle commanders out to coordinate scouting of the city. That left 엘레인 and 아비엔다 alone in the tent.

“Light, 아비엔다,” 엘레인 said, embracing her, “if the people who want me dead had half of your skill . . ”

“Did I do something wrong?” 아비엔다 said.

“Other than sneaking into my tent like an assassin?”

“But you are my first-sister…” 아비엔다 said. “Should I have asked? But we are not under a roof. Or… among wetlanders, is a tent considered a roof, as in a hold? I’m sorry, 엘레인. Do I have *toh!* You are such an unpredictable people, it’s hard to know what will offend you and what will not.” 엘레인 just laughed. “아비엔다, you’re a gem. A complete and total *gem.* Light, but it’s good to see your face. I needed a friendly one tonight.”

“Caemlyn has fallen?” 아비엔다 asked.

“Near enough,” 엘레인 said, face growing colder. “It was that bloody Waygate. I thought it was safe—I had that thing all but bricked up, with fifty guards at the door and the *Avendesora* leaves taken and both put on the outside.”

“Someone inside Caemlyn let them in, then.”

“어둠의 친구들,” 엘레인 said. “A dozen members of the Guard—we were lucky enough that one man survived their betrayal and found his way out. Light, I don’t know why I should be surprised. If they’re in the 백색 탑, they’re in 안도르. But these were men who had rejected Gaebril, and who seemed loyal. They waited all this time only to betray us now.”

아비엔다 grimaced, but took one of the chairs to join 엘레인 at the table, rather than staying on the floor. Her first-sister preferred sitting that way. Her stomach had swelled with the children she bore.

“I sent 비르기테 with the soldiers to the city to see what can be done,” 엘레인 said. “But we’ve done what we can for the night, the city watched, the refugees seen to. Light, I wish I could do more. The worst thing about being Queen is not the things you must do, but the things that you cannot.”

“We will bring the battle to them soon enough,” 아비엔다 said.

“We will,” 엘레인 said, eyes smoldering. “I will bring them fire and fury, repayment in kind for the flames they brought to my people.”

“I heard you speak to those men of not attacking the city.”

“No,” 엘레인 said. “I will not give them the satisfaction of holding my own walls against me. I have given 비르기테 an order—the 트롤록s will eventually abandon Caemlyn, of this we are sure. 비르기테 will find a way to hasten that, so we can fight them outside of the city.”

“Do not let the enemy choose your battleground,” 아비엔다 said with a nod. “A good strategy. And… 랜드’s meeting?”

“I will attend,” 엘레인 said. “I must, so it will be done. He had better not give us theatrics and stalling. My people die, my city burns, the world is two steps from the edge of a cliff. I will stay through the afternoon only; after that, I go back to 안도르.” She hesitated. “Will you come with me?”

“엘레인…” 아비엔다 said. “I cannot leave my people. I am a Wise One now.”

“You went to Rhuidean?” 엘레인 asked.

“Yes,” 아비엔다 said. Though it pained her to keep secrets, she said nothing of her visions there.

“Excellent. I—” 엘레인 began, but was cut off.

“My Queen?” the tent guard called from outside. “Messenger for you.”

“Let them in.”

The guard opened the flaps for a young Guardswoman with a messenger’s ribbon on her coat. She performed an ornate bow, one hand removing her hat as the other held out a letter.

엘레인 took the letter but didn’t open it. The messenger retreated. “Perhaps we can still fight together, 아비엔다,” 엘레인 said. “If I have my way, I will have 아일 at my side as I reclaim 안도르. The 트롤록s in Caemlyn present a serious threat to all of us; even if I draw their main force out, the Shadow can continue to pour 그림자태생 through that Waygate.

“I’m thinking that while my armies fight the main body of 트롤록s outside of Caemlyn—I will have to make the city inhospitable to the 그림자태생 somehow—I will send a smaller force through a gateway to seize the Waygate. If I could gain the aid of 아일 for that ... ”

As she spoke, she embraced the Source—아비엔다 could see the glow— and absently sliced the letter open, breaking the seal with a ribbon of Air. 아비엔다 raised an eyebrow.

“Sorry,” 엘레인 said, “I've reached the point in my pregnancy where I can channel again reliably, and I keep finding excuses…”

“Do not endanger the babes,” 아비엔다 said.

“I’m not going to endanger them,” 엘레인 said. “You’re as bad as 비르기테. At least no one has any goat’s milk here. 민 says…” She trailed off, eyes flickering back and forth as she read the letter. 엘레인’s expression darkened, and 아비엔다 prepared herself for a shock.

“Oh, that man…” 엘레인 said.

“랜드?”

“I think I may strangle him one of these days.”

아비엔다 set her jaw. “If he’s offended—”

엘레인 turned the letter around. “He *insists* that I return to Caemlyn to see to my people. He gives a dozen reasons why, going so far as to release me from my obligation’ to meet with him tomorrow.”

“He should not be insisting on anything with you.”

“Particularly not so forcefully,” 엘레인 said. “Light, this is clever. He’s obviously trying to bully me into *staying.* There’s a touch of *Daes Dae’mar* in this.”

아비엔다 hesitated. “You seem proud. Yet I gather this letter is only one step away from being insulting!”

“I am proud,” 엘레인 said. “And angry at him. But proud because he knew to make me angry like that. Light! We’ll make a king out of you yet, 랜드. Why does he want me at the meeting so badly? Does he think I’ll support his side just because of my affection for him?”

“You don’t know what his plan is, then?”

“No. It obviously involves all of the rulers. But I will attend, even though I’m likely to do so without having had any sleep tonight. I am meeting with 비르기테 and my other commanders in an hour to go over plans for drawing out, then destroying, the 트롤록s.” A fire still burned behind those eyes of hers. 엘레인 was a warrior, as true a one as 아비엔다 had ever known.

“I must go to him,” 아비엔다 said.

“Tonight?”

“Tonight. 최후의 전투 will soon begin.”

“As far as I’m concerned, it started the moment those bloody 트롤록s set foot in Caemlyn,” 엘레인 said. “May the Light favor us. It is here.”

“Then the day of dying will come,” 아비엔다 said. “Many of us will soon wake from this dream. There may not be another night for 랜드 and myself. I came to you, in part, to ask you about this.”

“You have my blessing,” 엘레인 said softly. “You are my first-sister. Have you spent time with 민?”

“Not enough, and under other circumstances I would remedy that lack immediately. There is no time.”

엘레인 nodded.

“I do think she feels better about me,” 아비엔다 said. “She did me a great honor in helping me understand the last step to becoming a Wise One. It may be appropriate to bend some of the customs. We have done well, under the circumstances. I would speak to her together with you, if there is time.”

엘레인 nodded. “I can spare a moment or two between meetings. I’ll send for her.”

**CHAPTER 3**

![](images/00119.jpg)

*A Dangerous Place*

“Lord 로가인 and 타임 have indeed patched up their differences,” 웰린 said, sitting inside the common room of The Great Gathering. He wore bells in his dark braids, and he smiled widely. He always had smiled too much. “Both were worried about the division we’ve been suffering and agree it isn’t good for morale. We need to be focused on the Last Battle. This isn’t a time for squabbling.”

안드롤 stood just inside the door, 페바라 beside him. It was surprising, how quickly this building—a former warehouse—had been transformed into a tavern. Lind had done her work well. There were a respectable bar and stools, and though the tables and chairs spread through the room didn’t match yet, the place could seat dozens. She also had a library with a considerable number of books, although she was very particular about who she allowed to use it. On the second floor, she planned private dining chambers and sleeping rooms for visitors to the 검은 탑. Assuming 타임 started letting visitors in again.

The room was quite packed, and the crowd included a large number of newer recruits, men who didn’t yet fall on either side of the growing dispute— either with 타임 and his men, or with those loyal to 로가인.

안드롤 listened to 웰린, feeling chilled. 웰린’s 에스 세다이, Jenare, sat beside him, hand resting fondly on his arm. 안드롤 didn’t know her well, but he *did* know 웰린. And this thing with 웰린’s face and voice was *not* the same man.

We met with the Lord Dragon,” 웰린 continued. “Surveying the 국경지대, preparing for humankind’s assault against the Shadow. He has rallied the armies of all nations to his banner. There are none who do not support him, other than the 쇼엔찬, of course—but they have been driven back.

This is the time, and we will soon be called upon to strike. We need to focus one last time on our skills. The Sword and Dragon will be awarded liberally in the next two weeks. Work hard, and we will be the weapons that break the 어둠의 존재’s hold upon this land.”

“You say 로가인 is coming,” a voice demanded. “Why isn’t he back yet?” 안드롤 turned. Jonneth Dowtry stood near 웰린's table. With his arms folded, glowering at 웰린, Jonneth was an intimidating sight. The 두 강 man often had a friendly way about him, and it was easy to forget that he stood a head taller than you and had arms like those of a bear. He wore his black Asha’man coat, though it had no pins on the high collar— despite the fact that he was as strong in the 하나의 힘 as any 헌신자.

‘Why isn’t he here?” Jonneth demanded. “You said that you returned with him, that he and 타임 have spoken. Well, where is he?”

*Don’t push, lad*, 안드롤 thought. *Let him think we believe his lies!*

“He took the M’Hael to visit the Lord Dragon,” 웰린 said. “Both should be back on the morrow, the day after at the latest.”

“Why did 타임 need 로가인 to show him the way?” Jonneth said stubbornly. “He could have gone on his own.”

“That boy is a fool,” 페바라 hissed.

“He’s honest,” 안드롤 replied quietly, “and he wants honest answers.” These 두 강 lads were a good lot—straightforward and loyal. They weren’t particularly practiced in subterfuge, however.

페바라 fell silent, but 안드롤 could *feel* her as she considered channeling and hushing Jonneth with some bindings of Air. They weren’t serious thoughts, just idle fancies, but 안드롤 could sense them. Light! What had they done to one another?

*She’s in my head,* he thought. *There’s an 에스 세다이, inside my head.*

페바라 froze, then glanced at him.

안드롤 sought the void, that old soldier’s trick to help him seek clarity before a battle. *Saidin* was there, too, of course. He didn’t reach for it.

“What did you do?” 페바라 whispered. “I can feel you there, but sensing your thoughts is harder.”

Well, that was something at least.

“Jonneth,” Lind called across the common room, interrupting the lad’s next question to 웰린. “Didn’t you hear the man saying how much traveling he’s been doing? He’s exhausted. Let him drink his ale and rest a spell before you pry stories out of him.”

Jonneth glanced at her, looking hurt. 웰린 smiled deeply as the lad withdrew, pushing his way out of the common room. 웰린 continued talking about how well the Lord Dragon was doing, and about how much each of them would be needed.

안드롤 released the void, feeling more relaxed. He looked around the room, trying to judge who in here he could rely upon. He liked many of these men, and many weren’t completely for 타임, yet he still couldn’t trust them. 타임 had complete control of the Tower now, and private lessons with him and his chosen were coveted by the newcomers. Only the 두 강 lads could be counted on to give any sort of support to 안드롤’s cause— and most of them other than Jonneth were too unpracticed to be of use.

Evin had joined 날람 on the other side of the room, and 안드롤 nodded his head to him, sending him out to follow Jonneth into the storm. Nobody was to be alone. That done, 안드롤 listened to 웰린’s boasting, and noticed Lind picking her way through the crowd toward him.

Lind Taglien was a short, dark-haired woman; her dress was covered in lovely embroidery. She had always seemed to him a model of what the 검은 탑 *could* be. Civilized. Educated. Important.

Men made way for her; they knew not to spill their drinks or start fights in her inn. Lind’s anger was not something a wise man ever wanted to know. It was a good thing she ran the place so tightly. In a city full of male channelers, a simple tavern brawl could potentially go very, very wrong.

메자르 laughed, and 안드롤 heard 웰린 stand up behind him. “Ah, there you are! I was telling them you’d talk about defenses in 아라펠.”

아일. “Wait,” he said. “How have I taken you from them?”

She smiled in satisfaction and woozily took 안드롤’s hand, letting him help her to her feet. “What did you think the 적색 아자 does with its time, 안드롤? Sit around and complain about men? We train to fight other channeled.”

페바라 took a breath, then raised a hand and steadied herself against the wall.

안드롤 looked up sharply. “We need to take you to one of the others for 치유.”

“Yes,” she admitted, glancing away.

“Slight.”

He grunted, then took a handkerchief out of his pocket and poured some water on it from his flask. He adopted a look of concentration, and his light winked out. The handkerchief crackled softly, and when he handed it to her, it was frozen. “Hold this to the wound,” he said. “Tell me if you start to feel drowsy. It could grow worse if you fall asleep.”

“Are you worried for me?” she asked, amused, doing as he said.

“Just… what was it you told me earlier? Keeping watch over our assets?

I’m sure,” she said, pressing the iced bandanna to her head. “So you know field medicine as well?”

“I apprenticed with a town’s Wise Woman once,” he said absently as he knelt to bind the fallen men. 페바라 was glad to release the weaves of Air on them, though she did keep the shields up.

“A Wise Woman took on a *male* apprentice?”

“Not at first,” 안드롤 said. “It’s ... a long story.”

“Excellent; a long story will keep me from falling asleep until the others come for us.” 에마린 and the others had been instructed to go and be seen, establishing an alibi for the group, in case Dobser’s disappearance was noted.

안드롤 eyed her, replacing his light. Then he shrugged, continuing his work. “It started when I lost a friend to the fevers during a silverpike run out of Mayene. When I came back to the mainland, I started thinking that we could have saved Sayer if any of us had known what to do. So I went looking for someone who could teach me . . ”

**CHAPTER 4**

*Advantages to a Bond*

“And that was the end of it,” 페바라 said, sitting against the wall.

“I still hate them,” she said. “I can think about my family without pain, but the 어둠의 친구들 ... I *hate* them. At least I have some vengeance, as the 어둠의 존재 certainly didn’t defend them. 페바라 was still thinking about her family. She had been telling the truth; she did hate the 어둠의 친구들. All of them. It was a measured hate, not out of control, but it was still strong after all of these years.

She looked at him.

That was shocking to me; he’d always been so gentle. What had changed, in those last few years, to make her fear him?” 안드롤 turned to 페바라. “She said that he saw things in the shadows. That he’d started to go mad.”

“You asked me why I came to the 검은 탑. You wanted to know why I *asked* to be tested. Well this thing that I am, it answers a question for me. It tells me who my father was, and why he did what he felt he needed to do.

“The fear in his eyes. I *know* that fear now.” He hesitated. “My father jumped off that cliff to save his family’s lives.”

“Knowing what I am, what *he* was, helps.”

안드롤 blinked. The man held himself taller, more proudly, more… authoritatively. His voice became powerful, dismissive. Just like that, he had become a nobleman.

“No one will think to look for us there,” 에마린 continued. “I will accept you as my associates, and the lesser among us—young Evin, for instance— can enter my employ as servants. If we play our hand correctly, we can build up a rival 검은 탑.”

페바라 hesitantly did as instructed. Dobser dropped to the floor, barely catching himself. He stumbled for a moment, unsteady on his feet, then immediately glanced toward the exit.

에마린 reached behind his back, pulled something from his belt and tossed it to the floor. A small sack. It clinked as it hit. “Master Dobser,” 에마린 said.

“What’s this?” Dobser asked, tentatively crouching down, taking the sack. He peeked into it, and his eyes widened noticeably.

Dobser narrowed his eyes. “To do what?”

“I merely wished to speak with you. I did not intend to see you wrapped up in Air and tormented.”

“I see that we understand each other,” 에마린 said, smiling. “You’ll maintain my front for me, then?”

“Yes,” 에마린 said. “That *is* going to be a problem, isn’t it? You don’t suppose we could just give 안드롤 to 타임 and blame him for this?”

“안드롤?“ Dobser said, snorting. “The pageboy? Taking down two Ashaman? Nobody would believe it. Nobody.”

“A valid point, Master Dobser,” 에마린 said.

“Just give em the 에스 세다이,” Dobser said, jerking a finger toward her.

“Alas, I have need of her. A mess, this is. A pure mess.”

“That would be much appreciated,” 에마린 said, taking a chair from beside the wall and setting it down, then placing another before it. He sat, waving for Dobser to sit down. “안드롤, make yourself useful. Find something for Master Dobser and me to drink. Tea. You like sugar?”

“Wine, 안드롤,” 에마린 said, snapping his fingers.

*Well,* 안드롤 thought, *best to play the part.* He bowed, shooting Dobser a calculated glare, then fetched some cups and wine from the storeroom. When he returned, Dobser and 에마린 were chatting amicably.

“I understand,” 에마린 said. “I have had *such* trouble finding proper help inside the 검은 탑. You see, the need to preserve my identity is *imperative*.”

“I can see that, m’Lord,” Dobser said. “Why, if anyone else knew a High Lord of 티어 was among our ranks, there’d be no end to the boot licking. That I can tell you! And the M’Hael, well, he wouldn’t like someone with so much authority being here. No, not at all!”

“You see why I had to maintain my distance,” 에마린 explained, holding out a hand and accepting a cup of wine as 안드롤 poured it.

*A High Lord of 티어?* 안드롤 thought, amused. Dobser seemed to be drinking it in as he did strong liquor.

“And we all thought you were fawning over 로가인 because you was stupid!” Dobser said.

“Alas, the lot I’ve been given. 타임 would see through me in a moment if I were to spend too much time around him. So I was forced to go with 로가인. He and that Dragon fellow, both are obviously farmers and wouldn’t recognize a highborn man.”

“I’ll say, m’Lord,” Dobser said, “I was suspicious.”

“As I thought,” 에마린 said, taking a sip of the wine. “To prove it’s not poisoned,” he explained, before passing the cup to Dobser.

“ ’S all right, m’Lord,” Dobser said. “I trust you.” He gulped down the wine. “If you can’t trust a High Lord himself, who can you trust, right?”

“Quite right,” 에마린 said.

“I can tell you this,” Dobser said, holding out his cup and wagging it for 안드롤 to refill, “you’ll need to find a better way of keeping away from 타임. Following 로가인 won’t work anymore.”

에마린 took a long, contemplative sip from his cup of wine. “타임 has him. I see. I did guess it would be so. 웰린 and the others showing up tells the tale.”

“Yeah,” Dobser said, letting 안드롤 refill his cup again. “로가인 is a strong one, though. Takes a lot of work to Turn a man like him. Willpower, you know? It will be a day or two to Turn him. Anyway, you might as well come out to 타임, explain what you’re up to. He’ll understand, and he keeps saying men are more useful to him if he doesn’t have to Turn them. Don’t know why. No choice but to Turn 로가인, though. Awful process.” Dobser shivered.

“I’ll go and speak with him then, Master Dobser. Would you vouch for me, by chance? I’ll ... see you paid for the effort.”

“Sure, sure,” Dobser said. “Why not?” He downed his wine, then lurched to his feet. “He’ll be checking on 로가인. Always does, this time of night.”

“And that would be where?” 에마린 said.

“The hidden rooms,” Dobser said. “In the foundations we’re building. You know the eastern section, where the collapse made all of that extra digging? That was no collapse, just an excuse for covering up extra work being done. And…” Dobser hesitated.

“And that’s enough,” 페바라 said, tying the man up in air again and stopping his ears. She folded her arms, looking at 에마린. “I’m impressed.” 에마린 spread his hands apart in a gesture of humility. “I have always had a talent for making men feel at ease. In truth, I didn’t suggest picking Dobser because I thought he’d be easy to bribe. I picked him because of his… well, understated powers of cognitive expression.”

“Turning someone to the Shadow doesn’t make him any less stupid,” 안드롤 said. “But if you could do this, why did we have to jump him in the first place?”

“It’s a matter of controlling the situation, 안드롤,” 에마린 said. “A man like Dobser mustn’t be confronted in his element, surrounded by friends with more wits than he. We had to scare him, make him writhe, then offer him a way to wiggle out.” 에마린 hesitated, glancing at Dobser. “Besides, I don’t think we wanted to risk him going to 타임, which he very well might have done if I’d approached him in private without the threat of violence.”

“And now?” 페바라 asked.

“Now,” 안드롤 said, “we douse these three with something that will keep them sleeping until Bel Tine. We gather 날람, Canler, Evin and Jonneth. We wait for 타임 to finish his inspection of 로가인; we break in, rescue him and seize the Tower back from the Shadow.”

They stood in silence for a moment, the room lit only by the single, flickering lamp. Rain sprayed the window.

“Well,” 페바라 said, “so long as it’s not a *difficult* task you’re proposing, 안드롤…”

랜드 opened his eyes to the dream, somewhat surprised to find that he had fallen asleep. 아비엔다 had finally let him doze. In truth, she was probably letting herself doze as well. She’d seemed as tired as he had. More, perhaps.

He climbed to his feet in the meadow of dead grass. He had been able to sense her concern not only through the bond but in the way she had held him. 아비엔다 was a fighter, a warrior, but even a warrior needed something to hold on to once in a while. Light knew that he did.

He looked about. This didn't feel like *Tel’aran’rhiod*', not completely. The dead field extended into the distance on all sides, presumably into infinity. This wasn't the true World of Dreams; it was a dreamshard, a world created by a powerful Dreamer or dreamwalker.

랜드 began walking, feet crunching on dead leaves, though there were no trees. He could probably have sent himself back to his own dreams; though he had never been as good as many of the 버림받은 자들 at walking dreams, he could manage that much. Curiosity drove him forward.

*I shouldn’t be here,* he thought. *I set wards.* How had he come to this place and who had created it? He had a suspicion. There was one person who had often made use of dreamshards.

랜드 felt a presence nearby. He continued walking, not turning, but knew that someone was now walking beside him.

“Elan,” 랜드 said.

“르웨어스 테린.” Elan still wore his newest body, the tall, handsome man who wore red and black. “It dies, and the dust soon will rule. The dust… then nothing.”

“How did you pass my wards?”

“I don’t know,” 모리딘 said. “I knew that if I created this place, you would join me in it. You cant keep away from me. 패턴 won’t allow it. We are drawn together, you and I. Time after time after time. Two ships moored on the same beach, beating against one another with each new tide.”

“Poetic,” 랜드 said. “You’ve finally let Mierin off her leash, I’ve seen.” 모리딘 stopped, and 랜드 paused, looking at him. The man’s rage seemed to come off him in waves of heat.

“She came to you?” 모리딘 demanded.

랜드 said nothing.

“Do not *pretend* that you knew she still lived. You didn’t know, you couldn’t have known.”

랜드 kept still. His emotions regarding 란피어—or whatever she called herself now—were complicated. 르웨어스 테린 had despised her, but 랜드 had known her primarily as Selene, and had been fond of her—until, at least, she tried to kill 에그웨인 and 아비엔다.

Thinking of her made him think of 모이라인, made him *hope* for things he shouldn’t hope for.

*If 란피어 still lives*… *might 모이라인 as well?*

He faced 모리딘 with calm confidence. “Loosing her is pointless, now,” 랜드 said. “She no longer holds any power over me.”

“Yes,” 모리딘 said. “I believe you. She does not, but I do think she still harbors something of a… grievance with the woman you chose. What is her name again? The one who calls herself 아일 but carries weapons?”

랜드 did not rise to the attempt to rile him.

“Mierin hates you now, anyway,” 모리딘 continued. “I think she blames you for what happened to her. You should call her 신데인. She has been forbidden to use the name she took upon herself.”

“신데인…” 랜드 said, trying out the word. “ ‘Last Chance’? Your master has gained humor, I see.”

“It was not meant to be humorous,” 모리딘 said.

“No, I suppose that it was not.” 랜드 looked at the endless landscape of dead grass and leaves. “It is hard to think that I was so afraid of you during those early days. Did you invade my dreams then, or bring me into one of these dreamshards? I was never able to figure it out.”

모리딘 said nothing.

“I remember one time…” 랜드 said. “Sitting up by the fire, surrounded by nightmares that felt like *Tel’aran’rhiod.* You would not have been able to pull someone fully into the World of Dreams, yet I’m no dream-walker, able to enter on my own.”

모리딘, like many of the 버림받은 자들, had usually entered *Tel’aran’rhiod* in the flesh, which was dangerous. Some said that entering in the flesh was an evil thing, that it lost you a part of your humanity. It also made you more powerful.

모리딘 gave no clue as to what had happened on that night. 랜드 remembered those days faintly, traveling toward 티어. He remembered visions in the night, visions of his friends or family that would try to kill him. 모리딘… 이샤마엘… had been pulling him against his will into dreams intersecting *Tel’aran’rhiod.*

“You were mad, during those days,” 랜드 said softly, looking into 모리딘’s eyes. He could almost see the fires burning there. “You’re still mad, aren't you? You just have it contained. No one could serve him without being at least a little mad.”

모리딘 stepped forward. “Taunt as you wish, 르웨어스 테린. The ending dawns. All will be given to the great suffocation of the Shadow, to be stretched, ripped, *strangled*.”

랜드 took a step forward as well, right up to 모리딘. They were the same height. “You hate yourself,” 랜드 whispered. “I can *feel* it in you, Elan. Once you served him for power; now you do it because his victory—and an end to all things—is the only release you’ll ever know. You’d rather not exist than continue to be you. You must know that he will not release you. Not ever. Not you.”

모리딘 sneered. “He’ll let me kill you before this ends, 르웨어스 테린. You, and the golden-haired one, and the 아일 woman, and the little darkhaired—”

“You act as if this is a contest between you and me, Elan,” 랜드 interrupted.

모리딘 laughed, throwing his head back. “Of course it is! Haven’t you seen that *yet?* By the blood falls, 르웨어스 테린! It is about us two. Just as in Ages past, over and over, we fight one another. You and I.”

“No,” 랜드 said. “Not this time. I’m done with you. I have a greater battle to fight.”

“Don’t try to—”

Sunlight exploded through the clouds above. There was often no sunlight in the World of Dreams, but now it bathed the area around 랜드.

모리딘 stumbled back. He looked up at the light, then gazed at 랜드 and narrowed his eyes. “Don’t think… don’t think I will believe your simple tricks, 르웨어스 테린. Weiramon was shaken by what you did to him, but it’s not such a difficult thing, holding *세이딘* and listening for people’s heartbeats to speed up.”

랜드 exerted his will. The crackling dead leaves began to transform at his feet, turning green again, and shoots of grass broke through the leaves.

The green spread from him like spilled paint, and clouds above boiled away.

모리딘’s eyes opened wider. He stumbled, staring at the sky as the clouds retreated… 랜드 could feel his shock. This was *모리딘’s* dream-shard.

However, to draw another in, he had had to place it close to *Tel’aran’rhiod.* Those rules applied. There was something else, too, something about the connection between the two of them…

랜드 strode forward, lifting his arms out to the sides. Grass sprouted in waves, red blossoms burst from the ground like a blush upon the land. The storm stilled, the dark clouds burned away by light.

“Tell your master!” 랜드 commanded. “Tell him this fight is not like the others. Tell him I’ve tired of minions, that I’m finished with his petty movement of pawns. Tell him that *I’m coming for HIM!”*

“This is wrong,” 모리딘 said, visibly shaken. “This isn’t . . ” He looked at 랜드 for a moment, standing beneath the blazing sun, then vanished.

랜드 let out a deep breath. The grass died around him, the clouds sprang back, the sunlight faded. Though 모리딘 was gone, holding on to that transformation of the landscape had been difficult. 랜드 sagged, panting, recovering from the exertion.

Here, willing something to be true could make it so. If only things were that simple in the real world.

He closed his eyes and sent himself away, to sleep for the short time before he had to rise. Rise, and save the world. If he could.

페바라 crouched beside 안드롤 in the rainy night. Her cloak was soaked completely through. She knew a couple of weaves that would have been useful for that, but she didn’t dare channel. She and the others would be facing Turned 에스 세다이 and women of the 흑색 아자. They could sense it if she channeled.

“They’re definitely guarding the area,” 안드롤 whispered. Ahead of them, the ground broke away into a large sequence of mazelike brickworks and trenches. These were the foundation rooms of what would eventually become the 검은 탑 proper. If Dobser was right, other rooms had been created within the foundation—hidden chambers, already complete, that would continue to be secret as the Tower itself was constructed.

A pair of 타임’s Asha’man stood chatting nearby. Though they tried to appear nonchalant, the effect was spoiled by the weather. Who would *choose* to stand outside on a night like this one? Despite a warm brazier lighting them and a weave of Air to send the rain streaming away, their presence was suspicious.

*Guards.* 페바라 tried sending the thought to 안드롤 directly.

It worked. She could feel his surprise as the thought intruded onto his own.

Something returned, fuzzy. *We should take advantage.*

*Yes,* she sent back. The next thought was too complex, though, so she whispered it. “How have you never before noticed that he left the foundation guarded at night? If there really are secret rooms, then the work on them would be done at night as well.”

“타임 set a curfew,” 안드롤 whispered. “He lets us ignore it only when convenient to him—such as for 웰린’s return tonight. Besides, this area is dangerous, with those pits and trenches. It would be a good enough reason to set guards, except . . ”

“Except,” 페바라 said, “타임 isn’t exactly the type to care if a child or two break their necks poking around.”

안드롤 nodded.

페바라 and 안드롤 waited in the rain, counting their breaths, until three ribbons of fire flew from the night and struck the guards directly in their heads. The two Asha’man dropped like sacks of grain. 날람, 에마린 and Jonneth had done their work perfectly. Quick channeling; with luck, it either wouldn’t be noticed or would be thought the work of 타임’s men on guard.

*Light,* 페바라 thought. *안드롤 and the others really are weapons.* She hadn’t stopped to consider that 에마린 and the others would lead with lethal attacks. It was completely outside her experience as an 에스 세다이. 에스 세다이 didn’t even kill false 용 if they could help it.

“온순화 kills,” 안드롤 said, eyes forward. “Albeit slowly.”

Light. Yes, there might be advantages to their bond—but it was also blasted inconvenient. She would have to practice shielding her thoughts.

에마린 and the others came in from the darkness, joining 페바라 and 안드롤 at the brazier. Canler remained behind, with the other 두 강 lads, ready to lead them from the 검은 탑 in an escape attempt if something went wrong tonight. It made sense to leave him, despite his protests. He had a family.

They dragged the corpses into the shadows, but left the brazier burning. Someone looking for the guards would see that the light was still there, but the night was so misty and rainy one would have to draw close to realize that its attendants had vanished.

Though he often complained that he didn’t know why the others followed him, 안드롤 immediately took charge of this group, sending 날람 and Jonneth to watch at the edge of the foundation. Jonneth carried his bow, unstrung in the wet night. They were hoping the rain would let up, and that he’d be able to use it when they couldn’t risk channeling.

안드롤, 페바라 and 에마린 slid down one of the muddy slopes into the foundation pits that had been dug. Mud splashed over her as she landed, but she was already soaked, and the rain washed away the grime.

The foundation was made of stones built up to form walls between rooms and hallways; down here, this became a labyrinth, with a steady stream of rain falling from above. In the morning, the Asha’man soldiers would be set to drying out the foundation.

*How do we find the entrance?* 페바라 sent.

안드롤 knelt, a very small globe of light hovering above his hand. Drops of rain passed through the light, looking like tiny meteorites for a moment as they flashed and vanished. He rested fingers in the pooling water on the ground.

He looked up, then pointed. “It runs this way,” he whispered. “It’s going somewhere. That is where we’ll find 타임.”

에마린 grunted appreciatively. 안드롤 raised a hand, summoning Jonneth and 날람 down into the foundation with them, then led the way, stepping softly.

*You. Quietly. Move. Well,* she sent.

*Trained as scout,* he sent back. *In woods. Mountains of Mist.*

How many jobs had he done in his life? She had worried about him. A life such as he had led could indicate a dissatisfaction with the world, an impatience. The way he spoke of the 검은 탑, though… the passion with which he was willing to fight… that said something different. This wasn’t just about a loyalty to 로가인. Yes, 안드롤 and the others respected 로가인, but to them, he represented something far greater. A place where men like them were accepted.

A life like 안드롤’s *could* indicate a man who would not commit or be satisfied, but it could also indicate something else: a man who searched. A man who knew that the life he wanted existed out there. He just had to find it.

“They teach you to analyze people like that in the 백색 탑?” 안드롤 whispered to her as he stopped beside a doorway and moved his globe of light in, then waved the others to follow.

*No,* she sent back, trying to practice this method of communicating, to make her thoughts smoother. *Is something a woman picks up after her first century of life.*

He sent back tense amusement. They passed into a series of unfinished rooms, none of them roofed, before reaching a section of unworked earth. Some barrels here held pitch, but they had been shifted to the side and the boards they normally sat upon had been pulled away. A pit opened in the ground here. The water trailed over the lip of the pit and down into darkness. 안드롤 knelt and listened, then nodded to the others before slipping down into it. His splash came a second later.

페바라 followed him, dropping only a few feet. The water was cold on her feet, but she was already soaked. 안드롤 hunched, leading the way under an earthen overhang, then stood up on the other side. His little globe of light revealed a tunnel. A trench had been dug here to hold the rainwater. 페바라 judged they’d been standing directly above this when they’d taken down the guards.

*Dobser right,* she sent as the others splashed down behind. *타임 building secret tunnels and chambers.*

They crossed the trench and continued on. A short distance down the tunnel, they reached an intersection where the earthen walls were shored up, like the shafts of a mine. The five of them gathered there, looking in one direction, then another. Two paths.

“That way slopes upward,” 에마린 whispered, pointing left. “Perhaps to another entrance into these tunnels?”

“We should probably move deeper,” 날람 said. “Don’t you think?”

“Yes,” 안드롤 said, licking his finger and testing the air. “The wind is blowing right. We’ll go that way first. Be careful. There will be other guards.”

The group slipped further down into the tunnels. How long had 타임 been working on this complex? It didn’t seem terribly extensive—they didn’t pass other branchings—but still, it was impressive.

Suddenly 안드롤 stopped, and the others pulled to a halt. A grumbling voice echoed up the tunnel, too soft for them to make out the words, accompanied by a flickering light on the walls. 페바라 embraced the Source and prepared weaves. If she channeled, would someone in the foundation notice? 안드롤 was obviously hesitant as well; channeling above, to kill the guards, had been suspicious enough. If 타임’s men down here sensed the 하나의 힘 being used…

The figure was approaching, the light illuminating him.

A creak came from beside her, as Jonneth drew his restrung 두 강 bow. There was barely room in the tunnel for it. He loosed with a snap, the air whistling. The grumbling cut off, and the light fell.

The group scrambled forward to find 코테렌 down on the ground, eyes staring up glassily, the arrow through his chest. His lantern burned fitfully on the ground beside him. Jonneth retrieved his arrow, then wiped it on the dead mans clothing. *“That’s* why I still carry a bow, you bloody son of a goat.”
“Here,” 에마린 said, pointing at a thick door. “코테렌 was guarding it.”

“Prepare yourselves,” 안드롤 whispered, then shoved open the thick wooden door. Beyond, they found a line of crude cells built into the earthen wall—each one little more than a roofed cubbyhole burrowed into the earth with a door set in the opening. 페바라 peeked in one, which was empty. The cubby didn’t have enough room for a man to stand up inside, and the room was unlit. Being locked in those cells would mean being trapped in blackness, squeezed into a space like a grave.

“Light!” 날람 said. “안드롤! He’s in here. It’s 로가인!”

The others hurried to join him, and 안드롤 picked the door’s lock with a surprisingly adept hand. They pulled open the cell door, and 로가인 rolled out with a groan. He looked horrible, covered in grime. Once, that curling dark hair and strong face might have made him handsome. He looked as weak as a beggar.

He coughed, then rose to his knees with 날람’s help. 안드롤 knelt immediately, but not in reverence. He looked 로가인 in the eyes as 에마린 gave the Asha’man leader his flask for a drink.

*Well?* 페바라 asked.

*It’s him,* 안드롤 thought, a wave of relief coming through the bond. *It’s still him.*

*They’d have let him go if they’d Turned him,* 페바라 sent back, growing increasingly comfortable with this method of communicating.

*Maybe. Unless this is a trap.* “My Lord 로가인.”

“안드롤.” 로가인’s voice was raspy. “Jonneth. 날람. And an 에스 세다이?” He inspected 페바라. For a man who had apparently suffered days, perhaps weeks, of incarceration, he looked remarkably lucid. “I remember you. What 아자 are you, woman?”

“Does it matter?” she replied.

“Greatly,” 로가인 said, trying to stand. He was too weak, and 날람 had to support him. “How did you find me?”

“That is a story for once we are safe, my Lord,” 안드롤 said. He peeked out the doorway. “Let’s move. We still have a difficult night ahead of us. I—”

안드롤 froze, then slammed the door.

“What is it?” 페바라 asked.

“Channeling,” Jonneth said. “Powerful.”

Yells, muffled by the door and the dirt walls, sounded outside in the hallway.

“Someone found the guards,” 에마린 said. “My Lord 로가인, can you fight?”

로가인 tried to stand on his own, then sagged again. His face grew determined, but 페바라 felt 안드롤’s disappointment. 로가인 had been given forkroot; either that, or he was simply too tired to channel. Not surprising. 페바라 had seen women in better shape than this who were too worn out to embrace the Source.

“Back!” 안드롤 shouted, stepping to the side of the door—against the earthen wall. The door exploded in a weave of fire and destruction.

페바라 didn’t wait for the debris to settle; she wove Fire and released a column of destruction down the corridor beyond. She knew she was facing 어둠의 친구들, or worse. The 세 가지 맹세 did not hinder her here.

She heard shouts, but something deflected the fire. Immediately, a shield tried to slam between her and the Source. She fought it off, barely, and ducked to the side, breathing deeply.

“Whoever it is, they’re strong,” 페바라 said.

A voice called orders distantly, echoing in the tunnels.

Jonneth knelt down beside her, bow out. “Light, that’s 타임’s voice!”

“We cannot stand here,” 로가인 said. “안드롤. A gateway.”

“I’m trying,” 안드롤 said. “Light, I’m trying!”

“Bah,” 날람 set 로가인 down beside the wall. “I’ve been in tighter spots before!” He joined the others at the doorway, flinging weaves down the corridor. Blasts shook the side walls, and dirt rained down from the roof above.

페바라 jumped in front of the doorway, releasing a weave, then knelt down beside 안드롤. He stared ahead, not seeing, face a mask of concentration. She could feel determination and frustration pulsing through the bond. She took his hand.

“You can do it,” she whispered.

The doorway erupted, and Jonneth fell back, arm burned. The ground trembled; the walls started to break apart.

Sweat dripped down the sides of 안드롤’s face. He gritted his teeth, his face going red, eyes opening wide. Smoke poured through the doorway, making 에마린 cough as 날람 Healed Jonneth.

안드롤 yelled, and he neared the top of that wall in his mind. He was almost there! He could—

A weave *thumped* against the room, a ripple in the earth, and the strained roof finally gave out. Earth poured down atop them, and all went black.
