**CHAPTER 5**

![](images/00442.jpg)

*To Require a Boon*

랜드 al’Thor awoke and drew in a deep breath. He slipped from the blankets in his tent, leaving 아비엔다 slumbering there, and threw on a robe. The air smelled wet.

He was reminded, in passing, of mornings during his youth, rising before dawn to milk the cow, which would need milking twice a day. Eyes closed, he remembered the sounds of Tam—already up—cutting new fence posts in the barn. Remembering the chilly air, stomping his feet into his boots, washing his face with water left to warm beside the stove.

On any morning, a farmer could open his door and look out on a world that was still new. Crisp frost. The first, tentative calls of birds. Sunlight breaking the horizon, like the morning yawn of the world.

랜드 stepped up to the flaps of his tent and drew them back, nodding to Katerin, a short, golden-haired Maiden who was on guard. He looked out on a world that was far from new. This world was old and tired, like a peddler who had been to the 세계의 척추 and back on foot. Tents crowded the Field of Merrilor, cook fires trailing pillars of smoke toward the still-dark morning sky.

Everywhere, men worked. 병사s oiled armor. Smiths sharpened spearheads. Women prepared feathers for fletching arrows. Breakfasts were served from meal wagons to men who should have slept better than they had. Everyone knew these were their last moments before the storm arrived.

랜드 closed his eyes. He could *feel* it, the land itself, like a faint 감시자 bond. Beneath his feet, grubs crawled through the soil. The roots of the grasses continued to spread, ever so slowly, seeking nutrients. The skeletal trees were not dead, for water seeped through them. They slumbered. Bluebirds clustered in a nearby tree. They did not call out with the arrival of dawn. They huddled together, as if for warmth.

The land still lived. It lived like a man clinging to the edge of a cliff by his fingertips.

랜드 opened his eyes. “Have my clerks returned from 티어?”

“Yes, 랜드 al’Thor,” said Katerin.

“Send word to the other rulers,” 랜드 said. “I will meet with them in one hour at the center of the field where I commanded no tents be placed.”

Katerin went off to relay his command, leaving three other Maidens nearby to guard. 랜드 let the tent flaps close in front of him and turned around, then jumped as he found 아비엔다—as bare as the day she’d been born—standing in the tent.

“It is very difficult to sneak up on you, 랜드 al’Thor,” she announced with a smile. “The bond gives you too much of an advantage. I have to move very slowly, like a lizard at midnight, so that your sense of where I am does not change too quickly.”

“Light, 아비엔다! Why do you need to sneak up on me in the first place?”

“For this,” she said, then jumped forward, snatching his head and kissing him, her body pressed against his.

He relaxed, letting the kiss linger. “Unsurprisingly,” he mumbled around her lips, “this is much more fun now that I don’t have to worry about freezing my bits off while doing it.”

아비엔다 pulled back. “You should not speak of that event, 랜드 al’Thor.”

“But—”

“My *toh* is paid, and I am now first-sister to 엘레인. Do not remind me of a shame that is forgotten.”

Shame? Why would she be ashamed of that when just now… He shook his head. He could hear the land breathing, could sense a beetle on a leaf half a league away, but sometimes he could not fathom 아일. Or maybe it was just women.

In this case, it was probably both.

아비엔다 hesitated beside the tent’s barrel of fresh water. “I suppose that we will not have time for a bath.”

“Oh, you like baths now?”

“I have accepted them as a part of life,” she said. “If I am going to live in the wetlands, then I will adopt some wetlander customs. When they are not foolish.” Her tone indicated that most of them were.

“What’s wrong?” 랜드 asked, stepping up to her.

“Wrong?”

“Something bothers you, 아비엔다. I can see it in you, feel it in you.” She looked him over with a critical eye. Light, but she was beautiful. “You were much easier to manage before you received the ancient wisdom of your former self, 랜드 al’Thor.”

“I was?” he asked, smiling. “You didn’t act that way at the time.”

“That was when I was as a new child, inexperienced in 랜드 al’Thor’s boundless capacity to be frustrating.” She dipped her hands into the water and washed her face. “It is well; if I had known some of what was to come with you, I might have put on the white and never removed it.”

He smiled, then channeled, weaving Water and drawing the liquid from the barrel in a stream. 아비엔다 stepped back, watching with curiosity.

“You no longer seem bothered by the idea of a man channeling,” he noted as he fanned the water out into the air and heated it with a thread of Fire.

“There is no longer a reason to be bothered. If I were to be uncomfortable with you channeling, I would be behaving like a man refusing to forget a woman’s shame after her *toh* has been met.” She eyed him.

“I can’t imagine anyone being that crass,” he said, tossing aside his robe and stepping up to her. “Here. This is a relic from that ancient wisdom’ you apparently find so frustrating.”

He brought the water in, warmed perfectly, and shattered it into a thick misting spray that wove about them in a rush. 아비엔다 gasped, clutching his arm. She might be growing more comfortable with wetlander ways, but water still made her both uncomfortable and reverent.

랜드 snatched some soap with Air and shaved it into part of the mix of water, sending a spinning whirl of bubbles around them, swirling up their bodies and pulling their hair into the air, twisting 아비엔다’s about like a column before dropping it back lightly to her shoulders.

He used another wave of warm water to remove the soap, then pulled most of the wetness away, leaving them damp but not soaked. He dumped the water back into the barrel and, with a hint of reluctance, released *세이딘.*

아비엔다 was panting. “That… That was completely crackbrained and irresponsible.”

“Thank you,” he said, fetching a towel and tossing it to her. “You would consider most of what we did during the 전설의 시대 to be crackbrained and irresponsible. That was a different time, 아비엔다. There were many more channelers, and we were trained from a young age. We didn’t need to know things like warfare, or how to kill. We had eliminated pain, hunger, suffering, war. Instead, we used the 하나의 힘 for things that might seem common.”

“You’d only assumed that you’d eliminated war,” 아비엔다 said with a sniff. “You were wrong. Your ignorance left you weak.”

“It did. I can’t decide if I would have changed things, though. There were many good years. Good decades, good centuries. We believed we were living in paradise. Perhaps that was our downfall. We wanted our lives to be perfect, so we ignored imperfections. Problems were magnified through inattention, and war might have become inevitable if the 구멍 hadn’t ever been made.” He toweled himself dry.

“랜드,” 아비엔다 said, stepping up to him. “Today, I will require a boon.” She laid her hand on his arm. The skin of her hand was rough, callused from her days as a Maiden. 아비엔다 would never be a milk-softened lady like those from the courts of 케렌 and 티어. 랜드 liked that just fine. Hers were hands that had known work.

“What boon?” he asked. “I’m not certain I could deny you anything today, 아비엔다.”

“I’m not yet certain what it will be.”

“I don’t understand.”

“You needn’t understand,” she said. “And you needn’t promise me you will agree. I felt I needed to give you warning, as one does not ambush a lover. My boon will require you to change your plans, perhaps in a drastic way, and it will be important.”

“All right…”

She nodded, as mystifying as ever, and began gathering up her clothing to dress for the day.

에그웨인 strode around a frozen pillar of glass in her dream. It almost looked like a column of light. What did it mean? She could not interpret it.

The vision changed, and she found a sphere. The world, she knew somehow. Cracking. Frantic, she tied it with cords, striving to hold it together. She could keep it from breaking, but it took so much effort…

She faded from the dream and started awake. She embraced the Source immediately and wove a light. Where was she?

She was wearing a nightgown and lying in bed back in the 백색 탑. Not her own rooms, which were still in disrepair following the assassins’ attack. Her study had a small sleeping chamber, and she’d bedded down in that.

Her head pounded. She could vaguely remember growing bleary-eyed the night before, listening in her tent at the Field of Merrilor to reports of Caemlyn’s fall. At some point during the late hours of the night, 가윈 had insisted that 니나브 make a gateway back to the 백색 탑 so 에그웨인 could sleep in a bed, rather than on a pallet on the ground.

She grumbled to herself, rising. He’d probably been right, though she could remember feeling *distinctly* annoyed at his tone. Nobody had corrected him on it, not even 니나브. She rubbed at her temples. The headache wasn’t as bad as those she’d had when Halima had been “caring” for her, but it did hurt mightily. Undoubtedly, her body was expressing displeasure at the lack of sleep she’d given it in recent weeks.

A short time later—dressed, washed and feeling a *little* better—she left her rooms to find 가윈 sitting at Silviana’s desk, looking over a report, ignoring a 수련생 who was lingering near the doorway.

“She’d hang you out the window by your toes if she saw you doing that,” 에그웨인 said dryly.

가윈 jumped. “It’s not a report from her stack,” he protested. “It’s the latest news from my sister about Caemlyn. It came by gateway for you just a few minutes ago.”

“And you’re reading it?”

He blushed. “Burn me, 에그웨인. It’s my *home.* It wasn’t sealed. I thought.. ”

“It’s all right, 가윈,” she said with a sigh. “Let’s see what it says.”

“There’s not much,” he said with a grimace, handing it to her. At a nod from him the 수련생 scurried away. A short time later, the girl came back with a tray of wizened bellfruit, bread and a pitcher of milk.

에그웨인 sat down at her desk in the study to eat, feeling guilty as the 수련생 left. The bulk of the Tower’s 에스 세다이 and soldiers camped in tents on the Field of Merrilor while she dined on fruit, no matter how old, and slept in a comfortable bed?

Still, 가윈’s arguments had made sense. If everyone thought she was in her tent on the Field, then potential killers would strike there. After her near-death at the hands of the 쇼엔찬 assassins, she was willing to accept a few extra precautions. Particularly those that helped her get a good night’s sleep.

“That 쇼엔찬 woman,” 에그웨인 said, staring into her cup. “The one with the 일리안er. Did you speak with her?”

He nodded. “I have some Tower guards watching the pair. 니나브 vouched for them, in a way.”

“In a way?”

“She called the woman several variations of wool-headed, but said she probably wouldn’t do you any *intentional* harm.”

“Wonderful.” Well, 에그웨인 could make use of a 쇼엔찬 who was willing to talk. Light. What if she had to fight them and the 트롤록s at the same time?

“You didn’t take your own advice,” she said, noting 가윈’s red eyes as he sat down in the chair in front of her desk.

“Someone had to watch the door,” he said. “Calling for guards would have let everyone know that you were not at the Field.”

She took a bite of her bread—what *had* it been made of?—and looked over the report. He was right, but she didn’t like the idea of him going without sleep on a day like this. The 감시자 bond would only help him so far.

“So the city is truly gone,” she said. “Walls breached, palace seized. The 트롤록s didn’t burn all of the city, I see. Much of it, but not all.”

“Yes,” 가윈 said. “But it is obvious that Caemlyn is lost.” She felt his tension through the bond.

“I’m sorry.”

“Many people escaped, but it’s hard to say what the city population was before the attack, with so many refugees. Hundreds of thousands are likely dead.”

에그웨인 breathed out. A large army’s worth of people, wiped out in one night. That was probably only the start of the brutality to come. How many had died in 캔도르 so far? They could only guess.

Caemlyn had held much of the 안도르an army’s food supply. She felt sick, thinking of so many people—hundreds of thousands of them— stumbling across the landscape away from the burning city. Yet that thought was less terrifying than the risk of starvation to 엘레인’s troops.

She drew up a note to Silviana, requiring her to send all sisters strong enough to provide 치유 for the refugees, and gateways to carry them to Whitebridge. Perhaps she could deliver supplies there, though the 백색 탑 was strained as it was.

“Did you see the note at the bottom?” 가윈 asked.

She had not. She frowned, then scanned a sentence added at the bottom in Silviana’s hand. 랜드 al’Thor had demanded that everyone meet with him by…

She looked up at the room’s old, freestanding wooden clock. The meeting was in a half-hour. She groaned, then began shoveling the rest of her breakfast into her mouth. It wasn’t dignified, but Light *burn* her if she was going to meet with 랜드 on an empty stomach.

“I’m going to throttle that boy,” she said, wiping her face. “Come on, let’s move.”

“We could always be last,” 가윈 said, rising. “Show him he doesn’t order us about.”

“And allow him the chance to meet with everyone else while I’m not there to counter what he has to say? I don’t like it, but 랜드 holds the reins right now. Everyone’s too curious to see what he’s going to do.”

She made a gateway back to her tent, into the corner that she’d set aside for 이동. She and 가윈 stepped through and left the tent, into the clamor of the Field of Merrilor. People shouted outside; with a distant thunder of hooves, troops cantered and galloped as they took positions for the meeting. Did 랜드 realize what he’d done here? Putting soldiers together like this, leaving them edgy and uncertain, was like tossing a handful of 불꽃놀이 into a stewpot and setting it onto the stove. Eventually, things were going to start exploding.

에그웨인 needed to manage the chaos. She strode out of her tent, 가윈 a step behind and to her left, and smoothed her face. The world needed an Amyrlin.

Silviana waited outside, dressed formally with stole and staff, as if she were going to a meeting of the 탑의 회의실.

“See to this, once the meeting starts,” 에그웨인 said, handing her the note.

“Yes, Mother,” the woman said, then fell into step just behind 에그웨인 and to her right. 에그웨인 didn’t need to look to know that Silviana and 가윈 were pointedly ignoring each other.

At the west side of her camp, 에그웨인 found a cluster of 에스 세다이 arguing with one another. She passed through them and pulled silence in her wake. A groom brought her horse Sifter, a testy dapple gelding, and as she mounted, she looked at the 에스 세다이. “의석자들 only.”

That produced a sea of calm, orderly complaints, each made with an 에스 세다이 sense of authority. Each woman thought she had a right to be at the meeting. 에그웨인 stared at them, and the women slowly came into line. They were 에스 세다이; they knew that squabbling was beneath them.

The 의석자들 gathered, and 에그웨인 looked out over the Field of Merrilor as she waited. It was a large triangular area of 시엔나르an grassland, bounded on two sides by converging rivers—the Mora and the Erinin—and on the other by woods. The grass was broken by Dashar Knob, a rocky outcrop about a hundred feet high, with cliff walls, and on the 아라펠lin side of the Mora by Polov Heights, a flat-topped hill about forty feet high, with gradual slopes on three sides and a steeper slope on the river side. Southwest of Polov Heights lay an area of bogs, and nearby, the River Mora’s shallows, known as Hawval Ford, a convenient crossing place between 아라펠 and 시엔나르.

There was an 오지어 *stedding* nearby, opposite some old stone ruins to the north. 에그웨인 had paid her respects soon after arriving, but 랜드 had not invited the 오지어 to his meeting.

Armies were converging. Borderlander flags came in from the west, where 랜드 had made his camp. 페린’s own flag flew among those. Odd, that 페린 should have a flag.

From the south, 엘레인’s procession wound its way toward the meeting place, smack in the middle of the Field. The Queen rode at the front. Her palace had burned, but she kept her eyes forward. Between 페린 and 엘레인, the 타이런s and 일리안ers—Light, who had let those armies camp so near one another?—marched in separate columns, both bringing almost their entire forces.

Best to be quick. Her presence would calm the rulers, perhaps prevent problems. They wouldn’t like being near so many 아일. Each clan but the Shaido was represented. She *still* didn’t know if they’d support 랜드 or her. Some of the 현명한 이들 seemed to have listened to 에그웨인’s pleas, but she had received no commitments.

“Look there,” 사에린 said, pulling up beside 에그웨인. “Did you invite the Sea Folk?”

에그웨인 shook her head. “No. I thought there was little chance they’d side against 랜드.” In truth, after her meeting with the Windfinders in *Tel’aran’rhiod*, she hadn’t wanted to swim in negotiations with them again. She was afraid she’d wake up and find that she’d traded away not only her firstborn, but the 백색 탑 itself.

They put up quite a show, appearing through gateways near 랜드’s camp, wearing their colorful clothing, Wavemistresses and Swordmasters as proud as monarchs.

*Light,* 에그웨인 thought. *I wonder how long it’s been since a meeting of this scale occurred.* Nearly every nation was represented, and then some, considering the Sea Folk and the 아일. Only 무란디, 아라드 도만 and the 쇼엔찬-held lands were missing.

The last of the 의석자들 finally mounted and pulled up beside her. Eager to move forward, but not daring to show it, 에그웨인 started a slow ride toward the meeting place. Bryne’s soldiers fell in and formed an escort of tromping boots and pikes held high. Their white tabards were emblazoned with the Flame of 타르 발론, but they did not outshine the 에스 세다이. The way they marched accented the women at their center. Other armies relied on the strength of arms. The 백색 탑 had something better.

Each army converged on the meeting place, the center of the field, where 랜드 had ordered no tents erected. So many armies together on ground perfect for a charge. This had better not go wrong.

엘레인 set precedent by leaving the vast bulk of her force halfway there, continuing on with a smaller guard of about a hundred men. 에그웨인 did the same. Other leaders began to trickle forward, their retinues coming to rest in a large ring around the central field.

Sunlight shone down upon 에그웨인 as she approached the center. She couldn’t help but notice the large, perfectly broken circle of clouds above the field. 랜드 did affect things in strange ways. He needed no announcement to say that he was in attendance, no banner. The clouds pulled back and sunlight shone down when he was near.

It did not seem that he’d arrived at the center yet, however. She met up with 엘레인. “엘레인, I’m sorry,” she said, not for the first time.

The golden-haired woman kept her eyes forward. “The city is lost, but the city is not the nation. We must have this meeting, but do so quickly, so that I can return to 안도르. Where is 랜드?”

“Taking his time,” 에그웨인 said. “He’s always been like that.”

“I have spoken to 아비엔다,” 엘레인 said, her bay horse shifting and snorting. “She spent last night with him, but he wouldn’t tell her what he intends this day.”

“He has mentioned demands,” 에그웨인 said, watching the rulers gather with their retinues. 달린 Sisnera, King of 티어, was first. He would support her, for all the fact that he owed 랜드 his crown. The 쇼엔찬 threat still bothered him deeply. The middle-aged man with a dark, pointed beard was not particularly handsome, but self-composed and sure of himself. He bowed from horseback to 에그웨인, and she held out her ring.

He hesitated, then dismounted and came forward, bowing his head and kissing the ring. “빛 illumine you, Mother.”

“I am glad to see you here, 달린.”

“So long as your promise holds. 관문s to my homeland should the moment require it.”

“It will be done.”

He bowed again, eyeing a man riding up toward 에그웨인 from the other side. 그레고린, Steward of 일리안, was 달린’s equal in many ways-- but not all. 랜드 had named 달린 Steward of 티어, but the High Lords had asked for him to be crowned king. 그레고린 remained merely a Steward. The tall man had lost weight recently, his round face—with its customary 일리안er beard—starting to look sunken. He didn’t wait for 에그웨인 to prod him; he swung from his horse and seized her hand, executing a flourishing bow and a kiss to the ring.

“I’m pleased the two of you could put aside differences to join me in this endeavor,” 에그웨인 said, drawing their attention away from glares at one another.

“The Lord Dragon’s intentions are… troubling,” 달린 said. “He chose me to lead 티어 because I opposed him when I felt it necessary. I believe he will listen to reason if I present it to him.”

그레고린 snorted. “The Lord Dragon do be perfectly reasonable. We do need to offer a good argument, and I do think he will listen.”

“My Keeper has some words for each of you,” 에그웨인 said. “Please listen to what she has to say. Your cooperation will be remembered.”

Silviana rode forward and drew 그레고린 aside to speak to him. There wasn’t much of importance to say, but 에그웨인 had feared these two would end up chipping at one another. Silviana’s instruction was to keep them apart.

달린 regarded her with a discerning gaze. He seemed to understand what she was doing, but didn’t complain as he mounted his horse.

“You seem troubled, King 달린,” she said.

“Some old rivalries run deeper than the ocean’s depths, Mother. I can almost wonder if this meeting was the work of the 어둠의 존재, hoping that we would end up destroying one another and doing his work for him.”

“I understand,” 에그웨인 said. “Perhaps it would be best if you advised your men—again, if you’ve already done so—that there are to be *no* accidents’ this day.”

“A wise suggestion.” He bowed, pulling back.

They were both with her, as was 엘레인. 게알단 would stand for 랜드, if what 엘레인 said about Queen Alliandre was true. 게알단 wasn’t so powerful that Alliandre worried her—the Borderlanders were another matter. 랜드 seemed to have won them over.

Each of their flags flew over their respective armies, and each ruler was in attendance save Queen Ethenielle, who was in 캔도르 trying to organize the refugees fleeing her homeland. She had left a sizable contingent for this meeting—including Antol, her eldest son—as if to state that what happened here was as important to 캔도르’s survival as fighting on the border.
캔도르. The first casualty of the Last Battle. The entire country was said to be aflame. Would 안도르 be next? The 두 강? *Steady,* 에그웨인 thought.

It felt awful to have to consider who was “for” whom, but it was her duty to do so. 랜드 could not direct the Last Battle personally, as he would undoubtedly wish to do. His mission would be to fight the 어둠의 존재; he would have neither the presence of mind nor the time to act as a commanding general as well. She intended to come from this meeting with the 백색 탑 acknowledged as leading the collected forces against the Shadow, and she would *not* give up responsibility for the seals.

How much could she trust this man 랜드 had become? He wasn’t the 랜드 she’d grown up with. He was more akin to the 랜드 she’d come to know out in the 아일 황무지, only more confident. And, perhaps, more cunning. He had grown quite proficient at the Game of Houses.

None of these changes in him were terrible things, assuming he could still be reasoned with.

*Is that the flag of 아라드 도만?* she thought, surprised. It wasn’t just the flag, it was the *King’s* flag, indicating he was riding with those forces that had just arrived on the field. Had 로델 이투랄데 finally ascended to the throne, or had 랜드 picked someone else? The 도마니 king’s flag flew next to that of 다브람 바쉐어, uncle to the Queen of 살다에아.

“Light.” 가윈 nudged his horse up beside hers. “That flag…”

“I see it,” 에그웨인 said. “I’ll have to pin down 시우안: have her sources mentioned who took the throne? I was afraid the 도마니 would ride into battle without a leader.”

“The 도마니? I was talking about *that.”*

She followed his eyes. A new force was approaching, moving with apparent haste, under the banner of the red bull. “무란디,” 에그웨인 said. “Curious. Roedran has finally decided to join the rest of the world.”

The newly arrived Murandians made more show than they probably deserved. Their apparel, at least, was pretty: yellow and red tunics over mail; brass helmets with wide brims. The wide red belts bore the symbol of the charging bull. They kept their distance from the 안도르ans, wrapping around behind the 아일 forces and coming in from the northwest.

에그웨인 looked toward 랜드’s camp. Still no sign of the Dragon himself.

“Come,” she said, nudging Sifter into motion toward the Murandian force. 가윈 fell in beside her, and Chubain brought a force of twenty soldiers as a guard.

Roedran was a corpulent man swathed in red and gold; she could practically hear the man’s horse groaning with each step. His thinning hair was more white than black, and he watched her with an unexpectedly keen expression. The King of 무란디 was little more than ruler of one city, Lugard, but her reports indicated that this man wasn’t doing a bad job of expanding his rule. Given a few years, he might actually have a full kingdom to call his own.

Roedran held up a meaty hand, stopping his procession. She reined in her horse and waited for him to approach her, as would be customary. He didn’t.

가윈 muttered a curse. 에그웨인 let a smile tug at the edges of her lips. 감시자s could be useful, if only to express what she should not. Finally, she nudged her horse forward.

“So.” Roedran looked her over. “You’re the new Amyrlin. An 안도르an.”

“The Amyrlin has no nationality,” 에그웨인 said coolly. “I am curious to find you here, Roedran. When did the Dragon extend an invitation to you?”

“He didn’t.” Roedran waved for a cupbearer to bring him some wine. I thought it was high time 무란디 stopped being left out of events.”

“And through whose gateways did you arrive? Surely you didn't cross 안도르 to reach here.”

Roedran hesitated.

“You came from the south,” 에그웨인 said, studying him. “안도르. 엘레인 sent for you?”

“She did not *send* for me,” Roedran snapped. “The bloody Queen promised me if I supported her cause, she’d release a proclamation of intention, promising not to invade 무란디.” He hesitated. “Besides, I’ve been curious to see this false Dragon. Everybody in the world seems to have taken leave of their senses regarding him.”

“You *do* know what this meeting is about, don’t you?” 에그웨인 said.

He waved a hand. “Talking this man out of his conquering ways, or something like that.”

“Good enough.” 에그웨인 leaned forward. “I hear your rule is consolidating nicely, and that Lugard may actually have some real authority in 무란디 for once.”

“Yes,” Roedran said, sitting up a bit straighten “That is true.”

에그웨인 leaned forward further. You're welcome, she said softly, then smiled. She turned Sifter and led her retinue away.

“에그웨인,” 가윈 said softly, trotting his horse beside hers, “did you really just do that?”

“Does he look troubled?”

가윈 glanced over his shoulder. “Very.”

“Excellent.”

가윈 continued riding for a moment, then broke into a deep grin.

“That was positively evil.”

“He’s as boorishly rude as reports have made him out to be,” 에그웨인 said. “He can suffer a few nights spent wondering how the 백색 탑 has been pulling strings in his realm. If I’m feeling particularly vengeful, I’ll set up some good secrets for him to unearth. Now, where *is* that sheepherder? He has the audacity to demand that we . . ”

She trailed off as she saw him coming. 랜드 strode across the browning grass of the field, wearing red and gold. A tremendous bundle hovered in the air beside him, held up by weaves she could not see.

The grass greened at his feet.

It wasn’t a large change. Where he trod, the turf recovered, spreading from him like a soft wave of light through opening shutters. Men stepped back; horses stamped their hooves. Within minutes, the entire ring of troops stood on grass that lived again.

How long had it been since she’d seen a simple field of green? 에그웨인 breathed out. Some of the gloom to the day had been lightened. “I’d give good coin to know how he does that,” she murmured under her breath.

“A weave?” 가윈 asked. “I’ve seen 에스 세다이 make flowers bloom in winter.”

“I know of no weave that would be so extensive,” 에그웨인 said. “It feels so *natural.* Go see if you can find out how he’s doing it. Maybe one of the 에스 세다이 with Asha’man 감시자s will let the truth out.”

가윈 nodded, slipping away.

랜드 continued his walk, trailed by that large floating bundle, Asha’man in black and an honor guard of 아일. The 아일 spurned regular ranks, sweeping the land like a swarm, fanning out. Even soldiers who followed 랜드 shied back from the 아일. For many of the older soldiers, a wave of browns and tans like that meant death.

랜드 walked calmly, purposefully. The cloth bundle he carried with Air began to unravel in front of him. Large swaths of canvas rippled in the wind before 랜드, braiding with one another, leaving long trails behind themselves. Wooden poles and metal stakes fell from inside them, and 랜드 caught those in unseen threads of Air, spinning them.

He never broke stride. He didn’t look at the maelstrom of cloth, wood and iron, as canvas rippled in front of him like fish from the depths. Small clods of soil erupted from the ground. Some soldiers jumped.

*He’s grown into quite the showman,* 에그웨인 thought as the poles spun and came down in the holes. Sweeping bands of cloth wrapped around them, tying themselves. In seconds, a massive pavilion settled into place, the Dragon banner flapping from one end, the banner with the ancient symbol of the 에스 세다이 on the other.

랜드 didn’t break stride as he reached the pavilion, cloth sides parting for him. “You may each bring five,” he announced as he stepped inside.

“Silviana,” 에그웨인 said, “사에린, Romanda, Lelaine. 가윈 will be our fifth when he returns.”

의석자들 behind suffered the decision in silence. They couldn’t complain about her taking her 감시자 for protection or her Keeper for support. The other three she’d chosen were widely considered among the most influential in the Tower, and together the four she brought included two 에스 세다이 each from Salidar and the 백색 탑 loyalists.

The other rulers allowed 에그웨인 to enter before them. All understood that this confrontation was, at its core, between 랜드 and 에그웨인. Or, rather, the Dragon and the 아미를린 석좌.

There were no chairs inside the pavilion, though 랜드 hung *세이딘* globes of light at the corners, and one of the Asha’man deposited a small table at the center. She did a quick count. Thirteen glowing globes.

랜드 stood facing her, arms behind his back, hand clasping his other forearm as had become his habit. 민 stood at his side, one hand on his arm.

“Mother,” he said, nodding his head.

So he would pretend respect, would he? 에그웨인 nodded back. “Lord Dragon.”

The other rulers and their small retinues filed in, many doing so with timidity until 엘레인 swept in, the sorrow on her face lightening as 랜드 smiled warmly at her. The wool-headed woman was still impressed with 랜드, pleased with how he’d managed to bully everyone into coming here. 엘레인 considered it a matter of pride when he did well.

*And you don’t feel a small measure of pride?* 에그웨인 asked herself. *랜드 al’Thor, once simple village boy and your near-betrothed, now the most powerful man in the world? You don’t feel proud of what he’s done?*

Perhaps a little.

The Borderlanders entered, led by King Easar of 시엔나르, and there was nothing timid about them. The 도마니 were led by an older man that 에그웨인 did not know.

“알살람,” Silviana whispered, sounding surprised. “He has returned.”

에그웨인 frowned. Why hadn’t any of her informants told her he had shown up? Light. Did 랜드 know that the 백색 탑 had tried to take him into custody? 에그웨인 herself had discovered that fact only a few days before, buried in a pile of 엘라이더’s papers.

Cadsuane entered, and 랜드 nodded to her, as if giving permission. She didn’t bring five, but neither did he seem to require her to be counted among 에그웨인’s five. That struck her as a bothersome precedent. 페린 stepped in with his wife, and they stayed to the side. 페린 folded his tree-trunk arms, wearing his new hammer at his belt. He was far easier to read than 랜드 was. He was worried, but he trusted 랜드. 니나브 did, too, burn her. She took her position near 페린 and 파일.

The 아일 clan chiefs and 현명한 이들 entered in a large mass—랜드’s “Bring only five” probably meant that each clan chief could bring five. Some 현명한 이들, including Sorilea and Amys, made their way to 에그웨인’s side of the tent.

*Light bless them*, 에그웨인 thought, releasing a held breath. 랜드’s eyes flickered toward the women, and 에그웨인 caught a tightening of his lips. He was surprised that all the 아일 didn’t back him, each and every one.

King Roedran of 무란디 was one of the last to enter the tent, and 에그웨인 noticed something curious as he did. Several of 랜드’s Asha’man— Narishma, Flinn, Naeff—moved in behind Roedran. Others, near 랜드, looked as alert as cats who had seen a wolf wander by.

랜드 stepped over to the shorter, wider man and looked down into his eyes. Roedran stuttered for a moment, then started wiping his brow with a handkerchief. 랜드 continued to stare at him.

“What is it?” Roedran demanded. “You’re the 용의 환생, so they say. I do not know that *I'd* have let you—”

“Stop,” 랜드 said, raising a finger.

Roedran quieted immediately.

“Light burn me,” 랜드 said. “You’re not him, are you?”

“Who?” Roedran asked.

랜드 turned away from him, waving his hand to make Narishma and the others stand down. They did so reluctantly. “I thought for certain…” 랜드 said, shaking his head. “Where *are* you?”

“Who?” Roedran asked loudly, almost squeaking.

랜드 ignored him. The flaps to the pavilion had finally stilled, everyone inside. “So,” 랜드 said. “We are all here. Thank you for coming.”

“It’s not like we did have much of a bloody choice,” 그레고린 grumbled. He’d brought a handful of 일리안er nobility with him as his five, all members of the Council of Nine. “We did be caught between you and the 백색 탑 itself. Light burn us.”

“You know by now,” 랜드 continued, “that 캔도르 has fallen and Caemlyn has been taken by the Shadow. The last remnants of 말키에르 are under assault at Tarwin’s Gap. The end is upon us.”

“Then why are we standing here, 랜드 al’Thor?” demanded King Paitar of 아라펠. The aging man had only a thin ribbon of gray hair remaining on his head, but he was still broad-shouldered and intimidating. “Let us put an end to this posturing and be to it, man! There is fighting to be done.”

“I promise you fighting, Paitar,” 랜드 said softly. “All that you can stomach, and then some. Three thousand years ago, I met the 어둠의 존재s forces in battle. We had the wonders of the 전설의 시대, 에스 세다이 who could do things that would make your mind reel, *ter’angreal* that could enable people to fly and make them immune to blows. We still *barely won*. Have you considered that? We face the Shadow in much the same state as it was then, with 버림받은 자들 who have not aged. But we are not the same people, not by far.”

The tent fell silent. Flaps blew in the breeze.

“What are you saying, 랜드 al’Thor?” 에그웨인 said, folding her arms. “That we are doomed?”

“I’m saying we need to plan,” 랜드 said, “and present a unified attack. That we did poorly last time, and it nearly cost us the war. We each thought we knew the best way to go.” He met 에그웨인’s eyes. “In those days, every man and woman considered themselves to be the leader on the field. An army of generals. *That* is why we nearly lost. *That* is what left us with the taint, the Breaking, the madness. I was as guilty of it as anyone. Perhaps the most guilty.

“I will not have that happen again. I will not save this world only to have it broken a second time! I will not die for the nations of humanity, only to have them turn upon one another the moment the last 트롤록 falls. You’re planning it. Light burn me, I *know* that you are!”

It would have been easy to miss the glances that 그레고린 and 달린 shot at one another, or the covetous way Roedran watched 엘레인. Which nations would be broken by this conflict, and which would step in—out of altruism—to help its neighbors? How quickly would altruism become greed, the chance to hold another throne?

Many of the rulers here were decent people. It took more than a decent person to hold that much power and not look afield. Even 엘레인 had gobbled up another country when the opportunity presented itself. She would do so again. It was the nature of rulers, the nature of nations. In 엘레인’s case, it even seemed appropriate, as 케렌 would be better off beneath her rule than it had been.

How many would assume the same? That they, of course, could rule better—or restore order—in another land?

“Nobody wants war,” 에그웨인 said, drawing the crowd’s attention. “However, I think what you are trying to do here is beyond your calling, 랜드 al’Thor. You cannot change human nature and you cannot bend the world to your whims. Let people live their lives and choose their own paths.”

“I *will not*, 에그웨인,” 랜드 said. There was a fire in his eyes, like the one she’d seen when he first sought to bring the 아일 to his cause. Yes, that emotion seemed very like 랜드—frustration that people didn’t see the world as clearly as he thought he did.

“I don’t see what else you can do,” 에그웨인 said. “Would you appoint an emperor, someone to rule over us all? Would you become a true tyrant, 랜드 al’Thor?”

He didn’t snap back a retort. He held out his hand to the side, and one of his Asha’man slipped a rolled paper into it. 랜드 took it and placed it on the table. He used the Power to unroll it and to keep it flat.

The oversized document was filled with tight, cramped letters. “I call it the Dragon’s Peace,” 랜드 said softly. “And it is one of the three things which I will require of you. Your payment, to me, in exchange for my life.”

“Let me see that.” 엘레인 reached for it, and 랜드 obviously let it go, because she was able to snatch it off the table before any of the other surprised rulers.

“It locks the borders of your nations to their current positions,” 랜드 said, arms behind his back again. “It forbids country from attacking country, and it requires the opening of a great school in each capital—fully funded and with doors open to those who wish to learn.”

“It does more than that,” 엘레인 said, one finger to the document as she read. “Attack another land, or enter into a minor armed border dispute, and the other nations of the world have an obligation to defend the country attacked. Light! Tariff restrictions to prevent the strangling of economies, barriers on marriage between rulers of nations unless the two lines of rule are clearly divided, provisions for stripping the land from a lord who starts a conflict… 랜드, you *really* expect us to sign this?”

“Yes.”

The outrage from the rulers was immediate, though 에그웨인 stood calmly, and shot a few glances at the other 에스 세다이. They seemed troubled. As well they should be—and this was only part of 랜드’s “price.”

The rulers muttered, each wanting a chance at the document, but not wanting to shoulder in and look over 엘레인’s shoulder. Fortunately, 랜드 had thought ahead, and smaller versions of the document were distributed.

“But there are very good reasons for conflict, sometimes!” 달린 said, looking over his document. “Such as creating a buffer between you and an aggressive neighbor.”

“Or what if some people from our country do be living across the border?” 그레고린 added. “Do we not have the mandate to step in and protect them, if they do be oppressed? Or what if someone like the 쇼엔찬 do claim land that is ours? Forbidding war do seem ridiculous!”

“I agree,” 달린 said. “Lord Dragon, we should have the *mandate* to defend land that is rightfully ours!”

“I,” 에그웨인 said, cutting through the arguments, “am more interested to hear his other two requirements.”

“You know one of them,” 랜드 said.

“The seals,” 에그웨인 said.

“Signing this document would mean nothing to the 백색 탑,” 랜드 said, apparently ignoring the comment. “I cant very well forbid all of you to influence the others; that would be foolishness.”

“Its *already* foolishness,” 엘레인 said.

엘레인 was not feeling so proud of him any longer, 에그웨인 thought. “And as long as there are political games to be played,” 랜드 continued to 에그웨인, “the 에스 세다이 will master them. In fact, this document benefits you. The 백색 탑 always *has* believed war to be, as they say, shortsighted. Instead, I demand something else of you. The seals.”

“I am their Watcher.”

“In name only. They were only just discovered, and I possess them. It is out of respect for your traditional title that I approached you about them first.”

“Approached me? You didn’t make a request,” she said. “You didn’t make a *demand.* You came, told me what you were going to do and walked away.”

He didn’t understand the 아일—Light, he didn’t understand Gaul, who had been with him for so long. Still, he’d noticed that the 아일 liked to be doing something. Even when they lounged, they were alert. A terrible choice, when I left them last time… We *cannot* have them striking at our backs while we fight the Shadow.” He shook his head, and 민 stepped up to take his arm. “I will find a way to deal with them. Somehow, I'll find a way.”

The signing progressed. Some did it with great flourish, others in more casual fashion. 랜드 had 페린, 가윈, 파일 and Gareth Bryne sign as well. He seemed to want anyone here who might rise to a position of leadership to have their names on the document.

“We cannot defeat them,” 아비엔다 said, speaking softly. 페린 eyed her. She smelled frustrated, but determined. “If we go to war with them, we will fall ”

“아비엔다 is right,” Amys said. “The 아일 will *not* fight the 쇼엔찬.” Rhuarc, startled, looked back and forth between the two.

“They have done horrible things,” 랜드 said, “but so far, the lands they have taken have benefited from strong leadership. If forced to it, I am content to allow them the lands they have, so long as they do not spread further. As for the women… what is done is done. Let us worry about the world itself first, then do what we can for those held captive.”

엘레인 held the document for a moment, perhaps for the drama of it, then bent down and added her name to the bottom with a flourish.

“It is done,” 모이라인 said as 랜드 picked up the document. “You *will* have peace this time, Lord Dragon.”

Angry lightning blistered the clouded sky. Despite the shade, sweat lined 란’s neck, matting his hair underneath his helmet. He’d not worn one in years; much of his time with 모이라인 had required them to be nondescript, and helmets were anything but.

“How… how bad is it?” Andere grimaced, holding his side, and leaning back against a rock.

란 looked to the battle. The 그림자태생 were amassing again. The monsters almost seemed to blend and shift together, one enormous dark force of howling, *miasmic* hatred as thick as the air—which seemed to hold in the heat and the humidity, like a merchant hoarding fine rugs.

“It’s bad,” 란 said.

“Knew it would be,” Andere said, breathing in and out quickly, blood seeping between his fingers. “Nazar?”

“Gone,” 란 said. The white-haired man had gone down in the same set-to that had nearly taken Andere. 란’s rescue had not been quick enough. “I saw him gut a 트롤록 as it killed him.”

“That is why I tried to stop you.”

Andere scowled. “I—”

“Peace, Andere,” 란 said, rising. “What I wished was selfish. I came to die for 말키에르. I have no right to deny that privilege to others.”

“Lord Mandragoran!” Prince Kaisel rode up, his once-fine armor bloodstained and dented. The 캔도리 prince still looked too young for this battle, but he’d proven himself to be as coolheaded as any grizzled veteran. “They’re forming up again.”

란 walked across the rocky ground to where a groom held Mandarb. The black stallion bore cuts on his flanks from 트롤록 weapons. Thank the Light, they were superficial. 란 rested a hand on the horse’s neck as Mandarb snorted. Nearby, his standard-bearer, a bald man named Jophil, raised the flag of 말키에르, the Golden Crane. This was his fifth standard-bearer since yesterday.

란’s forces had seized the Gap with their initial charge, shoving the 그림자태생 back before they were able to emerge into the valley. That was more than 란 had expected. The Gap was a long, narrow piece of rocky ground nestled between craggy rises and peaks.

Holding this position required nothing clever. You stood, you died and you killed—as long as you could.

란 commanded a cavalry. It wasn’t ideal for this kind of work— cavalries did best where they could spread out and had room to charge—but the passage through Tarwin’s Gap was narrow enough that only a small number of 트롤록s could come through at once. That gave 란 a chance. At least it was more difficult for the 트롤록s to take advantage of their superior numbers. They would have to pay a butcher’s bill for every yard they gained.

트롤록 carcasses had formed an almost furlike blanket leading through the canyon. Each time the creatures tried to push through the gorge, 란’s men had resisted them with lances and polearms, swords and arrows, eventually slaughtering thousands and leaving them heaped for their fellows to climb over. But each clash similarly reduced 란’s numbers.

Each assault forced his men to withdraw a little farther. Toward the mouth of the Gap. They were less than a hundred feet from it now.

란 felt the fatigue pressing deep into his bones.

“Our forces?” 란 asked Prince Kaisel.

“Maybe six thousand still able to ride, Dai Shan.”

Less than half of what they’d started with a day before. “Tell them to mount up.”

Kaisel looked shocked. “We’re going to retreat?”

란 turned to the lad.

Kaisel paled. 란 had been told that his gaze could unnerve any man; 모이라인 had liked to joke that he could outstare rocks and had the patience of an oak. Well, he didn’t feel as sure of himself as people thought, but this boy should have known better than to ask if they were retreating.

“Of course,” 란 said, “and then we're going to attack.”

*“Attack?”* Kaisel said. “We are on the defensive!”

“They’ll sweep us out,” 란 said, pulling himself into Mandarb’s saddle. “We’re exhausted, worn out and nearly broken. If we stand here and let them come at us again, we’ll fall without a whimper.”

란 knew an ending when he saw one.

“Pass these orders,” 란 said to Prince Kaisel. “We will slowly pull out of the pass. You have the rest of the troops assemble on the plain, mounted and ready to attack the 그림자태생 as they come out of the Gap. A charge will do great damage; they won’t know what hit them.”

“Wont we be surrounded and overrun if we leave the pass?” Kaisel asked.

“This is the best we can do with the resources we have.”

“And then?”

“And then they eventually break through, slice our force into pieces and overrun us.”

Kaisel sat for a moment, then nodded. Again, 란 was impressed. He’d assumed this boy had come with him to find the glory of battle, to fight at the side of Dai Shan and sweep their enemies away. But no. Kaisel was a Borderlander to the core. He hadn’t come for glory. He’d come because he’d had to. *Good lad.*

“Give the order now. The men will be glad to get back on their horses again.” Too many of them had been forced to fight on foot because of the lack of maneuverability in the narrow confines.

Kaisel gave the orders, and those orders burned through 란’s men like an autumn fire. 란 saw Andere being helped into his saddle by Bulen.

“Andere?” 란 said, heeling Mandarb toward him. “You are in no condition to ride. Go join the wounded at the back camp.”

Andere waved him off and forced himself upright. “We’ve already moved the mountain, 란. Let’s budge this feather and be through with it.”

란 could offer no argument. He called the retreat to the men ahead of him in the pass. His remaining men bunched around him, slowly backing out toward the plain.

The 트롤록s hooted and yelled in excitement. They knew that once they were free of the walls that restricted their movement, they would win this fight easily.

란 and his small force left the narrow confines of the Gap, those on foot running toward their horses tethered near the mouth of the canyon.

The 트롤록s—for once—needed no push from the 미르드랄 to charge. Their footfalls were a low rumble on the stony ground.

Several hundred yards out of the Gap, 란 slowed Mandarb and turned. Andere brought his horse up beside 란’s with difficulty, and they were joined by the other riders, who formed long lines of cavalry. Bulen cantered up to the other side of 란.

The storm of 그림자태생 neared the mouth of the Gap, a charging force of thousands of 트롤록s that would soon burst out into the open— and try to consume them.

란’s forces were silently lined up around him. Many were old men, the last remnants of their fallen kingdom. This force that had managed to plug the narrow gap now seemed tiny on the much larger plain.

“Bulen,” 란 said.

“Yes, Lord Mandragoran?”

“You claim to have failed me, years ago.”

“Yes, my Lord. It—”

“Any failing on your part is forgotten,” 란 said, eyes forward. “I am proud to have given you your *hadori.*”

Kaisel rode up, nodding to 란. “We are ready, Dai Shan.”

“This is for the best,” Andere said, grimacing, still holding to his wound, barely able to remain in the saddle.

“It is what must be,” 란 said. Not an argument. Not exactly.

“No,” Andere said. “It is more than that, 란. 말키에르 is like a tree that lost its roots to whiteworms, the branches withering slowly. I’d rather be burned away in a flash.”

란 nodded, turning and raising his sword high above his head. He gave no speeches. He had given those already. The men knew what this was. One more charge, while they still had some strength, would mean something. Fewer 그림자태생 to flood into civilized lands. Fewer 트롤록s to kill those who could not fight back.

The enemy seemed endless. A slavering, rampaging horde without battle line or discipline. Anger, destruction incarnate. Thousands upon thousands of them. They came forward like floodwaters suddenly released, surging out of the canyon.

란’s little force was but a pebble before them.

The men silently raised their swords to him, a final salute.

“Now!” 란 yelled. *Now as they begin to spread out. It will do the most damage.* 란 kicked Mandarb forward, leading the way.

Andere galloped beside 란, clinging to his pommel with both hands. He didn’t try to raise a weapon; he’d have fallen from his saddle if he had.

니나브 was too far away for 란 to feel much of her through the bond, but sometimes very powerful emotions could stand out despite the distance. He tried to project confidence in case it reached her. Pride in his men. Love for her. He wished deeply for those to be the last things she remembered of him.

*My arm will be the sword*…

Hooves clattered on the ground. The 트롤록s ahead hooted in delight, realizing that their prey had transformed a retreat into a charge of men rushing right into their grasp.

*My breast itself a shield*…

란 could hear a voice, his father’s voice, speaking these words. That was foolish, of course. 란 had been a baby when 말키에르 had fallen.

*To defend the Seven Towers*…

He had never seen the Seven Towers stand against the 황무지. He’d only heard stories.

*To hold back the darkness*…

The horses’ hooves were becoming a thunder. So loud, louder than he’d have thought possible. He held himself straight, sword out.

*I will stand when all others fall.*

The oncoming 트롤록s leveled spears as the distance between the two opposing forces narrowed.

*Al Chalidholara 말키에르.* For my sweet land 말키에르.

It was the oath a 말키에르i soldier took during their first posting to the Border. 란 had never spoken it.

He did so now in his heart.

“*Al Chalidholara 말키에르!*” 란 screamed. “란ces, set!” Light, but those hoofbeats were loud! Could six thousand make so much noise? He turned to look at those behind him.

At least ten thousand rode there.

*What?*

He pressed Mandarb forward through his surprise.

“Forward the Golden Crane!”

목소리s, shouts, screams of power and joy.

The air ahead to the left *split* with a sudden vertical slash. A gateway three dozen paces wide—as large as 란 had ever seen—opened as if into the sun itself. From the other side, the brightness spilled out, *exploded* out. Charging men in full armor burst from the gateway, falling into place at 란’s flank. They flew the flag of 아라펠.

More gateways. Three, then four, then a dozen. Each broke the field in coordination, charging horsemen bursting forth with lances leveled, flying the flags of 살다에아, 시엔나르, 캔도르. In seconds, his charge of six thousand had become a hundred thousand.

트롤록s in the front lines screamed, and some of them stopped running. Some held steady, spears angled to impale oncoming horses. Bunching up behind them—not being able to see clearly what was happening in front—other enraged hordes pushed eagerly forward, waving large swords with scythe-like blades and double-bitted battle-axes.

Those 트롤록s at the front, holding spears, exploded.

From somewhere behind 란, Asha’man began to send weaves to rip the earth, completely destroying the front ranks of 트롤록s. As the carcasses collapsed to the ground, the middle ranks found themselves completely exposed, facing a storm of hooves, swords and lances.

란 hit, swinging, crashing Mandarb through the snarling 트롤록s. Andere was laughing.

“Back, you fool!” 란 yelled to him as he lashed out at the nearby 트롤록s. “Direct the Asha’man to our wounded; have them protect the camp!”

“I want to see you smile, 란!” Andere shouted, clinging to his horse’s saddle. “Show more emotion than a stone, for once! Surely this deserves it!”

란 looked at the battle he’d never thought to win, seeing a last stand instead become a promising fight, and couldn’t help himself. He didn’t just smile, he laughed.

Andere obeyed his order, riding off to seek 치유 and organize the back lines.

“Jophil,” 란 called. “Raise my banner high! 말키에르 lives on this day!”

*Into the Thick of It*

엘레인 stepped out of the pavilion after the meeting—and entered a grove of a dozen or so trees. The way she froze and gaped would have been embarrassing if everyone else hadn’t been doing the same. She looked to the side, where 에그웨인 stood, mouth open, as she stared up into the huge trees. The sun still shone above, but the green leaves shaded the area, explaining why the light had dimmed inside the tent.

They burst from the ground; it took less than five minutes for them to become so tall. I swear it, my Lord, or may I never draw blade again.”

“All right,” 엘레인 said, releasing the Source. “Lets begin. Nations are burning. Maps! We need maps!”

The other rulers turned toward her. In the meeting, with 랜드 standing there, few of them had objected to her being chosen to lead them. That was how it could be around him; a person was swept up in the tides of 랜드’s will. Things seemed so logical when he spoke of them.

Many now looked displeased to have her put above them. Best to give them no time to dwell on it. “Where is Master Norry?” she said to Dyelin. “Could he have—”

“I have maps, Your Majesty,” Gareth Bryne said as he left the pavilion, 시우안 at his side.

He seemed grayer than she remembered him; he wore a stiff white coat and trousers, the breast marked with the Flame of 타르 발론. He bowed in respect, but did not step too close. His uniform made his allegiance plain, as did 시우안’s protective hand on his arm.

엘레인 remembered him standing with that same quiet expression behind her mother. Never presuming, always protecting the Queen. That queen had put him out to pasture. That event hadn’t been 엘레인’s fault, but she could read the breached trust in Bryne’s face.

엘레인 could not change what had come and gone. She could look only to the future. “If you have maps of this area and the potential battlefields presented to us, Lord Bryne, we would love to see them. I would like maps for the area between here and Caemlyn, a detailed map of 캔도르 and your best maps of the other Borderland areas.” To the rulers, she continued, “Gather your commanders and advisors! We must meet immediately with the other great captains to discuss our next course of action.”

It didn’t take long, though the confusion was pervasive as two dozen different factions set to work. Servants pulled open the sides of the pavilion, and 엘레인 ordered Sumeko to gather Kinswomen and guards to fetch tables and some chairs through a gateway from her camp. 엘레인 also sent for specific reports of what was happening at the Gap, where 랜드 had asked the bulk of the Borderlander armies to go and rescue 란. The rulers and great captains had remained behind for the planning.

Shortly, 엘레인 and 에그웨인 stood surveying Bryne’s detailed maps, which had been spread out across four tables. The rulers stood back and allowed the commanders to deliberate.

“This is good work, Bryne,” Lord Agelmar said. The 시엔나르an was one of the four remaining great captains. Bryne was another. The final two great captains—다브람 바쉐어 and 로델 이투랄데—stood side by side at the end of another table, making corrections to a map of the western 국경지대. 이투랄데 had bags under his eyes, and his hands sometimes shook. From what 엘레인 had heard, he had suffered quite an ordeal in 마라도나, having been rescued only very recently. She was surprised he was here, actually.

“All right,” 엘레인 said to the assembly. “We must fight. But how? Where?”

The Gap should not be abandoned, assuming our armies are enough to help Lord Mandragoran stabilize there. The likely result of our push there today will be the 그림자태생 pulling back into the pass. Keeping the enemy plugged up there is an unsuitable task for the 말키에르i heavy cavalry alone. Perhaps we would best send him some pike companies? If he continues to plug that breach, we can devote the majority of our forces to combat in 안도르 and 캔도르.”

“Nobody travels the Ways,” 이투랄데 said, aghast.

“The 트롤록s do,” Agelmar said.

“I’ve been through them,” 페린 said, approaching the table. “And I’m sorry, my Lords, but I don’t think that taking the Waygate from the other side would work. From what I understand, we couldn’t destroy it—even with the 하나의 힘. And we couldn’t hold it inside, not with the Black Wind in there. Our best choice is to somehow get those 트롤록s out of Caemlyn and then hold this side of the Waygate. If it is properly guarded, the Shadow would never be able to use it against us.”

엘레인 frowned. “ ‘Something’?”

“I’m always careful,” 엘레인 said absently. “So how do we get those 트롤록s out of Caemlyn?”

“Perhaps we can hide a large assault force in Braem Wood; it’s here, almost fifty leagues north of Caemlyn.” Bryne pointed at the map. “If a smaller company of soldiers were to go up to the city gates and get the 트롤록s to chase them back to the Wood as bait in the trap ... I always worried that an invading army would use the Wood for cover as a base for attacking the city. I never thought I’d be considering the same option myself.”

이투랄데 scratched at his chin. “This entire matter is going to be difficult. Three 트롤록 armies, with us forced to divide our attention between them. Yes, more and more, I realize that the right move is to focus on one of them and set delaying forces against the other two.”

“그림자’s army at Caemlyn is likely the smallest,” Agelmar said, “as the size of the Waygate has restricted their entry into the city.”

“Yes,” 바쉐어 agreed. “Our chance for a quick victory on one of the battlefronts is best at Caemlyn. We should strike hard there with the largest of our assault forces. If we can win in 안도르, it will reduce the number of fronts we have to fight on—and that will be extremely advantageous.”

“Yes,” 엘레인 said. “We reinforce 란, but tell him that his job will be to hold there as long as he can. We place a second force at the border of 캔도르, with the purpose of delaying there as well—perhaps a slow withdrawal, as conditions dictate. While those two fronts are held, we can focus our true attention—and our largest army—at breaking the 트롤록s in Caemlyn.”

“The 백색 탑?” 엘레인 asked. “If we send the 에스 세다이 to 캔도르, they can slow the 트롤록s’ advance across the border. That will let the rest of us concentrate on Caemlyn.”

“And what of the fourth battlefront?” 이투랄데 asked. “세이올 굴? Does anyone know what the Lord Dragon plans there?”

Nobody spoke.

“The 아일 will see to his needs,” Amys said from beside the clan chiefs. “You needn’t worry about us. Make your battle plans, and we will make ours.”

“No,” 엘레인 said.

“엘레인?” 아비엔다 said. “We—”

“This is precisely what 랜드 wished to avoid,” 엘레인 said forcefully. “The 아일 will work with the rest of us. The battle at 세이올 굴 could be the most important of all. I won’t have one group presuming to keep to themselves and fight alone. You’ll accept our help.”

*And,* she added to herself, *our direction.* The 아일 were excellent warriors, but there were some things they just wouldn’t admit. The usefulness of cavalry, for one.

The 아일 obviously did *not* like the prospect of wetlander command. They bristled, eyes narrowing.

“The 아일 are excellent irregulars,” Bryne said, looking to them. “I faced you on the Blood Snow, and I know how deadly you can be. However, if the Lord Dragon attacks 세이올 굴, we will likely need to seize the valley and then hold it for as long as it takes him to battle with the 어둠의 존재. I don’t know how long that will take, but it could take hours. Days. Tell me, have you ever had to entrench and fight a protracted, defensive war?”

“We will do what needs to be done,” Rhuarc said.

“Rhuarc,” 엘레인 said. “You yourselves insisted on signing the Dragon’s Peace. You yourselves insisted that you be part of our coalition. I expect you to live up to your word. You *will* do as you are told.”

Bryne’s and 이투랄데’s questions had set them off, but being told directly what to do made them back down. Rhuarc nodded. “Of course,” he said. “I have *toh.”*

“Meet it by listening,” 엘레인 said, “and offering your opinion. If we’re going to fight on four different fronts at once, we’ll need a lot of coordination.” She looked at the gathered generals. “It occurs to me. We have four battlefronts, and four great captains…”

바쉐어 nodded. “No coincidence, that.”

“Well, it might be one.”

“There are no coincidences, Highness,” 바쉐어 said. “If I’ve learned one thing traveling with the Lord Dragon, that is it. Four of us, four battlefronts.

“We each take one, with Queen 엘레인 coordinating among us and overseeing the war effort as a whole.”

“I will go to the 말키에르i,” Agelmar said. “Most of the Borderlanders fight there now.”

“If the 에스 세다이 are to fight there,” Bryne said, “so will I. My place is with the 백색 탑.”

*He doesn’t want to fight in 안도르,* 엘레인 thought. *He doesn't want to fight alongside me. He wishes the break to be clean.* “Who comes to 안도르 with me, then?”

“I’ll go,” 바쉐어 said.

“And I to 세이올 굴, then,” 이투랄데 said, nodding. “To fight alongside 아일. A day I never thought I’d see, in truth.”

“Good,” 엘레인 said, pulling over a chair. “Then let’s dig into the thick of it and get to details. We need a central location for me to work from, and Caemlyn is lost. For now, I will use Merrilor. It is central, and has plenty of room to move troops and supplies around in. 페린, do you think you could take charge of the logistics of this camp? Set up a 이동 ground, and organize the channelers to help with communications and supply operations?”

페린 nodded.

“The rest of you,” she said, “let’s get to dividing the forces in detail and fleshing out the plans. We need a firm idea of how we are going to push those 트롤록s out of Caemlyn so we can fight them on even ground.”

Hours later, 엘레인 stepped from the pavilion, her mind spinning with details of tactics, supply needs and troop placements. When she blinked, she could see maps in her mind’s eye, covered with Gareth Bryne’s cramped notations.

The others from the meeting began trailing away to their separate camps to begin executing their battle plans. The dimming sky had required lanterns to be set up around the pavilion. She vaguely remembered both lunch and dinner being brought to the meeting. She’d eaten, hadn’t she? There had simply been so much to *do.*

She nodded to those rulers who passed her, giving farewells. Most of the initial planning details had been worked out. On the morrow, 엘레인 would take her troops to 안도르 and begin the first leg of the counterattack against the Shadow.

The ground here was now soft and springy with deep green grass. 랜드’s influence lingered, though he had departed. As 엘레인 inspected those towering trees, Gareth Bryne stepped up beside her.

She turned, surprised he hadn’t left the pavilion already. The only ones still here now were the servants and 엘레인’s guards. “Lord Bryne?” she asked.

“I just wanted to say that I’m proud,” Bryne told her softly. “You did well in there.”

“I had hardly anything to add.”

“You added leadership,” Bryne said. “You aren’t a general, 엘레인, and nobody expects you to be one. She grinned. Light, but it was hard not to positively beam at his words. He wasn’t her father, but in many ways, he was as close to one as she had. “Thank you. And Bryne, the crown apologizes for—”

“Not a word of that,” he said. “수레바퀴 weaves as it wills. I don’t blame 안도르 for what happened to me.” He hesitated. “I’m still going to fight together with the 백색 탑, 엘레인.”

“I understand.”

He bowed to her and strode off toward 에그웨인’s section of camp.

비르기테 stepped up to 엘레인. “Back to our camp, then?” the woman asked.

“I…” 엘레인 hesitated, hearing something. A faint sound, yet somehow deep and powerful. She frowned, walking toward it, holding up a hand to still 비르기테 as she started to ask what was happening.

The two of them rounded the pavilion, crossing green grass and blossoming morning’s breath, walking toward the sound, which grew stronger and stronger. A song. A beautiful song, unlike any she had ever heard, that made her tremble with its striking sonority.

It washed over her, enveloped her, vibrated *through* her. A joyful song, a song of awe and wonder, though she could not understand the words. She approached a group of towering creatures, like trees themselves, standing with their hands on the gnarled trunks of the trees 랜드 had grown, their eyes closed.

Three dozen 오지어 of various ages, from those with eyebrows as white as new snow to those as young as 로이알. He stood there with them, a smile raising the sides of his mouth as he sang.

페린, arms folded, stood nearby with his wife. “Your talk of going to the Asha’man had me thinking—if we need allies, what about the 오지어? I was going to see if I could find 로이알, but before I could set out, I found them already here among these trees.”

엘레인 nodded, listening to the 오지어 song reach its climax, then fade, the 오지어 bowing their heads. For a moment, all was peaceful.

Finally, an ancient 오지어 opened his eyes and turned toward 엘레인. His white beard reached low on his chest, below the white mustaches that drooped on either side of his mouth. He stepped forward, other ancients both male and female joining him. With them came 로이알.

“You are the Queen,” the ancient 오지어 said, bowing to her. “The one who leads this journey. I am 하만, son of Dal son of Morel. We have come to lend our axes to your fight.”

An older 오지어 woman shook her head. “So hasty. So quick. Know this, young one. There were some who would have abandoned you, and the world, to the Shadow.”

“I myself took that position,” the woman said. “I made the argument, though I did not truly believe it was right.”

The woman looked to him. “Trees will not grow if the 어둠의 존재 claims this world.”

로이알 looked surprised. “But why did you—”

“An argument must have opposition if it is to prove itself, my son,” she said. “One who argues truly learns the depth of his commitment through adversity. Did you not learn that trees grow roots most strongly when winds blow through them?” She shook her head, though she did seem fond. “That is not to say you should have left the *stedding* when you did. Not alone. Fortunately, that has been taken care of.”

로이알 waved to 페린, apparently wanting to catch up. “Allow me to borrow him for a moment, 로이알,” 엘레인 said, steering 페린 toward the center of the grove.

파일 and 비르기테 joined her, and 로이알 waited behind. He seemed distracted by the mighty trees.

“I have a duty I want to assign you,” 엘레인 said softly to 페린. “Losing Caemlyn threatens to send our armies into a supply crisis. Despite complaints of food prices, we had been keeping everyone fed, as well as accumulating stores for the battle ahead. Those stores are now gone.”

“What of 케렌?” 페린 asked.

“It still has some food,” 엘레인 said. “As do the 백색 탑 and 티어. Baerlon has good supplies of metals and powder—I need to find what we can draw from the other nations, and discover their food situation. “Yes.”

“I’m sorry,” 페린 said. “엘레인, 랜드 needs me.”

“He needs me more,” 페린 said. “민 saw it, he said. Without me at the Last Battle, he’ll die. Besides, I have a few fights to finish.”

“I’ll do it,” 파일 said.

엘레인 turned toward her, frowning.

“It is my duty to manage the affairs of my husband’s army,” 파일 said. “You are his liege lady, Your Majesty, so your needs are his needs. If 안도르 is to command the Last Battle, then the 두 강 will see it fed. It was logical and rational, but not what 엘레인 needed. How far did she trust this woman? 파일 had proven herself deft at politics. That was useful, but did she really consider herself part of 안도르? 엘레인 studied the woman.

“There is nobody better you can trust with this task, 엘레인,” 페린 said. “파일 *will* see it done.”

“페린,” 엘레인 said. “There is a different matter involved in this. May we speak privately for a moment?”

“I’ll just tell her what it is when we're done, Your Majesty,” 페린 said. “I don’t keep secrets from my wife.”

파일 smiled.

엘레인 eyed the two of them, then sighed softly. “에그웨인 came to me during our battle preparations. There is a certain… item of importance to the Last Battle that she needs to be delivered.”

“발레르의 뿔,” 페린 said. “You still have it, I hope.”

“We do. In the Tower, hidden. We moved it from the strongroom none too quickly. Last night, that room was broken into. I know only because of certain wards we set. 그림자 knows we have the Horn, 페린, and the 어둠의 존재’s minions are looking for it. They can’t use it; it’s tied to 맷 until he dies. But if the Shadow’s minions can capture it, he can keep 맷 from using it. Or, worse—kill him, then blow it themselves.”

엘레인 nodded slowly. “Very well. I’ll send word to you on how it will be delivered. For now, begin running supplies to establish precedent. Too many people know about the Horn. Evening approached, bringing its most dangerous hours. Fortunately, those black clouds above made nights so dark that 트롤록s had trouble seeing anything. Dusk, however, was a time of strength to them—a time when the eyes of humans were hampered but the eyes of 그림자태생 were not.

The power of the united Borderlander attack had pushed the 트롤록s back toward the mouth of the Gap. 란 was getting reinforced by the hour with pikemen and other foot to help him hold position. All in all, it looked far better here now than it had just a day before.

Still grim, though. If what Bulen said was right, his army would be stationed here as a stalling force. That meant fewer troops for him than he would have liked. He could not fault the tactics presented, however.

란 passed into the area where the 시엔나르an lancers cared for their horses. A figure emerged from them and rode up beside 란. King Easar was a compact man with a white topknot, recently arrived from the Field of Merrilor following a long day making battle plans. 란 began a horseback bow, but stopped as King Easar bowed to *him.*

We were sworn to come to your aid, so we have.” He hesitated, and then his voice grew grim. “캔도르 is beyond recovery now, Dai Shan. The Queen admits it. The 백색 탑s job is not to recover it, but to stop the 그림자태생 from taking more territory.”

They turned and rode through the ranks of lancers. The men were required to spend dusk within a few paces of their mounts, and they made themselves busy, caring for armor, weapons and horses. Each man wore a longsword, sometimes two, strapped to his back, and all had maces and daggers at their belts. Most of the men wore yellow surcoats over their plate-and-mail, bearing the black hawk. They gave their salutes with stiff backs and serious faces. Indeed, the 시엔나르ans were a serious people. Living in the 국경지대 did that.

The soldiers nearby turned toward him.

란 turned, frowning, but the King gave no explanation for the poem. If his people were a serious people, their king was more so. Easar had wounds deep within that he chose not to share. 란 did not fault him in this; 란 himself had done the same.

“What am I?” 란 asked, swinging into the saddle. “Some sheepherder from a forgotten village? I will do my duty. If men are foolish enough to put me in charge of them, I’ll send them about theirs as well.”

Narishma saluted 란 as he passed. 란 could not be certain that the great captains had chosen Borderlander Ashaman for him on purpose, but it seemed not to be a coincidence. He had at least one from each Borderlander nation—even one born to 말키에르i parents.

*We fight together.*
