*That Smoldering City*

Atop Moonshadow, her deep brown mare from the royal stables, 엘레인 Trakand rode through a gateway of her own making.

Those stables were now in the hands of 트롤록s, and Moonshadow’s stablemates had undoubtedly found their way into cookpots by now. 엘레인 did not think too hard about what else*—who* else—might have ended up in those same pots. She set her face in determination. Her troops would not see their queen look uncertain.

She had chosen to come to a hill about a thousand paces to the northwest of Caemlyn, well out of bow range but close enough to see the city. Several mercenary bands had made their camp in these hills during the weeks following the Succession War. Those had all either joined the armies of Light or had disbanded, becoming roving thieves and brigands.

The foreguard had already secured the area, and Captain Guybon saluted as members of the Queens Guard—both male and female—surrounded 엘레인’s horse. The air still smelled of smoke, and seeing Caemlyn smoldering like 용산 itself tossed a handful of bitter powder into the stew of emotions churning inside of her.

The once-proud city was dead, a pyre that pitched a hundred different columns of smoke toward the storm clouds above. The smoke reminded her of the spring burnings, when farmers would occasionally fire their fields to help clear them for planting. She hadn’t ruled Caemlyn for a hundred days, and already it was lost.

*If dragons can do that to a city,* she thought, surveying the hole that 탈마네스 had made in the nearest wall, *the world will need to change. Everything we know about warfare will change.*

“How many, would you say?” she asked the man who rode up beside her. 탈마네스 was only one day of rest away from the ordeal that should have cost him his life. He probably should have remained at Merrilor; he certainly wouldn’t be doing any frontline fighting in the near future.

“It is impossible to count their numbers, hidden as they are in the city, Your Majesty,” he said, bowing respectfully. “Tens of thousands, but probably not hundreds of thousands.”

The fellow was nervous around her, and he manifested it in a very 케렌인 way—by speaking with flowery respect. He was said to be one of 맷’s most trusted officers; she would have assumed that, by now, 맷 would have corrupted the fellow far more. He didn’t curse once. Pity.

Other gateways opened nearby onto the yellow grass, and her forces came through, filling the fields and topping the hills. She had taken charge of a large army of warriors, which included many of the *siswai’aman*, to bolster her Queen’s Guard and the 안도르an regulars under the command of 비르기테 and Captain Guybon. A second contingent of 아일—Maidens, 현명한 이들 and the remaining warriors—had been chosen to travel north to 세이올 굴 with 랜드.

Only a handful of 현명한 이들 had come with 엘레인, the ones who followed 페린. 엘레인 would have liked more channelers than that. Still, she did have the Band and their dragons, which should make up for the fact that her only other channelers were the Kinswomen, many of whom were on the weaker side of strength in the Power.
페린 and his force had come with her. That included Mayene’s Winged Guards, the 게알단in cavalry, the 백의단—she still wasn’t sure what she thought of *that*—and a company of 두 강 archers with Tam. Filling out her army was the group who called themselves the Wolf Guard, mostly refugees turned soldiers, some of whom had received combat training. And, of course, she had Captain 바쉐어 and his Legion of the Dragon.

She had approved 바쉐어’s plan for the battle at Caemlyn. *We will need to draw the fighting into the woods,* he had explained. *The archers will be deadly, loosing at the 트롤록s upon their approach. If these lads can move as well as I am told they can in the forest, they’ll be just as dangerous once they’ve pulled back.*

The 아일, too, would be deadly in a forest, where the 트롤록s wouldn’t be able to use their masses to overrun their opponents. 바쉐어 himself rode nearby. Apparently, 랜드 had specifically told him to watch over her. As if she didn’t have 비르기테 jumping every time she moved.

*랜드 had better stay safe so I can tell him what I think of him,* she thought as 바쉐어 approached in quiet conversation with 비르기테. 바쉐어 was a bowlegged man with a thick mustache. He didn’t talk to 엘레인 the way a man should a queen… but then, the Queen of 살다에아 was his niece, so perhaps he was just very comfortable around royalty.

*He is first in line for the throne,* 엘레인 reminded herself. Working with him would offer opportunities to further secure her ties to 살다에아. She still liked the idea of seeing one of her children on that throne. She lowered a hand to her stomach. The babes kicked and elbowed frequently now. Nobody had told her it would feel so much like… well, indigestion. Unfortunately, Melfane had, against all expectation, found some goat’s milk.

“What word?” 엘레인 asked as 비르기테 and 바쉐어 arrived, 탈마네스 moving his horse aside to make room.

“Scout reports of the city are in,” 바쉐어 said.

“바쉐어 was right,” 비르기테 said. “The 트롤록s have been reined in, and the burning has mostly died out. A good half of the city still stands. Much of that smoke you see is from cook fires, not buildings.”

“트롤록s are stupid,” 바쉐어 said, “but Halfmen are *not.* The 트롤록s would have gleefully ransacked the city and lit fires all across it, but that would have threatened to let the fires get away from them. Either way, the truth is we don’t know what the Shadow is planning here, but they at least have the option of trying to hold the city for a time, should they desire.”

“Will they try that?” 엘레인 asked.

“I can’t say, honestly,” 바쉐어 replied. “We don’t know their goals. Was this attack on Caemlyn intended to sow chaos and bring fear to our armies, or is it intended to take a stronghold and hold it long-term as a base from which to harry our forces? Back during the 트롤록 전쟁, the 페이드s did hold cities for that purpose.”

엘레인 nodded.

“Pardon, Your Majesty?” a voice said. She turned to see one of the 두 강 men stepping up. One of their leaders, Tam’s second-in-command. *Dannil,* she thought, *that's his name.*

“Your Majesty,” Dannil repeated. He fumbled a little, but actually spoke with some polish. “Lord Goldeneyes has his men set up in the forest.”

“Lord 탈마네스, do you have your dragons in position?”

“Almost,” 탈마네스 said. “Pardon, Your Majesty, but I’m not certain the bows will be needed once those weapons fire. Are you certain you don’t want to lead with the dragons?”

“We need to goad the 트롤록s into battle,” 엘레인 said. “The placement I outlined will work best. 바쉐어, what of my plan for the city itself?”

“I think everything is almost ready, but I’ll want to check,” 바쉐어 said, knuckling his mustache in thought. “Those women of yours made gateways well enough, and Mayene gave us the oil. You’re sure you want to go through with something so drastic?”

“Yes.”

바쉐어 waited for more of a response, perhaps an explanation. When she didn’t give one, he moved off, issuing the last orders. 엘레인 turned Moonshadow to ride down the ranks of soldiers here at the front lines, where they’d set up near the forests. There wasn’t much she could do now, in these last moments as her commanders gave orders, but she *could* be seen riding with confidence. Where she passed, the men raised their pikes higher, lifted their chins.

엘레인 kept her own eyes on that smoldering city. She would not look away, and she would not let anger control her. She would use the anger.

바쉐어 returned to her a short time later. “It’s done. The basements of many buildings that are still standing have been filled with oil. 탈마네스 and the others are in place. Once your 감시자 returns with word that the Kinswomen are prepared to open another round of gateways, we can proceed.”

엘레인 nodded, and then removed her hand from her belly as 바쉐어 glanced at it. She hadn’t realized she’d been holding it again. “What do you think of me going to battle while pregnant? Is it a mistake?”

He shook his head. “No. It proves just how desperate our situation is. It will make the soldiers think. Make them more serious. Besides…

“What?”

바쉐어 shrugged. “Perhaps it will remind them that not *everything* in this world is dying.”

엘레인 turned back, looking at the distant city. Farmers burned their fields in the spring to prepare them for new life. Maybe that was what 안도르 was suffering now.

“Tell me,” 바쉐어 said. “Are you going to tell the men that you’re carrying the Lord Dragon’s child?”

*Children,* 엘레인 corrected in her head. “You presume to know something that may or may not be true, Lord 바쉐어.”

“I have a wife, and a daughter. I recognize the look in your eyes when you see the Lord Dragon. No woman with child touches her hand to her womb so reverently when looking on a man who is not the father.”

엘레인 drew her lips into a line.

“Why do you hide it?” 바쉐어 asked. “I’ve heard what some of the men think. They talk of some other man, a Darkfriend named Mellar, once Captain of your Guardswomen. I can see that the rumors are false, but others are not so wise. You could kill those rumors if you wished.”

“랜드’s children will be targets,” she said.

“Ah…” he replied. He knuckled his mustache for a moment.

“If you disagree with the reasoning, 바쉐어, speak your mind. I will not suffer a toady.”

“I’m no toady, woman,” he said with a huff. “But regardless, I hardly doubt your child could be a greater target than he or she already is. You’re high commander of the armies of the Light! I think your men deserve to know what exactly they’re fighting for.”

“It is not your business to know,” 엘레인 said, “nor is it theirs.”

바쉐어 raised an eyebrow at her. “The heir to the realm,” he said flatly, “is not the business of its subjects?”

“I believe you are overstepping your bounds, *General*.”

“Perhaps I am,” he said. “Maybe spending so much time with the Lord Dragon has warped the way I do things. That man… you could never tell what he was thinking. Half of the time, he wanted to hear my mind, as raw as I could lay it out. The other half of the time, it seemed like he’d break me in two just for commenting that the sky looked a little dark.” 바쉐어 shook his head. “Just give it some thought, Your Majesty. You remind me of my daughter. She might have done something similar, and this is the advice I’d give her. Your men will fight more bravely if they know that you carry the 용의 환생s heir.”

*Men,* 엘레인 thought. *The young ones try to impress me with every stunt that comes into their fool heads. The old ones assume every young woman is in need of a lecture.*

She turned her eyes toward the city again as 비르기테 rode up and gave her a nod. The basements were filled with oil and pitch.

“Burn it,” 엘레인 said loudly.

비르기테 waved a hand. The Kinswomen opened their round of gateways, and men hurled lit torches through into the basements of Caemlyn. It didn’t take long for the smoke rising above the city to grow darker, more ominous.

“They won’t soon put *that* out,” 비르기테 said softly. “Not with the dry weather we’ve been having. The entire city will go up like a haystack.”

The army gathered to stare at the city, particularly the members of the Queen’s Guard and the 안도르an military. A few of them saluted, as one might salute the pyre of a fallen hero.

엘레인 ground her teeth, then said, “비르기테, make it known among the Guards. The children I carry were fathered by the 용의 환생.”

바쉐어’s smile deepened. *Insufferable man!* 비르기테 was smiling as she went to spread the word. She was insufferable, too.

The men of 안도르 seemed to stand taller, prouder, as they watched their capital burn. 트롤록s started pouring from the gates, driven by the fires. 엘레인 made sure the 트롤록s saw her army, then announced, “Northward!” She turned Moonshadow. “Caemlyn is dead. We take to the forests; let the 그림자태생 follow!”

안드롤 awoke with dirt in his mouth. He groaned, trying to roll over, but found himself bound in some way. He spat, licked his lips and blinked crusty eyes.

He lay with Jonneth and 에마린 against an earthen wall, tied by ropes. He remembered… Light! The roof had fallen in.

*페바라?* he sent. Incredible how natural that method of communication was beginning to feel.

He was rewarded with a groggy sensation from her. The bond let him know that she was nearby, probably tied up as well. The 하나의 힘 was also lost to him; he clawed at it, but ran up against a shield. His bonds were tied to some kind of hook in the ground behind him, hindering his movement.

안드롤 shoved panic down with some effort. He couldn’t see 날람. Was he here? The group of them lay tied in a large chamber, and the air smelled of damp earth. They were still underground in a part of 타임’s secret complex.

*If the roof fell in,* 안드롤 thought, *the cells were probably destroyed.* That explained why he and the others were tied up, but not locked away.

Someone was sobbing.

He strained around and found Evin tied nearby. The younger man wept, shaking.

“It’s all right, Evin,” 안드롤 whispered. “We’ll find a way out of this.”

Evin glanced at him, shocked. The youth was tied in a different way, in a seated position, hands behind his back. “안드롤? 안드롤, I’m *sorry.”*

안드롤 felt a twisting emotion. “For what, Evin?”

“They came right after the rest of you left. They wanted 에마린, I think. To Turn him. When he wasn’t there, they began asking questions, demands. They broke me, 안드롤. I broke so easily. I’m sorry…”

So 타임 hadn’t discovered the fallen guards. “It’s not your fault, Evin.”

Footsteps sounded on the ground nearby. 안드롤 feigned unconsciousness, but someone kicked him. “I saw you talking, pageboy,” Mishraile said, leaning down his golden-haired head. “I’m going to enjoy killing you for what you did to 코테렌.”

안드롤 opened his eyes and saw 로가인 sagging in the grip of 메자르 and 웰린. They dragged him near and dropped him roughly to the ground. 로가인 stirred and groaned as they tied him up. They stood, and one spat on 안드롤 before moving over to 에마린.

“No,” 타임 said from somewhere near. “The youth is next. The Great Lord demands results. 로가인 is taking too long.”

Evin’s sobs grew louder as 메자르 and 웰린 moved over to seize him under the arms.

“No!” 안드롤 said, twisting. “No! 타임, burn you! Leave him alone! Take me!”

타임 stood nearby, hands clasped behind his back, in a sharp black uniform that resembled those of the Asha’man, but trimmed with silver. He wore no pins at his neck. He turned toward 안드롤, then sneered. “Take you? I am to present to the Great Lord a man who couldn’t channel enough to break a pebble? I should have culled you long ago.”

타임 followed the other two, who were dragging away the frantic Evin. 안드롤 screamed at them, yelling until he was hoarse. They took Evin somewhere on the other side of the chamber—it was very large—and 안드롤 could not see them because of the angle at which he was tied. 안드롤 dropped his head back against the floor, closing his eyes. That didn’t prevent him from hearing poor Evin’s screams of terror.

“안드롤?” 페바라 whispered.

“Quiet.” Mishraile’s voice was followed by a thump and a grunt from 페바라.

*I am really starting to hate that one,* 페바라 sent to him.

안드롤 didn’t reply.

*They took the effort to dig us out of the collapsed room,* 페바라 continued. *I remember some of it, before they shielded me and knocked me unconscious. It seems to have been less than a day since then. I guess 타임 hasn’t yet hit his quota of Dread-lords Turned to the Shadow.*

She sent it, almost, with levity.

Behind them, Evin’s screams stopped.

*Oh, Light!* 페바라 sent. *Was that Evin?* All wryness vanished from her tone. *What’s happening?*

*They’re Turning him,* 안드롤 sent back. *Strength of will has something to do with resisting. That is why 로가인 hasn’t been Turned yet.*

페바라’s concern was a warmth through the bond. Were all 에스 세다이 like her? He’d assumed they had no emotions, but 페바라 felt the full range—although she accompanied it with an almost inhuman control over how those emotions affected her. Another result of decades of practice?

*How do we escape?* she sent.

*I’m trying to untie my bonds. My fingers are stiff.*

*I can see the knot. It’s a hefty one, but I might be able to guide you*.

He nodded, and they began, 페바라 describing the turns of the knot as 안드롤 tried to twist his fingers around them. He failed to get enough purchase on the bonds; he tried pulling his hands free and wiggling them out, but the ropes were too tight.

By the time he accepted defeat, his fingers were numb from the lack of circulation. *It’s not going to work,* he sent.

안드롤 sent back agreement, though he couldn’t keep from feeling frustrated. How long could Evin hold out?

The silence taunted him. Why couldn’t he hear any sounds? Then he sensed something. Channeling. Could that be thirteen men? Light. If there were thirteen 미르드랄 as well, the situation was dire. What would they do *if* they escaped? They couldn’t fight so many.

랜드 rifled through the pile of maps, notes and reports. He stood with his arm folded behind his back, a single lamp burning on the desk. Sheathed in glass, the flame danced as breezes eddied through the tent where he stood alone.

*A world without the 어둠의 존재. A world without evil.*

랜드 turned back to the maps. What he saw impressed him. 엘레인 was preparing well. He had not attended the meetings planning each battle. His attention was directed toward the north. Toward 세이올 굴. His destiny. His grave.

“엘레인 . . ”

“I’m sorry,” she said, turning back to him. “I *am* happy to see you, and I *am* glad you came. I’m just trying to get into my head how you fit into all of this. How *we* fit into all of this.”

“I don’t know,” 랜드 said. “I’ve never figured it out. I’m sorry.”

She sighed, sitting down in the chair beside her desk. “I suppose it is good to find there are some things you can’t fix with a wave of your hand.

“There is much I can’t fix, 엘레인.” He glanced at the desk, and the maps. “So much.”

*Don't think about that.*

He knelt before her, getting a cocked eyebrow until he placed his hand on her belly—hesitantly, at first. “I didn’t know,” he said. “Not until just recently, the night before the meeting. Twins, it is said?”

“Yes.”

But this… this wasn’t a surprise. He found that deep down, he’d hoped that someday he would be a father. It had happened. That gave him warmth. One thing was going right in the world, even if so many had gone wrong.

Children. *His* children. He closed his eyes, breathing in, enjoying the thought.

He would never know them. He would leave them fatherless before they were even born. But, then, Janduin had left 랜드 fatherless—and he had turned out all right. Just a few rough edges, here and there.

랜드 let himself go still as he felt her womb. Was that motion? A kick? “No,” 랜드 said softly. “Please do not name either child after me, 엘레인. Let them live their own lives. My shadow will be long enough as it is.”

He looked up to meet her eyes, and he found her smiling with fondness. She rested a smooth hand on his cheek. “You will be a fine father.”

랜드 sighed, but rose, seating himself in the chair beside hers as she called to the guards at the tent flap for their meal.

“Can we at least discuss tactics?” 랜드 asked. “I am truly impressed by what you’ve done here. I don’t think I could have done a better job.”

“The great captains did most of it.”

“I saw your annotations,” 랜드 said. “바쉐어 and the others are wonderful generals, geniuses even, but they think only of their specific battles. Someone needs to coordinate them, and you are doing that marvelously. You have a head for this.”

“No, I don’t,” 엘레인 said. “What I *do* have is a lifetime spent as the Daughter-Heir of 안도르, being trained for wars that might come. Thank General Bryne and my mother for what you see in me. Did you find anything in my notes that you would change?”

“Everything depends on them beating the 트롤록s to the Wood. Our harrying forces will be using the strongest, fastest mounts available. It will be a grueling race, there’s no question, and the horses will be near death by the time they reach the Wood. But we are hoping that the 트롤록s will be the worse for wear by then as well, which should make our job easier.”

They talked tactics, and evening became night. Servants arrived with dinner, broth and wild boar. 랜드 had wished to keep his presence in the camp quiet, but there was nothing for that now that the servants knew.

He settled himself to dine, and let himself flow into the conversation with 엘레인. Which battlefield was in the most danger? Which of the great captains should she champion when they disagreed, which they often did? How would this all work with 랜드’s army, which still waited for the right time to attack 세이올 굴?

The conversation reminded him of their time in 티어, stealing hidden kisses in the Stone between sessions of political training. 랜드 had fallen in love with her during those days. Real love. Not the admiration of a boy falling off a wall, looking at a princess—back then, he hadn’t understood love any more than a farmboy swinging a sword understood war.

Their love was born of the things they shared. With 엘레인, he could speak of politics and the burden of rule. She understood. She truly did, better than anyone he knew. She knew what it was to make decisions that changed the lives of thousands. She understood what it was to be owned by the people of a nation. 랜드 found it remarkable that, though they had often been apart, their connection held. In fact, it felt even stronger. Now that 엘레인 was queen, now that they shared the children growing within her. “You wince,” 엘레인 said.

랜드 looked up from his broth. 엘레인’s dinner was half-finished—he had been making her speak a great deal. She seemed through anyway, and held a warm cup of tea.

He looked at her, meeting her eyes. “I don’t believe I can, but their deaths weigh on me. I feel as if I should be able to do more, now that I remember. He tried to break me, and he failed.”

“Is that what happened that day atop 용산?”

He hadn’t spoken of it to anyone. He pulled his seat closer to hers. “Up there, I realized that I had been thinking too much on strength. I wanted to be *hard,* so hard. In driving myself so, I risked losing the ability to care. That was wrong. For me to win, I *must* care. That, unfortunately, means I must allow myself pain at their deaths.”

“And you remember 르웨어스 테린 now?” she whispered. “Everything he knew? That is not just an air you put on?”

“I am him. I always was. I remember it now.”

엘레인 breathed out, eyes widening. “What an *advantage.*” Of all the people he had told that to, only she had responded in such a way. What a wonderful woman.

“I have all of this knowledge, yet it doesn’t tell me what to do.” He stood up, pacing. “I should be able to *fix* it, 엘레인. No more should need to die for me. This is my fight. Why must everyone else go through such suffering?”

She stood, taking his arm. He turned to her.

Then she kissed him.

“I love you,” she said. “You *are* a king. But if you would try to deny the good people of 안도르 the right to defend themselves, the right to stand in the Last Battle…” Her eyes flared, her cheeks flushed. Light! His comments had truly made her angry.

He never quite knew what she was going to say or do, and that excited him. Like the excitement of watching nightflowers, knowing that what was to come would be beautiful, but never knowing the exact form that beauty would take.

“I said I wouldn’t deny you the right to fight,” 랜드 said.

“It’s about more than just me, 랜드. It’s about everyone. Can you understand *that?”*

“I suppose that I can.”

“Good.” 엘레인 settled back down and took a sip of her tea, then grimaced.

“It’s gone bad?” 랜드 asked.

“Yes, but I’m used to it. Still, it’s almost worse than drinking nothing at all, with how spoiled everything is.”

랜드 walked to her and took the cup from her fingers. He held it for a moment, but did not channel. “I brought you something. I forgot to mention it.”

“Tea?”

“No, this is just an aside.” He handed the cup back to her and she took a sip.

Her eyes widened. “It’s *wonderful*. How do you do it?”

“I don’t,” 랜드 said, sitting. “패턴 does.”

“But—”

“I am *taveren*,” 랜드 said. “Things happen around me, unpredictable things. For the longest time, there was a balance. In one town, someone would discover a great treasure unexpectedly under the stairs. In the next I visited, people would discover that their coins were fakes, passed to them by a clever counterfeiter.

I once saw a feather drift down from the sky and fall point-first into the mud so it stuck there. The next ten that fell did the same thing. It was all random. Two sides to a flipping coin.”

“This tea is not random.”
“Yes, it is,” 랜드 said. “But, you see, I get only one side of the coin these days. Someone else is doing the bad. 어둠의 존재 injects horrors into the world, causing death, evil, madness. But the Pattern ... the Pattern is balance. So it works, through me, to provide the other side. The harder the 어둠의 존재 works, the more powerful the effect around me becomes.”

“The growing grass,” 엘레인 said. “The splitting clouds. The food unspoiled…”

“Yes.” Well, some other tricks helped on occasion, but he didn’t mention them. He fished in his pocket for a small pouch.

“If what you say is true,” 엘레인 replied, “then there can never be good in the world.”

“Of course there can.”

“Will the Pattern not balance it out?”

He hesitated. That line of reasoning cut too close to the way he had begun thinking before 용산—that he had no options, that his life was planned for him. “So long as we care,” 랜드 said, “there can be good. 패턴 is not about emotions—it is not even about good or evil. 어둠의 존재 is a force from outside of it, influencing it by force.”

And 랜드 would end that. If he could.

“Here,” 랜드 said. “The gift I mentioned.” He pushed the pouch toward her.

She looked at him, curious. She untied the strings, and took from it a small statue of a woman. She stood upright, with a shawl about her shoulders, though she did not look like an 에스 세다이. She had a mature face, aged and wise, with a wise look about her and a smile on her face.

“An *angreal*?” 엘레인 asked.

“No, a Seed.”

“A… seed?”

“You have the Talent of creating *ter’angreal*,” 랜드 said. “Creating *angreal* requires a different process. It begins with one of these, an object created to draw your Power and instill it into something else. It takes time, and will weaken you for several months, so you should not attempt it while we are at war. But when I found it, forgotten, I thought of you. I had wondered what I could give you.”

“Oh, 랜드, I have something for you as well.” She hurried over to an ivory jewelry chest that rested on a camp table and took a small object from it. It was a dagger with a short, dull blade and a handle made of deerhorn wrapped in gold wire.

랜드 glanced at the dagger quizzically. “No offense, but that looks like a poor weapon, 엘레인.”

“It’s a *ter’angreal*, something that may be of use when you go to 세이올 굴. With it, the Shadow cannot see you.” She reached up to touch his face. He placed his hand on hers.

They stayed together long into the night.

“Yes, I have indeed,” 맷 said. “The oaths to the great 쇼엔찬 제국, and the 여제 herself, may she live forever. I’m just a poor, traveling sell-sword, once attendant to House Haak, a noble family in 무란디. I lost my eye to some bandits in the Tween Forest two years back while protecting a young child I discovered in the woods. I raised her as my own, but—”

The soldier waved him on. The fellow did not look as if he had been listening. 맷 considered staying put out of principle. Why would the soldiers force people to wait in such a long line and give them time to think of a cover story, only to not hear it out? That could offend a man. Not 매트림 카우톤, who was always lighthearted and never offended. But someone else, surely.

He rode on, containing his annoyance. Now, he just needed to make his way to the right tavern. Pity Setalle’s place was not an option any longer. That had—

맷 stiffened in the saddle, though Pips continued his leisurely pace forward. 맷 had just taken a moment to look at the other guard at the gate. It was *Petra*, the strongman from Valan Luca’s menagerie!

맷 looked the other way and slumped again in his saddle, then shot another glance over his shoulder. That was Petra, all right. There was no mistaking those log arms and that tree-stump neck. Petra was not a tall man, but he was so wide, an entire army could have taken shade in his shadow. What was he doing back in Ebou Dar? Why was he wearing a 쇼엔찬 uniform? 맷 almost went over to talk to him, as they had always been amiable, but that 쇼엔찬 uniform made him reconsider.

Well, at least his luck was with him. If he had been sent to Petra instead of the guard he had ended up talking to, he would have been recognized for sure. 맷 breathed out, then climbed down to lead Pips. The city was crowded, and he did not want the horse pushing someone over. Besides, Pips was laden down enough to look like a packhorse—if the looker knew nothing of horses—and walking might make 맷 less memorable.

Perhaps he should have started his search for a tavern in the Rahad. Rumors were always easy to find in the Rahad, as was a game of dice. It was also the easiest place to find a knife in your gut, and that was saying something in Ebou Dar. In the Rahad people were as likely to take out their knives and begin killing as they were to say hello in the morning.

He did not go into the Rahad. The place looked different, now. There were soldiers camped outside it. Generations of successive rulers in Ebou Dar had allowed the Rahad to fester unchecked, but the 쇼엔찬 were not so inclined.

맷 wished them luck. The Rahad had fought off every invasion so far. Light. 랜드 should have just hidden there, instead of going up to fight the Last Battle. The 트롤록s and 어둠의 친구들 would have come for him, and the Rahad would have left them all unconscious in an alley, their pockets turned inside out and their shoes sold for soup money. 맷 caught a glimpse of 랜드 shaving, but he squashed the image.

맷 shouldered his way over a crowded canal bridge, keeping a close eye on his saddlebags, but so far, not a single cutpurse had tried for them. With a 쇼엔찬 patrol on every other corner, he could see why. As he passed a man yelling out the days news, with hints that he had good gossip for a little coin, 맷 found himself smiling. He was surprised at how familiar, even comfortable, this city felt. He had liked it here. Though he could vaguely remember grumbling about wanting to be away—probably just after the wall fell on him, as 매트림 카우톤 was not often one for grumbling—he now realized that his time in Ebou Dar had been among the best of his life. Plenty of cards and dice in the city.

Tylin. Bloody ashes, but that had been a fun game. She had had the better of him time and again. Light send him plenty of women who could do that, though not in rapid succession, and always when he knew how to find the back door. 투온 was one. Come to think of it, he would probably never need another. She was enough of a handful for any man. 맷 smiled, patting Pips on the neck. The horse blew down 맷’s neck in return.

Strangely, this place felt more like home to him than the 두 강 did. Yes, the Ebou Dari were prickly, but all peoples had their quirks. In fact, as 맷 thought about it, he had never met a people who were not prickly about one thing or another. The Borderlanders were baffling, and so were the 아일—that went without saying. The 케렌인 and their strange games, the 타이런s and their ridiculous hierarchies, the 쇼엔찬 and their… 쇼엔찬-ness.

That was the truth of it. Everyone outside the 두 강, and to a lesser extent 안도르, was *bloody* insane. A man just had to be ready for that.

He strolled along, careful to be polite, lest he find a knife in his gut. The air smelled of a hundred sweetmeats, the chattering crowd a low roar in his ears. The Ebou Dari still wore their colorful outfits—maybe that was why the Tinkers had come here, drawn to the bright colors like soldiers drawn to dinner—anyway, the Ebou Dari women wore dresses with tight laced tops that showed plenty of bosom, not that 맷 looked. Their skirts had colorful petticoats underneath and they pinned up the side or front to show them off. That never had made sense to him. Why put the colorful parts underneath? And if you did, why take such pains to cover them over, then go around with the outside pinned up?

The men wore long vests that were equally colorful, perhaps to hide the bloodstains when they were stabbed. No point in throwing away a good vest just because the fellow wearing it was murdered for inquiring after the weather. Though ... as 맷 walked along, he found fewer duels than he had expected. They never had been as common in this part of the city as in the Rahad, but some days, he had hardly been able to take two steps without passing a pair of men with knives out. This day, he saw not a single one.

Some of the Ebou Dari—you could often tell them by their olive skin—were parading around in 쇼엔찬 dress. Everyone was very polite. As polite as a six-year-old boy who had just heard that you had a fresh apple pie back in the kitchen.

The city was the same, but different. The feel was off a shade or two. And it was not just that there were no Sea Folk ships in the harbor any longer. It was the 쇼엔찬, obviously. They’d made rules since he’d left. What kind?

맷 took Pips to a stable that seemed reputable enough. A quick glance at their stock told him that; they were caring well for the animals, and many were very fine. It was best to trust a stable with fine horses, though it cost you a little more.

He left Pips, took his bundle, and used the still-wrapped *ashandarei* as a walking staff. Choosing the right tavern was as tough as choosing a good wine. You wanted one that was old, but not broken down. Clean, but not too clean—a spotless tavern was one that never saw any real use. 맷 could not stand the types of places where people sat around quietly and drank tea, coming there primarily to be seen.

No, a good tavern was worn and used, like good boots. It was also sturdy, again like good boots. So long as the ale did not *taste* like good boots, you would have a winner. The best places for information were over in the Rahad, but his clothing was too nice to visit, and he did not want to run into whatever the 쇼엔찬 were doing there.

He stuck his head into an inn named The Winter Blossom, and immediately turned around and stalked away. 죽음감시대s in uniform. He did not want to take any slight chance of running into Furyk 카레데. The next inn was too well lit, and the next too dark. After about an hour of hunting—and not a duel to be seen—he began to despair of ever finding the right place. Then he heard dice tumbling in a cup.

At first, he jumped, thinking that it was those blasted dice in his head. Fortunately, it was just ordinary dice. Blessed, wonderful dice. The sound was gone in a moment, carried on the wind through the throng of people in the streets. Hand on his coin purse, pack over his shoulder, he pushed through the crowd, muttering a few apologies. In a nearby alleyway, he saw a sign hanging from a wall.

He stepped up to it, reading the words “The Yearly Brawl” in copper on its face. It had a picture of clapping people, and the sounds of dice mixed with the smells of wine and ale. 맷 stepped inside. A round-faced 쇼엔찬 stood just inside the door, leaning casually against the wall, a sword on his belt. He gave 맷 a distrustful stare. Well, 맷 had never met a shoulderthumper who did not give that look to every man who entered. 맷 reached up to tip his hat to the man, but of course he was not wearing it. Bloody ashes. He felt naked without it, sometimes.

“Jame!” a woman called from beside the bar. “You aren’t glaring at customers again, are you?”

“Only the ones that deserve it, Kathana,” the man called back with a 쇼엔찬 slur. “I’m sure this one does.”

“Oh, stop it,” the woman, Kathana, said. She had crossed the common room and took 맷 by the sleeve of his coat, dragging him toward the bar. She was a short thing, dark-haired and fair-skinned. She was not that much older than he was, but she had an unmistakable motherly air. “Don’t mind him. Just don’t make trouble, and he won’t be forced to stab you, kill you, or anything in between.”

She plunked 맷 down on a bar stool and started busying herself behind the bar. The common room was dim, but in a friendly way. People diced at one side, the good kind of dicing. The kind that had people laughing or clapping their friends on the back at a good-natured loss. No haunted eyes of men gambling their last coin, here.

“You need food,” Kathana declared. “You have the look of a man who hasn’t eaten anything hearty in a week. How’d you lose that eye?”

“Light, man. You expect someone to walk off with it? Get over here.” Jame grumbled but made his way over to the bar beside 맷, settling down on a stool. Kathana put a mug of ale down, and he took it up to his lips, staring straight ahead. “I'm watching you,” he muttered to 맷.

맷 was not certain this was the right inn for him, but he also was not certain he would be able to escape with his head unless he ate the woman’s food as instructed. He took a taste; it was pretty good. She had moved over and was wagging a finger while lecturing a man at one of the tables. She seemed the type who would lecture a tree for growing in the wrong spot.

*This woman,* 맷 thought, *must never be allowed to enter the same room as 니나브. At least not when I’m within shouting distance.*

Kathana came bustling back. She wore a marriage knife at her neck, though 맷 did not stare for more than a few seconds on account of him being a married man. She had her skirt pinned up on the side after the fashion of Ebou Dari commoners. As she came back to the bar and readied a plate of food for Jame, 맷 noticed him watching her fondly, and made a guess. “You two been married long?” 맷 asked.

Jame eyed him. “No,” he finally said. “Haven’t been on this side of the ocean for long.”

“I suppose that would make sense,” 맷 said, taking a drink of the ale she set before him. It was not bad, considering how awful most things tasted these days. This was only a little awful.

Kathana walked over to the dicing men and demanded they eat more food, as they were looking pale. It was a wonder this Jame fellow did not weigh as much as two horses. She did talk some, though, so perhaps he could wiggle the information he needed out of her.

“There don’t seem to be as many duels as there used to be,” 맷 said to her as she passed.

“That's because of a 쇼엔찬 rule,” Kathana said, “from the new 여제, may she live forever. She didn’t forbid duels entirely, and a bloody good thing she didn’t. The Ebou Dari won’t riot at something as unimportant as being conquered, but take away our duels… *then* you’ll see something. Anyway, duels now have to be witnessed by an official of the government. You can’t duel without answering a hundred different questions and paying a fee. It’s drained the whole life out of it all.”

“Duels aren’t about thinking,” Kathana said. “But I suppose it *does* mean that I don’t have to worry about your pretty face being cut up on the street.”

Jame snorted, resting his hand on his sword. The hilt, 맷 noticed for the first time, was marked with herons—though he could not see if the blade was or not. Before 맷 could ask another question, Kathana marched away and began squawking at some men who had spilled ale on their table. She did not seem the type to stand in one place for very long.

“Hows the weather, to the north?” Jame asked, eyes still straight ahead.

“Dreary,” 맷 replied, honestly. “As everywhere.”

“Men say it’s the Last Battle,” Jame said.

“It is.”

Jame grunted. “If it is, it would be a bad time for interfering with politics, wouldn’t you think?”
“Bloody right it would be,” 맷 said. “People need to stop playing games and have a look at the sky.”

Jame eyed him. “That’s the truth. You should listen to what you are saying.”

*Light,* 맷 thought. *He must think I'm a spy of some sort.* “It’s not my choice,” 맷 said. “Sometimes, people will only listen to what they want to hear.” He took another bite of his meat, which tasted as good as could be expected. Eating a meal these days was like going to a dance where there were only ugly girls. This, however, was among the better of the bad that he had had the misfortune of eating, lately.

“A wise man might just learn the truth,” Jame said.

“You have to find the truth first,” 맷 said. “It’s harder than most men think.”

From behind, Kathana snorted, bustling past. “The ‘truth’ is something men debate in bars when they’re too drunk to remember their names. That means it’s not in good company. I wouldn’t put too much stock in it, traveler.”

“I’m sure it is,” Kathana said. She looked him over then. “Has anyone ever told you that you should wear a hat? It would fit the missing eye quite well.”

“Is that so,” 맷 said dryly. “You give fashion advice as well as force-feeding men?”

She swatted him on the back of the head with her cleaning rag. “Eat your food.”

“Look, friend,” Jame said, turning toward him. “I know what you are and why you are here. The fake eye bandage is not fooling me. You have throwing knives tucked into your sleeves and six more on your belt that I can count. I’ve never met a man with one eye who could throw worth a dried bean. She’s not as easy a target as you foreigners think. You’ll never make it into the palace, let alone through her bodyguards. Go find some honest work instead.”

맷 gaped at the man. He thought 맷 was an *assassin?* 맷 reached up and took off the bandage, exposing the hole where his eye had been. Jame started at that.

“There are assassins,” 맷 said calmly, “after 투온?”

“Don’t use her name like that,” Kathana said, beginning to snap her cleaning rag at him again.

맷 reached up beside his head without looking, catching the tip of the rag. He held Jame's eyes with his single one, not flinching.

“There are assassins,” 맷 repeated calmly, “after 투온?”

Jame nodded. “Mostly foreigners who don’t know the right way of things. Several have moved through the inn. Only one admitted the reason he was here. I saw that his blood fed the dusty earth of the dueling grounds.”

“Then I count you a friend,” 맷 said, standing. He reached into his bundle and took out his hat and put it upon his head. “Who is behind it? Who has brought them in, put the bounty on her head?”

Nearby, Kathana inspected his hat and nodded in satisfaction. Then she hesitated and squinted at his face.

“This isn’t what you think,” Jame said. “He isn’t hiring the best assassins. They’re foreigners, so they aren’t meant to succeed.”

“I don’t care how bloody likely their chances are,” 맷 said. “Who is hiring them?”

“He’s too important for you to—”

“*Who?”* 맷 said softly.

“General Lunal Galgan,” Jame said. “Head of the 쇼엔찬 armies. I can’t make you out, friend. Are you an assassin, or are you here hunting assassins?”

“I’m no bloody assassin,” 맷 said, pulling the brim of his hat down and picking up his bundle. “I never kill a man unless he demands it— demands it with screams and thunder so loudly, I figure it would be impolite not to agree to the request. If I stab you, friend, you’ll know that it is coming, and you will know why. I promise you that.”

“Jame,” Kathana hissed. “It’s *him”*

“What now?” Jame asked as 맷 brushed past, raising his covered *ashandarei* to his shoulder.

“The one the guards have been looking for!” Kathana said. She looked to 맷. “Light! Every soldier in Ebou Dar has been told to watch for your face. How did you make it through the city gates?”

“By luck,” 맷 said, then stepped out into the alleyway.

“What are you waiting for?” 모이라인 asked.

랜드 turned toward her. They stood in 란’s command tent in 시엔나르. He could smell the smoke of burning fields, set aflame by 란 and Lord Agelmar's troops as they withdrew from the Gap.

They were burning the lands they would rather defend. A desperate tactic, but a good one. It was the sort of all-in tactic that 르웨어스 테린 and his people in the 전설의 시대 had been hesitant to try, at least at first. It had cost them dearly then.

The Borderlanders showed no such timidity.

“Why are we here?” 모이라인 pressed, stepping up to him. His Maidens guarded the tent from the inside; better to not let the enemy know 랜드 was here. “You should be at 세이올 굴 right now. That is your destiny, 랜드 al’Thor. Not these lesser fights.”

“My friends die here.”

“I thought you were beyond such weaknesses.”

“Compassion is not a weakness.”

“Is it not?” she said. “And if, in sparing your enemy because of compassion, you allow them to kill you? What then, 랜드 al’Thor?”

He had no answer.

“You cannot risk yourself,” 모이라인 said. “And regardless of whether or not you agree that compassion itself can be a weakness, acting foolishly because of it certainly is.”

He had often thought about the moment when he had lost 모이라인. He had agonized over her death, and he still reveled in her return. At times, however, he had forgotten how… insistent she could be.

“I will move against the 어둠의 존재 when the time is right,” 랜드 said, “but not before. He must think I am with the armies, that I am waiting to seize more ground before striking at him. We must coax his commanders to commit their forces southward, lest we be overwhelmed at 세이올 굴 once I enter.”

“It will not matter,” 모이라인 said. “You will face him, and that will be the time of determination. All spins on that moment, 용의 환생. All threads in the Pattern are woven around your meeting, and the turning of the Wheel pulls you toward it. Do not deny that you feel it.”

“I feel it.”

“Then go.”

“Not yet.”

She took a deep breath. “Stubborn as ever.”

“And a good thing,” 랜드 said. “Stubbornness is what brought me this far. 랜드 hesitated, then fished in his pocket. He came out with something bright and silvery—a 타르 발론 mark. “Here,” he said, holding it out to her. “I’ve been saving this.”

She pursed her lips. “It cannot be…”

“The same one? No. That is long lost, I fear. I’ve been carrying this one around as a token, almost without realizing what I’d been doing.”

She took the coin, turning it over in her fingers. She was still inspecting it when the Maidens looked with alertness toward the tent flap. A second later, 란 lifted the flap and strode in, flanked by two 말키에르i men. The three could have been brothers, with those grim expressions and hard faces.

랜드 stepped up, resting his hand on 란’s shoulder. The man did not look tired—a stone could not look tired—but he did look *worn.* 랜드 understood that feeling.

란 nodded to him, then looked at 모이라인. “Have you two been arguing?”

모이라인 tucked the mark away, face becoming impassive. 랜드 didn’t know what to make of the interaction between the two of them since 모이라인’s return. They were civil, but there was a distance between them that he had not expected.

“You should listen to 모이라인,” 란 said, turning back to 랜드. “She has prepared for these days longer than you have been alive. Let her guide you.”

“She wants me to leave this battlefield,” 랜드 said, “and strike immediately for 세이올 굴 instead of trying to fight those channelers for you so you can retake the Gap.”

란 hesitated. “Then perhaps you should do as she—”

“No,” 랜드 said. “Your position here is dire, old friend. I can do something, and so I will. If we can’t stop those Dreadlords, they’ll have you retreating all the way back to 타르 발론.”

“I have heard what you did at 마라도나,” 란 said. “I will not turn away a miracle here if one is determined to find us.”

“마라도나 was a mistake,” 모이라인 said tersely. “You cannot afford to expose yourself, 랜드.”

“I cannot afford not to, either. I won’t just sit back and let people die! Not when I can protect them.”

“The Borderlanders do not need to be sheltered,” 란 said.

“No,” 랜드 replied, “but I’ve never known one who would refuse a sword when one was offered in a time of need.”

란 met his eyes, then nodded. “Do what you can.”

랜드 nodded to the two Maidens, who nodded back.

“Sheepherder,” 란 said.

랜드 raised an eyebrow.

란 saluted him, arm across his chest, bowing his head.

랜드 nodded back. “There is something for you on the floor over there, Dai Shan.”

란 frowned, then walked to a pile of blankets. There were no tables in this tent. 란 knelt, then raised a bright, silvery crown—thin, yet strong. “The crown of 말키에르,” he whispered. “This was lost!”

“My smiths did what they could with old drawings,” 랜드 said. “The other is for 니나브; I think it will suit her. You have ever been a king, my friend. 엘레인 taught me to rule, but you… you taught me how to stand. Thank you.” He turned to 모이라인. “Keep a space clear for my return.”

랜드 seized the 하나의 힘 and opened a gateway. He left 란 kneeling, holding the crown, and followed his Maidens out onto a black field. Burned stalks crunched beneath his boots and smoke wreathed the air.

The Maidens immediately sought shelter in a small depression in the field, huddling against the blackened earth, prepared to weather the storm.

Because one was *certainly* brewing. 트롤록s milled in a large mass before 랜드, prodding at the soil and at the remains of farmhouses. The River Mora rushed nearby; this was the first cultivated land south of Tarwin’s Gap. 란’s forces had burned it before preparing to retreat downriver ahead of the 트롤록 advance.

There were tens of thousands of the beasts here. Perhaps more. 랜드 raised his arms, forming a fist, drawing in a deep breath. In the pouch at his belt, he carried a familiar object. The small fat man with the sword, the *angreal* he had recently found at Dumai’s Wells. He had returned there for one last look and found it buried in the mud. It had been useful at Mara-don. Nobody knew he had it. That was important.

But there was more to what he would do here than tricks. 트롤록s shouted as the winds whipped up around 랜드. This was not the result of channeling, not yet.

It was 랜드. Being here. Confronting *him*.

Seas grew choppy when different streams of water crashed into one another. Winds grew powerful when hot air and cool mixed. And where Light confronted Shadow… storms grew. 랜드 shouted, letting his nature stir the tempest. 어둠의 존재 pressed upon the land, seeking to smother it. 패턴 needed equalization. It needed balance.

It needed the Dragon.

The winds grew more powerful, lightning breaking the air, black dust and burned stalks flipping up, twisting about in the maelstrom. 랜드 finally channeled as 미르드랄 forced the 트롤록s to attack him; the beasts charged against the wind, and 랜드 directed the lightning.

It was so much easier to *direct* than *control.* With a storm already in place, he didn’t need to force the lightning—he needed only to cajole it.

Strikes destroyed the front groups of 트롤록s, a hundred bolts of lightning in succession. The pungent scent of burned flesh soon swirled in the storm, joining the charred stalks of grain. 랜드 roared as the 트롤록s kept coming. Deathgates sprang up around him, gateways that zipped across the ground like water striders, sweeping 트롤록s into death. 그림자태생 could not survive 이동.

The stormwinds rose around 랜드 as he struck down those 트롤록s who tried to reach him. 어둠의 존재 thought to rule here? He would see that this land already had a king! He would see that the fight would not—

A shield tried to sever 랜드 from the Source. He laughed, spinning, trying to pinpoint the shield’s origin. “타임!” he yelled, though the storm captured his voice and overwhelmed it. “I had hoped you would come!”

This was the fight that 르웨어스 테린 had constantly demanded of him, a fight 랜드 hadn’t dared begin. Not until now, not until he had control. He summoned his strength, but then another shield struck at him, and another.

랜드 drew in more of the 하나의 힘, tapping nearly all that he could through the fat man *angreal.* Shields continued to snap at him like biting flies. None were strong enough to sever him from the Source, but there were *dozens* of them.

랜드 calmed himself. He sought peace, the peace of destruction. He was life, but he was also death. He was the manifestation of the land itself.

He struck, destroying an unseen Dreadlord hiding in the rubble of a burned building nearby. He summoned fire and directed it at a second, burning him to nothingness.

He could not see the weaves of the women out there—he could only feel their shields.

Too weak. Each shield was too weak, and yet their attacks had him worried. They had come quickly, at least three dozen Dreadlords, each trying to cut him off from the Source. This was dangerous—that they had anticipated him. That was why they had hit 란 so hard with channelers. To draw 랜드 out.

랜드 fought off the attacks, but none of them were in danger of truly shielding him. A single person could not cut off someone holding as much *세이딘* as he was. They should have…

He saw it right before it happened. The other attacks were cover, feints. One that was coming would be created by a circle of men and women. A man would be leading.

*There!* A shield slammed against him, but 랜드 had had just enough time to prepare. He channeled Spirit in the tempest, weaving by instinct from 르웨어스 테린's memories, and rebuffed the shield. He shoved it away, but could not destroy it.

Light! That had to be a full circle. 랜드 grunted as the shield slipped closer to him; it made a vibrant pattern in the sky, motionless despite the tempest. 랜드 resisted it with his own surge of Spirit and Air, holding it back as if it were a knife hanging above his throat.

He lost control of the tempest.

Lightning crashed around him. The other channelers wove to enhance the storm—they didn’t try to control it, for they didn’t need to. It being out of control served them, as at any moment, it could strike 랜드.

He roared again, louder this time, more determined. *I will beat you, 타임! I will finally do what I should have months ago!*

But he did not let the anger, the wildness, force him into conflict. He couldn’t afford to. He had learned better than that.

*Doses of Forkroot*

“Light*…* ” 페린 whispered to Gaul, looking across the landscape.

The boiling, thrashing, churning black sky of the wolf dream was nothing new, but the storm that the sky had been foreshadowing for months had finally arrived. Wind blew in enormous gusts, moving this way, then that, in unnatural patterns. 페린 closed his cloak, then strengthened it with a thought, imagining the ties holding it to be fixed strongly in place.

A little bubble of calmness extended out from him, deflecting the worst of the winds. It was easier than he anticipated, as if he’d reached for a heavy piece of oak and found it as light as pine.

The landscape seemed less real than it usually did. The raging winds actually *smoothed* out hills, like erosion at high speed. In other places, the land swelled up, forming ripples of rock and new hillsides. Chunks of earth sprayed into the air, shattering. The land itself was coming apart.

The winds whipped at them, but weren’t so strong that he had to keep them at bay. They felt like the winds at the beginning of a storm, right before the rain and lightning. The heralds of oncoming destruction.
