*A Silence Like Screaming*

로이알, son of 아렌트 son of 할란, had secretly always wanted to be hasty.

Humans fascinated him, of *that* he made no secret. He was sure most of his friends knew, though he could not be certain. It amazed him what humans didn’t hear. 로이알 could speak to them all day, then find that they had heard only part. Did they think that someone would speak without intending for others to listen?

로이알 listened when they spoke. Every word out of their mouths revealed more about them. Humans were like the lightning. A flash, an explosion, power and *energy.* Then gone. What would it be like?

Hastiness. There were things to learn from hastiness. He was starting to wonder if he had learned that particular lesson too well.

로이알 strode through a forest of too-silent trees, 에리스 at his side, other 오지어 surrounding them. All held axes on shoulders or carried long knives as they marched toward the battlefront. 에리스’s ears twitched; she was not a Treesinger, but she could sense that the trees did not feel right.

It was horrible, horrible indeed. He could not explain the sense of a healthy stand of trees any more than he could explain the sensation of wind on his skin. There was a rightness, like the scent of morning rain, to healthy trees. It was not a sound, but it felt like a melody. When he sang to them, he found himself swimming in that rightness.

These trees had no such rightness. If he drew close to them, he felt he could hear something. A silence like screaming. It was not a sound, but a feeling.

Fighting raged ahead of them in the forest. Queen 엘레인’s forces carefully withdrew eastward, out of the trees. They were nearly to the edge of Braem Wood now; once out, they would march for the bridges, cross them and burn them behind. Then the soldiers would launch volleys of destruction at the 트롤록s trying to cross the river after them on their own bridges. 바쉐어 hoped to reduce the enemy’s numbers considerably at the Erinin before they continued east.

로이알 was certain this would all make fascinating information for his book, once he wrote it. If he was able to write it. He laid his ears flat as the 오지어 began their war song. He lent his voice to theirs, glad for the terrible song—the call to blood, to death—as it filled the silence left by the trees.

He started running with the others, 에리스 at his side. 로이알 drew out in front, axe raised above his head. Thoughts left him as he found himself angry, *furious,* at the 트롤록s. They didn’t just kill trees. They took the peace from the trees.

The call to blood, to death.

Bellowing his song, 로이알 laid into the 트롤록s with his axe, 에리스 and the other 오지어 joining him and stopping the brunt of this 트롤록 flanking force. He had not intended to lead the 오지어 charge. He did anyway.

He hacked at the shoulder of a ram-faced 트롤록, shearing its arm free. The thing yelled and fell to its knees, and 에리스 kicked it in the face, throwing it back into the legs of a 트롤록 behind.

로이알 did not stop his song, the call to blood, to death. Let them hear! Let them *hear!* Swing after swing. Chopping dead wood, that was all this was. Dead, rotting, horrible wood. He and 에리스 fell into place with 장로 하만, who—with ears laid back—looked utterly fierce. Placid 장로 하만. He felt the rage too.

A beleaguered line of 백의단—whom the 오지어 had relieved— stumbled back, making way for the 오지어.

He sang and fought and roared and killed, hacking at 트롤록s with an axe meant for cutting wood, and never flesh. Working with wood was a reverent business. This*…* this was killing weeds. Poisonous weeds. Strangling weeds.

He continued to chop the 트롤록s, losing himself in the call to blood, to death. The 트롤록s began to fear. He saw terror in their beady eyes, and he loved it. They were used to fighting men, who were smaller than themselves.

Well, let the 트롤록s fight someone their own size. They snarled as the 오지어 line forced them back. 로이알 landed blow after blow, shearing through arms, hacking through torsos. He shoved his way between two bear 트롤록s, laying about him with his axe, yelling in fury—fury now for what the 트롤록s had done to the 오지어. They should be enjoying the peace of the *stedding.* They should be able to build, sing, and grow.

They could not. Because of these*…* these *weeds*, they could not! The 오지어 were forced to kill. The 트롤록s made builders into destroyers. They forced 오지어 and humans to be like themselves. The call to blood, to death.

Well, the Shadow would see just how dangerous the 오지어 could be. They *would* fight, and they *would* kill. And they would do it better than any human, 트롤록 or 미르드랄 could imagine.

By the fear 로이알 saw in the 트롤록s—by their terrified eyes—they were beginning to understand.

“Light!” 갈라드 exclaimed, falling back from the thick of the fight. *“Light!”*

The 오지어 attack was terrible and glorious. The creatures fought with ears drawn back, eyes wide, broad faces flat as anvils. They seemed to transform, all placidity gone. They cut through ranks of 트롤록s, hacking the beasts to the ground. The second row of 오지어, made up mostly of females, sliced up 트롤록s with long knives, bringing down any who made it through the first line.

갈라드 had thought 트롤록s fearsome with their twisted mix of human and animal features, but the 오지어 disturbed him more. 트롤록s were simply horrible*…* but 오지어 were gentle, soft-spoken, kindly. Seeing them enraged, bellowing their terrible song and attacking with axes nearly as long as men were tall*…* Light!

랜드 let the swirling colors fade from his vision. “It is nearly time for me to go,” he said.

Questions. So many questions. Shouldn’t he have some answers by now? “어둠의 존재 is part of the Wheel,” 모이라인 said.

랜드 immediately seized control of his emotions, and did not lash back at her. The surest way to be thought of as a youth was to act like one. That said, I am one of the oldest people in existence.”

모이라인 held her warm cup of tea, which 랜드 had fetched for her before leaving. He had become ruler of so much since they had parted, and he was as humble now as when she had first found him in the 두 강. Maybe more so.

*Humble toward me, perhaps,* she thought. *He believes he can slay the 어둠의 존재. That is not the sign of a humble man.* 랜드 al’Thor, such an odd mixture of self-effacement and pride. Yes, the Wheel wove as it willed. Sometimes, she wished that weaving were easier to understand.

“Everyone knows what to do?” 란 asked, turning in Mandarb’s saddle.

The 시엔나르ans had left nothing edible in any of the nearby cities. Four days without food. The 트롤록s didn’t use supply lines; they ate what they came across. They’d be starving. Lord Agelmar saw it, too. The horns blew, and a yellow streak of light rose into the air. 란 turned Mandarb, the horse snorting at the command. He was tired, but so was 란. Both could stand another battle. They had to.

*“Tai’shar 말키에르!”* 란 roared, lowering his sword and leading his force back onto the field. All five Borderlander armies converged on the fractured 그림자태생 horde. The 트롤록s had broken lines completely to fight over the corpses.

*To Feel 황무지d*

A 트롤록 came for him, snorting, face bearing the melded features of a ram and a man. This one was more human than most, including a sickeningly human mouth with bloodied teeth. 가윈 dodged to the side, then brought his shield up and to the right under the expected blow. The shield shook with repeated impacts. One, two, three. Standard 트롤록 berserking—hit hard, hit fast and assume that the opponent would break.

Many did. They would trip, or their arms would go numb from the pounding. That was the value of pikewalls or halberd lines. Bryne used both, and a newly improvised half-spear, half-halberd line. 가윈 had read of its like in history books. Bryne’s army used them for hamstringing 트롤록s. The pike lines would keep them back, and then the halberds would reach through and slice their legs.

Their job was to blast apart the groups of 트롤록s, shattering lines and letting the soldiers work on the scattered remnants.

With the 에스 세다이 keeping the 트롤록s from solid battle formations, the fight—though grueling—was proceeding well. They hadn’t had to fall back since leaving the hills behind, and had effectively stalled the 트롤록 advance for a week here.

The ground was ripped and furrowed just in front of them, Silviana’s attacks having torn it asunder, leaving trenchlike depressions all over the field. 가윈 saw movement in the nearest trench and strode forward. A wolf-featured 트롤록 crouched inside. It snarled at him, scrambling up.

Water Flows Downhill.

The 트롤록 fell back into the trench, and 가윈 wiped his blade on the bloody rag. Five. Not bad for one of his two-hour shifts. Often the 에스 세다이 were able to repel the 트롤록s, and he just ended up standing beside 에그웨인. Of course, today she was accompanied by Silviana—they always came to the battlefront in pairs—and 가윈 was half-convinced the Keeper let a few through now and then just to keep him working.

A sudden series of explosions nearby drove him backward, and he glanced over his shoulder. Their relief had arrived. 가윈 raised his sword to Sleete as the man took up position with Piava Sedai's 감시자 to guard the area.

가윈 joined 에그웨인 and Silviana as they left the battlefield. He could feel 에그웨인’s growing exhaustion. She was pushing herself too hard, insisting on joining too many shifts.

They made their way across the trampled grass, passing a group of 일리안er Companions charging into the fray. 가윈 didn’t have a good enough view of the battle as a whole to know where specifically they were needed. He watched them go with a hint of envy.

He knew 에그웨인 needed him. Now more than ever. 페이드s slipped into camp at night, bringing Thakan’dar-forged blades to take the lives of 에스 세다이. 가윈 kept watch personally when 에그웨인 slept, relying on her to wash his fatigue away when it overwhelmed him. He slept when she was in conference with the 탑의 회의실.

He insisted that she sleep in a different tent each night. Once in a while, he convinced her to Travel to Mayene and the beds in the palace. She hadn’t done that in a few days. His arguments that she should check on the Yellows, and inspect the 치유 work, were growing thin. Rosil Sedai had things in hand there.

가윈 and the two women continued on into the camp. Some soldiers bowed, the ones who were not currently on duty, while others hastened toward the battlefield. 가윈 eyed some of these. Too young, too new.

Others were 용worn, and who knew what to make of them? There were 아일 among the 용worn, which made sense to him, since all 아일 seemed basically 용worn to him. But there were also 에스 세다이 among the 용worn ranks. He didn’t think much of their choice.

가윈 shook his head and continued on. Their camp was enormous, though it contained virtually no camp followers. Food was brought in daily through gateways in wagons—some pulled by those unreliable metal machines from 케렌. When those wagons left, they carried away clothing for washing, weapons to be repaired and boots to be mended.

It made for a very efficient camp; one not heavily populated, however, as almost everyone spent long hours on the battlefield fighting. Everyone but 가윈.

He knew he was needed, and that what he did was important, but he couldn’t help feeling wasted. He was one of the finest swordsmen in the army, and he stood on the battlefield for a few hours a day, killing only the occasional 트롤록 stupid enough to charge two 에스 세다이. What 가윈 did was more like putting them out of their misery than fighting them.

에그웨인 nodded farewell to Silviana, then turned her horse toward the command tent.

“에그웨인 . . ” 가윈 said.

“I only want to check on things,” she said calmly. “엘레인 was supposed to have sent new orders.”

“You need sleep.”

“It seems that all I do these days is sleep.”

“When you fight on the battlefield, you are easily worth a thousand soldiers,” 가윈 said. “If sleeping twenty-two hours a day were required to keep you in good enough shape to protect the men for two, I’d suggest you do it. Fortunately, that isn’t required—and neither is it required that you run yourself as hard as you do.”

He could feel her annoyance through the bond, but she snuffed it out. “You are right, of course.” She eyed him. “And you needn’t feel surprised to hear me admit it.”

“I wasn’t surprised,” 가윈 said.

“I can feel your emotions, 가윈.”

“That was from something else entirely,” he said. “I remembered something Sleete said a few days back, a joke I didn’t understand until now.” He looked at her innocently.

That, finally, earned a smile. A hint of one, but that was enough. She didn’t smile much these days. Few of them did.

“In addition,” he said, taking her reins and helping her dismount as they reached the command tent, “I’d never given much thought to the fact that a 감시자 can, of course, ignore the 세 가지 맹세. I wonder how often sisters have found that convenient?”

“I hope not too often,” 에그웨인 said. A very diplomatic answer. Inside the command tent, they found Gareth Bryne looking down through his now customary gateway; it was being maintained by a mousy Gray whom 가윈 didn’t know. Bryne stepped to his map-littered desk, where 시우안 was attempting to bring order. He made a few notes on a map, nodding to himself, then looked to see who had entered.

“Mother,” Bryne said, and took her hand to kiss her ring.

“The battle seems to be going well,” 에그웨인 said, nodding to 시우안. “We have held here well. You have plans to push forward, it seems?”

“We can’t loiter here forever, Mother,” Bryne said. “Queen 엘레인 has asked me to consider an advance farther into 캔도르, and I think she is wise to do so. I worry that the 트롤록s will pull back into the hills and brace themselves. You notice how they’ve been pulling more of the bodies off the field each night?”

“Yes.”

가윈 could sense her displeasure; she wished the 에스 세다이 had the strength to burn the 트롤록 carcasses with the 하나의 힘 each day.

“They’re gathering food,” Bryne said. “They might decide to move eastward and try to get around us. We need to keep them engaged here, which might mean pushing into those hills. It would be costly, normally, but now…” He shook his head, walking over and looking down through his gateway onto the front lines. “Your 에스 세다이 dominate this battlefield, Mother. I’ve never seen anything like it.”

“There is a reason,” she replied, “that the Shadow did everything in its power to bring down the 백색 탑. It knew. The 백색 탑 has the ability to rule this war.”

“We’ll need to watch for Dreadlords,” 시우안 said, shuffling through papers. Scouting reports, 가윈 suspected. He knew little of 시우안 산체, despite having spared her life, but 에그웨인 commonly spoke of the woman’s greed for information.

“Yes,” 에그웨인 said. “They will come.”

“The 검은 탑,” Bryne said, frowning. “Do you trust the word from Lord Mandragoran?”

“With my life,” 에그웨인 said.

“Asha’man fighting for the enemy. Why wouldn’t the 용의 환생 have done something? Light, if all of the remaining Asha’man side with the Shadow…”

에그웨인 shook her head. “Bryne, I want you to saddle up riders and send them to the area outside the 검은 탑 where gateways can still be made. Send them, riding hard, to the sisters still camped outside the 검은 탑.”

“You want them to attack?” 가윈 asked, perking up.

“No. They are to retreat back as far as it takes to make gateways, and then they are to join us here. We can’t afford any further delays. I want them here.”

She tapped the table with one finger. “타임 and his Dreadlords *will* come. They have stayed away from this battlefield, instead focusing on Lord Mandragoran. That lets them dominate their battlefield as we have this one. I will choose more sisters to send to the Borderlander army. We will have to confront them eventually.”

가윈 said nothing, but drew his lips tight. Fewer sisters here meant more work for 에그웨인 and the others.

And now, 에그웨인 said, “I need to…” She trailed off, seeing 가윈’s expression. “I suppose I need to sleep. If I am needed, send to… Light, I don’t know where I’m sleeping today. 가윈?”

“I have you in Maerin Sedai’s tent. She’s on duty in the rotation after this, so that should give you some hours of uninterrupted sleep.”

“Unless I’m needed,” 에그웨인 reminded him. She walked toward the tent flaps.

“Of course,” 가윈 said, following her out, but shaking his head toward Bryne and 시우안. Bryne smiled back, nodding. On a battlefield, there was little that would absolutely require the Amyrlin’s attention. The 탑의 회의실 had been given direct oversight of their armies.

Outside, 에그웨인 sighed, closing her eyes. He put his arm around her, and let her slump against him. The moment lasted but a few seconds before she pulled back, standing up straight and putting on the face of the Amyrlin. *So young,* he thought, *to have so much required of her.*

Of course, she wasn’t much younger than al’Thor himself. 가윈 was pleased, and a little surprised, that thinking of the man did not provoke any anger. Al’Thor would fight his fight. Really, what the man did was none of 가윈’s business.

가윈 led 에그웨인 to the 녹색 아자 section of camp, the several 감시자s at the perimeter greeting them with nods of respect. Maerin Sedai had a large tent. Most of the 에스 세다이 had been allowed to bring what housing and furniture they wished, so long as they could make their own gateway for it and use their own 감시자s to carry it. If the army had to move quickly, such things would be abandoned. Many 에스 세다이 had chosen to bring very little, but others… well, they were not accustomed to austerity. Maerin was one of those. Few had brought as much as she.

Leilwin and 베일 도몬 waited outside the tent. They had been the ones to inform Maerin Sedai that her tent was being borrowed, and that she wasn’t to tell anyone that 에그웨인 was the one using it. The secret could be discovered if anyone asked around—they hadn’t hidden themselves while walking here—but at the same time, someone asking where the Amyrlin was sleeping would draw attention. It was the best protection 가윈 could arrange, since 에그웨인 was unwilling to Travel each day to sleep.

에그웨인’s emotions immediately turned sour when she saw Leilwin.

“You did say you wanted to keep her close,” 가윈 said softly.

“I don’t like her knowing where I sleep. If their assassins *do* come looking for me in camp, she might be the one to lead them to me.”

가윈 fought down the instinct to argue. 에그웨인 was a cunning, insightful woman—but she had a blind spot regarding anything 쇼엔찬. He, on the other hand, found himself trusting Leilwin. She seemed to be the type who dealt straight with people.

“I'll keep an eye on her,” he said.

에그웨인 composed herself with a breath, then walked to the tent and passed Leilwin without saying a word. 가윈 didn’t follow her inside.

“The Amyrlin seems intent on not letting me provide service,” Leilwin said to 가윈 in that telltale 쇼엔찬 drawl.

“She doesn’t trust you,” 가윈 said frankly.

“Is one’s oath worth so little on this side of the ocean?” Leilwin said. “I swore an oath to her that none would break, not even a Muyami!”

“A Darkfriend will break any oath.”

The woman eyed him coolly. “I begin to think she assumes all 쇼엔찬 to be 어둠의 친구들.”

가윈 shrugged. “You beat her and imprisoned her, making her into an animal to be led by a collar.”

*“I* did not,” Leilwin said. “If one baker made you foul bread, would you assume all of them seek to poison you? Bah. Do not argue. There is no point. If I cannot serve her, then I will serve you. Have you eaten today, 감시자?”

가윈 hesitated. When *had* he last had something to eat? This morning… no, he’d been too eager for the fight. His stomach grumbled loudly.

“I know you will not leave her,” Leilwin said, “particularly under the watch of a *쇼엔찬*. Come, Bayle. Let us fetch this fool some food so that he does not faint if assassins do come.” She stalked off, her large 일리안er husband following. The fellow shot a glare over his shoulder that could have cured leather.

가윈 sighed and settled down on the ground. From his pocket, he pulled three black rings; he selected one, then shoved the others back into his pocket.

Talk of assassins always made him think of the rings, which he’d taken off the 쇼엔찬 who *had* come to kill 에그웨인. The rings were *ter’angreal.* They were the means by which those 피의 칼날 had moved quickly and blended into shadows.

He held up the ring toward the light. It didn’t look like any *ter’angreal* he had seen, but an object of the Power could look like anything. The rings were of some heavy black stone he did not recognize. The outside was carved like thorns, though the inside surface—the side that touched the skin—was smooth.

He turned the ring over in his fingers. He knew that he should go to 에그웨인 with it. He also knew how the 백색 탑 treated *ter’angreal.* They locked the objects away, afraid to experiment with them. But this was the Last Battle. If there was ever a time to take risks…

*You decided to stand in 에그웨인’s shadow, 가윈,* he thought. *You decided you would protect her, do what she needed of you.* She was winning this war, she and the 에스 세다이. Would he let himself grow as jealous of her as he had been of al’Thor?

“Is that what I believe it to be?”

가윈 snapped his head up, fist closing around the ring. Leilwin and 베일 도몬 had been to the mess tent and returned with a bowl for him. From the smell of it, the meal was barley stew again. The cooks used so much pepper it was almost sickening. 가윈 suspected they did so because the black flakes hid the bits of weevil.

*I can’t act like I’m doing something suspicious,* he thought immediately. *I can’t let her go to 에그웨인.*

“This?” he asked, holding up the ring. “It’s one of the rings we recovered from the 쇼엔찬 assassins who tried to kill 에그웨인. We assume it’s a *ter’angreal* of some sort, though it’s not one the 백색 탑 has ever heard of.”

Leilwin hissed softly. “Those are to be bestowed only by the 여제, may she—” She cut herself off and took a deep breath. “Only one appointed as a 피의 칼, one who has given their life to the 여제, is allowed to wear such a ring. For you to put one on would be very, very wrong.”

“Fortunately,” 가윈 said, “I’m not wearing it.”
“The rings are dangerous,” Leilwin said. “I do not know much of them, but they are said to kill those who use them. Do not let your blood touch the ring, or you will activate it, and that could be deadly, 감시자.” She handed him the bowl of stew, then strode away.

Domon didn’t follow her. The 일리안er scratched at his short beard. “She do not always be the most accommodating of women, my wife,” he said to 가윈. “But she do be strong and wise. You would do well to listen to her.”

가윈 pocketed the ring. “에그웨인 would never allow me to wear it in the first place.” That was true. If she knew about it. “Tell your wife that I appreciate the warning. I should warn you that the subject of the assassins is still a very sore subject for the Amyrlin. I’d suggest avoiding the topic of the 피의 칼날, or their *ter’angreal*.”

Domon nodded and then went after Leilwin. 가윈 felt only a small prick of shame at the deception. He hadn’t said anything untrue. He just didn’t want 에그웨인 asking any awkward questions.

That ring, and its brothers, represented something. They weren’t the way of the 감시자. Standing beside 에그웨인, watching for danger to her… that was the way of the 감시자. He would make a difference on the battlefield by serving her, not by riding out like some hero.

He told himself that time and time again as he ate his stew. By the time he was done, he was nearly certain he believed it.

He still didn’t tell 에그웨인 about the rings.

랜드 remembered the first time he’d seen a 트롤록. Not when they had attacked his farm in the 두 강. The *true* first time he’d seen them. During the last Age.

*There will come a time when they no longer exist,* he thought, weaving Fire and Air, creating an explosive wall of flames that roared to life in the middle of a pack of 트롤록s. Nearby, men of 페린’s Wolf Guard raised weapons in thanks. 랜드 nodded back. He wore the face of Jur Grady in this fight, for now.

Once 트롤록s had not scourged the land. They could return to that state. If 랜드 killed the 어둠의 존재, would it happen immediately?

The flames of his fire wall brought sweat on his forehead. He drew carefully on the fat-man *angreal*—he couldn’t afford to seem *too* powerful—and struck down another group of 트롤록s here on the battlefield just west of the River Alguenya. 엘레인’s forces had crossed the Erinin and the countryside to the east, and were waiting for their bridges across the Alguenya to be constructed. These were almost completed, but meanwhile a vanguard of 트롤록s had caught up with them, and 엘레인’s army had formed up in defensive positions to hold them off until they could cross the river.

랜드 was happy to help. The real Jur Grady rested back in his camp in 캔도르, worn out from 치유. A convenient face that 랜드 could wear and not draw the attention of the 버림받은 자들.

The 트롤록 screams were satisfying as they burned. He had loved that sound, near the end of the War of Power. It had always made him feel as if he were *doing* something.

He hadn’t known what 트롤록s were the first time he’d seen them. Oh, he’d known of 아지노르’s experiments. 르웨어스 테린 had named him a madman on more than one occasion. He hadn’t understood; so many of them hadn’t. 아지노르 had loved his projects far too much. 르웨어스 테린 had made the mistake of assuming that 아지노르, like 세미르하제, enjoyed the torture for its own sake.

And then the 그림자태생 had come.

The monsters continued burning, limbs twitching.

Still, 랜드 worried that these *things* might be humans reborn. 아지노르 had used people to create the 트롤록s and 미르드랄. Was this the fate of some? To be reborn as twisted creations such as this? The idea sickened him.

He checked the sky. The clouds had begun to withdraw, as they did near him. He could force them to not do so, but... no. Men needed the Light, and he could not fight here too long, lest it become obvious that one of the Asha’man was too strong for the face he wore.

랜드 let the light come.

All across the battlefield near the river, people glanced toward the sky as sunlight fell on them, the dark clouds pulling back.

*No more hiding*, 랜드 thought, removing his Mask of Mirrors and raising his hand in a fist above his head. He wove Air, Fire and Water, creating a column of light extending from himself high into the sky. 병사s across the battlefield cheered.

He would not bring down the traps the 어둠의 존재 had waiting for him. He moved through a gateway back to Merrilor. He never stayed long at a battlefront, but he always revealed himself before he left. He let the clouds break above, proving he had been there, then withdrew.

민 waited for him at the Merrilor 이동 ground. He looked behind himself as his gateway closed, leaving the people to fight without him. 민 placed a hand on his arm. His Maiden guards waited here; they reluctantly allowed him to fight alone as they knew that their presence would give him away.

“You look sad,” 민 said softly.

A hot breeze blew from somewhere north. Nearby soldiers saluted him. Most of what he had here were 도마니, 타이런s and 아일. The assault force, led by 로델 이투랄데 and King 달린, that would try to hold the valley of Thakan’dar while 랜드 wrestled with the 어둠의 존재.

The time had almost arrived for that. 그림자 had seen him fighting on all fronts. He had joined 란’s fighting, 에그웨인’s fighting and 엘레인’s in turn. By now the Shadow had committed most of its armies to the fighting in the south. The time for 랜드 to strike 세이올 굴 was at hand.

He looked to 민. “모이라인 calls me a fool for these attacks. She says that even a small risk to me is not worth what I accomplish.”

“모이라인 is probably right,” 민 said. “She often is. But I prefer you as the person who would do this. *That* is the person who can defeat the 어둠의 존재: the man who cannot sit and plan while others die.”

랜드 put his arm around her waist. Light, what would he have done without her? *I'd have fallen,* he thought. *During the dark months ... I'd have fallen for certain.*

Over 민’s shoulder, 랜드 saw a gray-haired woman approaching. And behind her, a smaller figure in blue stopped and pointedly turned the other way. Cadsuane and 모이라인 gave one another wide berth in the camp. He thought he caught a hint of a glare in 모이라인’s eyes when she saw that Cadsuane had spotted 랜드 first.

Cadsuane came up to him, then walked around him, looking him up and down. She nodded to herself several times.

“Trying to decide if I’m up to the task?” 랜드 said to Cadsuane, keeping emotions—in this case, annoyance—from his voice.

“I never wondered,” Cadsuane said. “Even before I found you were reborn, I never wondered if I would be able to make you into the man you needed to be. Wondering, in that manner at least, is for fools. Are you a fool, 랜드 al’Thor?”

“An impossible question,” 민 replied. “If he says that he is, then a fool he becomes. If he says that he is not, then he implies he does not seek further wisdom.”

“Phaw. You’ve been reading too much, child.” Cadsuane seemed fond as she said it. She turned to 랜드. “I hope you give her something nice.”

“What do you mean?” 랜드 asked.

“You’ve been giving things to people,” Cadsuane said, “in preparation for death. It’s common for the elderly or for men riding into a battle they don’t think they can win. A sword for your father, a *ter’angreal* for the Queen of 안도르, a crown for 란 Mandragoran, jewelry for the 아일 girl, and for this one.” She nodded at 민.

랜드 stiffened. He’d known what he was doing, on some level, but to hear it explained was disconcerting.

민’s expression darkened. Her grip on him tightened.

“Walk with me,” Cadsuane said. “Just you and me, Lord Dragon.” She glanced at him. “If you will.”

민 looked to 랜드, but he patted her on the shoulder and nodded. “I’ll meet you at the tent.”

She sighed, but retreated. Cadsuane had already started on the path. 랜드 had to jog a few steps to catch up. She probably enjoyed seeing that.

“모이라인 Sedai grows restless with your delays,” Cadsuane said.

“And what are your thoughts?”

“I think she has a portion of wisdom to her. However, I do not find your plan to be complete idiocy. You must not delay much longer, however.”

He purposely did not say when he would give the order to attack 세이올 굴. He wanted everyone guessing. If nobody around him knew when he would strike, then chances were good the 어둠의 존재 wouldn’t know either.

“Regardless,” Cadsuane said, “I am not here to speak about your delays. I feel that 모이라인 Sedai has your… education in that matter well in hand. Something else worries me far more.”

“And that is?”

“That you expect to die. That you are giving so much away. That you do not even seek to live.”

랜드 took a deep breath. Behind, a group of Maidens trailed him. He passed the Windfinders in their small camp, huddled and speaking over the Bowl of Winds. They looked toward him and Cadsuane with placid faces.

“Leave me go to my fate, Cadsuane,” 랜드 said. “I have embraced death. I will take it when it comes.”

“I am pleased at that,” she said, “and do not think—for a moment— that I would not trade your life for the world.”

“You’ve made that obvious from the start,” 랜드 said. “So why worry now? This fight will claim me. So it must be.”

“You must not assume that you will die,” Cadsuane said. “Even if it is nearly inevitable, you must not take it as *completely* inevitable.”

“엘레인 said much the same thing.”

“Then she has spoken wisdom at least once in her life. A better average than I had assumed of that one.”

랜드 refused to rise to that comment, and Cadsuane let slip a smile. She was pleased at how he controlled himself now. That was why she tested him. Would the tests never end?

*No,* he thought. *Not until the final one. The one that matters most.*

Cadsuane stopped in the path, causing him to stop as well. “Do you have a gift for me as well?”

“I am giving them to those I care about.”

That actually made her smile more deeply. “Our interactions have not always been smooth, 랜드 al’Thor.”

“That would be one way to say it.”

“However,” she continued, eyeing him, “I will have you know that I am pleased. You have turned out well.”

“So I have your permission to save the world?”

“Yes!” She looked upward, where the dark clouds boiled. They began to split at his presence, as he did not try to mask it or keep them back.

“Yes,” Cadsuane repeated, “you have my permission. So long as you do it soon. That darkness grows.”

As if in concert with her words, the ground rumbled. It did that more and more lately. The camp shook, and men stumbled, wary.

“There will be 버림받은 자들,” 랜드 said. “Once I enter. Someone will need to face them. I intend to ask 아비엔다 to lead the resistance against them. She could use your aid.”

Cadsuane nodded. “I will do my part.”

“Bring Alivia,” 랜드 said. “She is strong, but I worry about putting her with others. She does not understand limits in the way that she should.” Cadsuane nodded again, and from the look in her eyes, he wondered if she’d already planned to do just that. “And the 검은 탑?”

랜드 set his jaw. The 검은 탑 was a trap. He *knew* it was a trap. 타임 wanted to lure 랜드 into a place where he couldn’t escape through a gateway.

“I sent 페린 to help.”

“And your determination to go yourself?”

*I have to help them. Somehow. I let 타임 gather them. I can’t just leave them to him…*

“You still aren’t certain,” Cadsuane said, dissatisfied. “You’d risk yourself, you’d risk us all, stepping into a trap.”

“I . . ”

“They’re free.” Cadsuane turned to walk away. “타임 and his men have been cast out of the 검은 탑.”

“What?” 랜드 demanded, taking her by the arm.

“Your men there freed themselves,” Cadsuane said. “Though, from what I’ve been told, they took a beating doing it. Few know it. Queen 엘레인 might not be able to use them in battle for some time. I don’t know the details.”

“They freed themselves?” 랜드 said.

“Yes.”

*They did it. Or 페린 did.*

랜드 exulted, but a wave of guilt slammed against him. How many had been lost? Could he have saved them, if he’d gone? He’d known for days now of their predicament, and yet he’d left them, obeying 모이라인’s insistent counsel that this was a trap he could not afford to spring.

And now they’d escaped it.

“I wish that I’d been able to draw an answer out of you,” Cadsuane said, “about what you intended to do there.” She sighed, then shook her head. “You have cracks in you, 랜드 al’Thor, but you’ll have to do.”

She left him.

“Deepe was a good man,” Antail said. “He survived the fall of 마라도나. He was on the wall when it blew, but he lived and kept fighting. The Dreadlords came for him eventually, sending an explosion to finish the job. Deepe spent the last moments throwing weaves at them. He died well.”

The 말키에르i soldiers raised cups toward Antail, saluting the fallen. 란 raised his own cup, though he stood just outside the ring of men around the fire. He wished Deepe had followed orders. He shook his head, downing his wine. Though it was night, 란’s men were on rotation to be awake in case of an attack.

란 turned his cup between two fingers, thinking of Deepe again. He found he couldn’t drum up anger at the man. Deepe had wanted to kill one of the Shadow’s most dangerous channelers. 란 couldn’t say he would turn down a similar opportunity, if it were given him.

The men continued their toasts to the fallen. It had become a tradition every evening, and had spread among all of the Borderlander camps. 란 found it encouraging that the men here were starting to treat Antail and Narishma as fellows. The Asha’man were aloof, but Deepe’s death had forged a link between the Asha’man and the ordinary soldiers. Now they’d all paid the butcher’s bill. The men had seen Antail grieving, and had invited him to make a toast.

란 stepped away from the fire and walked through the camp, stopping by the horselines to check on Mandarb. The stallion was holding up well, though he bore a large wound on his left flank where his coat would never grow back; it seemed to be healing well. The grooms still spoke in hushed tones about how the wounded horse had appeared out of the night following the fight where Deepe had died. Many riders had been killed or unhorsed in the fighting that day. Very few horses had escaped the 트롤록s and made their way back to camp.

란 patted Mandarb’s neck. “We’ll rest soon, my friend,” he said softly. “I promise.”

Mandarb snorted in the darkness, and nearby, several of the other horses nickered.

“We’ll make a home,” 란 said. “그림자 defeated, 니나브 and I will reclaim 말키에르. We’ll make the fields bloom again, cleanse the lakes. Green pastures. No more 트롤록s to fight. Children to ride on your back, old friend. You can spend your days in peace, eating apples and having your pick of mares.”

It had been a very long time since 란 had thought of the future with anything resembling hope. Strange to find it now, in this place, in this war. He was a hard man. At times, he felt he had more in common with the rocks and the sand than he did with the men who laughed together beside the fire.

That was what he’d made of himself. It was the person he’d needed to be, a person who could someday journey toward 말키에르 and uphold the honor of his family. 랜드 al’Thor had begun to crack that shell, and then 니나브’s love had ripped it apart completely.

*I wonder if 랜드 ever knew,* 란 thought, taking out the currycomb and working on Mandarb’s coat. 란 knew what it was like to be chosen, from childhood, to die. He knew what it was like to be pointed toward the 황무지 and told he would sacrifice his life there. Light, but he did. 랜드 al’Thor would probably never know how similar the two of them were.

란 brushed Mandarb for a time, though he was bone tired. Perhaps he should have slept. 니나브 would have told him to sleep. He played out the conversation in his head, allowing himself a smile. She’d have won, explaining that a general needed sleep and that there were plenty of grooms to care for the horses.

But 니나브 wasn’t there. He kept brushing.

Someone approached the horselines. 란 heard the footsteps long before the person arrived, of course. Lord Baldhere retrieved a brush from the groom station, nodding to one of the guards there, and walked toward his own horse. Only then did he notice 란.

“Lord Mandragoran?” he said.

“Lord Baldhere,” 란 said, nodding toward the 캔도리. Queen Ethenielle’s Swordbearer was slender, with streaks of white in his otherwise black hair. Though Baldhere was not one of the great captains, he was a fine commander, and had served 캔도르 well since his king’s death. Many had assumed that the Queen would marry Baldhere. That, of course, was foolish; Ethenielle looked at him as she would a brother. Besides, anyone who paid attention would know that Baldhere clearly preferred men to women.

“I am sorry to disturb you, Dai Shan,” Baldhere said. “I had not realized that anyone else would be here.” He moved to withdraw.

“I was nearly done,” 란 said. “Do not let me stop you.”

“The grooms do well enough,” Baldhere said. “I wasn’t here to check on their work. I have found, at times, that doing something simple and familiar helps me think.”

“You’re not the only one to have noticed that,” 란 said, continuing to brush Mandarb.

Baldhere chuckled, then fell silent for a moment. Finally, he spoke. “Dai Shan,” he said, “are you worried about Lord Agelmar?”

“In what regard?”

“I worry that he’s pushing himself too hard,” Baldhere said. “Some of the choices he is making… they confuse me. It’s not that his battle decisions are *bad.* They simply strike me as too aggressive.”

“It is war. I don’t know that one can be too aggressive in defeating one’s enemy.”

Baldhere fell quiet for a time. “Of course. But did you notice the loss of Lord Yokata’s two cavalry squadrons?”

“That was unfortunate, but mistakes do happen.”

“This isn’t one that Lord Agelmar should have made. He’s been in situations like this before, Dai Shan. He should have seen.”

It had happened during a recent raid against the 트롤록s. The Asha’man had been setting fire to Fal Eisen and the surrounding countryside. At Agelmar’s orders, Yokata had taken his cavalry in a swing around a large hill to attack the right flank of the 트롤록 army advancing on the Asha’man. Using a classic pincer movement, Agelmar was to send in more cavalry against the enemy’s left flank, and the Asha’man would turn to meet the 트롤록s head-on.

But the Shadow’s leaders had seen through the maneuver. Before Agelmar and the Asha’man could act, a large contingent of 트롤록s had come over the hill to hit Yokata’s own right flank, while the remainder hit Yokata head-on, enveloping his cavalry.

The cavalry had been killed to the last man. Immediately after, the 트롤록s went after the Asha’man, who had barely been able to save themselves.

“He is tired, Dai Shan,” Baldhere said. “I *know* Agelmar. He would never have made a mistake like that if he were awake and alert.”

“Baldhere, anyone could have made a mistake like that.”

“Lord Agelmar is one of the great captains. He should see the battle differently than ordinary men do.”

“Are you certain you aren’t expecting too much of him?” 란 asked. “Agelmar is just a man. We all are, at the end of the day.”

“I… Perhaps you are right,” Baldhere said, hand on his sword, as if worried. He wasn’t carrying the Queen’s weapon, of course—he did that only when she was acting in her station. “I guess it comes down to an instinct, 란. An itch. Agelmar seems tired a lot, and I worry it’s affecting his ability to plan. Please, just watch him.”

“I’ll watch,” 란 said.

“Thank you,” Baldhere said. He seemed less troubled now than when he’d approached.

란 gave Mandarb a final pat, left Baldhere to tend his horse and walked through camp to the command tent. He went in; the tent was lit and well guarded, though the soldiers on guard weren’t allowed clear views of the battle maps.

란 moved around the hung cloths that obscured the entry and nodded to the two 시엔나르an commanders, subordinates to Agelmar, who attended this inner sanctum. One was studying the maps spread out on the floor. Agelmar himself wasn’t there. A leader needed to sleep sometime.

란 squatted, looking at the map. After tomorrow’s retreat, it appeared that they would reach a place called Blood Springs, named for the way the rocks beneath the water made the river seem to run red. At Blood Springs, they would have a slight advantage of height because of the adjacent hills, and Agelmar wanted to stage an offensive against the 트롤록s with bowmen and cavalry lines working together. And, of course, there would be more burning of the land.

란 knelt on one knee, looking over Agelmar’s notes about which army would fight where and how he’d divide the attacks. It was ambitious, but nothing looked particularly troublesome to 란.

As he was studying, the tent flaps rustled, and Agelmar himself entered, speaking softly with Lady Ells of 살다에아. He stopped when he saw 란, excusing himself quietly from his conversation. He approached 란.

Agelmar did not slump with exhaustion, but 란 had learned to read beyond a man’s posture for signs of tiredness. Redness to the eyes. Breath that smelled faintly of flatwort, an herb chewed to keep the mind alert when one had been up too long. Agelmar was tired—but so was everyone else in camp.

“Do you approve of what you see, Dai Shan?” Agelmar asked, kneeling.

“It is very aggressive for a retreat.”

“Can we afford any other action?” Agelmar asked. “We leave a swath of burned land behind us, destroying 시엔나르 almost as surely as if the Shadow had taken her. I will bring 트롤록 blood to quench those ashes.”

란 nodded.

“Baldhere came to you?” Agelmar asked.

란 looked up sharply.

Agelmar smiled wanly. “I assume it was regarding the loss of Yokata and his men?”

“Yes”

“It was a mistake, to be certain,” Agelmar said. “I wondered if anyone would confront me on it; Baldhere is one to believe I should never have made such an error.”

“He thinks you’re pushing yourself too hard.”

“He is clever in tactics,” Agelmar said, “but he does not know so much as he thinks. His head is full of the stories of great captains. I am not without flaw, Dai Shan. This will not be my only error. I will see them, as I saw this one, and learn from them.”

“Still, perhaps we should see that you get more sleep.”

“I am perfectly hale, Lord Mandragoran. I know my limits; I have spent my entire life learning them. This battle will push me to my utmost, and I must let it.”

“But—”

“Relieve me or let me be,” Agelmar said, cutting in. “I will listen to advice—I am not a fool—but I will not be second-guessed.”

“Very well,” 란 said, rising. “I trust your wisdom.”

Agelmar nodded, lowering his eyes to his maps. He was still working on his plans when 란 finally left to turn in.

*The Choice of a Patch*

엘레인 found 바쉐어 pacing on the east bank of the river.

Riverbanks were among the few places that still felt alive to her. So much was lifeless these days, trees that did not put forth leaves, grass that did not grow, animals that huddled in their dens and refused to move.

The rivers kept flowing. There was a sense of life to that, though the plants were dreary.

The Alguenya was one of those deceptively mighty rivers that looked placid from a distance, but could pull a woman under its surface until she drowned. She remembered Bryne making a lesson of that to 가윈 once during a hunting trip they’d taken along it. He’d been speaking to her, too. Maybe to her primarily, though he’d always been careful not to overstep himself with the Daughter-Heir.

*Be careful of currents,* he’d said. *River currents are one of the most dangerous things under the Light, but only because men underestimate them. The surface looks still because nothing is fighting it. Nothing wants to. The fish go along with it and men stay out of it, all except the fools who think to prove themselves.*

엘레인 stepped down the rocky bank, toward 바쉐어. Her guards stayed behind—비르기테 wasn’t with them just now. She was seeing to the archer companies miles downriver, where they were busy pounding the 트롤록s building rafts to get them across the river. 비르기테’s archers and 탈마네스’ dragons were doing an outstanding job of reducing the 트롤록 numbers there, but it was still only a matter of time before their vast army would pour across the Alguenya.

엘레인 had pulled her forces out of 안도르 a week before, and she and 바쉐어 had been pleased with their progress. Until they had discovered the trap.

“Amazing, isn't it?” she asked, stepping up beside 바쉐어, who stood at the river’s bank.

바쉐어 glanced at her, then nodded. “We don’t have anything like it, back home.”

“What of the Arinelle?”

“It doesn't grow this big until it’s outside of 살다에아,” he said absently. “This is almost like an ocean, settled right here, dividing bank from bank. It makes me smile, thinking of how the 아일 must have regarded it after first crossing the Spine.”

The two of them were silent for a time.

“How bad is it?” 엘레인 finally asked.

“Bad,” 바쉐어 said. “I should have realized, burn me. I should have seen.”

“You can’t plan for everything, 바쉐어.”

“Pardon,” he said, “but that is *exactly* what I’m supposed to be doing.” Their march eastward from Braem Wood had gone according to plan. Burning the bridges across the Erinin and the Alguenya, they had taken out large numbers of 트롤록s trying to cross after them. 엘레인 was now on the road that went upriver to the city of 케렌. 바쉐어 had planned to set up their final confrontation with the 트롤록s in hills along the road that lay twenty leagues south of 케렌.

그림자 had out-thought them. Scouts had spotted a second army of 트롤록s just to the north of their current position, marching east, heading toward the city of 케렌 itself. 엘레인 had stripped that city of defenders to fill out her army. Now it was filled only with refugees—and was as crowded as Caemlyn had been.

“How did they do it?” she asked. “Those 트롤록s couldn’t have come down from Tarwin’s Gap.”

“There hasn't been enough time for that,” 바쉐어 agreed.

“Another Waygate?” she asked.

“Perhaps,” 바쉐어 said. “Perhaps not.”

“How, then?” she asked. “Where did that army come from?” That army of 트롤록s was almost close enough to knock on the city gates. Light!

“I made the mistake of thinking like a human,” 바쉐어 said. “I accounted for 트롤록 marching speed, but not for how the 미르드랄 might push them. A foolish mistake. The army in the woods must have split in two, with half taking a northeastern route through the woods toward 케렌. It’s the only thing I can think of.”
“We’ve been moving as quickly as we can,” 엘레인 said. “How could they have overtaken us?” Her army had gateways. She couldn’t move everyone through them, as she didn’t have enough channelers to hold gateways for long periods. However, she *could* move the supply carts, the wounded, and the camp followers through. That let them march at the speed of trained soldiers.

“We’ve moved as quickly as we could *safely*,” 바쉐어 said. “A human commander would never have pushed his forces into such a terrible march. The terrain they went through had to have been awful—the rivers they had to cross, the forests, the wetlands, Light! They must have lost thousands of 트롤록s to fatigue during such a march. The 페이드s risked it, and now they have us in a pincer. The city could be destroyed as well.”

엘레인 fell silent. “I *won’t* let that happen,” she finally said. “Not again. Not if we can prevent it.”

“Do we have a choice?”

“Yes,” 엘레인 said. “바쉐어, you’re one of the greatest military minds the land has known. You have resources that no man has ever had before. The dragons, the Kinswomen, 오지어 willing to fight in battle… You can make this work. I know you can.”

“You show surprising faith in me for someone you have known a very short time.”

“랜드 trusts you,” 엘레인 said. “Even during the dark times, 바쉐어— when he would look at every second person around him with darkness in his eyes—he trusted you.”

바쉐어 seemed troubled. “There is a way.”

“What is it?”

“We march and hit the 트롤록s near 케렌 as quickly as we can. They’re tired; they have to be. If we could beat them quickly, before the horde to the south reaches us, we may have a chance. It will be difficult. The northern force probably wants to seize the city, then use it against us as the southern 트롤록s arrive.”

“Could we open gateways into the city and hold it?”

“I doubt it,” 바쉐어 said. “Not with channelers as tired as these. Beyond that, we need to *destroy* the northern 트롤록s, not just hold against them. If we give them time to rest, they will recover from their march, be joined by the 트롤록s from the south, then use Dreadlords to rip open 케렌 like an overripe apple. No, 엘레인. We have to attack and *crush* that northern army while it is weak; only then could we possibly hold against the southern one. If we fail, the two will smash us between them.”

“It is the risk we must take,” 엘레인 said. “Make your plans, 바쉐어. We’ll make them work.”

에그웨인 stepped into *Tel’aran’rhiod.*

The World of Dreams had always been dangerous, unpredictable. Lately, it was even more so. The grand city of 티어 reflected strangely in the dream, the buildings weathered as if by a hundred years of storms. The city walls were now little more than ten feet high, their tops rounded and smooth, blown by the wind. Buildings inside had worn away, leaving foundations and lumps of weathered stone.

Chilled by the sight, 에그웨인 turned toward the Stone. It, at least, stood as it had. Tall, strong, unchanged by the weathering of the winds. That comforted her.

She sent herself into its heart. The 현명한 이들 waited for her. That, too, was comforting. Even in this time of change and tempest, they were solid like the Stone itself. Amys, Bair and Melaine waited for her. She overheard part of their conversation before they noticed her.

“I saw it just as she did,” Bair was saying. “Though it was my own descendants who lent me their eyes. I think we will all see it now, if we return the third time. It should be required.”

“Three visits?” Melaine said. “That brings change indeed. We still do not know if the second visit will show this, or the previous vision.”

Conscious of her eavesdropping, 에그웨인 cleared her throat. They turned toward her, immediately falling silent.

“I did not mean to intrude,” 에그웨인 said, walking among the columns and joining them.

“It is nothing,” Bair said. “We should have guarded our tongues. We were the ones to invite you here to meet us, after all.”

“It is good to see you, 에그웨인 al’Vere,” Melaine said, smiling with affection. The woman looked so far along in her pregnancy, she must be close to delivering. “From reports, your army gains much *ji.*”

“We do well,” 에그웨인 said, settling herself on the floor with them. “You shall have your own chance, Melaine.”

“The *Car’a’carn* delays,” Amys said, frowning. “The spears grow impatient. We should be moving against 시야 가리는 자.”

“He likes to prepare and plan,” 에그웨인 said. She hesitated. “I cannot remain with you long. I have a meeting with him later today.”

“About what?” Bair asked, leaning forward, curious.

“I don’t know,” 에그웨인 said. “I found a letter from him on the floor of my tent. He said he wanted to see me, but not as Dragon and Amyrlin. As old friends.”

“Tell him that he must not dally,” Bair said. “But here, there is something we need to speak of with you.”

“What is it?” 에그웨인 asked, curious.

“Have you seen anything like this?” Melaine said, concentrating. On the floor between them, the rock split with cracks. She was imposing her will upon the World of Dreams, creating something specific for 에그웨인 to see.

At first, she was confused. Cracks in the rock? Of course she had seen cracks in rock before. And with the earthquakes striking the land so often recently, they were probably becoming even more common.

There *was* something distinctive about these. 에그웨인 leaned forward, and found that the cracks seemed to empty into *nothing.* A deep blackness. Unnaturally so.

“What is it?” 에그웨인 asked.

“Our people report seeing these,” Amys said softly. “Those fighting in 안도르 and those in the Blasted 란ds with 랜드 al’Thor. They appear like fractures in the pattern itself. They remain dark like that for a few moments, then fade, leaving behind ordinary cracks.”

“It is a very dangerous sign,” Bair said. “We sent one of ours to ask at the 국경지대, where 란 Mandragoran fights. It appears that the cracks are most common there.”

“They appear more frequently when the Dreadlords fight,” Amys said. “When they use the weave known as balefire.”

에그웨인 stared at that darkness, shivering. “마화 weakens the Pattern. During the War of Power, even the 버림받은 자들 grew to fear using it, lest they unravel the world itself.”

“We must spread the word to all of our allies,” Amys said. “We *must* not use this weave.”

“It is forbidden of 에스 세다이 already,” 에그웨인 said. “But I will make it known that nobody is to consider breaking that rule.”

“That is wise,” Melaine said. “For a people with so many rules for themselves, I have found that the 에스 세다이 are very proficient at ignoring guidelines if their situation allows it.”

“We trust our women,” 에그웨인 said. “The Oaths hold them; otherwise, their own wisdom must guide them. If 모이라인 had not been willing to bend this rule, 페린 would be dead—as would 맷, had 랜드 ignored the rule. But I *will* speak to the women.”

마화 bothered her. Not that it existed or did what it did. It was uniquely dangerous. And yet, what was it 페린 had said to her in the dream? *It’s only another weave*…

It seemed unfair that the Shadow should have access to such a weapon as this, one that unraveled the Pattern as it was used. How would they fight it, how could they counter it?

“This is not the only reason we sent to you, 에그웨인 al’Vere,” Melaine said. “You have seen the changes to the World of Dreams?”

에그웨인 nodded. “The storm grows worse here.”

“We will not be visiting here often in the future,” Amys said. “We have made the decision. And, despite our complaints about him, the *Car’a’carn* does prepare his armies to move. It will not be long before we march with him to the Shadow’s own hold.”

에그웨인 nodded slowly. “So this is it.”

“I am proud of you, girl,” Amys said. Amys, tough-as-rocks Amys, looked teary-eyed. They rose, and 에그웨인 embraced them one at a time.

“Light shelter you, Amys, Melaine, Bair,” 에그웨인 said. “Give my love to the others.”

“It will be done, 에그웨인 al’Vere,” Bair said. “May you find water and shade, now and always.”

One by one, they faded from 티어. 에그웨인 took a deep breath, looking upward. The building groaned, like a ship in a tempest. The rock itself seemed to shift around her.

She had loved this place—not the Stone, but *Tel’ararirhiod.* It had taught her so much. But she knew, as she prepared to leave, that it was like a river in dangerous flood. Familiar and loved it might be, but she could not risk herself here. Not while the 백색 탑 needed her.

“And farewell to you, old friend,” she said to the air. “Until I dream again.”

She let herself wake.

가윈 waited beside the bed, as usual. They were back in the Tower, 에그웨인 fully dressed, in the chamber near her study. It was not yet evening, but the request from the Wise One was not something she had wished to ignore.

“He's here,” 가윈 said quietly, glancing at the door to her study.

“Then let us meet him,” 에그웨인 said. She prepared herself, rising, smoothing her skirt. She nodded to 가윈, and they stepped out and went to meet the 용의 환생.

랜드 smiled when he saw her. He waited inside with two Maidens she did not know.

“What is this about?” 에그웨인 asked tiredly. “Convincing me to break the seals?”

“You’ve grown cynical,” 랜드 noted.

“The last two times we met,” 에그웨인 said, “you pointedly tried to infuriate me. Am I not to expect it again?”

“I am not trying to infuriate you,” 랜드 said. “Look, here.” He pulled something from his pocket. A hair ribbon. He held it out to her. “You always looked forward so to being able to braid your hair.”

“So now you imply I’m a child?” 에그웨인 asked, exasperated. 가윈 rested a hand on her shoulder, comforting.

“What? No!” 랜드 sighed. “Light, 에그웨인. I want to make amends. You’re like a sister to me; I never had siblings. Or, at least, the one I have doesn’t know me. I only have you. Please. I’m not trying to rile you.”

For a moment, he seemed just as he had long ago. An innocent boy, earnest. 에그웨인 let her frustration melt away. “랜드, I’m busy. *We* are busy. There isn’t time for things like this. Your armies are impatient.”

“Their time will soon come,” 랜드 said, growing harder. “Before this is through, they will wonder why they were so eager, and will look with longing at these restful days waiting.” He still held the ribbon in his hand, forming a fist. “I just ... I didn’t want to go to my fight with our last meeting having been an argument, even if it was an important one.”

“Oh, 랜드,” 에그웨인 said. She stepped forward, taking the ribbon. She embraced him. Light, but he’d been difficult to deal with lately—but she’d thought the same thing about her parents on occasion. “I support you. It doesn’t mean I’m going to do as you say with the seals, but I *do* support you.” 에그웨인 released 랜드. She would *not* be teary-eyed. Even if it did seem like a last parting for them.

“Wait,” 가윈 said. “Sibling? You have a sibling?”

“I am the son of Tigraine,” 랜드 said, shrugging, “born after she went to the 황무지 and became a Maiden.”

가윈 looked stunned, though 에그웨인 had figured this out ages ago. “You are 갈라드’s *brother*?” 가윈 asked.

“Half-brother,” 랜드 said. “Not that it would probably mean much to a Whitecloak. We had the same mother. His father, like yours, was Taringail, but mine was an 아일.”

“I think 갈라드 would surprise you,” 가윈 said softly. “But 엘레인…”

“Not to tell you your own family history, but 엘레인 is not related to me.” 랜드 turned to 에그웨인. “May I see them? The seals. Before I go to 세이올 굴, I would look upon them one last time. I promise not to do anything with them.”

Reluctantly, she fished them from the pouch at her waist where she often kept them. 가윈, still looking stunned, walked to the window and pushed it open, letting light into the room. The 백색 탑 felt still… silent. Its armies were gone, its masters at war.

She unwrapped the first seal and handed it to 랜드. She would not give him all of them at once. Just in case. She did trust his word; it was 랜드 after all, but… just in case.

랜드 held up the seal, staring at it, as if seeking wisdom in that sinuous line. “I crafted these,” he whispered. “I made them to never break. But I knew, as I did it, that they would eventually fail. Everything eventually fails when he touches it . . ”

에그웨인 hefted another of the seals, holding it gingerly. It would not do to break the thing by accident. She kept them wrapped and the pouch stuffed with cloth; she worried about breaking them while carrying them, but 모이라인 had indicated that 에그웨인 would break them.

She felt that was foolish, but the words she had read, the things 모이라인 had said… Well, if the moment did come to break them, 에그웨인 would need to have them at hand. And so she carried them—carried with her the potential death of the world itself.

랜드 suddenly went as white as a sheet. “에그웨인,” he said. “This does not fool me.”

“What doesn’t?”

He looked at her. “This is a fake. Please, it is all right. Tell me the truth. You made a copy and gave it to me.”

“I did nothing of the sort,” she said.

“Oh… Oh, *Light”* 랜드 raised the seal again. “Its a fake.”

“What!” 에그웨인 snatched it from his hand, feeling it. She sensed nothing wrong. “How can you be sure?”

“I made them,” 랜드 said. “I know my handiwork. That is *not* one of the seals. It is… Light, someone took them.”

“I’ve had these with me each moment since you gave them to me!” 에그웨인 said.

“Then it happened before,” 랜드 whispered. “I didn’t look them over carefully after I fetched them. He knew, somehow, where I’d put them.” Taking the other one from her, he shook his head. “It’s not real either.” He took the third. “Nor this one.”

He looked at her. “He has them, 에그웨인. He’s stolen them back, somehow. 어둠의 존재 holds the keys to his own prison.”

For much of 맷’s life, he had wished that people would not look at him so much. They gave him frowns at the trouble he had ostensibly caused— trouble that really was not his fault—and glances of disapproval when he walked about completely innocent, trying his best to be pleasant. Every boy filched a pie now and then. No harm in it. It was practically expected.

Normal life had been harder for 맷 than for other boys. For no good reason, everyone watched him extra carefully. 페린 could have stolen pies all day, and people would have just smiled at him and maybe mussed his hair. 맷 they came at with the broom.

When he entered a place to dice, he drew looks. People watched him as they would watch a cheater—though he never was—or with envy in their eyes. Yes, he had always figured that *not* being watched would be a grand situation. A cause for real celebration.

Now he had it, and it made him sick.

“You can look at me,” 맷 protested. “Really. Burn you, it’s all right!”

“My eyes would be lowered,” the serving woman said as she piled fabric on the low table against the wall.

“Your eyes are *already* lowered! They’re staring at the bloody floor, aren’t they? I want you to raise them.”

The 쇼엔찬 continued her work. She was of fair skin with freckles under her eyes, not too bad to look at, though he was more in favor of darker shades these days. He still would not have minded if this girl showed him a smile. How could he talk to a woman if he could not try to make her smile?

A few other servants entered, eyes downcast, carrying other folds of fabric. 맷 stood in what were apparently “his” chambers in the palace. They were more numerous than he would ever need. Perhaps 탈마네스 and some of the Band could move in with him and keep the place from feeling so empty.

맷 sauntered over to the window. Below, in the Mol Hara, an army organized. It was going to take longer than he wanted. Galgan—맷 had only met the man briefly, and he did not trust the fellow, no matter what 투온 said about his assassins not being intended to succeed—was gathering the 쇼엔찬 forces from the borders, but too slowly. He worried about losing Almoth Plain with the withdrawal.

Well, he had better listen to reason. 맷 had little reason to like the man already, but if he delayed in this…

“Honored One?” the serving girl asked.

맷 turned, raising an eyebrow. Several *da’covale* had entered with the last of the fabric, and 맷 found himself blushing. They hardly wore any clothing at all, and what they did wear was transparent. He could look, though, could he not? They would not wear clothing like that if a man was not supposed to look. What would 투온 think?

*She doesn’t own me,* 맷 thought, determined. *I will* not *be husbandly.*

The freckled servant—she was *so’jhin*, half of her head shaved—gestured toward a person who had entered behind the *da’covale*, a middle-aged woman with her dark hair in a bun, none of her head shaved. She was squat, shaped kind of like a bell, with a grandmotherly air.

The newcomer inspected him. Finally someone who would look at him! If only her face did not have the expression of one studying horses at the market.

“Black for his new station,” the woman said, clapping her hands once. “Green for his heritage. A deep forest, in moderation. Someone bring me a variety of eyepatches, and someone else burn that hat.”

“What?” 맷 exclaimed. Servants swarmed around him, picking at his clothing. “Wait, now. What is this?”

“Your new regalia, Honored One,” the woman said. “I am Nata, and I will be your personal tailor.”

“You aren’t burning my hat,” 맷 said. “Try, and we’ll bloody well see if you can fly from four stories up. Do you understand me?”

The woman hesitated. “Yes, Honored One. Do not burn his clothing. Keep it safe, should it be needed.” She seemed doubtful it ever would be.

맷 opened his mouth to complain further, and then one of the *da’covale* opened a box. Jewelry shone inside it. Rubies, emeralds, firedrops. 맷’s breath caught in his throat. There was a *fortune* in there!

He was so stunned that he almost did not notice that the servants were undressing him. They pulled at his shirt, and 맷 let them. Although he held on to his scarf, he was not bashful. That blush on his cheeks had nothing to do with his trousers being taken off. He was just surprised at the jewelry.

Then one of the young *da’covale* reached for 맷’s smallclothes.

“You’d be real funny without any fingers,” 맷 growled.

The *da’covale* looked up—his eyes widening, face paling. He immediately looked down again, bowing, backing away. 맷 was not bashful, but the smallclothes were far enough.

Nata clicked her tongue. Her servants began draping 맷 in fine cloth, black and deep green—so dark it was nearly black itself. “We shall tailor you outfits for military expression, court attendance, private functions, and civic appearances. It—”

“No,” 맷 said. “Military only.”

“But—”

“We're at the bloody Last Battle, woman,” 맷 said. “If we survive this, you can make me a bloody feastday cap. Until then, we're at war, and I don’t need anything else.”

She nodded.

맷 reluctantly stood with arms out to the sides, letting them drape him in the fabric, taking measurements. If he had to put up with this business of being called “Honored One” and “Highness,” then he could at least make certain he was dressed in a reasonable way.

In truth, he *had* been growing tired of the same old clothing. There did not seem to be much lace used by the 쇼엔찬 tailor, which was a shame, but 맷 did not want to correct her in doing her job. He could not complain about every little thing. Nobody liked a complainer, least of all 맷.

As they dealt with the measurements, a servant approached with a small, velvet-lined case displaying a variety of eyepatches. He hesitated, considering; some were marked with gemstones, others painted with designs.

“That one,” he said, pointing at the least ornamented patch. Simple black with only two small rubies, cut thin and long, set at the right and left edges of the patch opposite one another. They fitted it on him as the other servants finished measuring.

That done, the tailor had her servants dress him in a costume she had brought. Apparently, he was not going to be allowed back to his old clothing while he waited for his new outfits to be tailored.

The clothing started off simple enough. A silk robe of fine weave. 맷 would have preferred trousers, but the robe was comfortable. However, they overlaid it with a larger, stiffer robe. It was also silk, of dark green, every inch of it embroidered with scrollwork patterns. The sleeves were large enough to trot a horse through, and they felt heavy and bulky.

“I thought I said to give me warrior’s clothing!” he said.

“This is a ceremonial warrior’s uniform for a member of the Imperial family, Highness,” Nata said. “Many will see you as an outsider, and though nobody would question your loyalty, it would be well for our soldiers to see you as Prince of the Ravens first and an outlander second. Would you agree?”

“I suppose,” 맷 said.

The servants continued, buckling on an ornate girdle and placing forearm bands of the same design on his arms inside the large sleeves. That was all right, 맷 supposed, as the girdle pulled in the waist of the clothing and kept it from feeling quite so bulky.

Unfortunately, the next piece of clothing was the most ridiculous of all. The stiff, pale piece of cloth fitted onto his shoulders. It draped down his front and back like a tabard, the sides open, but they flared out to the sides a good foot each, making him seem inhumanly wide. They were like shoulder plates from heavy armor, only made of cloth.

“Here now,” 맷 said. “This isn’t a kind of trick you play on a fellow, just because he’s new, is it?”

“Trick, Honored One?” Nata asked.

“You can’t really . . ” 맷 trailed off as someone passed outside his door. Another commander. The man was wearing a costume not unlike 맷’s, though not as ornate, and with shoulders not quite as wide. Not Imperial family armor, but ceremonial armor for one of the Blood. Still, it was almost as lavish.

The man stopped and bowed to 맷, then continued on his way.

“Burn me,” 맷 said.

Nata clapped and the servants began draping 맷 in gemstones. They chose mostly rubies, which made 맷 uncomfortable. That had to be a coincidence, did it not? He did not know what he thought of being covered in all of these gemstones. Perhaps he could sell them. Actually, if he could put these on a gambling table, he could probably end up owning all of Ebou Dar…

*투온 already owns it,* he realized. *And I married her.* It sank in that he was rich. *Really* rich.

He sat there, letting them lacquer his fingernails, as he considered what this all meant. Oh, he had not needed to worry about money for some time, as he could always gamble for more. This was different. If he already had everything, what point was there to gambling? This did not sound like much fun. People were not supposed to give you things like this. You were supposed to find a way to come to them yourself, by wits, luck or skill.

“Burn me,” 맷 said, lowering his arms to his side as the lacquering finished. “I’m a *bloody* nobleman.” He sighed, plucking his hat from the hands of a startled servant—who was walking past with his old clothing— and set it on his head.

“Honored One,” Nata said. “Please forgive my forwardness, but it is my place to advise on fashion, if you please. That hat looks… particularly out of place with that uniform.”

“Who cares?” 맷 said, marching out of the room. He almost had to go out the door sideways! “If I’m going to look ridiculous, I might as well do it with style. Someone point me toward where our flaming generals are meeting. I need to figure out how many troops we have.”
