**CHAPTER 20**

![](images/00273.jpg)

*Into Thakan'dar*

Later in the day after her meeting with 랜드, 에그웨인 thrust Vora’s *sa’angreal* out in front of her and wove Fire. Threads came together, tiny glowing ribbons forming a complex weave in the air before her. She could almost feel their heat shining upon her, turning her skin a violent orange.

She finished the weave, and a fiery ball as large as a boulder arced in the air, crackling and roaring. It fell upon the distant hilltop like a meteor. The blast flung bow-wielding 트롤록s aside, scattering their carcasses.

Romanda opened a gateway beside 에그웨인. Romanda was among the Yellows who had insisted on staying at the battlefront to provide emergency 치유. She and her small crew had been invaluable in saving lives.

Today, however, there would be no opportunity for 치유. The 트롤록s had pulled back into the hills, as Bryne had indicated they would. After a day and a half of rest, many of the 에스 세다이 were recovered. Not to full strength—not after over a week of grueling combat—but enough.

가윈 jumped through the gateway right after it opened, his sword out. 에그웨인 followed, along with Romanda, Lelaine, 리안, Silviana, Raemassa and a handful of 감시자s and soldiers. They stepped out onto the very hilltop 에그웨인 had just cleared. The charred earth was still warm under her feet, blackened; the scent of burned flesh hung in the air.

This hill was in the very middle of the 트롤록 army. All around, 그림자태생 scrambled for safety this way and that. Romanda held the gateway and Silviana began weaving Air to create a dome of wind against arrows. The rest of them began to send weaves outward.

The 트롤록s reacted slowly—they’d been waiting here, in these hills, ready to surge down into the valleys as 에그웨인’s army entered. Normally, this would have been a disaster. The 트롤록s could rain projectiles down on 에그웨인’s troops, and her cavalry would have been at a disadvantage trying to get up those hills. The hilltops would have given the 트롤록s and 페이드s a better perspective to spot weak points in 에그웨인’s forces, and attack accordingly.

에그웨인 and her commanders had been disinclined to give the enemy that advantage. The beasts scattered as the battle reversed on them, 에스 세다이 seizing the hilltops. Some of the beasts tried to charge up and retake them, but others scrambled away for their lives. 에그웨인’s heavy cavalry came next, thundering through the valleys. What had once been a very efficient position for the 트롤록s became a killing field; with the 트롤록 archers removed by 에스 세다이, the heavy cavalry could kill practically unmolested.

That opened the way for the foot, who marched in formation to sweep the 트롤록s back, smashing them against hillsides so that the 에스 세다이 could kill them in groups. Unfortunately, the 트롤록s had grown more accustomed to facing the 하나의 힘. Either that, or the 미르드랄 had grown more thorough at encouraging them.

Soon, more coordinated groups of 트롤록s charged the hilltops, while others managed to form resistance to the foot assault. *Bryne is right,* 에그웨인 thought, leveling a contingent of 트롤록s that had almost clawed their way to her. *The 페이드s are linked to the 트롤록s again.* The 그림자태생 had been hesitant to use that tactic recently, as killing the 페이드 would drop all linked 트롤록s. However, she suspected that it was the only way they could make the 트롤록s climb toward almost-certain death on these hills.

If she could find the 미르드랄 linked to the 트롤록s nearby, she could stop them all with one well-placed weave of Fire. Unfortunately, the 페이드s were crafty, and had begun hiding among the 트롤록s.

“They’re closing in,” Lelaine said, panting.

“Fall back,” 에그웨인 said.

They ducked through Romanda’s gateway, followed by their 감시자s. Romanda came last, leaping through as a group of 트롤록s claimed their hilltop. One of the beasts, a shaggy-furred bearlike monstrosity, stumbled through the gateway after her.
The thing dropped dead immediately, a faint wisp of smoke rising from its carcass. Its fellows hooted and growled on the other side. 에그웨인 glanced at the other women, then shrugged and released flame straight through the gateway. A few fell dead, twitching, while the others scrambled away, howling, dropping their weapons.

“That is effective,” 리안 noted, folding her arms and raising an immaculate eyebrow at the gateway. It was the middle of the Last Battle, and the woman *still* took time each morning to do her face.

Their gateway had taken them back to camp, which was now mostly empty. With the reserves formed up and ready to move when required, the only soldiers who remained in the camp were a force of five hundred guarding Bryne’s command tent.

She still carried the pouch with the false seals at her side. 랜드's words had shaken her hard. How would they get the seals back? If the minions of the Shadow broke them at the wrong time, it would be a catastrophe.

Had they broken them already? Would the world know? 에그웨인 felt a dread she could not abandon. And yet, the war continued, and she had no recourse but to keep fighting. They would think of a way to recover the seals, if they could. 랜드 swore to try. She wasn’t certain what he could do.

“They’re fighting so hard,” 가윈 said.

에그웨인 turned to find him standing a short distance away, inspecting the battlefield with his looking glass. She felt a longing from him. Without some men to lead as he had the Younglings, she knew, he felt useless in these battles.

“The 트롤록s are driven by 미르드랄,” 에그웨인 said, “linked to give the 페이드s greater control over them.”

“Yes, but *why* resist so strongly?” 가윈 said, still looking through the glass. “They don’t care about this land. It’s obvious that these hills are lost to them, and yet they fight savagely. 트롤록s are base—they fight and win or they scatter and retreat. They don’t hold land. They’re trying to do so here. It’s like… like the 페이드s think that even after a rout like this one, they’re in a good position.”

“Who knows why 페이드s do what they do?” Lelaine remarked, arms folded, looking through the still-open gateway.

에그웨인 turned, looking through it, too. The hilltop was now empty, strangely isolated amid the battle. Her soldiers had crashed up against the 트롤록s in the small valley between the hills, and the fighting was brutal down there. She heard grunts, yells, clangs. Bloodied pikes were raised in the air as a group of men were forced back, and halberdiers moved in to try to slow the 트롤록s.

The 그림자태생 were taking terrible casualties. It *was* an oddity; Bryne had expected them to retreat.

“Something’s wrong,” 에그웨인 said, the hairs of her arms standing on end. Her worry about the seals vanished, for now. Her army was in danger. “Gather the 에스 세다이 and have the army pull back.”

The other women looked at her as if she were mad. 가윈 took off at a dash toward the command tent to give her orders. He didn’t question.

“Mother,” Romanda said, letting her gateway die. “What is—”

Something split the air on the other side of 에그웨인’s war camp, opposite the battlefield. A line of light, longer than any gateway 에그웨인 had seen. It was nearly as wide as her *camp itself.*

The line of light turned upon itself, opening a view that was *not* of southern 캔도르. Instead, it was a place of ferns and drooping trees— though they were brown, like everything else, they were still alien and unfamiliar.

An enormous army stood silently upon this unfamiliar landscape. Thousands of banners flew above it, emblazoned with symbols 에그웨인 didn’t recognize. The foot soldiers wore knee-length garments that appeared to be some kind of padded armor, reinforced with chain in a large-squared pattern. Others wore metal shirts that seemed sewn from coins tied together.

Many carried hand axes, though of a very strange design. They had long, thin handles that bulged like bulbs at the end and the axe heads were narrow and thin, almost like picks. The hafts of all of their weapons—from polearms to swords—had a flowing, organic design. Smooth and not of a uniform width, made of some dark red wood that had been painted with colorful dots down the sides.

에그웨인 took in all of this in moments, her mind searching for any kind of origin for this strange force. She found nothing to latch on to until she sensed the channeling. The glow of *세다르* surrounded *hundreds* of women, all of them riding, wearing strange dresses made entirely of stiff black silk. The dresses were not tied at the waists, but instead pulled relatively tight around the shoulders, and flared wide toward the bottoms. Long, rectangular tassels of a multitude of colors hung from ties at the front, just below the neck. The faces of the women were all tattooed.

“Release the Power,” 에그웨인 said, letting go of *세다르.* “Don’t let them sense you!” She dashed to the side, Lelaine following, the glow winking out from around her.

Romanda ignored 에그웨인, letting out a curse. She began weaving a gateway to escape.

A dozen different weaves of fire suddenly thrashed the area where Romanda stood. The woman didn’t have a chance to scream. 에그웨인 and the other women scrambled through the camp as weaves of the 하나의 힘 destroyed tents, consumed supplies and set the entire place aflame.

에그웨인 reached the command tent just as 가윈 stumbled out. She grabbed him and pulled him to the ground as a ball of fire passed just overhead, then crashed into a collection of tents nearby.

“Light!” 가윈 said. “What is it?”

“Sharans.” Lelaine, breathless, huddled down beside them.

“Are you certain?” 에그웨인 whispered.

Lelaine nodded. “Accounts from the Cairienin before the 아일 War are plentiful, if not very informative. They weren't allowed to see much, but what they did see looked a lot like an army.”

“Army?” 가윈 said, stretching to the side and looking between the tents toward the force marching through the unnaturally wide gateway. “Blood and bloody ashes!” he swore, ducking back. “There are thousands of them!”

“Far too many to fight,” 에그웨인 agreed, mind working furiously. “Not pinned between them and the 트롤록s as we are. We have to fall back.”

“I just passed the order to Byrne to disengage the troops,” 가윈 said. “But ... 에그웨인. Where are we going to go? 트롤록s in front, that army behind! Light. We'll be crushed between them!”

Byrne would react quickly. He'd send a messenger to the line captains. *Oh no ...*

에그웨인 grabbed 가윈 and pulled him away from the command tent just as she felt channeling within. Lelaine cried out, ducking in the other direction.

The Sharan women reacted immediately to the channeling. The ground ripped up underneath the tent, destroying it in a burst of overwhelming power. Tattered shreds of cloth flew into the air amid stones and clods of earth.

에그웨인 fell backward, and 가윈 pulled her toward a toppled cart that had been hit, one wheel shattered, its burden of firewood tumbling out. 가윈 pulled 에그웨인 to the sheltered place just under the edge of the cart, beside the tumble of wood. They huddled there, though the wood flickered with flames and the ground was afire. The heat was distressing, but not unbearable.

에그웨인 huddled against the ground, blinking through eyes that burned with smoke, searching for signs of Lelaine. Or ... Light! 시우안 and Byrne had been inside that tent, along with 유키리 and many of their command staff.

에그웨인 and 가윈 hid as flames rained on the camp, tearing up the earth. The Sharans struck at any sign of movement; several women who ran were instantly immolated.

“Be ready to run,” 가윈 said, “once the fire stops falling.”

The flames *did* wane, but just as they did, riders in Sharan armor charged through the camp. They hooted and yelled, leveling bows at anyone they saw, dropping dozens with arrows to the back. After that, the Sharan troops moved through the camp in tight formations. 에그웨인 waited tensely, trying to think of how to slip away.

She saw no opportunity. 가윈 pulled 에그웨인 back farther, rubbed soot on her cheeks and motioned for her to stay low, then draped his 감시자 cloak over them both. With the smoke from the wood burning nearby, perhaps they wouldn’t be seen.

Her heart thumped urgently in her chest. 가윈 pressed something to her face, a kerchief he had soaked with his waterskin. He held another one to his face and breathed through it. She took the one he was holding to her, but barely breathed. Those soldiers were so *close.*

One of the soldiers turned toward the cart, peering at the woodpile, but when he glanced through the smoke toward them he didn’t seem to see anything. 에그웨인 silently contemplated the 감시자 cloak. Its color-shifting nature made them nearly invisible, if they were careful not to move.

*Why don’t I have one of these cloaks?* she thought with annoyance. *Why should they only be for 감시자s?*

The soldiers were busy flushing out servants. Those who ran, they killed with arrows from bows that stretched extremely far. Servants who moved more slowly, they rounded up and forced to the ground.

에그웨인 longed to embrace the Source, to do something. To bring down fire and lightning upon these invaders. She still had Vora’s *sa’angreal.* She could—

She quashed that line of thinking. She was surrounded by the enemy, and the swift reaction of the channelers indicated that they were watching for 에스 세다이. If she wove for a single moment, she’d be killed before she could escape. She huddled beside 가윈, under his cloak, hoping none of the Sharan channelers walked close enough to sense her ability. She could use a weave to hide that ability, but would have to channel first to use it. Dared she try that?

They hid for a good hour or more. If the cloud cover hadn’t been so complete, casting the land into perpetual twilight, they’d certainly have been spotted, cloak or no cloak. She almost cried out at one point when a few of the Sharan soldiers tossed some buckets of water onto the woodpile, stifling the fire and soaking both of them.

She couldn’t make out anything of her own army, though she feared the worst. The Sharan channelers and a large portion of their army moved

through the camp quickly, toward the battlefield. With Bryne and the

Amyrlin gone, and with a surprise force coming in from behind…

에그웨인 felt sick. How many were dying, dead? 가윈 caught her arm

as he felt her stir, then shook his head, mouthing a few words. *Wait until night.*

*They’re dying!* she mouthed.

*You can’t help.*

It was true. She let him hold her, letting his familiar scent calm her. But how could she simply *wait* as soldiers and 에스 세다이 who depended on her were slaughtered? Light, a huge portion of the 백색 탑 was out there! If this army fell, and those women with it…

*I am the 아미를린 석좌,* she told herself firmly. *I will be strong. I will survive. So long as I live, the 백색 탑 stands.*

She still let 가윈 hold her.

아비엔다 crawled across the rock like a winter lizard seeking warmth. Her fingertips, though callused, were beginning to burn from the bitter cold. 세이올 굴 was cold, with air that smelled as if it came from a tomb.

Rhuarc crawled to her left, a Stone Dog named Shaen to her right. Both wore the red headband of the *siswai’aman.* She didn’t know what to make of Rhuarc, a clan chief, donning that headband. He had never spoken of it; it was as if the headband did not exist. So it was with all of the *siswai’aman.* Amys crawled on Shaen’s right. For once, no one had objected to 현명한 이들 joining the advance scouts. In a place such as this, at a time such as this, the eyes of one who could channel might see what ordinary eyes would not.

아비엔다 pulled herself forward, making no noise, despite the necklaces she wore. No plants sprouted on these rocks, not even mold or lichen. They were deep within the Blasted 란ds, now. Almost as deep as one could go.

Rhuarc reachcd the ridge first, and she saw him tense. 아비엔다 arrived next, peering over the side of the rock, keeping low so as not to be seen. Her breath stopped dead in her throat.

She'd heard stories of this place. Of the massive forge near the base of the slope, a single black stream running past it. That water had been poisoned to the point that it would kill any who touched it. Hearths dotted the valley like open wounds, reddening the fog around them. As a young Maiden, she'd listened with wide eyes as an ancient roofmistress told of the creatures who worked the Shadow's forges, creatures that were not dead and not alive. Silent and horrible, the brutish things moved with steps that held no life—like the ticking hands of a clock.

The forgers paid little heed to the cages full of humans whose blood would be spilled to temper newly forged blades. The captives might as well have been chunks of iron. Though 아비엔다 was too far to hear the humans’ whimpers, she felt them. Her fingers grew taut upon the rocks.

세이올 굴 itself dominated the valley, its black slopes rising like a serrated knife into the sky. The sides were rent with cuts, like the skin of a man who had been whipped a hundred times, each score leaving a gash that spat steam. Perhaps that steam created the fog that lay over the valley. The fog churned and surged, as if the valley were a cup holding liquid.

“Such a terrible place,” Amys whispered.

아비엔다 had never heard such dread in the woman’s voice. That chilled 아비엔다 nearly as much as the bitter wind that ruffled their clothing. Distant *pings* broke the air, the workers forging. A black column of smoke rose from the nearest forge, and did not dissipate. It rose like an umbilical cord to the clouds above, which rained down lightning with dreadful frequency.

Yes, 아비엔다 had heard stories of this place. Those stories had failed to convey the full truth. One could not *describe* this place. One had to experience it.

A scraping from behind, and in a few moments, 로델 이투랄데 crawled up next to Rhuarc. He moved quietly, for a wetlander.

“You were so impatient that you could not await our report?” Rhuarc asked softly.

“No report can convey what a man’s own eyes can,” 이투랄데 said. “I didn’t promise I’d stay behind. I told you to go ahead. And you did.” He raised his looking glass, shading the front with his hand, though that probably wasn’t necessary with those clouds.

Rhuarc frowned. He and the other 아일 who had come north had agreed to follow a wetlander general, but it did not sit well with them. Nor should it. They would do this thing without growing comfortable. Comfort was the great killer of men.

*Let it be enough*, 아비엔다 thought, turning back to look at the valley. *Enough for my people. Enough for 랜드 and the task he ynust accomplish.*

Seeing the end of her people had nauseated and horrified her, but also awakened her. If the end of the 아일 was the sacrifice required for 랜드 to win, she would make it. She would scream and curse the Creator’s own name, but she would pay that price. Any warrior would. Better that one people should end than the world fall completely under Shadow.

빛 willing, it would not come to that. 빛 willing, her actions with the 용 Peace would serve to protect and shelter the 아일. She would not let the possibility of failure stop her. They would fight. Waking from the dream was always a possibility when the spears were danced.

“Interesting,” 이투랄데 said softly, still looking through his glass. “Your thoughts, 아일?”

“We need to create a distraction,” Rhuarc said. “We can come down the slope just to the east of the forge and set those captives free and break the place apart. This stops the 미르드랄 from receiving new weapons and will keep the 어둠의 존재s eyes on us and not the *Car’a’carn”*

“How long will it take the Dragon?” 이투랄데 asked. “What do you think, 아일? How much time do we give him to save the world?”

“He will fight,” Amys said. “Enter the mountain, duel with Sight-blinder. It will take as long as a fight needs to take. A few hours, perhaps? I have not seen a duel last much longer than that, even between two men of great skill.”

“Let us assume,” 이투랄데 said with a smile, “that there is going to be more to it than a duel.”

“I am not a fool, 로델 이투랄데,” Amys said coolly. “I doubt that the *Car’a’carris* fight will be one of spears and shields. However, when he cleansed the Source, did that not happen in the space of a single day? Perhaps this will be similar.”

“Perhaps,” 이투랄데 said. “Perhaps not.” He lowered the glass and looked to the 아일. “Which possibility would you rather plan for?”

“The worst one,” 아비엔다 said.

“So we plan to hold out as long as the Dragon needs,” 이투랄데 said. “Days, weeks, months… years? As long as it takes.”

Rhuarc nodded slowly. “What do you suggest?”

“The pass into the valley is narrow,” 이투랄데 said. “Scout reports put most of the 그림자태생 left in the 황무지 out beyond the pass there. Even they spend as little time as they can in this forsaken place. If we can close off the pass and seize this valley—destroy those forgeworkers and the few 페이드s down there—we could hold this place for ages. You 아일 are good at slash-and-run tactics. Burn me, but I know *that* from personal experience. You lot attack that forge, and we’ll set about closing up the pass.”

Rhuarc nodded. “It is a good plan.”

The four of them walked down the ridge to where 랜드 waited, dressed in red and gold, arms behind his back, accompanied by a force of twenty Maidens and six Asha’man, plus 니나브 and 모이라인. He seemed very troubled by something—she could feel his anxiety—though he should have been pleased. He had convinced the 쇼엔찬 to fight. What was it that, in his meeting with 에그웨인 al’Vere, had disturbed him so?

랜드 turned and looked upward, toward the peak of 세이올 굴. Staring at it, his emotions changed. He seemed a man looking at a fountain in the Three-fold 란d, savoring the idea of cool water. 아비엔다 could feel his anticipation. There was also fear in him, of course. No warrior ever rid himself completely of the fear. He controlled it, overwhelmed it with the thirst to be on with the fight, to test himself.

Men or women could not know themselves, not truly, until they were strained to their absolute limit. Until they danced the spears with death, felt their blood seeping out to stain the ground, and drove the weapon home into the beating heart of an enemy. 랜드 al’Thor wanted this, and she understood him because of it. Strange to realize, after all of this time, just how alike they were.

She stepped up to him, and he moved so that he stood just beside her, his shoulder touching hers. He did not drape an arm around her, and she did not take his hand. He did not own her, and she did not own him. The act of his movement so that they faced the same direction meant far more to her than any other gesture could.

“Shade of my heart,” he said softly, watching his Asha’man open a gateway, “what did you see?”

“A tomb,” she replied.

“민e?”

“No. That of your enemy. The place where he was buried once, and the place he will slumber again.”

Something hardened inside 랜드. She could feel it, his resolve.

“You mean to kill him,” 아비엔다 whispered. “시야 가리는 자 himself.”

“Yes.”

She waited.

“Others tell me I am a fool for thinking this,” 랜드 said. His guards moved through the gateway to return to Merrilor.

“No warrior should enter a battle without intending to see that battle finished,” 아비엔다 said. She hesitated after saying it, something else occurring to her.

“What is it?” 랜드 asked.

“Well, the *greatest* victory would be to take your enemy *gai’shain*.”

“I doubt he would submit to that,” 랜드 said.

“Don’t make jest,” she said, elbowing him in the side, earning a grunt. “This must be considered, 랜드 al’Thor. Which is the better way of *ji’e’toh*?”

“Is imprisoning the 어둠의 존재 like taking him *gai’shain?* If so, that would be the proper path.”

“I’m not certain I care what is proper’ this time, 아비엔다.”

“A warrior must *always* consider *ji’e’toh*,” she said sternly. “Have I taught you nothing? Do not speak like that, or you will shame me again before the other 현명한 이들.”

“I had hoped that—considering how our relationship has progressed—we would be through with the lectures, 아비엔다.”

“You thought that growing closer to me would *end* the lectures?” she asked, baffled. 랜드 al’Thor, I have been among wetlander wives, and I’ve seen that they—”

He shook his head, leading the way through the gateway, 아비엔다 following. He seemed amused, and that was good. Some of his anxiety had faded. But truly, this was not a jest. Wetlanders did not have good senses of humor. Sometimes, they did not understand at all when to laugh.

On the other side of the gateway, they entered a camp made up of many groups. 랜드 had command of the Maidens and the *siswai’aman*, along with most of the 현명한 이들.

Just outside of the 아일 camp were the 에스 세다이. 랜드 had command of some three dozen—all of the 에스 세다이 who had sworn to him personally, and most who were bonded to his Asha’man. That meant another two dozen Asha’man, of various ranks.

He also had 로델 이투랄데 and his force, composed primarily of 도마니. Their king, with his wispy beard and the beauty mark on his cheek, rode with them as well, but left the command to the great captain. The monarch gestured, and 이투랄데 walked over to give a report. 알살람 seemed uncomfortable around 랜드, and did not go on any excursions when the Dragon did. 아비엔다 liked that arrangement. She wasn’t certain she trusted this 알살람.

Outside the 아일 tents camped another large military force, the 타이런 army, including the elite force known as the Defenders of the Stone, led by a man named Rodrivar Tihera. Their king was with them as well, and was generally considered the highest authority in their gathered armies, aside from 랜드.

The 타이런s would form a key part of 로델 이투랄데’s plans. As much as it galled 아비엔다 to admit it, 이투랄데 was right. The 아일 were not a defensive force, and though they could hold a pass if needed, they would be better used for offensive maneuvers.

The 타이런s would be perfect for holding ground. They had well-trained companies of pikemen, and a full banner of crossbowmen with a new kind of crossbow crank, knowledge of which the smiths had only just received. They had spent the last week converting the equipment to the new style.

There was one other group in 랜드's force, and it was the most baffling to 아비엔다. 용worn in large numbers. They camped together, and flew a flag that placed the image of the dragon over the ancient symbol of the 에스 세다이. The group was made up of common men, soldiers, lords, ladies and some 에스 세다이 and 감시자s. They came from all nations, including the 아일, and shared only one common bond: They had put aside all loyalties, broken all bonds, to fight in the Last Battle. 아비엔다 had heard discomforting rumors that many of the 아일 among them were *gai’shain* who had put aside the white, claiming they would take it up again when the Last Battle was won.

랜드's coming was said to remove all bonds from men. Oaths shattered when he drew near, and any loyalty or alliance was secondary to the need to serve him in this last fight for humankind. Part of her wanted to name that wetlander foolishness, but perhaps she used that term too easily. A Wise One had to see with better eyes than that.

Now that they were on the other side of the gateway, 아비엔다 finally allowed herself to release *세다르.* The world dulled around her, the added sense of life and wonder evaporating. Every time she released the 하나의 힘, she felt slightly hollow, the joy and thrill now passed, over.

이투랄데 and Rhuarc went to join King 달린, speaking together about their battle plans. 아비엔다 joined 랜드 as he walked toward his tent.

“The dagger worked,” 랜드 said. He reached down and fingered the black sheath that held the dull dagger. “Artham. I had heard them spoken of, back in the 전설의 시대, but nobody created one. I wonder who finally managed it…”

“Are you certain it worked?” 아비엔다 said. “He could have been watching you, but not exposed his hand.”

“No, I would have felt the attention,” 랜드 said. “It *did* work. With this, he won’t sense me until I step right up to the 구멍. Once he does know I’m there, he will have trouble envisioning me, striking at me directly. 아비엔다, that you should find this and identify it when you did, that 엘레인 should give it to me… 패턴 weaves us all where we need to be.” 랜드 smiled, then added, “엘레인 sounded sad when she gave me the dagger. I think a part of her wanted to keep it because it would let her curse by the 어둠의 존재’s name without drawing his attention.”

“Is this really a time for levity?” 아비엔다 asked, scowling at him.

“If ever there was a need for laughter, this is it,” 랜드 said, though the laughter seemed to have left his voice. That anxiety of his returned as they reached his tent.

“What is troubling you?” 아비엔다 asked him.

“They have the seals,” 랜드 said.

“What!”

“Only 에그웨인 knows, but it is true. They were stolen, perhaps from my hiding place, perhaps after I delivered them to 에그웨인.”

“Then they are broken.”

“No,” 랜드 said. “I would feel that. I think they must be waiting. Perhaps they know that in breaking the seals, they clear the way for me to reforge his prison. They’ll break them at just the wrong moment, to let the 어둠의 존재 touch the world, perhaps to give him the strength to overwhelm me as I face him…”

He looked to her and smiled. “Always the warrior.”

“Of course.” What else would she be?

“I have another concern. The 버림받은 자들 will try to strike at me when I enter to face him. 어둠의 존재 cannot see me, does not know where I am, and so is committing some of his forces to each of the different battlefronts. 그림자 pushes hard at 란, trying to destroy him—the 어둠의 존재 presses 엘레인 almost as badly in 케렌. Only 에그웨인 seems to be having some success.

“He searches for me at each of these battlefields, committing his creatures in large numbers. When we attack 세이올 굴, we should be able to hold the valley against armies. The 버림받은 자들, however, will come through gateways. Holding a pass will not stop them, or the Dreadlords, male or female. My confrontation with the 어둠의 존재 will draw them as the cleansing did—only a thousand times more urgently. They will come, with fire and thunder, and they will kill.”

“So will we.”

“I'm counting on it,” 랜드 said. “But I cannot afford to take you into the cavern with me, 아비엔다.”

She felt a sinking feeling, though she attacked it, stabbed it, left it to die. “I suspected. Do not think to send me away to safety, 랜드 al’Thor. You would—”

“I wouldn’t dare,” he said. “I’d fear for my life if I were to try—there isn’t any place that is safe, now. I cannot take you into the cavern because you will be needed out in the valley, watching for the 버림받은 자들 and the seals. I *need* you, 아비엔다. I need all three of you to watch, to be my hands—my heart—during this fight. I am going to send 민 to 에그웨인. Something is going to happen there, I’m certain. 엘레인 will fight in the south, and you ... I need you in the valley of Thakan’dar, watching my back.
“I will leave orders for the 에스 세다이 and Asha’man, 아비엔다. 이투랄데 leads our troops, but *you* command our channelers at 세이올 굴. You must keep the enemy from entering the cavern after me. You are my spear in this battle. If they reach me while I am in the cavern, I will be helpless. What I must do will take all of me—all of my concentration, every scrap of power I have. I’ll be like a babe lying in the wilderness, defenseless against the beasts.”

“And how is this different from how you usually are, 랜드 al’Thor?” she asked.

“Someone must keep you humble,” 아비엔다 said. “It would not do for you to think yourself something grand, simply because you save the world.” He laughed again, leading her up to the tent where 민 was. 니나브 and 모이라인 waited there, too, one with annoyance on her face, the other serenity. 니나브 looked very odd with her hair not long enough to braid. Today, she’d pulled it up and pinned it back.

모이라인 sat quietly on a large stone, *칼란도르*—the Sword That Is Not a Sword—lying across her lap, one hand resting protectively on its hilt. 톰 sat beside her, whittling a stick and whistling softly to himself.

“You should have taken me, 랜드,” 니나브 said, folding her arms. “You had work to do,” 랜드 said. “You have tried as I instructed?”

“Time and time again,” 니나브 said. “There’s no way around the flaw, 랜드. You *cannot* use *칼란도르.* It will be too dangerous.”

랜드 came up to 모이라인, reaching out his hand, and she lifted *칼란도르* for him to take. He raised it up before him, looking through its crystalline substance. It started to glow softly. “민, I have a task for you,” he whispered. “에그웨인 is progressing well, and I feel her battlefront will be key. I wish you to go and watch her and the 쇼엔찬 여제, whom I have asked to join that battlefront once their forces are ready.”

“You would have the 쇼엔찬 join *에그웨인’s* battlefront?” 모이라인 asked, aghast. “Is that wise?”

“I cannot tell wisdom from brashness these days,” 랜드 said. “But I would feel better if someone were keeping an eye on those two factions. 민, will you do it?”

“I was hoping…” 민 looked away.

*Hoping he’d take her into the cavern,* 아비엔다 thought. But of course he could not.

“I’m sorry, 민,” 랜드 said. “But I need you.”

“I will do it.”

“랜드,” 니나브 said. “You are taking *칼란도르* when you attack him? Its weakness ... so long as you are channeling into that… *thing,* anyone can seize control of you. They can use you, and can draw the 하나의 힘 through *칼란도르* into you until it burns you out—leaving you powerless, and leaving them with the strength to level mountains, destroy cities.

“I will take it,” 랜드 said.

“But it’s a trap!” 니나브 said.

“Yes,” 랜드 said, sounding tired. “A trap I must stride into and allow to spring shut upon me.” He laughed, suddenly, throwing his head back. “As always! Why should I be surprised? Spread the word, 니나브. Tell 이투랄데, Rhuarc, King 달린. Tomorrow, we invade 세이올 굴 and claim it as our own! If we must put our head into the lion’s mouth, let us make certain that he chokes upon our flesh!”

**CHAPTER 21**

![](images/00274.jpg)

*Not a Mistake to Ignore*

시우안 rolled her shoulder. She grimaced at the sharp pain. “유키리,” she grumbled, “that weave of yours still needs work.”

The tiny Gray cursed softly, standing up from beside a soldier who had lost his hand. She hadn’t Healed him, instead leaving him to more mundane healers with bandages. To spend energy 치유 this man would be a waste, as he would never fight again. They needed to save their strength for soldiers who could rejoin the battle.

It was brutal reasoning. Well, these were brutal times. 시우안 and 유키리 moved on to the next soldier in the line of wounded. The man with the missing hand would survive without 치유. Probably. They had the Yellows in Mayene, but their energy was consumed in 치유 에스 세다이 who had survived the escape and soldiers who could still fight.

All through the makeshift camp, set up on 아라펠lin soil east of the river’s ford, soldiers wept and groaned. So many wounded, and 시우안 and 유키리 were among the few 에스 세다이 left with any strength to Heal. Most of the others had drained themselves making gateways to bring their army out from between the two attacking forces.

The Sharans had attacked aggressively, but securing the 백색 탑’s camp had occupied them for a while, giving time for the army to flee. Pieces of it, at least.

유키리 Delved the next man, then nodded. 시우안 knelt down and began a 치유 weave. She’d never been very good at this, and even with an *angreal*, it took a lot out of her. She brought the soldier back from the edge of death, 치유 the wound in his side. He gasped, much of the energy for the 치유 coming from his own body.

시우안 wavered, then fell to her knees in exhaustion. Light, she was as unsteady as a noblewoman her first day on the deck of a ship!

유키리 looked her over, then reached out for the *angreal*, a small stone flower. “Go rest, 시우안.”

시우안 clenched her teeth, but handed over the *angreal.* The 하나의 힘 slipped from her, and she let out a deep sigh, half-relieved and half-saddened at losing the beauty of *세다르.*

유키리 moved to the next soldier. 시우안 lay back where she was, her body complaining of its numerous bruises and aches. The events of the battle were a blur to her. She remembered young 가윈 Trakand bursting into the command tent, yelling that 에그웨인 wanted the army to retreat.

Bryne had moved quickly, dropping a written order through the gateway in the floor. That was his newest method of passing commands—an arrow shaft with a note and a long ribbon tied to it, dropped through a gateway high above. There were no heads on the shafts, just a small stone to weight them.

Bryne had been restless before 가윈 appeared. He hadn’t liked the way the battle had been playing out. The way the 트롤록s moved had warned him that the Shadow had been planning something. 시우안 was certain he’d already prepared the orders.

Then there had been the explosions in camp. And 유키리 yelling for them to jump *through* the hole in the floor. Light, she’d assumed the woman was mad! Mad enough to save all of their lives, apparently.

*Burn me if I’m going to lie here like a piece of yesterday’s catch on the deck*, 시우안 thought, staring up at the sky. She hauled herself to her feet and started stalking through the new camp.

유키리 claimed her weave wasn’t all *that* obscure, though 시우안 had never heard of it. A massive cushion of Air, meant to cradle someone who had fallen a great distance. Crafting it had drawn the attention of the Sharans—*Sharans*, of all things!—but they’d escaped. She, Bryne, 유키리 and a few aides. Burn her, they’d gotten out, though that fall still made her wince to remember. And 유키리 kept saying she thought the weave might be the secret behind discovering how to fly! Fool woman. There was a good reason the Creator hadn’t given people wings.

She found Bryne at the edge of the new camp, sitting exhausted on a stump. Two battle maps spread out by stones lay on the ground in front of him. The maps were wrinkled; he’d grabbed them as the tent started to explode around him.

*Fool man,* she thought. *Risking his life for a couple of pieces of paper.*

“*…*from reports,” said General Haerm, the new commander of the 일리안er Companions. “I’m sorry, my Lord. The scouts don’t dare sneak too close to the old camp.”

“No sign of the Amyrlin?” 시우안 asked.

Bryne and Haerm both shook their heads.

“Keep looking, young man.” 시우안 wagged a finger at Haerm. He raised an eyebrow at her use of the word “young.” Burn this youthful face she’d been given. “I mean it. The Amyrlin is alive. You *find* her, you hear me?”

“I… Yes, 에스 세다이.” He showed some measure of respect, but not enough. These 일리안ers didn’t know how to treat 에스 세다이.

Bryne waved the man off, and for once, it didn’t look as if anyone was waiting to meet with him. Everyone was probably too exhausted. Their “camp” looked more like a collection of refugees from a terrible fire than it did an army. Most of the men had rolled themselves in cloaks and gone to sleep. 병사s were better than sailors at sleeping whenever, and wherever, they could.

She couldn’t blame them. She’d been exhausted *before* the Sharans arrived. Now she was tired as death itself. She sat down on the ground beside Bryne’s stump.

“Arm still hurting you?” Bryne asked, reaching down to rub her shoulder. “You can feel that it is,” 시우안 grumbled.

“Merely trying to be pleasant, 시우안.”

“Don’t think I have forgotten that you’re to blame for this bruise.”

“Me?” Bryne said, sounding amused.

“You pushed me through the hole.”

“You didn’t seem ready to move.”

“I was just about to jump. I was almost there.”

“I’m certain,” Bryne said.

“It’s your fault,” 시우안 insisted. “I tumbled. I hadn’t intended to tumble. And 유키리’s weave… horrible thing.”

“It worked,” Bryne said. “I doubt many people can claim to have fallen three hundred paces and survived.”

“She was too eager,” 시우안 said. “She was probably longing to make us jump, you know. All that talk about 이동 and weaves of movement…” She trailed off, partly because she was annoyed at herself. This day had gone poorly enough without her griping at Bryne. “How many did we lose?” Not a much better topic, but she needed to know. “Do we have reports yet?”

“Nearly one in two of the soldiers,” Bryne said softly.

Worse than she’d suspected. “And the 에스 세다이?”

“We have somewhere around two hundred and fifty left,” Bryne said. “Though a number of those are in shock at having lost 감시자s.”

That was more of a disaster. A hundred and twenty 에스 세다이 dead in a matter of hours? The 백색 탑 would require a very long time to recover from that.

“I’m sorry, 시우안,” Bryne said.

“Bah,” 시우안 said, “most of them treated me like fish guts anyway. They resented me as Amyrlin, laughed when I was cast down, and then made a servant of me when I returned.”

Bryne nodded, still rubbing her shoulder. He could feel that she was hurt, despite her words. There were good women among the dead. Many good sisters.

“She’s out there,” 시우안 said stubbornly. “에그웨인 will surprise us, Bryne. You watch.”

“If I’m watching, it won’t be much of a surprise, will it?”

시우안 grunted. “Fool man.”

“You’re right,” he said solemnly. “On both counts. I think 에그웨인 *will* surprise us. I’m also a fool.”

“Bryne…”

“I *am,* 시우안. How could I miss that they were stalling? They wanted to occupy us until this other force could gather. The 트롤록s pulled back into those hills. A defensive move. 트롤록s aren’t defensive. I assumed they were trying to set up an ambush only, and that was why they were pulling back corpses and preparing to wait. If I’d attacked them earlier, this could have been avoided. I was too careful.”

“A man who thinks all day about the catch he missed because of stormy weather ends up wasting time when the sky is clear.”

“A clever proverb, 시우안,” he said. “But there’s a saying among generals, written by Fogh the Tireless. ‘If you do not learn from your losses, you will be ruled by them.’ I can’t see how I let this happen. I’ve trained better than this, prepared better than this! It’s *not* just a mistake I can ignore, 시우안. 패턴 itself is at stake.”

He rubbed his forehead. In the dim light of the setting sun, he looked older, his face wrinkled, his hands frail. It was as if this battle had stolen decades from him. He sighed, hunching forward.

시우안 found herself at a loss for words.

They sat in silence.

Lyrelle waited outside the gates to the so-called 검은 탑. It took every ounce of her training not to let her frustration show.

This entire expedition had been a disaster from the start. First, the 검은 탑 had refused them entry until the Reds had done their business, and that had been followed by the trouble with gateways. *That* had been followed by three bubbles of evil, two attempts by 어둠의 친구들 to murder the lot of them and the warning from the Amyrlin that the 검은 탑 had joined the Shadow to fight.

Lyrelle had sent most of her women to fight alongside 란 Mandragoran at the Amyrlin’s insistence. She’d remained behind with a few sisters to watch the 검은 탑. And now… now this. What to make of it?

“I can assure you,” the young Asha’man said, “the danger has passed. We drove off the M’Hael and the others who turned to the Shadow. The rest of us walk in the Light.”

Lyrelle turned to her companions. A representative from each 아자, along with backup—sent for desperately this morning when the Asha’man had first approached her—in the form of thirty other sisters. They accepted Lyrelle’s leadership here, if only reluctantly.

“We will discuss it,” she said, dismissing the young Asha’man with a nod.

“What do we do?” 미렐 asked. The Green had been with Lyrelle from the start, one of the few that she’d not sent away, partially because she wanted the woman’s 감시자s near. “If some of their members are fighting for the Shadow…”

“관문s can be made again,” 세인 said. “Something has changed about this place in the days since we felt that channeling inside.”

“I don’t trust it,” 미렐 said.

“We must know for certain,” 세인 said. “We cannot leave the 검은 탑 unattended during the Last Battle itself. We *must* see these men taken care of, one way or another.” The 검은 탑 men claimed that only a few of their number had joined the Shadow, and that the channeling had been the result of an attack by the 흑색 아자.

It galled her to hear them use those words. 흑색 아자. For centuries, the 백색 탑 had denied the existence of 어둠의 친구들 among 에스 세다이. The truth had, unfortunately, been revealed. That didn’t mean Lyrelle wanted to hear men tossing around the term so casually. Particularly men like these.

“If they’d wanted to attack us,” Lyrelle said speculatively, “they’d have done it when we couldn’t escape with gateways. For now, I will assume they have cleansed the… problems among their ranks. As was required of the 백색 탑 itself.”

“So we go in?” 미렐 asked.

“Yes. We bond the men we were promised, and from them draw out the truth, if it is obscured.” It troubled Lyrelle that the 용의 환생 had refused them the highest-ranking among the Asha’man, but Lyrelle had devised a plan when she first came here. It should still work. She would first ask for a display of channeling among the men, and would bond the one she felt was strongest. She would then have that one tell her which among the trainees were the most talented so her sisters could bond those.

From there… well, she hoped that would contain the majority of these men. Light, what a mess. Men who could *channel*, walking about unashamed! She did not accept this fable of the taint having been cleansed. Of course these… men… would claim such a thing.

“Sometimes,” Lyrelle muttered, “I wish I could go back and slap myself for accepting this commission.”

미렐 laughed. She never *did* take events as seriously as she should. Lyrelle felt annoyed at having missed the chances to be had at the 백색 탑 during her long absence. Reunification, fighting the 쇼엔찬… These were the times when leadership could be proven, and a woman could gain a reputation for strength.

Opportunities appeared during times of upheaval. Opportunities now lost to her. Light, but she hated that thought.

“We will enter,” she called up to the walls framing the gate before her. Then, more softly, she continued to her women: “Hold the 하나의 힘 and be careful. We do not know what could happen here.” Her women would be a match for a larger number of untrained Asha’man, if it came to that. It shouldn’t, logically. Of course, the men *were* likely mad. So perhaps assuming logic from them was imprudent.

The large gates opened to allow her people in. It said something about these 검은 탑 men that they chose to finish the walls around their grounds before actually building their tower.

She kneed her horse forward, and 미렐 and the others followed in a clopping of hooves. Lyrelle embraced the Source and used the new weave, which would tell her if a man channeled nearby. It was not the young man from a short time ago who met them at the gates, however.

“What is this?” Lyrelle asked as she was joined by 페바라 Tazanovni. Lyrelle knew the Red Sitter, though not well.

“I’ve been asked to accompany you,” 페바라 said cheerfully. “로가인 thought that a familiar face might make you more comfortable.”

Lyrelle held in a sneer. 에스 세다이 should not be cheerful. 에스 세다이 should be calm, collected, and—if anything else—stern. A man should look at an 에스 세다이 and immediately wonder what he had done wrong and how he could fix it.

페바라 fell in beside her as they rode onto the grounds of the 검은 탑. “로가인, who is in charge now, sends his regards,” 페바라 continued. “He was gravely wounded in the attacks and has not yet fully recovered.”

“Will he be well?”

“Oh, certainly. He should be up and about in another day or two. He will be needed to lead the Asha’man as they join the Last Battle, I suspect.” *Pity,* Lyrelle thought. The 검은 탑 would have been more easily controlled without a false Dragon at their head. Better that he had died.

“I am certain his aid will be useful,” Lyrelle said. “His leadership, however… Well, we shall see. Tell me, 페바라. I have been told that bonding a man who can channel is different from bonding a normal man. Have you been through the process?”

“Yes,” 페바라 said.

“Is it true, then?” Lyrelle asked. “Ordinary men can be compelled with the bond to obey, but not these Asha’man?”

페바라 smiled, seeming wistful. “Ah, what would that be like? No, the bond cannot force Asha’man. You will have to use more inventive means.” That was not good. “How obedient are they?” Aledrin asked from the other side.

“It depends on the man, I suspect,” 페바라 said.

“If they cannot be forced,” Lyrelle said, “will they obey their 에스 세다이 in battle?”

“Probably,” 페바라 said, though there was something ambiguous about the way she said it. “I must tell you something, all of you. The mission I was sent on, and the one you also pursue, is a fool’s errand.”

“Is that so?” Lyrelle asked evenly. She was hardly going to trust a Red after what they had done to 시우안. “Why is that?”

“I was once where you are,” 페바라 said. “Ready to bond all of the Asha’man in an attempt to control them. But would you ride into another city and select fifty men there, at a whim, and bond them as 감시자s? Bonding the Asha’man just to bond them is foolish. It will not control them. I do think some Asha’man will make excellent 감시자s, but—like many men— others will not. I suggest that you abandon your plan to bond exactly forty-seven and take those who are most willing. You will gain better 감시자s.”

“Interesting advice,” Lyrelle said. “But, as you mentioned, the Asha’man will be needed at the battlefront. There is not time. We will take the forty-seven most powerful.”

페바라 sighed, but said nothing further as they passed several men in black coats with two pins on the high collars. Lyrelle felt her skin crawling, as if insects burrowed beneath it. Men who could channel.

Lelaine felt that the 검은 탑 was vital to the 백색 탑’s plans. Well, Lyrelle did not belong to Lelaine. She was her own person, and a Sitter in her own right. If she could find a way to bring the 검은 탑 under her direct authority, then perhaps she could finally wiggle out from under Lelaine’s thumb.

For that prize, bonding Asha’man was worthwhile. Light, but she wasn’t going to enjoy it. They needed all of these men controlled, somehow. 용 would be growing mad, unreliable by this point, tainted by the 어둠의 존재’s touch on *세이딘*. Could he be manipulated into letting the rest of the men be bonded?

*Not having control through the bond*. . . *that will be dangerous.* She imagined going into battle with ranks of two or three dozen Asha’man, bonded and forced to her will. How could she make it happen?

They reached a line of men in black coats waiting at the edge of the village. Lyrelle and the others approached them, and Lyrelle did a quick count. Forty-seven men, including the one standing at the front. What trick were they trying to pull?

The one at the front came forward. He was a sturdy man in his middle years, and he looked as if he’d recently suffered some kind of ordeal. He had bags under his eyes and wan skin. His step was firm, however, and his gaze steady as he met Lyrelle’s eyes, then bowed to her.

“Welcome, 에스 세다이,” he said.

“And you are?”

“안드롤 Genhald,” he said. “I’ve been put in charge of your forty-seven until they have been bonded.”

*“My* forty-seven? I see that you have forgotten the terms already. We are to be given any soldier or 헌신자 we wish, and they cannot refuse us.”

“Yes, indeed,” 안드롤 said. “That is true. Unfortunately, all of the men in the 검은 탑 other than these are either full Asha’man, or have been called away on urgent business. The others would, of course, follow the Dragon’s commands if they were here. We made certain to keep forty-seven for you. Actually, forty-six. I’ve already been bonded by 페바라 Sedai, you see.”

“We will wait until the others return,” Lyrelle said coldly.

“Alas,” 안드롤 said, “I do not think they will return any time soon. If you intend to join the Last Battle, you will have to make your selections quickly.”

Lyrelle narrowed her eyes at him, then looked at 페바라, who shrugged.

“This is a trick,” Lyrelle said to 안드롤. “And a childish one.”

“I thought it clever myself,” 안드롤 returned, voice cool. “Worthy of an 에스 세다이, one might say. You were promised that any member of the 검은 탑, save full Asha’man, would respond to your request. They will. Any of them to whom you can *make* the request.”

“Undoubtedly, you chose for me the weakest among your numbers.”

“Actually,” 안드롤 said, “we took those who volunteered. They are good men, every one of them. They are the ones who wanted to be 감시자s.”

“The 용의 환생 will hear of this.”

“From what I’ve heard,” 안드롤 said, “he’s heading to 세이올 굴 any time now. Are you going to join him there just to make your complaint?”

Lyrelle drew her lips into a line.

“Here’s the thing, 에스 세다이,” 안드롤 said. “The 용의 환생 sent a message to us, just earlier today. He instructed us to learn one last lesson: that we’re not to think of ourselves as weapons, but as men. Well, men have a choice in their fate, and weapons do not. Here are your *men*, 에스 세다이. Respect them.”

안드롤 bowed again and walked away. 페바라 hesitated, then turned her horse, following him. Lyrelle saw something in the woman’s face as she looked at the man.

*So that is it,* Lyrelle thought. *No better than a Green, that one is. I would have expected more of one her age.*

Lyrelle was tempted to refuse this manipulation, to go to the Amyrlin and protest what had happened. Only… news from the Amyrlin’s battle-front was jumbled. Something about an unexpected army appearing; details were not available.

Certainly the Amyrlin would not be happy to hear complaints at this point. And certainly, Lyrelle admitted to herself, she also wanted to be done with the 검은 탑.

“Each of you pick two,” Lyrelle said to her companions. “A few of us will take only one. Faolain and Theodrin, you are among those. Be quick about it, all of you. I want away from this place as soon as possible.”

페바라 caught up to 안드롤 as he slipped into one of the huts.

“Light,” she said. “I’d forgotten how *cold* some of us can be.”

“Oh, I don’t know,” 안드롤 replied. “I’ve heard that some of you aren’t quite so bad.”

“Be careful of them, 안드롤,” she said, looking back out. “Many will see you as only a threat or a tool to be used.”

“We won you over,” 안드롤 said, walking into a room where Canler, Jonneth and 에마린 waited with cups of warm tea. All three were beginning to recover from the fighting, Jonneth most quickly. 에마린 bore the worst scars, most of them emotional. He, like 로가인, had been subjected to the Turning process. 페바라 noticed him staring blankly, sometimes, face etched by fear as if remembering something horrible.

“You three shouldn’t be here,” 페바라 said, hands on hips, facing 에마린 and the other two. “I know 로가인 promised you advancement, but you still wear only the sword on your collars. If any of those women saw you, they could take you as 감시자s.”

“They won’t see us,” Jonneth said with a laugh. “안드롤 would have us through a gateway before we had time to curse!”

“So what do we do now?” Canler asked.

“Whatever 로가인 wishes of us,” 안드롤 said.

로가인 had… changed since the ordeal. 안드롤 whispered to her that he was darker now. He spoke less. He did still seem determined to get to the Last Battle, but for now, he gathered the men in and pored over things they’d found in 타임’s rooms. 페바라 worried that the Turning had broken him inside.

“He thinks there might be something in those battle maps he found in 타임’s chambers,” 에마린 said.

“We’ll go where 로가인 decides we can be of most use,” 안드롤 replied. A straightforward answer, but one that didn’t actually say much.

“And what of the Lord Dragon?” 페바라 asked carefully.

She felt 안드롤’s uncertainty. The Asha’man Naeff had come to them, bearing news and instructions—and with them, some implications. The 용의 환생 had known all was not well at the 검은 탑.

“He left us alone on purpose,” 안드롤 said.

“He would have come if he could have!” Jonneth said. “I promise you.”

“He left us to escape on our own,” 에마린 said, “or to fall on our own. He has become a harsh man. Perhaps callous.”

“It doesn’t matter,” 안드롤 said. “The 검은 탑 has learned to survive without him. Light! It always survived without him. He barely had anything to do with us. It was 로가인 who gave us hope. It is 로가인 who will have my allegiance.”

The others nodded. 페바라 felt something important happening here. *They couldn’t have leaned upon him forever anyway,* she thought. *The 용의 환생 will die at the Last Battle.* By intention or not, he had given them the chance to become their own men.

“I will take his last order to heart, however,” 안드롤 said. “I will not be merely a weapon. The taint is cleansed. We fight not to die, but to live. We have a *reason* to live. Spread the word among the other men, and let us take oaths to uphold 로가인 as our leader. And then, to the Last Battle. Not as minions of the 용의 환생, not as pawns of the 아미를린 석좌, but as the 검은 탑. Our own men.”

“Our own men,” the other three whispered, nodding.

**CHAPTER 22**

*The Wyld*

에그웨인 was shocked awake as 가윈 clamped his hand over her mouth. She tensed, memories returning like the light of a sunrise. They were still hiding beneath the broken cart; the air still smelled of burned wood. The land nearby was dark as coal. Night had fallen.

She looked to 가윈 and nodded. Had she really drifted off? She wouldn’t have thought it possible, under the circumstances.

“I’m going to try to slip away,” 가윈 whispered, “and make a distraction.”
“I’ll go with you.”

“I can go more quietly.”

“Obviously you’ve never tried to sneak up on someone from the 두 강, 가윈 Trakand,” she said. “I’d bet you a hundred 타르 발론 marks that I’m the quieter of us two.”

“Yes,” 가윈 whispered, “but if you draw within a dozen steps of one of their channelers, you’ll be spotted, no matter how quiet. They’ve been patrolling through camp, particularly at the perimeters.”

She frowned. How did he know that? “You went out scouting.”

“A little,” he whispered. “I wasn’t seen. They’re scavenging through the tents, taking captive anyone they find. We won’t be able to hide here much longer.”

He should not have gone out without asking her. “We—”

가윈 stiffened, and 에그웨인 cut off, listening. Feet, shuffling. The two of them pulled back, watching as ten or twelve captives were led into an open space near where the command tent had stood. Sharans placed torches on poles around the ragged prisoners. A few of these were soldiers, beaten to the point where they could barely walk. There were cooks and laborers as well. They had been lashed, their trousers frayed. All of their shirts had been removed.

On their backs, someone had tattooed a symbol that 에그웨인 did not recognize. At least, she thought they were tattoos. The symbols might have been burned into them.

As the captives were gathered, someone yelled nearby. In a few minutes, a dark-skinned Sharan guard walked up, dragging a young messenger boy he'd apparently found hiding in camp. He ripped off the boys shirt and shoved him, crying, to the ground. The Sharans, oddly, wore clothing that had a large diamond shape cut out of the back. 에그웨인 could see that the guard bore a mark on his own back, a tattoo she could barely make out against his dark skin. His clothing was very formal, with a large, stiff robe that came almost to his knees. It didn’t have sleeves, but underneath he wore a shirt, with a diamond cut-out, that had long sleeves.

Another Sharan came out of the darkness, and this man was almost completely naked. He wore ripped trousers, but no shirt. Instead of a tattoo on his back, he had tattoos all across his shoulders. They crept up his neck, like twisted vines, before reaching up to cup his jaw and cheeks. They looked like a hundred twisted hands, long fingers with claws holding his head from below.

This man went over to the kneeling messenger boy. The other guards shuffled; they weren’t comfortable with this fellow, whoever he was. He held out a hand, sneering.

The boy’s back burned, suddenly, with a tattoo mark like that of the other captives. Smoke rose, and the boy cried out in pain. 가윈 exhaled softly in shock. That man with the tattoos running up onto his face… that man could channel.

Several of the guards muttered. She could *almost* understand the words, but they had a thick accent. The channeler snapped like a feral dog. The guards stepped back, and the channeler prowled off, disappearing into the shadows.

*Light!* 에그웨인 thought.

Rustling in the darkness resolved into two women in the wide silk dresses. One had lighter skin, and as 에그웨인 searched, she found that some of the soldiers did, too. Not all Sharans were dark as the fellows she’d seen so far.

The women’s faces were very beautiful. Delicate. 에그웨인 shrank back. From what she had seen earlier, these two would probably be channelers. If they stepped too close to 에그웨인, they might sense her.

The two women inspected the captives. By the light of their lanterns, 에그웨인 made out tattoos on their faces as well, though theirs were not as disturbing as those upon the men. These were like leaves, tattooed from the back of the neck forward, going under the ears and spreading like blossoms on the cheeks. The two women whispered to one another, and again 에그웨인 felt as if she could almost understand them. If she could weave a thread to listen—

*Idiot,* she thought. Channeling would get her killed here.

Others gathered around the captives. 에그웨인 held her breath. A hundred, two hundred, more people approached. They did not talk much; they seemed a quiet, solemn people, these Sharans. Most of those who came had open backs to their garments, revealing their tattoos. Were those symbols of status?

She had assumed that the more important one was, the more intricate the tattoos. However, officers—she had to assume that was what they were, with their feathered helmets and fine silken coats and golden armor made as if of coins that had been sewn together through the holes at their centers—they had only small openings, revealing tiny tattoos at the base of shoulders.

*They’ve removed pieces of armor to display the tattoos,* she thought. Surely they did not do battle with the skin exposed. This was something done during more formal times.

The last people who joined the crowd—ushered to the front—were the strangest of all. Two men and a woman atop small donkeys, all three wearing beautiful silk skirts, their animals draped with gold and silver chains. Plumes of vibrant colors fanned out from intricate headdresses upon these three. They were nude from the waist up, including the woman, save for the jewelry and necklaces that covered much of their chests. Their backs were exposed, their heads shaven just on the back to show their necks. There were no tattoos.

So… lords of some sort? Except all three had hollow, haunted expressions. They slumped forward, eyes down, faces wan. Their arms seemed thin, almost skeletal. So frail. What had been done to these people?

It made no sense to her. The Sharans were undoubtedly a people as baffling as the 아일, probably more so. *But why come now?* 에그웨인 thought. *Why, after centuries upon centuries of isolation, have they finally decided to invade?*

There were no coincidences, not of this magnitude. These had come to ambush 에그웨인’s people, and had worked with the 트롤록s. She let herself seize upon that. Whatever she learned here would be of vital importance. She could not help her army right now—Light send that some of its members, at least, had managed to flee—so she should learn what she could.

가윈 prodded her softly. She looked to him, and felt his worry for her.

*Now?* he mouthed, gesturing behind them. Perhaps, with everyone’s attention drawn by… whatever was happening, the two of them could sneak away. They started to back up, shuffling quietly.

One of the Sharan channelers called out. 에그웨인 froze. She’d been spotted!

No. No. 에그웨인 breathed deeply, trying to calm her heart, which seemed to be trying to beat its way out through her chest. The woman was speaking to the others. 에그웨인 thought she’d heard the words “It is done” through the thick accent.

The group of people knelt down. The bejeweled trio bowed their heads further. And then, near the captives, the air *bent.*

에그웨인 couldn’t describe it any other way. It warped and… and seemed to rip apart, twisting like it did above the road on a hot day. Something formed from this disruption: a tall man in glistening armor.

He wore no helmet and had dark hair and light skin. His nose was slightly hooked, and he was very handsome, particularly in that armor. It looked to be constructed all of *coins,* silvery and overlapping. The coins were polished to such a shine, they reflected the faces around him like a mirror.

“You have done well,” the man announced to those bowing before him. “You may stand.” His voice bore hints of the Sharan accent, but it was not nearly as thick.

The man placed his hand on the pommel of the sword at his waist as the others rose. From the darkness behind, a group of the channelers crawled forward. They bobbed for this newcomer in a kind of bow. He removed one of his gauntlets, reached out with an offhanded gesture and scratched the head of one of the men, as a lord might favor a hound.

“So these are the new *inacal*,” the man said speculatively. “Do any of you know who I am?”

The captives cringed before him. Though the Sharans had risen, the captives were smart enough to remain on the ground. None of them spoke.

“I suspected not,” the man said. “Though one can never tell if one’s fame has spread unexpectedly. Tell me, if you know who I am. Speak it, and I will let you free.”

No replies.

“Well, you will listen and remember,” the man said. “I am Bao, the Wyld. I am your savior. I have crawled through the depths of sorrow and have risen up to accept my glory. I have come seeking what was taken from me. Remember that.”

The captives cowered further, obviously uncertain what to do. 가윈 tugged on 에그웨인’s sleeve, motioning backward, but she did not move. There was something about that man…

He looked up suddenly. He focused on the women channelers, then gazed about, peering into the darkness. “Do any of you *inacal* know the Dragon?” he asked, though he sounded distracted. “Speak up. Tell me.”

“I did see him,” said one of the captive soldiers. “Several times.”

“Did you speak with him?” Bao asked, strolling away from the captives.

“No, great Lord,” the soldier said. “The 에스 세다이, they did speak with him. Not I.”

“Yes. I worried you would be of no use,” Bao said. “Servants, we are being watched. You have not searched this camp as well as you claimed. I sense a woman nearby who can channel.”

에그웨인 felt a spike of alarm. 가윈 pulled on her arm, meaning to go, but if they ran, they’d be captured for certain. Light! She—

The crowd turned at a sudden noise near one of the fallen tents. Bao raised a hand, and 에그웨인 heard a furious yell in the darkness. Moments later, 리안 floated through the crowd of Sharans, tied in Air, her eyes wide. Bao brought her up close to him, holding her wrapped in weaves that 에그웨인 could not see.

Her heart continued to pound. 리안 was alive. How had she remained hidden? Light! What could 에그웨인 do?

“Ah,” Bao said. “One of these… 에스 세다이. You, you have spoken with the Dragon?”

리안 didn’t respond. To her credit, she kept her face blank.

“Impressive,” Bao said, reaching up fingers and touching her chin. He held up another hand, and the collected captives suddenly started to writhe and scream. They burst into flames, yelling in agony. 에그웨인 had to forcibly stop herself from reaching for the True Source as she watched. She was crying by the time it ended, though she did not remember starting.

The Sharans shuffled.

“Do not be displeased,” Bao said to them. “I know you went to great trouble to take some alive for me, but they would have made poor *inacal.* They are not raised to it, and during this war, we do not have time to train them. Killing them now is a mercy compared to what they would have had to endure. Besides, this one, this… 에스 세다이 will serve our purpose.”

리안’s mask had cracked, and despite the distance, 에그웨인 could see her hatred.

Bao still had her chin cupped in his hand. “You are a beautiful thing,” he said. “Unfortunately, beauty is meaningless. You are to deliver a message for me, 에스 세다이, to 르웨어스 테린. The one who calls himself the 용의 환생. Tell him that I have come to slay him, and in so doing, I will claim this world. I will take what originally should have been mine. Tell him that. Tell him you have seen me, and describe me to him. He will know me.

“Just as the people here awaited him with prophecy, just as they showered him with glory, the people of *my* land awaited me. I have fulfilled their prophecies. He is false, and I am true. Tell him I will finally have satisfaction. He is to come to me, so that we may face one another. If he does not, I will slaughter and destroy. I will seize his people. I will enslave his children, I will take his women for my own. One by one, I will break, destroy, or dominate everything he has loved. The only way for him to avoid this is for him to come and face me.

“Tell him this, little 에스 세다이. Tell him that an old friend awaits. I am Bao, the Wyld. He Who Is Owned Only by the 란d. The dragonslayer. He knew me once by a name I have scorned, the name Barid Bel.”

*Barid Bel?* 에그웨인 thought, memories from her lessons in the 백색 탑 returning to her. *Barid Bel Medar…* *디만드레드.*

The storm in the wolf dream was a changeable thing. 페린 spent hours prowling the 국경지대, visiting packs of wolves as he ran down dry riverbeds and across broken hills.

Gaul had learned quickly. He wouldn’t stand for a moment against Slayer, of course, but at least he had learned to keep his clothing from changing— though his veil did still snap up to cover his face when he was startled.

The two of them bounded through 캔도르, leaving blurs in the air as they moved from hilltop to hilltop. The storm was sometimes strong, sometimes weak. At the moment, 캔도르 was hauntingly still. The grassy highland landscape was strewn with all kinds of debris. Tents, roofing tiles, the sail of a large ship, even a blacksmith’s anvil, deposited point-first into a muddy hillside.

The dangerously powerful storm could arise anywhere in the wolf dream and rip apart cities or forests. He’d found 타이런 hats blown all the way to 시엔나르.

페린 came to rest on a hilltop, Gaul streaking into place beside him. How long had they been searching for Slayer? A few hours, it seemed on one hand. On the other… how much ground had they crossed? They had returned to their food stores now three times to eat. Did that mean a day had passed?

That was a good question. 페린's stomach suddenly growled, and he made them a meal of dried meat and a hunk of bread. He gave some to Gaul. Would summoned bread sustain them in the wolf dream, or would it merely vanish once they consumed it?

The latter. The food vanished even as 페린 ate it. They would need to rely upon their supplies, perhaps getting more from 랜드’s Asha’man during the daily opening of that portal. For now, he *shifted* back to their packs and dug out some dried meat, then rejoined Gaul in the north.

*어린 황소!* This from a wolf named White Eyes. *The Last Hunt is here. Will you lead us?*

Many asked this, lately, and 페린 couldn’t figure out how to interpret it. *Why do you need me to lead you?*

*It will be by your call*’ White Eyes replied. *By your howl.*

*Not this prey, 어린 황소.*

페린 shook his head. A response like others he’d received. *White Eyes,* he sent. *Have you seen Slayer? The killer of wolves? Has he stalked you here?*

페린 sent it out broadly, and some of the other wolves replied. They knew of Slayer. His image and scent had been passed among many wolves, much as had 페린's own. None had seen him recently, but time was an odd thing to wolves; 페린 wasn’t certain how recent their “recently” really was.

페린 took a bite of dried meat, and caught himself growling softly. He stifled that. He had come to a peace with the wolf inside of him, but that didn’t mean he intended to let it start tracking mud into the house.

*어린 황소,* another wolf sent. Turn Bow, an aged female pack leader. *Moonhunter walks the dreams again. She seeks you.*

*Thank you,* he sent back. *I know this. I will avoid her.*

*Avoid the moon?* Turn Bow sent back. *A difficult thing, 어린 황소. Difficult.*

She had the right of that.

*I saw Heartseeker just now,* sent Steps, a black-furred youth. *She wears a new scent, but it is her.*

Other wolves sent agreement. Heartseeker was in the wolf dream. Some had seen her to the east, but others said that she had been seen to the south.

But what of Slayer? Where was the man, if not hunting wolves? 페린 caught himself growling again.

Heartseeker. That must be one of the 버림받은 자들, though he didn’t recognize the images they sent of her. She was ancient, and so were the memories of wolves, but often the things they remembered were fragments of fragments that their ancestors had seen.

“Any news?” Gaul said.

“Another one of the 버림받은 자들 is here,” 페린 said with a grunt. “Doing something to the east.”

“Does it involve us?”

“The 버림받은 자들 always involve us,” 페린 said, standing. He reached down, touched Gaul on the shoulder and *shifted* them in the direction Steps had indicated. The position wasn’t exact, but once 페린 arrived, he found some wolves who had seen Heartseeker on their way to the 국경지대 the day before. They sent 페린 eager greetings, asking if he was going to lead them.

He rebuffed their questions, pinpointing where Heartseeker had been spotted. It was Merrilor.

페린 *shifted* there. A strange mist hung over the landscape here. Tall trees, the ones 랜드 had grown, reflected here, and their lofty tops poked out of the mist above.

Tents dotted the landscape, like the tops of mushrooms. 아일 tents were plentiful, and between them cook fires glowed in the mist. This camp had been here long enough to manifest in the wolf dream, though tent flaps changed places and bedrolls vanished, flickering in the insubstantial way of this place.

페린 led Gaul between the neat rows of tents and horseless horse pickets. They both froze as they heard a sound. Someone muttering. 페린 used the trick he’d seen 란피어 use, creating a pocket of. . . something around himself that was invisible, but which stopped sound. It was strange, but he did it by creating a barrier with no air in it. Why would that make the sound stop?

He and Gaul crept forward to the canvas of a tent. That of the man 로델 이투랄데, one of the great captains, judging by the banner. Inside, a woman in trousers picked through documents on a table. They kept vanishing in her fingers.

페린 didn’t recognize her, though she was painfully homely. That certainly wasn’t what he’d have expected from one of the 버림받은 자들; not that large forehead, bulbous nose, uneven eyes or thinning hair. He didn’t recognize her curses, though he grasped the meaning from her tone.

Gaul looked at him, and 페린 reached for his hammer, but hesitated. Attacking Slayer was one thing, but one of the 버림받은 자들? He was confident of his ability to resist weaves here in the wolf dream. But still…

The woman cursed again as the paper she was reading vanished. Then she looked up.

페린’s reaction was immediate. He created a paper-thin wall between her and him, her side painted with an exact replica of the landscape behind him, his side transparent. She looked right at him, but didn’t see him, and turned away.

Gaul nodded. 페린 cautiously followed Heartseeker, lifting himself into the air with a thought. She began to move more quickly, and 페린 forced himself to keep up.

He glanced down, and was rewarded with the stomach-churning sight of Merrilor’s landscape dwindling below. Then it grew dark and vanished into blackness.

They didn’t pass through the clouds. As the ground faded away, so did the clouds, and they entered someplace black. Pinpricks of light appeared all around 페린. The woman above stopped and hung in the air for a few moments before streaking away to the right.

페린 followed again, coloring himself—his skin, his clothing, everything—black to hide. The woman approached one of the pinpricks of light until it expanded and dominated the sky in front of her.

Heartseeker reached her hands forward and pressed them against the light. She was muttering to herself. Feeling he *needed* to hear what she was saying, 페린 dared move closer, though he suspected that the pounding of his heart was so loud it would give him away.

“…take it from me?” she said. “You think I care? Give me a face of broken stone. What do I care? That’s not *me.* I will have your place, 모리딘. It *will be mine.* This face will just make them underestimate me. Burn you.” 페린 frowned. He couldn’t make much sense of what she was saying. “Go ahead and throw your armies at them, you fools,” she continued to herself. “I’ll have the greater victory. An insect can have a thousand legs, but only one head. Destroy the head, and the day is yours. All you’re doing is cutting off the legs, stupid fool. Stupid, arrogant, *insufferable* fool. I’ll have what is due me, I’ll…”

She hesitated, then pivoted. 페린, spooked, immediately sent himself back to the ground. It worked, thankfully—he hadn’t known if it would, up in that place of lights. Gaul jumped, and 페린 took a deep breath. “Let’s—”

A ball of blazing fire crashed into the ground beside him. 페린 cursed and rolled, cooling himself with a gust of wind, imagining his hammer up into his hand.

Heartseeker dropped to the ground in a wave of energy, power rippling around her. “Who are you?” she demanded. “Where are you? I—”

She focused suddenly on 페린, seeing him completely for the first time, the blackness having faded from his clothing. “You!” she screeched. “You are to blame for this!”

She raised her hands; her eyes almost seemed to *glow* with hatred. 페린 could smell the emotion in spite of the blowing wind. She released a white-hot bar of light, but 페린 bent it around himself.

The woman started. They always did that. Didn’t they realize that nothing was real here except what you thought to be real? 페린 vanished, appearing behind her, raising his hammer. Then he hesitated. A woman?

She spun about, screaming and ripping the earth beneath him. He jumped up into the sky, and the air around him tried to seize him—but he did what he’d done before, creating a wall of nothingness. 페린 vanished, leaving behind a statue of himself. He appeared beside the tent, where Gaul watched carefully, spear raised. 페린 put a wall between them and the woman, coloring it to hide them, and made a barrier to block the sound.

“She can’t hear us now,” 페린 said.

“You are strong here,” Gaul said thoughtfully. “Very strong. Do the 현명한 이들 know of this?”

“I’m still a pup compared to them,” 페린 said.

“Perhaps,” Gaul said. “I have not seen them, and they do not speak of this place to men.” He shook his head. “Much honor, 페린 Aybara. You have much honor.”

His feet crunched on bits of frost on the ground that he hadn’t noticed, and she immediately spun on him and released another weave of balefire. *Clever,* 페린 thought, barely managing to bend the light away. It struck the hillside behind, drilling a hole straight through it.

페린 filled her mouth with forkroot. It was difficult to do; changing anything directly about a person was always harder. However, this was much easier than trying to transform her into an animal or the like. She raised a hand to her mouth, eyes adopting a look of panic. She began to spit and hack, then desperately opened a gateway beside her.

페린 growled, imagining ropes reaching for her, but she destroyed them with a weave of Fire—she must have gotten the forkroot out. She hurled herself through the gateway, and he *shifted* himself to be right in front of it, preparing to leap through. He froze when he saw her entering the middle of an enormous army of 트롤록s and 페이드s at night. Many faced the gateway, eager.

페린 stepped back as Heartseeker raised a hand to her mouth, looking aghast and coughing out more forkroot. The gateway closed.

“You should have killed her,” 란피어 said.

페린 turned to find the woman standing nearby, her arms folded. Her hair had changed from silver to dark brown. In fact, her face had changed, too, becoming slightly more like it had been before, when he’d first seen her nearly two years ago.

페린 said nothing, returning his hammer to its straps.
