“Maybe,” 페린 said. “I don’t know if it would be good to distract 니나브 again, considering what she is up to.” 페린 turned about, looking at the bedrolls that flickered, then vanished in the wolf dream. He and Gaul had checked at Merrilor for a gateway, but none was there currently. If he wanted to go back to the waking world, he’d need to camp there and wait for hours. It seemed like such a waste.

If only he could figure out how to *shift* back to the real world himself. 란피어 implied that he might be able to learn the trick, but his only clue in how to do so lay in Slayer. 페린 tried remembering the moment when the man had *shifted* out. Had 페린 sensed anything? A hint to how Slayer did what he did?

He shook his head. He’d gone over and over that, and had come to no conclusions. With a sigh, he quested out for the wolves. *Any sign of Heartseeker?* he asked hopefully.

The wolves sent amusement. He had been asking them too frequently.

*Have you seen any camps of two-legs, then?* 페린 sent.

This earned a vague response. Wolves paid attention to men only to avoid them; in the wolf dream, that didn’t matter much. Still, where men congregated, nightmares sometimes ran wild, so the wolves had learned to keep their distance.

He would have liked to know how the other battles were progressing. What of 엘레인’s army, 페린’s men, Lord and Lady 바쉐어? 페린 led Gaul away; they ran with quick strides, rather than jumping to a place immediately. 페린 wanted to think.

The longer he remained in the wolf dream in the flesh, the more he felt that he should know how to *shift* back. His body seemed to understand that this place was not natural for it. He hadn’t slept here, despite… how long had it been? He could not say. They were almost at the end of their rations, though he felt as though he and Gaul had been here only a handful of hours. Part of that sensation was caused by frequent approaches to the 구멍 to check on the dreamspike, but it was generally so easy to lose track of time here.

There was also an ache of fatigue inside him, growing stronger. He didn’t know if he could sleep in this place. His body wanted rest, but had forgotten how to find it. It reminded him a little of when 모이라인 had dispelled their fatigue while fleeing the 두 강 all that time ago. Two years now.

A very long two years.

페린 and Gaul inspected 란’s camp next. It was even more ephemeral than 에그웨인’s; using the wolf dream for surveillance here was pointless. 란 moved with lots of cavalry, retreating at speed. He and his men did not remain in one place long enough to reflect in the wolf dream except in the most fleeting of ways.

There were no signs of 그랜달. “*Aan'allein* is retreating too” Gaul guessed, surveying the rocky ground that they thought was 란’s camp. There were no tents here, just the occasional fleeting appearance of sleeping rings marked by a pole at the center where horsemen would hobble their animals.

Gaul looked up, scanning the landscape to the west. “If they keep falling back from here, they will eventually reach the Field of Merrilor again. Perhaps that is the goal.”

“Perhaps,” 페린 said. “I want to visit 엘레인’s battlefront and—”

*어린 황소,* a wolf called to him. He found the “voice” of the sending to be familiar somehow. *She is here.*

*Here?* 페린 sent. *Heartseeker?*

*Come.*

페린 grabbed Gaul by the arm and *shifted* them far to the north. 그랜달 was at 세이올 굴? Was she trying to break in and kill 랜드?

They arrived on a ledge overlooking the valley. He and Gaul went down immediately to their stomachs, peering over the edge, inspecting the valley. An old, grizzled wolf appeared beside 페린. He knew this wolf, he was certain of it—the scent was familiar, but he could not place a name to him, and the wolf did not send one.

“Where?” 페린 whispered. “Is she in the cavern?”

*No,* the grizzled wolf sent. *There.*

The wolf sent an image of tents clustered in the valley just below the entrance to the cavern. She had not been spotted in this valley since that first time 페린 had caught her here.

이투랄데’s troops had been holding here for long enough that their tents were becoming more and more stable in the wolf dream. 페린 *shifted*, carefully, down below. Gaul and the wolf joined him as he prowled forward, relying on the wolfs Sending to lead him.

*There,* the wolf said, nodding toward a large tent at the center. 페린 had seen 그랜달 here before, at this tent, the tent of 로델 이투랄데.

페린 froze as the tent’s flap rustled. 그랜달 stepped out. She looked as she had before, with a face like a slab of rock.
페린 created a thin, painted wall to hide himself, but he needn’t have bothered. 그랜달 immediately created a gateway and stepped into the waking world. It was night there, though time passed at such a strange rate this close to the 구멍, that might not mean much for the rest of the world.

페린 could see the same tent darkly on the other side of the gateway, two 도마니 guards out front. 그랜달 waved a hand, and both stood up straighter and saluted her.

The gateway began to close as 그랜달 slipped into the tent. 페린 hesitated, then *shifted* to stand just in front of the gateway. He had a moment to decide. Follow?

No. He had to keep watch on Slayer. However, being this close, he felt something ... an awareness. Stepping through that gateway would be like…

Like waking up.

The gateway snapped shut. 페린 felt a stab of regret, but knew staying in the wolf dream had been right. 랜드 was all but defenseless against Slayer here; he would need 페린's help.

“We need to send warning,” 페린 said.

*I suppose I could take the message for you, 어린 황소,* sent the unnamed wolf.

페린 froze, then spun, pointing. “엘리아스!”

*I am Long Tooth here, 어린 황소.* 엘리아스 sent amusement.

“I thought you said you didn’t come here.”

*I said I avoided it. This place is strange and dangerous. I have enough strangeness* and *danger in my life in the other world.* The wolf sat down on his haunches. *But someone needed to check on you, foolish pup.*

페린 smiled. 엘리아스’ thoughts were a strange mix of wolf and human. His way of sending was very wolflike, but the way he thought of himself was too individual, too *human.*

“How goes the fight?” 페린 asked eagerly. Gaul took up position nearby, watching, alert, in case 그랜달 or Slayer appeared. The field before them, the floor of the valley, was quiet for once. The winds had died down, the dust on the sandy ground stirring in small rifts and ripples. Like water.

*I do not know of the other battlefields,* 엘리아스 sent, *and we wolves stay far from the two-legs. We fight, here and there, at the edges of the battle. Mostly, we have attacked the Twisted Ones and Neverborn from the other side of the canyon, where there are no two-legs except those strange 아일.*

*It is a grueling fight. Shadowkiller must do quick work. We have stood five days, but may not last many more.*

Five days here in the north. Much longer had passed in the rest of the world since 랜드 entered to face the 어둠의 존재. 랜드 himself was so close to the 구멍 that it was likely only hours—maybe minutes—had passed for him. 페린 could feel how time moved differently when he drew near to where 랜드 fought.

“이투랄데,” 페린 said, scratching at his beard. “He’s one of the great captains.”

*Yes,* 엘리아스 sent, smelling of amusement. *Some call him “Little Wolf.”* “바쉐어 is with 엘레인’s army,” 페린 said. “And Gareth Bryne is with 에그웨인. Agelmar is with the Borderlanders and 란.”

*I do not know.*

“He is. Four battlefronts. Four great captains. *That’s* what she’s doing.

“그랜달?” Gaul asked.

“Yes,” 페린 said, anger gathering. “She’s doing something to them, changing their minds, corrupting them. I overheard her saying… Yes. That’s it, I’m certain. Instead of fighting our armies with armies of her own, she plans to bring down the great captains. 엘리아스, do you know how a man can *shift* in and out of the wolf dream in the flesh?”

*Even if I knew this thing—which I do not—I would not teach it to you,* 엘리아스 said with a growl. *Has nobody told you it is a terrible, dangerous thing that you do?*

“Too many,” 페린 said. “Light! We need to warn 바쉐어. I must—”

“페린 Aybara!” Gaul said, pointing. “He is here!”

페린 spun to see a dark blur streak upward toward the entrance to the Pit of Doom. Wolves whimpered and died. Others howled, beginning the hunt. This time, Slayer did not back away.

The way of the predator. Two or three quick lunges to determine weakness, then an all-out attack.

“Wake!” 페린 called to 엘리아스, running up the incline. “Warn 엘레인, 에그웨인, anyone you can! And if you cannot, stop 이투랄데 somehow. The great captains are being corrupted. One of the 버림받은 자들 controls their minds, and their tactics cannot be trusted!”

*I will do it, 어린 황소,* 엘리아스 sent, fading.

“Go to 랜드, Gaul!” 페린 roared. “Guard the way to him! Do not let any of those red-veils pass you!”

페린 summoned his hammer to his hands, not waiting for a reply, then *shifted* to confront Slayer.

랜드 clashed with 모리딘, sword against sword, standing before the darkness that was the essence of the 어둠의 존재. The cold expanse was somehow both infinite and empty.

랜드 held so much of the 하나의 힘 that he nearly burst. He would need that strength in the fight to come. For now, he resisted 모리딘 sword against sword. He wielded *칼란도르* as a physical weapon, fighting as if with a sword made of light itself, parrying 모리딘's attacks.

Each step 랜드 took dripped blood to the ground. 니나브 and 모이라인 clung to stalagmites as if something were battering them, a wind that 랜드 could not sense. 니나브 closed her eyes. 모이라인 stared straight ahead as if determined not to look away, no matter the price.

랜드 turned aside 모리딘’s latest attack, the blades throwing sparks. He had always been the better swordsman of the two, during the 전설의 시대.

He had lost his hand, but thanks to Tam, that no longer mattered as it once might have. And he was also wounded. This place… this place changed things. Rocks on the ground seemed to move, and he often stumbled. The air grew alternately musty and dry, then humid and moldy. Time slipped around them like a stream. 랜드 felt as if he could see it. Each blow here took moments, yet hours passed outside.

He scored 모리딘 across the arm, drawing his blood to spray against the wall.

“My blood and yours,” 랜드 said. “I have you to thank for this wound in my side, Elan. You thought you were the 어둠의 존재, didn’t you? Has he punished you for that?”

“Yes,” 모리딘 snarled. “He returned me to life.” 모리딘 came swinging hard in a two-handed blow. 랜드 stepped backward, catching the blow on *칼란도르*; but he misjudged the slope of the ground. Either that, or the slope changed on him. 랜드 stumbled, the blow forcing him down on one knee.

Blade against blade. 랜드’s leg slipped backward, and brushed the darkness behind, which waited like a pool of ink.

All went black.

The distant 오지어 song was comforting to 엘레인 as she slumped in her saddle atop the hill just north of 케렌.

The women around her weren’t in any better shape than she was. 엘레인 had gathered all of the Kinswomen who could hold on to *세다르*—no matter how weak or tired—and formed two circles with them. She had twelve with her in her own circle, but their collective strength in the Power at the moment was barely more than that of a single 에스 세다이.

엘레인 had stopped channeling in an attempt to let the women recover. Most of them slumped in their saddles or sat on the ground. In front of them extended a ragged battle line. Men fought desperately before the 케렌인 hills, trying to hold against the sea of 트롤록s.

Their victory over the northern 트롤록 army had been short-lived, as they now found themselves strung-out, exhausted and in serious danger of being surrounded by the southern one.

“We almost managed,” Arganda said from beside her, shaking his head. “We almost made it.”

He wore a plume in his helmet. It had belonged to Gallenne. 엘레인 hadn’t been there when the Mayener commander had fallen.

That was the frustrating part. They *were* close. Despite 바쉐어’s betrayal, despite the unexpected arrival of the southern force, they had almost pulled it off. If she’d had more time to position her men, if they’d been able to catch more than a moment’s breather between defeating the northern army and then turning to meet this southern one…

But that was not the case. Nearby, the proud 오지어 fought to protect the dragons, but the 오지어 were slowly being overrun. The ancient creatures had begun to collapse, like felled trees, pulled down by 트롤록s. One by one, their songs broke off.

Arganda held a bloodied hand to his side, pale-faced, barely able to speak. She didn’t have the strength to Heal him. “That 감시자 of yours is a *fiend* on the battlefield, Your Majesty. Her arrows fly like light itself. I’d swear...” Arganda shook his head. He might never hold a sword again, even if Healed.

He should have been sent with the other wounded… somewhere. There wasn’t really anywhere to take them; the channelers were too exhausted to make gateways.

Her people were fracturing. The 아일 fought in clumps, the White-cloaks nearly surrounded, the Wolf Guard in no better shape. The Legion of the Dragon heavy cavalry still rode, but 바쉐어’s betrayal had shaken them.

Now and then, a dragon fired. 알루드라 had rolled them back up to the top of the highest hill, but they were out of ammunition, and the channelers didn’t have strength to make gateways to Baerlon to fetch the new dragons’ eggs. 알루드라 had fired bits of armor until her powder ran low. Now they had only enough for the occasional shot.

The 트롤록s would push through her lines soon, fragmenting her army like ravenous lions. 엘레인 watched from one of the hilltops, guarded by ten of her Guardswomen. The rest had gone to fight. 트롤록s broke through the 아일 to the east of her position, right near the dragoner hilltop position.

The beasts charged up the hill, killing the few 오지어 defenders on that side, roaring their victory as the dragoners pulled out sabers and grimly stood to defend.

엘레인 wasn’t ready to let the dragons go yet. She gathered strength through the circle; women groaned around her. She took up barely a dribble of the Power, far less than she’d hoped, and directed Fire at the lead 트롤록s.

Her attack arced in the air toward the 그림자태생. She felt she was trying to stop a storm by spitting at the wind. That lone ball of fire hit.

The earth exploded beneath it, ripping the hillside and hurling *dozens* of 트롤록s back in the air.

엘레인 started, causing Moonshadow to shuffle beneath her. Arganda cursed.

Someone rode up beside her on a large black horse, emerging as if from smoke. The man was of medium build and had dark curls of hair down to his shoulders. 로가인 looked thinner than she remembered from last time she’d seen him, his cheeks sunken, but his face was still handsome.

“로가인?” she said, shocked.

The Asha’man gestured sharply. Explosions sounded all across the battlefield. 엘레인 turned to see over a hundred men in black coats marching through a large gateway on top of her hill.

“Pull those 오지어 back,” 로가인 said. His ragged voice was raw. Those eyes of his seemed darker now than they once had been. “We will hold this position.”

엘레인 blinked, then nodded for Arganda to pass the command. *로가인 shouldn’t give orders to me,* she thought absently. For the moment, she let it pass.

로가인 turned his horse and rode to the side of the hilltop, looking down at her army. 엘레인 followed, feeling numb. 트롤록s fell as Asha man called up strange attacks, gateways that seemed tied to the ground somehow. They stormed forward, killing the 그림자태생.

로가인 grunted. “You’re in bad shape.”

She forced her mind to work. The Asha’man were here. “Did 랜드 send you?”

“We sent ourselves,” 로가인 said. “그림자 has been planning this trap for a long time, according to notes in 타임’s study. I only just managed to decipher them.” He looked at her. “We came to you first. The 검은 탑 stands with the Lion of 안도르.”

“We need to get my people out of here,” 엘레인 said, forcing her mind to think through the cloud of fatigue. Her army needed a queen. “Mothers milk in a cup! This is going to cost us.” She’d probably lose half her force withdrawing. Better half than all of them. “I’ll start bringing my men back in ranks. Can you make enough gateways to lead us to safety?”

“That wouldn’t be a problem ” 로가인 said absently, looking down the slope. His impassive face would have impressed any 감시자. “But it will be a slaughter. There’s no room for a good retreat, and your lines will grow weaker and weaker as you pull back. The last ranks will be overwhelmed and consumed.”

“I don’t see that we have any other choice,” 엘레인 snapped, exhausted. Light! Here, help had come, and she was snapping. *Stop it.* She composed herself, sitting up straighter. “I mean to say that your arrival, while appreciated greatly, cannot turn a battle that is this far gone. A hundred Asha’man cannot stop a hundred thousand 트롤록s on their own. If we could arrange our battle lines better, get at least a short rest for my men… but no. That is impossible. We must retreat—unless you can produce a miracle, Lord 로가인.”

He smiled, perhaps at her use of “lord” for him. “안드롤!” he barked.

A middle-aged Asha’man hurried over, a plump 에스 세다이 joining him. *페바라?* 엘레인 thought, too exhausted to make sense of it. *A Red?*

“My Lord?” the man, 안드롤, asked.

“I need to slow that army of 트롤록s long enough for the army to regroup and refield itself, 안드롤,” 로가인 said. “How much will it cost us for a miracle?”

“Well, my Lord,” 안드롤 said, rubbing his chin. “That depends. How many of those women sitting back there can channel?”

It was a thing of legends.

엘레인 had heard of the great works performed by large circles of men and women. Every woman in the 백색 탑 was taught of these feats from the past, stories of different days, better days. Days when one half of the 하나의 힘 had not been a thing to fear, when two halves of one whole had worked together to create incredible wonders.

She wasn’t sure the days of legend had truly returned. Certainly, the 에스 세다이 during those times hadn’t been so worried, so desperate. But what they did now left 엘레인 in awe.

She joined in the circle, making the total fourteen women and twelve men. She barely had any strength to lend, but her trickle added to the increasingly large stream. More importantly, a circle had to have at least one more woman than it had men—and now that she had joined, 로가인 could come in last of all and add his considerable strength to the flow.

At the head of this circle was 안드롤, an odd choice. Now that she was part of the circle, she could feel his relative strength. He was extremely weak, weaker than many women who were turned away from the Tower, refused the shawl because of their lack of innate talent.

엘레인 and the others had relocated to the far side of the battlefield. The rest of the Asha’man held back the attacking 트롤록 horde as 안드롤 prepared. Whatever he did, it would need to be swift. 엘레인 still had trouble believing anything could be done. Even with this much power, even with thirteen men and fourteen women working together.

“Light,” 안드롤 whispered, standing between her horse and 로가인’s. “Is this what it feels like to be one of you people? How do you handle so much of the 하나의 힘? How do you keep it from consuming you alive, burning you away?”

페바라 rested her hand on his shoulder in a gesture that was unmistakably tender. 엘레인 could barely rub two thoughts together amid her fatigue, but she still found herself shocked. She had not expected affection from a Red for a man who could channel.

“Move the soldiers back,” 안드롤 said softly.

엘레인 gave the order, worried. The man beside her had never held this kind of power before. It could go to someone’s head; she had seen it happen. Light send that he knew what he was doing.

The soldiers and others retreated, passing by 엘레인’s group. Several tired 오지어 nodded to her in passing, their shoulders slumped, their arms scored with cuts. The 트롤록s poured forward, but the Asha’man who weren’t in the circle disrupted their attack with weaves of the 하나의 힘.

It wasn’t enough. Though the Asha’man fought well, there were just *so* many 트롤록s. The Asha’man could not stop this tide. What did 로가인 think could be done?

안드롤 smiled widely, and held his hands out in front of himself as if pressing against a wall. He closed his eyes. “Three thousand years ago the Lord Dragon created 용산 to hide his shame. His rage still burns hot. Today ... I bring it to you, Your Majesty.”

A beam of light split the air, easily a hundred feet tall. Moonshadow shied back and 엘레인 frowned. Why a column of light? What good would that… The beam of light began to twist in the air, rotating upon itself. Only then did 엘레인 recognize it for the start of a gateway. An enormous gateway, large enough to swallow buildings. She could have moved an entire wing of the Caemlyn palace through that thing!

The air shimmered in front of them, the way a gateway always looked from behind. She couldn’t see where the gateway was leading. Did they have an army waiting on the other side?

She could see the expressions on the slavering 트롤록 faces as they looked into the opening. Absolute horror. They broke away, running, and 엘레인 felt a sudden heat, almost overpowering.

Something exploded out of the gateway, as if pushed by an incredible force. A column of lava a hundred feet in diameter, blazing hot. The column broke apart as the lava crashed down, splashing to the battlefield, gushing forward in a river. The Asha’man outside the circle used weaves of Air to keep it from splashing back on the circle and to shepherd it in the right direction.

The river of fire washed through the foremost 트롤록 ranks, consuming them, destroying hundreds in an eyeblink. The lava *was* under pressure on the other side; that was the only way she could explain the force with which it sprayed from the enormous gateway, turning 트롤록s into cinders, burning a large swath through their army.

안드롤 held the gateway for long minutes as the Shadow’s army pulled back. Asha’man to the sides used gusts of wind to blow the 그림자태생 back into the ever-widening river. By the time 안드롤 finished, he had created a barrier of red-hot death between 엘레인’s army and the bulk of the 트롤록s, whose backs were against the northern walls of 케렌.

안드롤 took a breath, closed the gateway, then pivoted and made two others in quick succession, one pointing southeast, the other southwest.

A second and third column of lava spurted forth—smaller this time, as 안드롤 was obviously weakened. These went tumbling over the land to the east and west of 케렌, singeing away dead weeds and casting smoke into the air. Some of the 트롤록 army had pulled back, but many others had perished, boxed in, with the walled city on one side and lava on others. It would be some time before the 페이드s could organize the survivors to resume their attacks on 엘레인’s forces.

안드롤 let the gateway close. He slumped, but 페바라 caught him.

“One miracle, my Lord,” 안드롤 said, voice soft, as if strained. “Delivered as requested. That should hold them back for a few hours. Long enough?”

“Long enough,” 엘레인 said. “We will be able to regroup, bring through supplies for the dragons, and fetch as many 에스 세다이 from Mayene as we can get to Heal our men and wash away their fatigue. Then we can sort through who is strong enough to continue and reposition our ranks for a much more effective battle.”

“You intend to keep fighting?” 안드롤 asked, surprised.

“Yes,” 엘레인 said. “I can barely stand, but yes. We cannot afford to leave that 트롤록 horde here intact. You and your men give us an edge, 로가인. We will use it, and everything we have, and we *will* destroy them.”

*A Tempest of Water*

에그웨인 looked across the river at the struggle raging between her forces and the Sharan army. She had arrived back at her camp on the 아라펠lin side of the ford. She was itching to join the battle against the Shadow again, but she also needed to talk with Bryne about what had happened at the hills. She had arrived to find the command tent empty.

에그웨인 summoned the messenger who was standing in front of the command tent. “Get word to the sisters that they have less than an hour to rest. Those 트롤록s we were fighting will be joining the battle at the river soon, now that we have left the hills.

She’d move the 에스 세다이 downriver on this side, then attack them across the water as they moved across the fields to attack her soldiers. “Tell the archers they’ll be marching with us as well,” she added. “They may as well put their remaining arrows to good use, until we can get them another supply.”

As the messenger rushed off, 에그웨인 turned to Leilwin, who was standing with her husband, 베일 도몬, nearby. “Leilwin, those look like 쇼엔찬 cavalry troops across the river. Do you know anything about that?”

“Yes, Mother, they are 쇼엔찬. That man standing over there-” She pointed to a man with shaved temples standing by a tree down toward the river; he wore voluminous trousers and, incongruously, a tattered brown coat which looked as if it might have come from the 두 강. “—he told me that a legion commanded by Lieutenant-General Khirgan had come from the 쇼엔찬 camp, and that they had been summoned by General Bryne.”

“He also said that they do be accompanied by the Prince of Ravens,” Domon interjected.

“맷?”

“He did more than accompany them. He do be leading one of the cavalry banners, the ones giving the Sharans a hiding on our army’s left flank. He got there just in time, our pikemen were getting the worst of it before he showed up.”

“에그웨인,” 가윈 said, pointing.

To the south, a few hundred paces below the ford, a small number of soldiers were hauling themselves from the river. They had stripped to their smallclothes and carried swords tied to their backs. It was too far to be sure, but one of their leaders looked familiar.

“Is that Uno?” 에그웨인 frowned, then waved for her horse. She mounted and galloped, with 가윈 and her guards, along the river to where the men lay gasping on the bank, and the sound of one man cursing filled the air.

“Uno!”

“It’s about bloody flaming time someone came!” Uno stood as he saluted in respect. “Mother, we’re in bad shape!”

“I saw.” 에그웨인 gritted her teeth. “I was in the hills when your force was attacked. We did what we could, but there were just too many of them. How did you get out?”

“How did we flaming get out, Mother? When the men started dropping all around us and we figured we was goners, we flaming rode out of there like a flaming lightning bolt had struck our flaming hindquarters! We got to the frog-kissing river on the run, stripped and jumped in, swimming for all we were bloody worth, Mother, with all due respect!” Unos topknot danced as he continued to blaspheme, and 에그웨인 could have sworn the eye painted on his eyepatch became a more intense red.

Uno took a deep breath and continued, a little more subdued. “I can’t understand it, Mother. Some goat-headed messenger told us that the 에스 세다이 on the hills were in trouble and we needed to go up the flaming backsides of the 트롤록s attacking them. I said, who’s going to mind the left flank at the river, and, for that bloody matter, our own bloody flank when we attack the 트롤록s, and he said that General Bryne had that taken care of, reserve cavalry would move up into our position at the river, and the 일리안ers would watch out for our bloody flanks. Some protection they were, all right, one flaming squadron, like a flaming fly trying to fend off a flaming falcon! Oh, they were just waiting for us, like they knew we was coming. No, Mother, this can’t be the fault of Gareth Bryne, we’ve been tricked by some sheep-gutted milk-drinking traitor! With all due respect, Mother!”

“I can’t believe that, Uno. I just heard that General Bryne had brought in a legion of 쇼엔찬 cavalry. Maybe they were simply late getting here. We'll sort it all out when I find the general. Meanwhile, get your men back to camp so they can have a proper rest. Light knows you’ve earned it.”

Uno nodded, and 에그웨인 galloped back toward camp.

Using Vora’s *sa’angreal*, 에그웨인 wove Air and Water, spinning them together. A funnel of water surged up, drawn from the river beneath. 에그웨인 blew her tornado of water into the 트롤록s that were beginning their assault against her army’s left flank on the 캔도리 side of the river. Her tempest of water surged across them. It wasn’t strong enough to pull any of them into the air—she didn’t have the energy for that—but it drove them back, hands to their faces.

Behind her and the other 에스 세다이 positioned on the 아라펠lin side of the river, archers loosed volleys of arrows into the sky. Those didn’t darken the sky the way she would have liked—there weren’t so many—but they did take down more than a hundred 트롤록s with each wave.

To the side, Pylar and a couple of other Browns—all adept with weaves of Earth—caused the ground to erupt under the charging 트롤록s. Spread out next to her, 미렐 and a large contingent of Greens wove fireballs that they lobbed over the water into bunched-up groups of 트롤록s, many of whom continued to run a considerable distance before they collapsed, engulfed in flames.

The 트롤록s howled and roared, but continued their relentless progress against the defenders at the river’s edge. At one point, several ranks of 쇼엔찬 cavalry moved out from the defensive lines and attacked the 트롤록 onslaught head-on. It happened so quickly that many of the 트롤록s were unable to raise their spears before contact was made; large swaths of the foe in the front ranks went down. The 쇼엔찬 swept to the side and returned to their lines at the river.

에그웨인 held to her channeling, forcing herself to work through sheer exhaustion. But the 트롤록s didn’t break; they grew enraged, attacking the humans with a frenzy. 에그웨인 could hear their yells distinctly over the sounds of wind and water.

The 트롤록s grew angry, did they? Well, they would not *know* anger until they had felt that of the 아미를린 석좌. 에그웨인 pulled in more and more of the Power until she was at the very edges of her ability. She put heat into her tempest so that the scalding water burned 트롤록 eyes, hands, hearts. She felt herself yelling, Vora’s *sa’angreal* thrust before her like a spear.

What seemed like hours went by. Eventually, exhausted, she allowed 가윈 to talk her into pulling back for a time. 가윈 went to fetch her horse and as he was returning, 에그웨인 looked across the river.

There was no doubt about it; her army’s left flank had already been pushed another thirty paces. Even with the 에스 세다이 aid, they were losing this battle.

It was long past time for her to find Gareth Bryne.

When 에그웨인 and 가윈 got back to camp, she climbed from her horse and gave it to Leilwin, telling her to use it to help carry the wounded. There were plenty of those who had been dragged across the ford to safety, bloodied soldiers slumping against the arms of friends.

Unfortunately, she hadn’t the strength for 치유, let alone a gateway to send wounded to 타르 발론 or Mayene. Most of the 에스 세다이 not busy at the riverbank didn’t look as if they were doing any better.

“에그웨인,” 가윈 said softly. “Rider. 쇼엔찬. Looks like a noblewoman.”
One of the Blood? 에그웨인 thought, standing and looking through camp toward where 가윈 pointed. At least he had the strength left to keep a lookout. Why any woman would voluntarily go without a 감시자 was beyond her.

The woman approaching wore fine 쇼엔찬 silks, and 에그웨인’s stomach turned at the sight. That finery existed because of a foundation of enslaved channelers, forced into obedience to the Crystal Throne. The woman was certainly one of the Blood, as a contingent of 죽음감시대s accompanied her. You had to be very important for…

“Light!” 가윈 exclaimed. “Is that *민*?”

에그웨인 gaped. It *was.*

민 rode up, scowling. “Mother,” she said to 에그웨인, bowing her head amid her stone-faced guards in dark armor.

“민… are you well?” 에그웨인 asked. *Careful, don’t give out too much information.* Was 민 a captive? Surely she couldn’t have *joined* the 쇼엔찬, could she?

“Oh, I’m well,” 민 said sourly. “I’ve been pampered, stuffed in this outfit, and offered all sorts of somewhat delicate foods. I might add that among the 쇼엔찬, delicate does not necessarily mean tasty. You should see the things they *drink*, 에그웨인.”

“I've seen them,” 에그웨인 said, unable to keep her tone from coldness. “Oh. Yes. I suppose you have. Mother, we have a problem.”

“What kind of problem?”

“Well, it depends on how much you trust 맷.”

“I trust him to find trouble,” 에그웨인 said. “I trust him to find drinking and gambling, no matter where he goes.”

“Do you trust him to lead an army?” 민 asked.

에그웨인 hesitated. Did she?

민 leaned forward, sparing a glance for the 죽음감시대s, who didn’t seem *about* to let her draw any closer to 에그웨인. “에그웨인,” she said softly, “맷 thinks that Bryne is leading your army to destruction. He says ... he says he thinks Bryne is a Darkfriend.”

가윈 started laughing.

에그웨인 jumped. She would have expected anger from him, outrage. “Gareth Bryne?” 가윈 asked. “A *Darkfriend*? I’d believe my own *mother* to be a Darkfriend before him. Tell 카우톤 to stay out of his wife’s royal brandy; hes obviously had too much.”

“I’m inclined to agree with 가윈,” 에그웨인 said slowly. Still, she could not ignore the irregularities in how the army was being led.

She would sort through that. “맷 is always looking out for people who don’t need to be looked out for,” she said. “He’s just trying to protect me. Tell him that we appreciate the… warning.”

“Mother,” 민 said. “He seemed certain. This isn’t a joke. He wants you to turn your armies over to him.”

“My armies,” 에그웨인 said flatly.

“Yes.”

“In the hands of 매트림 카우톤.”

“Um… yes. I should mention, the 여제 has given him command of all the 쇼엔찬 forces. He’s now Marshal-General 카우톤.”

*Ta'veren.* 에그웨인 shook her head. “맷 is a good tactician, but handing him the 백색 탑’s armies… No, that is beyond possibility. Besides, the armies are not mine to give him—the 탑의 회의실 has authority for them. Now, how can we persuade these gentlemen surrounding you that you’ll be safe accompanying me?”

As little as 에그웨인 wanted to admit it, she needed the 쇼엔찬. She wouldn’t risk their alliance to save 민, particularly since it didn’t seem that she was in immediate danger. Of course, if the 쇼엔찬 realized that 민 had sworn their oaths back in Falme, then fled…

“Don’t worry about me,” 민 said with a grimace. “I suppose I’m better off with Fortuona. She… knows about a certain talent of mine, thanks to 맷, and it might let me help her. And you.”

The statement was laden with meaning. The 죽음감시대s were too stoic to respond overtly to 민’s use of the 여제’s name, but they did seem to stiffen, their faces hardening. *Take care, 민,* 에그웨인 thought. *You’re surrounded by autumn thornweeds.*

민 didn’t seem to care. “Will you at least consider what 맷 is saying?”

“That Gareth Bryne is a Darkfriend?” 에그웨인 said. It really was laughable. “Go back and tell 맷 to submit his battle suggestions to us, if he must. For now, I need to find my commanders to plan our next steps.” *Gareth Bryne, where are you?*

A flight of black arrows rose almost invisibly into the air, then fell like a breaking wave. They hit 이투랄데’s army at the mouth of the pass to the valley of Thakan’dar, some bouncing off shields, others finding flesh. One fell inches from where 이투랄데 stood atop a rocky outcropping.

이투랄데 didn’t flinch. He stood, straight-backed, hands clasped behind him. He did, however, mutter, “Letting things draw a little close, aren’t we?” Binde, the Asha’man who stood beside him in the night, grimaced. “Sorry, Lord 이투랄데.” He was supposed to keep the arrows away. He’d done well, so far. Sometimes, however, he got a distant look in his face and started muttering about “them” trying to “take his hands.”

“Stay sharp,” 이투랄데 said.

His head throbbed. More dreams earlier tonight, so real. He had seen 트롤록s eating members of his family alive, and had been too weak to save them. He had struggled and wept as they ate Tamsin and his children, but at the same time had been lured by the scents of the boiling and burning flesh.

At the end of the dream, he had joined the monsters in their feast.

*Put that from your mind,* he thought. It was not easy to do so. The dreams had been so vivid. He had been glad to be awakened by a 트롤록 attack.

He’d been ready for this. His men lit bonfires at the barricades. The 트롤록s had finally pushed through his thorn fortifications, but their butchers bill had been high. Now, 이투랄데’s men fought at the mouth of the pass, holding the tides back from entering the valley.

They had applied their time well during the days the 트롤록s had pushed their way through arduous barriers to the mouth of the pass. The entrance to the valley was now fortified with a series of chest-high earthen bulwarks. Those would be excellent for crossbowmen to use as cover, if 이투랄데’s pike formations were ever pushed back too far.

For now, 이투랄데 had split his army into groups of around three thousand men each, then organized them into square formations of pikes, billhooks and crossbows. He used mounted crossbowmen as skirmishers in the front and on the flanks, and had formed up a vanguard—about six ranks deep— of pikemen. Big pikes, twenty feet long. He’d learned from 마라도나 that you wanted to keep your distance from the 트롤록s.

Pikes worked wonderfully. 이투랄데’s pike squares could pivot and fight in all directions in case they were surrounded. 트롤록s could be forced to fight in ranks, but these squares—properly applied—could break up their lines. Once the 트롤록 ranks were shattered, the 아일 could kill with abandon.

Behind ranks of pikemen he positioned foot soldiers carrying billhooks and halberds. Sometimes 트롤록s fought their way through the pikes, pushing the weapons aside or pulling them down with the weight of corpses. The billhookmen then moved up—slipping between the pikemen—and hamstrung the leading 트롤록s. This gave the leading foot soldiers time to pull back and regroup while the next wave of soldiers—more foot, with pikes moved up to engage the 트롤록s.

It was working, so far. He had a dozen such squares of troops facing the 트롤록s in the night. They fought defensively, doing whatever they could to break the surging tide. The 트롤록s threw themselves at the pikemen, trying to crack them, but each square operated independently. 이투랄데 didn’t worry about the 트롤록s that made it through the gauntlet, because they would be handled by the 아일.

이투랄데 had to keep his hands clasped behind his back to conceal their shaking. Nothing had been the same after 마라도나. He’d learned, but he’d paid dearly for that education.

*Burn these headaches,* he thought. *And burn those 트롤록s.*

Three times, he had nearly given the order to send his armies in with a direct assault, abandoning the square formations. He could imagine them slaughtering, killing. No more delaying. He wanted *blood.*

Each time, he’d stopped himself. They weren’t here for blood, they were here to hold. To give that man the time he needed in the cavern. That was what it was all about… wasn’t it? Why did he have so much trouble remembering that lately?

Another wave of 트롤록 arrows dropped onto 이투랄데’s men. The 페이드s had some of them stationed on the tops of the slopes above the pass, in places that 이투랄데’s own archers had once held. Getting them up there must have been quite an undertaking; the walls of the pass were very steep. How many would have dropped to their deaths making the attempt? Regardless, 트롤록s weren’t good shots with bows, but they didn’t need to be, when firing at armies.

The halberdiers raised shields. They couldn’t fight while holding those, but they kept them strapped to their backs for need. The falling arrows increased, plummeting through the lightly foggy night air. The storm rumbled overhead, but the Windfinders were at their task again, keeping it away. They claimed that at several moments, the army had been mere breaths away from an all-out storm of destruction. At one point, hail the size of a man’s fist had fallen for about a minute before they’d wrested control of the weather again.

If that was what awaited them if the Windfinders weren’t using their bowl, 이투랄데 was more than happy to leave them at their task. 어둠의 존재 wouldn’t care how many 트롤록s he destroyed while sending a blizzard, twister or hurricane to kill the humans they fought.

“They’re gathering for another surge at the mouth of the pass!” someone yelled in the night air, followed by other calls confirming it. 이투랄데 peered through the mist, aided by light from the bonfires. The 트롤록s were indeed regrouping.

“Withdraw the seventh and ninth infantry squads,” 이투랄데 said. “They’ve been at it too long. Pull the fourth and fifth out of reserve and have them take flanking positions. Prepare for more arrows. And ...” He trailed off, frowning. What *were* those 트롤록s doing? They’d pulled back farther than he’d have expected, drawing into the darkness of the pass. They couldn’t be retreating, could they?

A dark wave slid out of the mouth of the pass. 미르드랄. Hundreds upon *hundreds of* them. Black cloaks that did not move, in defiance of the breeze. Faces with no eyes, lips that sneered, black swords. The creatures moved like eels, sinuous and sleek.

They gave no time for orders, no time for response. They flowed into the squares of defenders, sliding between pikes, whipping deadly swords.

“아일!” 이투랄데 bellowed. “Bring in the 아일! All of them, and channelers! Everyone except for those who guard at the Pit of Doom itself! Move, move!”

Messengers scrambled away. 이투랄데 watched in horror. An *army* of 미르드랄. Light, it was as bad as his nightmares!

The seventh infantry collapsed before the attack, square formation shattering. 이투랄데 opened his mouth to order the primary reserve—the one defending his position—to give support. He needed the cavalry to ride out and draw pressure off the infantry.

He didn’t have much cavalry; he’d agreed that most of the horsemen would be needed on other fronts. But he did have some. They’d be essential here.

Except…

He squeezed his eyes shut. Light, but he was exhausted. He had trouble thinking.

*Pull back before the attack*, a voice seemed to be saying to him. *Pull back to the 아일, then make a stand there.*

“Pull back . .” he whispered. “Pull . .”

Something felt very, *very* wrong about doing that. Why was his mind insisting upon it?

*Captain Tihera,* 이투랄데 tried to whisper. *You have command.* It wouldn’t come out. Something physical seemed to be holding his mouth shut.

He could hear men screaming. What was happening? Dozens of men could die fighting a single 미르드랄. At 마라도나, he’d lost an entire company of archers—one hundred men—to two 페이드s who had slipped into the city at night. His defensive squads were built to deal with 트롤록s, to hamstring them, to drop them.

The 페이드s would crack those pike squares open like eggs. Nobody was doing what needed to be done.

“My Lord 이투랄데?” Captain Tihera said. “My Lord, what was it you said?”

If they retreated, the 트롤록s would surround them. They needed to stand firm.

이투랄데’s lips opened to give the order to retreat. “Pull the—”

Wolves.

Wolves appeared in the fog like shadows. They leaped at the 미르드랄, growling. 이투랄데 started, spinning, as a man in furs pulled himself up onto the top of the rocky outcrop.

Tihera stumbled back, calling for their guards. The newcomer in furs leaped for 이투랄데 and shoved him off the top of the rocks.

이투랄데 did not fight back. Whoever this man was, 이투랄데 was grateful to him, feeling a moment of victory as he fell. He hadn’t given the order to retreat.

He hit the ground not far below, and it knocked the wind out of him. The wolves took his arms in gentle mouths and pulled him off into the darkness as he slowly drifted into unconsciousness.

에그웨인 sat in the camp as the battle for the border of 캔도르 continued.

Her army held back the 트롤록s.

The 쇼엔찬 fought alongside her troops just across the river.

에그웨인 herself held a small cup of tea.

Light, it was galling. She was the *Amyrlin.* But she was drained of energy.

She still hadn’t found Gareth Bryne, but that wasn’t unexpected. He moved about. Silviana was hunting him, and should have word soon.

에스 세다이 had been sent to take the wounded to Mayene. The sun drooped low in the sky, like an eyelid that refused to stay open. 에그웨인’s hands shook as she held her cup. She could still hear the battle. It seemed that the 트롤록s would fight into the night, grinding the human armies against the river.

Distant shouts rose like the calls of an angry crowd, but the explosions from the channelers had slowed.

She turned to 가윈. He didn’t seem tired at all, though he was strangely pale. 에그웨인 sipped her tea and silently cursed him. It was unfair, but she wasn’t concerned with fairness right now. She could grumble at her 감시자. That was what they were for, wasn’t it?

A breeze blew through camp. She was a few hundred paces east of the ford, but she smelled blood in the air. Bryne raised a hand to his head. Then he sagged, as if suddenly his limbs had lost their strength. “I don’t know what’s wrong with me,” he whispered, sounding hollow. “I keep making mistakes, Mother. “강제,” 에그웨인 said, feeling cold. “You’ve been Compelled. They’re attacking our great captains.”

Several women in the room embraced the Source.

도신 shook her head. “Who can we trust? Any bloody man or woman we put in command could have suffered 강제.”

*A Yellow Flower-Spider*

He turned back to 투온 and 민. They were still staring at one another. No knives, but he felt as if someone had been stabbed. If only 민 would learn a little respect. A gateway suddenly split the air on the side of the room where 투온 had indicated it should go. Suddenly, it occurred to 맷 why she had moved her throne. If that *다만* had been captured and forced to say where 투온 was sitting, an 에스 세다이 could have opened a gateway where she sat, slicing her in two. It was so unlikely it was laughable—an 에스 세다이 could sooner fly than kill someone who wasn’t a Darkfriend—but 투온 took no chances.

The gateway opened to reveal the 탑의 회의실 seated in a tent. Behind them, 에그웨인 sat upon a large chair. The 아미를린 석좌 itself, 맷 realized. *Blood and ashes ... she had them fetch it.*

에그웨인 looked exhausted, though she was doing a good job of hiding it. The others were no better. The 에스 세다이 had been strained to their limits. If she were a soldier, he’d never send her into battle. Blood and bloody ashes—if he had a soldier with that cast to his skin and that look in his eyes, 맷 would send the fellow to bed rest for a week.

“We are curious to know the purpose of this meeting,” 사에린 said calmly.

Silviana sat in a smaller chair by 에그웨인’s side, and the other sisters were organized by 아자. Some were missing, including one of the Yellows, by 맷’s best guess.

투온 nodded to 맷. He was to lead this meeting. He tipped his hat to her, which earned him a half-raised eyebrow. Her dangerous look was gone, although she was still 여제.

“에스 세다이,” 맷 said, standing up and tipping his hat to the 의석자들. “The Crystal Throne appreciates you coming to your bloody senses and letting us direct the battle.”

Silviana’s eyes bulged as if someone had just stepped on her foot. From the corner of his eye, 맷 caught a hint of a smile on 투온’s lips. Blood and bloody ashes, both women should know better than to encourage him so.

“You are as eloquent as ever, 맷,” 에그웨인 said dryly “Do you still have your pet fox?”

“I do,” 맷 said. “He’s snuggled up nice and warm.”

“Take care of him,” 에그웨인 said. “I would not see you suffer Gareth Bryne’s fate.”

“So it was really 강제?” 맷 asked. 에그웨인 had sent him word. “As near as we can tell,” 사에린 said. “니나브 Sedai can see the weaves on someone’s mind, I'm told, but none of the rest of us can.”

“We have our Healers looking at Bryne,” said a stocky 도마니 에스 세다이. “For now, we cannot trust any battle plans that he touched, at least not until we determine how long he’s been under the Shadow’s thumb.”

맷 nodded. “That sounds good. Also, we need to withdraw our forces from the ford.”

“Why?” Lelaine demanded. “We have stabilized here.”

“Not well enough,” 맷 said. “I don’t like this terrain, and we shouldn’t have to fight where we don’t want to.”

“I hesitate to give an extra *inch* to the Shadow,” 사에린 said.

“A pace given up now could earn us two at the dawn,” 맷 replied. General Galgan murmured in agreement, and 맷 realized that he’d quoted Hawkwing.

사에린 frowned. The others seemed to be letting her lead the meeting. 에그웨인 mostly stayed out of it, fingers laced before her, sitting at the back.

“I should probably tell you,” 사에린 said, “that our great captain was not the only one targeted. 다브람 바쉐어 and Lord Agelmar also tried to lead their respective armies to destruction. 엘레인 Sedai did well in her battle, destroying a large force of 트롤록s, but she was only able to do so because of the 검은 탑’s arrival. The Borderlanders were crushed, losing nearly two-thirds of their numbers.”

맷 felt a chill. *Two-thirds?* Light! They were among the best troops the Light had. “란?”

“Lord Mandragoran lives,” 사에린 said.

Well, that was something. “And what of that army up in the 황무지?”

“Lord 이투랄데 fell in battle,” 사에린 replied. “No one quite seems to know what happened to him.”

“This was planned very well,” 맷 said, mind racing. “Blood and bloody ashes. They tried to crush all four battlefronts at once. I can’t imagine the amount of coordination that would take…”

“As I noted,” 에그웨인 said softly, “we must be very careful. Keep that fox of yours near at all times.”

“What does 엘레인 want to do?” 맷 said. “Isn’t she in charge?”

“엘레인 Sedai is currently helping the Borderlanders,” 사에린 said. “She has instructed us that 시엔나르 is all but lost, and is having the Asha’man bring Lord Mandragoran’s army to a place of safety. Tomorrow, she plans to move her army through gateways and hold the 트롤록s in the 황무지.”

맷 shook his head. “We need to make a unified stand.” He hesitated. “Could we bring her through one of these gateways? At least contact her?” There seemed to be no good objection. In a short time, another gateway opened in the tent with 에그웨인 and the 의석자들. 엘레인 strode through, thick with child, eyes practically on fire. Behind her, 맷 caught a glimpse of soldiers with slumped postures, trudging across a dim evening field. “Light,” 엘레인 said, “맷, what is it you want?”

“You’ve won your battle?” 맷 asked.

“Barely, but yes. The 트롤록s in 케렌 have been destroyed. The city is safe, as well.”

맷 nodded. “I need to withdraw from our position here.”

“Fine,” 엘레인 said. “Perhaps we can meld your force with what’s left of the Borderlanders.”

“I want to do more than that, 엘레인,” 맷 said, stepping forward. “This ploy the Shadow tried ... it was clever, 엘레인. *Bloody* clever. We’re bloodied and almost broken. We don’t have the luxury of fighting on multiple battlefronts anymore.”

“What, then?”

“A last stand,” 맷 said softly. “All of us, together, at one place where the terrain favors us.”

엘레인 quieted, and someone brought her a chair to sit beside 에그웨인. She maintained the posture of a queen, but her disheveled hair and clothing burned in several places indicated what she’d been through. 맷 could smell smoke coming from her battlefield, where the gateway was still open.

“That sounds desperate,” 엘레인 finally said.

“We *are* desperate,” 사에린 said.

“We should ask our commanders . .” 엘레인 trailed off. “If there are any we can trust not to be under 강제.”

“There’s only one,” 맷 said grimly, meeting her eyes. “And he’s telling you we are finished if we continue as we have. The earlier plan was a good enough one, but after what we lost today… 엘레인, we’re dead unless we choose one place to stand, gather together, and fight.”

One last toss of the dice.

엘레인 sat for a time. “Where?” she finally asked.

“타르 발론?” 가윈 asked.

“No,” 맷 said. “They’d just besiege it and move on. It can’t be a city where we can get boxed in. We need a territory that will work in our favor, also a land that can’t feed the 트롤록s.”

“Well, a place in the 국경지대 should work for that,” 엘레인 said with a grimace. “란’s army burned almost every city or field they passed to deny the Shadow resources.”

“Maps,” 맷 said, waving. “Someone get me maps. We need a location in southern 시엔나르 or 아라펠. Someplace close enough that the Shadow will see it as tempting, a place to fight us all at once . .

“맷,” 엘레인 asked. “Won’t that be giving them what they want? A chance to wipe us out?”

“Yes,” 맷 said softly as the 에스 세다이 sent over maps. These had markings on them, notations that appeared to be in General Bryne’s hand, judging by what they said. “We have to be a tempting target. We have to draw them in, face them and either defeat them or be crushed.”

A drawn-out fight would serve the Shadow. Once enough 트롤록s reached southern lands, there would be no containing them. He had to win or lose quickly.

One last toss of the dice indeed.

맷 pointed at a location on the maps, a place that Bryne had annotated. It had a good water supply, a nice meeting of hills and rivers. “This place. Merrilor? You’ve been using it as a supply dump?”

사에린 chuckled softly. “And so we go back where we began, do we?”

“It does have some small fortifications,” 엘레인 said. “The men built a palisade on one side, and we could expand it.”

“It’s what we need,” 맷 said, envisioning a battle there.

Merrilor would put them where the two major 트롤록 armies could come in, try to crush the humans between them. That would be tempting. But the terrain would be wonderful for 맷 to use…

Yes. It would be like the Battle of the Priya Narrows. If he put archers along those cliffs—no, dragons—and if he could give the 에스 세다이 a few days of rest… Priya Narrows. He had counted on using a large river to trap the 햄arean army at the mouth of the Narrows. But as he sprung the trap, the blasted river dried up on him; the 햄areans had dammed it up on the other side of the Narrows. They had stepped right over the riverbed, and got clean away. *That’s a lesson I won’t forget.*

“This will do,” 맷 said, placing his hand on the map. “엘레인?”

“Let it be done,” 엘레인 said. “I hope you know what you’re doing, 맷.”

As she spoke, the dice started tumbling inside his head.

갈라드 closed Trom’s eyes. He’d searched the battlefield north of 케렌 for over an hour to find him. Trom had bled out, and only a few corners of his cloak were still white. 갈라드 ripped the officer’s knots off his shoulder— amazingly unsoiled—and stood up.

He felt weary to the bone. He started back across the battlefield, passing heaps of the dead. The crows and the ravens had come; they blanketed the landscape behind him. An undulating, quivering blackness that coated the ground like mold. From a distance, it seemed as if the ground had been burned, there were so many carrion birds.

Occasionally, 갈라드 passed men like himself who sifted through the corpses for friends. There were surprisingly few looters—you had to watch for those on a battlefield. 엘레인 had caught a few trying to sneak out of 케렌. She’d threatened to hang them.

*She’s grown harder,* 갈라드 thought, trudging back toward camp. His boots felt like lead on his feet. *That is good.* As a child, she had often made decisions with her heart. She was a queen now, and acted it. Now, if only he could right her moral compass. She wasn’t a bad person, but 갈라드 wished that she—like other monarchs—could see as clearly as he did.

He was beginning to accept that they didn’t. He was beginning to accept that it was all right, so long as they tried their best. Whatever he had inside of him that allowed him to see the right of things was obviously a gift of the Light, and holding others to scorn because they had not been born with it was wrong. Just as it would be wrong to hold a man to scorn because he had been born with only one hand, and was therefore an inferior swordsman.

Many of the living he passed sat on the ground in the rare spots where there were no corpses and no blood. These men did not look like the victors of a battle, though the arrival of the Asha’man had saved this day. The trick with the lava had given 엘레인’s army the breather it needed to regroup and attack.

That battle had been swift, but brutal. 트롤록s did not surrender, and they couldn’t be allowed to break and flee. So 갈라드 and the others had fought, bled and died long past when it was obvious they would be victorious.

The 트롤록s were dead now. The remaining men sat and stared out at the blanket of corpses, as if numbed by the prospect of searching out the few living among the many thousands dead.

The setting sun and choking clouds made the light red, and gave faces a bloody cast.

갈라드 eventually reached the long hill that had marked the division between the two battlefields. He climbed it, slowly, forcing down thoughts of how good a bed would feel. Or a pallet on the floor. Or some flat rock in an out-of-the-way place, where he could roll up in his cloak.

The fresher air atop the hill shocked him. He’d been smelling blood and death for so long that now it was the clean air that smelled wrong. He shook his head, walking past tired Borderlanders who were trudging through gateways. The Asha’man had gone to hold off the 트롤록s to the north so Lord Mandragoran’s armies could escape.

From what 갈라드 heard, the Borderlander armies were a fraction of what they had been. The betrayal of the great captains had been felt most deeply by Lord Mandragoran and his men. It sickened 갈라드, for this battle had not gone easily for him or anyone else with 엘레인. It had been horrible— and as bad as it had been, the fight had gone more poorly for the Borderlanders.

갈라드 kept his stomach settled with difficulty as his view from atop the hill let him see just how many carrion birds had come to feast. 어둠의 존재s minions fell, and the 어둠의 존재’s minions glutted themselves.

갈라드 eventually found 엘레인. Her passionate words, being spoken to Tam al’Thor and Arganda, took him by surprise.

“맷 is right,” she said. “The Field of Merrilor is a good battlefield. Light! I wish we could give the people more time to rest. We’ll have only a few days, a week at most, before the 트롤록s reach Merrilor behind us.” She shook her head. “We should have seen those Sharans coming. When the deck starts to look like it’s stacked against the 어둠의 존재, of *course* he will just add a few new cards to the game.”

갈라드’s pride demanded that he remain standing as he listened to 엘레인 talk to the other commanders. For once, however, his pride lost out, and he settled down on a stool and slumped forward.

“갈라드,” 엘레인 said, “you really should allow one of the Asha’man to wash away your fatigue. Your insistence upon treating them like outcasts is foolish.”

갈라드 straightened up. “It has nothing to do with the Asha’man,” he snapped. Too argumentative. He *was* tired. “This fatigue reminds me of what we lost today. It is an exhaustion my men must endure, and so I will, lest I forget just how tired they are and push them too far.”
엘레인 frowned at him. He had stopped worrying that his words offended her long ago. It seemed he couldn’t claim that a day was pleasant or his tea warm without her taking offense somehow.

It would have been nice if Aybara hadn’t run off. That man was a leader—one of the few that 갈라드 had ever met—that one could actually talk to without worrying that he’d take offense. Perhaps the 두 강 would be a good place for the 백의단 to settle.

Of course, there *was* something of a history of bad blood between them. He could work on that…

*I called them 백의단,* he thought to himself a moment later. *Inside my head, that’s how I thought of the Children just now.* It had been a long time since he’d done that by accident.

“Your Majesty,” Arganda said. He stood beside 로가인, the leader of the Asha’man, and Havien Nurelle, the new commander of the Winged Guard. 탈마네스 of the Band of the Red Hand trudged up with a few commanders from the 살다에안s and the Legion of the Dragon. 장로 하만 of the 오지어 sat on the ground a short distance away; he stared off, toward the sunset, seeming dazed.

“Your Majesty,” Arganda continued, “I realize you consider this a great victory—”

“It *is* a great victory,” 엘레인 said. “We must persuade the men to see it that way. Not eight hours ago, I assumed that our entire army would be slaughtered. We won.”

“At a cost of half of our troops,” Arganda said softly.

“I will count that a victory,” 엘레인 insisted. “We were expecting complete destruction.”

“The only victor today is the butcher,” Nurelle said softly. He looked haunted.

“No,” Tam al’Thor said, “she’s right. The troops have to understand what their losses earned. We *must* treat this as a victory. It must be recorded that way in the histories, and the soldiers must be convinced to see it so.”

“That is a lie,” 갈라드 found himself saying.

“It is not,” al’Thor said. “We lost many friends today. Light, but we all did. Focusing on death, however, is what the 어둠의 존재 wants us to do. I dare you to tell me I’m wrong. We must look and see Light, not Shadow, or we’ll all be pulled under.”

“By *winning* here,” 엘레인 said, deliberately emphasizing the word, “we earn a reprieve. We can gather at Merrilor, entrench there, and make our last stand in our strength against the Shadow.”

“Light,” 탈마네스 whispered. “We’re going to go through this again, aren’t we?”

“Yes,” 엘레인 said reluctantly.

갈라드 looked out over the fields of the dead, then shivered. “Merrilor will be worse. Light help us… it’s going to get worse.”

*The Prince’s Tabac*

페린 chased Slayer through the skies.

He leaped from a churning, silver-black cloud, Slayer a blur before him in the charred sky. The air pulsed with the rhythm of lightning bolts and furious winds. Scent after scent assailed 페린, with no logic behind them. Mud in 티어. A burning pie. Rotting garbage. A death-lily flower.

Slayer landed on the cloud ahead and *shifted*, turning around in an eye-blink, bow drawn. The arrow loosed so quickly the air cracked, but 페린 managed to slap it down with his hammer. He landed on the same thunder-head as Slayer, imagining footing beneath him, and the vapors of the storm cloud became solid.

페린 charged forward through a churning dark gray fog, the top layer of the cloud, and attacked. They clashed, Slayer summoning a shield and sword. 페린's hammer beat a rhythm against that shield, pounding alongside the booming of thunder. A crash with each blow.

Slayer spun away to flee, but 페린 managed to snatch the edge of his cloak. As Slayer attempted to *shift* away, 페린 imagined them staying put. He knew they would. It was not a possibility, it *was.*

They both fuzzed for a moment, then returned to the cloud. Slayer growled, then swept his sword backward, shearing off the tip of his cloak and freeing himself. He turned to face 페린, stalking to the side, sword held in wary hands. The cloud trembled beneath them, and a flash of phantom lightning lit the misty vapor at their feet.

“You become increasingly annoying, wolf pup,” Slayer said.

“You’ve never fought a wolf that can fight you back,” 페린 said. “You’ve killed them from afar. The slaughter was easy. Now you’ve tried to hunt a prey who has teeth, Slayer.”

Slayer snorted. “You’re like a boy with his father’s sword. Dangerous, but completely unaware of why, or how to use your weapons.”

“We’ll see who—” 페린 began, but Slayer lunged, sword out. 페린 braced himself, imagining the sword growing dull, the air becoming thick to slow it, his skin turning hard enough to turn the weapon aside.

A second later, 페린 found himself tumbling through the air.

*Fool!* he thought. He’d focused so much on the attack that he hadn’t been ready when Slayer changed their footing. 페린 passed through the rumbling cloud, breaking out into the sky below, wind tugging at his clothing. He prepared himself, waiting for the hail of arrows to follow him down out of the cloud. Slayer could be so predictable…

No arrows came. 페린 fell for a few moments, then cursed and twisted to see a storm of arrows shooting up from the ground below. He *shifted* seconds before they passed through where he’d been.

페린 appeared in the air a hundred feet to the side, still falling. He didn’t bother to slow himself; he hit the ground, increasing his body’s strength to deal with the shock of the blow. The ground cracked. A ring of dust blew out from him.

The storm was far worse than it had been. The ground here—they were in the south, somewhere, with overgrown brush and tangled vines growing up the sides of the trees—was pocked and torn. Lightning lashed repeatedly, so frequent that he could hardly count to three without seeing a bolt.

There was no rain, but the landscape crumbled. Entire hills would suddenly disintegrate. The one just to 페린’s left dissolved like an enormous pile of dust, a trail of dirt and sand streaking out into the wind.

페린 leaped through the debris-laden sky, hunting Slayer. Had the man *shifted* back up to 세이올 굴? No. Two more arrows pierced the sky, heading for 페린. Slayer was very good at making them ignore the wind.

페린 slapped the arrows aside and hurled himself in Slayer’s direction. He spotted the man on a peak of rock, ground crumbling to either side of him and whipping into the air.

페린 came down with hammer swinging. Slayer *shifted* away, of course, and the hammer struck stone with a sound like thunder. 페린 growled. Slayer was too quick!

페린 was fast, too. Sooner or later, one of them would slip. One slip would be enough.

He caught sight of Slayer bounding away, and followed. When 페린 jumped off the next hilltop, the stones shattered behind him, rising up into the wind. 패턴 was weakening. Beyond that, his will was much stronger now that he was here in the flesh. He no longer had to worry about entering the dream too strongly and losing himself. He had entered it as strongly as one could.

And so, when 페린 moved, the landscape shuddered around him. The next leap showed him sea ahead. They had traveled much farther to the south than 페린 had realized. Were they in 일리안? 티어?

Slayer hit the beach, where water crashed against rocks; the sand—if there had been any—had been blown away. The land seemed to be returning to a primal state, grass ripped free, soil eroded, leaving only stone and crashing waves.

페린 landed beside Slayer. For once, there was no *shifting.* Both men were intent on the fight, the swings of hammer and sword. Metal clanged against metal.

페린 nearly landed a hit, his hammer brushing Slayer’s clothing. He heard a curse, but the next moment, Slayer was rounding from his dodge with a large axe in hand. 페린 braced himself and took it on the side, hardening his skin.

The axe didn’t draw blood, not with 페린 braced as he was, but it *did* carry a huge amount of force behind it. The blow tossed 페린 out over the sea.

Slayer appeared above him a second later, plunging down with that axe. 페린 caught it on his hammer as he fell, but the force of the blow flung him downward, toward the ocean.

He commanded the water to recede. It rushed away, churning and bubbling, as if pursued by a powerful wind. 페린 righted himself as he fell, landing and cracking the still-wet, rocky bottom of the bay. Seawater rose high to either side of him, a circular wall some thirty feet high.

Slayer crashed down nearby. The man was panting from the exertion of their fight. Good. 페린’s own fatigue manifested as a deep burning in his muscles.

“I’m glad you were there,” Slayer said, raising his sword to his shoulder, his shield vanishing. “I had so hoped that, when I appeared to kill the Dragon, you would interfere.”

“What are you, Luc?” 페린 asked, wary, *shifting* to the side, keeping opposite Slayer in the circle of stone with walls of sea. “What are you really?”

Slayer prowled to the side, talking—페린 knew—to lull his prey. “I’ve seen him, you know,” Slayer said softly. “어둠의 존재, the Great Lord as some would call him. Both terms are gross, almost insulting, understatements.”

“Do you really think he’ll reward you?” 페린 spat. “How can you not realize that once you’ve done what he wishes of you, he’ll just discard you, as he has so many?”

Slayer laughed. “Did he discard the 버림받은 자들, when they failed and were imprisoned with him in the 구멍? He could have slaughtered them all and kept their souls in eternal torment. Did he?”

페린 didn’t reply.

“어둠의 존재 does not discard useful tools,” Slayer said. “Fail him, and he may exact punishment, but he never discards. He’s like a goodwife, with her balls of tangled yarn and broken teakettles hidden away in the bottoms of baskets, waiting for the right moment to return them to usefulness. That is where you’re wrong, Aybara. A mere human might kill a tool who succeeds, fearing that the tool will threaten him. That is not the 어둠의 존재’s way. He *will* reward me.”

페린 opened his mouth to reply, and Slayer *shifted* right in front of him to attack, thinking him distracted. 페린 vanished and Slayer struck only air. The man spun about, sword splitting the air, but 페린 had *shifted* to the opposite side. Small sea creatures with many arms undulated near his feet, confused at the sudden lack of water. Something large and dark swam through the shadowy water behind Slayer.

“You never answered my question,” 페린 said. “What *are* you?”

“I’m bold,” Slayer said, striding forward. “And I’m tired of being afraid. In this life, there are predators and there are prey. Often, the predators themselves become food for someone else. The only way to survive is to move up the chain, become the hunter.”

“That’s why you kill wolves?”

Slayer smiled a dangerous smile, his face in shadows. With the storm clouds above and the high walls of water, it was dim here at the bottom— though the strange light of the wolf dream pierced this place, if in a muted way.

“Wolves and men are the finest hunters in this world,” Slayer said softly. “Kill them, and you elevate yourself above them. Not all of us had the *privilege* of growing up in a comfortable home with a warm hearth and laughing siblings.”

페린 and Slayer rounded one another, shadows blending, lightning blasts above shimmering through the water.

“If you knew my life,” Slayer said, “you’d howl. The hopelessness, the agony ... I soon found my way. My power. In this place, I am a king.”

He leaped across the space, his form a blur. 페린 prepared to swing, but Slayer didn’t draw his sword. He crashed into 페린, throwing them both into the wall of water. The sea churned and bubbled around them.

Darkness. 페린 created light, somehow making the rocks at his feet glow. Slayer had hold of his cloak with one hand and was swinging at him in the dark water, his sword trailing bubbles but moving as quickly as in the air. 페린 yelled, bubbles coming from his mouth. He tried to block, but his arms moved lethargically.

In that frozen moment, 페린 tried to imagine the water not impeding him, but his mind rejected that thought. It wasn’t natural. It couldn’t be.

In desperation, Slayer’s sword nearly close enough to bite, 페린 froze the water solid around both of them. Doing so nearly crushed him, but it held Slayer still for a precarious moment while 페린 oriented himself. He made his cloak vanish so he wouldn’t take Slayer with him, then *shifted* away.

페린 landed on the rocky beach beside a steep hillside that was half broken away by the power of the sea. He fell on hands and knees, gasping. Water streamed from his beard. His mind felt… numb. He had trouble thinking the water away from him to dry himself.

*What’s happening?* he thought, trembling. Around him, the storm raged, the bark ripping from tree trunks, their limbs already stripped away. He was just so… tired. Exhausted. How long had it been since he slept? Weeks had passed in the real world, but it couldn’t actually have been weeks here, could it? It—

The sea boiled, churning. 페린 turned. He’d kept his hammer, somehow, and he raised it to face Slayer.

The waters continued to move, but nothing came from them. Suddenly, behind him, the hill split in half. 페린 felt something heavy hit him in the shoulder, like a punch. He fell to his knees, twisting to see the hillside broken in two, Slayer standing on the other side, nocking another arrow to his bow.

페린 *shifted*, desperate, pain belatedly flaring up his side and across his body.

“All I’m saying is that battles are being fought,” Mandevwin said, “and we are not there.”

“Battles are always being fought *somewhere*,” Vanin replied, leaning back against the wall outside a warehouse in 타르 발론. 파일 listened to them with half an ear. “We’ve fought our share of them. All *I’m* saying is that I’m pleased to avoid this particular one.”

아비엔다 returned to her group, then started to draw on their power. The more of the 하나의 힘 you held, the harder it was to cut you off from the True Source. She intended to hold so much that no man could separate her from it.

Helplessness. She *hated* feeling helpless. She let the anger at what had been done to her rage inside of her, and led her group toward the nearest source of male channeling that Flinn could identify.

*Drifting*

랜드 stood in a place that was not.

A place outside of time, outside of the Pattern itself.

It looked like thousands upon thousands of twisting ribbons of light; they spun around him, above him, undulating and shimmering, twisting together. Everything that had ever been, everything that could be, everything that could have been ... it all lay right there, before him.

랜드 could not comprehend it. The blackness around it sucked on him, *pulled* him toward it. He reached out to the Pattern and somehow anchored himself in it, lest he be consumed.

That changed his focus. It locked him, slightly, into a time. The pattern before him rippled, and 랜드 watched it being woven. It was not actually *the* Pattern, he knew, but his mind saw it that way. Familiar, as it had been described, the threads of lives weaving together.

랜드 anchored himself in reality again and moved with it. Time had meaning again, and he could not see ahead or behind. He still could see all places, like a man standing above a globe as it turned.

랜드 faced the emptiness. “So,” he said into it. “This is where it will really happen. 모리딘 would have had me believe that a simple sword fight would decide this all.”

HE IS OF ME. BUT HIS EYES ARE SMALL.

“Yes,” 랜드 said. “I have noticed the same.”

SMALL TOOLS CAN BE EFFECTIVE. THE THINNEST OF KNIVES CAN STOP A HEART. HE HAS BROUGHT YOU HERE, ADVERSARY.

None of this had happened the last time, when 랜드 had worn the name of 르웨어스 테린. He could only interpret that as a good sign.

Now the battle truly began. He looked into the nothingness and felt it welling up. Then, like a sudden storm, the 어둠의 존재 brought all of his force against 랜드.

페린 fell back against a tree, gasping at the pain. Slayers arrow had impaled his shoulder, the arrowhead coming out his back. He didn’t dare pull it free, not with…

페린 slipped and hit the ground with a grunt. His shoulder flared with pain. He rolled over, staring up at the sky. He’d broken the arrow when falling.

*It’s… it’s the wolf dream. I can just make the arrow vanish.*

He tried to gather the strength to do so, but was too weak. He found himself floating, and he sent outward, seeking for wolves. He found the minds of some, and they started, sending back surprise.

His nature seemed to frighten them, and they pushed him out of their minds. How could they not know what he was? Wolves had long, long memories. Surely… surely…

“Here you are,” a voice said.

란피어. He looked up at her, his vision blurry.

Yes… Yes, he could go to her, couldn’t he? Where was she? The Field of Merrilor. That was where he’d left her. It was where she would be. He *shifted* there, somehow gathering himself just enough to manage it. But of course she wasn’t there. He was in the wolf dream.

The wolves could hold 세이올 굴 on this side now, couldn’t they? They could keep 랜드 safe… They’d have to.

파일 poked a stick at their meager cook fire. Darkness had fallen, and the fire glowed with a faint red light. They hadn’t dared make it larger. Deadly things prowled the 황무지. 트롤록s were the least of the dangers here.

The still, too-silent air made 파일 feel as if they were being watched by a thousand eyes. If the Shadow had planned a trap for her caravan, it meant the Shadow knew about the Horn. In that case, they were in very serious danger. More serious, even, than being in the 황무지 itself.
