Setalle laughed. “Child, I couldn’t light a candle. I was burned out in an accident. I haven’t held the 하나의 힘 in over twenty-five years.”

“I see,” 파일 said. “Thank you.”

Setalle moved off, and 파일 found herself wondering. How truthful was her story? Setalle had been very helpful in their days together, and 파일 couldn’t blame the woman for keeping secret her ties to the 백색 탑. In any other situation, 파일 wouldn’t have given the woman’s story a moment of doubt.

However, there was no way out here to confirm what she said. If Setalle was 흑색 아자 in hiding, her story about being burned out could simply be that—a story. Perhaps she could still channel. Or perhaps she couldn’t, but had been stilled as a punishment. Could this woman be an escaped prisoner of the most dangerous type, an agent who had waited decades for the right moment to strike?

Setalle had been the one to suggest they go to 세이올 굴. Was she seeking to bring the Horn to her master?

Feeling cold, 파일 entered her tent as several members of *Cha 파일* set up watch around it. 파일 wrapped herself in her bedroll. She knew that she was being overly suspicious. But how else was she to be, considering the circumstances?

*Light,* she thought. *발레르의 뿔, lost in the 황무지.* A nightmare.

아비엔다 knelt on one knee beside the smoldering corpse, holding her *angreal*—the turtle brooch that 엘레인 had given her. She breathed through her mouth as she gazed down on the man’s face.

There were a surprising number of these red-veils. Whatever their origins, they were *not* 아일. They did not follow *ji’e’toh.* During the night’s fighting, she had seen two Maidens take a man captive. He had acted like *gai’shain*, but had then killed one from behind with a hidden knife.

“Well?” Sarene asked, breathless. While those at the Field of Merrilor rested and prepared for their challenge ahead, this battle at 세이올 굴 continued. The red-veil attack had lasted all through the night, the following day and now into the night again.

“I think I knew him,” 아비엔다 said, disturbed. “He channeled for the first time when I was a child, making *algode* grow when it should not.” She let the veil fall down on his face. “His name was Soro. He was kind to me. I watched him run across the dry ground at sunset after vowing to spit in 시야 가리는 자’s eye.”

“I'm sorry,” Sarene said, though her voice was uncolored by any sympathy. 아비엔다 was growing accustomed to that in the woman. It wasn’t that Sarene didn’t care; she just didn’t let caring distract her. At least, not when her 감시자 was elsewhere. The 에스 세다이 would have made a fine Maiden.

“Let’s keep moving,” 아비엔다 said, taking off with her pack of channelers. During the days and nights of fighting, 아비엔다’s team had shifted, melded and split as women needed rest. 아비엔다 herself had slept sometime during the day.

By common agreement, the one leading the circle avoided drawing on her own power—thus 아비엔다 was still at reasonable strength, despite so many hours of fighting. This allowed her to remain alert, on the hunt. The other women became wells of power to be drawn upon.

She had to be careful not to drain them too far. Tire a woman, and she could sleep for a few hours and be back up to fight again. Drain her completely, and she could be useless for days. At the moment, 아비엔다 had Flinn and three 에스 세다이 with her. She had learned the weave to tell her when a man was channeling nearby—it was moving through the 에스 세다이 and 현명한 이들—but having a male channeler with her was far more useful.

Flinn pointed toward some flashes of fire on the side of the valley. They loped in that direction, passing corpses and places where the ground smoldered. With the growing light of dawn, 아비엔다 could see through the cold mist that 달린’s forces still held the mouth of the valley.

The 트롤록s had pushed forward to the low earthen mounds that 이투랄데 had built. Killing had been done there on both sides. The 트롤록s had taken far more losses—but then, they were also far more numerous. It seemed from her quick glance that they had overrun one of the earthen bulwarks, but 도마니 riders had come in from the reserves and were pushing them back.

Bands of 아일 roved and fought in the mouth of the valley itself. Some with red veils, some with black. *Too many,* 아비엔다 thought, as she slowed her team with a raised hand. She then continued forward on her own, quietly. She could draw a few hundred paces away from the women and still have access to their power.

She picked her way through the barren rocky fields of the valley. There were three dead bodies to her right, two with black veils. She tested them with a quick Delving; she would not be caught by the old trick of hiding among the corpses. She had used that one herself.

These three were truly dead, so she continued on in a crouch. In addition to the place where the 타이런s and 도마니 held the 트롤록s back, they had a second force guarding their camp and the pathway up to where 랜드 fought. In the space between, 아일 and red-veils roved in bands, each trying to best the other. Only, some of the red-veils could channel.

The ground thumped and shook nearby. A spray of soil fell through the air. 아비엔다 crouched down lower, but quickened her pace.

Ahead, over a dozen *siswai’aman* were rushing the position of two red-veils, both channelers. The red-veils cast up the earth beneath the attackers, sending bodies flying.

아비엔다 understood why the 아일 kept going. These red-veils were an affront, a crime. The 쇼엔찬, who would dare take 현명한 이들 captive, were not as disgusting as these. Somehow, the Shadow had taken the bravest of the 아일 and made them into these… these *things.*

아비엔다 struck quickly, pulling strength through her *angreal* and her circle, weaving two lines of fire and hurling them at the red-veils. She began new weaves immediately, casting up the ground beneath the two channelers, and started a third set of weaves. She threw fire at the red-veils as they stumbled; one jumped away as the other was caught in her earthen blasts.

She struck the one who had fled with spears of flame. Then she hit both corpses with an extra burst of power, just to make certain. These men no longer held to *ji’e’toh.* They were no longer alive. They were weeds to be pulled.

She moved forward to check on the *siswai’aman.* Eight still lived, three of them wounded. 아비엔다 was not particularly good with 치유, but she was able to save the life of one man, keeping a wound in his throat from bleeding out. The other survivors gathered the wounded and moved back toward the camp.

아비엔다 stood above the two corpses. She decided not to look at them closely. Seeing one man she had known was bad enough. These—

A shock went through her, and one of her wells of power vanished. 아비엔다 gasped. Another one winked out.

She immediately released the circle, then dashed back to where she had left the women. Flashes and explosions shook her. 아비엔다 clung to the 하나의 힘, her own strength now seeming pitifully small compared to what she’d been using.

She stumbled to a halt before the smoldering corpses of Kiruna and Faeldrin. The hideous woman she had seen before—the woman that 아비엔다 was increasingly certain was one of the 버림받은 자들—stood there smiling at her. The horrid woman had her hand on Sarene’s shoulder; the slender White stood with her head turned toward the 버림받은 자들, staring at her with vapid, adoring eyes. Sarene’s 감시자 lay dead at her feet.

Both vanished, twisting upon themselves, 이동 without use of a gateway. 아비엔다 fell to her knees beside the dead. Nearby, Damer Flinn groaned and tried to pull himself free of the cast-up earth. His left arm was completely gone, burned away at the shoulder.

아비엔다 cursed and did what she could to Heal him, though he slipped into unconsciousness. She suddenly felt very tired and very, *very* alone.

**CHAPTER 35**

*A Practiced Grin*

올버 missed Wind. Bela—the stout, shaggy mare he now rode— wasn’t bad, really. She was just slow. 올버 knew this because he kept trying to nudge her forward, but she continued plodding along behind the other horses. Nothing he did could make her go any faster. 올버 wanted to ride like a storm. Instead, he rode like a sturdy log in a placid river.

He wiped his brow. The 황무지 was pretty scary, and the others—most of them didn’t have horses—walked as if each step was going to bring a thousand 트롤록s down on them. The rest of the caravan spoke in hushed voices, and they looked at the hillsides with suspicion.

They passed a group of withered trees, with sap leaking from open sores in the bark. That sap looked too red. Almost like blood. Nearby, one of the caravan drivers stepped up to inspect it.

Vines snapped down from the limbs above—vines that looked brown and dead, yet moved like snakes. Before 올버 could scream, the caravan driver was hanging, dead, from the upper branches of the tree.

The entire line of people froze in place, horrified. Above, the tree actually *pulled* the dead man into itself through a split in the bark. Ingesting him. Maybe that sap *was* blood.

올버 looked on, horrified.

“Steady,” Lady 파일 said, a slight tremor in her voice. “I’ve told you, don’t draw close to plants! Don’t touch anything.”

They moved on, a solemn bunch. Sandip, riding nearby, muttered to himself. “That’s the fifteenth one. Fifteen men, dead in a few days. Light! We’re never going to survive this!”

If only it were 트롤록s! 올버 couldn’t fight trees and insects. Who could? But 트롤록s, those he’d be able to fight. 올버 had his knife, and he’d learned a few things about using it from Harnan and Silvic. 올버 wasn’t that tall, but he figured that would make 트롤록s underestimate him. He could lunge low and go for their vitals before they knew what was happening.

He told himself this to keep his hands from shaking as he kicked Bela, hoping to move up by Lady 파일. In the distance, he heard a screeching sound, like something dying in a horrible way. 올버 shivered. He’d heard that same sound earlier in the day. Did it sound closer now?

Setalle gave him a worried glance as he neared the front. The others tried everything they could to keep him from danger. He steeled himself, ignoring that horrid screeching off in the distance. Everyone thought 올버 was fragile, but he wasn’t. They hadn’t seen what he had, growing up. In truth, he didn’t like thinking about those times. It seemed as if he’d lived three lives. One before his parents died, one when he’d been alone and now this one.

Anyway, he was used to fighting people bigger than he was. It was the Last Battle. They kept saying everyone would be needed. Well, why not him? When the 트롤록s came, the first thing he’d do was climb down off this slow mount. He could *stroll* faster than this animal could gallop! Well, the 아일 didn’t need horses. 올버 hadn’t gone to train with them yet, but he would. He had it planned out. He hated all 아일, but mostly the Shaido, and he would need to learn their secrets if he was going to kill them.

He’d go among them and demand to be trained. They’d take him in, and would treat him poorly, but eventually they’d respect him and let him train with their warriors. There were stories about that. It was how things happened.

After he knew their secrets, he’d go to the 뱀들 and 여우들 and receive answers on how to locate the Shaido who had murdered his father. From there, tracking and killing them would be a quest worthy of its own story.

*I’ll take Noal,* he thought. *He’s been everywhere. He can be my guide. He .. .*

Noal was dead.

Sweat crawled down the side of 올버’s face as he stared at the rocky path ahead. They passed more of those terrible trees, and now everyone gave them a wide berth. Beside the path, though, one of the men pointed out a large patch of that killing mud. It looked brown and thick, and 올버 spotted several bones peeking out.

This place was horrible!

He wished Noal were here. Noal had gone everywhere, seen everything. He’d know how to get them out of this place. But Noal was gone. 올버 had only heard the news recently, filtered through things that the Lady 모이라인 had shared about what happened at the Tower of Ghenjei.

*Everyone’s dying,* 올버 thought, eyes still forward. *Everyone*…

맷 had run off to the 쇼엔찬, 탈마네스 to fight alongside Queen 엘레인. One by one, everyone in this group was being eaten by trees, mud or monsters.

Why did they all leave 올버 alone?

He rubbed at his bracelet. Noal had given it to him, shortly before leaving. Woven of rough fibers, it was of a type warriors wore in a faraway land, so Noal had told him. It was the mark of a man who had seen battle and lived.

Noal… dead. Would 맷 die, too?
올버 felt hot, tired and very frightened. He nudged Bela forward, and fortunately she obeyed, trotting a little faster up the slope so 올버 moved up the line. They’d abandoned the wagons, then left for some place called the Blasted 란ds, which required them to climb some foothills. In the morning, they’d entered a pass between the mountains. Though he felt warm, the air *was* getting cooler as they climbed. He didn’t mind that at all. It still smelled awful, though. Like rotting corpses.

Their group had started with fifty soldiers and almost half as many wagon drivers and workers. There were also a handful of others like 올버, Setalle and the half-dozen members of Lady 파일’s bodyguard.

So far, they’d lost fifteen people to hazards of the 황무지, including five killed by some horrible three-eyed things that had attacked the camp yesterday morning. He’d overheard Lady 파일 saying that she considered them lucky to have lost only fifteen so far, that it could have been worse.

It didn’t seem lucky to 올버. This place was awful and he wanted to be out of it. The 황무지 wouldn’t be as bad as this, would it? *Cha 파일’s* men and women acted like 아일. A little bit like 아일. Maybe they’d done as 올버 wanted to, and trained in the 황무지. He’d have to ask them.

He rode on for another half-hour or so. Eventually, he coaxed Bela up to the front of the line. Lady 파일’s brilliant black mare looked fast. Why couldn’t 올버 have been given a horse like that one?

파일 had 맷’s chest tied to the back of her horse. At first, 올버 had been pleased with that, as he figured 맷 would want that tabac pretty badly. 맷 always complained about not having good tabac. Then 올버 had heard 파일 explaining to someone else that the chest had simply been a convenient place to stow some of her things. Had she thrown away the tabac? 맷 wouldn’t like that.

파일 looked at him, and 올버 grinned, giving it as much confidence as he could. It wouldn’t do for her to see how scared he was.

Most women liked his grin. He’d been practicing it, though he didn’t use 맷’s grin as a model. 맷’s always made him look guilty. You learned grins when you were forced to fend for yourself, and 올버 needed one that made him seem innocent. And he *was* innocent. Mostly.

파일 did not smile back. 올버 figured that she was pretty good to look at, despite that nose. She wasn't very soft, though. Bloody ashes, but she had a glare that could rust good iron.

파일 rode between Aravine and Vanin. Though they spoke softly, 올버 could hear what they were saying. He made sure to stare in the other direction, so they'd think he wasn’t eavesdropping. And he wasn’t. He just wanted to be out of the trail dust of the other horses.

“Yes,” Vanin was whispering. “It may not seem it, but we're close to the Blasted 란ds. Burn my own mother, I can’t believe we're going there. But do you feel the air? Its getting cooler. We haven’t seen anything *really* nasty since those three-eyed things yesterday morning.”

“We are close,” Aravine agreed. “Soon, we will be near the 어둠의 존재, in a land where nothing grows, corrupted or not, where there is no life, not even the nastier things from the 황무지.”

“I suppose that should be a comfort.”

“Not really,” Vanin said, wiping his brow. “Because the 그림자태생 up here are more dangerous. If we survive, it will be because there’s a bloody war going on. The 그림자태생 are all locked in battle. If we're lucky, the Blasted 란ds, except right around 세이올 굴, will be as empty as a man’s purse after a deal with the bloody Sea Folk. Pardon my language, my Lady.”

올버 squinted at the approaching mountain peak.

*That’s where the bloody 어둠의 존재 lives,* 올버 thought. *And that’s probably where 맷 is, not Merrilor.* 맷 talked about staying away from danger, but he always found his way to it anyway. 올버 figured that 맷 was just trying to be humble, but was bad at it. Why else would you say you don’t want to be a hero, then always bloody end up charging right into danger?

“And this path?” 파일 asked Vanin. “You said there might have been traffic here recently. Wouldn’t that indicate that this place is far from as empty as you so colorfully described?”

Vanin grunted. “It does look used.”

“So someone has been moving wagons through the area,” Aravine said.

“I don’t know if that is a good sign or a bad one.”

“I don’t think there are *any* good signs up here,” Vanin said. “Maybe we should just pick someplace nearby and hole up, waiting.” He sighed, wiping his brow again, though 올버 didn’t see why. It was growing pretty cold—he could tell, even through the course of the day. And there seemed to be fewer plants, too. He was just fine with that.

He glanced over his shoulder at the stand of trees that had taken that poor man’s life. There didn’t seem to be any others like it nearby, particularly not ahead of them along the path.

“We can’t afford to wait, Vanin,” 파일 said. “I intend to get back to Merrilor, one way or another. The 용의 환생 will be fighting at Thakan’dar. That’s where we need to go to get out of this forsaken place.”

Vanin groaned, but 올버 smiled. He *would* find his way to 맷, and show how dangerous he could be in battle. Then…

Well, then maybe 맷 wouldn’t leave him like the others had. That would be good, as 올버 was going to need 맷’s help tracking down those Shaido. After all he’d learned training with the Band, he was certain nobody would push him around. And nobody would take those he loved from him ever again.

“There are accounts in the archives that explain what we saw.” Cadsuane picked up her cup of tea to warm her hands.

The 아일 girl, 아비엔다, sat on the floor of the tent. *What I wouldn’t give to have that one in the Tower,* Cadsuane thought. These 현명한 이들… they had fight to them. Real bite, like the best of the women in the 백색 탑.

Cadsuane was increasingly convinced that the Shadow for years had been carrying out a complex plan to undermine the 백색 탑. It went deeper than 시우안 산체’s unfortunate unseating and 엘라이더’s reign. It might be decades, centuries, before they understood the extent of the Shadow’s planning. However, the sheer number of Black sisters—hundreds, not the few dozen Cadsuane had guessed—shouted of what had happened.

For now, Cadsuane had to work with what she had. That included these 현명한 이들, poorly trained in using weaves but never lacking in grit. Useful. Like Sorilea, despite her weakness in the 하나의 힘, who sat farther back in the tent, watching.

“I have made some inquiries, child,” Cadsuane said to 아비엔다. “What this woman does is *indeed* 이동. However, the only fragments of documents mentioning it date back to the War of Power.”

아비엔다 frowned. “I saw no weaves, Cadsuane Sedai.”

Cadsuane masked a smile at the respectful tone. The al’Thor boy had put this girl in command—and, in truth, better her than some others. However, he *should* have chosen Cadsuane, and 아비엔다 likely knew it.

“That is because the woman was not weaving the 하나의 힘,” Cadsuane replied.

“What else would it be?”

“Do you know why the 어둠의 존재 was originally freed?”

아비엔다 looked as if remembering something. “Ah… yes. Then they are channeling the 어둠의 존재’s power?”

“It is called the 진정한 힘,” Cadsuane said. “The accounts say that 이동 by 진정한 힘 works in the way you have seen this woman move. Few saw it happen. 어둠의 존재 was miserly with his essence during the War of Power, and only the most favored were granted access. I surmise from this fact that this is *most definitely* one of the 버림받은 자들. From your description of what she did to poor Sarene, I would suspect it is 그랜달.”

“The stories never mentioned 그랜달 being so ugly,” Sorilea said softly.

“If you were one of the 버림받은 자들, easily recognized by description, would you not wish to change your appearance to remain unknown?”

“Perhaps,” Sorilea said. “But then I would not use this… 진정한 힘, as you name it. That would defeat the purpose of my disguise.”

“From what 아비엔다 has told us,” Cadsuane noted, “the woman did not have much of a choice. She had to escape quickly.”

Cadsuane and Sorilea met eyes, and each nodded in agreement. They would hunt this 버림받은 자들, the two of them.

*I won’t have you dying on me now, boy,* Cadsuane thought, glancing over her shoulder toward where al’Thor, 니나브 and 모이라인 continued their work. Every channeler in the camp could feel that pulsing. *At least, not until you’ve done what you need to do.* Cadsuane had expected the 버림받은 자들 to be here. It was why she’d come to this battlefront.

Wind shook the tent, chilling Cadsuane down deep. This place was awful, even when the battle slowed. The dread that hung here was like that of a funeral for a child. It stifled laughter, killed smiles. 어둠의 존재 watched. Light, but it would be good to leave this place.

아비엔다 drank her tea. The woman still looked haunted, although she had obviously lost allies in battle before.

“I left them to die,” she whispered.

“Phaw,” Cadsuane said to her. “You are not to blame for what one of the 버림받은 자들 did, child.”

“You don’t understand,” 아비엔다 said. “We were in a circle, and they tried to break free—I felt them—but I didn’t know what was happening. I held on to their Power, and so they couldn’t fight her. I left them helpless.”

“Well, from now on don’t leave those in your circle behind,” Cadsuane said briskly. “You could not have known what would happen.”

“If you suspect this one is nearby, 아비엔다,” Sorilea said, “you will send word to Cadsuane, me or Amys. There is no shame in admitting that another is too strong to face alone. We will defeat this woman together and protect the *Car’a’carn”*

“Very well,” 아비엔다 said. “But you will do the same for me. All of you.”

She waited. Cadsuane reluctantly agreed, as did Sorilea.

파일 crouched in a dark tent. The air had grown even colder, now that they were close to Thakan’dar. She ran her thumb along the hilt of her knife, breathing in slowly and evenly, then releasing the breath in the same manner. She stared at the tent flaps, unblinking.

She’d placed the Horn’s chest there with one corner sticking out into the night. She felt more alone here on the border of the Blasted 란ds— surrounded by supposed allies—than she had in the Shaido camp.

Two nights ago, she’d been called out of her tent to inspect some odd tracks that had worried the men. They hadn’t lost anyone since drawing so close to the Blasted 란ds—that part of the plan was working—but tensions were still high. She’d been gone only a few minutes, but when she’d returned, the Horn’s chest in her tent had been moved just slightly.

Someone had tried to open it. *Light.* Fortunately, they hadn’t managed to break the lock, and the Horn had still been there when she’d looked.

The traitor could be anyone. One of the Redarms, a wagon driver, a member of *Cha 파일.* 파일 had spent the past two nights being extra— even obviously—vigilant with the chest to frustrate the thief. Then, tonight, she’d complained of a headache and allowed Setalle to fix her some tea to help her sleep. She’d brought the tea back to her tent, had not taken a sip and now crouched, waiting.

The chest’s corner would be obvious, poking out into the night. Would they try again? As a precaution, she’d removed the Horn from the chest and taken it when she went out to answer the call of nature. She’d hidden it there in a cubby of rock and, upon returning, had put *Cha 파일* on patrol duty for the night, away from her tent. They had not liked leaving her unguarded, but 파일 had made it clear that she was worried about tensions among the men.

That would be enough. Light, let it be enough.

Hours passed with 파일 crouched in that same position, ready to leap up and call the alarm the moment someone tried to enter her tent. Surely they would try again tonight, when she was supposedly ill.

Nothing. Her muscles ached, but she didn’t move. The thief could be out there, in the dark, waiting. Wondering if this was the right moment to strike, to grab the Horn and run off to his or her masters. It—

A scream shattered the night.

파일 wavered. A distraction?

*That scream,* she thought, judging the direction. *It came. . . from just west of here.*

Near where she’d hidden the Horn. 파일 cursed, making a snap decision. The chest was empty. If she took the bait and it really was just a distraction, then she would not lose anything. If, on the other hand, the thief had anticipated her… She darted from the tent as others scrambled from bedrolls. Members of *Cha 파일* raced through the camp. The yell came again.

It was accompanied by a haunting screech, a type that had been following them in the distance.

She crashed through some thin, 황무지-stained weeds. Running through them was a foolish move in a place where a twig could kill, but she was not thinking clearly.

She arrived first on the scene, reaching the area where she’d hidden the Horn. There stood not only Vanin, but Harnan as well. Vanin clutched the 발레르의 뿔 in thick arms while Harnan fought against some kind of beast with dark fur, shouting and swinging his sword.

Vanin looked at 파일 and grew as pale as a Whitecloak’s shirt.

“Thief!” 파일 shouted. “Stop him! He has stolen the 발레르의 뿔!”

Vanin cried out, tossing the Horn as if it had bitten him, then dashing away. Light, but he could move quickly for one of his bulk! He grabbed Harnan by the shoulder, pulling him to the side as the beast screamed that haunting wail.

Other roars came in the distance. 파일 skidded to the ground, grabbing the Horn and clutching it close. These men were no common thieves. They had not only seen through her plan, but anticipated exactly where she’d hidden the Horn. She felt like a farmgirl who had just fallen for a townsman’s three-cup scam.

Those who had come running with her stood stunned, either by the sight of the Horn or the monster. The creature screeched—it looked like some kind of bear with too many arms, though it was larger than any bear 파일 had seen. She stumbled to her feet. There was no time to look for the thieves as the beast smashed its way into 파일’s guards. It ripped the head off a member of *Cha 파일*, screeching.

파일 shouted, flinging a knife at the thing as Arrela hacked at one of its shoulders with her sword. Just then, a *second* beast came lumbering over the rocks next to 파일.

She cursed, leaping away, flinging a knife. She hit it—or, at least, the thing cried out in what sounded like anger and pain. As Mandevwin rode up on horseback, bearing a torch, the light revealed that the horrible things had faces like those of insects, with a multitude of fanglike teeth. 파일’s knife protruded from one bulblike eye.

“Protect the lady!” Mandevwin yelled, throwing spears to nearby Red-arms, who rammed them at the first monster, pushing it back from Arrela—who scrambled away, bleeding. The woman hadn’t lost her sword, though.

파일 fell back as *Cha 파일* organized around her, then looked down at what she held. 발레르의 뿔 itself, pulled from the sack in which she’d hidden it. She could blow it…

*No,* she thought. *It is bound to 카우톤.* To her, it would be just an ordinary horn.

“Steady!” Mandevwin said, dancing his warhorse back as one of the beasts lunged at it. “Verdin, Laandon, we need more spears! Go! The things fight like boars. Draw them forward, impale them!”

The tactic worked on one of the monsters, but as Mandevwin yelled, the other one charged at him and grabbed his horse by the neck. The beast brushed aside soldiers who tried to strike, and Mandevwin crashed to the ground, groaning.

Still clutching the Horn, 파일 dashed past where a group of Redarms had managed to skewer the other beast. She grabbed a freshly lit torch and threw it at the other monster, lighting the fur on its back. The thing bellowed as fire raced up its spine, the fur burning like dry tinder. It dropped Mandevwin’s dead horse, the head ripped nearly free, as it thrashed, yelling and howling.

“Grab the wounded!” 파일 ordered. She took a member of the Band by the arm. “See to Mandevwin!”

The man looked down at the Horn she held, eyes wide, then shook himself and nodded, calling for two others to help him lift the man.

“My Lady?” Aravine asked, standing near the bushes behind. “What is happening?”

“Two Redarms tried to steal what I have been carrying,” 파일 said. “Now we’re going to ride away into the night.”

“But—”

“Listen!” 파일 said, pointing into the darkness.

Distantly, a dozen different screeches sounded, responding to the cries of the dying beast.

“The screams will draw further horrors, as will the scent of spilled blood. We go. If we can get deeply enough into the Blasted 란ds tonight, we might be safe. Rouse the camp and get the wounded onto horses. Prepare everyone else for a forced quick march. Quickly!”

Aravine nodded, scrambling off. 파일 spared a glance in the direction Harnan and Vanin had gone. She longed to hunt them down, but tracking them in the night would require them to move slowly, and that would mean death this night. Besides, who knew what resources a pair of 어둠의 친구들 had access to?

They would flee. And Light, she hoped that she hadn’t been deceived more than it seemed. If Vanin had somehow known to prepare a dummy Horn, a replica to drop and leave for 파일 to “rescue” as he fled…

She’d never know. She’d reach the Last Battle with a fake Horn, and perhaps doom them all. That possibility haunted her as the caravan’s members hastily moved into the darkness, hoping in Light and luck to escape the dangers of the night.

**CHAPTER 36**

*Unchangeable Things*

Something was wrong with 랜드.

니나브 clutched the stalagmite deep within the Pit of Doom, holding herself from being pulled by the winds into that nothingness in front of her. 모이라인 had called it the 어둠의 존재’s essence, but wouldn’t that make it the 진정한 힘? Worse, if his essence was in the world, wouldn’t that mean that he had broken free? Whatever it was, its nature was pure evil, and it filled 니나브 with a terror like none she had ever felt before in her life.

It pulled with a powerful force, drawing all that was nearby into it. She feared that if she let go, she would be yanked in. Already, it had stolen her shawl, making it vanish. If that nothingness pulled her in, her life would end. Perhaps her soul as well.

*랜드!* 니나브 thought. Could she do something to help him? He stood before 모리딘, the two of them locked together, sword against sword. Frozen as if in a moment. Sweat trickled down 랜드’s face. He did not speak. He didn’t so much as blink.

His foot had touched the darkness. At that moment, he had frozen, and so had 모리딘. They were like statues. The air howled around them, but did not seem to affect them as it did 니나브. They’d been standing like that, frozen, for a good fifteen minutes.

All in all, it had been less than an hour since the group of them had entered the pit to face the 어둠의 존재.

니나브 watched rocks slide across the ground, then be sucked into that blackness. Her clothing rippled and flapped as if in a strong wind, as did 모이라인 s, who huddled nearby holding to her own tooth of stone. Mercifully, the stench of sulfur that had filled the cavern was drawn away here into the blackness.

She couldn’t use the 하나의 힘. 랜드 drew every bit of it she could hold, though he didn't seem to be doing anything with it. Could she reach 모리딘? He didn’t seem to be able to move. What if she took a rock to his head? It would be better than waiting.

니나브 tested her weight against the pull of the nothingness ahead, relaxing her grip on the stalagmite. She immediately started to slip, and pulled herself back.

*I am* not *spending the Last Battle dinging to a rock!* she thought. *Not the same one the whole time, at the very least.* She had to risk moving. Going directly forward seemed too dangerous, but if she moved sideways… yes, there was another stalagmite nearby to her right. She managed to let go of her hold and half-slip, half-scuttle to the next stalagmite. From there, she picked out another one, carefully eased off her hold and grabbed it instead.

The process was very slow. *랜드, you wool-headed fool,* she thought. If he’d let her or 모이라인 lead the circle, then maybe they could have done something while he was fighting!

She reached another stalagmite, then stopped as she saw something to her right. She almost screamed. A *woman* huddled there, hidden against the wall, sheltered from the wind by the rocks. She appeared to be crying.

니나브 glanced at 랜드, who was still locked in stasis with 모리딘, then approached the woman. The greater number of stalagmites here meant that 니나브 could crawl more safely, the stones blocking the pull of the nothingness.

니나브 reached the woman. She was chained to the wall. “Alanna?” 니나브 shouted over the wind. “Light, what are you doing here?”

The 에스 세다이 blinked reddened eyes at 니나브. Her eyes stared dully, as if she had no mind. As 니나브 examined the woman, she noticed that the entire left side of Alanna’s body was bloodied from a knife wound to the gut. Light! 니나브 should have known that from the paleness of the woman’s face.

Why stab her and leave her here? *She bonded 랜드,* 니나브 realized. *Oh, Light.* It was a trap. 모리딘 had left Alanna bleeding, then confronted 랜드. When Alanna died, 랜드—as her 감시자—would be driven mad with rage, making him easy for 모리딘 to destroy.

Why hadn’t he noticed? 니나브 fished at her pouches for herbs, then stopped short. Could herbs do anything at this point? She needed to use the 하나의 힘 to Heal such a wound. 니나브 ripped the woman’s clothing, making a bandage, then tried to draw *세다르* for 치유.

랜드 had it, and he wouldn’t let go. Frantic, she tried to batter him away, but 랜드 held tight. Tighter, as she tried to push against him. He *did* seem to be channeling it, somehow, but she couldn’t see the weaves. She could feel something, but with the howling wind and the strange nature of the pit, it was like a tempest swirling around her. The Power was wrapped up in that somehow.

Blast it! She needed *세다르!* It wasn’t 랜드’s fault. He could not give her any power while leading the circle.

니나브 pressed her hand against Alanna’s wound, feeling helpless. Dared she call for 랜드 to release her from the circle? If she did, 모리딘 would undoubtedly turn on her and attack Alanna.

What to do? If this woman died, 랜드 would lose control. That, likely, would be the end of him… and of the Last Battle.

맷 hacked at the wood with his axe to sharpen it to a point. “See,” he said, “it doesn’t need to be fancy. Save your pretty carpentry to impress the mayor’s daughter.”

The watching men and women nodded with grim determination. They were farmers, villagers and craftsmen, like people he’d known back in the 두 강. 맷 had thousands of them under his command. He’d never have suspected that there would be so many. The good people of the land had come to fight.

맷 figured they were insane, to a person. If he had been able to escape, he would be hiding in a basement somewhere. Burn him, but he would have tried.

Those dice rattled in his head, just as they’d been doing ever since 에그웨인 gave him control of all of the armies of the Light. Being bloody *타베렌* was not worth two beans.

He kept at it, shaping his stake for the palisade. One fellow watched particularly carefully, an old farmer with skin so leathery that 트롤록 swords would likely just bounce off. He looked familiar to 맷 for some reason.

*Burn these memories,* 맷 thought. Undoubtedly, this fellow resembled someone from one of those old memories 맷 had been given. Yes, that felt right. He could not *quite* remember. A… cart? A 페이드?

“Come on, Renald,” the fellow said to one of his companions—another farmer, Borderlander stock from the looks of him. “Let’s go on down the line, and see if we can hurry the other lads up.”

The two headed off as 맷 finished his stake, then wiped his brow. He reached for another length of wood—he had better give these sheepherders another demonstration—when a *cadin’sor*-clad figure ran up along the mostly finished palisade wall.

Urien had bright red hair, kept short save for the tail in the back. He raised a hand to 맷 as he passed. “They are agitated, 매트림 카우톤,” Urien said, not stopping. “I believe they are coming in this direction.”

“Thanks,” 맷 called. “I owe you.”

The 아일 turned as he ran, jogging backward for a second and facing 맷. “Just win this battle! I have bet a skin of *oosquai* upon our success.”

맷 snorted. The only thing more discomforting than a stoic 아일 was a grinning one. Bet? On the outcome of this battle? What kind of bet was that? If they lost, nobody would live long enough to collect…

맷 frowned. Actually, that was a pretty *good* bet to be making. “Who did you find to take that bet?” 맷 called. “Urien?” But the man was already too far away to hear.

맷 grumbled, but handed his axe to one of the people nearby, a slender 타이런 woman. “Keep them in line, Cynd.”

“Yes, Lord 카우톤.”

“I’m no bloody lord,” 맷 said by habit as he picked up his *ashandarei.* He walked off, then turned to look at the palisade being erected and caught sight of a handful of 죽음감시대s walking along the rows of working people. Like wolves among the sheep. 맷 hurried on.

His armies did not have much time left to prepare. Using gateways had put them ahead of the 트롤록s, but they had not escaped. Light, there *was* no escape. 맷 had been given his choice of battlefields, though, and this Merrilor place would work best.

*Like picking the plot for your own grave,* 맷 thought. *Sure*, *I’d rather not have to choose in the first place.*

The palisade was rising in front of the woods east of the field. He did not have time to section off or surround the entire area with a palisade, and doing so would not make much sense anyway. With those Sharan channelers, the Shadow could rip through walls like a sword through silk. But some palisades, with catwalks on top, would give his archers height to target 트롤록s.

맷 had two rivers to work with here. The River Mora flowed in a southwest direction, running between the Heights and Dashar Knob. Its southern bank was in 시엔나르, the northern bank in 아라펠. It joined the River Erinin, which ran directly westward at the southern edge of the field.

Those rivers would serve better than any walls, particularly now that he had the resources to defend them correctly. Well, if you could call them resources. Half his soldiers were as new as spring grass and the other half had fought near to death the week before. The Borderlanders had lost two men out of three—Light, two out of *three.* A lesser army would have disbanded.

Counting everyone he had, 맷 would be outnumbered four to one when those 트롤록s arrived, at least according to the reports from the Fists of Heaven. It was going to be messy.
맷 pulled his hat down further, then scratched at the side of the new eyepatch that 투온 had given him. Red leather. He liked it.

“Here now,” he said, passing some of the new Tower Guard recruits. They were sparring with quarterstaffs—spearheads were still being forged to go on the ends. The men looked more likely to hurt themselves than the enemy.

맷 handed his *ashandarei* to a man, then took a quarterstaff from another as the first hastily saluted. Most of these men were not old enough to need to shave more than once a month. If the boy whose staff he had taken was a day over fifteen, 맷 would eat his boots. He would not even boil them first!

“You cant cringe every time the staff hits something!” 맷 said. “Close your eyes on the battlefield, and you’re dead. Didn’t you lot pay any attention last time?”

맷 held up the staff, showing them where to grip it, then put them through the blocking practice his father had shown him back when he had been young enough to think fighting might actually be fun. He worked up a sweat, hitting at each of the new recruits in turn, forcing each to block.

“Burn me, but you *will* figure this out,” 맷 said loudly to all of them. “I wouldn’t care so much, as you lot seem to have the wits of stumps, but if you get yourselves killed, your mothers will be expecting me to send them word. I won’t do it, mind you. But I might feel a little guilty between games of dice, and I hate feeling guilty, so pay attention!”

“Lord 카우톤?” said the lad who had given him the staff.

“I’m not—” He stopped. “Well, yes, what is it?”

“Can’t we just learn the sword?”

“Light!” 맷 said. “What’s your name?”

“Sigmont, sir.”

“Well, Sigmont, how much time do you think we have? Maybe you could wander out, talk to the Dreadlords and the 그림자태생 and ask them to give me a few more months’ time so I can train you all properly.”

Sigmont blushed, and 맷 handed back his staff. *City boys.* He sighed.

“Look here, all I want is for you lot to be able to defend yourselves. I don’t have time to make you great warriors, but I *can* teach you to work together, keep a formation, and not shy away when the 트롤록s come. That will get you farther than any kind of fancy swordplay, trust me.”

The youths nodded reluctantly.

“Get back to your practice,” 맷 said, wiping his brow and looking over his shoulder. Bloody ashes! The 죽음감시대s were heading his way.

He grabbed his *ashandarei* and rushed off, then ducked around the side of a tent, only to stumble into a group of 에스 세다이 approaching on the path.

“맷?” 에그웨인 asked from the middle of the group of women. “Are you well?”

“They’re bloody chasing me,” he said, glancing around the side of the tent. “Who is chasing you?” 에그웨인 said.

“죽음감시대s,” 맷 said. “I’m supposed to be back at 투온’s tent.” 에그웨인 waved a few fingers, sending the other women off, except her two shadows—가윈 and that 쇼엔찬 woman—who remained with her. “맷,” 에그웨인 said in a suffering tone, “I’m glad you’ve finally decided to see reason and leave the 쇼엔찬 camp, but couldn’t you have waited until *after* the battle was over to defect?”

“Sorry,” he said, only half-listening. “But can we walk on toward the 에스 세다이 quarter of camp? They won’t follow me there.” Maybe not. If all 죽음감시대s were like 카레데, maybe they would. 카레데 would dive after a man falling off a cliff in order to catch him.

에그웨인 started back, seeming displeased with 맷. How was it 에스 세다이 could be so perfectly emotionless, yet still let a man know they disapproved of him? Come to think of it, an 에스 세다이 would probably follow a man off a cliff, too, if only to explain to him—in detail—all the things he was doing incorrectly in the way he went about killing himself.

맷 wished so many of his thoughts lately did not involve feeling like he was the one jumping off the cliff.

“We’ll have to find a way to explain to Fortuona why you ran,” 에그웨인 said as they approached the 에스 세다이 quarter. 맷 had placed it as far from the 쇼엔찬 as was reasonable. “The marriage is going to present a problem. I suggest that you—”

“Wait, 에그웨인,” 맷 said. “What are you talking about?”

“You are running from the 쇼엔찬 guards,” 에그웨인 said. “Weren’t you listening ... Of course you weren’t. It is pleasant to know that, as the world crumbles, a few things are completely unchangeable. *퀜딜라* and 맷 카우톤.”

“I’m running from them,” 맷 said, looking over his shoulder, “because 투온 wants me to sit in judgment. Any time a soldier is seeking the 여제’s mercy for a crime, *I’m* the one who is supposed to bloody hear his case!”

“You,” 에그웨인 said, “passing judgment?”

“I know,” 맷 said. “Too much bloody work, if you ask me. I’ve been dodging guardsmen all day, trying to steal a little time for myself.”

“A little honest work wouldn’t kill you, 맷.”

“Now, you know that’s not true. 병사ing is honest work, and it gets men killed all the bloody time.”

가윈 Trakand was apparently practicing to be an 에스 세다이 sometime, because he kept giving 맷 glares that would have made 모이라인 proud. Well, let him. 가윈 was a prince. He had been raised to do things like pass judgment. He probably sent a few men to the gallows each day at his lunch break, just to keep in practice.

But 맷… 맷 was not going to order men to be executed, and that was that. They passed a group of 아일 sparring together. Was this group what Urien had been running to reach? Once they had passed—맷 trying to make the others walk faster so the 쇼엔찬 would not catch up—he drew closer to 에그웨인.

“Have you found it yet?” he asked softly.

“No,” 에그웨인 said, eyes forward.

No need to mention what *it* was. “How could you have lost the thing? After all the work we bloody went through to find it?”

“We? From the telling I hear, 랜드, 로이알 and the Borderlanders had far more to do with finding it than you.”

“I was there,” 맷 said. “I rode across the entire bloody continent, didn’t I? Burn me, first 랜드, then you. Is everybody going to chivvy me about those days? 가윈, you want a turn?”

“Yes, please.” He sounded eager.

“Shut up,” 맷 said. “It seems that nobody can remember straight but me. I hunted down that bloody Horn like a madman. And, I’ll mention, it was me blowing the thing that let you all escape Falme.”

“Is that how you remember it?” 에그웨인 asked.

“Sure,” 맷 said. “I mean, I have some holes in there, but I’ve pieced it mostly together.”

“And the dagger?”

“That trinket? Hardly worth anyone’s time.” He caught himself reaching to his side, to where he had once carried it. 에그웨인 raised an eyebrow at him. “Anyway, thats not the point. We're going to need that bloody instrument, 에그웨인. We’ll *need* it.”

“We have people searching,” she said. “We’re not sure exactly what happened. There was a 이동 residue, but it’s been a while and… Light, 맷. We’re trying. I promise it. It’s not the only thing the Shadow has stolen from us recently…”

He glanced at her, but she gave him no more. Flaming 에스 세다이. “Has anyone seen 페린 yet?” he asked. “I don’t want to be the one to tell him his wife has gone missing.”

“Nobody has seen him,” 에그웨인 said. “I assume he is at work helping 랜드.”

“Bah,” 맷 said. “Can you make a gateway for me up to the top of the Knob?”

“I thought you wanted to go to my camp.”

Its on the way, 맷 said. Well, sort of, it was. “And those 죽음감시대s won’t expect it. Burn me, 에그웨인, but I think they’ve guessed where we were heading.”

에그웨인 after pausing for a moment—opened them a gateway to the 이동 ground atop the Knob. They stepped through onto it.

More than a hill, less than a mountain, Dashar Knob rose a good hundred feet into the air near the middle of the battlefield. The rock formation was unscalable, and gateways were the only way to reach the top. From here, 맷 and his commanders would be able to watch the entire battle play out.

“I have never known anyone else,” 에그웨인 said to him, “who will work so hard to avoid hard work, 매트림 카우톤.”

“You haven’t spent enough time around soldiers.” 맷 waved at the men who saluted him as he walked out of the 이동 grounds.

He looked north toward the River Mora and across it into 아라펠. Then northeast, toward the ruins of what had once been some kind of fort or watchtower. Eastward, toward the rising palisade and the forest. He continued to turn, southward to gaze at the River Erinin in the far distance, and the strange little grove of tall trees that 로이알 was so in awe of. They said 랜드 had grown those, during the meeting where the treaty had been signed. 맷 looked southwest toward the only good ford on the Mora nearby, named Hawal Ford by the locals who had farmed this area; beyond the ford on the 아라펠 side was a large expanse of bogs.

Westward, across the Mora, lay Polov Heights—a forty-foot-tall plateau with a steep slope on the east and more gradual slopes on the other sides.

Between the base of the southwestern slope and the bogs was a corridor roughly two hundred paces across, well worn by travelers who used the ford to cross between 아라펠 and 시엔나르. 맷 could use these features to his advantage. He could use them all. Would that be enough? He could feel something pulling on him, tugging him northward. 랜드 would need him soon.

He turned, ready to bolt, as someone approached across the top of the Knob, but it was not the 죽음감시대s. It was just leather-faced Jur Grady.

“I fetched those soldiers for you,” Grady said, pointing. 맷 could see a small force coming through a gateway to the 이동 grounds near the palisade. A hundred men of the Band, led by Delarn, flying a bloody red flag. The Redarms were accompanied by some five hundred people in worn clothing.

“What was the point of this?” Grady asked. “You sent those hundred to a village in the south to recruit, I assume?”

That, and more. *I saved your life, man,* 맷 thought, trying to pick Delarn out of the group. *And then you volunteer for this. Bloody fool.* Delarn acted as if it were his fate.

“Take them upriver,” 맷 said. “The maps show there is only one good place to block the Mora, a narrow canyon a few leagues northeast of here.”

“All right,” Grady said. “There will be channelers involved.”

“You will have to handle them,” 맷 said. “Mostly, though, I want you to let those six hundred men and women defend the river. Don’t risk your self too much. Let Delarn and his people do the work.”

“Pardon,” Grady said. “But that doesn’t seem like a very large force. Most of them aren’t trained soldiers.”

“I know what I’m doing,” 맷 said. *I hope.*

Grady nodded reluctantly and moved off.

에그웨인 watched 맷 with curious eyes.

“We can’t fall back from this fight,” 맷 said softly. “We don’t retreat. There isn’t anywhere to go. We stand here, or we lose it all.”

“There is *always* a retreat,” 에그웨인 said.

“No,” 맷 said. “Not anymore.” He rested his *ashandarei* on his shoulder, his other hand out, palm forward. He scanned the landscape, memories appearing as if from light and dust before him. Rion at Hune Hill. Naath and the San d’ma Shadar. The Fall of Pipkin. Hundreds upon hundreds of battlefields, hundreds of victories. Thousands of deaths.

맷 watched figments of memories flash across the field. “Have you spoken to the supply masters? We’re out of food, 에그웨인. We can’t win a protracted war, fighting and falling back. The enemy will overwhelm us if we do that. Just like Eyal in the Marches of Maighande. We are at our strongest now, broken though we are. Fall back, and we resign ourselves to starvation as the 트롤록s destroy us.”

“랜드,” 에그웨인 said. “We just have to hold out until he is victorious.”

“That’s true in a fashion,” 맷 said, turning toward the Heights. In his mind’s eye, he saw what could come, the possibilities. He imagined riders on the Heights, like shadows. He would lose if he tried to hold those Heights, but maybe… “If 랜드 loses, it won’t matter. 수레바퀴 is bloody broken, and we all become nothing, if we’re lucky. Well, we can’t do anything more about it. But here’s the thing. If he does what he’s supposed to, we could still lose—we will lose, if we don’t stop the Shadow’s armies.” He blinked, seeing it, the entire battlefield spread before him. Fighting at the ford. Arrows from the palisade. “We can’t just beat them, 에그웨인,” 맷 said. “We can’t just stand and hold on. We have to destroy them, drive them away, then hunt them to the last 트롤록. We can’t just survive ... we have to *win.”*

“How are we going to do that?” 에그웨인 asked. “맷, you’re not talking sense. Weren’t you just saying yesterday how outnumbered we’ll be?”

He looked toward the bog, imagining shadows trying to slog through it. Shadows of dust and memory. “I have to change it all,” he said. He could not do what they would expect. He could not do what spies might have reported he was planning. “Blood and bloody ashes… one last toss of the dice. Everything we have, piled into a heap…”

A group of men in dark armor came through a gateway to the top of the Knob, panting deeply, as if they’d had to chase down a *다만* to get them up here. Their breastplates were lacquered a deep red, but this batch did not need a fearsome display to be frightening. They looked furious enough to scramble eggs with a stare.

“You,” said the lead 죽음감시대, a man named Gelen, pointing at 맷, “are *needed* at the—”

맷 held up a hand to cut him off.

“I will not be denied again!” Gelen said. “I have orders from—”

맷 shot the man a glare, and he stopped short. 맷 turned northward again. A cool, somehow *familiar* wind blew across him, rippling his long coat, brushing at his hat. He narrowed his eye. 랜드 was tugging on him.

The dice still tumbled in his head.

“They’re here,” 맷 said.

“What did you say?” 에그웨인 asked.

“They’re here.”

“The scouts—”

“The scouts are wrong” 맷 said. He looked up, and noticed a pair of *raken* speeding back toward the camp. They had seen it. The 트롤록s must have marched through the night.

*Sharans will come first,* 맷 thought, *to give the 트롤록s a breather. They’ll have arrived through gateways.*

“Send runners,” 맷 said, pointing at the 죽음감시대s, “get the men and women to their posts. And warn 엘레인 that I’m going to change the battle plan.”

“What?” 에그웨인 said.

“They’re *here!*” 맷 said, turning on the Guards. “Why aren’t you bloody running! Go, *go!”* Above, the *raken* screeched. Gelen, to his credit, saluted, then ran—pounding in that massive armor—with his companions.

페린 drifted in darkness. He felt so *tired.*

*Slayer still lives,* a piece of himself thought. *그랜달 is corrupting the great captains. The end is near. You can’t slip away now! Hold on.*

Hold on to what? He tried to open his eyes, but was so exhausted. He should.… should have gotten out of the wolf dream sooner. His entire body felt numb, except…

Except for his side. Moving fingers that felt like bricks, he touched the warmth. His hammer. It was blazing hot. That warmth seemed to move up his fingers, and 페린 took a deep breath.

He needed to wake up. He hovered at the edges of consciousness, as when he was close to sleep, but still partially aware. In that state, he felt as if he faced a forked pathway before him. One path led deeper into darkness. And one led… He couldn’t see, but he knew that it meant ... It meant waking up.

Warmth from the hammer radiated up his arm. His mind gathered sharpness. *Awaken.*

That was what Slayer had done. He had… awakened… somehow…

페린’s life was trickling away. Not much time left. Half within death’s embrace, he gritted his teeth, drew in a deep breath and forced himself to *wake.*

The silence of the wolf dream shattered.

페린 hit soft earth, and entered a place of shouts. Something about a battlefront, about preparing the lines…

Nearby, someone cried out. And then someone else. And others. “페린?” He knew that voice. “페린, lad!”

루한 장인? 페린’s eyelids felt so heavy. He couldn’t open them. Arms grabbed him.

“Hang on. I have you, lad. I have you. *Hang on.”*

“Uh…” Uno said.

“That question wasn’t intended for you,” she said, scanning the sky. “Einar! Why didn’t you spot those weaves?”

A line of light split the air behind them. It was enormous, as long as the keep of 팔 다라. It rotated upon itself, opening a vast gateway that split the ground at the center of the Heights. Standing on the other side was a man in brilliant armor made of silver, coinlike rings, his helmetless head bearing dark hair and a strong nose. He held before him a scepter of gold, the top shaped like an hourglass or a fine goblet.

Kwamesa reacted immediately, raising her hand and releasing a stream of fire. The man waved his hand, and the stream of fire deflected; then he pointed—almost indifferently—and something thin, hot and *white* connected him to Kwamesa. Her form glowed, and then she was gone, motes drifting toward the ground.

Uno jumped away, Einar joining him as he rolled behind the rubble of a broken dragon.

A bar of white-hot light cut through the broken dragon, vaporizing it and striking Einar. The man was gone in an instant, and Uno scrambled back, cursing. He ducked away as the wreckage of dragons crashed to the ground around him.

로가인 Ablar released the 하나의 힘. He stood beside the Mora, below the Heights, and felt the attacks up above.

Releasing the 하나의 힘 today was one of the most difficult things he’d ever done. More difficult than the decision to name himself Dragon, more difficult than keeping himself from strangling 타임 during their early days together in the 검은 탑.

“로가인?” 안드롤 asked.

로가인 turned his head toward the shorter man and his companions. They were loyal. 로가인 didn’t know why, but they were loyal. The whole lot of them. Fools. Faithful fools.

It didn’t matter if those men channeling were Sharans. The Asha’man would help this battle by removing enemy channelers anyway. They had discussed the tactic earlier. When they sensed channeling from men, they could use gateway jumps to pinpoint where they were, then try to surprise them and attack.

Be wary that he might be carrying the seals; it would not do to destroy them in our attack. If you see him, return and bring me word of his location.”

가브렐 looked at 로가인 with level eyes. “What of Toveine?” she asked.

“We will kill her if we find her.”

“It is that simple for you?”

“Yes.”

“She—”

“Would you rather live, 가브렐, if you were she? Live and serve *him?”*

She closed her mouth, lips drawn tight. She still feared him; he could sense that. Good.

*Was this what you wished for,* his mind whispered, *when you raised the banner of the Dragon? When you sought to save mankind? Did you do it to be feared? Hated?*

디만드레드’s channeling radiated strength. Such *power.*

He used his *angreal* to draw more, and then the Power from the others streamed into him. He laughed louder.

가윈 felt so tired. This week of preparation would normally have rested him, but he felt today as if he’d hiked for tens of leagues.

“That sounds exactly like something 맷 would do,” 에그웨인 said, resigned.

“The strength of those weaves,” Lelaine said, “that *power*…”

“디만드레드 is in a circle,” 에그웨인 said. “Eyewitnesses say a full circle. Something that hasn’t been seen since the 전설의 시대. And he has a *sa’angreal.* Some of the soldiers saw it—a scepter.”

가윈 watched the fighting far below, his hand on his sword. He could hear men scream as 디만드레드 aimed wave after wave of fire at them.

The 버림받은 자들’s voice boomed, suddenly, reaching high into the air. “Where are you, 르웨어스 테린! You were seen at each of the other battlefields in disguise. Are you here, too? Fight me!”

가윈’s hand tightened on his sword. 병사s flooded down the southwestern side of the Heights, to cross the ford. A few small groups held on the slopes, and dragoners there—tiny as insects to 가윈—led the remaining dragons to safety, pulled by mules.

디만드레드 flung destruction at the fleeing troops. He was an army unto himself, hurling bodies into the air, exploding horses, burning and destroying. Around him, his 트롤록s seized the high ground. Their brutish cheers floated through the gateway.

Killing thousands. And here they stood.

가윈 stepped back.

Nobody seemed to notice his withdrawal other than 유키리, who eagerly stepped up and took his place beside 에그웨인. 가윈 slipped out of the tent, and when the tent guards glanced at him, said he needed some fresh air. 에그웨인 would approve. She sensed how tired he was lately; she’d mentioned it to him several times. His eyelids felt as if they had weights of iron pulling them down. 가윈 looked toward the blackened sky He could hear the distant booms. How long would he just stand around and do nothing while men died?

*You promised,* he thought to himself. *You said you were willing to stand in her shadow.*
That didn’t mean he had to stop doing important work, did it? He fished in his pouch and took out a ring of the 피의 칼날. He put it on, and immediately his strength returned, his exhaustion fleeing.

He hesitated, then took out the other rings and slipped them on as well.

On the south bank of the River Mora, in front of the ruins northeast of Dashar Knob, Tam al’Thor summoned the void as Kimtin had taught him all of those years ago. Tam imagined the single flame, and poured his emotions into it. He grew calm, then the calmness left him, leaving nothing. Like a newly painted wall, beautiful and white, that had just been washed. Everything melted away.

Tam was the void. He drew his bow, the good black yew bending, arrow to his cheek. He took aim, but this was only a formality. When he was this strongly within the void, the arrow would do exactly as he commanded. He didn’t *know* this, any more than the sun knew that it would rise or the branches knew that their leaves would fall. These were not things *known\* they were things that *were.*

Tam’s arrow hit a 페이드 right where its eyes should have been. Nearby, a large man named Bayrd whistled in appreciation, leaning on his axe and watching the arrows fall. He was part of the group of soldiers set just behind the archers to move in and protect them, once the 트롤록s were forced to cross.

Bayrd was one of the mercenary leaders who had drifted into the army, and though he was an 안도르an, neither he nor the hundred or so men he led would speak of where they’d come from. “I need to get one of those bows,” Bayrd said to his companions. “Burn me, do you *see* that?”

Nearby, Abell and Azi smiled, continuing to shoot. Tam did not smile. There was no humor within the void, though outside of the void, a thought did flutter. Tam knew why Abell and Azi had smiled. Having a 두 강 bow did not make one into a 두 강 archer.

Five more 트롤록s dead. In all, he’d loosed over thirty arrows. He’d missed once, but only because Abell had killed the 트롤록 that Tam had aimed for.

*페린, youd better heal up strong.* When Haral had found the boy lying in the grass on the outskirts of camp the day before, bloodied and near death… Light, that had given them all a fright.

페린 was safely in Mayene, where he would likely spend the rest of the Last Battle. A man didn’t quickly recover from the type of wound the lad had taken, even with 에스 세다이 치유. It would probably drive 페린 near mad to miss the fighting, but sometimes that happened. It was part of being a soldier.

Arrows started to fly from the 트롤록s on the other bank toward 갈라드 and his men. The clanks and pings of arrowheads on the Whitecloak armor and shields sounded like hail on a roof. Tam ordered Arganda to bring in their foot soldiers, including Bayrd and the mercenaries.

Thick 트롤록 arrows sprayed around 페바라 as she desperately wove Air. Her gust blew away the arrows like stones swept off the board by a furious player. Sweating, she clung to *세다르* and wove a stronger shield of Air, moving it into the sky to defend against further volleys.

*Here,* she sent him. Not completely a thought, more an image, a sense of place.

A gateway split beside her, and he dashed through, 에마린 on his heels. Both men carried swords, but 에마린 spun and thrust his hand backward, a streak of fire shooting through the open gateway. Screaming sounded from the other side. Human screaming.

*I heard that,* 안드롤 sent her. “에마린, to me. 페바라 Sedai, if you’d graciously agree to accompany us…”

She sniffed, but joined the other two as they moved along the southwestern base of the Heights, passing some wounded stumbling toward the rallying point. 안드롤 glanced at them, then wove a gateway back to their camp. The flagging men cried out in surprise and thanks, and shambled through it to safety.

안드롤 had grown… more confident since they had left the 검은 탑. When they’d first met, he’d displayed hesitation about whatever he did. A kind of nervous humility. No more.

“안드롤 . . ” 에마린 said, pointing up the slope with his sword.

“I see them,” 안드롤 said. Above, 트롤록s poured over the top of the Heights like pitch boiling over the side of a pot. Behind, 안드롤’s gateway closed, that group of soldiers safe. Others cried out as they saw it close.

The three of them moved through the soldiers, angling toward several channelers they could feel ahead. Jonneth, Canler and Theodrin were there, throwing fire at groups of 트롤록s. Their position was being overrun.

Jonneth and the others followed, joining them as the group dashed past a group of startled 트롤록s.

안드롤 opened another gateway for them as a few bursts of flame came from the direction of some Sharans atop the Heights. 페바라 ran through, beginning to pant. They appeared on the other side of the Sharans, who were firing at where 페바라 had been moments before.

He had tried making those Deathgates that the other Asha’man used, but the weave was apparently just different enough that he had trouble. Instead, he stuck to what he was good at doing.

Thousands upon thousands of 트롤록s howled, most at the edges of the Heights, loosing arrows on those below. Despite practice over the last few months, Tam wasn’t nearly as strong as he had been in his youth. Fortunately, a reed did not need strength. He was not as practiced as he once had been, but no reed practiced how to bend in the wind.

It simply *did.*

Years of maturing, years of age, had brought Tam an understanding of the void. He understood it now, better than he ever had. Years teaching 랜드 responsibility, years of living without Kari, years of listening to the wind blow and the leaves rustle…

Tam al’Thor became the void. He brought it to the 트롤록s, showed it to them and sent them into its depths.

He danced around a goat-featured 트롤록, sweeping his sword to the side and slicing the beasts leg at the heel. It stumbled and Tam turned, letting the men behind take it. He flashed his sword up—the weapon trailing blood—and sprayed the dark droplets across the eyes of a charging 트롤록 with nightmare features. It howled, blinded, and Tam flowed forward, arms out, and opened its stomach below the breastplate. It stumbled in front of a third 트롤록, who brought an axe down toward Tam, but hit its ally instead.

Each step was part of a dance, and Tam invited the 트롤록s to join him. He had only fought like this once before, long ago, but memory was something that the void did not allow. He did not think of other times; he did not think of anything. If he knew that he’d done this once before, it was because of the resonance of his motions, an understanding that seemed to permeate his muscles themselves.

Tam stabbed the neck of a 트롤록 with a face that was nearly human, with only a little too much hair on its cheeks. It fell backward and collapsed, and Tam suddenly found no more foes. He stopped, bringing his sword up, feeling a soft wind blow across him. The dark beasts were thundering away downriver in a rout, chased by horsemen flying Borderlander flags. Shortly they would hit a wall of troops, the Legion of the Dragon, and be crushed between them and the pursuing Borderlanders.

Tam cleaned his blade, leaving the void. The gravity of the situation hit him. Light! His men should be dead. If those Borderlanders hadn’t arrived…

He placed his sword back into its lacquered sheath. The red and gold dragon caught sunlight, sparkling, though Tam wouldn’t have thought there was anything to catch with that cloud cover above. He searched for the sun, and found it—behind the clouds—nearly at the horizon. It was almost night!

Fortunately, it looked like the 트롤록s here at the battle by the ruins were finally breaking. Already weakened severely by the drawn-out river crossing, they now crumbled as 란’s men hit them from behind.

In a short time it was done. Tam had held.

Nearby, a black horse trotted up. Its rider, 란 Mandragoran—with standard-bearer and guards behind—looked over the 두 강 men.

“I had long wondered,” 란 said to Tam. “About the man who had given 랜드 that heron-marked blade. I wondered if he had truly earned it. Now I know.” 란 raised his own sword in salute.

Tam turned back toward his men, an exhausted, bloodied group clutching weapons. The path of their wedge showed easily on the trampled plain; dozens of 트롤록s lay behind where the wedge had cut into them. To the north, the men of the second wedge raised their weapons. They had been pushed back nearly to the forest, but they’d held there and some had survived. Tam couldn’t help but see that dozens of good folk had died.

His exhausted men sat down right there on the battlefield, surrounded by corpses. Some weakly began tying their own bandages or seeing to the wounded they’d pulled into the interior of the wedge. To the south, Tam spotted a dismaying sight. Were those the 쇼엔찬 pulling out from their camp at Dashar Knob?

“Have we won, then?” Tam asked.

“Far from it,” 란 said. “We’ve seized this part of the river, but it is the lesser fight. 디만드레드 pressed his 트롤록s hard here to keep us from drawing resources to the larger battle at the ford downriver.” 란 turned his horse. “Gather your men, blademaster. This battle will not end with the setting sun. You will be needed again in the coming hours. *Tai’shar Manetheren”*

란 thundered toward his Borderlanders.

“No, lad. We're not. But we’ll take a break, get the men Healed and find some food.” He saw gateways opening beside the field. 카우톤 had been smart enough to send a means for Tam to take his wounded to Mayene. It—

People poured through the openings. Hundreds of them, thousands. Tam frowned. Nearby, the 백의단 were picking themselves up—they’d been hit hard by the 트롤록 attacks, but Tam’s arrival had kept them from being destroyed. Arganda’s force was forming up at the ruins, and the Wolf Guard hoisted their flag high, bloodied, heaps of 트롤록 corpses surrounding them.

Others began picking through the fallen, looking for signs of those people who were still alive and could be Healed. Women and children began to pick arrows out from among the fallen. That would be helpful. *Very* helpful. With surprise, Tam saw hundreds of Tinkers pour out of one gateway. They went searching for the wounded under the direction of several Yellow sisters.

Tam found himself nodding. It still worried him, allowing the children to see such sights. *Well,* he thought, *they’ll see a worse sight if we fail here.* If they wanted to be of use, they should be allowed.

“Tell me, Tam al’Thor,” Berelain asked, “is… 갈라드 Damodred well?”

“Ah. Well, let’s Heal and feed your men. Perhaps word of Lord Damodred will be forthcoming.”

Right now though, 엘레인, you need to shut your mouth and let me protect you.”

She was right. Burn her, she was. 엘레인 hung on as 비르기테 galloped across the battlefield, her horse churning clods of dirt behind them in a flight toward safety.

*At least he’s making it easy to find him,* 갈라드 thought as he rode, watching the lines of fire streak from the enemy position toward 엘레인’s army.

갈라드’s heels dug into the flanks of his stolen horse, tearing across the Heights toward its eastern edge. Over and over, he saw 가윈’s dying body in his arms.

디만드레드 came at him, and the contest began.

Her back pressed against a stalagmite, seeing only by the light of *칼란도르* reflected against the walls of the cavern, 니나브 worked to save Alanna’s life.

If any of those women had been here instead of 니나브, the world would have ended.
The conditions were horrible. Little light, no tools besides the implements she kept in her pouch. Still, 니나브 sewed, using the needle and thread she always carried. She had mixed a draught of herbs for Alanna and forced it through her lips. It wouldn’t do much, but every little bit might help. It would keep Alanna’s strength up, help her with the pain, keep her heart from giving out as 니나브 worked.

The wound was messy, but she had sewn messy wounds before. Though she trembled inside, 니나브’s hands were steady as she sewed up the wound and coaxed the woman back from the very precipice of death.

랜드 and 모리딘 did not move. But she felt something thrumming from them. 랜드 was fighting. Fighting a fight she could not see.

“매트림 카우톤, you bloody fool. You’re still alive?”

맷 glanced over as 다브람 바쉐어 rode up beside him in the early evening darkness. 맷 had moved with the 죽음감시대 to the back of the 안도르an lines fighting at the river.

맷 nodded. At Tenobia’s fall, this man had become king of 살다에아— but he had refused the crown, so far. The corruption in his mind had shaken him. *Bloody ashes,* 맷 thought. *Poor 페린.*

Poor him. How was he going to do this without the Horn? Light. He was not certain he could do it *with* the bloody Horn.

He heeled Pips into motion, the 오지어 falling in around him and the 죽음감시대s. The 오지어 had no trouble keeping up.

No colors formed, only blackness. Dark as a 미르드랄’s heart. The tugging grew stronger.

맷 dismissed the vision. *Not. Now.*

He had work to do here. He had a plan. Light, let it work.

Tinna turned out to be a pretty girl, younger than he had expected, tall and strong of limb. She wore her long brown hair in a tail, though curls of it seemed to want to break out here and there. “Yes, I did ”

And now… now he had a chance to finish this. 엘레인’s forces holding along the river, 에그웨인 fighting in the west… 맷 had to seize the northern part of the Heights. He knew that with the 쇼엔찬 gone and most of his own troops occupied around the lower part of the Heights, 디만드레드 would send a strong force of Sharans and 트롤록s across the top to the northeast, to swing down across the riverbed and behind 엘레인’s armies. The armies of Light would be surrounded and at 디만드레드’s mercy. His only chance was to keep 디만드레드’s troops from coming off the Heights, despite their superior numbers. Light. It was a long shot, but sometimes you had to take the only shot you had.

“If 랜드 were dead,” 맷 said, “we’d know it. He’ll have to watch out for himself, without 매트림 카우톤 saving him this time. Teslyn, let’s have that gateway! Tinna, organize your forces. Have them ready to charge through the opening. We need to seize the northern slope of those Heights fast and then hold it *no matter* what the Shadow tosses at us!”

에그웨인 opened her eyes. Though she shouldn’t have been in a room at all, she lay in one. And a fine one. The cool air smelled of salt, and she rested on a soft mattress.

*I’m dreaming,* she thought. Or perhaps she had died. Would that explain the pain? Such terrible pain. Nothingness would be better, far better, than this agony.

The Amyrlin has sympathy for 에그웨인 al’Vere, as she would have sympathy for any 에스 세다이 dealing with such loss. “ . . then I will give you this suggestion. Emotion will threaten to crush you. This is the danger. In the face of a lost 감시자, summoning *세다르* will be difficult. If you do manage it, 에스 세다이 serenity will likely be impossible. This can be dangerous. Very dangerous.”

Silviana opened her mouth, undoubtedly to suggest that 에그웨인 sit back down. At that moment, 에그웨인 found *세다르,*; the bud in her mind flowering, the 하나의 힘 rushing into her. She gave Silviana a defiant look, then began weaving a gateway.

에그웨인 stopped her with a look. Yes, most women waited. Yes, 에그웨인 al’Vere was pained from her loss, and 가윈 could never be replaced. But she *believed* in 감시자s. The 아미를린 석좌 needed someone to watch her back. Beyond that, every person with a 감시자 bond was a better fighter than those without. To go without a 감시자 was to deny the Light another soldier.

There was a person here who had saved her life. *No,* a piece of her said, her eyes falling on Leilwin. *Not a 쇼엔찬.*

Another piece of her, the Amyrlin, laughed at that. *Stop being such a child.* She would have a 감시자. “Leilwin Shipless,” 에그웨인 said loudly, “will you take this duty?”

The woman knelt, bowing her head. “I… yes.”

에그웨인 formed the weave for the bond. Leilwin stood, looking less fatigued, taking a deep breath. 에그웨인 opened a gateway to the other side of the chamber, then used her immediate knowledge of this room to open another one to where her people fought. Explosions, screams and the beating of weapons against shields poured through.

에그웨인 strode back onto the killing fields, bringing the fury of the Amyrlin with her.

디만드레드 was a blademaster. 갈라드 had assumed this would be the case, but he preferred to test his assumptions.

The two danced back and forth inside the ring of watching Sharans. 갈라드 wore lighter armor, mail under his tabard, and stepped more quickly. The interwoven coins 디만드레드 wore were heavier than simple mail, but good against a sword.

“You are better than your brother was,” 디만드레드 said. “He died easily.”

The man was trying to enrage 갈라드. He did not succeed. Cold, careful. 갈라드 moved in. The Courtier Taps His Fan. 디만드레드 responded with something very similar to The Falcon Stoops, slapping away 갈라드’s attack. 디만드레드 stepped back, walking around the perimeter of the ring, sword out to the side. At the beginning, he had spoken a great deal. Now he made only the occasional gibe.

They circled each other in the darkness, lit by torches held in Sharan hands. One rotation. Two.

“Come now,” 디만드레드 said. “I’m waiting.”

갈라드 remained silent. Each moment he stalled was a moment 디만드레드 was not sending destruction upon 엘레인 or her armies. The 버림받은 자들 seemed to realize it, for he came in swiftly. Three strikes: down, side, backhand. 갈라드 met each one, their arms a blur.

Motion to the side. It came from a rock that 디만드레드 had thrown at 갈라드 by channeling. 갈라드 dodged it, barely, then raised his sword against the blows that came next. Furious strikes downward, The Boar Rushes Down the Mountain, crashing against 갈라드’s blade. He held against that, but was not able to stop the following twist of the blade that cut his forearm.

디만드레드 stepped back, his sword dripping 갈라드’s blood. They circled around again, watching one another. 갈라드 felt warm blood inside his glove, from where it had seeped down his arm. A little blood loss could slow a man, weaken him.

갈라드 breathed in and out, abandoning thought, abandoning worry. When 디만드레드 next struck, 갈라드 anticipated it, stepping aside and striking down with two hands, biting deeply into the leather behind 디만드레드’s knee guard. The sword glanced off the side of the armor, but cut true otherwise. As 갈라드 whipped back around, 디만드레드 was limping.

The 버림받은 자들 grimaced. “You’ve blooded me,” he said. “It has been a very long time since someone did that.”

The ground began to heave and break beneath 갈라드. Desperate, he leaped forward, getting close to 디만드레드—forcing him to stop channeling, lest he topple himself. The 버림받은 자들 grunted, swinging, but 갈라드 was inside his enemy’s guard.

Too close to do a full swing, 갈라드 raised his sword and bashed it— pommel first—at 디만드레드’s face. 디만드레드 caught 갈라드’s hand with his, but 갈라드 grabbed 디만드레드 by the helmet, holding tightly, trying to force the helmet down over the 버림받은 자들’s eyes. He grunted, both men locked, neither moving.

Then, with a sickening sound 갈라드 heard quite distinctly, his muscle ripped in the arm where he’d been cut. His sword slipped from numb fingers, his arm spasming, and 디만드레드 threw him backward and struck with a flash of the blade.

갈라드 fell to his knees. His right arm—severed at the elbow by 디만드레드’s slice—flopped to the ground in front of him.

디만드레드 stepped back, panting. He had been worried. Good. 갈라드 held to his bleeding stump, then spat at 디만드레드’s feet.

디만드레드 snorted, then swung his blade once more.

All went black.

안드롤 felt as if he’d forgotten what it was like to breathe fresh air. The land around him smoldered and quaked, smoke churning in the wind, bringing with it the stench of burning bodies.

He and the others had moved up across the top of the Heights to the western side, searching for 타임. Much of the Sharan army fought here, contending with the 백색 탑 army.

He still wore Nensen’s face, but with his head down and his posture low, that mattered very little.

안드롤 froze. Up ahead, through the shifting smoke, he saw a ring of 트롤록s protecting something. They stood on an outcropping of rock that jutted out of the hillside like the seat of a chair.

안드롤 crept forward, hoping to steal a peek.

*안드롤!* 페바라’s voice in his mind made him jump nearly out of his skin.

*What?*

*You were alarmed at something,* she said. *I was reacting to you.*
