Gaul cursed, breaking out of his hiding place. This, apparently, was what Slayer had been wanting. Slayer launched a spear—one of Gaul’s own. It hit Gaul in the side. Gaul grunted, falling to his knees.

Slayer laughed, then raised his hands. A jet of air blew out from him, flinging wolves away. Gaul could barely hear the whimpers over the rushing wind.

“Here,” Slayer screamed into the tempest, “I am a *king!* Here, I am more than the 버림받은 자들. This place is mine, and I will…”

Perhaps the pain of Gauls wound was addling him; he thought that the winds were starting to die down.

“Here, I will…”

The winds stopped.

The entire valley grew silent. Slayer stiffened, then turned worried eyes toward the cavern beyond. Nothing there seemed to have changed.

“You are not a king,” a soft voice said.

Gaul twisted about. A figure stood on a rocky protrusion behind him, wearing the greens and browns of a 두 강 woodsman. His deep green cloak rippled faintly from the stilling winds. 페린 stood with his eyes closed, chin raised at a slight angle, as if toward the sun above—though, if there was one, it was blocked by clouds.

“This place belongs to the wolves,” 페린 said. “Not to you, not to me, not to any man. You cannot be a king here, Slayer. You have no subjects, and you never will.”

“Insolent pup,” Slayer snarled. “How many times must I kill you?”

페린 drew in a deep breath.

“I laughed when I found that Fain had killed your family,” Slayer yelled. “I *laughed.* I was supposed to kill him, you know. 그림자 thinks him wild and rogue, but he’s the first one who has managed to do something meaningful to bring you pain.”

페린 said nothing.

“Luc wanted to be part of something important,” Slayer shouted. “In that, we’re the same, though I sought the ability to channel. 어둠의 존재 cannot grant that, but he found something different for us, something better. Something that requires a soul to be melded with something else. Like what happened with you, Aybara. Like you.”

“We are nothing alike, Slayer,” 페린 said softly.

“But we are! That’s why I laughed. And you know, there’s a prophecy about Luc? That he’ll be important to the Last Battle. That’s why we’re here. We’ll kill you; then we’ll kill al’Thor. Just like we killed that wolf of yours.”

Standing on the rocky protrusion, 페린 opened his eyes. Gaul pulled back. Those golden eyes glowed like beacons.

The storm started again. And yet, that tempest seemed mild compared to the one Gaul saw in 페린’s eyes. Gaul felt a *pressure* from his friend. Like the pressure of the sun at noon after four days without having any water to drink.

Gaul stared up at 페린 for a few moments, then held a hand against his wound and ran.

The wind whipped at 맷 as he clung to the saddle of a winged beast hundreds of feet in the air.

“Oh, blood and bloody ashes!” 맷 yelled, one hand on his hat, the other clutching the saddle. He was tied in with some straps. Two little leather straps. Far too thin. Could they not have used more? Maybe ten or twenty? He would have been fine with a hundred!

*Morat’to’raken* were bloody insane. Every one of them! They did this every day! What was wrong with them?

Tied into the saddle in front of 맷, 올버 laughed with glee.

*Poor lad\* 맷 thought. *He’s so frightened he’s going mad. The lack of air up here is getting to him.*

“There it is, my Prince!” the *morat’to’raken*, Sulaan, called to him from her place at the front of the flying beast. She was a pretty thing. Completely insane, too. “We’ve reached the valley. Are you sure you want to set down in there?”

“No!” 맷 shouted.

“Good answer!” The woman made her beast swoop.

“Blood and bloody—”

올버 laughed.

The *to’raken* brought them down over a long valley clogged with a frenzied battle. 맷 tried to let his attention settle on the fighting, rather than on the fact that he was in the air flying on a lizard with two bloody lunatics.

Heaps of 트롤록 bodies told that story as well as any map could have. The 트롤록s had burst through defenses at the valley mouth behind 맷. He flew over that, toward the mountain of 세이올 굴 ahead, valley walls to his right and left.

It was mayhem below. Roving bands of 아일 and 트롤록s moved through the valley, striking at each other here and there. Some soldiers, not 아일, defended the way up to the Pit of Doom, but that was the only organized formation 맷 could see.

Along the side of the valley a deep mist had begun to flood down onto its floor. At first, 맷 was confused, thinking it had come from the heroes of the Horn. But no, the Horn was strapped to the saddle beside 맷’s *ashandarei.* And this mist was too… silvery. If that was the right word. He thought he’d seen that mist before.

Then, 맷 felt something. From that mist. A prickling cold sensation, followed by what he swore was whispering in his mind. He knew immediately what it was.

Oh, Light!

“맷, look!” 올버 called, pointing. “Wolves!”

A group of jet black animals, almost as large as horses, were assaulting the soldiers defending the path up to 세이올 굴. The wolves were making quick work of the men. Light! As if things had not been difficult enough.

“Those aren’t wolves,” 맷 said grimly. The Wild Hunt had come to Thakan’dar.

Maybe they and Mashadar would destroy one another? Was that too much to hope for? With the dice tumbling in his head, 맷 was not going to bet on it. 랜드’s forces—what was left of the 아일, 도마니, Dragon-sworn and 타이런 soldiers who had come here—would be crushed by the 어둠의 사냥개s. If they survived, Mashadar would take them. They could not fight either one.

That voice in there ... It wasn’t just Mashadar, the mindless mist. Fain was here somewhere, too. And the dagger.

세이올 굴 loomed above. High in the air, clouds churned. Surprisingly, some white thunderheads had rolled in from the south, colliding with the black as they spun together. Actually, those two together looked an awful lot like the—

The *to’raken* turned and winged about, then swooped down lower, maybe only a hundred feet off the ground.

“Be careful!” 맷 hollered, holding on to his hat. “Are you bloody trying to kill us!”

“Apologies, my Prince,” the woman yelled back. “I just need to find a safe place to put you down.”

“A *safe* place?” 맷 said. “Good luck on that.”

“It’s going to be difficult. Dhana is strong, but I—”

A black-fletched arrow grazed the side of Sulaan’s head, loosed from somewhere down below, along with a flight of a dozen others that zipped around 맷, one hitting the wing of the *to’raken.*

맷 cursed, dropping his hat and reaching for Sulaan as 올버 cried out in shock. Sulaan went limp, dropping the reins. Below, a group of red-veiled 아일 prepared another volley.

맷 undid his straps. He leaped—well, more crawled—over 올버 and the unconscious woman and grabbed the reins of the panicked *to’raken.* This could not be too much harder than riding a horse, could it? He pulled as he had seen Sulaan do, turning the *to'raken* as arrows cut the air behind them, several taking the beast in the wings.

They veered straight toward the rock wall, and 맷 found himself on his feet, standing on the saddle and gripping the reins tightly as he tried to keep the wounded beast from bloody killing them all. That turn nearly tossed him free, but he held himself in place with feet wedged and holding the reins even tighter.

The rush of air as they turned caught up 올버’s next words. The creature’s badly wounded wings beat wildly and it screeched wretchedly. 맷 was not certain *either* of them were in control as the beast twisted toward the ground.

They hit the floor of the valley in a heap. Bones cracked—Light, 맷 hoped they belonged to the *to’raken*—and he found himself tumbling end over end across the broken ground.

He finally came to a rest, flopping over.

He breathed in and out, stunned by it all. “That,” he finally groaned, “is the bloody worst idea I’ve ever had.” He hesitated. “Maybe the second worst.” He *had* decided to kidnap 투온, after all.

He stumbled to his feet, and his legs still seemed to work. He did not limp too badly as he ran to the twitching *to’raken*. “올버? 올버!”

He found the boy still tied in the saddle, blinking and shaking his head to clear it. “맷,” 올버 said, “next time I think you should let me fly it. I don’t think you did a very good job.”

“If there is a next time,” 맷 said, “I’ll eat a whole bag of 타르 발론 gold.” He yanked free the ties holding his *ashandarei* and 올버’s Horn, then handed the instrument to the boy. He reached for the pack with 랜드’s banner, which he’d carried tied at his waist, but it was gone.

Panicked, 맷 looked about. “The banner! I dropped the bloody banner!”

올버 smiled, looking up at the sign made by the swirling clouds. “It will be fine—we're beneath his banner already,” he said, then lifted the Horn and blew a beautiful note.

*To Awaken*

랜드 broke free from the darkness and entered the Pattern fully again.

From his watching of the Pattern, he knew that although only minutes had passed here since he’d entered, in the valley outside this cavern, days had passed, and farther out into the world, it had been much longer.

랜드 threw 모리딘 back from the position they’d held during those tense minutes with blades locked. Still full of the 하나의 힘, so sweet, 랜드 whipped the blade of *칼란도르* at his old friend.

모리딘 got his sword up in time to block, but only barely. He growled, pulling a knife from his belt and stepping back into a knife-and-sword stance.

“You don’t matter any longer, Elan,” 랜드 said, the torrent of *세이딘* raging within him. “Let us finish this!”

“I don’t?” 모리딘 laughed.

Then he spun and threw the knife at Alanna.

니나브 watched in horror as the knife spun through the air. The winds didn’t touch it for some reason.

*No!* After she had coaxed the woman back to life. *I cannot lose her now!* 니나브 tried to catch the knife or block it, but she moved just a hair too slowly.

The knife buried itself in Alanna’s breast.

니나브 looked at it, horrified. This was not a wound that sewing and herbs could heal. That blade hit the heart.

“랜드! I need the 하나의 힘!” 니나브 cried.

“Its… all right…” Alanna whispered.

니나브 looked at the woman's eyes. She was lucid. *The andilay,* 니나브 realized, remembering the herb she’d used to give the woman strength. *It brought her out of her stupor. It awakened her.*

“I can . . ” Alanna said. “I can release him…”

The light faded from her eyes.

니나브 looked at 모리딘 and 랜드. 랜드 glanced at the dead woman with pity and sorrow, but 니나브 saw no rage in his eyes. Alanna had released the bond before 랜드 could feel the effects of her death.

모리딘 turned back to 랜드, another knife in his left hand. 랜드 raised *칼란도르* to strike 모리딘 down.

모리딘 dropped his sword, and stabbed his own right hand with the knife. 랜드 twitched suddenly, and *칼란도르* dropped from his grip as if *his* hand somehow hurt from 모리딘’s attack.

The glow emanating from the blade winked out, and the crystalline blade rang as it hit the ground.

페린 did not hold back in the fight with Slayer.

He did not try to distinguish between wolf and man. He finally let everything out, every bit of rage at Slayer, every bit of pain at the deaths of his family—pressures which had been growing inside him unnoticed for months.

He let it out. Light, he let it out. As he had on that terrible night when he’d killed those 백의단. Ever since then, he’d clamped a firm grip on himself and his emotions. Just as 루한 장인 had said.

He could see it now, in a frozen moment. Gentle 페린, always afraid of hurting someone. A blacksmith who had learned control. He had rarely let himself strike with all of his strength.

This day, he took the leash off the wolf. It had never belonged there anyway.

The storm *conformed* to his rage. 페린 didn’t try to keep it back. Why would he? It matched his emotions perfectly. The fall of his hammer was like claps of thunder, the flashing of his eyes like lightning bolts. Wolves howled alongside the wind.

Slayer tried to fight back. He jumped, he *shifted*, he stabbed. Each time, 페린 was there. Jumping at him as a wolf, swinging at him as a man, buffeting him like the tempest itself. Slayer got a wild look in his eyes. He raised a shield, trying to put it between himself and 페린.

페린 attacked. Without thought, now, he became instinct only. 페린 roared, smashing his hammer into that shield time and time again. *Driving* Slayer before him. *Beating* the shield like a stubborn length of iron. *Pounding* away his anger, his fury.

His last blow threw Slayer back and flung the shield from the man’s hands, sending it spinning a hundred feet in the air. Slayer hit the valley floor and rolled, gasping. He came to rest in the middle of the battlefield, shadowy figures rising all around him and dying as they fought in the real world. He looked at 페린 with panic, then vanished.

페린 sent himself into the waking world to follow. He appeared amid the battle, 아일 against 트롤록s in a furious fight. The winds were surprisingly strong on this side, and black clouds spun above 세이올 굴, which rose like a crooked finger into the sky.

The nearby 아일 barely took time to notice him. The bodies of 트롤록s and humans lay in heaps across the battlefield, and the place stank of death. The ground had once been dusty here, but now it churned with mud made from the blood of the fallen.

Slayer pushed through a group of 아일 nearby, growling, slashing with his long knife. He didn’t look back—and it didn’t seem that he knew 페린 had followed him into the real world.

A new wave of 그림자태생 pushed in off the slope, out of a silvery white mist. Their skin looked strange, pocked with holes, their eyes milky white. 페린 ignored these and barreled after Slayer.

*어린 황소!* Wolves. *그림자brothers are here! We fight!*

어둠의 사냥개s. Wolves hated all 그림자태생; an entire pack would die pulling down a 미르드랄. But 어둠의 사냥개s they feared.

페린 looked around to spot the creatures. Ordinary men could not fight 어둠의 사냥개s, whose mere saliva was death. Nearby, the human forces broke before a tide of black wolves the size of horses. The Wild Hunt.

Light! Those 어둠의 사냥개s were enormous. Scores of the jet black, corrupted wolves ripped through the defensive lines, throwing 타이런 and 도마니 soldiers about as if they were rag dolls. Wolves attacked the 어둠의 사냥개s, but in vain. They screamed and howled and died.

페린 raised his voice alongside their cries of death, a ragged yell of rage. For the moment, he could not help. His instincts and passions drove him. Slayer. He *had* to defeat Slayer. If 페린 did not stop Slayer, the man would shift to the World of Dreams and kill 랜드.

페린 turned and ran through the fighting armies, chasing after the distant figure ahead. Slayer had gained a lead by 페린’s distraction, but the man had slowed a little. He had not yet realized that 페린 could leave the World of Dreams.

Ahead, Slayer stopped and inspected the battlefield. He glanced back and saw 페린—then his eyes widened. 페린 couldn’t hear his words over the din, but could read Slayer’s lips as he whispered, “No. No, it can’t be.”

*Yes,* 페린 thought. I *can follow you now, wherever you run. This is a hunt. You, finally, are the prey.*

Slayer vanished, and 페린 *shifted* into the wolf dream after him. The people fighting around him became patterns in the dust, exploding and reforming. Slayer yelled in fright at seeing him, then *shifted* back into the waking world.

페린 did likewise. He could *smell* Slayer’s trail. Slick with sweat, panicked. To the dream, then to the waking world again. In the dream, 페린 ran on four legs, as 어린 황소. In the waking world, he was 페린, hammer held aloft.

He *shifted* back and forth between the two as frequently as he blinked, chasing Slayer. When he hit a patch of fighting bodies, he would jump into the wolf dream and crash through the figures made of sand and blown dust, then *shift* back into the waking world to keep on the trail. The *shifting* started to happen so quickly, he flickered between the two with each heartbeat.

Thump. 페린 raised his hammer, leaping off a small ridge after the scrambling form ahead.

Thump. 어린 황소 howled, summoning the pack.

Thump. 페린 was close now. Only a few steps behind. Slayer’s odor was pungent.

Thump. The spirits of wolves appeared around 어린 황소, howling their thirst for the hunt. Never had a prey deserved it more. Never had a prey done more damage to the packs. Never had a man been more feared.

Thump. Slayer stumbled. He twisted as he fell, sending himself to the wolf dream by reflex.

Thump. 페린 swung *Mah’alleinir*; emblazoned with the leaping wolf. He who soars.

Thump. 어린 황소 leaped for the throat of the killer of his brothers. Slayer fled.

The hammer connected.

Something about this place, this moment, sent 페린 and Slayer into a spiraling series of flickers between worlds. Back and forth, back and forth, flashes of moments and thoughts. Flicker. Flicker. Flicker.

Men died around them. Some of dust, some of flesh. Their world, alongside shadows of other worlds. Men in strange clothing and armor, fighting beasts of all shapes and sizes. Moments where the 아일 became 쇼엔찬, who became something between the two, with spears and light eyes but helmets shaped like monstrous insects.

In all of those moments, in all of those places, 페린’s hammer struck and 어린 황소’s fangs grabbed Slayer by the neck. He tasted the salty warmth of Slayer’s blood in his mouth. He felt the hammer vibrate as it hit, and he heard bones crack. The worlds flashed like bolts of lightning.

Everything crashed, shook, then pulled together.

페린 stood on the rocks in the valley of Thakan’dar, and Slayer’s body crumpled in front of him, head crushed. 페린 panted, the thrill of the hunt clinging to him. It was over.

He turned, surprised to find that he was surrounded by 아일. He frowned at them. “What are you doing?”

One of the Maidens laughed. “You looked like you were running to a great dance, 페린 Aybara. One learns to watch for warriors like you on the battlefield and follow. They often have the most fun.”

He smiled grimly, surveying the battlefield. It was not going well for his side. The 어둠의 사냥개s ripped apart the defenders in a ruthless frenzy. The way up to 랜드 was completely exposed.

“Who commands this battle?” 페린 asked.

“Nobody, now,” the Maiden said. He did not know her name. “로델 이투랄데 did first. Then 달린 Sisnera led—but his command post fell to 드라그카르. I have not seen any 에스 세다이 or clan chiefs in hours.”

Her voice was grim. Even the stalwart 아일 were flagging. A quick scan of the battlefield showed 페린 that the remaining 아일 fought wherever they were, often in small groups, doing as much harm as they could before being cut down. The wolves who had fought here in packs were broken, their sendings those of pain and fear. And 페린 didn’t know what those 그림자태생 with the pocked faces meant.

The battle was finished, and the side of Light had lost.

The 어둠의 사냥개s broke through the line of 용worn nearby, the last group who held falling before them. A few tried to flee, but one of the 어둠의 사냥개s leapt on them, pushing several to the ground and gnawing one. Frothing saliva sprayed across the others, and they dropped, twitching.

페린 lowered his hammer, then knelt, pulling off Slayer’s cloak and wrapping the cloth around his hands as he picked up his hammer again. “Don’t let their spittle touch your skin. It is deadly.”

The 아일 nodded, those with bare hands wrapping them. They smelled of determination, but also resignation. 아일 would run toward death if it was the only option, and would laugh while doing so. Wetlanders thought them mad, but 페린 could smell the truth on them. They were not mad. They did not fear death, but they did not welcome it.

“Touch me, all of you,” 페린 said.

The 아일 did so. He *shifted* them to the wolf dream—taking so many was a strain, like bending a bar of steel—but he managed it. He immediately *shifted* them to the path up to the Pit of Doom. The spirits of wolves had gathered here, silent. Hundreds of them.

페린 brought the 아일 back to the waking world, his *shift* placing him and his small force between 랜드 and the 어둠의 사냥개s. The Wild Hunt looked up, corrupted eyes shining like silver as they fixed on 페린.

“We will hold here,” 페린 said to his 아일, “and hope that some others aid us.”

“We will stand,” one of the 아일 said, a tall man wearing one of those headbands marked with 랜드’s symbol.

“And if we do not,” another said, “and wake instead, then we will at least water the earth with our blood and let our bodies nourish the plants that will now grow here.” 페린 had barely noticed the plants growing, incongruously, green and vibrant in the valley. Small, but strong. A manifestation of the fact that 랜드 still fought.

The 어둠의 사냥개s slunk toward them, tails down, ears back, fangs exposed, gleaming like bloodstained metal. What was that he heard over the wind? Something very soft, very distant. It seemed so soft that he shouldn’t have noticed it. But it pierced through the clamor of war. Faintly familiar…

“I know that sound,” 페린 said.

“Sound?” the 아일 Maiden said. “What sound? The calls of the wolves?”

“No,” 페린 said as the 어둠의 사냥개s began to lope up the path. “발레르의 뿔.”

The heroes would come. But upon which battlefield would they fight? 페린 could expect no relief here. Except…

*Lead us, 어린 황소.*

Why must the heroes all be human?

A howl rose in the same pitch as that of the sounded Horn. He looked upon a field suddenly filled with a multitude of glowing wolves. They were great pale beasts, the size of 어둠의 사냥개s. The spirits of those wolves who had died, then gathered here, waiting for the sign, waiting for the chance to fight.

The Horn had called them.

페린 let loose a yell of his own, a howl of pleasure, then charged forward to meet the 어둠의 사냥개s.

The Last Hunt had finally, truly arrived.

맷 left 올버 with the heroes again. The boy looked like a prince, riding in front of Noal as they attacked the 트롤록s and prevented anyone from climbing that path to kill 랜드.

맷 borrowed a horse from one of the defenders who still had one, then galloped over to find 페린. His friend would be among those wolves, of course. 맷 did not know how those hundreds of big glowing wolves had entered the battlefield, but he was not going to complain. They met the Wild Hunt head-on, snarling and savaging the 어둠의 사냥개s. Howls from both sides flooded 맷’s ears.
He passed some 아일 fighting a 어둠의 사냥개, but the people did not stand a chance. They tripped the beast, hacking at it, but it pulled back together as if it were made of darkness and not flesh—then ripped into them. Blood and bloody ashes! Those 아일 weapons did not even seem to scratch, it. 맷 continued galloping, avoiding the tendrils of silvery mist making their way across the whole valley.

Light! That mist was approaching the path up to 랜드. It was picking up speed, rolling over 아일, 트롤록s and 어둠의 사냥개s alike.

*There,* 맷 thought, picking out a man fool enough to fight 어둠의 사냥개s. 페린 slammed his hammer down on a 어둠의 사냥개s head, cracking it and forcing it into the ground. When he raised his hammer, it trailed smoke behind it. The 어둠의 사냥개, amazingly, remained dead.

페린 turned, then stared. “맷!” he called. “What are you doing here?”

“Coming to help!” 맷 said. “Against my bloody better judgment!”

“You can’t fight 어둠의 사냥개s, 맷,” 페린 said as 맷 rode up beside him. “I can, and so can the Last Hunt.” He cocked his head, then looked toward the sound of the Horn.

“No,” 맷 said, “I didn’t sound it. That bloody burden has passed to someone who actually seems to enjoy it.”

“It’s not that, 맷.” 페린 stepped up, reaching and taking him by the arm as he sat mounted. “My wife, 맷. Please. She had the Horn.”

맷 looked down, feeling grim. “The lad said… Light, 페린. 파일 was at Merrilor, and led the 트롤록s away from 올버 so he could escape with the Horn.”

“Then she could still be alive,” 페린 said.

“Yes. Of course she could,” 맷 said. What else could he say? “페린, you need to know something else. Fain is here on this battlefield.”

“Fain?” 페린 growled. “Where?”

“He’s in that mist! 페린, he’s brought Mashadar, somehow. Don’t let it touch you.”

“I was in Shadar Logoth too, 맷,” 페린 said. “I have a debt to settle with Fain.”

“And I don’t?” 맷 said. “I—”

페린’s eyes opened wide. He stared at 맷’s chest.

There, a small white ribbon of silvery mist—Mashadar’s mist—had speared 맷 from behind through the chest. 맷 looked at it, jerked once, then tumbled off his horse.

*Watching the Flow Writhe*

아비엔다 struggled on the slopes of the valley of Thakan’dar, trying to avoid the shield of Spirit 그랜달 was attempting to slip into place. A weave, like lace, defying her attempts to reach for the 하나의 힘. Her feet ruined, she could not stand. She lay, in pain, barely able to move.

She fought it off, but barely.

The 버림받은 자들 leaned against the rocks of the ledge, as she had been doing for a short time, muttering to herself. Her side bled bright red blood. Below them, in the valley, the battle raged. A silvery white mist was rolling across the dead and some of the living.

아비엔다 tried to crawl toward her gateway. That lay open still, and through it she could see the valley floor. Something must have drawn Cadsuane and the others away—either that, or 아비엔다 had made the gateway to the wrong place.

The glow of *세다르* surrounded 그랜달 again. More weaves; 아비엔다 broke them, but they delayed her progress toward the gateway.

그랜달 groaned, then pulled herself upright. She staggered in 아비엔다’s direction, though the woman looked dazed by her blood loss.

아비엔다 could do little to defend herself, weak as she was from blood loss. She was helpless.

“Let them know. All of them.”

Flinn nodded, and 페린 stepped out after 니나브. He found what he’d hoped to see, the reason why she’d left so quickly. Just outside the tent, 란 held her tightly. The man looked as bloodied and tired as 페린 felt. Their eyes met, and they nodded to one another.

“Several of the Windfinders have opened a gateway between here and Merrilor,” 란 said to 페린. “어둠의 존재 is sealed away again. The Blasted 란ds are blooming, and gateways can open here again.”

“Thank you,” 페린 said, passing him by. “Has anyone . . . heard anything about 파일?”

페린 nodded. He’d already spoken with 맷, and 올버. It seemed to him that . . . that he’d been avoiding thinking about what must have happened.

*Don’t think about it,* he told himself. *Don’t you dare.* He steeled himself, then went to seek the gateway 란 had mentioned.

And, he admitted to himself, he wanted to see 맷 and 페린. See that they were all right. So much had happened; he wanted to talk to his friends and make certain they were well. With what was happening to 랜드 . . .

The 아일 woman smiled at him drunkenly. 로이알 sighed, then continued through the camp. The day was coming to an end. The day of the Last Battle! It was the Fourth Age now, wasn’t it? Could an age start in the middle of a day? That would be inconvenient for the calendars, wouldn’t it? But everyone agreed. 랜드 had sealed the 구멍 at noon.

로이알 continued through the camp. They hadn’t moved from the base of 세이올 굴. 니나브 said she was too worried to move 랜드. 로이알 kept searching, peeking into tents. In the next, he found the grizzled general 이투랄데, surrounded by four 에스 세다이.

The Merchant Council . . .”

로이알 slipped away and shook his head, feeling sorry for the man. *Four* 에스 세다이. 이투랄데 would be crowned before the day was out.

로이알 stopped by the main 치유 tent again to check if anyone had seen 맷. He had been to this battlefield, and people said he was smiling and healthy, but . . . well, 로이알 wanted to see for himself. Wanted to talk to him.

He peeked in on 랜드. His friend looked worse than before. 란 stood by the wall. He wore a crown—it was just a simple silver band—where the *hadori* used to rest. That wasn’t odd, but the matching one 니나브 wore did give 로이알 a start.

니나브 seemed troubled. She still had red eyes, but before, she had chivvied anyone who mentioned them, so 로이알 said nothing. Humans often seemed to want him to say nothing, which was odd for people who lived lives so hastily.

She looked at 로이알, and he bowed his head to her.

로이알 left them, though he did check in on 아비엔다 in a nearby tent. She sat while several women attended to her twisted, bleeding feet. She had lost several of her toes. She nodded her head to 로이알; the 치유s done so far had apparently taken away her pain, for though she seemed tired, she did not seem in agony.

“I have not seen him, 로이알, son of 아렌트 son of 할란,” 아비엔다 replied. “At least, not since you asked a short time ago.”

로이알 blushed, then left her. He passed 엘레인 and 민 outside. He would get their stories—he had already asked a few questions—but the three *ta’veren* . . . they were most important! Why were humans always bustling around so quickly, never sitting still? Never any time to think. This was an important day.

It *was* odd, though. 민 and 엘레인. Shouldn’t they be at 랜드’s side? 엘레인 seemed to be taking reports on casualties and refugee supplies, and 민 sat looking up at 세이올 굴, a far-off expression in her eyes. Neither went in to hold 랜드’s hand as he slipped toward death.

*Well,* 로이알 thought, *maybe 맷 sneaked by me and went back to Merrilor.* Never staying put, these men. Always so hasty . . .

매트림 카우톤 sauntered into the 쇼엔찬 camp on the south side of Merrilor, away from the piles of the dead.

All around, 쇼엔찬 men and women gasped, hands to their mouths. He tipped his hat to them.

투온 looked at 맷 and frowned. “Where have you been?”

맷 raised his arm, and 투온 frowned, looking upward at nothing. 맷 spun and thrust his hand farther toward the sky.

The sounds of the display washed over them.

투온 frowned. The explosions reflected in her dark eyes. “I’m with child,” she said. “The Doomseer has confirmed it.”

맷 felt a jolt, as sure as if a firework had gone off inside of his stomach. An heir. A son, no doubt! What odds that it was a boy? 맷 forced a grin. “Well, I guess I’m off the hook, now. You have an heir.”

“I have an heir,” 투온 said, “but I am the one off that hook. Now I can kill you, if I want.”

맷 felt his grin widen. “Well, we’ll have to see what we can work out. Tell me, do you ever play dice?”

페린 sat down among the dead and finally started weeping.

Lord and Lady 바쉐어 were dead. 파일 would have been queen, if she’d lived. 페린 shook and trembled, and he could not make himself move any more. There were hundreds of thousands of dead on this battlefield. The other searchers ignored a body if it had no life, marking it and moving on. He had tried to spread the word for them to seek 파일, but the searchers had to look for the living.

Fireworks exploded in the darkening sky. 페린 buried his head in his hands, then felt himself slide sideways and collapse among the corpses.

모그헤디엔 winced at the display in the sky. Each explosion made her see that deadly fire again, tearing through the Sharans. That flare of light, that moment of panic.

And then . . . and then darkness. She’d awakened some time later, left for dead among the bodies of Sharans. When she’d come to, she had found these fools all across the battlefield, claiming to have won the day.

*Claiming?* she thought, wincing again as another round of 불꽃놀이 sounded. *The Great Lord has fallen.* All was lost.

No. No. She continued forward, keeping her step firm, unsuspicious. She had strangled a worker, then taken her form, channeling only a tiny bit and inverting the weave. That should let her escape from this place. She wove around bodies, ignoring the stink to the air.

All was not lost. She still lived. And she was of the Chosen! That meant . . . that meant that she was an empress among her lessers. Why, the Great Lord was imprisoned again, so he could not punish her. And certainly most, if not all, of the other Chosen were dead or imprisoned. If that were true, no one could rival her in knowledge.

This might actually work out. This might be a *victory*. She stopped beside an overturned supply cart, clutching her *cour’souvra*—it was still whole, thankfully. She smiled with a wide grin, then wove a small light to illuminate her way.

Yes . . . Look at the open sky, not the thunderclouds. She could turn this to her advantage. Why ... in the matter of a few years, she could be ruling the world herself!

Something cold snapped around her neck.

모그헤디엔 reached up with horror, then screamed. “No! Not *again!*” Her disguise melted away and the 하나의 힘 left her.

Her companion nodded, and the *다만* made a gateway.

They had to drag 모그헤디엔 through.

니나브 emerged from the 치유 tent at 세이올 굴. The sun was almost below the horizon.

란 came out of the tent behind her, putting an arm around her shoulders. She raised her hand to his. Nearby, 민 and 엘레인 looked at one another.

He followed.

. . with Rhuarc dead,” 아비엔다 was saying to Sorilea and Bair, “I think that whatever I saw *must* be able to change. It has already.”

The other two nodded, then glanced at 니나브 and grew as still-faced as 에스 세다이. 아비엔다 was just as bad as the others, completely calm as she sat in her chair, her feet wrapped in bandages. She might walk again someday, but she would never fight.

“니나브 al’Meara,” 아비엔다 said.

니나브 leaned down. “All right,” she said menacingly, embracing the Source. “Out with it. I chose you because you can’t run away from me.”

아비엔다 displayed a moment of what might have been fear. It was gone in a flash. “Let us prepare his pyre.”

페린 ran in the wolf dream. Alone.

Other wolves howled their sorrow for his grief. After he passed them, they would return to their celebrations, but that did not make their empathy any less real.

He did not howl. He did not cry out. He became 어린 황소, and he ran.

He did not want to be here. He wanted slumber, true slumber. There, he could not feel the pain. Here he could.

*I shouldn’t have left her.*

A thought of men. Why did it creep in!

*But what could I do? I promised not to treat her like glass.*

Run. Run fast. Run until exhaustion came!

*I had to go to 랜드. I* had *to. But in doing so, I failed her!*

To the 두 강 in a flash. Back out, along the river. The 황무지, then back, a long run toward Falme.

*How could I be expected to hold them both, then let one go?*

To 티어. Then to the 두 강. A blur, growling, moving as quickly as he could. Here. Here he had wed her.

Here he howled.

Caemlyn, 케렌, Dumai’s Wells.

Here he saved one of them.

케렌, 게알단, Malden.

Here he had saved another.

Two forces in his life. Each had pulled at him. 어린 황소 finally collapsed near some hills somewhere in 안도르. A familiar place.

*The place where I met 엘리아스.*

He became 페린 again. His thoughts were not wolf thoughts, his troubles not wolf troubles. He stared up at the sky that was now, after 랜드's sacrifice, empty of clouds. He had wanted to be with his friend as he died.

This time, he would be with 파일 where she had died.

“I learned . . .”

A bird’s cry.

It sounded like a falcon.

Here he found a tiny falcon—as small as his hand—crying softly, with a broken leg pinned beneath a rock. Its heartbeat was faint.

Flowery soap. A hint of perfume in the air. 페린 dashed toward it, throwing his weight against the corpse of an enormous 트롤록, lying almost chest-high atop other bodies. Beneath it, he found the carcass of a horse. Unable to truly consider what he was doing, or of the strength it should have required, 페린 pulled the horse aside.

Beneath, 파일 lay bloodied in a small hollow in the ground, breathing shallowly. 페린 cried out and dropped to his knees, cradling her in his arms, breathing in her scent.

파일, his falcon, trembled and stirred. Then she opened her eyes and smiled at him.

And what am I planning?”

비르기테 smiled, then closed her eyes, and let herself drift away.

As evening settled onto the land, Tam looked up across what had once been the most feared place of all. 세이올 굴. The last flickers of light showed plants growing here, flowers blooming, grass growing up around fallen weapons and over corpses.

랜드 could finally rest.

*I need a mirror.*

He found one beyond the next partition of the tent. Apparently, he’d been left completely alone. He held up the candle, looking into the small mirror. 모리딘’s face looked back at him.

랜드 touched his face, feeling it. In his right eye hung a single *saa,* black, shaped like the dragon’s fang. It didn’t move.

랜드 slipped back into the portion of the tent where he’d awakened. Laman’s sword was there, sitting atop a neat pile of mixed clothing. Alivia apparently hadn’t known what he would want to wear. She had been the one to leave these things, of course, along with a bag of coins from a variety of nations. She hadn’t ever cared much for either clothing or coin, but she had known he’d need both.

*She will help you die.* 랜드 shook his head, dressing and gathering the coins and the sword, then slipping out of the tent. Someone had left a good horse, a dappled gelding, tied not far away. That would do him well. From 용의 환생 to horsethief. He chuckled to himself. Bareback would have to do.

He hesitated. Nearby, in the darkness, people were singing. This was 세이올 굴, but not as he remembered it. A blooming 세이올 굴, full of life.
The song they sang was a Borderlander funeral song. 랜드 led the horse through the night to get a little closer. He peered between the tents to where three women stood around a funeral pyre.

*모리딘,* he thought. *He’s being cremated with full honors as the 용의 환생.*

랜드 backed away, then mounted the dapple. As he did so, he noticed one figure who was not standing by the fire. A solitary figure, who looked toward him when all other eyes were turned away.

Cadsuane. She looked him up and down, eyes reflecting firelight from the glow of 랜드's pyre. 랜드 nodded, waited for a moment, then turned the horse and heeled it away.

Cadsuane watched him go.

*Curious,* she thought. Those eyes had confirmed her suspicions. That would be information she could use. No need to keep watching this sham of a funeral, then.

She walked away through the camp, and there strolled directly into an ambush.

“사에린,” she said as the women fell in around her. “유키리, Lyrelle, Rubinde. What is this?”

“We would like direction,” Rubinde said.

“Direction?” Cadsuane snorted. “Ask the new Amyrlin, once you find some poor woman to put into the position.”

The other women continued to walk with her.

As it hit her, Cadsuane stopped in place.

“Oh, *blood and ashes*, no!” Cadsuane said, spinning on them. “No, no, *no”*

The women smiled in an almost predatory way.

“You always talked so wisely to the 용의 환생 of responsibility,” 유키리 said.

“You speak of how the women of this Age need better training,” 사에린 added.

“It is a new Age,” Lyrelle said. “We have many challenges ahead of us . . . and we will need a strong Amyrlin to lead us.”

Cadsuane closed her eyes, groaning.

랜드 breathed a sigh of relief as he left Cadsuane behind. She did not raise an alarm, though she had continued to study him as he put distance between them. Glancing over his shoulder, he noticed her walking off with some other 에스 세다이.

She worried him; she probably suspected something he wished she did not. It was better than her raising an alarm, though.

He sighed, fishing in his pocket, where he found a pipe. *Thank you, Alivia, for that,* he thought, packing it with tabac from a pouch he found in the other pocket. By instinct, he reached for the 하나의 힘 to light it.

He found nothing. No *세이딘* in the void, nothing. He paused, then smiled and felt an enormous relief. He could not channel. Just to be certain, he tentatively reached for the 진정한 힘. Nothing there either.

He regarded his pipe, riding up a little incline to the side of Thakan dar, now covered in plants. No way to light the tabac. He inspected it for a moment in the darkness, then *thought* of the pipe being lit. And it was.

랜드 smiled and turned south. He glanced over his shoulder. All three women at the pyre had turned from it to look directly at him. He could make them out, though not much else, by the light of the burning body.

*I wonder which of them will follow me,* he thought, then smiled deeper. *랜드 al’Thor, you’ve built up quite a swelled head, haven’t you? Assuming that one, or more, would follow.*

Maybe none of them would. Or maybe all of them would, in their own time. He found himself chuckling.

Which would he pick? 민 ... but no, to leave 아비엔다? 엘레인. No. He laughed. He couldn’t pick. He had three women in love with him, and didn’t know which he would like to have follow him. Any of them. All of them. *Light, man. You’re hopeless. Hopelessly in love with all three, and there's no way out of it.*

He heeled the horse into a canter, heading farther south. He had a purse full of coin, a good horse and a strong sword. Laman’s sword, which was a better sword than he’d have wanted. It might draw attention. It was a true heron-marked sword with a fine blade.

Did Alivia realize how much money she’d given him? She didn't know a thing about coins. She’d probably stolen the lot of it, so he wasn't just a horsethief. Well, he’d told her to get him some gold, and she’d done it. He could buy an entire farm in the 두 강 with what he carried.

South. East or west would do, but he figured he wanted to go someplace away from it all for good. South first, then maybe out west, along the coast. Maybe he could find a ship? There was so much of the world he hadn't seen. He’d experienced a few battles, he’d gotten caught up in a huge Game of Houses. Many things he hadn’t wanted anything to do with. He’d seen his father’s farm. And palaces. He’d seen a lot of palaces.

He just had not had the leisure to have a real look at much of the world. *That will be new,* he thought. 이동 without being chased, or having to rule here or there. 이동 where he could just sleep in a barn in exchange for splitting someone’s firewood. He thought about that, and found himself laughing, riding on south and smoking his impossible pipe. As he did so, a wind rose up around him, around the man who had been called lord, 용의 환생, king, killer, lover and friend.

The wind rose high and free, to soar in an open sky with no clouds. It passed over a broken landscape scattered with corpses not yet buried. A landscape covered, at the same time, with celebrations. It tickled the branches of trees that had finally begun to put forth buds.

The wind blew southward, through knotted forests, over shimmering plains and toward lands unexplored. This wind, it was not the ending. There are no endings, and never will be endings, to the turning of the Wheel of Time.

But it was *an* ending.

> And it came to pass in those days, as it had come before and would come again, that the Dark lay heavy on the land and weighed down the hearts of men, and the green things failed, and hope died. And men cried out to the Creator, saying, O Light of the Heavens, Light of the World, let the Promised One be born of the mountain, according to the prophecies, as he was in ages past and will be in ages to come. Let the Prince of the Morning sing to the land that green things will grow and the valleys give forth lambs. Let the arm of the Lord of the Dawn shelter us from the Dark, and the great sword of justice defend us. Let the Dragon ride again on the winds of time.

*The Cycle of the Dragon.*
